figures.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering

taxonomy.task: novel-view synthesis / radiance field optimisation

arrangement.units: unenclosed flat grey/white rectangles plus two free-floating data glyphs (dot scatter, Gaussian cluster); no containers
arrangement.inputs_as: scatter of black SfM points; Camera box enters from the top
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; gradient flow shown by blue reverse arrows
arrangement.shared: the 3D Gaussians hub is shared by projection and density control branches

insights.structure: A short left-to-right lead-in (SfM point scatter -> Initialization -> 3D Gaussians) feeds a loop in which Projection (top) and Adaptive Density Control (bottom) sit between the Gaussians and the Differentiable Tile Rasterizer, which then pairs with an Image box at far right.
insights.data: The two data ends are drawn as data rather than boxes: SfM points as a scatter of black dots and the 3D Gaussians as a cluster of soft blurred green ellipses; Camera and Image are white boxes, processing steps are grey boxes.
insights.emphasis: The only coloured, non-rectangular element is the green Gaussian cluster with a bold label, placed at the hub where every loop arrow starts and ends.
insights.flow: Black curved arrows carry the forward operation flow clockwise around the loop while light-blue arrows run beside them in the opposite direction for gradients, keyed in a two-entry legend at the bottom right.
insights.avoid: The Camera box enters only Projection with a long straight arrow and floats unaligned above the loop; the rasterizer-to-Image arrows are a cramped pair.

core.what: an optimisation loop drawn as a ring around the 3D Gaussians: Gaussians -> Projection (top) -> Differentiable Tile Rasterizer (right) -> Adaptive Density Control (bottom) -> back into the Gaussians, with curved arrows closing the cycle

relations.form: a straight left-to-right lead-in on the middle row: SfM point scatter -> Initialization box -> 3D Gaussians cluster
curved paired arrows run Gaussians -> Projection -> Rasterizer and Rasterizer -> Adaptive Density Control -> Gaussians, forming one loop to the right of the Gaussians
a Camera box above-left of Projection sends a single straight arrow into it, the view entering the loop from the side
the rendered Image box at far right is linked to the Rasterizer by a black forward arrow and a blue gradient arrow back, the rendered-vs-image comparison implied, not drawn as a loss

channels.colour: line colour = direction of flow (black operation flow, light-blue gradient flow, keyed in a boxed legend); green fill appears only on the 3D Gaussians, marking the representation
channels.shape: grey-filled rectangles = operations, white rectangles = data endpoints (Camera, Image); the SfM points and the Gaussians are drawn as their own primitives (dots, blurred ellipses)
channels.line: solid arrows throughout; colour, not style, separates forward and backward passes
channels.frame: no grouping frames; only the legend is boxed

quality.strengths: the representation is drawn as data (blurred green ellipses, black dot scatter) and is the only saturated element, sitting at the hub where the loop starts and ends; forward/gradient arrows are paired side by side so differentiability reads without words; the loop geometry itself shows the optimisation
quality.weaknesses: the training target (ground-truth image vs render, the loss) is not drawn - the Image box only has arrows to the rasterizer, so what is compared stays implicit; the blue arrow from the Rasterizer to Adaptive Density Control mixes a gradient signal into the loop without saying what it carries

figures.lesson: Make the scene representation the hub of the optimisation loop and draw it as its own primitives (soft coloured ellipses), with paired black forward and light-blue gradient arrows so the differentiable path reads without words.

figures.title: 4D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Dynamic Scene Rendering

taxonomy.task: dynamic scene novel-view rendering

arrangement.units: two dotted rounded containers side by side: encoder (six coloured HexPlane grids, feature column, MLP) and decoder (three stacked deformation heads); inputs and outputs sit outside the containers
arrangement.inputs_as: a rendered 3D character and its Gaussian blob thumbnail stacked at the far left, with x,y,z and t as math labels on curved arrows entering the encoder
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Two dotted rounded containers sit side by side, encoder left and three-head decoder right, with input and output Gaussians as renders outside on the left and right edges.
insights.data: The 4D field is drawn as six small 4x4 grids in two rows (xt, yt, zt above xy, yz, xz), each in its own border colour with faded copies behind, feeding a tall orange feature column.
insights.emphasis: The encoder's multicolour plane grid takes the largest area, and each decoder head ends in its math output (Δx,Δy,Δz, Δr, Δs) so the predicted deformations are named directly.
insights.flow: Curved black arrows carry x,y,z and t from the left render into the encoder, a straight arrow runs through feature column and MLP, then fan out to three heads, and a curved arrow loops up and right to the deformed Gaussians and down via 'Splatting' to the final render.
insights.avoid: The container labels sit below the dotted frames in plain small type and the right label touches the crop edge, and the symbol key is a dense grey text box crowding the top right.

core.what: a left-to-right deformation pipeline: input Gaussians and t at the far left, a dotted encoder container (six HexPlane grids -> feature column -> MLP), a dotted decoder container (three heads), and the deformed Gaussians and splatted render at the far right

relations.form: one horizontal axis: x,y,z and t curve in from the left edge into the encoder, the MLP output fans right into the decoder, and the deformed Gaussians drop down to the render via a vertical 'Splatting' arrow
the spatial-temporal encoder is drawn as its own structure: six stacked multi-resolution plane grids labelled xt, yt, zt (top row) and xy, yz, xz (bottom row), each a small 4x4 cell lattice
the six plane grids feed a single vertical feature column (one small curved arrow), which enters the MLP; the position x,y,z and timestamp t converge on one point at the encoder's left edge
the MLP output splits into three curved arrows fanning to three stacked heads (position, rotation, scaling), each with its output delta written beside it

channels.colour: colour = identity: each of the six planes has its own hue (gold, green, blue, black, salmon, grey), each head its own pale fill, and the MLP is saturated orange; colours carry no shared meaning across encoder and decoder, and the feature column's salmon echoes the yz plane without meaning to
channels.shape: lattices = plane feature grids, tall bars = MLP layers, small rounded bars = heads; the Gaussians and render are drawn as rendered images of the character
channels.line: solid black curved arrows for all data flow; dotted lines only for the two module containers
channels.frame: two dotted rounded containers, each = one named module (encoder, decoder), titled underneath; a grey box at top right is a symbol key

quality.strengths: the HexPlane factorisation is drawn as six labelled grids, so the encoder's structure (3 space-time + 3 space planes) reads at a glance and gets the largest area; inputs and outputs are drawn as actual rendered Gaussians of the character rather than boxes; the three decoder heads with their deltas make the split output explicit
quality.weaknesses: colour is decorative - six unrelated plane hues plus orange MLP and pastel heads encode nothing beyond 'different'; the input enters by long curved arrows looping up and down at the left, and the output Gaussians are reached by an arcing arrow over the decoder; the symbol key sits in a grey box that crowds the decoder title area

figures.lesson: Draw a factorised spatio-temporal field as its labelled planes (xt, yt, zt over xy, yz, xz) in pair-specific colours with faded copies behind for resolutions, so the decomposition reads without text.

figures.title: Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware

taxonomy.task: bimanual imitation learning, action chunking with temporal ensembling
taxonomy.note: architecture other: the figure shows no network, only a timestep x action-index grid of overlapping predicted action chunks combined by temporal ensembling

arrangement.units: two stacked panels separated only by underlined italic headings; cells are coloured squares in a timestep x index grid, columns grouped by grey rounded outlines
arrangement.inputs_as: column index numbers 0-7 across the top, timestep labels t= down the left
arrangement.shared: the action-index axis is shared by both panels

insights.structure: Two stacked sub-panels with underlined italic headings: top 'Action Chunking' shows chunks at t=0 and t=4 laid on a shared action-index axis 0-7; bottom 'Action Chunking + Temporal Ensemble' shows rows t=0..3 each shifted one column right, forming a staircase.
insights.data: Each predicted action is a small coloured square (red, orange, yellow, green by position in the chunk), so the same colour sequence repeats diagonally across rows.
insights.emphasis: A bold black rounded box outlines column 3 across all rows (the actions predicted for one timestep), and an inline equation 'x [0.5, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1] =' turns it into one blended glowing yellow square.
insights.flow: Read top to bottom as time steps and left to right as action index; grey rounded outlines group each column's predictions with no arrows at all.
insights.avoid: The weights equation sits awkwardly on the top row far from the highlighted column, and the light grey column outlines are faint enough to be missed.

core.what: repeated chunk predictions unrolled as rows of a timestep x action-index grid, each query step's chunk shifted one column right so the overlaps form a staircase, with one column ringed to show which predictions are averaged

relations.form: rows t=0..t=3 in the lower panel, each a four-square chunk shifted one column right of the row above, giving a diagonal staircase
two stacked panels sharing the 0-7 index axis: plain 'Action Chunking' above (chunks at t=0 and t=4, no overlap) and 'Action Chunking + Temporal Ensemble' below (a chunk every step)
a bold black rounded outline encloses column 3 across all four rows, and the inline 'x [0.5, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1] =' turns it into one glowing yellow result square at the right of the top row
grey rounded outlines group every other column's stacked predictions, showing the operation repeats on each timestep of the grid

channels.colour: square fill = position within the predicted chunk (red 1st, orange 2nd, yellow 3rd, green 4th), consistent in both panels; the glowing yellow square is the blended action
channels.shape: rounded squares = individual predicted actions
channels.line: outline weight = selection: black outline = the column being combined now, light grey = other columns' groups
channels.frame: no containers; the two panels are separated only by underlined italic headings

quality.strengths: the core relation is pure geometry - the staircase of shifted chunks shows overlap without any arrows; colour has one meaning (position in chunk) kept identical across both panels, so the eye sees that column 3 mixes four different chunk positions; the plain-chunking panel above sets up the comparison on the same axis
quality.weaknesses: the weight vector equation sits at the end of the top row, a column's width away from the ringed column it applies to; the light grey column outlines are faint and easy to miss

figures.lesson: Lay predicted actions on a time x query-step grid of coloured squares (colour = position within the chunk) so overlapping chunks form a staircase, and ring one column to show which predictions are averaged for that timestep.

figures.title: Act3D: 3D Feature Field Transformers for Multi-Task Robotic Manipulation

taxonomy.task: language-conditioned multi-task manipulation: classify 3-D ghost points sampled coarse to fine in a lifted CLIP feature cloud

arrangement.units: four headed columns of scene renders in the top row, the third enclosed in a black rounded frame; an unframed bottom bus of a language encoder, coloured feature pills and one transformer bar
arrangement.inputs_as: a rendered simulator image of the robot scene and the quoted instruction in a pink rounded box
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; outputs are Q_pos in a box at the top right and (Q_rot, Q_open, Q_col) as text at the bar's right end
arrangement.shared: one transformer bar receives language, occupied-point, ghost-point (two-way arrow) and proprioception inputs

insights.structure: Scene renders run along the top in four headed columns, while the network is a single bus along the bottom whose transformer bar spans most of the width.
insights.data: Every scene stage is the real data: a simulator image, the CLIP-feature-coloured point cloud with tilted feature tiles beaming into it, and red ghost points in three refinement steps.
insights.emphasis: The coarse-to-fine steps are the only framed content and the widest panel; the transformer is the only gradient-filled element.
insights.flow: Left to right in both rows: a 'Ghost Point Sampling' arrow enters the frame, curved blue arrows step through it, a straight arrow leaves for Q_pos; the bottom bus runs from the instruction to the output tuple.
insights.avoid: Do not leave the network and the iterative panel it drives unconnected; a long diagonal from the top row to the bottom bus is not a substitute.

core.what: ghost points are drawn in the scene's feature cloud three times inside one frame - a dense red cloud, a tight cluster, a single point - so the coarse-to-fine search is seen on the scene itself

relations.form: red ghost points scattered over the scene render, and CLIP feature tiles lifted into the point cloud by blue rays
three copies of the same scene in one black frame, joined by curved blue arrows, the samples contracting each step
four headed columns left to right from environment image to action prediction, linked by a 'Ghost Point Sampling' arrow and a long arrow to Q_pos
language, occupied-point, ghost-point and proprioception pills converge on one long transformer bar from the left and above

channels.colour: pill fills name the token type (pink language, light blue occupied points, green ghost points, yellow proprioception) and the transformer bar's gradient blends them; point-cloud colours are feature values; red = ghost points and predicted position
channels.shape: outlined white boxes = column headings, rounded pills = feature tokens, long bar = transformer, renders = data
channels.line: two meanings on blue: straight blue rays lift feature tiles into 3-D, curved blue arrows step between coarse-to-fine copies; black arrows carry data, one two-way black arrow ties ghost features to the transformer
channels.frame: one black rounded frame = the iterative sampling unit

quality.strengths: The method's search is drawn on its data: the same scene three times with the red samples contracting, inside one frame. The lifted feature cloud is the real point cloud, not a box. The framed coarse-to-fine panel is the widest unit, so space follows the novelty.
quality.weaknesses: The tie between the transformer bar and each refinement step is not drawn - only a long diagonal line from the feature cloud down to the bar and a two-way arrow to the ghost tag - so how each step uses the transformer is not visible. Blue serves rays, step arrows and the occupied-feature pill. Outputs are split between a boxed Q_pos at the top right and a typeset tuple at the bottom right.

figures.lesson: Draw a coarse-to-fine search as three copies of the same scene inside one frame, the sample points shrinking from a dense cloud to a single point, joined by curved arrows.

figures.title: Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning for NLP

taxonomy.task: parameter-efficient fine-tuning of a pretrained Transformer for text classification

arrangement.units: Left: one Transformer layer as a vertical stack inside a white dashed rounded frame; right: the adapter's internal stack inside a cream-filled dashed rounded frame; whitespace between the two, no connecting arrow.
arrangement.inputs_as: a bare arrow entering each stack from below; no data drawn
arrangement.shared: none; the Adapter box appears twice in the left stack and the right panel shows its inside once

insights.structure: The host Transformer layer stack sits on the left and the adapter's own stack sits beside it on the right at the same height, each in its own dashed rounded frame labelled inside its top-left corner.
insights.data: No data is drawn; activations appear only as rows of small circles, six wide at input and output and two wide at the bottleneck, so the down/up projection reads from the width alone.
insights.emphasis: The inserted Adapter boxes are the only cream-filled boxes in the left stack, and the whole right panel carries the same cream fill, tying the zoom to its source by colour.
insights.flow: Both stacks read bottom-to-top along a single vertical arrow, with residual skips drawn as right-angled lines along the right edge rejoining at '+' circles.
insights.avoid: Nothing marks which boxes are frozen and which are trained (the green on the left Layer Norms and right projections is not keyed), so the reader needs the caption to know what is tuned.

core.what: the host Transformer layer stack on the left with two small cream 'Adapter' boxes inserted, and beside it a cream-tinted dashed panel opening the Adapter's inside, tied to the boxes by the matching tint alone

relations.form: right panel = the Adapter's interior, its cream background matching the two cream Adapter boxes in the left stack; no connecting line between the panels

both stacks read bottom to top on one straight vertical axis: attention -> feed-forward -> Adapter -> + -> Layer Norm -> 2x feed-forward -> Adapter -> + -> Layer Norm, and inside the adapter: neurons -> down-project -> two-neuron bottleneck -> nonlinearity -> up-project -> neurons -> +
the bottleneck is drawn as rows of neuron circles narrowing from six to two and widening back to six, so the dimension change reads without text
skip connections run as right-angled lines up the right side of each stack into a circled '+' (two in the host layer, one around the whole adapter)

channels.colour: cream = the adapter module (box fill and zoom-panel background); green fills Layer Norm and the adapter's internal layers, grey the pre-existing attention and feed-forward blocks - green vs grey appears to separate trained from frozen parts but is not keyed in the drawing
channels.shape: rounded rectangles = layers, rows of circles = activation vectors of a given width, circled '+' = residual add
channels.line: solid black arrows for the forward path and skip connections alike
channels.frame: dashed rounded frame = one layer (Transformer Layer, Adapter Layer), each titled at its top-left corner

quality.strengths: zoom done by matching tint, so the inserted module and its interior read as the same thing without a callout line; the narrowing neuron rows draw the bottleneck as geometry; the two insertion points in the host layer are small and the new module's interior gets a whole panel of its own
quality.weaknesses: green and grey carry the trainable/frozen distinction with no key in the figure; the Adapter boxes in the host stack are the smallest, palest boxes, so the novelty is not the most salient element on the left; skip connections wrap around the outside of each stack as long right-angled lines

figures.lesson: Show a plug-in module twice: as a small tinted box inside the host layer, and as a zoom panel beside it filled with the same tint, with neuron rows of changing width to show a bottleneck.

figures.title: Adaptive-RAG: Learning to Adapt Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models through Question Complexity

taxonomy.task: open-domain question answering that routes each query to no-retrieval, single-step or multi-step retrieval by a complexity classifier

arrangement.units: three unframed panels titled (A), (B), (C) side by side, the paper's panel (C) last and widest; iterative outputs boxed in thin black rectangles
arrangement.inputs_as: quoted example questions in colour-tinted rounded boxes headed by their complexity ('Simple Query:', 'Complex Query:', 'Straightforward Query:')
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; failures are marked by highlighted verdict words ('Inaccurate', 'Inefficient') with a cartoon icon under the baseline panels
arrangement.shared: the same simple and complex example questions recur in all three panels; the database icon is redrawn at each retrieval

insights.structure: Two baseline panels and the paper's panel stand side by side, ours last; in ours a classifier sits in the middle between the queries on the left and the three strategies on the right.
insights.data: The inputs are real example questions, tinted by complexity; outputs are named grey boxes (Documents, Answer, (Intermediate) Answers).
insights.emphasis: The adaptive panel is the widest and the only one with coloured routing lines; 'Classifier' is highlighted in yellow.
insights.flow: Short straight arrows run from query to retrieval to outputs; in panel C orange, green and blue curves converge on the classifier and fan out to the strategy rows in the same colours.
insights.avoid: Yellow highlight marks both the baselines' failures and the paper's classifier, and the classifier itself is a small hand icon; give the new component a shape and size of its own.

core.what: single-step, multi-step and adaptive strategies drawn as three panels side by side, ours last, the same example queries reused in each

relations.form: three panels in a row, (A) single-step and (B) multi-step each with the simple and complex query, (C) the paper's adaptive panel last and widest
in panel C three tinted query boxes send orange, green and blue curves that converge on one classifier icon at the panel's centre
from the classifier three coloured lines fan out right to three rows: Answer only (orange), one retrieval then Documents/Answer (green), a k-times loop box (blue)
the multi-step strategy is a thin black box around Documents and (Intermediate) Answers with a curved arrow between them and a circular-arrow icon labelled 'k times' on its corner
a database-with-magnifier icon labelled 'Retrieval' on the arrow from each query to its documents

channels.colour: colour = query complexity (orange straightforward, green simple, blue complex) on the query boxes and on the routing lines that carry them; yellow highlight carries two meanings - failure verdicts ('Inaccurate', 'Inefficient') and the new 'Classifier'
channels.shape: tinted outlined boxes = input queries, plain grey rounded boxes = generated outputs, icons = retriever, classifier and verdicts
channels.line: black arrows = data flow in every panel; coloured curves in C = routing by complexity; a curved arrow inside a box = a repeated step
channels.frame: a thin black rectangle = one iterated unit (the k-times retrieval-answer loop)

quality.strengths: The comparison is geometry: baselines and ours side by side with the same quoted queries, ours last and widest. The router is drawn as convergence and fan-out with each query's colour kept on its route, so which query takes which path reads without labels. Lines are short; the k-times loop is a compact boxed cycle rather than an unrolled chain.
quality.weaknesses: Yellow highlight means both failure and novelty. The classifier, the paper's contribution, is a small icon smaller than the query boxes. Baseline verdicts lean on cartoon icons (a frustrated person, a warning gear). Panels are separated only by whitespace and the outputs in C are not aligned with those in A and B, so the rows do not line up across panels.

figures.lesson: Show a router by keeping each input's colour on the line it travels: three tinted queries converge on one classifier, and three lines of the same colours fan out to the three strategies.

figures.title: AgentVerse: Facilitating Multi-Agent Collaboration and Exploring Emergent Behaviors

taxonomy.task: dynamic expert-agent group collaboration with recruitment, discussion, execution and evaluation

arrangement.units: four tinted rounded stage panels in a clockwise 2x2 cycle inside one dashed 'x N rounds' frame, plus a lower strip of three dotted round boxes reached by dotted zoom lines
arrangement.inputs_as: a 'Goal: Build' box with a house emoji outside the loop on the left edge
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn (training-free); a 'Reward Feedback' arrow returns from Evaluation to Expert Recruitment
arrangement.shared: the same three pixel-face agents recur in recruitment, decision-making, action execution and the round examples

insights.structure: Four tinted stage panels form a clockwise 2x2 cycle inside a dashed 'x N rounds' frame, with Goal and Outcome boxes outside on the left edge and a dotted zoom fan-out to a three-round example strip underneath.
insights.data: Everything is pictorial: agents are pixel faces, expert profiles are face-plus-text-line cards, the environment state is a house emoji (outline, broken, sparkling) and actions are tool emoji, with no tensors or text prompts.
insights.emphasis: Each stage gets its own pastel tint plus a title icon (magnifier, bulb, gear, refresh), and the decision panel's speech bubbles and 'x M turns' cycle glyph make the agents' discussion the most detailed part.
insights.flow: Goal enters at the left into Expert Recruitment, a 'Group' arrow runs right to Decision-Making, a bent arrow drops to Action Execution, 'New State' runs left to Evaluation, and a 'Reward Feedback' arrow curls back up to recruitment while another exits left to Outcome.
insights.avoid: The vertical 'Reward Feedback' label is set sideways in two lines squeezed between the Goal box and the loop frame, and the Outcome arrow and the feedback arrow leave Evaluation from the same point, making the exit hard to tell from the loop.

core.what: four tinted stage panels arranged as a clockwise 2x2 cycle (Expert Recruitment -> Collaborative Decision-Making -> Action Execution -> Evaluation) inside a dashed 'x N rounds' frame, a Reward Feedback arrow closing the loop

relations.form: the 2x2 stage panels are joined by arrows running clockwise (right across the top, down the right edge, left along the bottom) and a vertical 'Reward Feedback' arrow up the left side back into Expert Recruitment, all inside the 'x N rounds' dashed frame
Goal box at the far left enters the loop at Expert Recruitment, and the loop exits from Evaluation to the Outcome box below Goal on the same left edge
dotted lines fan out from the bottom corners of the loop frame to a grey strip below holding a concrete example run
the example strip shows Round 1 -> Round 2 -> Round 3 as three dotted panels left to right, each listing recruited roles with face icons and the resulting house state
inside Collaborative Decision-Making, three agent faces with speech bubbles are linked by double-headed arrows around a circular 'x M turns' glyph, a nested inner loop
the Evaluation panel places the Goal house and the New State house side by side with a '?==' between them

channels.colour: panel tint = stage identity (pink recruitment, yellow-green decision, tan execution, sage evaluation), each with a matching emoji icon; the example strip is uniformly light grey
channels.shape: pixel faces = agents, house emoji = environment state (outline, broken, finished), tool emoji = actions, rounded cards = expert profiles
channels.line: solid black arrows for the stage flow; dashed frame = repetition scope ('x N rounds'); dotted lines = the zoom fan-out and the example round panels
channels.frame: dashed outer frame = the repeated loop; tinted rounded panels = one stage each; dotted panels = one example round - three frame styles, three meanings

quality.strengths: the loop is geometry - a clockwise 2x2 cycle inside a repetition frame - so the iteration reads without labels; agents and states are drawn as data (faces, house in three conditions) and reused unchanged in the example strip below, which teaches the stages once and then shows them run
quality.weaknesses: the four stage tints only say 'different stage' and add no further meaning; the evaluation's '?==' comparison and the inner 'x M turns' loop are both small glyphs inside crowded panels; the Goal and Outcome boxes on the left edge sit close to the Reward Feedback arrow, so the loop's entry, exit and feedback paths crowd one side

figures.lesson: Lay the four stages of an agent loop as a clockwise 2x2 cycle inside a dashed 'x N rounds' frame, then zoom out below to a strip of concrete rounds that reuses the same character icons.

figures.title: Align before Fuse: Vision and Language Representation Learning with Momentum Distillation

taxonomy.task: vision-language representation pretraining

arrangement.units: one dashed frame for the model; the momentum model a separate box outside it on the right
arrangement.inputs_as: the words 'image input' and 'text input' under each tower
arrangement.losses_at: the contrastive loss between the two towers; ITM and MLM as boxes on top of the fusion encoder
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Inside one dashed cream container, an image encoder (12x) at lower left and a text encoder (x6) at lower right feed a central Image-Text Contrastive Loss box and a multimodal encoder (x6: self-attention, cross-attention, feed-forward) at upper right topped by ITM and MLM heads; a separate dashed yellow Momentum Model box sits outside on the right.
insights.data: Encoder outputs are rows of small 3-D cubes (green tokens with a yellow [CLS] cube at the end), and the contrastive box shows CLS cubes plus stacked negative cube rows with an ellipsis.
insights.emphasis: Layer sublayers are colour-coded (blue feed-forward, orange attention) and the momentum mechanism is pulled out as a big separate box linked by two fat coloured arrows (blue momentum update, orange momentum distillation) keyed in the right legend.
insights.flow: Bottom-to-top: inputs enter at the bottom, encoders rise to token rows, rows go sideways into the contrastive box and up to the fusion encoder; a dashed arrow carries 'hard negatives' from the contrastive box to ITM.
insights.avoid: The legend and momentum box crowd the right edge and the momentum model is only a labelled box, so which modules it copies is not drawn.

core.what: image encoder (lower left) and text encoder (lower right) face each other across a central Image-Text Contrastive Loss box that holds their [CLS] cubes and negative queues, placed below and before the multimodal encoder ('align before fuse')

relations.form: the image [CLS] cube and the text [CLS] cube are drawn inside the contrastive-loss box, arrows from each tower's embedding row running straight into it from left and right, with stacked cube rows labelled 'negatives' below

each tower reads bottom to top from its 'image input' / 'text input' label through its Self Attention / Feed forward block to an embedding row of cubes; the text side continues up into the multimodal encoder and its ITM and MLM heads
the image embedding row sends a right-angled line up and right into the multimodal encoder's Cross Attention layer, which sits on top of the text encoder's output
the multimodal encoder's output feeds two head boxes side by side on top, ITM and MLM
a dashed 'hard negatives' arrow rises from the contrastive-loss box to the ITM head, the negatives mined by one objective feeding the other
a separate dashed yellow Momentum Model box outside the main frame on the right, exchanging a blue 'momentum update' arrow and an orange 'momentum distillation' arrow with it

channels.colour: block fill = layer type (orange attention, blue feed-forward); cube colour = token kind (yellow [CLS], green other tokens); arrow fill = momentum direction (blue update, orange distillation) - so blue and orange each carry two meanings, and yellow also fills the Momentum Model box
channels.shape: cubes = embeddings, rounded rectangles = layers grouped in grey stacks with a repeat count (12x, x6), small boxes = objective heads
channels.line: solid arrows = data flow; dashed arrow = hard-negative mining; block arrows = momentum relations (keyed)
channels.frame: dashed cream frame = the trained model; dashed yellow box = the momentum copy outside it

quality.strengths: the paper's idea is placed as geometry - the contrastive loss sits between the two towers and below the fusion encoder, so 'align before fuse' reads from position; the compared representations are drawn as [CLS] cubes inside the loss box, with the negative queue as stacked cube rows
quality.weaknesses: blue and orange are reused for both layer type and momentum arrows, and yellow for both [CLS] cubes and the Momentum Model; the image-to-cross-attention connection is a long right-angled line over the contrastive box; the Momentum Model is a blank box whose relation to each encoder is only two keyed block arrows

figures.lesson: Put the objective that is the paper's idea where the two towers meet, before the module that fuses them, so the order of the title reads in the drawing.

figures.title: Scaling Up Visual and Vision-Language Representation Learning With Noisy Text Supervision

taxonomy.task: image-text pretraining for zero-shot classification and retrieval

arrangement.units: top band = pre-training panel (left) and zero-shot visual tasks (right) split by a vertical rule; bottom band = three retrieval examples split by dotted rules; bands split by a horizontal rule; no frames
arrangement.inputs_as: a cloud labelled 'Noisy Image-Text Data' under the encoders; downstream inputs as real photos and quoted text queries
arrangement.losses_at: one 'Contrastive Learning' box above the two encoders, where their arrows meet
arrangement.shared: the two encoders are drawn once, in the pre-training panel; arrows from them point into each downstream panel

insights.structure: A small pre-training diagram sits in the top-left corner and the rest of the canvas is a grid of downstream-task panels, split by thin solid and dotted rules rather than frames.

insights.flow: Inside the method panel the flow runs bottom-to-top (cloud, encoders, contrastive box); outside it, curved arrows carry the eye right and down to the application panels.
insights.avoid: The contrastive objective is only a plain text box with no hint of the image-text similarity it computes, and the borrowed ImageNet/VTAB figures add visual noise unrelated to the method.

core.what: one small pre-trained dual encoder (top left) whose curved arrows fan out to every downstream panel - zero-shot ImageNet and VTAB at top right and three retrieval examples in the bottom band - so the figure reads as one model, many uses

relations.form: curved and dashed arrows leave the Text and Image Encoder trapezoids and run to the '(Zero-shot) Visual Tasks' title and down to the 'Fine-grained Image-Text Retrieval' band
a blue Text Encoder and a pink Image Encoder trapezoid side by side above a 'Noisy Image-Text Data' cloud, both arrows rising into one 'Contrastive Learning' box above them

channels.shape: trapezoids = encoders, cloud = noisy web data, box = objective; downstream data drawn as real photos and quoted text strings

channels.frame: no frames; solid and dotted rules partition the panels

quality.strengths: the method is drawn tiny and the uses large, matching the paper's claim that a simple dual encoder transfers widely; retrieval queries and results are drawn as real data (quoted strings, photos), and the three retrieval directions are aligned in one band for comparison
quality.weaknesses: the reused ImageNet grid and VTAB diagram import other papers' visual vocabularies and colours into the figure; the long curved arrows from the encoders sweep across panel boundaries and end at titles rather than at what uses each encoder; the contrastive objective is a bare text box with no embeddings drawn between encoders and loss

figures.lesson: A dual-encoder method can be drawn as a tiny two-trapezoid diagram whose curved arrows reach into every application panel, so the whole figure reads as 'one model, many uses'.

figures.title: AnimateDiff: Animate Your Personalized Text-to-Image Diffusion Models without Specific Tuning

arrangement.inputs_as: stack of noisy video frames z_t
arrangement.shared: the personalised T2I U-Net is shared and frozen

relations.form: the U-Net is a peach hourglass silhouette with orange-outlined image-layer bars whose height falls to the waist and rises again, and each motion module sits beside its image layer inside it
noisy frame stack z_t at the left of the bow-tie and cleaner stack z_{t-1} at the right, the denoising read left to right through the U-Net
a dashed grey ellipse labelled 'Iterative Denoise' loops under the U-Net from right back to left

channels.colour: blue body with green cap = motion module (ours); orange outline on peach = image layers of the frozen personalized T2I (keyed at the bottom); grey = the iteration loop and insert label

channels.line: dashed blue arrows = module insertion; dashed grey ellipse = sampling iterations; one solid black arrow = the training pipeline feeding the modules
channels.frame: the peach bow-tie stands in for the U-Net container; no other frames

quality.strengths: the plug-in relation is geometry - the module row drops vertically onto exactly the slots it fills, bar heights matching layer depth; the new modules are the only blue-green elements, while the frozen T2I is a muted peach shape; inputs and outputs are drawn as noisy and clean squirrel frame stacks
quality.weaknesses: the 'Iterative Denoise' loop and z_t / z_{t-1} labels are small and grey, so the sampling direction is easy to miss; the 'Training Pipeline' arrow points at the modules but nothing shows what training uses; the dashed insertion arrows cross a grey label box that partly hides them

figures.lesson: Show plug-in temporal modules as a separate row of columns above the image network, dropped in by dashed arrows beside each matching image layer of a tinted bow-tie U-Net, with noisy and cleaner frame stacks at the two ends and a dashed loop for the sampling iterations.

figures.title: Anomaly Transformer: Time Series Anomaly Detection with Association Discrepancy

taxonomy.task: time-series anomaly detection via association discrepancy

arrangement.units: left: a rounded card with two horizontal tinted bands plus a pink objective column; right: a dashed box with a vertical block stack
arrangement.inputs_as: letter X with fan-out arrows
arrangement.losses_at: right side of the left panel (discrepancy column)
arrangement.shared: one Linear projection feeds both association branches

insights.structure: Left: a large card (stacked behind two ghost copies for multi-head) with an orange Prior-Association band over a blue Series-Association band and a pink Minimize/Maximize Discrepancy column at right; right, behind a vertical dashed separator, an L x block stack (Anomaly Attention, Add, Layer Norm, Feed Forward, Layer Norm) with 'Reconstruction' on top.
insights.data: The prior branch shows its Gaussian kernel as an explicit column vector of G(|j-i|; sigma) entries; Q, K, V and operations (MatMul, Scale, SoftMax, Rescale) are plain tilted text labels, not boxes.
insights.emphasis: The minimax objective gets its own pink column with red 'Minimize' and blue 'Maximize' text, and coloured Grad arrows with dashed Stop-Grad crossings show which branch each step updates.
insights.flow: Input X enters bottom-left, splits up into the two tinted bands left-to-right, and the V path runs along the bottom to an output Linear; the block-stack panel reads bottom-to-top.
insights.avoid: The tilted operation labels and crossing Stop-Grad curves in the middle are hard to parse, and the stacked ghost cards add clutter without labels.

core.what: two stacked full-width tinted bands - Prior-Association (orange, top) and Series-Association (blue, below) - both ending at a shared pink column at right where crossing arrows set them against each other as Minimize / Maximize Discrepancy

relations.form: the two branch outputs sit one above the other at the right end of their bands; grey arrows cross in an X into the pink column, red 'Grad' arrows return to Prior-Association for Minimize and blue 'Grad' arrows to Series-Association for Maximize, with dashed bar-headed 'Stop Grad' arrows between

the two bands run in parallel left to right from one shared Linear projection of X: the top through sigma -> a Gaussian-kernel column vector G(|j-i|; sigma) -> Rescale, the bottom through Q, K -> MatMul -> Scale -> SoftMax
V runs along the bottom of the card under both bands to a MatMul with Series-Association and out through a Linear at the right edge

the large left card (with two ghost copies behind it for multiple heads) is the inside of the pink 'Anomaly Attention' block at the bottom of the L x layer stack at right, behind a vertical dashed separator
the right stack reads bottom to top: Anomaly Attention -> + -> Layer Norm -> Feed Forward -> + -> Layer Norm -> Reconstruction, residuals as lines wrapping round the right side

channels.colour: band tint = branch (orange prior, blue series); text and gradient-arrow colour match the branch they update (red Minimize to prior, blue Maximize to series); pink = the discrepancy objective column and also the Anomaly Attention block in the stack - pink carries two meanings; green and lavender fill the standard Layer Norm and Feed Forward blocks
channels.shape: operations are bare tilted text labels (MatMul, Scale, SoftMax, Rescale), not boxes; the prior kernel is drawn as a bracketed column vector; only the right-hand stack uses boxes
channels.line: solid black = data flow; coloured solid = gradient; dashed with bar heads = stopped gradient
channels.frame: the stacked card with ghost copies = multi-head attention; the dashed rounded frame with 'L x' = one repeated layer

quality.strengths: the two compared associations are drawn as parallel bands that end side by side against one objective column, so the minimax pairing is geometry; gradient arrows are coloured like the branch they update and stopped gradients are drawn as dashed bar-headed arrows, making the alternating optimisation readable; the new attention gets the large panel and the standard layer stack is compact
quality.weaknesses: pink means both 'the discrepancy objective' and 'the Anomaly Attention block'; the zoom between the stack's pink block and the big card is implied by tint and a dashed separator, with no callout; the crossing grey arrows and the Grad/Stop Grad labels pile up in a small region at the band ends; the Gaussian kernel is typeset as formula entries rather than drawn

figures.lesson: Paint two competing branches as full-width tinted bands and give their objective a separate column, with gradient arrows coloured like the band they update and grey bar-headed arrows for stopped gradients.

figures.title: Atlas: Few-shot Learning with Retrieval Augmented Language Models

taxonomy.task: few-shot knowledge-intensive tasks (fact checking, question answering) with a retrieval-augmented LM

arrangement.units: Two horizontal lanes separated by a dashed rule: the top lane holds the pretraining (masked LM) input and output, the bottom lane the few-shot tasks; the central Atlas hub and the retrieved-passage stack straddle both lanes with no frame.
arrangement.inputs_as: quoted example sentences in italic inside pastel boxes, each headed by a bold underlined task name
arrangement.shared: the single Atlas hub and one retrieved-passage stack are drawn once and serve every task's arrows

insights.structure: A single grey Atlas hub sits in the centre with task inputs stacked on the left, matching outputs stacked on the right, and a stack of retrieved-passage cards directly below it.
insights.data: Inputs, outputs and the retrieved passage are all real sentences about one shared example (the Bermuda Triangle), italic in pastel boxes, so the retrieved text visibly contains the answers.
insights.emphasis: The model name is the largest text in the figure, in bold monospace on the biggest box, and the same example threads through every task.
insights.flow: Curved arrows converge from the left boxes into the hub, curve down to the passage stack and back up, then fan out to the right boxes.
insights.avoid: The model is a black box, so the figure shows what Atlas does but not how retriever and language model connect; do not use this pattern when the architecture is the contribution.

core.what: one central grey 'Atlas' hub serving every task: colour-matched input boxes on the left and output boxes on the right connect to it by curved arrows, the same hub for pretraining and few-shot tasks

relations.form: three task-input boxes on the left (masked LM, fact checking, question answering) converge by curved arrows on the hub's left edge, and three matching outputs fan out from its right edge

a stack of three grey passage cards below the hub, the top one quoting a real retrieved passage, fetched by a curved arrow from the hub's lower left and returned by a curved arrow up into its lower right

each input box and its output box share a pastel fill and sit on the same row across the hub (green MLM -> 'western part', yellow fact -> 'False', peach QA -> 'Western part of the North Atlantic Ocean')
a dashed horizontal rule splits the top Pretraining row from the Few-shot rows below, both rows using the same hub

channels.colour: pastel fill = task, matched between each input and its output (green, yellow, peach); grey = Atlas and its retrieved passages
channels.shape: rounded boxes with a bold underlined task name over an italic quoted sentence = task examples; stacked cards = retrieved documents; one large box = the model
channels.line: solid curved arrows for all flow; dashed rule = training phase boundary
channels.frame: no containers; the dashed rule partitions phases

quality.strengths: data drawn as data - every input, output and retrieved passage is a real quoted sentence about the same Bermuda Triangle fact, so the reader follows one example through every task; colour has one meaning (task), matched across the hub; retrieval drawn as a document stack beside the main flow with an out-and-back arrow
quality.weaknesses: the model is a blank labelled box, so nothing shows how the retrieved passages are combined with the query; curved arrows bundle into the hub's corners and cross the dashed phase rule; the hub and passages share grey, so retrieved data and model look the same kind of thing

figures.lesson: Show one model serving several tasks by putting it as a central hub with colour-matched input and output boxes on either side, and draw retrieval as a stack of text cards below the hub with an out-and-back curved arrow.

figures.title: Attention U-Net: Learning Where to Look for the Pancreas

taxonomy.task: pancreas segmentation with attention gates in skip connections

arrangement.units: one rounded frame with unenclosed blue (learned) and white glyph (fixed) boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: italic symbols g and x^l on incoming lines
arrangement.shared: x^l is used both as gate input and as the gated signal via a bottom skip

insights.structure: A single horizontal pipeline inside one rounded light-grey frame: two parallel 1x1x1 convolutions W_g (top) and W_x (bottom) merge at a plus node, then ReLU, psi 1x1x1, Sigmoid, Resampler, and a multiply node producing x_hat^l.
insights.data: Each tensor edge carries its shape as italic text below it (F_g x H_g x W_g x D_g etc.), and the nonlinearities and resampler are drawn as glyph boxes (ramp, S-curve, grid).
insights.emphasis: Learnable convolutions are the only blue-filled boxes, while parameter-free steps are white glyph boxes, so trainable parts stand out.
insights.flow: Left-to-right with hollow-triangle arrowheads; a long skip line runs along the bottom from x^l to the final multiply node, closing the gating.
insights.avoid: Tensor shape labels in small italic math crowd under every edge and some lack the multiply signs, making them hard to read.

core.what: a gating signal g (top) and skip feature x^l (bottom) pass through parallel blue 1x1x1 convolutions and converge on one plus node, then a single left-to-right chain turns the sum into a coefficient alpha that multiplies x^l at the far right

relations.form: two parallel rows W_g (top) and W_x (bottom) at the left edge, each line turning a right angle into a shared circled plus between them
one straight horizontal chain after the plus: ReLU glyph box -> psi 1x1x1 -> Sigmoid glyph box -> Resampler grid box -> alpha -> circled multiply -> x-hat^l
a long skip line runs along the bottom of the frame from x^l to the multiply node, closing the gate
each edge carries the tensor shape as italic text beneath it (F_g x H_g x W_g x D_g, F_int x ..., H_x x W_x x D_x)

channels.colour: blue fill = learned 1x1x1 convolutions only; every parameter-free step is white - one meaning
channels.shape: rounded blue boxes = learnable layers; white squares holding a sketch of their function (ramp = ReLU, S-curve = sigmoid, grid = resampler) = fixed operations; circles = elementwise add / multiply
channels.line: solid lines with hollow-triangle arrowheads for all tensors; no line-style distinctions
channels.frame: one rounded light-grey frame = the single attention-gate module

quality.strengths: colour carries exactly one meaning (learned vs fixed) and is obvious without a key; nonlinearities drawn as glyphs of their curves; the merge is a symmetric two-row convergence and the rest a straight continuing line, so path geometry is short and aligned
quality.weaknesses: tensor shapes are typeset as small italic formulas under almost every edge, crowding the chain; the bottom skip line spans the whole frame width to reach the multiply node; the coefficient alpha is only a letter on an arrow, never drawn as the attention map it is

figures.lesson: Draw each fixed nonlinearity as a white square holding a sketch of its curve (a ramp for ReLU, an S for sigmoid) and reserve the one tint for the learned 1x1x1 convolutions, so learned and fixed steps read apart without a legend.

figures.title: Audio Flamingo: A Novel Audio Language Model with Few-Shot Learning and Dialogue Abilities

taxonomy.task: retrieval-built in-context examples for an audio language model

arrangement.units: no enclosed regions: a bottom-up retrieval tree on the left and one black-framed prompt panel on the right
arrangement.inputs_as: a database cylinder glyph and a black waveform glyph for the training/test sample, both labelled underneath
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn (the figure builds training samples)
arrangement.shared: LAION-CLAP drawn twice, once per branch, as identical white boxes

insights.structure: Two LAION-CLAP branches rise from the database and the query sample and meet at a 'min distance' box; its output, a box of k retrieved waveforms, feeds a large prompt panel at the right.
insights.data: Audio is drawn as waveform glyphs (the query black, the retrieved set in blue, green and red) and the produced training sample is shown as its literal template text.
insights.emphasis: The only colour in the figure is the per-sample identity colour shared by each retrieved waveform and its prompt line.
insights.flow: Retrieval reads bottom-up, then one horizontal arrow carries the retrieved set into the prompt panel; the query's own path to the prompt runs as a long L along the bottom and up the panel's underside.
insights.avoid: The query sample reaches the prompt by a long L-shaped wire under the whole retrieval tree instead of sitting next to the panel line it fills; the CLAP embeddings that 'min distance' compares are not drawn.

core.what: a database cylinder and the query each pass through LAION-CLAP into one 'min distance' box, and the retrieved items are drawn as data (coloured waveforms) in a box that feeds the prompt

relations.form: the store is a cylinder at bottom left beside the query branch; the top-k results are a box of three coloured waveforms above the comparison box
the two LAION-CLAP boxes stand side by side and converge from below on one 'min distance' box between them
the retrieved-set box and the query sample both enter the right-hand prompt panel, whose lines list the k retrieved slots in their waveform colours followed by the query slot in black

channels.colour: identity of one retrieved sample (blue, green, red), shared between its waveform and its prompt line; black = the query sample and all operations
channels.shape: cylinder = store, waveform = audio data, rounded white box = operation, square panel = the assembled text sample
channels.line: solid black arrows for data flow only
channels.frame: the rounded box around the waveforms = the retrieved set as one unit; the large panel = one training sample

quality.strengths: Retrieved items are drawn as data in their own colours and the same colours mark their slots in the quoted prompt, so retrieval-to-prompt mapping reads without arrows; the store is a database glyph beside the query branch; the two encoders face one comparison box.
quality.weaknesses: The query's path to the prompt is a long L-shaped wire along the bottom edge; the CLAP embeddings compared by 'min distance' are not drawn (wires run from encoders straight into the comparison); LAION-CLAP is drawn twice with no mark that it is the same frozen model.

figures.lesson: Give each retrieved item its own colour and reuse that colour on the slot it fills in the assembled prompt, so the reader matches retrieval output to prompt position without arrows.

figures.title: AudioLDM: Text-to-Audio Generation with Latent Diffusion Models

taxonomy.task: text-to-audio generation, inpainting and style transfer

arrangement.units: three uncontained captioned panels of rounded coloured module boxes; (a) left full-height, (b) and (c) stacked on the right
arrangement.inputs_as: waveform thumbnails, spectrograms and quoted text prompts
arrangement.losses_at: centre-left of panel (a) (contrastive objective between audio and text encoders)
arrangement.shared: the same VAE, text encoder and latent diffusion modules reused in all three panels

insights.structure: Three captioned panels: a tall left panel (a) for training and sampling, and two stacked right panels (b) audio inpainting and (c) style transfer that reuse the same row of VAE Encoder, Text Encoder, Latent Diffusion and VAE Decoder boxes.
insights.data: Audio appears as blue waveforms and real magma-coloured mel spectrograms, text prompts as quoted bold sentences, embeddings E^x and E^y as vertical cell strips, and latents z_0 as small 3-D cuboids annotated with their R^{C x T/r x F/r} shapes.
insights.emphasis: Modules are colour-coded by role (blue encoders, yellow VAE with a small spectrogram icon, green Latent Diffusion), and the same colours repeat across panels so (b) and (c) read as reuses of (a).
insights.flow: Solid arrows mark training and dashed arrows sampling (legend under panel a); panel (a) runs top-to-bottom from audio to generated audio, panels (b)/(c) run left-to-right with dotted arrows.
insights.avoid: Panel (a) mixes solid, dashed and dash-dot grey arrows that cross around Latent Diffusion, and the latent shape formulas in tiny math add clutter.

core.what: every input converges on the single green Latent Diffusion block at the centre of panel (a): the audio embedding E^x on a solid (training) line, the text embedding E^y on a dashed (sampling) line, noise z_N from above and the latent z0 from the right

relations.form: E^x arrives from the upper left on a solid line and E^y from the lower left on a dashed line, both entering Latent Diffusion's left side; z_N ~ N(0, I) drops in from above
Audio Encoder (upper left) and Text Encoder (lower left) are stacked in one column with a grey dash-dot 'Contrastive objective' between them, each emitting a drawn column-vector embedding

a clockwise loop in (a): waveform -> STFT+MelFB bar across the top -> VAE Encoder (right column) -> z0 cube -> VAE Decoder -> spectrogram -> Vocoder along the bottom -> generated waveform under the input

panels (b) inpainting and (c) style transfer stacked at right as short left-to-right rows reusing (a)'s exact block shapes and colours (spectrogram -> VAE Encoder -> Latent Diffusion -> VAE Decoder -> spectrogram, Text Encoder raised above), (c) adding a grey textured Forward Diffusion box
training and sampling share one wiring in (a), separated only by line style (solid vs dashed, keyed below the panel)

channels.colour: fill = module family: blue the text/audio encoders, yellow the VAE and vocoder, green the latent diffusion model, grey-textured the forward diffusion step; cream cubes = latents and blue cell columns = embeddings; one meaning each and consistent across all three panels
channels.shape: rounded boxes = modules, 3D cubes = latents, cell columns = embeddings, waveform and spectrogram images = audio data; a stair glyph in VAE boxes marks down/up-sampling
channels.line: solid = training, dashed = sampling (keyed in (a)); grey dash-dot = contrastive objective; panels (b) and (c) use dotted lines throughout, a third style that is not keyed
channels.frame: no frames; each panel is set apart by whitespace and a sub-caption

quality.strengths: the shared-embedding idea is placed as geometry - audio and text embeddings enter the same side of Latent Diffusion on solid vs dashed lines, so training on audio and sampling on text read from line style alone; data drawn as data (waveforms, spectrograms, latent cubes, a quoted prompt); the zero-shot panels reuse the vocabulary compactly
quality.weaknesses: panel (a)'s clockwise loop sends the STFT path across the full top and the Vocoder path back along the bottom, long routes around the centre; dotted lines in (b)/(c) introduce an unkeyed line style; tensor shapes are typeset as formulas beside every latent; the contrastive objective is a small grey label with no compared vectors drawn at it

figures.lesson: Training and sampling share one drawing: the same blocks are wired once, with solid arrows for the training path and dashed arrows for the sampling path, and a two-entry line-style legend under the panel explains the difference.

figures.title: Autoformer: Decomposition Transformers with Auto-Correlation for Long-Term Series Forecasting

taxonomy.task: long-term time-series forecasting with series decomposition

arrangement.units: two horizontal rounded containers (encoder above, decoder below) holding flat coloured blocks
arrangement.inputs_as: line-plot thumbnails of the input series and initialisations
arrangement.shared: encoder output feeds decoder cross auto-correlation

insights.structure: Two rounded containers stacked vertically: the Autoformer Encoder (N x) on top and a wider Autoformer Decoder (M x) below, each a row of Auto-Correlation, Series Decomp and Feed Forward blocks with add nodes; a decomposition example panel sits at top right.
insights.data: Inputs are small line-plot thumbnails (encoder input with a dashed 'To Predict' region, seasonal init with orange zero tail, trend-cyclical init with blue mean line), and a three-row plot at top right shows a series split into seasonal and trend parts.
insights.emphasis: Blocks are colour-coded by type (green Auto-Correlation, blue Series Decomp, pink Feed Forward), making the repeated decomposition blocks the dominant visual rhythm.
insights.flow: Left-to-right in each container; the encoder output drops by an elbow line into the decoder's second Auto-Correlation, and the decoder's trend path runs as a separate bottom line accumulating at add nodes before the final Prediction.
insights.avoid: The decomposition example panel floats in the top-right corner unconnected to any block, and the K/V/Q micro-labels on block inputs are too small to read.

core.what: the decoder runs two lanes inside one container: a seasonal row of blocks on top and a trend lane along the bottom that accumulates each Series Decomp block's output through a chain of circled pluses, the two summed at the Prediction edge

relations.form: in the Autoformer Decoder, each of three blue Series Decomp blocks drops a vertical arrow into a plus on one straight horizontal trend line that starts at the Trend-cyclical Init thumbnail and runs to the right edge
each container is one left-to-right row: Auto-Correlation -> + -> Series Decomp -> (Auto-Correlation ->) Feed Forward -> + -> Series Decomp, with residual lines looping over or under each block pair

the Encoder (N x) container sits above the wider Decoder (M x) container; the encoder output leaves its right edge and drops by a right-angled line into the K, V inputs of the decoder's second Auto-Correlation

inputs are drawn as small time-series thumbnails (encoder input with a dashed 'To Predict' region, seasonal init with an orange zero tail, trend init with a blue mean line), and a three-row inset at top right shows a real series split into seasonal and trend-cyclical curves
the seasonal row's last output and the trend lane meet at one circled plus beside a grey 'Prediction' tab at the right edge

channels.colour: block fill = block type (green Auto-Correlation, blue Series Decomp, pink Feed Forward), consistent in both containers; in the curves, orange = seasonal and blue = trend - blue thus marks both the decomposition block and the trend component
channels.shape: rounded rectangles = blocks, circled plus = addition, framed line plots = series data
channels.line: solid black lines throughout; residuals drawn as right-angled loops; the trend lane is a heavier straight line
channels.frame: rounded black-outlined container = one repeated layer (N x encoder, M x decoder)

quality.strengths: the decomposition is shown, not described - a real series split into seasonal and trend curves in the inset - and the trend accumulation is a dedicated straight lane under the decoder, so the dual-stream idea is geometry; the two new block types keep one fill each across encoder and decoder
quality.weaknesses: the encoder-to-decoder connection is a long right-angled line looping from the encoder's right edge back left into the decoder; residual loops over and under each block add many bends; blue doubles as block type and trend component; the decomposition inset is not linked to any Series Decomp block

figures.lesson: Explain the decomposition block with a small stacked inset of the input series, its seasonal part and its trend part drawn as real curves, and draw the trend as a separate lower lane that accumulates each decomposition block's output through circled pluses.

figures.title: AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation

arrangement.units: three tinted full-width horizontal bands, each labelled at left, holding icon boxes, code panels and a speech-bubble column
