relations.form: the three bands are stacked with no arrows between them except one red dashed arrow from the bottom band's 'Conversation-Driven Control Flow' callout up into the code panel

in the top band a ConversableAgent icon at top centre branches by thin arrows down to three agent types side by side (AssistantAgent, UserProxyAgent, GroupChatManager), each with its config snippet in a grey text box above
in the middle band User Proxy A and Assistant B face each other joined by one double-headed arrow, with the code that registers the reply function in a panel to their left

in the bottom band a rounded chat frame holds alternating blue and green speech bubbles, with a blue generate_reply box on the left and a green one on the right, each linked to the bubbles by dashed 'receive' / 'send' arrows

channels.colour: dashed-border colour = agent identity (blue user proxy, green assistant, red group chat manager), carried into the speech-bubble tint and generate_reply text in the bottom band; band tint = layer of the story; dark red text = framework concept callouts - and red also marks the critical code lines (red dashed outline), the control-flow arrow and the GroupChatManager border, so red carries two meanings
channels.shape: robot-head icons in dashed boxes = agents, with tool glyphs (LLM, human, python) inside; monospace text boxes = code and config; speech bubbles = messages; outlined boxes = reply functions
channels.line: solid thin arrows = inheritance (top) and conversation (middle); dashed arrows = message send/receive (bottom); red dashed = control flow from chat to code
channels.frame: full-width tinted band = one layer; dashed coloured box = one agent; rounded grey frame = one conversation

quality.strengths: agent identity colour is kept across all three bands, so the user proxy and assistant can be tracked from definition to code to chat; the conversation is drawn as real data (quoted messages, an actual error and fix) rather than as boxes; the band ordering moves from abstraction to concrete run
quality.weaknesses: red carries both 'framework concept' (callout text) and 'one agent' (GroupChatManager) plus highlight outlines; the bands are joined only by one red dashed arrow, so how the code produces the chat is left to labels; much of the area is monospace code and config text, so the reader reads rather than sees; numbered callouts '1.2' before '1.1' read out of order

figures.lesson: Draw each agent as one recognisable robot-head icon in a dashed frame of its own colour, keep that colour wherever the agent recurs, and show the conversation itself as chat-app speech bubbles tinted by sender.

figures.title: AutoInt: Automatic Feature Interaction Learning via Self-Attentive Neural Networks

taxonomy.task: CTR prediction via self-attentive feature interaction

arrangement.units: unenclosed flat coloured cards and a weight column, no containers
arrangement.inputs_as: stacked blue embedding cards e_M and a single e_m
arrangement.shared: the same e_M stack is projected to both keys and values

insights.structure: One attention head drawn as a scatter: stacked blue feature-embedding cards e_M at top left, a single query embedding e_m at bottom left, projected into gold value cards (top right), grey key cards (middle) and a peach query card, which combine via curly braces into the output e~_m^(h) at right.
insights.data: Embeddings are flat coloured rectangles stacked like cards with dots for elision, and attention weights alpha are a vertical column of dark-gold cells with sample values 0.1, 0.8, ..., 0.02.
insights.emphasis: Each projection role has its own fill colour (gold value, grey key, peach query) and the projection matrices W^(h) are italic labels on the blue arrows.
insights.flow: Left-to-right with blue diagonal arrows for projections, then curly braces gather keys with query into alpha and alpha with values into the output.
insights.avoid: Curly braces stand in for operations (dot product, weighted sum) without naming them, and the diagonal arrow layout scatters the elements loosely.

core.what: one query card (peach, bottom) is braced against a stack of key cards (grey, middle) to give a column of attention weights alpha drawn with example values, which is braced with the value cards (gold, top) into the single output card at the right

relations.form: a curly brace gathers the grey key stack and the peach query card into a dark-gold column of weight cells printed 0.1, 0.8, ..., 0.02
a second, tall curly brace gathers the gold value stack and the weight column into the grey output card e~_m^(h) at the far right

blue projection arrows run left to right from the blue feature-embedding stack e_M to the value stack (straight, top) and key stack (diagonal down), and from the single embedding e_m at bottom left up to the query card, each labelled W_Value / W_Key / W_Query

channels.colour: fill = role of the representation: blue raw embeddings, gold values, grey keys, peach query, dark gold attention weights; the output is a darker grey that echoes the keys without meaning to
channels.shape: flat rectangles stacked like cards with elision dots = sets of field embeddings; small square cells with numbers = attention weights; curly braces = combination operations
channels.line: blue arrows = learned projections, each labelled with its matrix; braces replace lines for the attention and weighted-sum steps
channels.frame: no frames

quality.strengths: the attention weights are drawn as data - a column of cells with example values - between the keys and the values, so the compared representations and the result of comparing them are all visible; each projection role has its own fill
quality.weaknesses: the two curly braces stand in for different operations (dot-product scoring and weighted sum) without naming either; the cards are scattered diagonally rather than aligned, so the query's long diagonal arrow and the key arrow cross the figure; the output's grey nearly matches the key cards

figures.lesson: Show attention over feature fields as a short column of small squares printed with example weights (0.1, 0.8, …, 0.02) between the keys and the values, braced together into the output, so the reader sees the weighting rather than reads about it.

figures.title: Agent Workflow Memory

taxonomy.task: web-navigation agents that induce reusable workflows from successful trajectories and add them to their memory

arrangement.units: one unframed diagram: a blue ellipse for agent + environment, a grey-bordered trajectory box, a pink-bordered workflow card
arrangement.inputs_as: a person icon with a quoted question in a speech bubble ('Who ordered order #0130?') above the Memory cloud
arrangement.losses_at: none (training-free); the success check is a YES/NO gate between the trajectory and the workflow card

insights.structure: Four regions around the page in loop order - agent ellipse top-left, trajectory bottom-left, evaluation gate bottom-right, workflow card top-right - with no outer frame.
insights.data: The query is a quoted speech bubble from a person icon, the trajectory is three commented action lines (click, scroll, send_msg_to_user), and the workflow is drawn as its actual text: a description d and steps p1..pn with [env desc] / [reason] / [action] fields.
insights.emphasis: Pink marks only memory content (the cloud and the workflow card), and the steps carry numbered orange title tags, so the induce-and-store path stands out against the grey trajectory.
insights.flow: Step 1 -> Step 2 is a thin black arrow into 'Query solved correctly?', the gate is a grey cross-shaped block arrow (YES up to Step 3, NO down to 'pass'), and a wide pink arrow carries the workflow left into Memory.
insights.avoid: The loop is not closed: no arrow runs from the agent down to the Step 1 trajectory, and three arrow styles (thin black, wide grey, wide pink) all mean 'next step'.

core.what: a counter-clockwise loop around the figure: Step 1 trajectory (bottom-left) -> Step 2 YES/NO gate (bottom-right) -> Step 3 workflow card (top-right) -> a wide pink arrow back into the agent's Memory cloud (top-left)

relations.form: three numbered steps placed at three corners of the figure, joined by arrows that turn back into the Memory cloud at the fourth corner

Memory drawn as a pink cloud inside the agent ellipse, the stored item drawn as data (a pink workflow card with description and steps) beside it, joined by one wide arrow labelled 'integrate into memory'
the agent-environment interaction as a two-arrow refresh glyph labelled 'action' and 'observation' between 'state s' and the Memory cloud

channels.colour: pink = memory content (Memory cloud, workflow card, integrate arrow); light blue = the agent-and-environment scope and 'Environment' / 'state s' text; orange = step title tags; green YES / red NO on the gate; grey = trajectory border and gate arrow
channels.shape: cloud = memory store, trapezoid = LM backbone, rectangles of text = data (trajectory, workflow), ellipse = agent in environment, refresh glyph = interaction loop, cross-shaped block arrow = decision
channels.line: three styles for the same 'next step' meaning: thin black arrow (trajectory to gate), wide grey block arrow (gate branches), wide pink block arrow (into memory); a blue bracket line ties the 'Environment' label to state s
channels.frame: the blue ellipse = agent plus environment; boxes = one data object each

quality.strengths: nouns are drawn as data: a quoted query, a commented action trajectory and the induced workflow's actual description and steps; one fill (pink) links the workflow card to the Memory cloud it is written into; numbered orange tags fix the loop order so it reads in a small column-width figure
quality.weaknesses: the loop has no edge from the agent to the Step 1 trajectory, so where actions come from is inferred; arrow style changes three times for one meaning; agent and environment share one ellipse, separated only by two labels; the gate's 'NO -> pass' branch trails off below the figure; the action/observation glyph is small and floats between 'state s' and Memory

figures.lesson: Give a stored item and its store the same fill (pink workflow card, pink memory cloud) and join them with one wide arrow, so writing to memory is legible before any label is read.

figures.title: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration

taxonomy.task: weight-only LLM quantization
taxonomy.note: architecture other: no network is drawn; the figure compares transformations of one weight matrix (round-to-nearest, mixed precision, per-channel scaling)

arrangement.units: three uncontained captioned panels of numeric/colour-shaded matrix grids
arrangement.inputs_as: FP16 weight matrix grid; activation matrix X below in (b),(c)
arrangement.shared: the same activation pattern X appears in (b) and (c)

insights.structure: Three side-by-side captioned panels (a) RTN quantization, (b) keep 1% salient weights in FP16, (c) scale before quantization, each built around a small weight matrix and, in (b) and (c), an activation matrix X multiplied into it.
insights.data: Weights are grids with printed numbers (cream FP16 values, blue INT3 integers), activations are pink grids whose shade marks magnitude with one salient red column, and the per-channel scale is a single pink row labelled alpha.
insights.emphasis: Captions carry perplexity in bold with colour (red 43.2 vs green 13.0), and in (b) one cream FP16 row inside the blue INT3 grid plus a red 'bad hardware efficiency' note marks the trade-off that (c) removes.
insights.flow: Read left to right as a progression of solutions; inside panels a dotted curved arrow goes from the salient activation column to the weight row and an 'average mag.' arrow leads up to the alpha row.
insights.avoid: The tiny numbers in every cell are unreadable at print size and add no information beyond the colour coding.

core.what: three side-by-side captioned panels built on the same weight-matrix grid - (a) round-to-nearest, (b) keep 1% salient weights in FP16, (c) scale before quantization - with the proposal last and each caption ending in its perplexity

relations.form: panels (a), (b), (c) left to right, each ending in a 4-column weight grid labelled Q(W) with its precision subscript, and a bold coloured PPL value in each caption (red 43.2, green 13.0, green 13.0)

the operation is drawn on small matrices with printed values: FP16 cream grid -> INT3 blue grid in (a); in (b) one cream FP16 row left inside the blue INT3 grid; in (c) the weight rows shaded by their scale

in (b) and (c) a pink activation matrix X lies beside the weight grid with a '*' between them, its one dark-red salient column matching the weight row it selects (dotted 'determine the salient weights by activation' arrow in (b))
in (c) X -> 'average mag.' arrow up to a one-row pink scale vector alpha -> curved 'scale before quantize' arrow into the weight grid, whose row 2 turns saturated blue

channels.colour: cream = FP16 values, blue = INT3 values (blue saturation in (c) = scaling applied per row), pink-to-red shade = activation magnitude; red/green in captions and subscripts = bad/good result - red thus means both 'large activation' and 'bad', and green both 'INT3' subscript and 'good PPL'
channels.shape: grids of numbered cells = matrices; a single-row grid = the per-channel scale vector
channels.line: solid arrows = operations (Q, average, scale); dotted curved arrow = selection by activation; a red curly arrow points the 'bad hardware efficiency' note at the MixPrec label
channels.frame: no frames; panels are separated by whitespace and their sub-captions

quality.strengths: the comparison is geometry - three panels on the same matrix vocabulary, ours last, each scored in its caption; the method is drawn on its structure (a salient activation column selects the matching weight row, kept FP16 in (b), scaled in (c)), so the reader sees why scaling replaces mixed precision; data drawn as real numbers in the grids
quality.weaknesses: red and green each carry two meanings (activation magnitude / bad result; INT3 subscript / good result); the (c) weight grid drops its printed values, so the effect of scaling on the quantised numbers is shown only by shade; the X-to-W correspondence relies on counting columns against rows, with no tie line

figures.lesson: Write the bit width as a coloured subscript on the matrix name (Q(W) INT3, MixPrec) and leave the high-precision channel as a differently tinted row inside the low-bit matrix, so precision is read from colour rather than from text.

figures.title: Barlow Twins: Self-Supervised Learning via Redundancy Reduction

taxonomy.task: self-supervised image representation learning
taxonomy.note: training 'other': redundancy-reduction objective that drives the cross-correlation matrix of two views' embeddings to the identity

arrangement.units: Two unframed horizontal lanes (branch A above, branch B below) separated by whitespace, sharing one input box at the left and one matrix comparison at the right.
arrangement.inputs_as: a white box labelled X (no photo); the two distortions are boxes Y^A, Y^B reached by arrows labelled T ~ calligraphic T
arrangement.losses_at: right end, after both lanes converge: matrix C, then a double arrow labelled L_BT, then target matrix I
arrangement.shared: the shared network is drawn once per lane as identical blue trapezoids; a single brace f_theta under the top lane names it

insights.structure: One input box forks into two stacked lanes, each data box -> blue encoder trapezoid -> smaller projector trapezoid -> embedding box, and both lanes meet at a cross-correlation grid followed by an identity grid at the far right.
insights.data: Images and embeddings are white outlined boxes with math symbols only (X, Y^A, Z^A), while the cross-correlation is drawn as an actual grey-level grid and the target as a black-diagonal grid, with 'feature dimension' marked by a double arrow under C.
insights.emphasis: The two matrices are the only picture-like elements and sit at the end of the reading path, joined by an L_BT double arrow, so the loss is the visual punchline.
insights.flow: Left-to-right: diagonal arrows fan out from X to the two lanes, run straight through the trapezoids, then converge diagonally into C; a dashed curved arrow rises from between encoder and projector to the 'Representations' label above.
insights.avoid: The labels 'Encoder' and 'Projector' sit only under the bottom lane while f_theta's brace sits under the top lane, so the naming is split across two places.

core.what: two identical horizontal branches (A above, B below) converge on one drawn grey-scale cross-correlation matrix C at the right, which faces a clean identity matrix I across a double-headed L_BT arrow

relations.form: Z^A and Z^B arrows converge diagonally on the noisy grey matrix C, and C is joined to the black-diagonal target matrix I by a double arrow labelled L_BT, the loss drawn as its target

two unframed lanes of the same shapes - distorted-image box Y, encoder trapezoid, projector trapezoid, embedding box Z - stacked top and bottom, a brace under the top lane naming the shared weights f_theta
input box X at the left forks by two diagonal arrows labelled T ~ calligraphic T into Y^A and Y^B, and each lane runs straight left to right
the objective acts on the feature-by-feature correlation matrix, drawn as a small grid of grey cells with a 'feature dimension' double arrow under it

channels.colour: pale blue = trainable network parts (encoder and projector trapezoids); grey levels in C = correlation strength, black in I = target ones; one meaning each
channels.shape: widening/narrowing trapezoids = encoder and projector, white boxes = data and embeddings, cell grids = matrices
channels.line: solid arrows = data flow; double-headed arrow = the loss comparison; dashed curved arrow = 'Representations (for transfer tasks)' pointer
channels.frame: no frames; lanes are separated by whitespace

quality.strengths: the objective is drawn as a picture of what it compares - an empirical correlation matrix beside its identity target - so the core idea reads in 5 s without text; the twin lanes are identical shapes stacked, showing symmetry by geometry; the transfer representation is pointed at the encoder-projector junction rather than drawn as an extra box; short straight paths
quality.weaknesses: inputs and distorted views are white boxes with letters instead of images; the shared weights f_theta are a brace under the top lane only, so weight sharing with the bottom lane is stated in text rather than drawn

figures.lesson: Draw the loss as a picture of its target: render the computed cross-correlation as a noisy grey grid and the target as a clean identity grid side by side, linked by a double arrow carrying the loss symbol.

figures.title: BEiT: BERT Pre-Training of Image Transformers

taxonomy.task: masked image modelling pre-training of a vision transformer
taxonomy.note: builds on BERT's masked language modelling; the visual tokenizer comes from a dVAE

arrangement.units: Top lane: tokenizer path running left-to-right, ending in a dashed-outline box (decoder + reconstructed image). Bottom lane: patch row along the bottom edge with stacked encoder and head bars above it; the left column holds the input image, patch grid and masked grid as a vertical lead-in.
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo (dog) at top-left, cut into a 4x4 thumbnail grid and a masked copy below, then flattened into a row of patch thumbnails along the bottom
arrangement.losses_at: above the Masked Image Modeling Head: predicted ids at masked positions, connected to their target ids in the top-row token grid by dashed green arrows; no explicit loss label
arrangement.shared: the original image is drawn once and feeds both lanes (right to the tokenizer, down to the patches)

insights.structure: A top lane for the tokenizer (image -> tokenizer -> token-id grid -> dashed-boxed decoder) sits above a bottom lane where a flattened patch row feeds a wide encoder bar and a wide head bar, with a left column of labelled image stages leading down into the patch row.
insights.data: The input is a real photo cut into thumbnail patches, masked patches are flat grey squares and [M] cells, position embeddings are numbered blue cells with '+' between rows, and visual tokens are drawn as actual integer ids in a bracketed matrix.
insights.emphasis: The encoder is the widest and tallest shape with the model name in large type, and dashed green arrows — the only coloured lines — connect shaded target ids to the predictions at masked positions.
insights.flow: Reading starts top-left: right along the tokenizer row, down the left column through patching and masking, right along the bottom 'Flatten' arrow, then up through encoder and head, with green dashed arrows descending from the token grid.
insights.avoid: The decoder box is drawn at full prominence and only a small tag says it is unused, so it competes for attention with the pre-training path.

core.what: the visual-token ids at the masked positions in the top token grid (grey-shaded 234, 456, 876, 765, 322) are tied by dashed green arrows to the same ids predicted above the Masked Image Modeling Head below, target and prediction drawn as the same numbers

relations.form: five dashed green arrows run diagonally down from grey-shaded cells of the 4x4 token-id matrix to the matching ids printed above the MIM head
two lanes: a tokenizer row across the top (image -> Tokenizer trapezoid -> token-id matrix -> decoder -> reconstructed image) and the pre-training path below (patches -> encoder -> head)

the left column reads top to bottom: original image -> 4x4 image patches -> blockwise masking (grey squares), then 'Flatten' turns right into a patch row along the bottom edge with [S] and [M] tokens, position-embedding cells 0-16 above it
the pre-training path rises bottom to top: patch row -> wide BEiT Encoder -> hidden states h^L at the masked positions only -> wide MIM Head -> predicted ids
the decoder and reconstructed image sit inside a dashed grey box tagged 'Unused During Pre-Training' at top right, a dashed arrow leading into it

channels.colour: grey = masked (the shaded token ids and the [M] patches); lavender = the tokenizer and decoder (the dVAE); pale green = the encoder, yellow = the MIM head, light blue = position cells and hidden states; dashed dark green = target links - green appears on both the encoder fill and the target arrows
channels.shape: trapezoids = tokenizer and decoder, wide bars = encoder and head, small rounded squares = tokens and hidden states, bracketed number matrix = discrete token ids; images drawn as real photo crops
channels.line: solid black = data flow; dashed black = the unused decoder path; dashed green = which target each prediction is scored against
channels.frame: dashed grey box = parts not used during pre-training

quality.strengths: the compared things are drawn as data - the same token ids appear as targets in the matrix and as predictions above the head, with masked positions shaded grey both in the patch grid and in the id matrix; the real image is cut, masked and flattened step by step; the unused decoder is boxed and tagged in plain language
quality.weaknesses: the target links are long diagonal dashed wires crossing from the top matrix over the panel to the head outputs, one running almost the figure's width; the BEiT Encoder, a standard Transformer, is the largest element while the masking and token targets are small; green fills the encoder and colours the target arrows

figures.lesson: Link prediction targets to their source with a distinct colour of dashed arrow (green here) that crosses from the tokenizer row to the head's outputs, and box the parts unused in pre-training with a dashed outline and a plain-language tag.

figures.title: BEiT v2: Masked Image Modeling with Vector-Quantized Visual Tokenizers

taxonomy.task: visual tokenizer training (vector-quantized knowledge distillation)

arrangement.units: unenclosed peach ViT boxes and yellow l2-norm pills; codebook in a dashed rounded box above
arrangement.inputs_as: real photo
arrangement.shared: one codebook used by both the lookup and the decoder input

insights.structure: A left-to-right pipeline: input bird photo -> ViT tokenizer encoder -> l2-norm -> nearest-neighbour lookup against a dashed codebook box at top -> grid of visual token ids -> ViT decoder -> semantic reconstruction feature map, with a Teacher box above the output.
insights.data: Patch features are grey bar stacks (N x D), codebook entries are coloured vertical bars v_1..v_k in a dashed rounded box, visual tokens are a 4x4 grid of integer ids, and the target is a dark heatmap of teacher features.
insights.emphasis: The codebook is set apart at the top in a dashed box with pastel bars, and a red curved arrow labelled 'Straight-Through Gradients' under the token grid singles out the non-differentiable quantization step.
insights.flow: Curved black arrows lead from photo to encoder and decoder to output; grey dashed arrows pass through the token grid, while the codebook feeds down through l2-norm into both lookup circles.
insights.avoid: Light grey annotation text ('Nearest Neighbor Lookup', 'Visual Tokens', shape labels) is too faint, and the Teacher's input is not drawn.

core.what: vector quantisation as a lookup against a store: a dashed Codebook Embeddings container sits above the middle of a left-to-right tokenizer pipeline, curved arrows dropping from it to the two lookup nodes either side of the visual-token grid, and grey feature bars come out recoloured in their codebook entries' colours

relations.form: the codebook's pastel bars v_1..v_k in a dashed rounded box at top centre feed an l2-norm box whose output splits into two curved arrows down to the dotted lookup circles left and right of the token grid

one horizontal axis: bird photo -> peach ViT tokenizer encoder -> grey N x D feature bars -> l2-norm -> lookup -> 4x4 grid of integer token ids -> lookup -> coloured feature bars -> peach ViT decoder -> semantic reconstruction heat map
a blue Teacher box sits directly above the reconstruction heat map with one arrow down into it, the teacher's features being the reconstruction target
a red curved 'Straight-Through Gradients' arrow runs under the token grid from the right lookup node back to the left one, bypassing the non-differentiable step

channels.colour: pastel bar colour = codebook entry identity, so bars before lookup are grey and after lookup take their entry's colour; peach = ViT encoder and decoder, yellow = l2-norm; red = the straight-through gradient only; the Teacher's light blue is close to codebook entry v_1's blue
channels.shape: rounded boxes = networks and operations, thin bars = feature vectors, dotted circles = lookup, number grid = discrete tokens; the input is a real photo and the target a heat map
channels.line: solid black = forward data flow; grey dashed = flow through the discrete token grid; red curved = gradient path
channels.frame: dashed rounded container = the codebook store

quality.strengths: quantisation is shown by recolouring - grey bars in, codebook-coloured bars out - with the codebook drawn as the same coloured bars in a store above; the straight-through trick is the only red element and is drawn as the bypass it is; the data ends are a real photo and a heat map
quality.weaknesses: the reconstruction loss is not drawn - the Teacher arrow lands on the heat map, so what is compared with what is left implicit; both ViT boxes are small while the routine l2-norm boxes get the saturated yellow; the codebook's split arrows curve down to nodes far apart, adding long bends around the token grid

figures.lesson: Show vector quantisation by recolouring the feature bars: grey before the lookup, each bar in its codebook entry's colour after, with the codebook drawn as a row of the same coloured bars in a dashed container above.

figures.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

taxonomy.task: bidirectional language-model pretraining then task fine-tuning

arrangement.units: two light-grey rounded panels, 'Pre-training' (left) and 'Fine-Tuning' (right, a fanned stack of three task cards MNLI / NER / SQuAD), titled below each panel
arrangement.inputs_as: pink token tags ([CLS], Tok 1 ... Tok N, [SEP], Tok 1 ... Tok M) bracketed into two segments with a text label under each bracket and a blue arrow pointing at the pair description
arrangement.losses_at: on top of the unit they train: red block arrows above the output cells labelled NSP and Mask LM (pre-training) and Start/End Span (fine-tuning)
arrangement.shared: the same BERT box is drawn again in each panel; three dotted grey arrows connect the pre-training box to the stacked fine-tuning cards to show the weights carry over

insights.structure: Two grey rounded stage panels sit side by side, the right one fanned into three overlapping task cards, and each holds the same blue BERT box sandwiched between an embedding row and an output row.
insights.data: Tokens are drawn as a row of pink tags under yellow embedding cells, with brackets grouping them into Sentence A / Sentence B (or Question / Paragraph) and green output cells along the top edge.
insights.emphasis: Red block arrows above the output row name each objective or head, making the heads the only coloured accent that changes between the two stages.
insights.flow: Within each panel the eye goes bottom-to-top (pair description, tokens, embeddings, BERT, heads), and three dotted arrows carry it left-to-right from pre-training into the stacked fine-tuning cards.
insights.avoid: The ghosted network of grey circles inside the BERT box is too faint to read and adds texture without information.

core.what: two stage panels left to right - Pre-training and Fine-Tuning - each holding the identical blue BERT box with the same token, embedding and output rows, joined by dotted arrows, only the red heads on top and the segment labels underneath changing

relations.form: the Pre-training panel at left and the Fine-Tuning panel at right, same size and same internal layout, three dotted grey arrows running from the left BERT box into the fine-tuning cards
fine-tuning is drawn as a fanned stack of three overlapping cards (MNLI, NER, SQuAD) with only the front SQuAD card filled in
inside each BERT box the layout reads bottom to top: pink token tags ([CLS], Tok 1..N, [SEP], Tok 1..M) -> yellow embeddings E -> faint neuron mesh -> green outputs C, T -> red head arrows
the output row feeds several red block-arrow heads on top: NSP from C and Mask LM from the token outputs in pre-training, Start/End Span from the paragraph outputs in fine-tuning
two brackets under the token row group them into two segments (Masked Sentence A / B; Question / Paragraph), joined by a blue arrow from the pair description below

channels.colour: pink = input tokens, yellow = input embeddings, green = output representations, blue = the BERT encoder body, red = task heads, dark blue = the input-pair arrow - one meaning each, identical across both panels
channels.shape: rounded cells = tokens and vectors, block arrows = heads and inputs, a faint grid of circles = the Transformer layers
channels.line: grey block arrows = token-to-embedding; dotted grey arrows = transfer of the pre-trained model; thin black brackets = segments
channels.frame: light grey rounded panel = one stage; fanned cards = several tasks of the same stage

quality.strengths: the transfer is shown by repetition - the identical BERT box, rows and colours in both panels - so 'same model, different heads' reads by comparison; the representations (E, C, T) are drawn as rows of cells between the tokens and the heads; the fanned card stack shows many tasks in the space of one
quality.weaknesses: the BERT body is a large blue rectangle over a faint neuron mesh that carries no information, so the attention layers are not shown; the dotted transfer arrows end at the edges of the back cards rather than at a corresponding element; the masking itself (which tokens are masked) is not drawn, only named in the segment label

figures.lesson: Show fine-tuning on several tasks as a fanned stack of identical cards with only the front one drawn in full, so many downstream tasks cost the space of one.

figures.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer

taxonomy.task: sequential recommendation (next-item prediction)
taxonomy.note: modality is a sequence of item IDs from user interaction histories; 'tabular' is the closest list item

arrangement.units: four sub-figures captioned (a)-(d) below: (a), (c), (d) enclosed by dotted rectangles; (b) the proposed model unframed and widest; each panel holds a column-per-position stack of embedding and Trm/GRU boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: italic item ids v1 ... v_{t-1} and the literal [mask] token under each column, feeding pink+peach embedding boxes
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the predicted item v_t sits on top of the Projection box at the top of (b)
arrangement.shared: the Trm block is detailed once in (a) and reused as identical green 'Trm' boxes in (b) and (c); the same pink embedding boxes appear in all model panels

insights.structure: Four captioned sub-figures in a row: (a) the Transformer layer in a dotted frame at far left, (b) the proposed model large and unframed in the centre, (c) SASRec and (d) the RNN baseline stacked in dotted frames at right, all drawn as one column per sequence position.
insights.data: Inputs are italic item symbols v1 ... v_{t-1} and a literal [mask] under each column, turned into pink item-embedding and peach position-embedding boxes joined by bold '+' signs; outputs are hidden states h^L and the predicted item v_t on top.
insights.emphasis: The proposed model is the biggest, the only one without a frame, and the only one with a [mask] token and a bright green Projection head, while baselines reuse the same green Trm/pink embedding blocks so the difference is only in the arrow pattern (all-to-all vs left-to-right vs GRU chain).
insights.flow: Bottom-to-top inside every panel; between layers the arrows encode the attention direction (every block to every block in b, only to same/later positions in c, horizontal chain in d), and an L× brace at the left of (b) groups the repeated layers.
insights.avoid: The all-to-all crossing arrows between Trm rows in (b) form a dense thicket of diagonals, and the sideways 'Embedding Layer' label is hard to read; do not copy the crossing-arrow mesh for more than three columns.

core.what: the proposed model and two baselines drawn with the same blocks - one column per item position, pink embedding cells at the bottom, green Trm/GRU boxes stacked above - so the only visible difference is the connection pattern between columns: all-to-all in (b), forward-only in (c) SASRec, a left-to-right chain in (d) RNN

relations.form: (b) BERT4Rec large and unframed in the centre with crossing arrows in both directions between columns; (c) SASRec and (d) RNN stacked at right in dotted frames, same cell shapes and colours, arrows only rightward (c) or a horizontal GRU chain (d)

(a) at far left opens one Trm block as a dotted-frame vertical stack (Multi-Head Attention -> Dropout -> Add & Norm -> Feed-Forward -> Dropout -> Add & Norm) with residual lines down its left side, tagged 'Trm' at its corner
in (b) each column adds a pink item embedding v and a peach position embedding p with a bold '+', the item input v reaching the embedding by a right-angled line around it
the last column's input is the literal [mask] token, and only that column carries a lime Projection box on top predicting v_t

channels.colour: pink = item embeddings, peach = position embeddings, mint green = Transformer (Trm) or GRU blocks, lime = projection head; in (a) each sub-layer has its own fill (orange attention, blue feed-forward, yellow Add & Norm, pale green dropout) - the attention's orange is close to the position-embedding peach
channels.shape: rounded rectangles for every block and embedding; a curly brace with 'L x' marks repeated layers
channels.line: thin black arrows; their pattern between columns (all-to-all, forward-only, chain) is the comparison
channels.frame: dotted frame = a module detail or a baseline (a, c, d); the proposed model is the only unframed panel

quality.strengths: the core difference is pure geometry - identical columns and blocks in all three models, only the wiring between positions changing; the proposed model gets the largest space and the only [mask] input and projection head; the Trm block is taught once in (a) and reused compactly
quality.weaknesses: ours sits in the centre rather than last, so the baselines read after it; the dense crossing arrows in (b) make individual connections hard to follow; frames mean both 'detail' (a) and 'baseline' (c, d); the item input lines in (b) bend round each embedding stack instead of entering it straight

figures.lesson: Draw the proposed sequence model and its baselines with identical blocks (same green Trm boxes, same pink item cells v1 … vt) so that the only visible difference is the connection pattern between positions: all-to-all for bidirectional, forward-only for causal, a chain for recurrent.

figures.title: Self-supervised Learning with Random-projection Quantizer for Speech Recognition

taxonomy.task: self-supervised speech pretraining with a random-projection quantizer
taxonomy.note: BEST-RQ = BERT-based speech pretraining; the frozen random projection + random codebook produces the discrete targets

arrangement.units: no enclosures; the encoder is a flat green box, the codebook a rounded white container titled 'codebook', branches separated only by space
arrangement.inputs_as: a real log-mel spectrogram strip at bottom left (and its masked copy above it)
arrangement.losses_at: implicit at the top: encoder arrows point into the row of target indices; no loss label
arrangement.shared: the same unmasked spectrogram feeds both the masking path and the Projection branch

insights.structure: Two unframed branches side by side: at left the learning path (raw spectrogram -> masked spectrogram -> green ASR Encoder), at right the target path (Projection box -> small orange vector -> rounded 'codebook' container), meeting at a row of integers across the top.
insights.data: Speech is drawn as real purple-orange spectrogram strips, with masked spans shown as flat light-grey blocks cut out of the second strip; targets are a literal row of code indices (897 139 23 4981 2750 6079) and the codebook is a row of grey vertical code-vector bars with an ellipsis.
insights.emphasis: The quantizer's novelty is marked by light-blue text 'random init, frozen' placed beside both the Projection box and the codebook, the only coloured annotation in the figure.
insights.flow: Bottom-to-top on the left via hollow block arrows (Masking, encoder), a thin diagonal line from the unmasked spectrogram to Projection at bottom right, up through the codebook, and an 'index' line that loops over the top and drops onto the integer row, where encoder arrows point up at the masked positions.
insights.avoid: No loss is named: the reader must infer that the encoder arrows into the integer row are a prediction target, and the index line wraps around the top edge instead of feeding the targets directly; label the objective explicitly.

core.what: two branches from one spectrogram meet in a row of six integer labels across the top: the masked spectrogram's ASR Encoder sends arrows up into three of them, and the frozen projection-and-codebook branch at right drops its 'index' bus onto all six

relations.form: the label row 897 139 23 4981 2750 6079 sits between the encoder below (three upward arrows onto 139, 4981, 2750) and a horizontal bus above it fed by the codebook's index line (six downward arrows)

two unframed columns rise from the same bottom-left spectrogram: left, Masking -> masked spectrogram (grey gaps) -> green ASR Encoder; right, a long diagonal arrow to Projection -> small orange vector -> rounded codebook container
the codebook is a rounded box holding a row of grey vector bars with an ellipsis; the projected orange vector enters it from below and an 'index' line leaves its top
speech is drawn as real spectrogram strips, masking shown as light grey blanked spans cut out of the strip

channels.colour: green = the trainable encoder, light blue = the frozen projection, with the same light-blue 'random init, frozen' margin text beside projection and codebook - training status carried by blue; orange = the projected vector; grey = masked spans and codebook entries
channels.shape: rectangles = networks, a rounded container of bars = the codebook store, plain integers = discrete targets, spectrogram images = speech data
channels.line: thin dark arrows for data; hollow block arrows for masking and encoding the spectrogram; the top bus is a right-angled line from the codebook across the label row
channels.frame: only the codebook has a container; no grouping frames

quality.strengths: the compared things are drawn as data - predictions and quantiser targets meet at real integer labels, masking is visible as blanked spans of a real spectrogram; frozen parts are marked by one coloured margin note instead of a legend; the figure is small with few elements
quality.weaknesses: the projection branch is reached by a long diagonal arrow from the bottom spectrogram across the whole figure; the index bus routes up and over the full label row; grey marks both masked spans and codebook entries; which labels the encoder is scored on is shown only by which three arrows reach the row, without a loss drawn

figures.lesson: Training status is written as a coloured margin note ('random init, frozen' in light blue) beside each frozen box, instead of a hatch pattern, lock icon or legend.

figures.title: BEVFormer: Learning Bird's-Eye-View Representation from Multi-Camera Images via Spatiotemporal Transformers

taxonomy.task: bird's-eye-view perception from multi-camera images

arrangement.units: no containers; three standalone BEV grids and one stacked photo deck, each captioned beneath
arrangement.inputs_as: a grid of BEV queries with one highlighted cell, plus real multi-camera photos (top-middle) and the previous BEV map (bottom-middle)
arrangement.shared: the query cell is the same position in the input and output grids; both routes converge on it

insights.structure: Three BEV grids sit at the left (BEV Queries), bottom-middle (BEV at t-1) and right (BEV at t), with a deck of overlapping street-camera photos top-middle, joined into a parallelogram by two routes.
insights.data: BEV space is a grey square grid with one highlighted query cell (and an 'Ego' red arrow); BEV maps carry orange road and blue vehicle marks; camera inputs are real faded street photos with a car circled and red triangles at sampled points.
insights.emphasis: The two attention mechanisms are colour-coded routes: blue 'Spatial Attention' through the camera images on top, green 'Temporal Attention' through the previous BEV below, each with a circled lens on the region attended.
insights.flow: Left to right: from the query cell the line splits into the blue upper and green lower paths and rejoins at the same cell in the output grid; a plain-language sentence across the top ('What's in here at timestamp t ?' -> Lookup & Aggregate -> 'There is a car !') narrates the same path.
insights.avoid: The top-row narration duplicates the paths with dotted drops to the grids, and the dark-grey camera deck is low contrast against the faint labels; as a teaser it shows no network blocks, so it cannot stand in for an architecture figure.

core.what: one BEV query cell splits into two routes forming a parallelogram - a blue Spatial Attention route up through the multi-camera images and a green Temporal Attention route down through the previous BEV - that rejoin at the same outlined cell of the BEV at time t

relations.form: from the outlined query cell in the left grid a line forks into a blue upper path and a green lower path, which converge again on a point left of the outlined cell in the right grid

each route passes through the data it reads: the blue path through a deck of faded street-camera photos with an ellipse around a car and red triangles at sampled points, the green path through the t-1 BEV grid with a circled lens over a road region
BEV space drawn as square grids - a blank grey query grid with an 'Ego' arrow and one outlined cell, and BEV maps at t-1 and t with orange road and blue vehicle marks
a plain-language line across the top, 'What's in here at timestamp t ?' -> 'Lookup & Aggregate' -> 'There is a car !', pinned by dotted drop-lines to the query cell and the output cell

channels.colour: blue = spatial attention route and its label, green = temporal attention route and its label; within the BEV maps orange = road and blue = vehicles, so blue carries both 'spatial attention' and 'vehicle'; dark red = the Ego arrow and sample triangles
channels.shape: square grids = BEV space, a black outlined cell = the one query followed, photos = camera input, circles/ellipses = the region attended
channels.line: coloured solid lines = attention routes; dotted vertical lines = pin the question/answer to the cells
channels.frame: no frames; the camera images are a stacked deck

quality.strengths: the two attention mechanisms are drawn as routes through the data they read, so 'query looks in images and in history, then combines' is geometry with no module boxes; one query cell is followed from input to output grid; the question-and-answer line gives the 5 s reading in plain language; inputs are real photos and BEV maps
quality.weaknesses: blue means both the spatial-attention route and vehicles in the BEV maps; the parallelogram's diagonal segments bend twice per route, and the two routes land on one point left of the output cell instead of on the cell; the camera-deck images are faded so the sampled points are small

figures.lesson: Explain a BEV query with a question-and-answer line across the top ('What's in here at timestamp t?' -> 'There is a car!') whose dotted drop-lines pin both ends to the same black-outlined cell of the input and output BEV grids.

figures.title: BEVFormer: Learning Bird's-Eye-View Representation from Multi-Camera Images via Spatiotemporal Transformers

taxonomy.task: BEV detection and segmentation from multi-camera images

arrangement.units: main unit (a) = input column + light-grey encoder rectangle with ×6; two detail units (b), (c) as dashed rounded containers on the right, each captioned below
arrangement.inputs_as: real multi-camera photos around a car icon at bottom-left; History BEV and BEV Queries as cube grids under the encoder
arrangement.losses_at: none; a 'Det & Seg Heads' callout at the top of (a)
arrangement.shared: the camera feature planes and the BEV cube grids reappear in the detail panels (b) and (c)

insights.structure: (a) Overall Architecture fills the left two-thirds: a left column (six camera photos ringed around a top-view blue car, a three-pill backbone, a bracketed set of six coloured camera feature planes) feeding a light-grey encoder-layer block with ×6; (b) Spatial Cross-Attention and (c) Temporal Self-Attention are dashed rounded zoom panels stacked on the right.
insights.data: Inputs are real camera photos arranged around the ego car; camera features are flat coloured parallelograms; BEV maps (history B_{t-1}, queries Q, current B_t) are small 3-D cube grids in orange and blue; sampled reference points are coloured dots and triangles.
insights.emphasis: The two novel attention layers are the only tinted blocks in the encoder stack (beige Spatial Cross-Attention, gold Temporal Self-Attention), and each is zoomed by grey dashed lines into its own detail panel.
insights.flow: Bottom-to-top inside the encoder (History BEV and BEV Queries enter at the bottom, Current BEV and a 'Det & Seg Heads' callout exit at top); camera features enter from the left on a long curved arrow; dashed zoom lines fan right into (b) and (c).
insights.avoid: The curved arrow from the feature planes to the cross-attention block is long and the zoom wedges cut across white space; the 3-D geometry in (b) packs pillars, points and hit-view circle with tiny math labels that are hard to read.

core.what: an encoder-layer stack in (a) whose two new attention layers - the only warm-filled blocks - are each opened in a dashed rounded panel at right, (b) Spatial Cross-Attention and (c) Temporal Self-Attention, tied by grey dashed callout lines and reusing the BEV slabs at larger size

relations.form: two grey dashed fan lines run from the Spatial Cross-Attention and Temporal Self-Attention blocks to the right-hand panels (b) and (c), stacked one above the other

(a) reads bottom to top: History BEV slab and BEV Queries slab enter a light-grey x6 encoder stack (Temporal Self-Attention -> Add & Norm -> Spatial Cross-Attention -> Add & Norm -> Feed Forward -> Add & Norm) -> Current BEV slab -> Det & Seg Heads

the left column reads bottom to top: six camera photos ringed around a top-view blue car -> three-pill Backbone -> bracketed set of six coloured feature planes F_t, whose curved arrow enters Spatial Cross-Attention from the left

(b) draws a pillar of cells rising from one query cell (x', y') of a blue BEV slab with red sample points (x', y', z_j') projected onto camera feature planes, the planes actually hit circled by a green dashed 'Hit Views' ring
(c) draws the peach History BEV slab beside the blue BEV Queries slab, with red curved arrows from sampled points in the history to the query cell (x, y)

channels.colour: slab colour = BEV role (blue queries, peach BEV at t-1 and t); camera feature planes each have their own pastel hue = camera identity; teal = standard layers, gold and peach = the two new attention layers; yellow highlights the query cell in the detail panels; green dashed = hit views - peach thus means both 'BEV state' and 'spatial cross-attention block'
channels.shape: oblique slabs of cube cells = BEV grids, flat parallelograms = camera feature maps, rounded pills = layers, photos = camera inputs
channels.line: solid black arrows = data flow and residuals; grey dashed fans = zoom callouts; red arrows = sampling offsets in the detail panels; green dashed ring = selection
channels.frame: light-grey block = one repeated encoder layer (x6); dashed rounded panel = an opened detail

quality.strengths: the two contributions are the only warm blocks in a teal stack and each gets its own detail panel, so space follows novelty; the detail panels draw the operation on the structure (a pillar of sample points projected into the hit camera planes; offsets from history to query); BEV slabs are taught once in (a) and reused at larger size
quality.weaknesses: peach carries both 'BEV state' slabs and the Spatial Cross-Attention block fill; the camera-feature curved arrow from the left column crosses into the stack's side; residual lines run up the stack's right edge as long right-angled wires; the detail panels repeat camera-plane hues with no key

figures.lesson: Draw the BEV as an oblique slab of cube cells whose colour gives its role (blue = queries, peach = BEV at t-1 and t) and reuse those slabs in the zoomed detail panels, where one highlighted pillar of cells with sample points shows where a query looks into the camera features.

figures.title: BEVFusion: Multi-Task Multi-Sensor Fusion with Unified Bird's-Eye View Representation

taxonomy.task: multi-sensor BEV 3D detection and map segmentation

arrangement.units: two unframed horizontal lanes (camera top, LiDAR bottom) separated by whitespace and colour family, merging into a central fused-BEV trunk, plus a right column of two framed head images with tinted label strips
arrangement.inputs_as: real photos: a stacked fan of multi-view street images and a LiDAR point-cloud render, each labelled underneath
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; task heads are shown as output images
arrangement.shared: the BEV encoder and fused features are drawn once in the merged trunk feeding all heads

insights.structure: Camera and LiDAR branches run as two parallel rows of identical step types (encoder, features, view transform, BEV grid), converge diagonally into one stacked block in the middle, and a single shared trunk then forks into a right-hand column of task heads.
insights.data: Inputs and task outputs are real images (a stacked set of street photos, a black LiDAR sweep, a coloured BEV map, a LiDAR BEV with orange boxes), while intermediates are drawn as stacked sheets for 2D camera features and gridded 3-D cuboids for voxel and BEV features.
insights.emphasis: The fused BEV block stacks an orange camera grid on a blue LiDAR grid so the fusion is visible as geometry and colour, and every downstream element turns teal to mark the unified space.
insights.flow: Short thick black arrows run left to right along each row, two short diagonal arrows bring both BEV grids into the centre block, and a bracket-shaped arrow splits the fused features to the two head images at the right edge.
insights.avoid: The view-transform icons (a tiny frustum, a flatten press) are small black pictograms that are hard to decode at print size, and the elided heads are only a bare ellipsis between two images.

core.what: two parallel sensor rows - camera (orange) on top, LiDAR (blue) below - converge by short diagonal arrows on one cuboid in the middle where the orange camera BEV grid is stacked directly on the blue LiDAR BEV grid, after which a single teal trunk continues

relations.form: two identical rows of step types (encoder trapezoid pair -> features -> view-transform box -> BEV grid), the camera row in orange outlines above and the LiDAR row in blue below, aligned column by column
the camera BEV grid and LiDAR BEV grid sit above and below a central stacked block (orange layer on blue layer), each joined by one short diagonal arrow
after fusion one horizontal row: stacked block -> teal BEV Encoder (encoder-decoder trapezoids) -> teal Fused BEV Features cuboid
a bracket arrow forks the fused features into a right-hand column of task heads drawn as output images (BEV map segmentation, an ellipsis, 3D object detection), each captioned in a teal bar
each view transform is drawn as a glyph of its geometry - a camera frustum projecting a patch in the camera row, a slab squeezed by two arrows ('Flatten along z-axis') in the LiDAR row

channels.colour: colour family = sensor branch (orange camera, blue LiDAR) through every element of its row, teal = everything after fusion; the fused block literally stacks orange on blue - one meaning throughout, though the detection output image also uses orange for its boxes
channels.shape: trapezoid pairs = encoders, stacked sheets = 2D feature maps, gridded cuboids = voxel/BEV features, rounded boxes with a glyph = view transforms; inputs and outputs are real images (street photos, LiDAR sweep, BEV map)
channels.line: short black arrows throughout, one bracket arrow for the fan-out to heads
channels.frame: no frames; task outputs are boxed images with caption bars

quality.strengths: fusion is drawn as geometry - two coloured grids stacked into one block where two parallel rows converge - and colour has one meaning (sensor) carried through every element, then switched to teal downstream; representations are drawn between modules (sheets, voxel cuboids, BEV grids); the view transforms are glyphs of the geometric operation; arrows are short and straight
quality.weaknesses: the BEV Encoder and task heads get as much space as the fusion step, so the contribution is not the largest element; the task heads are output images with no head modules drawn; orange reappears as detection boxes in the output image

figures.lesson: Colour each sensor branch in its own family through every element and show fusion as the two coloured feature grids literally stacked into one block, then switch to a third colour for everything downstream.

figures.title: BioCLIP: A Vision Foundation Model for the Tree of Life

taxonomy.task: species-level image classification via taxonomic-label contrastive pretraining

arrangement.units: five unframed parts labelled (a)-(e): label rows top left, representation row bottom left, matrix centre right, two photos far right

arrangement.losses_at: the contrastive matrix in (c) sits between the label rows and the photos, with grey diagonal cells as positives
arrangement.shared: none

under (b), the label's cells in dashed outlines with three nested elbow arrows from Kingdom, Phylum and Class into Order, showing what an autoregressive token can see
a CLIP matrix with text embeddings T1..Tn as the header row and image features I1..In as the left column, grey cells on the diagonal

figures.title: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models
