each objective is shown as a mask over the Q and T token positions (grey = masked cells in a Q/T-labelled grid), keyed above

channels.colour: blue = frozen image encoder (with snowflake), pale yellow region = the trainable Q-Former, salmon = objectives, block fills (orange self-attention, grey cross-attention, purple/green feed-forward) = layer type, with feed-forward coloured differently per tower; small coloured squares = learned queries; grey/white mask cells keyed as masked/unmasked
channels.shape: trapezoid = encoder, rounded rectangles = layers and objectives, rounded tray of squares = queries, quoted pill = input text
channels.line: solid arrows = data flow; a dashed crossed-out arrow = blocked uni-modal attention
channels.frame: the yellow region frames the Q-Former; a thin outline groups each tower's xN stack; a vertical rule separates the mask panel

quality.strengths: Objectives are tied to their masks by repeating the same salmon box under each grid, so the reader sees how one module serves three objectives; the input image and the quoted sentence are drawn as data; the frozen encoder is marked by colour plus snowflake.
quality.weaknesses: In the left panel the three objectives sit as boxes above the towers with lines merging into them, so the compared representations (query output vs text [CLS]) are not drawn; the attention-masking types are text labels on arrows between the towers, duplicating the mask panel; feed-forward colours differ between towers without a stated meaning.

figures.lesson: When several objectives differ only in what each token may see, draw one small mask grid per objective beside the model rather than describing it in the boxes.

figures.title: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models

taxonomy.task: vision-to-language generative pretraining with a frozen LLM

arrangement.units: two horizontal rows, one per LLM variant, separated by a thin grey rule and labelled by a grey card at the left
arrangement.inputs_as: the same real photo (a cat in sunglasses with a patch grid) in each row; text as quoted italic pills ('a cat', 'wearing sunglasses')
arrangement.losses_at: no loss box; the target text sits as a labelled quoted pill above the LLM decoder at each row's right end
arrangement.shared: the Image Encoder, Q-Former and Fully Connected are drawn as identical copies in both rows

insights.structure: Two identical left-to-right rows stacked under a thin rule, one per LLM type, so the Image Encoder, Q-Former and Fully Connected line up in the same columns and only the LLM end differs.
insights.data: The input is a real photo with a white patch grid, learned queries are rows of four coloured squares in rounded trays above and below the Q-Former, and text is shown as quoted italic pills labelled Output, Prefix and Suffix Text.
insights.emphasis: Frozen blocks are saturated blue with white snowflakes and the trainable Q-Former and projection pale yellow, so the small trainable bridge reads at a glance between large frozen parts.
insights.flow: Straight arrows run left to right through each row, and a curved arrow carries the projected query row down under the LLM bar before turning up into it.
insights.avoid: The grey variant-label cards at the far left take as much width as the image, which pushes the whole pipeline right; a short row title would save space.

core.what: two identical left-to-right rows stacked under a thin rule, one per LLM type, with image, Image Encoder, Q-Former and Fully Connected in the same columns so only the right-hand LLM end differs (one Decoder vs Encoder + Decoder)

relations.form: two rows sharing columns, each labelled by a grey card at the far left; the decoder-only row ends in one wide LLM Decoder bar, the encoder-decoder row splits that width into LLM Encoder and LLM Decoder
within each row straight arrows run input photo -> blue Image Encoder trapezoid -> Q-Former -> Fully Connected -> LLM
the projected query row drops under the LLM bar on a curved arrow and enters it from below; in the second row the prefix text pill 'a cat' sits beside the query row as a second input

channels.colour: saturated blue with white snowflake = frozen (image encoder, LLM parts), pale yellow = trainable (Q-Former, Fully Connected); the four small coloured squares in rounded trays = learned query tokens
channels.shape: trapezoid = image encoder, wide bars = LLM, rounded boxes = trainable modules, rounded trays = query sequences, quoted white pills = text
channels.line: solid arrows only, all data flow
channels.frame: no frames; a thin grey horizontal rule separates the two variants

quality.strengths: The variants are drawn as identical rows aligned column for column, so the one difference (the LLM end) reads by position alone; frozen vs trainable is carried by one colour pair plus snowflakes; queries before and after the Q-Former and the prefix/suffix text are drawn as data.
quality.weaknesses: The grey variant-label cards at the far left take as much width as the input photo; the curved arrow from Fully Connected loops down and back under the LLM instead of entering it straight; the input photo and encoder are repeated in full in both rows, where the shared front end could be drawn once.

figures.lesson: To show one adapter plugging into two kinds of backbone, repeat the identical row twice under a thin rule and let only the right-hand end differ, with a grey label card at each row's left naming the variant.

figures.title: BLIP: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training for Unified Vision-Language Understanding and Generation

taxonomy.task: unified vision-language understanding and generation pretraining

arrangement.units: one column per objective, each a framed tower of identical structure; the image encoder is the first column
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo under the image encoder; one quoted caption at the bottom with a fan of arrows to each text tower
arrangement.losses_at: each objective's box on top of its own tower
arrangement.shared: the image features run along the top as one line with drops into the towers that cross-attend

insights.structure: Four rounded grey towers in a row (Image Encoder, Text Encoder, Image-grounded Text encoder, Image-grounded Text decoder), each an N× stack of Self-Att / Cross Attention / Feed Forward blocks with residual ⊕ nodes, labelled at the bottom-left.
insights.data: The image is a real photo cut into a 3×3 grid at bottom-left; text is one quoted caption in a rounded box at bottom-centre, entering each text tower with a different prefix ('[CLS]', '[Encode]', '[Decode]') plus a checkered token placeholder; embeddings are flat bars above the first two towers.
insights.emphasis: Towers are identical in shape and differ in one block: Cross Attention greyed out with hatching in the text encoder, Causal Self-Att in green in the decoder; block colours repeat across towers, and the three objectives are yellow boxes (ITC, ITM, LM) on top.
insights.flow: Bottom-to-top inside each tower; one caption fans up to three towers; the image embedding runs along a line across the top of the figure and drops into the Cross Attention blocks of the two image-grounded towers.
insights.avoid: The image line runs over the top edge and crosses unit boundaries to reach two towers, and nothing in the figure states that matching colours mean shared parameters.

core.what: four rounded grey transformer towers in a row (image encoder, text encoder, image-grounded text encoder, image-grounded text decoder), the three text towers fed by one quoted caption fanned up from the bottom and differing in one block each, with their objectives (ITC, ITM, LM) as yellow boxes on top

relations.form: one caption box at bottom-centre fans three arrows up into the three text towers, each entering with its own prefix ('[CLS]', '[Encode]', '[Decode]'); block fills repeat across towers (blue Feed Forward, orange Cross Attention, peach Bi Self-Att)
the text towers are identical in layout and differ in one block: Cross Attention hatched and greyed out in the text encoder, Causal Self-Att in green in the decoder
the image embedding bar and the text embedding bar sit at the tops of the first two towers with ITC between them, arrows from both pointing in
the image encoder's output runs along a line across the top of the figure and drops down into the Cross Attention block of the third and fourth towers from the left side
bottom-to-top inside each tower: input -> self-attention -> (cross attention) -> feed forward with residual ⊕ nodes, Nx

channels.colour: block fill = block type, repeated across towers (the crop carries no key saying whether a shared fill means shared weights); yellow = objectives; the image-side embedding bar is pale lilac and the text-side bar pale blue; hatched grey = a block absent in that tower
channels.shape: rounded rectangles = blocks, circles with + = residual adds, thin bars = embeddings, yellow rectangles = objectives
channels.line: solid black arrows for all data flow, including the long top line carrying image features
channels.frame: each tower is one rounded grey frame marked Nx

quality.strengths: The three text towers are identical in layout so each one's differing block (hatched absent cross-attention, green causal attention) is the visible difference; ITC is drawn between two embedding bars rather than wired from encoders; real photo and quoted caption are the inputs.
quality.weaknesses: The image features travel on one long line over the top of the whole figure with two right-angle drops, a wire across the panel rather than a placement; ITM and LM sit on their towers without drawing what they compare; the meaning of repeated block colours is not keyed in the figure.

figures.lesson: One tower per objective, all the same shape, each with its loss on top and one shared input fanned out beneath them, makes several objectives read as a comparison.

figures.title: Generating Physically Stable and Buildable Brick Structures from Text

taxonomy.task: text-to-brick-structure generation with an LLM, per-brick validity checks and physics-aware rollback

arrangement.units: three dashed rounded frames: tokenization and training side by side in the top row, inference across the bottom row
arrangement.inputs_as: quoted text prompts (a caption in (a), an instruction plus caption under the prompt tokens in (b), a user prompt beside a person icon in (c)) and a rendered brick chair with its numbered brick list
arrangement.losses_at: no loss is drawn; in (b) the next-token targets are the output token row above the LLM bar, shifted one token left of the input row
arrangement.shared: the brick tokenization taught in (a) is reused as the grey token boxes in (b), and the same render style carries through (a), (b) and (c)

insights.structure: A narrow tokenization panel and a wide training panel share the top row; the inference panel takes the whole bottom row as one left-to-right strip of generation steps.
insights.data: Brick sequences are shown as literal token boxes ('1 x 1 ( 7 , 8 , 0 )') and as 3-D renders after the 1st, 40th, 80th, 100th and 126th brick, so the token row and the structure it builds sit one above the other.
insights.emphasis: Failures are the most saturated marks: a red brick in the render, a red cross disc below it, and a red cross at the rollback note; valid steps get green check discs.
insights.flow: Short vertical arrows link token boxes to the LLM bar in (b); in (c) the row reads left to right, two curved black 'Resample' arcs jump from a rejected tile to the next, and a rollback line leaves the final stability check, runs over the row and drops back into it.
insights.avoid: Nine identical green check discs under the inference row cost space and repeat one fact; the physical stability analysis that triggers the rollback is only a text note, not drawn.

core.what: inference unrolled as a row of brick renders, one per generation step, each with a check or cross below, resample arcs at rejected steps and a rollback arrow from the final stability check back over the row

relations.form: nine equal grey render tiles left to right, separated by ellipses, the newest brick tinted brown in each
in (b) the input token row (prompt, SEP, brick tokens) runs under the LLM bar and the same row shifted by one, ending in EOS, runs over it
brick token groups in (b) sit directly above renders of the structure after that brick, joined by a brace, so tokens and geometry align column by column
three dashed panels (a) tokenization, (b) training, (c) inference, the first two side by side above the third
rejections are drawn on the structure: the colliding or out-of-library brick is red in the render with a labelled callout arrow

channels.colour: light blue = prompt tokens, pale pink = special tokens (SEP, EOS), grey = brick tokens; in renders yellow-green = placed bricks, brown = the brick just added, red = an invalid brick; green check disc = pass, red cross disc = fail (red carries invalid brick and failed check, the same meaning)
channels.shape: rounded token box = token, long bar = the LLM, rendered tile = intermediate structure, disc = validity verdict, line icon = actor (user, model)
channels.line: straight black arrows = data flow; curved black arrows = resample jumps and the rollback, the same style as data flow
channels.frame: dashed grey rounded frame = one sub-figure (tokenization, training, inference)

quality.strengths: The method's loop is visible as geometry: the generation steps are an unrolled row of real renders and both corrective moves (resample, rollback) are drawn as jumps within that row; the failing brick is tinted red on the structure itself; tokens and the renders they describe are aligned column by column in (b); the inference panel, which carries the contribution, takes the full width.
quality.weaknesses: Resample and rollback arrows use the same black solid style as data flow; the nine identical check discs and the 'Validity Check' key at the bottom left repeat one fact; the physics stability check is only a label at the end of the row; panel (a) restates the token format in a numbered list that (b) already shows as token boxes.

figures.lesson: Draw an autoregressive generator with per-step checks as a row of rendered intermediate states with a pass/fail disc under each, the offending part tinted red, and curved resample / rollback arrows that jump within the row.

figures.title: Bootstrap Your Own Latent: A New Approach to Self-Supervised Learning

taxonomy.task: self-supervised image representation learning

arrangement.units: Rows = the online and target branches as tinted bands (blue, red) labelled at the right; columns = the stages (view, representation, projection) as outlined frames spanning both rows, titled on top.
arrangement.inputs_as: one input box at the left edge that forks into both rows
arrangement.losses_at: one dashed 'loss' arc from the online row's last block down to the target output at the right edge, where the rows meet
arrangement.shared: none: each stage drawn once per row in the same column

insights.structure: A grid: two rows on full-width tinted bands (lavender 'online', pink 'target', labelled at far right) crossed by three tall grey-outlined columns (view, representation, projection) titled at the top, with a fourth 'prediction' step only in the online row.
insights.data: Everything is a math symbol in a rounded box: input x, views v and v', representations y_θ / y'_ξ, projections z_θ / z'_ξ, prediction q_θ(z_θ); function names f, g, q label the arrows between columns.
insights.emphasis: The asymmetry is the message: only the online row has the extra q_θ prediction box, and the target row ends in a '//' stop-gradient mark and plain-text sg(z'_ξ).
insights.flow: Left to right: x splits by two diagonal arrows (t, t') into the two rows; arrows run straight across each band; a dashed curved 'loss' arrow drops from q_θ(z_θ) down to sg(z'_ξ) at the right edge.
insights.avoid: No real images: the input and views are bare symbols, so the augmentation idea is invisible; the prediction stage has no column frame while the other stages do.

core.what: two parallel lanes on tinted bands (lavender 'online' above, pink 'target' below) run the same view -> representation -> projection steps in shared columns, the online lane alone extending one more box (q_θ(z_θ)) before a dashed loss arc drops to the target's sg(z'_ξ)

relations.form: two full-width tinted bands labelled 'online' and 'target' at the right edge, with the per-step boxes vertically aligned between them
three tall grey-outlined columns span both bands so the view, representation and projection of each branch share one column; the function names (f_ξ, g_ξ, sg) label the gaps between columns
the online prediction q_θ(z_θ) and the target projection sg(z'_ξ) sit one above the other at the right end, joined by a dashed curved arrow labelled 'loss'
the input x at the left forks on two diagonal arrows (t, t') into the bands, then straight horizontal arrows run left to right along each band
asymmetry by absence: the target band stops a column early and its last arrow carries a '//' stop-gradient mark

channels.colour: band tint = branch (lavender online, pink target); box fills follow the band
channels.shape: every entity is the same rounded box holding a symbol (x, v, y, z, q(z)); functions are only arrow labels
channels.line: solid arrows = forward computation, dashed curved arrow = loss, '//' on an arrow = stop-gradient
channels.frame: grey outlined columns group the same step across both branches

quality.strengths: The two-branch structure and its one asymmetry (the extra prediction box, the stop-gradient mark) are visible by position alone; every compared representation is drawn as its own box, and the loss joins the two compared ones directly at the right edge; arrows are straight and aligned along each band.
quality.weaknesses: Nothing is drawn as data: the image and its views are symbol boxes x, v, v'; network names appear only as letters on arrows, so the encoder/projector/predictor modules have no presence; the 'online'/'target' labels sit at the far right away from where the branches start.

figures.lesson: Pair the two branches as rows on tinted bands and pair their stages as tall outlined columns through both rows, so the one box the online row has and the target row lacks (the predictor) stands out by its empty slot below.

figures.title: CAMEL: Communicative Agents for "Mind" Exploration of Large Language Model Society

taxonomy.task: role-playing framework for autonomous cooperation between LLM agents

arrangement.units: two rounded grey panels with dark outline: 'Human Input' (left, titled top) and 'Role Playing Session' (right, titled bottom)
arrangement.inputs_as: a green card with the quoted human idea plus a beige role-assignment card
arrangement.shared: role colours (orange user, blue assistant) are shared between the role-assignment card, the agent icons and the messages

insights.structure: Two light-grey rounded panels side by side: a narrow 'Human Input' panel at left (idea card, human icon, role-assignment card) and a wide 'Role Playing Session' panel at right (robot-arm Task Specifier, pink specified-task card, two agent icons, and a column of chat messages).
insights.data: Everything is real example content: the human idea and specified task are quoted sentences in cards, roles are written out (Python Programmer, Stock Trader), and the dialogue column shows actual instruction and solution messages including pip commands and import lines.
insights.emphasis: Colour is tied to role throughout: orange for the AI User's name, icon and instruction messages, blue for the AI Assistant's name, icon and solution messages, green for the human idea, pink for the specified task.
insights.flow: Left to right: a curved arrow from the idea card to the Task Specifier, down to the specified task, then a branching curve to both agents, who exchange via a vertical double arrow; the transcript reads top-to-bottom alternating orange/blue, ending in a vertical ellipsis.
insights.avoid: The transcript column is set in very small text that is unreadable at print size, and the two panel titles sit at different places (top of the left panel, bottom of the right).

core.what: a left-to-right hand-off from a narrow 'Human Input' panel (idea card, role assignment) into a wide 'Role Playing Session' panel where a Task Specifier turns the idea into a specified-task card that two agents then discuss in a column of alternating chat messages

relations.form: curved arrow from the green idea card to the robot-arm Task Specifier, a short down arrow to the pink Specified Task card, then a forked arrow to the two agent icons
the AI User (orange robot) and AI Assistant (blue robot) are stacked with a double-headed vertical arrow between them
the dialogue is a right-hand column of alternating orange Instruction and blue Solution message cards, ending in a vertical ellipsis

channels.colour: role colour: orange = AI User (name, icon, instruction messages), blue = AI Assistant (name, icon, solution messages), green = human idea, pink = specified task, beige = role assignment
channels.shape: icons for actors (person, robot arm, two robots), rounded text cards for content
channels.line: solid black arrows only
channels.frame: two grey rounded panels = the human side and the agent session

quality.strengths: Colour carries one meaning, the role, from the role-assignment card through the agent icons to every chat message, so the column of messages can be read as a turn-taking dialogue without labels; all content is real quoted text (idea, task, pip commands).
quality.weaknesses: The chat column takes a third of the width with small dense text that the reader need not read, while the two agents sit as small icons; the link from agents to messages is implied by colour only, with no arrow from either icon to the column; the human-input panel spends half its height on a person icon.

figures.lesson: Give each role-playing agent a signature colour on its icon and name, then stack the dialogue as alternating message cards filled in the speaker's colour so turn-taking is visible at a glance.

figures.title: A Deep Cascade of Convolutional Neural Networks for Dynamic MR Image Reconstruction

taxonomy.task: dynamic/static MRI reconstruction from undersampled k-space
taxonomy.note: paradigm = Deep Cascade of CNNs (Schlemper et al.), the paper itself

arrangement.units: the cascade chain of plain rectangles at bottom; two zoom-detail units above it, framed by heavy-outlined tinted rectangles
arrangement.inputs_as: plain text boxes 'Input' at the chain start and 'k-space samples' at bottom-left feeding a bus line
arrangement.shared: one k-space bus feeds every DC block; CNN and DC blocks are repeated copies detailed once

insights.structure: One horizontal chain at the bottom (Input -> CNN1 -> DC -> CNN2 -> DC -> ... -> CNN_nc -> DC -> Output) with two square-cornered detail panels above it: a CNN-block detail at top-left and a data-consistency detail at top-right.
insights.data: Data are only math labels: x_u, x_cnn, x_rec, y for measured k-space; the CNN detail shows an optional dashed DS box, conv layers C1 ... C_rec and a residual ⊕; the DC detail shows F -> f_dc -> F^H with y entering from below.
insights.emphasis: Tint matching ties boxes to details: CNN boxes and the CNN panel share a faint lavender fill, DC boxes and the DC panel a faint green; detail panels have a heavier outline than the chain.
insights.flow: Strictly left to right along the chain; a 'k-space samples' bus line runs under the chain and rises into every DC box; dashed trapezoid lines open from CNN1 and the last DC up to their detail panels.
insights.avoid: No images of the undersampled input or reconstruction appear, so the k-space-vs-image alternation is only in symbols; the CNN zoom lines are long and shallow so the link from CNN1 to its panel is easy to miss.

core.what: one horizontal chain unrolls the cascade as alternating CNN_i and DC boxes (Input -> CNN1 -> DC -> CNN2 -> DC -> ... -> CNN_nc -> DC -> Output), each DC fed from below by a shared 'k-space samples' bus

relations.form: two full CNN/DC pairs then an ellipsis and a final pair along one row, the repeated unit drawn with the same box shapes and tints each time

two detail panels above the chain, tied by dashed trapezoid lines and matching tint: the CNN block (dashed optional DS, conv layers C1..C_rec, residual ⊕) at top-left from CNN1, the DC block (F -> f_dc -> F^H with y from below) at top-right from the last DC
a 'k-space samples' box at bottom-left feeds a bus line under the chain that rises vertically into every DC box

channels.colour: faint lavender = CNN block (chain boxes and its detail panel), faint green = data-consistency block (chain boxes and its detail panel); white = input/output
channels.shape: all plain rectangles; ⊕ circle for the residual add
channels.line: solid arrows = data flow; dashed box = optional layer (DS); dashed straight lines = zoom callouts — dashes carry two meanings
channels.frame: heavy-outlined tinted panels = opened details

quality.strengths: The cascade is drawn as an unrolled row with both repeated blocks opened once above it and tied by tint and callout lines, so the overview stays compact and each unit is taught once; the measured k-space enters each DC from one bus rather than separate wires; all lines are straight and orthogonal.
quality.weaknesses: Nothing is drawn as data: images and k-space are only symbols (x_u, x_cnn, y), so the reader never sees an undersampled image or a mask; dashes mean both 'optional layer' and 'zoom callout'; the CNN detail's output (x_cnn1) and the DC detail's input (x_cnn_i) use different indices.

figures.lesson: The measured k-space samples run as one horizontal bus beneath the cascade with a vertical tap into every DC block, so the repeated data consistency reads as one shared input rather than many separate arrows.

figures.title: Crystal Diffusion Variational Autoencoder for Periodic Material Generation

taxonomy.task: periodic material (crystal) generation

arrangement.units: three unenclosed horizontal rows (denoising training, property prediction, generation) branching from one latent; only the property row has a grey dashed rounded box
arrangement.inputs_as: a dashed unit-cell square with coloured atoms labelled M = (A, X, L)
arrangement.losses_at: right end of the top two rows (L_Dec, L_Agg)
arrangement.shared: the latent z feeds all three rows; PGNN_Dec(M|z) appears in both the training and generation rows

insights.structure: Input crystal at left -> encoder -> a vertical latent bar z in the middle, from which three rows run right: top a noise-and-denoise row ending in L_Dec, middle a grey dashed box of predicted properties ending in L_Agg, bottom a Langevin-dynamics generation row.
insights.data: Every material is a dashed black square unit cell holding red and teal atom discs; the latent is a vertical strip of grey cells; the predicted composition, lattice and number of atoms are drawn as atom discs with 0.5, an empty dashed square and the number 4 joined by plus signs.
insights.emphasis: Arrow colour separates the two phases (black training, blue generation) explained by a two-entry legend; the generation row shows shrinking intermediate cells to convey iterative Langevin refinement.
insights.flow: Left to right from input to z, then fanning right into three parallel rows; a dashed 'Add noises' line loops over the top from the input to the noisy cell; a blue 'Rand. init.' arrow drops from the property box into the generation row.
insights.avoid: The legend is squeezed directly under the input cell and the long dashed noise arrow over the top crosses above everything; the rows have no enclosure, so training and generation rows are separated only by arrow colour.

core.what: one vertical latent bar z in the middle feeds three rows that fan to the right: a noise-and-denoise row ending in L_Dec (top), a predicted-properties row ending in L_Agg (middle) and a Langevin-dynamics generation row (bottom)

relations.form: the latent z is a single tall cell strip from which three horizontal arrows leave, one per row ('Conditional' twice, 'Predict' once)
input crystal M at the left -> 'Encode' arrow labelled PGNN_Enc(M) -> z
every crystal is drawn as a dashed square unit cell holding red and teal atom discs; predicted composition, lattice and atom count are drawn as discs with 0.5, an empty dashed square and the number 4
the generation row shows a randomly initialised cell, two smaller intermediate cells under 'Langevin dynamics', and a final cell, joined by blue arrows
training and generation paths share the layout and are told apart by arrow colour (black training, blue generation) with a two-entry legend at bottom-left

channels.colour: arrow colour = phase (black = training, blue = generation, keyed); atom disc colour = element type
channels.shape: dashed squares = unit cells (crystal data), grey cell strip = latent
channels.line: solid = data flow; dashed black arrow = the noise-adding path; dashed outlines also draw unit cells and the grey predicted-properties box — dashes carry three meanings
channels.frame: a grey dashed box groups the predicted properties

quality.strengths: Crystals are drawn as toy unit cells with atoms at every stage, so noising, denoising and Langevin refinement act visibly on the structure; one latent bar feeding three rows shows the shared representation by geometry; phase is one colour channel with a legend.
quality.weaknesses: Dashed lines mean unit-cell border, noise path and property group at once; network names and formulas (PGNN_Dec(M̃|z), MLP_Agg(z), M̃ = (Ã, X̃, L)) are typeset on arrows; the noise path loops up and over from the input to the top row instead of starting at the row.

figures.lesson: Draw the crystal as one reusable glyph — a dashed unit-cell square with a few two-colour atom discs — and repeat it for every state (input, noised, denoised, random start, mid-Langevin, generated), colouring arrows black for training and blue for generation with a two-line legend.

figures.title: Center-based 3D Object Detection and Tracking

taxonomy.task: lidar 3D object detection and tracking

arrangement.units: four unframed data stages, each captioned (a)-(d) at the bottom, separated by tall rounded network pills
arrangement.inputs_as: a real top-down lidar point-cloud render
arrangement.losses_at: none; outputs (score and 3D box) at the right edge
arrangement.shared: coloured feature cells in the map-view grid reused as the second-stage feature stacks

insights.structure: Four data stages left to right, captioned (a)-(d) along the bottom (point cloud, map-view features, first stage, second stage), separated by tall narrow blue-outlined rounded pills ('3D Backbone', 'Head', 'MLP').
insights.data: The input is a real top-down lidar render in magenta; map-view features are a grid of grey 3-D cubes with a few coloured cells; first-stage outputs are blue box outlines with red centre dots over a faded point cloud; second-stage features are a stack of coloured cubes feeding MLPs that output 'score 0.765' and a 3D box.

insights.flow: Left to right through the pills; the two heavy arcs run backwards from the second-stage stacks over the top and under the bottom into the map-view grid.
insights.avoid: The two backward arcs are the heaviest marks in the figure and dominate the forward pipeline; the caption '(a) Point. cloud' has a stray period.

core.what: four data states captioned (a)-(d) left to right (point cloud, map-view feature grid, first-stage centres and boxes, second-stage feature stacks with scores), separated by tall narrow blue-outlined pills for the modules (3D Backbone, Head, MLP)

relations.form: each stage is drawn as its data (a magenta lidar render, a grid of grey 3-D cells, box outlines over a faded point cloud, coloured feature stacks), the modules only thin pills between them
first-stage detections are drawn on the point cloud as blue box outlines with dark-red centre dots, and grey arrows lead to enlarged copies with coloured dots at each face centre

two heavy dark curved arrows run back from the second-stage feature stacks over and under the Head and first stage to coloured cells in the map-view grid, the cell colours matching the face-centre dots and the stacked features
the second stage is drawn twice, one MLP row per detected object, each ending in a score (0.765, 0.436) and a box outline

channels.colour: magenta = raw points; the five accent colours (orange, dark red, green, purple, olive) = individual sampled points, matched across face-centre dots, grid cells and feature stacks; blue = both module pill outlines and predicted 3D box outlines (two meanings)
channels.shape: tall rounded pills = network modules, 3-D cubes = feature cells, rectangles = boxes
channels.line: heavy dark arcs = feature gathering from the map; thin grey arrows = zoom from a box to its sample points
channels.frame: no frames; stages are set off by the module pills and bottom captions

quality.strengths: Every stage is drawn as its real data rather than a box, and the method's point (detect centres, then sample features at box-face centres) is visible as coloured dots that reappear as coloured grid cells and feature stacks; module pills are kept thin so the data takes the space.
quality.weaknesses: The two heavy backward arcs sweep across the Head and the whole first stage, the longest and darkest lines in the figure for a side step; blue marks both modules and predicted boxes; the grid's selected cells do not visibly correspond to locations on the point cloud.

figures.lesson: Colour the BEV feature cells that are sampled for each box and repeat those colours on the box-edge points and on the stacked per-box features, with thick dark curved arrows reaching back from the second stage to the grid.

figures.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models

taxonomy.task: few-shot reasoning by prompting an LLM
taxonomy.note: family other = LLM prompting / in-context reasoning (no agent loop or environment); nearest family is llm-agent (Tree of Thoughts, Self-Refine)

arrangement.units: two columns (standard vs chain-of-thought), each holding an outlined rounded Model Input box above an outlined rounded Model Output box, tagged by coloured pills
arrangement.inputs_as: quoted few-shot prompt text (Q:/A: exemplars and the test question)
arrangement.shared: the same question text is repeated verbatim in both columns

insights.structure: Two equal columns, standard prompting left and chain-of-thought right, each a tall Model Input box over a short Model Output box, so the comparison is a strict before/after pair.
insights.data: Inputs and outputs are drawn as the literal Q:/A: prompt text (the tennis-ball and cafeteria-apples problems), not as abstract boxes, with a red cross after the wrong answer and a green check after the right one.
insights.emphasis: Only the inserted reasoning sentences carry colour, as blue (exemplar) and green (generated) highlighter backgrounds in the right column, matching the blue Model Input and green Model Output pill tags.
insights.flow: Read left column then right column, each top to bottom from input to output; there are no arrows, the vertical stacking alone implies input-then-output.

core.what: two equal columns, Standard Prompting left and Chain-of-Thought Prompting right, each a tall Model Input box over a short Model Output box holding the same literal Q/A text, the only difference being the highlighted reasoning sentences in the right column

relations.form: identical column layouts side by side under bold titles, prior method left, proposed method right, with the inserted reasoning sentences the only highlighted text
within each column input above output, implied by vertical stacking and the 'Model Input' / 'Model Output' pill tags, with no arrows

channels.colour: blue = the input side (Model Input tag and the highlighted exemplar reasoning), green = the output side (Model Output tag and the highlighted generated reasoning) and also the correct-answer check, with a red cross for the wrong answer — green carries both 'output' and 'correct'
channels.shape: rounded text boxes with pill tags; a cross and a check as verdict glyphs
channels.frame: each input or output is one rounded box

quality.strengths: The comparison is drawn as two identical columns so the reader's eye goes straight to the only difference, the highlighted reasoning text; inputs and outputs are the literal prompt and completion, not abstract boxes; there are no lines to follow.
quality.weaknesses: Most of the area is the repeated question text, identical in both columns; green means both 'model output' and 'correct' while blue/green highlighting is keyed only implicitly through the pill tags; the model itself is not drawn, so where the exemplar enters is left to the Q/A format.

figures.lesson: When the method is a change to text, show the same prompt twice side by side and mark only the inserted words with a highlighter background in the colour of the box tag they belong to.

figures.title: ChatDev: Communicative Agents for Software Development

taxonomy.task: role-playing LLM agents developing software through a phased chat chain

arrangement.units: five rows labelled at the left margin and split by dashed rules (phases, subtasks, instructor, chat chain, assistant), crossed by columns aligned to each subtask through dotted vertical guides
arrangement.inputs_as: the brace placeholder {task} at the start of the chat chain
arrangement.shared: the same agent role (CTO, Programmer) is redrawn as an identical sprite in every column where it acts

insights.structure: Five labelled rows stacked top to bottom (Phases, Subtasks, Instructor, Chat Chain, Assistant), with dotted vertical guides tying each phase box to the subtask and agent columns under it.
insights.data: Artefacts passed between steps are written as brace placeholders on the chain ({task}, {ideas}, {code}) rather than drawn, and agents are pixel-art people captioned by role.
insights.emphasis: Colour is reserved for the agent sprites; the chain of solid arrows and loop glyphs in the middle row, with sprites above and below each loop, makes the instructor-assistant dialogue per subtask the figure's centre.
insights.flow: Everything reads left to right: hollow block arrows step through phases and subtasks in the top rows, and solid arrows run along the chat chain, with short vertical lines connecting each loop node up to its instructor and down to its assistant.
insights.avoid: Row labels (Instructor, Chat Chain, Assistant) are bold and larger than the content, and the Design phase box is the same width as its single subtask, so the phase-to-subtask nesting is only shown by faint dotted guides.

core.what: a chat chain runs left to right through loop nodes, each node joined by short vertical lines to an instructor sprite above and an assistant sprite below, with the passed artefacts written between nodes as brace placeholders ({task}, {ideas}, {code})

relations.form: middle row: '{task}' -> loop glyph -> '{ideas}' -> loop glyph -> '{code}' ... solid arrows on one horizontal line

two top rows split by dashed horizontal rules: three phase boxes (Design, Coding, Testing) whose widths span the subtask boxes beneath them, with dotted vertical guides dropping from each box edge down to the agent columns
each loop node has one instructor sprite directly above and one assistant sprite directly below, captioned by role (CEO/CTO, CTO/Programmer, Reviewer/Programmer, Tester/Programmer)
the dialogue inside each subtask is a circular-arrow loop glyph on the chain

channels.colour: colour appears only in the pixel-art sprites, where it marks individual agents (the same CTO or Programmer sprite recurs); boxes and arrows are black and white
channels.shape: rectangles = phases and rounded rectangles = subtasks; loop glyph = multi-turn chat; sprites = agents
channels.line: hollow block arrows = phase/subtask order; thin solid arrows = artefact flow on the chain; short solid verticals = agent participation; dotted verticals = column guides
channels.frame: dashed horizontal rules separate the labelled rows

quality.strengths: Hierarchy is drawn by width: phase boxes span exactly the subtasks they contain and dotted guides carry that span down to the agents, so phase -> subtask -> dialogue aligns in columns; the instructor/assistant pairing is fixed by position above and below each loop.
quality.weaknesses: Artefacts are only brace words on the chain, never drawn as documents or code; a bold row-label column at the left takes about a sixth of the width; the loop glyph is tiny for the one mechanism the method adds, while the sprites dominate the area.

figures.lesson: Draw a multi-agent workflow as row lanes (phase, subtask, instructor, chain, assistant) so each chat step reads as one column: who instructs above, who answers below, and the artefact passed along on the chain.

figures.title: Illuminating protein space with a programmable generative model

taxonomy.task: programmable protein structure generation
taxonomy.note: 'other' architecture = equivariant geometry solver that turns predicted inter-residue geometries into coordinates; diffusion is a polymer-structured diffusion

arrangement.units: three unframed panels lettered a, b, c; (a) top full-width, (b) and (c) side by side below, with a grey wedge linking a to b
arrangement.inputs_as: a rendered collapsed-polymer bead model labelled x1
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; training direction shown only by the backward arrow in (a)
arrangement.shared: region colouring of the protein is constant across every snapshot in (a) and (b)

insights.structure: Three lettered unframed panels: a full-width row (a) of seven protein snapshots from collapsed polymer x1 to backbone x0 plus an all-atom complex with framed zoom, then below (b) a single denoising step on the left two-thirds and (c) the conditioning math on the right.
insights.data: Structures are rendered space-filling bead models coloured by chain region (blue, green, purple, magenta, red, yellow) consistently across snapshots; intermediate geometry in (b) is a faded copy with small three-colour axis triads at circled residues; conditions in (c) are small flat icons (symmetry pinwheel, helix, rabbit shape, CATH tiles).
insights.emphasis: Networks are never boxes: the two learned parts are triple-arrow transitions labelled 'Random Graph Neural Network' and 'Equivariant Geometry Solver', so the structures carry the figure.
insights.flow: Left to right across (a) under two opposed full-width arrows (Generation reverse diffusion → / ← Training forward diffusion); a grey translucent wedge zooms from x_t in (a) down into panel (b); in (c) prior and conditioner gradient terms combine with a '+' and a down arrow to the posterior.
insights.avoid: Seven near-identical blob renders take much of the width while the method steps in (b) get small text; the photo-like renders make the figure heavy and hard to reproduce as vector art.

core.what: panel (a) is a full-width row of rendered protein snapshots from a collapsed polymer x1 to a backbone x0 under two opposed arrows (Generation: reverse polymer diffusion, Training: forward), so the diffusion is shown acting on the protein itself

relations.form: seven space-filling snapshots unroll the diffusion trajectory left to right between x1 and x0, the chain colours kept the same in every snapshot
training and generation are two opposed full-width arrows over the same snapshot row, labelled in italics
after x0 a 'Design Network' arrow leads to an all-atom complex rendering at the top right

a grey wedge opens from the x_t -> x0 dash-dot arrow in (a) down into panel (b), which draws one denoising step: noisy structure -> Random Graph Neural Network -> faded structure with circled residues and arrows between them -> Equivariant Geometry Solver -> predicted denoised structure; a framed close-up of the all-atom complex is tied to it by a grey wedge
in (b) the predicted inter-residue geometries are drawn on a faded copy of the protein as circled residues joined by grey lines, each with a small three-colour axis triad

panel (c): a time-dependent prior plus time-dependent conditioners (symmetry, substructure, shape and semantics icons) join by a '+' and a down arrow into the time-dependent posterior, all written as gradient terms

channels.colour: on structures, colour = position along the chains (blue, cyan, green, purple, magenta, red, yellow), consistent across snapshots; pink/blue/green = the axes of each residue frame triad; condition icons in (c) carry their own unrelated colours
channels.shape: rendered molecules for data; networks are never boxes, only labelled triple arrows; small flat icons = condition types
channels.line: solid arrows = process direction; a dash-dot arrow marks the x_t -> x0 jump that (b) expands; grey wedges = zoom
channels.frame: only the all-atom close-up is framed; panels are lettered, not boxed

quality.strengths: Every state is the protein rendered at that step, so the reader sees collapse-to-fold without reading a block diagram; panel (b) expands one step of (a) through a wedge from the x_t -> x0 arrow, and the learned modules are kept to arrow labels so the structures get the space.
quality.weaknesses: Panel (c) is three typeset gradient formulas with an icon list, the one part drawn as notation rather than structure; the row's chain colouring is never keyed; the two opposed arrows in (a) stretch across the whole width above the snapshots and the dash-dot x_t -> x0 arrow sits apart from them.

figures.lesson: Draw generation and training as one row of structure snapshots under two opposed full-width arrows, then zoom one snapshot with a translucent wedge into a lower panel showing a single denoising step, with the intermediate geometry (residue frames) overlaid on a faded copy of the structure.

figures.title: Chronos: Learning the Language of Time Series

taxonomy.task: probabilistic time-series forecasting with a language model
taxonomy.note: Chronos tokenizes scaled, quantized values and trains an off-the-shelf LM (T5 family) with cross-entropy over bins.

arrangement.units: three unframed columns separated by full-height thin vertical rules, each titled in large bold text at its top
arrangement.inputs_as: a raw blue line plot ('Historical Time Series') at top-left; the other columns start from the context-token row at their top
arrangement.losses_at: the cross-entropy is a dotted vertical link labelled 'cross entropy' between the predicted-probability histogram and a pink 'Next Token ID' cell at the bottom of the Training column
arrangement.shared: the context-token row and the language-model box are redrawn identically in Training and Inference

insights.structure: Three stage columns separated by thin vertical rules and titled in bold at the top (Time Series Tokenization, Training, Inference); Training and Inference share an identical skeleton of context-token row -> pink 'Time Series Language Model' box -> output box.
insights.data: The input is a blue line plot, quantization is drawn as small squares on the curve dropping grey leaders onto a tick-marked number line, tokens are blue cells with integer IDs (2400, 2142 ...) in a light-blue rounded bar, predicted probabilities are a purple histogram on the number line, and the forecast is a red line with a shaded uncertainty band.
insights.emphasis: Colour carries the role: blue = observed context tokens, pink/red = model and predicted/sampled tokens and forecast; the same numbered token row reappears in all three columns so tokenization visibly feeds training and inference.
insights.flow: Each column reads top to bottom with straight vertical arrows; columns read left to right; step names (Mean Scaling, Quantization, Dequantization and Unscaling) are rotated purple labels on each column's left edge.
insights.avoid: The many grey quantization leaders from curve squares to the number line cross each other and are hard to follow; the token row is drawn three times identically, spending space.

core.what: three columns separated by thin vertical rules and titled Time Series Tokenization, Training and Inference, each read top to bottom, the last two sharing one skeleton (context-token row -> pink Time Series Language Model box -> output)

relations.form: three titled columns left to right; the token row produced at the bottom of the first column reappears at the top of the second and third
quantization drawn on the series itself: small squares on the mean-scaled curve drop grey leader lines onto a tick-marked number line, which then becomes a row of numbered blue token cells

Training and Inference columns are the same layout, differing only in the output: a purple histogram with a cross-entropy line to a red 'Next Token ID' cell versus a row of sampled red tokens dequantised into a red forecast line with a shaded band

within each column a single vertical arrow chain, with the operation names (Mean Scaling, Quantization, Predicted Probabilities, Dequantization and Unscaling) as rotated purple labels on the left margin

channels.colour: blue = observed data (input series and context tokens); pink/red = model-produced (model box, predicted next token, sampled tokens, forecast) — pink fills both the model and its outputs; purple = probability histogram, model name text and operation labels
channels.shape: square cells with integer IDs = tokens, rounded light bar = token sequence, large rounded box = the model, line plots and histogram for data
channels.line: solid dark arrows = flow; thin grey leaders = value-to-bin mapping; a dashed vertical line labelled cross entropy = the loss
channels.frame: rounded bars group token rows; thin vertical rules separate the stages

quality.strengths: Tokenization is drawn on the data (curve -> leaders -> number line -> numbered cells), so the core idea needs no text; training and inference are identical columns so the only difference (loss vs sampling) stands out; the same numbered token row repeated across columns ties the stages.
quality.weaknesses: Pink/red marks both the model box and the predicted/sampled tokens and forecast; operation names are rotated small purple labels on the margins rather than on the arrows they describe; the model, the routine part, is one of the largest boxes in each column.

figures.lesson: Keep one colour for observed context (blue curve, blue tokens) and one for predictions (pink tokens, red forecast curve with an uncertainty band), and print each token's actual integer ID inside its square so the quantization is concrete.

figures.title: Large-scale Contrastive Language-Audio Pretraining with Feature Fusion and Keyword-to-Caption Augmentation

taxonomy.task: language-audio contrastive pretraining with feature fusion for variable-length audio and keyword-to-caption augmentation; zero-shot and supervised audio classification

arrangement.units: three panels stacked top to bottom, separated by dashed horizontal rules: pretraining (audio column with a beige dashed 'Audio Encoder' frame, text column, similarity matrix at bottom-right), zero-shot classification, supervised classification, each lower panel titled at its top
arrangement.inputs_as: a short and a long waveform image under 'Audio Waveforms'; white 'Captions' and 'Labels' boxes under 'Text Data'; symbolic inputs (Audio X^a, classes {C_1..C_M}) in the lower panels
arrangement.losses_at: the contrastive objective is the similarity matrix at the bottom-right of the top panel, entered by the audio MLP's arrow from the left and the text MLP from above
arrangement.shared: Audio Encoder, Text Encoder and MLP reappear in the lower panels as small boxes with the same fills

insights.structure: Audio tower on the left and text tower on the right descend to a similarity matrix at bottom-right; two thin downstream panels under dashed rules reuse the same encoder and MLP boxes.
insights.data: Audio is drawn as waveform images, the long clip split into three coloured-frame 10-sec chunks plus a grey downsampled clip; embeddings are labelled E_i^a (rows) and E_j^t (columns) on the matrix.
insights.emphasis: Nothing is marked as new; the fusion branch is the only audio path with extra blocks, and the matrix's pink diagonal is the only saturated pattern.
insights.flow: Each tower reads downward on short vertical arrows; the audio MLP's arrow runs right into the matrix rows while the text MLP sits directly above its columns.
insights.avoid: Blue fill mixes the new blocks with routine ones (Conv2D, Projection Layers), and the short branch's Conv2D output takes a long L-shaped wire down to Other Encoder Layers.

core.what: audio tower and text tower meet at a square similarity matrix: the audio MLP's arrow enters the rows E^a from the left, the text MLP sits above the columns E^t, positive pairs as pink diagonal cells marked 1

relations.form: a similarity matrix at bottom-right, rows = audio embeddings entered from the left, columns = text embeddings from above, pink '1' cells on the diagonal
the long waveform image is cut into three colour-framed 10-sec chunks and a grey downsampled clip, each chunk tied to its span by a matching-colour dashed line
inside the dashed Audio Encoder frame the long-audio branch stacks Mel-FilterBank, Conv2D, Merge Conv2D, Attention Feature Fusion, and the short branch's line joins it at Other Encoder Layers
the original Captions and the augmented Captions (Labels through Keyword-to-Caption Augmentation) converge by elbow lines on one Text Encoder
pretraining panel on top, then zero-shot and supervised classification as compact one-row panels below dashed rules, reusing the encoder and orange MLP boxes

channels.colour: module fill by kind, mostly: orange = MLP projection (same in every panel), grey = fixed preprocessing, lavender = remaining encoder layers, cream = encoders in the lower panels, but blue covers both the new fusion/augmentation blocks and routine Conv2D/Projection Layers; frame colours on the audio chunks (purple, blue, red, grey) mark which span of the long clip a chunk is - a second meaning; pink = positive pair in the matrix
channels.shape: rectangles = modules, white boxes = text data, framed waveform images = audio data, grid = similarity matrix
channels.line: solid arrows = data flow; coloured dashed lines = chunk-to-source correspondence; a hooked line labelled 'match' in the zero-shot panel; a brace marks the finetuned span
channels.frame: beige dashed frame = the Audio Encoder unit; full-width dashed rules = panel boundaries

quality.strengths: The two towers face each other across a CLIP-style matrix with labelled rows and columns, so what is compared is drawn; variable-length handling is drawn on real waveform images with colour-matched chunks; the orange MLP vocabulary is taught once and reused compactly in the downstream panels.
quality.weaknesses: Blue fill does not separate the new blocks from routine ones; the short branch's Conv2D output detours down a long L-shaped wire; the zero-shot 'match' is a hooked line rather than the two embeddings facing each other; the text column joins its two caption sources by elbows.

figures.lesson: Show variable-length handling on the data itself: cut the long waveform into colour-framed chunks tied to their source spans by matching-colour dashed lines, beside the short clip's repeat-and-pad branch.

figures.title: ClimaX: A foundation model for weather and climate

taxonomy.task: weather/climate variable aggregation across channels
taxonomy.note: Crop shows only the variable-grouping / cross-variable aggregation detail; training is not depicted (ClimaX pretrains by forecasting).

arrangement.units: one strip; sub-groups are variable groups marked by brackets below, not frames
arrangement.inputs_as: real colormapped field patches
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: One horizontal strip of field-map patches grouped per variable (T2m, U500, Q850), each group closed by a square bracket labelled underneath, with ellipses between patches and between groups.
insights.data: Each patch is a small red-blue colormapped field tile (real data), with a p x p size annotation on the first tile.
insights.emphasis: Coloured arcs (blue, green, purple) arch over the strip connecting the patch at the same spatial position in every variable group, so the cross-variable link is the only coloured element.
insights.flow: Left to right along the strip; arcs run over the top, one hue per patch position, without arrowheads.
insights.avoid: Arcs overlap and cross each other between groups and have no arrowheads or target, so what the aggregation produces is not shown; the figure is unreadable without its caption.

core.what: one horizontal strip of field-map patches grouped per variable (T2m, U500, Q850, closed by brackets underneath), with one coloured arc per patch position arching over the strip to join the patch at that position in every variable group

relations.form: the data are drawn as real red-blue colormapped field patches, the first one annotated p x p, with ellipses between patches and between groups
three arcs (blue, green, purple) each link the same-position patch across the variable groups, without arrowheads or a target node

channels.colour: arc colour = patch position (blue first, green second, purple last); red-blue in the tiles is the field colormap
channels.shape: square tiles = patches; brackets = variable groups
channels.line: solid curved arcs = cross-variable correspondence
channels.frame: square brackets under each group name the variable

quality.strengths: Patches are real field tiles and the variable groups are named by brackets, and colour is used for one thing only (which spatial position an arc links).
quality.weaknesses: The arcs overlap and cross between groups and end on no node, so what the aggregation produces is not drawn; the long arcs span the whole width; without the caption the reader cannot tell that the arcs mean grouping by location rather than a sequence.

figures.lesson: Show aggregation across variables at one location by drawing one coloured arc per patch position that links the matching patches in every variable group, with the groups named by brackets underneath.

figures.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision

taxonomy.task: image-text contrastive pretraining and zero-shot classification

arrangement.units: Three numbered panels separated only by whitespace and a '(1) …' heading: (1) training fills the left half; (2) and (3) stack in the right half. Inside (1) the text encoder sits ABOVE the image encoder, both at the left; their outputs become a row of T cells along the top of an N x N matrix and a column of I cells along its left side.
arrangement.inputs_as: a stack of real photos and a stack of typed caption cards, each with offset copies behind (a batch)
arrangement.losses_at: the objective is the matrix itself, at the right end of panel (1); positives tinted on its diagonal
arrangement.shared: panel (3) redraws the image encoder and reuses panel (2)'s T row rather than linking across panels

insights.structure: Three numbered unframed panels: (1) contrastive pre-training fills the left half with the text encoder stacked above the image encoder; (2) classifier-from-label-text and (3) zero-shot prediction stack in the right half and share one T1..TN embedding row.
insights.data: Inputs are a stacked deck of real dog photos and a stacked caption card in monospace ('Pepper the aussie pup'); embeddings are lilac T cells across the top and green I cells down the left of an N x N grid of I_i·T_j dot products.
insights.emphasis: Only the diagonal cells of the matrix (and the chosen I1·T3 cell in panel 3) are tinted blue, so the positive pairs / prediction pop out; encoder colour (lilac text, green image) is kept consistent across all panels.
insights.flow: Left to right with orthogonal bus lines fanning from each encoder to its embedding cells; panel (2) flows into (3) top to bottom via the shared T row.
insights.avoid: Panels have no frames and (2)/(3) share space tightly, so where panel (2) ends is ambiguous; the ellipsis cells pad the matrix but carry no information.

core.what: panel (1): text encoder above and image encoder below emit a purple row of T1..TN across the top and a green column of I1..IN down the left of an N x N matrix of I_i·T_j dot products whose diagonal cells are blue

relations.form: the matrix sits where the T row and the I column meet, so every cell is visibly one image paired with one text, positives on the blue diagonal
in each panel: data (a stacked caption card / stacked photos / label words) -> trapezoid encoder -> fan of arrows into a row or column of embedding tiles
three numbered panels: (1) contrastive pre-training on the left half, (2) classifier from label text at top-right and (3) zero-shot prediction at bottom-right
the trained encoders reappear in panels (2) and (3) with the same shapes and fills, and the T1..TN row produced in (2) sits directly above the I1·T_j row of (3) that uses it
in (3) one image embedding I1 is scored against all class embeddings; the highest cell (I1·T3) is blue and drops to the output text 'A photo of a dog.'

channels.colour: purple = text side (encoder and T tiles, class words in the prompt), green = image side (encoder and I tiles), blue = the matched pair (diagonal in (1), chosen class in (3))
channels.shape: trapezoids = encoders, square tiles = embeddings, grid = similarity matrix, monospace text cards = text data, photos = image data
channels.line: solid grey arrows with right-angle fans, all data flow
channels.frame: no frames; panels are numbered titles

quality.strengths: The pairing is geometry: embeddings border the matrix from two sides so each cell is a pair, with the positives on a coloured diagonal; colour has one meaning per hue (text, image, match) carried across all three panels; the compared representations are drawn as tiles between encoders and matrix; inputs are real photos and real captions.
quality.weaknesses: The fan arrows into the T row and I column are long right-angle rakes that add ink without information; in (2)-(3) the class embedding row from the upper panel is stacked over the score row of the lower panel, which reads as one block although it crosses the panel boundary.

figures.lesson: Drawing the batch objective as an N x N grid whose header row and column are the two encoders' coloured embedding cells, with only the diagonal tinted, makes the contrastive pairing readable without any equation.

figures.title: CoCa: Contrastive Captioners are Image-Text Foundation Models

taxonomy.task: image-text foundation model pretraining (contrastive + captioning)

arrangement.units: The model at the left, then an arrow to three panels separated by thin vertical rules, one per use of the model (single encoder, dual encoder, encoder-decoder), each with its own caption below.
arrangement.inputs_as: the words 'image' and 'text' under each tower
arrangement.losses_at: each loss named in colour next to the block it trains (contrastive loss between the towers, captioning loss above the decoder)
arrangement.shared: each panel redraws the towers it uses at the same size

insights.structure: The CoCa model at left (image encoder and unimodal text decoder side by side, multimodal text decoder above), then a hollow arrow to three panels separated by thin vertical rules, one per downstream use (single-encoder, dual-encoder, encoder-decoder).
insights.data: Inputs and outputs are plain words ('image', 'text', 'classification', 'alignment', 'image captioning & multimodal representation') at the bottom and top of each tower; modules are flat rounded rectangles.
insights.emphasis: Loss names are coloured with the hue of the module they train (orange 'Contrastive Loss' beside peach encoders, blue 'Captioning Loss' over the blue decoder); a coloured 'CoCa' wordmark tags the model.
insights.flow: Bottom to top within each tower; left to right across the model and the three use-case panels; a curved 'Cross-Attention' arrow arcs from image encoder into the decoder.
insights.avoid: The model panel has no frame or caption like the three right panels, and the wordmark logo adds branding rather than information.

core.what: the CoCa model on the left, then a hollow block arrow to three panels separated by thin vertical rules, each redrawing a subset of CoCa's blocks to show the single-encoder, dual-encoder and encoder-decoder models it subsumes

relations.form: three panels in a row, each built from the same block shapes and fills: image encoder alone (classification), image encoder + unimodal text decoder (alignment arc between them), and both plus the multimodal text decoder on top

in the CoCa panel one image encoder and one unimodal text decoder feed both objectives: the 'Contrastive Loss' label sits between them and the multimodal decoder stacked on the text decoder carries 'Captioning Loss' above it
a curved arrow labelled 'Cross-Attention' runs from the image encoder's top into the side of the multimodal text decoder
bottom-to-top inside each panel: 'image' / 'text' words -> encoders -> output label

channels.colour: orange = unimodal blocks (image encoder, unimodal text decoder) and the contrastive-loss label; blue = the multimodal text decoder and the captioning-loss label — colour marks the objective a part serves
channels.shape: every module is the same rounded rectangle; inputs and outputs are plain words
channels.line: straight arrows = data flow; curved arrows = cross-attention or alignment between towers; one hollow block arrow = 'specialises into'
channels.frame: no frames; thin vertical rules separate the three variant panels

quality.strengths: Reusing the same block shapes and two fills in every panel lets the three prior model families read as subsets of CoCa; the multimodal decoder is the only blue block, so the added part stands out.
quality.weaknesses: Neither objective is drawn: 'Contrastive Loss' is floating text between two blocks and no embeddings are shown, so what is compared is hidden; inputs are the words 'image' and 'text' rather than data; the coloured CoCa wordmark takes a corner of the main panel.

figures.lesson: Colour each loss name with the hue of the module it trains (orange 'Contrastive Loss' beside the peach encoders, blue 'Captioning Loss' over the blue decoder), so objectives attach to modules without extra lines or a legend.

figures.title: CogAgent: A Visual Language Model for GUI Agents

taxonomy.task: GUI-agent vision-language model: a light high-resolution image branch added to a VLM through per-layer cross-attention

arrangement.units: two vertical lanes side by side, each a dashed rounded frame: left the high-resolution cross-module (encoder plus stacked cross-attention layers), right the original VLM (low-resolution encoder, adapter, word embedding, decoder)
arrangement.inputs_as: a real 1120x1120 web screenshot, its 224x224 downsampled copy, and a quoted Task / Plan / Action text
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; a '[Target Text]' label sits at the top-right corner of the decoder lane
