core.what: three dashed-outline panels left to right, CNN-encoder -> DeTrans-encoder -> Decoder, with multi-scale CNN features flattened, merged by braces into a row of yellow DeTrans Layer columns, then split and reshaped into the decoder

relations.form: CT volume at bottom-left -> a stack of grey CNN feature bars -> flatten (F) and add positional encoding -> yellow DeTrans layers -> reshape (R) -> grey decoder bars -> segmented CT volume at bottom-right
thin lines open from one DeTrans Layer down into a yellow inset 'Deformable Transformer Layer' (MS-DMSA stack, Layer Norm, Feed Forward, Layer Norm, with blue reference points)

three feature scales each pass an F node and a ⊕ where vertical lines from the noise-textured positional-encoding sheets enter from below; braces then gather the three token bars into the transformer and fan them out again
input and output are tilted CT slices, the output overlaid with coloured organ masks

channels.colour: yellow = the deformable transformer contribution (layers and inset); grey = CNN feature maps and decoder features; light green = callout outlines naming operations (Flatten, Reshape, Positional encoding) and also the Layer Norm boxes; inside the inset orange = MS-DMSA, bright blue = feed forward and reference points; organ colours on the output
channels.shape: grey bars = feature maps, thin vertical bars = flattened token sequences, tall yellow columns = transformer layers, lettered circles = flatten/reshape, ⊕ = addition, speech bubbles = operation names
channels.line: solid arrows for all flow; curly braces merge and split the token sequences
channels.frame: dashed rounded frames = the three network parts; a solid yellow frame = the zoomed layer

quality.strengths: The new part (the deformable transformer) is the only saturated region and is opened once in an inset tied to one layer; real CT input and a coloured segmentation output bracket the flow; multi-scale tokens are drawn as separate bars entering and leaving the transformer.
quality.weaknesses: CNN and decoder blocks are unlabelled grey bars, so resolutions and stages are left to the caption; light green marks both callout bubbles and Layer Norm boxes; three operations are named in speech bubbles stuck onto the lines; the positional-encoding lines rise a long way through the panel to their ⊕ nodes.

figures.lesson: Conversion steps between the two model families (Flatten, Reshape) are tiny lettered circles on the arrows, each named once by a speech-bubble tag, so the interface is visible without adding boxes to the pipeline.

figures.title: CoTracker: It is Better to Track Together

taxonomy.task: long-term point tracking of many points jointly across video frames
taxonomy.note: family other: point tracking in video (PIPs / TAP line), not covered by the family list

arrangement.units: unframed left column (initialized tracks, loop step, estimated tracks) and one large light-grey rounded panel holding the opened update, each tensor on its own darker grey plate
arrangement.inputs_as: four tilted real video frames with coloured track dots joined by black dotted lines; inside the panel the update's inputs are ball-grid and cell-grid tensors plus false-colour feature maps along the top
arrangement.shared: no shared module; the same three track colours recur on frames, coordinate tensors and output

insights.structure: A narrow left column shows the whole loop (initialized tracks -> iterative updates 1..M -> estimated tracks); its loop step opens via dotted leader lines into a large grey panel that runs one update: top row of inputs and feature maps -> correlation features -> stacked tokens -> transformer -> output.
insights.data: Tracks are drawn as data throughout: coloured dots on real frames, then rows of same-coloured balls (T,N,2) for coordinates, white cell grids (T,N,d) for features and dark-grey grids for correlations, each with a shape label beside it.
insights.emphasis: The opened update fills most of the figure; inside it the transformer is marked only by a framed title, a small token grid with dotted attention arrows and a 'x6' loop, smaller than the stacks of input tensors around it.
insights.flow: The column reads top to bottom with hollow arrows; the panel reads along its top row, down through hollow arrows to the correlation box and the token stack, then left to right through the transformer to the output; the x6 loop is a thin return line beneath the transformer.
insights.avoid: The output (delta P-hat, delta Q) does not visibly return to the panel's input, so the m -> m+1 loop is only implied by labels; dotted lines mean track trajectory, zoom leader and attention direction at once.

core.what: one iterative update opened from the left column's loop step into a large panel - inputs P-hat(m), Q(m) and windowed feature maps -> correlation features -> stacked update tokens -> transformer (x6) -> delta P-hat, delta Q - between 'initialized tracks' above and 'estimated tracks' below in the column

relations.form: two grey dotted leader lines fan out from the circular-arrow step in the left column to the corners of the large grey rounded panel holding the opened update
inside the panel: top row of inputs, a hollow arrow down to the correlation-features box, down again to the stacked tokens, then hollow arrows right to the transformer and right to the output

correlation drawn on the feature maps: white window squares (2 Delta + 1) centred on each track's coloured dot on the false-colour phi(I_t) slabs; attention drawn as dotted vertical and horizontal arrows across a small token grid inside the transformer box
four token tensors (P-hat difference, v-hat, C, Q) stacked with offsets under one square bracket feed a single hollow arrow into the transformer

channels.colour: hue = track identity (magenta, yellow-green, teal) on frame dots, coordinate balls and output balls; grey value = tensor kind (white cells = features Q, dark grey = correlations C), but light grey also fills the zoom panel and the per-tensor plates; false colour = image features phi
channels.shape: ball = coordinate, square cell = feature vector, tilted slab = frame or feature map, outlined rectangle = operation, hollow block arrow = stage-to-stage flow
channels.line: black dotted = track trajectory across frames and attention direction inside the transformer; grey dotted = zoom leaders; thin solid = the x6 loop - dotted lines carry three meanings
channels.frame: large rounded light-grey panel = the opened update; darker rounded plate = one tensor; square bracket = the update's token inputs

quality.strengths: Track colour is held from video dots to coordinate balls to output balls; every intermediate tensor is drawn as a grid with its shape label between its maker and its consumer; correlation is drawn on the feature maps as windows around each point; the opened update gets most of the space while the overall loop stays a compact column.
quality.weaknesses: The transformer - where tracks attend to each other, the paper's point - is a small box beside larger input stacks; the m -> m+1 loop is not closed geometrically (the output does not return to the input); dotted lines mean trajectory, zoom and attention at once; the correlation shape tuple is typeset as long text inside its box.

figures.lesson: Give each track one hue and keep it on every drawing of that track - the dots on the video frames, the ball rows of the coordinate tensors and the output - so the reader follows the same points from frames into tensors without a legend.

figures.title: Convolutional Recurrent Neural Networks for Dynamic MR Image Reconstruction

taxonomy.task: dynamic (cine) MRI reconstruction
taxonomy.note: paradigm: cascaded CNN with data consistency (Schlemper DC-CNN); MoDL is the closest listed unrolled paradigm.

arrangement.units: three grey-outlined panels labelled (a)-(c): (a) tall on the left, (b) and (c) stacked on the right, linked by hollow block arrows
arrangement.inputs_as: tilted real MRI thumbnail (undersampled image) and k-space sample thumbnail
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; DC boxes sit at the top of (a) and (b)
arrangement.shared: the same layer stack (BCRNN-t-i, CRNN-i x3, CNN) appears compact in (a) and unrolled in (b)

insights.structure: Three grey-outlined panels: tall (a) CRNN-MRI on the left with a dashed CRNN sub-box of stacked layers; (b) top right unrolls over iterations as a grid of hidden-state circles (rows = layers, columns = iterations); (c) bottom right unrolls the recurrent layer over time.
insights.data: k-space samples and the image are small real 3D-tilted MRI thumbnails; hidden states are labelled circles H_l^(i); math labels x_rec^(i), x_u in serif bold.
insights.emphasis: Two big hollow block arrows labelled 'Unfolding (iteration)' (blue) and 'Unfolding (time)' (red) link (a) to (b) and (c); arrow colour (green W_l, blue W_i, orange W_t) is bound to one weight type in every panel.
insights.flow: Bottom to top within each panel with feedback lines on the left; left to right from compact to unrolled views.
insights.avoid: Panel (c) has many crossing coloured curves between circles that are hard to trace; legends are repeated in three places.

core.what: the CRNN-MRI block in (a) is unrolled twice: a blue 'Unfolding (iteration)' block arrow leads to (b), a grid of hidden-state circles with layers as rows and iterations as columns, and a red 'Unfolding (time)' block arrow leads to (c), one recurrent layer unrolled over time frames

relations.form: (b) three columns of H_l^(i) circles (iterations 1, 2, N) with blue arrows along each layer row from one iteration to the next and DC boxes on top of each column
two hollow block arrows from panel (a) to panels (b) and (c), each panel framed in grey
(a) bottom to top: undersampled image x_rec^(i-1) -> dashed CRNN stack (BCRNN-t-i, three CRNN-i, CNN) -> ⊕ with a residual line -> DC with k-space samples entering from the left -> x_rec^(i)
the k-space samples thumbnail feeds the DC block by an arrow labelled Ω; residual lines from the input loop round the stack into the ⊕
(c) draws forward and backward hidden states for frames t-1, t, t+1 receiving curved arrows from the previous iteration's states and the layer below

channels.colour: arrow colour = weight type, keyed and used in every panel (green feed-forward W_l, blue recurrent over iterations W_i, orange recurrent over time W_t); block-arrow colour and fills match it: blue = iteration (Unfolding (iteration) arrow, CRNN-i blocks and states), orange/red = time (Unfolding (time) arrow, the BCRNN-t-i block and its states)
channels.shape: rectangles = layers and DC, circles = hidden states, ⊕ = residual add, MRI and k-space thumbnails = data
channels.line: solid coloured arrows = connections by weight type; dark grey lines = residual and data-consistency wiring
channels.frame: grey frames = the three panels; a dashed blue box = the CRNN sub-network

quality.strengths: Colour is bound to one meaning across all three panels (weight type, which also marks iteration vs time recurrence), keyed in a legend; the two kinds of recurrence get their own unrolled panels tied to the block by matching-colour block arrows; data appear as real k-space and image thumbnails.
quality.weaknesses: Panel (c) is a tangle of crossing curved green, blue and orange arrows that is hard to trace; in (b) the dark lines from each column's output wander over to the next column's ⊕ with several bends; the legend in (a)'s corner and the separate W legends in (b) and (c) repeat the same key three times.

figures.lesson: Two big hollow arrows labelled by the axis they unroll (iteration, time) lead from the compact network to two unrolled panels, and arrow colour (green, blue, orange) stays bound to one weight type in every panel.

figures.title: CSDI: Conditional Score-based Diffusion Models for Probabilistic Time Series Imputation

taxonomy.task: probabilistic time-series imputation
taxonomy.note: architecture: conditional reverse-diffusion chain drawn as a Markov chain of states.

arrangement.units: one chain of state circles with a thumbnail box under each
arrangement.inputs_as: line-plot thumbnails: random noise at bottom-left, conditional observations at top-left
arrangement.shared: conditional observations shared by every denoising step via one top bus

insights.structure: A horizontal Markov chain of circled states x_T^ta ... x_t^ta -> x_{t-1}^ta ... x_0^ta, with a conditional-observation box at the top left feeding every step through a horizontal bus.
insights.data: Each state has a dotted-border thumbnail of two series (blue and red) below it: observed parts dashed, imputation targets solid, going from noisy jagged segments to smooth ones; the conditional observations are solid lines with gaps.
insights.emphasis: The reverse transition p_theta(x_{t-1}^ta | x_t^ta, x_0^co) is written above the central arrow, and the thumbnails show targets visibly denoising left to right.
insights.flow: Left to right along the chain; the condition bus runs right along the top and drops vertical arrows into each step.
insights.avoid: The condition bus's down-arrows land between and on states inconsistently; thumbnails are low-contrast with tiny dashed lines.

core.what: the reverse diffusion drawn as one left-to-right chain of circled states x_T^ta ... x_t^ta -> x_{t-1}^ta ... x_0^ta, with ellipsis arrows standing in for the hidden steps

relations.form: five circled state nodes on one horizontal axis, the step x_t -> x_{t-1} drawn as the one long arrow labelled with the reverse transition p_theta(x_{t-1}^ta | x_t^ta, x_0^co)
the conditional-observation thumbnail at top left feeds a single horizontal bus along the top that drops five vertical arrows down onto the chain
a dotted-border two-series time-series thumbnail under each state shows the imputation targets (solid segments) going from jagged noise to smooth inside the dashed observed curves

channels.colour: blue and red = the two series of the multivariate time series, identical in every thumbnail; no colour for roles or modules
channels.shape: circle = a diffusion state; dotted rectangle = a data thumbnail
channels.line: in thumbnails, dashed = observed values and solid = imputation targets; in the diagram, solid arrows for both the chain and the condition bus
channels.frame: a dotted rectangle frames each data sample (conditional observations, and the target at each step)

quality.strengths: The data is drawn as data: every state has its own time-series thumbnail, so the denoising of the target segments is visible left to right; the condition shared by all steps is one bus rather than five separate wires.
quality.weaknesses: The bus's down-arrows land inconsistently (two into the ellipsis gaps, one onto x_{t-1}, one beside it); the thumbnails sit under some states and not under the ellipses, so the state-to-thumbnail mapping is loose; the dashed-vs-solid distinction in the thumbnails is thin and low-contrast; the reverse transition is a typeset formula floating above the arrow.

figures.lesson: Under each diffusion-chain node, draw the same series with the observed parts dashed and faint and only the missing span solid, so the denoising of the imputed values reads across the row of thumbnails.

figures.title: Multi-Concept Customization of Text-to-Image Diffusion

taxonomy.task: customising a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model to new concepts by fine-tuning only cross-attention key/value weights and a new token, regularised with retrieved real images

arrangement.units: two titled halves without frames: a 2x2 photo-pair grid with rotated row labels (training data), and a grey rounded U-Net container with token row, text transformer and key (fine-tuning)
arrangement.inputs_as: real photos with monospace captions in a grid; in the fine-tuning half a noisy photo x_t at the left and a tokenised prompt 'photo of a V* dog' at the top
arrangement.losses_at: no objective is drawn; the denoising target is implied by the x_t to x_{t-1} photos on either side of the U-Net
arrangement.shared: the Text transformer's output reaches every Attention block's KV box by elbow arrows from one bar

insights.structure: A data half and a model half sit side by side under large titles; inside the model half the U-Net is a grey container of ResNet and Attention blocks with an ellipsis for depth.
insights.data: Training data are real photo pairs with monospace captions, split into new-concept and retrieved rows; the prompt is a row of rotated word tokens; the denoising step is a noisy and a cleaner photo on either side of the U-Net.
insights.emphasis: One keyed tan fill marks every trained part (KV boxes and the V* token), against pale blue-grey for everything frozen.
insights.flow: Text goes down from the token row through the Text transformer into each KV box by elbow arrows; the image goes left to right through the U-Net container.
insights.avoid: The data half is not connected to the fine-tuning half by any arrow, and retrieval is shown only as its result (a row of photos), not as a step.

core.what: inside each Attention block of the drawn U-Net, a tan trainable KV box sits on a pale frozen Q box, so which weights are fine-tuned is shown inside the architecture

relations.form: each Attention block is a rounded frame holding a tan KV box over a pale Q box, repeated in two blocks with an ellipsis between
noisy photo x_t at the left of the U-Net container, cleaner photo x_{t-1} at the right, ResNet and Attention blocks between
the tokenised prompt with a tan V* token passes through a Text transformer bar whose output drops by elbow arrows into each KV box
a second photo row 'Retrieved similar images' under the 'New concepts' row, each retrieved photo captioned with its text (Dog, Cute dog, Wisdom moon, Gated entry)
each new-concept photo pair sits directly above its retrieved pair in the same column (V* dog over Dog/Cute dog, Moongate over Wisdom moon/Gated entry)

channels.colour: tan = trainable, pale blue-grey = frozen (keyed at top-right); one meaning, applied to both weights and the V* token
channels.shape: rounded rectangles = modules, small vertical rounded rectangles = tokens, bordered photos = data
channels.line: solid arrows = text conditioning into KV; no other line types
channels.frame: grey rounded container = the U-Net; rounded frame = one Attention block

quality.strengths: Which weights are trained is drawn inside the block (KV tan, Q frozen) with one keyed colour that also marks the new token; data are real captioned photos, with new concepts directly above their retrieved counterparts; the denoising step is shown as photos on either side of the U-Net.
quality.weaknesses: Nothing connects the data half to the fine-tuning half, and retrieval appears only as its output; the elbow arrows from the Text transformer to the far KV box run across the top of the U-Net; the regularisation role of the retrieved row is left to the caption.

figures.lesson: Show which weights are trained by drawing them inside their block (a tan KV box stacked on a frozen Q box) and give the new token the same trainable fill, so one keyed colour tells the whole fine-tuning story.

figures.title: Putting the Object Back into Video Object Segmentation

taxonomy.task: semi-supervised video object segmentation
taxonomy.note: family other: memory-based video object segmentation (XMem line) with object queries; not covered by the family list

arrangement.units: unframed overview along the top; a large rounded light-blue panel below holding the l-th object transformer block, joined to the overview's object-transformer box by a same-tint funnel
arrangement.inputs_as: real video frames: one query frame and a fanned stack of memory frames with coloured object masks
arrangement.shared: object queries X and object memory S are summed at a circled plus at the block's left edge; positional-embedding circles are reused at every attention input

insights.structure: The overview runs left to right along the top (frames -> encoders -> memories and queries -> object transformer -> readout -> decoder -> mask), and the object transformer is opened below as a two-line block: a green pixel line along the top and a blue query line along the bottom, exchanging through masked cross-attention and cross-attention.
insights.data: Input and output are real frames (the output with a blue mask), and the stores show their contents as glyphs - coloured slabs for pixel memory, pentagons for object memory, hexagons for object queries - with shape labels such as F: T x H x W x C.
insights.emphasis: The object transformer is the darkest box and the only one expanded; its block detail takes the lower half of the figure.
insights.flow: Overview arrows are thin dark orthogonal lines with several right-angle bends into the object transformer; in the detail the green R line runs straight across the top and the blue X line across the bottom, with vertical taps between them.
insights.avoid: Orange / peach marks both the object memory (overview) and every attention unit (detail), and the V-branch lines in the block split and bend around boxes.

core.what: the dark-blue Object transformer box in the overview flows down through a light-blue tinted funnel into a large same-tint panel that details one block

relations.form: pixel memory (green) and object memory (orange) are stacked boxes beside the main flow, their contents drawn as slab and pentagon glyphs, read by the object transformer through right-angle lines
the overview's top row left to right: query frame -> query encoder -> pixel readout -> object transformer -> object readout, then down through the decoder to the masked output frame

inside the block the pixel feature R runs as a green line along the top and the object queries X as a blue line along the bottom, both left to right, exchanging through attention units placed between them

object queries X and object memory S meet at a circled plus at the block's left edge; in the overview pixel readout, pixel memory, object queries and object memory all converge on the object transformer

channels.colour: green = pixel-level (pixel readout, pixel memory, Pixel FFN, the R line); blue = object-level (object queries, object transformer, object readout, Query FFN, the X line); orange = object memory in the overview, but peach / orange also fills every attention unit in the block (two meanings); yellow / peach trapezoids = encoders and decoder
channels.shape: trapezoid = encoder / decoder; rounded rectangle = representation or module; hexagon = object-query token; pentagon = object-memory token; small circle = positional embedding; circled plus = addition
channels.line: in the block: green line = pixel features, blue line = object queries; in the overview: dark grey lines = data flow; Q / K / V letters label attention inputs
channels.frame: light-blue tinted panel plus funnel = the opened object-transformer block; grey box = legend

quality.strengths: The pixel vs object distinction is one colour code used in both overview and detail (green R line, blue X line), so the block reads from the overview; the memories show their contents as glyphs; the new module is the darkest box and the only one opened, tied to its detail by a tinted funnel; real frames in and a masked frame out.
quality.weaknesses: Orange / peach means object memory above and attention unit below; overview lines from pixel readout and object memory bend twice to reach the object transformer; inside the block the V branches split and bend around boxes; the legend sits inside the panel among content.

figures.lesson: Open the one new module into a panel joined to it by a tinted funnel of the panel's colour, and keep the overview's colour code (green = pixel-level, blue = object-level) on the detail's two lines so R and X are recognised inside the block.

figures.title: Unpaired Image-to-Image Translation using Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Networks

taxonomy.task: unpaired image-to-image translation

arrangement.units: three panels side by side behind dashed vertical rules; (b) and (c) are mirror images
arrangement.inputs_as: a domain square or sample at the left of each panel
arrangement.losses_at: each cycle-consistency loss inside its own panel, labelled with a dotted leader
arrangement.shared: the mappings G and F are redrawn in each panel

insights.structure: Three panels (a), (b), (c) separated by dashed vertical rules: (a) domains X and Y linked by mappings G and F with discriminators above; (b) forward cycle x -> Y_hat -> x_hat; (c) backward cycle mirroring (b).
insights.data: Domains are large squares with italic math letters; samples are blue and red dots inside domain squares; discriminators D_X, D_Y sit above with dotted up-arrows.
insights.emphasis: The cycle-consistency loss is a brace between the original and reconstructed dot with a dotted leader to the label, inside each cycle panel.
insights.flow: Left to right; curved arrows for mappings (G over the top, F underneath) and curved arcs between dots in the domain squares.
insights.avoid: Purely abstract: no example images, so the reader must already know what domains mean; monochrome styling gives no colour distinction between G and F.

core.what: the two domains X and Y face each other with the mappings G (arc over the top) and F (arc underneath) between them, and each cycle panel ends with the original and reconstructed sample paired by a cycle-consistency brace

relations.form: domain squares X and Y side by side in panel (a), linked by a top arc G and a bottom arc F; in (b)/(c) a brace joins the starting dot and its reconstruction inside one domain square
in (b) and (c) a top row x -> Y_hat -> x_hat (and y -> X_hat -> y_hat) runs left to right with curved arrows labelled G and F
three panels separated by dashed vertical rules, (b) forward cycle and (c) backward cycle drawn as mirror images of the same layout
below each cycle row, two domain squares hold coloured sample dots and the round trip is drawn as arcs between the dots

channels.colour: blue dot = a sample from X, red dot = a sample from Y (in panel (b) and (c)); otherwise monochrome, so G and F are told apart only by label
channels.shape: square = a domain or a sample of a domain; dot = an individual sample inside a domain square
channels.line: solid curved arrow = a mapping (G or F); dotted up-arrow = a discriminator reading a domain; thick dotted leader = points from the brace to the cycle-consistency loss label
channels.frame: none beyond the domain squares; panels are split by thin dashed rules

quality.strengths: Position carries the method: the two domains face each other with the two mappings as opposite arcs, and the cycle loss is drawn as a brace between the original dot and its reconstruction, so what is compared is visible as geometry; (b) and (c) are exact mirrors.
quality.weaknesses: No real images, so the domain abstraction must be known in advance; the brace in (b) is on X's left while in (c) it is on Y's right, which suits the mirror but separates the two loss labels to the outer edges; G and F share one line style and colour.

figures.lesson: Give each loss its own panel of the same structure, so the reader compares the panels instead of untangling one diagram.

figures.title: Controlling Vision-Language Models for Multi-Task Image Restoration

taxonomy.task: multi-task image restoration steered by degradation embeddings from a controlled CLIP

arrangement.units: unframed training panel (left, about two thirds of the width) and an unframed usage panel (right) holding a small dashed-framed DA-CLIP unit; a dashed legend strip spans the bottom
arrangement.inputs_as: quoted text cards ('snowy', 'seagull sitting on a post') and a real degraded photo at the left of the training panel; the usage panel takes a real LQ photo from its top right and puts the restored HQ photo below
arrangement.losses_at: one grey 'Contrastive Learning' bar in the middle of the training panel, between the text-side embeddings above and the image-side embeddings below
arrangement.shared: the image encoder appears in both panels; in the training panel the controller receives a 'copy' of it and sends 'control' back, drawn as two short vertical arrows

insights.structure: Text encoder over image encoder over controller form a left column; their four embedding bars sit to the right in a two-by-two block (text row above, image row below) around one Contrastive Learning bar; the deployed model sits in a separate right panel.
insights.data: Inputs are drawn as data (a stacked degradation word card, a stacked caption card, a real snowy photo), and every embedding is a stacked bar named with a symbol (e_c^T, e_d^T, e_c^I, e_d^I) that the bottom legend spells out.
insights.emphasis: The trainable controller is the only yellow module and the only red open padlock among the encoders; purple dashed gradient-flow arrows run only into the controller.
insights.flow: Thin black orthogonal arrows run left to right from inputs to encoders to embeddings and up or down into the objective; the gradient-flow arrows are dashed purple and run back along the bottom and up the encoder column; the right panel reads top to bottom from LQ to HQ.
insights.avoid: The degradation embedding e_d^I is wired to the controller by a long dashed gradient line that runs along the bottom of the panel, and the right panel repeats the encoder and controller at a much smaller scale without a visible link to the left one.

core.what: two text-side embeddings (caption e_c^T, degradation e_d^T) above and two image-side embeddings (content e_c^I, degradation e_d^I) below face each other across one grey Contrastive Learning bar

relations.form: the two contrastive pairs stand as two columns, each a purple text bar over a green or yellow image bar, with the shared objective bar running between the rows
one Contrastive Learning bar spans both pairs, with an arrow down from each text bar and up from each image bar
the controller sits directly under the image encoder; a 'copy' arrow runs down and a 'control' arrow runs up between them, both short and vertical
training on the left, deployment on the right: the trained DA-CLIP is redrawn small and its two embeddings enter the red restoration block from the left as 'Cross Attention' and 'Prompt'
in the right panel the green content embedding and the yellow degradation embedding converge on the red diffusion block from its left side by two short curved arrows

channels.colour: purple = text-side (text encoder and its embeddings), green = image encoder and its content embedding, yellow = controller and its degradation embedding, red = the downstream restoration model; padlock colour = frozen (blue closed) vs trainable (red open); purple is also used for the dashed gradient-flow arrows, a second meaning for that hue
channels.shape: trapezoid = encoder or controller, flat stacked bar = embedding, stacked card = text input, photo = image input, pill = objective, rounded rectangle = restoration model
channels.line: solid black = forward data flow; dashed purple = gradient flow (training only)
channels.frame: dashed light-blue rounded frame = one pretrained model (Pretrained CLIP, DA-CLIP); dashed grey = objective and legend

quality.strengths: Each embedding is drawn as a coloured bar between the encoder that makes it and the contrastive bar that compares it, so what is compared with what is visible from position and colour; frozen vs trainable is carried by one icon channel (padlock colour) rather than fill; the gradient-flow line style marks training-only paths; inputs are real data (a word card, a caption, a degraded photo).
quality.weaknesses: Purple marks both the text side and the gradient-flow arrows; the long dashed gradient line from e_d^I runs along the bottom and turns up into the controller; the deployment panel redraws DA-CLIP at about a quarter of the size with no tie to the training panel beyond the shared colours; the 'degradation type' output of the text encoder runs as a long elbow over the caption wire to reach e_d^T.

figures.lesson: Colour each embedding bar with the colour of the module that makes it and stack the text-side bar over the image-side bar with one objective bar between them, so the two contrastive pairs read by position and colour before any label.

figures.title: DAB-DETR: Dynamic Anchor Boxes are Better Queries for DETR

taxonomy.task: object detection with anchor-box queries
taxonomy.note: training not depicted; DETR-style Hungarian matching.

arrangement.units: one dashed rounded frame for the repeated layer (Nx), inputs outside it
arrangement.inputs_as: coloured labelled boxes outside the frame at bottom and left (features, embeddings, anchor boxes)
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: One large dashed rounded frame marked 'Nx' holding one decoder layer as a bottom-to-top stack (self-attention, add & norm, modulated cross-attention, add & norm, FFN, add & norm, output), with an anchor-box branch (sine encodings, MLPs, New Anchor boxes) on the right.

figures.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models

taxonomy.task: unconditional image generation

arrangement.units: no enclosed regions; one row of nodes
arrangement.inputs_as: a grey node x_T with a pure-noise thumbnail below it

a small image thumbnail at the lower right of x_T, x_{t-1} and x_0 shows the sample going from pure noise to a face

channels.line: solid arrow = the learned reverse process p_theta; dashed curved arrow = the fixed forward noising q
channels.frame: none

figures.title: Is Conditional Generative Modeling all you need for Decision-Making?

three condition chips in a row along the top, only 'returns' in full contrast

channels.colour: blue = known history tokens (darker for states, lighter for actions); pale-blue mosaic = noisy future states; orange = state diffusion module and its title word, pink/red = inverse dynamics and its output arrow

quality.strengths: The method is drawn as what happens to the trajectory itself: the same token row repeated with slots filling in, so a reader sees future states appear after diffusion and a_t appear after inverse dynamics; the diffusion bar spans exactly the tokens it reads and writes, and the module names are coloured to match their boxes.
quality.weaknesses: The noisy-state mosaic in row 1 is tiny and faint, so the noise-to-sample idea is easy to miss; blue carries both 'known history' and the input arrows into modules; the return-conditioning arrow bends down the left margin rather than entering from above.

figures.lesson: Draw the same token row once per stage and change only each token's box treatment (filled for known, dashed for unknown, noise texture for being denoised, pale fill for just generated), so the stack shows the process without step labels.

figures.title: Deep Image Prior

arrangement.units: One unframed composition of three identical rows (one per iteration), separated by whitespace, with the shared inputs at the top corners.

channels.line: colour and dotting together: dotted grey = constant input, solid coloured = computation; one meaning per style
channels.frame: none; rows are separated by whitespace only

quality.strengths: Iteration is drawn as unrolled identical rows, which is derive.md's prescribed form; the representation being optimised (the generated image) is drawn as a real picture between its maker theta and the energy that compares it to x_0; colour carries one meaning (role) throughout.
quality.weaknesses: Grey dotted lines from z and x_0 run long distances along both outer edges and cross under each row, competing with the main zigzag; energy and gradient boxes carry typeset formulas rather than names.

insights.avoid: Panels have no frames and the panel B curves are loosely placed with ellipses (vertical dots) for 'more samples', so B reads as a sketch next to the tidy block diagrams.

core.what: panels C and D draw the stacked and unstacked DeepONet as the same branch/trunk skeleton side by side, differing only in p stacked branch nets vs one branch net fanning out to p outputs

relations.form: C and D side by side with identical trunk halves and identical product node, the left showing Branch net_1 ... Branch net_p stacked and the right one Branch net with arrows fanning to b_1 ... b_p
a framed column of branch outputs b_1..b_p and a framed column of trunk outputs t_1..t_p converge on one circled-x node producing G(u)(y)
branch path (u sampled at sensors) in the upper half and trunk path (y) in the lower half of each panel, both running left to right
panel B draws the training data as dashed function curves with sensor dots x_1..x_m on the left and output curves with random locations y on the right, joined by an arrow G

channels.line: solid arrows = data flow; dashed curves in B = functions, not flow
channels.frame: a tall rectangle groups each output column (b's, t's) and the sensor-value list; panels A-D have letters but no frames

quality.strengths: The two architectures are drawn as matched panels with the same glyphs, so the single difference (branch stacking) is the visible difference; the branch and trunk outputs are drawn as named representations b_k and t_k between their networks and the product that combines them; lavender means 'learned network' everywhere.
quality.weaknesses: Panel B's curves and vertical ellipses are loosely placed and read as a sketch next to the tidy block diagrams; panel A repeats the problem statement with an opaque 'Network' box; the outputs from the b and t columns leave from the column edge as long diagonals to the product node.

figures.lesson: State the problem as a single black-box panel first, then redraw that box as the proposed two-network decomposition in the panels below, using the same fill for every learned network so the reader maps the black box onto its parts.

figures.title: DeepSeekMoE: Towards Ultimate Expert Specialization in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models

taxonomy.task: MoE layer design for language models

arrangement.units: Three unframed panels divided by dashed vertical lines, each a complete MoE layer, captioned (a)/(b)/(c) beneath and linked by arrows.
arrangement.inputs_as: a two-circle 'Input Hidden' box
arrangement.shared: identical input/router/output skeleton repeated in all three panels so only the expert row changes

insights.structure: Three panels separated by dashed vertical rules show the same MoE layer evolving: (a) conventional top-2 routing over N experts, (b) the experts split into 2N finer ones, (c) one expert isolated as shared; panel titles below are chained by thick black arrows.
insights.data: Hidden states are two-circle boxes (Input Hidden, Output Hidden), experts are numbered rounded rectangles, and the router's scores are a tiny yellow bar chart labelled K = 2 / 4 / 3.

insights.flow: Bottom to top in each panel: input to router, solid black lines to selected experts, yellow dashed curves carry gate weights to circled-x multipliers, then a circled-plus sums into the output; panels read left to right as an ablation progression.
insights.avoid: The many crossing yellow dashed gate curves in (b) and (c) tangle with the black routing lines; route gate weights more simply if copying.

core.what: three MoE layers side by side, each a router at the bottom, a row of experts, and a weighted sum at top, evolving left to right from conventional top-2 routing to fine-grained experts to an isolated shared expert, the panel titles chained by thick arrows

relations.form: three panels separated by dashed vertical rules with the same bottom-to-top skeleton (Input Hidden -> Router -> expert row -> circled-x gates -> circled-plus -> Output Hidden), the proposed DeepSeekMoE last
the panel captions (a) -> (b) -> (c) are joined by thick black arrows, so each panel adds one change to the previous
selected experts' outputs are each gated by a circled-x and converge on one circled-plus node under Output Hidden
in (c) the green expert 1 takes its own solid line straight from Input Hidden, bypassing the router, and feeds the sum without a gate

channels.colour: keyed: light blue = routed expert, green = shared expert; yellow = router and its gate-score histogram and the dashed gate-weight curves
channels.shape: rounded rectangle = expert or router; double circle box = hidden vector; circled x = gating multiply; circled plus = sum; bar glyph = router scores with K
channels.line: solid black = token/hidden flow; dashed yellow curves = gate weights from the router scores to each selected expert's multiply
channels.frame: dashed vertical rules split the panels; the legend has its own dashed rounded frame

quality.strengths: The variants are identical skeletons so each change is the visible difference (expert count doubles in (b), one expert turns green and bypasses the router in (c)); the shared-expert idea is drawn as geometry (its own line from the input) as well as colour; the router scores are drawn as a small histogram with K beside the router.
quality.weaknesses: The dashed yellow gate-weight curves in (b) and (c) loop over and through the expert row and tangle with black routing lines, a side signal drawn as long wires; experts in (b)/(c) shrink to fit, so the panels are not equally dense.

figures.lesson: Build the proposed layer as the last of a row of identical templates, each adding one change, so the reader sees exactly what differs (twice as many narrower experts, then one green always-on expert), and write the number of selected experts K under each router.

figures.title: Deformable DETR: Deformable Transformers for End-to-End Object Detection

arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the output is a photo with coloured bounding boxes above the decoder
arrangement.shared: repeated layers collapsed into a grey dashed box marked x 4 in both encoder and decoder

insights.data: Feature maps are drawn as tilted, faded copies of the real football photo stacked in threes, with purple triangles as sampled points and purple/red dots as reference points; object queries are small coloured vertical bars.
insights.emphasis: Three dashed-arrow colours, explained in a top-left legend, separate deformable self-attention (purple), deformable cross-attention (red) and plain decoder self-attention (black), so the sparse sampling is the visual signature.
insights.flow: Purple dashed lines run from sampled points on the pyramid up into a reference dot in the encoder; the encoder output is braced and sent right by red dashed lines into every decoder layer, which reads bottom to top to the predictions.
insights.avoid: Dozens of crossing purple dashed lines over the faded photos make the encoder busy; fewer samples would show the mechanism just as well.

core.what: deformable attention drawn on the feature maps themselves: dashed purple arrows run from a handful of sampled points (triangles) on stacked multi-scale feature maps to one query point (dot), so sparse sampling across scales is the visual signature

relations.form: photo-textured feature-map stacks at three scales, with purple triangles marking sampled keys and a purple dot the query they feed; decoder cross-attention samples drawn as red squares on the top stack
left to right: image and its feature pyramid, the encoder frame (stacks bottom to top), then the decoder frame (bottom to top) topped by the bounding-box photo
a grey dashed box marked x4 around the middle encoder stack and around the middle decoder layers marks the repeated layers
a red brace gathers the encoder's top feature maps and red dashed arrows branch into each decoder layer's red query bar

channels.colour: attention type, keyed top left: purple = encoder multi-scale deformable self-attention, red = decoder deformable cross-attention, black = decoder plain self-attention; the decoder bars' red/green/orange identify individual object queries, a second meaning
channels.shape: triangle = sampled key location, dot = query location, red square = cross-attention sample; tilted photo slab = a feature map; vertical bar = an object query
channels.line: dashed arrows = attention (colour-coded type); solid black arrows = data flow up the decoder
channels.frame: large black dashed frames = Encoder and Decoder; grey dashed frame = repeated block (x4)

quality.strengths: The mechanism is drawn on its structure (sampled points on multi-scale maps) and the attention kinds are separated by a keyed colour; encoder and decoder are framed units in reading order with repeated layers boxed x4.
quality.weaknesses: Dozens of crossing purple dashed lines over faded photos make the encoder busy; colour is used for both attention type and per-query identity (red bar vs red cross-attention arrow collide); the red cross-attention arrows run a long way down the gutter between frames; the input image-to-encoder arrows cross diagonally.

figures.lesson: Draw sparse attention by putting the sampling points as small coloured glyphs directly on faded, tilted copies of the input photo at each scale, with dashed arrows from them to the query's reference point.

figures.title: Training data-efficient image transformers & distillation through attention

taxonomy.task: data-efficient image classification via distillation

arrangement.units: One unframed column of stacked layer slabs between two brace-enclosed token rows.

arrangement.losses_at: top corners: L_CE above the class token, L_teacher above the distillation token

insights.structure: A single vertical column: a row of tokens at the bottom, four stacked two-tone layer slabs (blue self-attention under yellow FFN), and the same token row again at the top feeding two loss arrows.
insights.data: Tokens are plain squares in curly braces, with the class token a double circle at the left end and the new distillation token an octagon at the right end, each labelled underneath.

insights.flow: Bottom to top through fat hollow arrows; the two end tokens each go to a big blue upward arrow holding a sigmoid glyph and a loss symbol.
insights.avoid: The teacher network itself is never drawn, so the reader must infer where L_teacher's target comes from.

core.what: class token and distillation token placed at the two mirrored ends of the same token row, each rising to its own loss, L_CE on the left and L_teacher on the right

relations.form: the class token (double circle) at the far left and the distillation token (octagon) at the far right of both the input and output token rows, each ending in its own upward loss arrow
one vertical column bottom to top: input token row, four stacked two-tone layer slabs, output token row, two loss arrows
a bracket of arcs under the input row joins patch tokens with each other and with both special tokens, all entering the same layer stack

channels.colour: blue = self-attention half, yellow = FFN half of each layer slab; light blue fill on the loss arrows

channels.line: hollow block arrows = data flow; thin curved arrows below = token interaction
channels.frame: curly braces enclose each token row

quality.strengths: The new distillation token is distinguished by a unique shape and a mirrored position, and its separate loss sits directly above it, so what is new and what it is trained by is visible from position alone; the layer stack is compact and taught once by its first slab's labels.
quality.weaknesses: The teacher network that supplies L_teacher's target is never drawn, so the compared representation is half missing; the interaction arcs at the bottom are ambiguous about whether they show attention or input; the loss heads carry a sigmoid sketch but no named output.

figures.lesson: Give the added token a distinct glyph at the mirror end of the token row from the class token and send it to its own loss head, so a student's extra distillation input is traceable from input to loss without drawing the teacher.

figures.title: Dense X Retrieval: What Retrieval Granularity Should We Use?

arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the evaluation tasks are panels C and D

panel B: query card and grey corpus cylinder side by side at the top, arrows converging down into one Retriever box, then down to the unit tray

The three granularities are compared as side-by-side stacks of shrinking size in one tray. Panel A, the novelty, is the widest; all arrows are short and straight.

Panel B's proposition stack is grey, not the FactoidWiki pink, so the tie from A to B is carried by labels only.

taxonomy.task: end-to-end object detection

figures.title: Dynamic Graph CNN for Learning on Point Clouds

taxonomy.task: point cloud classification and segmentation

arrangement.units: Two unframed horizontal lanes (classification, segmentation) plus two dotted-border detail insets below the lanes.
arrangement.inputs_as: a grey tensor bar labelled 'point cloud n x 3' with a vertical text label

two insets at the bottom unpack the spatial-transform and EdgeConv blocks, tied to them by matching dotted border colour (red and blue) and grey fill

channels.shape: tall narrow bar with rotated dimension text = a tensor (n x 64, 1024); wide rounded dotted box = an operation block; circled plus = concatenation

figures.title: DiffDock: Diffusion Steps, Twists, and Turns for Molecular Docking

taxonomy.task: molecular docking (ligand pose prediction)

three columns split by vertical rules, headed 'ligand & protein' -> 'DiffDock' -> 'ranked poses & confidence score' with arrows between the headings

figures.title: Diffusion Policy: Visuomotor Policy Learning via Action Diffusion

taxonomy.task: visuomotor policy learning

arrangement.units: Three unframed panels divided by vertical lines, each a policy box (grey rectangle) plus an inset (dashed box of distributions in a, heatmap in b, gradient field in c), captioned below.

channels.colour: blue = action-space content (the a-hat node, the action-representation box, the energy colourmap and gradient arrows); grey = the policy box; black = the target action distribution

quality.weaknesses: Panels have different widths and (a)'s side box has no counterpart in (b)/(c), so the comparison is not fully parallel; dashed lines mean both 'callout' and 'iteration'; policy boxes carry typeset formulas (F_theta(o), argmin E, nabla E(a)) instead of names.
