figures.title: Directional Message Passing for Molecular Graphs

taxonomy.task: molecular property prediction with directional (angle-aware) message passing

arrangement.units: Five regions in a row: an untinted 'Model:' column (basis thumbnails, embedding + 6 interaction boxes, a sum circle), then tinted rectangular panels with bold colon titles: Embedding (green) above Residual (pink), Interaction (blue, widest, with a pale inset for directional message passing), Output (tan).
arrangement.inputs_as: bold italic math symbols (distances, angles, basis vectors, messages) with arrows entering each panel from the top; two small basis-function plots in the Model column
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; the target t leaves the sum circle at the right of the Model column
arrangement.shared: Output and Residual blocks are drawn as small coloured boxes inside other panels and expanded once in their own panel; inputs e_RBF and a_SBF reappear as text labels at the top of each panel rather than linked lines

insights.structure: A narrow model column at the left (basis inputs, embedding, a stack of interaction blocks, a sum) is followed by four colour-tinted detail panels, the Interaction panel the widest and holding a lighter inset for the directional message-passing core.
insights.data: Inputs are bold italic math with superscripts entering from panel tops, plus two small basis-function thumbnails (radial curves, spherical heat-map) feeding the model column; every layer box shows its formula with an empty square as the input slot.
insights.emphasis: The contribution is the only nested inset in the figure, a pale-blue labelled box inside the largest blue panel.
insights.flow: Each panel reads top to bottom with thin orthogonal arrows, while per-block outputs exit right through small tan Output boxes toward the Model column's sum circle.
insights.avoid: The Interaction panel has several long parallel input lines on its left edge running down to its bottom Output box, crossing the inset's border and making it hard to tell which input feeds which operation.

core.what: a narrow overview column on the left (RBF/SBF bases, Embedding, a stack of Interaction blocks, a sum) opened into detail panels tied by matching tint, the blue Interaction panel the widest with a nested pale inset for directional message passing

relations.form: the overview's green Embedding block and blue Interaction blocks are expanded into green and blue panels to the right, and a pink Residual and an orange Output panel unpack the blocks reused inside them
overview column top to bottom: Embedding, six Interaction blocks, each emitting an output to the right into one summation node producing t
in the Interaction panel the incoming message m_kj and the SBF basis are combined through W-projections, an element-wise product and a bilinear layer, summed over k, then added to m_ji
the RBF and SBF bases are drawn as small plots of the radial curves and the spherical pattern at the top of the overview

channels.colour: panel tint = block type, matching the overview: green = Embedding, blue = Interaction, pink = Residual, orange = Output; the pale-blue inset marks the directional message-passing core
channels.shape: white rectangle = a layer (W, sigma(W+b), Embedding); circle = an operation (product, concat, sum, plus)
channels.line: solid arrows only; inputs enter from the panel tops as long vertical lines
channels.frame: tinted panel = one block type; the nested inset = the contribution

quality.strengths: Each block is taught once in its own tinted panel and reused compactly by tint (Residual and Output appear as pink and orange boxes inside other panels); the contribution gets the largest panel and the only nested inset; the bases are drawn as plots.
quality.weaknesses: Several long parallel input lines down the Interaction panel's left edge cross the inset border and run to the bottom Output box, so which input feeds which operation is hard to trace; layers carry formulas (sigma(W□+b), □^T W□) rather than names; the overview's tinted blocks are not linked to the panels by callouts, only by tint.

figures.lesson: Writing each layer as its formula inside the box (sigma(W box + b), with a square as the input slot) lets detail panels show exact computation with no separate equations, and colour-matching each block type between the model stack and its panel removes zoom lines.

figures.title: Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction

taxonomy.task: click-through rate prediction
taxonomy.note: architecture other = target attention: a candidate-ad-conditioned attention pooling over user behaviour embeddings

arrangement.units: Two unframed model panels (Base Model, Deep Interest Network, titled at the bottom) plus a double-bordered inset detailing the Activation Unit.
arrangement.inputs_as: coloured ID circles grouped by feature field (User Profile, User Behaviors Goods 1..N, Candidate Ad, Context)
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; Output box at the top
arrangement.shared: the embedding layer and MLP tower drawn identically in both panels

insights.structure: Base Model on the left and Deep Interest Network in the middle share the same bottom-up skeleton (feature groups -> embeddings -> pooling -> concat -> MLP), with a double-bordered inset at top right expanding the Activation Unit.
insights.data: IDs are coloured circles (orange goods, blue shop, pink category, white other), embeddings are short multi-coloured vertical strips, pooled vectors are horizontal coloured cell bars, and FC layers are grey labelled boxes ('PReLU (200)').
insights.emphasis: DIN's change is the row of double-bordered Activation Unit boxes, each emitting a 'Goods i Weight' into a red X product circle before SUM Pooling, fed by a line from the candidate ad; the rest is identical to the base model so the difference pops.
insights.flow: Bottom to top in both models; the candidate ad embedding runs horizontally under the activation units to every behaviour, and the user-profile/context branches go straight up to Concat & Flatten.
insights.avoid: Small text and a dense tangle of thin grey arrows around the activation units make the middle panel hard to read at column width.

core.what: Base Model on the left and Deep Interest Network in the middle drawn on the same bottom-up skeleton, DIN's only change a row of activation units that weight each user behaviour by the candidate ad before sum pooling

relations.form: two side-by-side bottom-up networks with identical feature groups, embeddings, concat, pooling and MLP layers, the base model left and DIN right, each titled in bold beneath

in DIN a line from the Candidate Ad embedding runs left across the panel into every Activation Unit, each emitting a 'Goods i Weight' into a red X product node with its behaviour embedding before SUM Pooling

a double-bordered inset at top right expands the Activation Unit (inputs from user and ad -> Out Product -> Concat -> PReLU/Dice (36) -> Linear (1) -> Activation Weight), tied by the same double border
bottom to top in each network: ID circles -> embedding bars -> Concat per group -> pooling -> Concat & Flatten -> FC layers -> Output

channels.colour: keyed: orange = goods ID, blue = shop ID, pink = category ID, white = other ID, on the input circles and their embedding bars; grey = FC layer; pink-red circle = product
channels.shape: circle = an ID feature; striped bar = an embedding vector; rounded white box = concat or pooling op; grey box = FC layer; double-bordered box = activation unit
channels.line: grey arrows for data flow, black for the candidate-ad and other feature lines into the activation units and top concat; brace = grouping
channels.frame: double border = activation unit, used in both the DIN panel and the inset

quality.strengths: The base-vs-DIN comparison is drawn as identical skeletons side by side, so the activation-unit row is the visible difference; embeddings are drawn as coloured vector bars at each stage, and the activation unit is taught once in an inset tied by its double border.
quality.weaknesses: Small monospace text and a tangle of thin grey and black arrows around the activation units (the ad line crossing every behaviour group) make DIN's middle hard to read at column width; the inset is not called out from the DIN panel except by border style.

figures.lesson: Draw each input feature field as a coloured ID dot whose colour carries into its embedding cells, so the concatenated vectors further up visibly show which fields they mix and one small legend of dot colours explains the whole input side.

figures.title: Emerging Properties in Self-Supervised Vision Transformers

taxonomy.task: self-supervised visual representation learning

arrangement.units: Two unframed vertical branches (student, teacher) of stacked boxes, side by side.
arrangement.inputs_as: a single circled x splitting into two circled views x1, x2
arrangement.losses_at: top centre, as a text formula between p1 and p2
arrangement.shared: teacher is an EMA of the student, shown by a horizontal 'ema' arrow between the network boxes

insights.structure: Two mirrored vertical branches, student on the left and teacher on the right, rising from a single input x at the bottom centre that splits into two views x1 and x2.
insights.data: Variables (x, x1, x2, p1, p2) are circles, networks are grey-filled boxes (student g_theta_s, teacher g_theta_t), and post-processing steps are white boxes (softmax; centering + softmax on the teacher).
insights.emphasis: Asymmetry between the branches is the point: only the teacher has an extra 'centering' box and a double-slash 'sg' stop-gradient mark, and a horizontal 'ema' arrow runs from student to teacher.
insights.flow: Bottom to top: x splits by two diagonal arrows into the views, each passes up its branch to p1 / p2, and the cross-entropy 'loss: - p2 log p1' is written as text between the two outputs at the top.
insights.avoid: The loss is only floating text with no lines joining p1 and p2, so the comparison point is implied rather than drawn.

core.what: student and teacher drawn as two mirrored vertical branches rising from two views x1 and x2 of one input x, ending in outputs p1 and p2 that the loss text between them compares

relations.form: student branch on the left and teacher branch on the right, each x_i -> network -> softmax -> p_i, with the loss '- p2 log p1' written between the two output circles at the top
one input circle x at the bottom centre with two diagonal arrows up to x1 and x2
a horizontal 'ema' arrow from the student box to the teacher box shows the teacher's weights tracking the student's

channels.colour: grey fill = the networks g_theta (student and teacher); all else white and black
channels.shape: circle = a variable (x, views, outputs); rectangle = an operation (softmax, centering); grey rectangle = a network
channels.line: solid arrows = forward; the double slash 'sg' on the teacher's output = stop-gradient; the ema arrow is a thin grey arrow of the same style as data flow
channels.frame: none

quality.strengths: Mirrored branches make the asymmetry the point: only the teacher has the extra 'centering' box and the stop-gradient mark, so what differs between the sides is visible by position; the outputs p1 and p2 are drawn as named representations; all lines are short and straight.
quality.weaknesses: The loss is floating text with no lines to p1 and p2, so the comparison is implied rather than drawn; the ema update uses the same arrow style as data flow; no data is shown, only the symbol x.

figures.lesson: Draw the two networks as identical grey boxes and mark everything that makes them differ as small inline glyphs on the teacher column (an extra head box, an sg double slash on its output edge, an 'ema' arrow from the student), so the asymmetry is readable without colour.

figures.title: DINO: DETR with Improved DeNoising Anchor Boxes for End-to-End Object Detection

taxonomy.task: object detection (contrastive denoising training)

arrangement.units: one unframed composition: a grey slab between a row of input query cells and a row of output cells, grouped by brackets into two CDN groups; a separate square inset on the right
arrangement.inputs_as: rows of two-part query cells coloured by positive/negative, bracketed and labelled 'positive'/'negative' and 'CDN group0/1'
arrangement.losses_at: grey label boxes on top of each output group ('reconstruction loss', 'no object')
arrangement.shared: one decoder slab shared by both CDN groups

insights.structure: One wide grey 'Decoder Layers x M' slab spans the left of the figure, with a row of query cells below it and a matching row of output cells above it, both split into two 'CDN group' sets of three positive and three negative queries; a separate square inset sits to the right.
insights.data: Each query is a two-part cell (yellow or olive-brown top over a peach bottom); outputs reuse the same cells, and grey rounded label boxes above them name the target ('reconstruction loss' over positives, 'no object' over negatives).
insights.emphasis: The positive/negative idea is carried only by two fills, yellow and olive-brown, which the inset reuses as a yellow 'positive' square nested inside an olive 'negative' square, with lambda_1 and lambda_2 tick marks for the two noise radii.
insights.flow: Bottom to top: thin black arrows go up from each query into the slab and up again from each output to its label box; the inset has no arrows into the main drawing.
insights.avoid: The inset sits unlabelled and unconnected far to the right, so a reader must work out alone that it explains how the noise ranges make positive and negative boxes; the decoder is a featureless grey slab.

core.what: contrastive denoising queries drawn as matched groups of positive and negative cells: a row of query cells under one wide decoder slab and the matching row of outputs above, each positive set ending in 'reconstruction loss' and each negative set in 'no object'

relations.form: below and above the decoder, two CDN groups each split into three yellow positive and three olive negative cells, and over each set a grey label naming its target (reconstruction loss / no object)
one wide grey 'Decoder Layers x M' slab spans all twelve query columns, with short arrows in and out of each
a separate square to the right draws the noise ranges as nested boxes: a yellow 'positive' square inside an olive 'negative' square, with lambda_1 and lambda_2 ticks on a horizontal line
CDN group0 and CDN group1 drawn as identical copies side by side

channels.colour: yellow = positive query, olive-brown = negative query, used in the query cells, the output cells and the inset; pale peach lower half of each cell (unexplained); grey = decoder and target labels
channels.shape: two-part rectangle = one query (box + content halves); wide rounded slab = the decoder
channels.line: short dark arrows up through the decoder; in the inset a black line with two tick marks
channels.frame: none; braces under each set name it positive or negative and group it into CDN group0/1

quality.strengths: Colour carries one meaning (positive vs negative) consistently in the inputs, outputs and the inset, and each set's target sits directly above it, so which queries are reconstructed and which must predict 'no object' is read by position.
quality.weaknesses: The inset that explains how the noise radii lambda_1 and lambda_2 make positives and negatives is unlabelled and unconnected far to the right; the decoder is a featureless grey slab taking most of the area while the contribution (the query groups) is small cells; the peach lower half of each cell is never explained; no ground-truth box or image is drawn.

figures.lesson: Encode the two query kinds by one fill each and reuse exactly those fills in a small nested-square inset that shows the noise ranges, so the inset explains the main drawing's colour code.

figures.title: DINOv2: Learning Robust Visual Features without Supervision

taxonomy.task: automatic curation of a pretraining image dataset (embedding, deduplication, retrieval)
taxonomy.note: family 'other': the figure draws a dataset-curation pipeline for self-supervised pretraining (DINOv2), not a network; training 'other': no training is drawn, the stages are embedding similarity, deduplication and nearest-neighbour retrieval

arrangement.units: Three stage columns (Embedding, Deduplication, Retrieval) separated by dashed vertical rules, each holding three rows of photo-plus-embedding glyphs; open whitespace on both ends holds the input and output cylinders.
arrangement.inputs_as: two stacked database cylinders (grey uncurated, orange curated) containing real photo thumbnails
arrangement.losses_at: none: a data pipeline with no objective
arrangement.shared: the curated stream is a single long black arrow along the bottom row running through all stages to the retrieval query frame, rather than repeated per stage

insights.structure: Input cylinders on the left and an output cylinder on the right bracket three stage columns split by dashed vertical rules, with bold stage names lined up along the bottom.
insights.data: Every sample is a real food/car photo with a small strip of cells attached as its embedding, and datasets are flat cylinders whose fill colour (grey vs orange) encodes uncurated vs curated.
insights.emphasis: The effect of each stage is drawn on the samples themselves: red X marks over removed duplicates, faded thumbnails for unretrieved images, and a heavy rounded frame around the curated query.
insights.flow: Left-to-right with thick black block arrows entering each column row, and one long thin arrow along the bottom carrying the curated image through to the query frame, from which a short up arrow points to its retrieved neighbours.
insights.avoid: The same ratatouille photo repeats about ten times with only small crop differences, so tracking which copy is which takes effort; distinct samples would read faster.

core.what: a curated query image travels along one long line under three pipeline stages and, at the Retrieval stage, pulls its nearest uncurated neighbours up out of the deduplicated pool, landing in an augmented curated store on the right

relations.form: the curated image, framed heavy in the Retrieval column, sends an upward arrow into the uncurated column above it; retrieved images stay opaque while unretrieved ones fade and one gets a red X
three columns split by dashed vertical rules with bold names along the bottom (Embedding, Deduplication, Retrieval), each showing the same image thumbnails with their embedding bars
two lanes: uncurated images in the upper rows (from the grey cylinder) and the curated image on the bottom line (from the orange cylinder), running left to right in parallel
each stage's effect is drawn on the samples: red X over removed near-duplicates in Deduplication, faded thumbnails for images not retrieved

channels.colour: store identity: grey cylinder = uncurated data, orange cylinder = curated data; the output store stacks a grey part over an orange part; red X = removed
channels.shape: cylinder = a data store; thumbnail with a striped bar on its right = an image with its embedding
channels.line: thick black arrows = data flow; one long straight line carries the curated query across all three stages
channels.frame: heavy rounded frame = the query image at retrieval; dashed rules = stage boundaries; opacity = kept vs dropped

quality.strengths: Every stage is drawn as its effect on real samples (crossed-out duplicates, faded non-retrieved images) rather than as a module box; the stores are cylinders in a keyed colour that recombine in the output store, so 'curated + retrieved' is visible as geometry; arrows are short and straight.
quality.weaknesses: The same ratatouille photo repeats about ten times with small crop differences, so tracking which copy is which takes effort; the embedding step shows bars attached to images but never shows a model; one red X in Retrieval (on the car) reuses the deduplication mark for a different reason.

figures.lesson: Show a data-filtering pipeline by carrying the same real thumbnails through every stage and marking their fate in place (red X for dropped, faded for not retrieved, a heavy frame for the query) instead of drawing process boxes.

figures.title: Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers

taxonomy.task: class-conditional latent image generation

arrangement.units: an unframed overview column, then three equal tall rounded panels, one per block variant; the chosen variant outlined in black, the alternatives greyed
arrangement.inputs_as: grey 'Noised Latent' box with tensor size, and small blue 'Timestep t' and 'Label y' boxes; in the block panels 'Input Tokens' and 'Conditioning' boxes at the bottom edge
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; outputs Noise and Sigma boxes at the top of the overview
arrangement.shared: the same layer-type colours across all four columns; dashed zoom lines from the overview's DiT Block to the chosen panel

insights.structure: An unframed bottom-to-top overview column on the left (Noised Latent, Patchify, DiT Block x N, Layer Norm, Linear and Reshape, Noise and Sigma) is followed by three equal-height rounded panels, each showing one DiT block variant, all titled underneath.
insights.data: Tensors are grey-lavender rounded boxes carrying their shape in small text (32 x 32 x 4); timestep and label are small blue boxes feeding an Embed box beside Patchify.
insights.emphasis: The chosen adaLN-Zero block panel has a black outline, grey fill and fully saturated colours, while the cross-attention and in-context panels are drawn in faded grey outlines and washed-out fills, and two dashed lines fan from the overview's DiT Block into the chosen panel.
insights.flow: Every column reads bottom to top with short vertical arrows; residual paths loop up the left side of each block panel into circled plus nodes, and conditioning enters from the right through a vertical line with alpha, gamma, beta labels.
insights.avoid: The faded alternative panels are so light that their labels are hard to read in print; layer-type colours (blue norm, orange attention, green MLP) are never explained by a legend.

core.what: three DiT block variants as equal-height rounded panels side by side, the chosen adaLN-Zero block in full contrast and the cross-attention and in-context variants faded

relations.form: three equal rounded panels titled underneath (adaLN-Zero, Cross-Attention, In-Context Conditioning), each Input Tokens and Conditioning at the bottom, residual stacks going up, the chosen one first and saturated
two dashed lines fan from the overview's 'DiT Block' to the corners of the adaLN-Zero panel
an unframed bottom-to-top overview column: Noised Latent -> Patchify -> DiT Block (N x) -> Layer Norm -> Linear and Reshape -> Noise and Sigma, with Timestep t and Label y entering through Embed
in the adaLN-Zero panel the conditioning goes through an MLP to a vertical bus on the right that feeds gamma, beta and alpha into each Scale/Scale, Shift box

channels.colour: layer type: blue = norm/scale/embedding, orange = self-attention, green = feedforward/linear, pink = cross-attention, grey = data (latents, tokens); saturation separately marks chosen vs alternative variant
channels.shape: rounded rectangle = layer or tensor; circled plus = residual add
channels.line: solid arrows; heavy black lines for the residual and conditioning paths in the chosen panel; dashed = zoom callout
channels.frame: rounded panel = one block variant; black outline and grey fill = chosen, light grey outline = alternative

quality.strengths: The variants are compared as matched panels with the same bottom inputs, and saturation plus a zoom callout make the chosen block the most salient element; the conditioning path is a straight vertical bus feeding each modulation box from the side, with the signals named at the box.
quality.weaknesses: Faded alternative panels are so light their labels are hard to read in print; the layer-type colour code has no legend; colour saturation is a second meaning stacked on hue; the latents carry shapes (32 x 32 x 4) but no image is drawn.

figures.lesson: Rejected design variants are drawn at the same size and layout as the chosen one but uniformly faded to pale grey and pastel, so the reader sees the winner first and can still compare structures column by column.

figures.title: Are Transformers Effective for Time Series Forecasting?

taxonomy.task: long-term time-series forecasting with a linear map over time
taxonomy.note: architecture 'other': a single linear layer mapping the L-step history window directly to the T-step forecast window

arrangement.units: one rounded red-outlined frame holding a bottom-left row of L history nodes and a top-right row of T future nodes, offset horizontally, with a dashed vertical boundary at the end of the history row
arrangement.inputs_as: a row of grey circle nodes, one per history timestep, named by a curly bracket below
arrangement.shared: weight sharing across variates is not drawn

insights.structure: Two node rows sit offset inside one rounded frame, history low on the left and future high on the right, so the time axis reads left to right and the mapping rises diagonally.
insights.data: Timesteps are drawn as identical grey circles and the weight matrix as a dense fan of thin lines from every history node to every future node, with no numbers or values.
insights.emphasis: Nothing is highlighted; the bare bipartite drawing itself conveys how little machinery the baseline uses.
insights.flow: Lines run diagonally up and right from the history row to the future row, and a dashed vertical line marks where observed time ends.
insights.avoid: The fan of lines is so dense that individual connections merge into a dark wedge, and the drawing never shows the trend/seasonal decomposition that distinguishes the paper's DLinear variant.

core.what: the linear map is drawn on a toy instance of the series: a bottom-left row of L history nodes fully connected by straight lines to a top-right row of T future nodes, a bipartite fan that is the weight matrix

relations.form: time runs left to right: the history row ends at a dashed vertical line and the future row begins just after it, offset upward
every history circle sends a thin line to every future circle, so the dense fan between the two offset rows draws the L-by-T weight layer

channels.colour: one meaning only: all timestep nodes are the same grey and all weight lines the same dark blue; the red outline marks the single linear layer
channels.shape: circle = one timestep value
channels.line: thin solid line = one weight; the dashed vertical line = the boundary between observed and forecast time
channels.frame: one rounded red frame = the one-layer linear model

quality.strengths: The offset of the two rows makes past-before-future readable without labels, and the fan of lines shows directly that every output depends on every input; curly brackets name L and T without cluttering the nodes.
quality.weaknesses: The fan is so dense that the lines merge into a dark wedge between the rows, and the trend/seasonal decomposition that defines DLinear is not drawn, so the figure shows only the generic linear baseline; channel independence (one map shared across variates) is absent.

figures.lesson: A fully connected linear map over time can be shown as two offset node rows (history low-left, future high-right) joined by a fan of thin lines, with brackets naming each row's length symbol.

figures.title: Beyond a Gaussian Denoiser: Residual Learning of Deep CNN for Image Denoising

taxonomy.task: blind Gaussian image denoising via residual (noise) prediction
taxonomy.note: architecture 'other' = a plain feed-forward stack of conv layers predicting the residual noise (no skips, no encoder-decoder)

arrangement.units: one unframed row: input photo, five layer boxes with ellipsis gaps, output image
arrangement.inputs_as: a large real noisy photo titled 'Noisy Image'
arrangement.shared: none; repeated middle layers are drawn as identical blue boxes separated by '...'

insights.structure: A single unframed row runs from a noisy photo through a yellow first layer, repeated blue middle layers separated by '...', and an orange last layer to an output image.
insights.data: Input and output are both large square images the height of the layer boxes: a real noisy butterfly on the left and a grey pure-noise 'Residual Image' on the right.
insights.emphasis: The residual-learning contribution is shown only by the output being the noise rather than a clean image; the first and last layers are separated from the body by distinct yellow and orange fills.
insights.flow: Straight left-to-right with short blue arrows of equal length; '...' marks where layers are omitted.
insights.avoid: Nothing tells the reader the residual is subtracted from the input to give the clean image, and the layer count/depth is not stated in the drawing.

core.what: a single left-to-right chain from a real noisy photo through a yellow first layer, repeated blue middle layers broken by '...', and an orange last layer to a pure-noise residual image

relations.form: one horizontal row of equal-height vertical boxes joined by short straight blue arrows, input photo at the far left and output image at the far right
the repeated middle layer is drawn three times as identical blue 'Conv + BN + ReLU' boxes with '...' gaps standing for the omitted depth

channels.colour: layer type: yellow = first Conv+ReLU, blue = repeated Conv+BN+ReLU, orange = final Conv; arrows are all one blue
channels.shape: tall rectangle = layer, square image = data
channels.line: one style only: straight blue arrows for data flow
channels.frame: none

quality.strengths: Input and output are drawn as real images the height of the layers, so the output being the noise (the residual-learning idea) is visible without reading; the colour code for layer type is consistent and the row is straight with equal arrows.
quality.weaknesses: The subtraction of the residual from the input to obtain the clean image is not drawn, so the contribution is left to the label 'Residual Image'; depth is never stated, and the two '...' gaps take as much width as real layers.

figures.lesson: Make the learning target visible by drawing the actual output (here a pure-noise residual image) at the same size as the input photo, so the reader sees what the network predicts without reading a word.

figures.title: 3D Diffusion Policy: Generalizable Visuomotor Policy Learning via Simple 3D Representations

taxonomy.task: visuomotor imitation learning from 3D point clouds

arrangement.units: two tinted rounded panels on top (training, evaluation), two dashed zoom panels below for the Perception and Decision modules, each titled in bold at its top

relations.form: dashed wedge lines run from the Perception trapezoid in (a) down to a wide light-cyan dashed panel and from the Decision box in (b) down to a narrow dark-blue dashed panel
two tinted panels on the top row, '(a) End-to-End Training' left and '(b) Evaluation' right, redraw the same Perception + Decision pair
in (b) thick soft-blue arrows form a closed rectangle: Observation up the left into Perception, Decision out the right, Action up to Environment and back

Robot State and Compact 3D Repr. stacked as a pair at the Decision panel's left feed a horizontal 'Conditioning' bus that drops short arrows into each U-Net block
