channels.colour: light cyan = perception (trapezoid, zoom outline, Linear bars, Compact 3D Repr.), dark blue = decision; but pink carries two meanings (LayerNorm layers and the Robot State input), and the same light cyan also fills all data arrows
channels.shape: trapezoid = encoder, rectangle = decision/action blocks, cylinders = demonstration store, thin vertical bars = layers
channels.line: thick soft arrows = data flow; dashed outlines and wedges = zoom; a grey dashed arrow carries Compact 3D Repr. across the panel boundary
channels.frame: tinted solid panels = deployment phase; dashed coloured panels = detail of one module

quality.strengths: The zoom is drawn as geometry: each dashed detail panel takes its parent's colour and a wedge points to its parent, and the detail widths follow the paper's emphasis (Perception, the contribution, is the wide one); data are drawn as data (a real point-cloud photo, cropped points, height-coloured points); the evaluation loop is a closed rectangle of short straight arrows.
quality.weaknesses: Pink means both LayerNorm and robot state, and '(a)' labels both the training panel and the point-cloud sub-step; the U-Net is a field of unlabeled small bars, and the dashed grey connector between the two zoom panels is the only cross-panel link, easy to miss.

figures.lesson: Draw the policy once as a perception trapezoid plus decision box inside an Observation -> Environment -> Action loop, then zoom each half into its own dashed panel whose outline colour matches that half.

figures.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model

taxonomy.task: aligning language models to human preferences
taxonomy.note: architecture other: pipeline comparison, no network architecture drawn

arrangement.units: two rounded tinted panels, one per method, bold title in the top-left corner, no inner boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: speech-bubble icons for the preferred and dispreferred completions under a quoted example prompt
arrangement.losses_at: objective names in bold colour under each arrow
arrangement.shared: the same preference-data drawing repeated at the left of both panels; teal 'maximum likelihood' repeated

insights.structure: Two rounded tinted panels side by side: a wide pink 'RLHF' panel (preference data -> reward model <-> LM policy) and a narrower teal 'DPO' panel (preference data -> final LM), so the shorter pipeline is visibly the shorter panel.
insights.data: Preference data is two speech-bubble icons (y_w with a trophy, y_l) joined by a greater-than sign under a quoted prompt 'write me a poem about the history of jazz'; models are faint node-and-edge network glyphs with their names written large over them.
insights.emphasis: Each step's objective is written below its arrow in bold colour: 'maximum likelihood' in the same teal in both panels and 'reinforcement learning' in red only in the RLHF panel, and the DPO panel takes the teal tint.
insights.flow: Left to right within each panel with thick black straight arrows; in RLHF two curved arrows form a loop labelled 'label rewards' and 'sample completions'.
insights.avoid: The network glyphs are so faint they read as background texture, so the models are recognised only by their text labels.

core.what: prior method and ours as two tinted panels side by side, a wide pink RLHF panel then a narrower teal DPO panel, each starting from the same drawn preference data, so the shorter pipeline is visibly the shorter panel

relations.form: two rounded tinted panels on one row, RLHF left and DPO (ours) right and last, with the preference-data drawing repeated identically at the left of each
within each panel one straight black arrow runs left to right from preference data to the model it trains (reward model in RLHF, final LM in DPO)
in RLHF two curved arrows between reward model and LM policy form a loop labelled 'label rewards' and 'sample completions'
preference data drawn as two speech bubbles, y_w with a trophy and y_l, joined by a '>' sign under a quoted prompt

channels.colour: panel tint = method (pink RLHF, teal DPO); objective names are coloured by type, teal 'maximum likelihood' in both panels and red 'reinforcement learning' only in RLHF; teal therefore carries both 'DPO' (panel tint) and 'maximum-likelihood objective' (label), which here deliberately reinforce each other
channels.shape: speech bubble = completion, faint node-edge network glyph = model
channels.line: straight arrow = training/data flow, curved arrows = the RL loop
channels.frame: one tinted rounded panel = one method

quality.strengths: The comparison is carried by geometry: identical inputs, ours last, and the DPO panel is physically shorter because it has one step instead of a loop; the data are drawn as data (a quoted prompt and two ranked completion bubbles with a trophy); each arrow carries its objective by name instead of a loss box.
quality.weaknesses: The network glyphs are so faint they read as background texture behind the model names; teal doubles as the DPO panel tint and the maximum-likelihood label colour, so the reader may take the RLHF reward-model step as 'DPO-like'; the RL loop's two arcs are not tied to a policy-update arrow.

figures.lesson: Name the training objective under each arrow in bold coloured words, the same colour for a step both pipelines share and a contrasting colour for the step only the baseline needs, so the reader sees what was removed without a legend.

figures.title: Diffusion Posterior Sampling for General Noisy Inverse Problems

taxonomy.task: solving noisy (non)linear inverse problems with a pretrained diffusion prior
taxonomy.note: architecture other: posterior sampling that adds a measurement-gradient step to each reverse-diffusion step of a pretrained score model; the figure draws sampling trajectories on data manifolds, not a network. depicts plots: a conceptual geometric diagram of manifolds and a measurement line.

arrangement.units: Two unframed panels of identical size and background, side by side; the left shows a projection-based sampler, the right the proposed one.
arrangement.inputs_as: the measurement as a blue line with a blurred band labelled y = A(x) in bold math, and noise levels as labelled green arcs M_4 ... M_0
arrangement.losses_at: none as boxes; the data-consistency gradient is a magenta step arrow drawn at each point of the trajectory and keyed in the bottom legend
arrangement.shared: the manifolds, measurement line and ground truth x* are redrawn identically in both panels

insights.structure: Two identical geometric scenes sit side by side, nested green arcs M_4 to M_0 crossed by a blurred blue measurement line, and only the sampling trajectory drawn over them differs between left and right.
insights.data: Noise levels are drawn as nested arcs that darken toward the clean manifold M_0, the measurement constraint as a thin blue line in a soft glow, and the ground truth and final sample as small red and blue dots labelled x* and x_0.
insights.emphasis: The baseline's red projection arrows jump off the arcs onto the blue line and its x_0 lands away from x*, while the proposed right panel uses only purple and magenta steps and lands on x*, so the absence of red is the contribution.
insights.flow: Each trajectory starts at the top on M_4 and zigzags downward through the arcs, alternating purple score steps with short magenta gradient steps, ending where the blue line meets M_0.
insights.avoid: The two panels carry no titles naming the methods compared, so the reader must find the baseline/proposed split in the caption; the magenta and purple arrows are also very short and close in hue.

core.what: two identical geometric scenes side by side (nested green noise-level arcs M_4..M_0 crossed by a blurred blue measurement line), the projection-based sampler left and the proposed sampler right, differing only in the trajectory drawn over them

relations.form: two equal unframed panels on one row with the same arcs, line, x* and labels, ours on the right; each has its own arrow legend underneath
the sampling is drawn on a toy picture of the data geometry: arcs for noisy manifolds darkening toward M_0, a straight blue line with a soft glow for y = A(x), red and blue dots for x* and x_0
each trajectory steps down from M_4 to M_0 as a zigzag of short arrows, purple score step then magenta gradient step at every arc (plus red projection jumps onto the line on the left)

channels.colour: arrow colour = step type: purple = score step, magenta = measurement-gradient step, red = projection onto the measurement line (left only); green lightness = noise level of the manifold; blue = measurement subspace; red and blue dots = ground truth vs final sample (red here also means projection, a second meaning)
channels.shape: arc = noise-level manifold, straight line = measurement constraint, dot = a sample
channels.line: solid arrows only; the measurement line is distinguished by its glow, not its stroke
channels.frame: none; the two scenes are separated only by white space

quality.strengths: The comparison is purely geometric: same scene, same start, and the reader sees the left path leave the manifolds via red projections and land x_0 off x*, while the right stays on the arcs and lands at x*; the legend names steps by their mathematical terms instead of extra boxes.
quality.weaknesses: Neither panel is titled, so which side is the baseline relies on the caption and the presence of the red 'proj' key; red is both the projection step and the ground-truth dot; the legend is repeated under both panels instead of once.

figures.lesson: Explain a sampler by drawing the same geometry twice, side by side, and letting only the trajectory change: colour each kind of update step (score, data-gradient, projection) and key it in a one-line legend under each panel, so the missing step type in the proposed panel is the visible difference.

figures.title: Vision Transformers for Dense Prediction

taxonomy.task: monocular depth estimation and semantic segmentation

arrangement.units: three panels separated by thin vertical rules: the overview (no container) and two module details, each detail in a rounded container tinted to match its module colour with a bold title in the bottom corner
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo cut into a patch grid at bottom-left
arrangement.shared: module colour families reused between overview boxes and detail containers

insights.structure: Three untitled panels split by thin full-height vertical rules: an overview at left (a column of four Transformer blocks with rungs out to Reassemble_4..32 boxes and a column of Fusion boxes), then a Reassemble_s detail panel and a Fusion detail panel each in a rounded tinted container.
insights.data: The input is a real photo cut into a grid of patches, tokens are orange 3-D sticks (one red readout token), the reassembled feature is a yellow 3-D block, and the output is a real grey depth map.
insights.emphasis: Each module has one colour family (slate Transformer, green Reassemble, purple Fusion) and its detail panel's container takes a pale tint of the same colour, binding overview box to zoom without any connecting lines.
insights.flow: An upside-down U: input enters bottom-left, goes right through Embed and up the Transformer column, rungs go right to Reassemble and Fusion, then down the Fusion column through Head to the depth map at bottom-right.
insights.avoid: Detail panels have no explicit link to the overview other than colour, and the card's domain tag 'medical-imaging' does not match this natural-image figure.

core.what: an overview at left (a column of four Transformer blocks tapped by rungs into Reassemble_4..32 and a column of Fusion boxes) plus two detail panels for Reassemble_s and Fusion, each in a rounded container tinted like its overview boxes, separated by full-height vertical rules

relations.form: an upside-down U in the overview: photo patches enter bottom-left, Embed goes right, the Transformer column climbs upward, rungs go right, the Fusion column descends to Head and a real depth map at bottom right
four horizontal rungs from the Transformer column at four heights, each ending in a Reassemble box with its scale subscript (4, 8, 16, 32) and a Fusion box beside it, so scale is read by height
the Fusion column chains top-down, each Fusion box taking the box above plus its own Reassemble output from the left; the Fusion detail draws this as a side input joining at a circled plus
the green-tinted Reassemble_s panel and purple-tinted Fusion panel match the green Reassemble and purple Fusion boxes of the overview, with no connecting lines
the input photo is cut into a visible grid of patches and tokens are drawn as rows of orange 3-D sticks with one red readout token, reassembled into 3-D feature blocks

channels.colour: module type: slate = Transformer, green = Reassemble, purple = Fusion, brown = Head/Embed; token colour (orange sticks, red readout, yellow after Read) marks data kind, but orange also fills the final reassembled feature block, so orange means both 'transformer token' and 'output feature map'
channels.shape: rounded rectangle = operation, 3-D stick = token, 3-D block = image-like feature map, photo = input/output
channels.line: one style: thin black arrows for data flow
channels.frame: full-height vertical rules separate overview from details; a tinted rounded container = the inside of one module

quality.strengths: Zoom is bound by colour alone and the overview's geometry encodes scale by rung height, so the multi-resolution taps read without labels; tokens and features are drawn as data (patch grid, 3-D sticks with a distinct readout token, 3-D blocks) between the operations that make them; all paths are short and orthogonal.
quality.weaknesses: The detail panels are untitled at the top (names sit bottom-right inside the tint) and the overview has no panel label; orange covers both tokens and the reassembled output volume; the Fusion detail's two unlabeled entry arrows do not say which comes from Reassemble and which from the previous Fusion.

figures.lesson: Each proposed module keeps one hue across panels, a solid fill for its box in the overview and a pale tint of the same hue for its detail panel's rounded container, so the reader matches block to expansion without a legend or callout lines.

figures.title: DreamBooth: Fine Tuning Text-to-Image Diffusion Models for Subject-Driven Generation

taxonomy.task: subject-driven text-to-image fine-tuning

arrangement.units: Two lanes stacked: the subject lane (input photos, fine-tuned model, outputs) above, the prior lane (frozen model, fine-tuned model, outputs) below; no frames, the lanes are separated by space.
arrangement.inputs_as: real photos in a framed group, quoted prompts with an arrow into each model
arrangement.losses_at: each lane's loss is a dashed labelled arc along that lane's outer edge — reconstruction loss along the top, prior-preservation loss along the bottom
arrangement.shared: the fine-tuned model is drawn once in each lane, the copies joined by a vertical 'Shared Weights' double arrow

insights.structure: A 2 x 2 arrangement: top row the input-photo frame and the yellow fine-tuned model, bottom row the red frozen model and a second yellow copy, with the two yellow copies joined by a vertical 'Shared Weights' double arrow.
insights.data: Each model is a flat bow-tie glyph with 'Text -> Image' across it, a small grey noise square at its left, a quoted prompt ('A [V] dog', 'A dog') in a handwriting font, and a tall frame of three real dog photos as output.
insights.emphasis: Fill colour marks model state (red with a padlock = frozen, yellow = being fine-tuned), and the two losses are dashed elbow arcs labelled in italic serif that run around the outside of the figure.
insights.flow: Prompts enter vertically (from above in the top row, from below in the bottom row); the reconstruction loss arc runs across the top from the generated images back to the input photos, the prior-preservation arc along the bottom between the two generated stacks.
insights.avoid: The noise squares float unconnected to the left of each model, and the frozen model's output stack is not labelled as the target of the prior loss.

core.what: two losses each pair a fine-tuned model's output frame with a target frame: a dashed arc over the top joins the '[V] dog' outputs to the input photos (reconstruction), a dashed arc under the bottom joins the 'A dog' outputs to the frozen model's outputs (prior preservation)

relations.form: each loss is a dashed elbow arc with an italic label running round the outside of the figure between the two image frames it compares, top arc for reconstruction, bottom arc for prior preservation
the two yellow fine-tuned bow-ties are stacked in the right column and joined by a vertical double arrow labelled 'Shared Weights'
the bottom row puts a red padlocked frozen bow-tie (left) and a yellow trainable copy (right) side by side on the same prompt 'A dog', each followed by its frame of three generated dogs
each prompt enters its bow-tie as a short vertical arrow (from above in the top row, from below in the bottom row) while a grey noise square sits at the bow-tie's left without an arrow

channels.colour: model state: yellow = being fine-tuned, red + padlock = frozen; all other elements are black and white or real photos
channels.shape: bow-tie = text-to-image model, rounded tall frame = a set of images, grey square = noise
channels.line: solid arrows = prompt input and the weight-sharing link; dashed arcs = losses
channels.frame: a rounded black frame = one image set (input photos or a model's outputs)

quality.strengths: Images are drawn as real photos (the actual chow-chow and generated dogs), and both losses are drawn between the image sets they compare rather than as boxes; frozen vs trained is a single clean colour channel reinforced by a padlock; the shared-weights link is a short straight vertical arrow between aligned copies.
quality.weaknesses: Neither the noise squares nor the model outputs are connected by arrows, so the reader infers that the noise enters and the frame is produced; the two loss arcs are long detours round the whole figure; the generated '[V] dog' frame is small compared with the input photo frame it is compared with.

figures.lesson: When the figure explains a training procedure rather than an architecture, the network can be one coloured bow-tie glyph labelled 'Text -> Image', with frozen versus trained shown by fill colour plus a padlock and each loss drawn as a dashed labelled arc between the image sets it compares.

figures.title: Dream to Control: Learning Behaviors by Latent Imagination

taxonomy.task: visual continuous control by learning behaviours in a learned latent dynamics model

arrangement.units: three unframed panels side by side, each a horizontal chain of latent circles, separated by whitespace and labelled (a)/(b)/(c) underneath
arrangement.inputs_as: real rendered frames (o_1..o_3) along the bottom row with blue labels; reconstructions o-hat in panel (a) as frames under grey decoders
arrangement.losses_at: not drawn as losses; predicted targets (r-hat, v-hat, a-hat) sit as icons above each latent state in the panel that learns them
arrangement.shared: the encoder, latent chain and icons are redrawn identically in every panel; the same colour per component ties them together

insights.structure: Three side-by-side panels repeat one chain of three green latent circles joined by green arrows; encoders and frames hang below the chain and rewards, values and actions sit above it.
insights.data: Observations are real walker frames along the bottom, latent states plain green dots, and predictions are icons (star medal for reward, trophy for value, joystick for action) with hatted symbols coloured like the icon.
insights.emphasis: Panel (b) is visibly emptier at the bottom (one frame only) and fuller on top (value, reward and action per step), so imagination reads as the chain running without observations.
insights.flow: Upward within a step (frame -> blue encoder -> latent -> predictions) and left-to-right along the green transition arrows in time; panels read left to right as phases.
insights.avoid: Meaning rests entirely on colour and icon identity with no legend, so the trophy versus medal distinction (value vs reward) has to be learned from the caption.

core.what: three captioned phases side by side, each redrawing the same unrolled chain of three green latent circles, so learning dynamics, learning behaviour in imagination and acting differ only in what hangs below and above the chain

relations.form: three unframed panels left to right with captions (a) (b) (c) underneath, the green latent chain at the same height in each
time is unrolled as three green circles joined by horizontal green arrows, one column per step
within a step the flow is upward: real frame -> blue encoder trapezoid -> latent -> icons for reward, value and action above

the phases differ by presence: (a) has an encoder and a grey decoder with a reconstructed frame under every step, (b) has a single observed frame at the first step and value, reward and action predicted above every step, (c) has encoders every step and only the last action predicted

channels.colour: kind of quantity, used on arrows, icons and labels alike: blue = observation/encoder, grey = reconstruction/decoder, green = latent state/transition, orange = reward, brown = value, red = action; one meaning per colour
channels.shape: trapezoid = encoder or decoder (orientation gives direction), circle = latent state, icon = predicted quantity (medal reward, trophy value, joystick action), real frame = observation
channels.line: one style; arrow colour encodes what the arrow produces
channels.frame: none; panels are separated by white space and captions

quality.strengths: Using the same chain at the same height in all three panels makes the phases directly comparable, and the empty bottom of panel (b) shows 'imagination' as the absence of observations; colour carries one quantity type across arrows, icons and hatted symbols; observations are real walker frames; every arrow is short and straight.
quality.weaknesses: No legend: the reader must learn from icons alone that the trophy is value and the medal reward; the difference between actions as inputs (a) and outputs (b, c) rests only on arrow direction; the reconstruction loss in (a) is implied by the grey decoder and o-hat, never drawn as a comparison.

figures.lesson: Draw the training phases as the same unrolled chain repeated across panels and change only what attaches to it, so the difference between phases is what the eye picks up.

figures.title: DreamFusion: Text-to-3D using 2D Diffusion

taxonomy.task: text-to-3D generation via score distillation
taxonomy.note: training: the NeRF is optimised per prompt with a frozen diffusion prior (score distillation); no network is trained on a dataset

arrangement.units: one loop composition with two tinted rounded sub-panels naming the two models (pink NeRF bottom-left, cyan Imagen top-right), each with a white name tag
arrangement.inputs_as: a quoted text prompt in typewriter font at the top of the Imagen panel; Gaussian noise as a photo tile in the middle
arrangement.losses_at: the residual image tile at bottom-right with the gradient return arrow labelled 'Backpropagate onto NeRF weights'
arrangement.shared: the gradient-filled return arrow joining the two panel colours

insights.structure: Left half a 3-D render chain (pink NeRF panel holding density and albedo cubes, then normals, shading and colour cubes, a sun and a camera); right half the rendering plus noise passed into a cyan Imagen panel with text prompt, frozen Transformer and U-Net.
insights.data: Every 3-D quantity is a thin wireframe cube holding the peacock coloured by that quantity; images (rendering, Gaussian noise, noised latent, denoised output, residual) are square photo tiles with math labels underneath.
insights.emphasis: A long bottom arrow 'Backpropagate onto NeRF weights' filled with a pink-to-cyan gradient joins the two panel colours and closes the loop back to the NeRF panel.
insights.flow: Broad light-grey block arrows run left to right through rendering, then down and back right-to-left along the bottom to the NeRF panel; light enters as a yellow band arrow from the sun.
insights.avoid: Many grey block arrows of the same weight cross the middle with no labels, and the camera frustum lines tangle with them, so the order between shading, camera and rendering is hard to trace.

core.what: a loop from a pink NeRF panel on the left through rendering and noising into a cyan frozen Imagen panel on the right, closed by a long pink-to-cyan gradient arrow along the bottom labelled 'Backpropagate onto NeRF weights'

relations.form: broad grey block arrows run left to right through the render chain to Imagen, down to the predicted noise and back right-to-left to the residual, and a long gradient arrow returns along the bottom into the NeRF panel

the differentiable renderer is a chain of wireframe cubes, density -> normals (via grad tau) -> shading (n . l, lit by a sun-icon P(light)) -> colour, then a camera glyph P(camera) projects to the rendering tile
the rendering and a Gaussian-noise tile meet at a '+' to form the noised image z_t entering the Imagen panel, and the quoted text prompt drops into the frozen Transformer and U-Net from above
the predicted noise tile and the sampled noise tile sit on one row with a grey arrow giving the residual tile eps_hat - eps, the compared terms drawn as images
every 3-D quantity (density, albedo, normals, shading, colour) is the same peacock rendered inside a thin wireframe cube and coloured by that quantity

channels.colour: panel tint = model: pink = NeRF (trainable), cyan = Imagen (frozen, also padlock icons); the gradient arrow blends the two tints to show the update going from one to the other; inside the cubes colour is the rendered quantity itself
channels.shape: wireframe cube = a 3-D field, square tile = an image, extruded box = network block, sun and camera icons = sampled light and viewpoint
channels.line: broad light-grey block arrows = forward data, thin grey lines = camera rays, the gradient-filled arrow = backpropagation
channels.frame: rounded tinted panels group the NeRF parameters and the frozen Imagen model

quality.strengths: Every intermediate is drawn as the real peacock in its own representation (density, albedo, normals, shading, colour, noise, denoised image, residual), so the compared noise terms are visible between the model that makes them and the gradient they produce; the training loop is drawn as one closed path whose return arrow carries both panel colours.
quality.weaknesses: The many broad grey arrows have a uniform weight that does not separate the main path from side inputs, and the rendering-to-Imagen path makes a diagonal jump with a large gap; the residual row reads right-to-left against the rest of the figure; the shading step's curved arrow from normals with a starred multiply is hard to follow.

figures.lesson: Draw each rendered quantity (density, albedo, normals, shading, colour) as its own wireframe cube holding the object coloured by that quantity, and close the loop with one long gradient-tinted return arrow whose two end colours match the two model panels it connects.

figures.title: DreamGaussian: Generative Gaussian Splatting for Efficient 3D Content Creation

taxonomy.task: image-to-3D and text-to-3D generation with Gaussian splatting and mesh export

arrangement.units: three dashed rounded light-orange frames, each titled in italic gold: stages i and ii share the top row, stage iii spans the bottom row
arrangement.inputs_as: the words 'Text/Image' above each diffusion-prior bow-tie with a down arrow; stage iii also starts from a UV texture map at its left
arrangement.losses_at: inside the stage they train: 'SDS Loss' in blue under the stage-i diffusion prior; 'MSE Loss' in blue on a long return arrow along the bottom of stage iii
arrangement.shared: the diffusion prior is drawn twice as the same grey bow-tie, once in stage i and once in stage iii; '3D Gaussians' are drawn again at the start of stage ii

insights.structure: Three dashed rounded frames: two short stages side by side on the top row and the long texture-refinement stage across the full bottom row, each with an italic numbered title in its corner.
insights.data: Intermediate results are renders of the actual generated character at each step (blurry Gaussians, densified Gaussians, a half-wireframe textured mesh, a UV atlas, refined views), and the diffusion model is an abstract grey bow-tie.
insights.emphasis: Blue is reserved for optimisation - the 'Optimize' arrows and the 'SDS Loss' and 'MSE Loss' labels - so the training signals stand apart from black data arrows.
insights.flow: Read stage i then ii across the top and then stage iii left to right below; inside stage iii the forward path goes right through the diffusion prior and a long blue arrow along the bottom returns the MSE loss to the random view.
insights.avoid: No arrow links the three stages to each other, so the hand-off from Gaussians to mesh to UV map must be inferred from repeated images and panel numbers.

core.what: three dashed rounded stage frames with italic numbered titles, i) and ii) side by side on the top row and the longer iii) spanning the full bottom row, each showing the actual generated character at its stage

relations.form: stage frames read i -> ii across the top then iii below; no arrow links the frames, the order is given only by the numerals and by the same character reappearing (3D Gaussians end i and start ii)

in i) a blue 'Optimize' arrow and a black 'Random View' arrow run in opposite directions between the grey diffusion-prior bow-tie and the Gaussians; in iii) a long blue 'MSE Loss' arrow along the bottom returns from Refined Image to Random View
stage iii) is one left-to-right row: UV map -> Mapping -> random view -> Add Noise (T = 0.8) -> Diffusion Prior -> Denoising -> refined image

each representation is drawn as a render of the character: half-blurred/half-scattered Gaussians before and after Densify, a magnifier over the Gaussians for density query, a half-textured half-wireframe mesh, a patchwork UV atlas
the MSE loss pairs Refined Image with Random View by the bottom blue arrow between them, without drawing the comparison as its own element

channels.colour: blue = optimisation signal only (Optimize arrows, SDS Loss and MSE Loss labels); black = data/forward path; orange dashed outline and gold italic title = a stage; grey = the frozen diffusion prior
channels.shape: grey bow-tie = diffusion prior, character renders = 3-D representations, square atlas = UV texture
channels.line: black arrows = forward data, blue arrows = gradient/optimisation
channels.frame: dashed rounded orange frame = one stage

quality.strengths: Blue is reserved for optimisation, so the training signal is separable from the forward path in every stage; the representations are drawn as real renders whose change (blurry -> dense -> meshed -> refined) is the method's story; each stage has its own titled frame and short straight arrows.
quality.weaknesses: Nothing connects the stage frames, so the hand-off from i) to ii) to iii) relies on numerals; the half-and-half renders (blurred vs points, textured vs wireframe) are not explained in the figure; stage ii) is drawn as large as i) although it is a non-learned step.

figures.lesson: Lay out a three-stage pipeline as two short stages side by side above one long stage, each in a titled dashed rounded frame, and colour only the gradient arrows and loss labels blue so the optimisation reads apart from the data path.

figures.title: Learning A Sparse Transformer Network for Effective Image Deraining

taxonomy.task: single-image deraining

arrangement.units: a top band with the full network on one row, then a row of three dashed rounded panels for module details, each titled with full name and acronym at its bottom edge
arrangement.inputs_as: a real rainy photo at the left edge of the top band
arrangement.shared: block-type colours (blue conv, green MEFC, orange STB, grey Reshape) reused across both bands

insights.structure: Two bands split by a full-width dashed rule: the top band unfolds the whole U-shaped encoder-decoder onto one row with the bottleneck STB expanded in place as an orange dashed container; the bottom band holds three equal dashed panels (MEFC, TKSA, MSFN) each titled along its bottom edge.
insights.data: Rainy input and derained output are real photos at the two ends; feature sizes appear only as italic H x W x C text under each stage, and the TKSA panel draws its top-k mask as a small green 0/... grid.
insights.emphasis: The proposed modules get the only saturated fills (green MEFC, orange STB, yellow Top-k) while plain convs are blue, and the bottleneck STB is opened up in situ rather than in a separate panel.
insights.flow: Left to right; skip connections rise above the row as nested orthogonal polylines from each encoder stage to its concat circle in the decoder, and a global residual runs over the top from input to the final add.
insights.avoid: The symbol legend (multiply, concat, addition) is boxed at the far right of the top band and competes with the output photo; module labels are rotated 90 degrees in bold serif, which is hard to read.

core.what: the whole U-shaped encoder-decoder flattened onto one left-to-right row from a rainy photo to a derained photo, with the bottleneck STB opened in place as an orange dashed container and skip connections arching over the row as nested polylines

relations.form: one row: 3x3 conv, green MEFC, three peach STB stages, the expanded STB, three STB stages with concat circles, MEFC, 3x3 conv and a global residual adder, with H x W x C sizes in italics under each stage
skip connections leave each encoder stage, rise to nested heights above the row and drop into the matching decoder concat circle, the outermost one being the global residual from the input

the bottleneck STB is opened in situ as a wide orange dashed box (LN -> TKSA -> + -> LN -> MSFN -> +); MEFC, TKSA and MSFN are opened in three equal dashed panels below a full-width dashed rule, tied to the row only by matching names
in the MEFC panel the expert-weights strip and the stacked Expert 1..8 boxes converge on a multiply and concat before a 1x1 conv and a residual adder
the top-k mask is drawn as a small green grid of 0 / ... cells feeding the softmax in the TKSA panel

channels.colour: block type: blue = plain conv / layer, peach = STB, green = MEFC, yellow = Top-k, light colours for Mask/Scatter/Softmax; the expert boxes are cyan; the zoom panels carry no tint, so colour does not tie a detail to its overview block
channels.shape: rounded vertical bar = layer, circle = operator (keyed: multiply, concat, addition), photo = input/output
channels.line: solid black arrows for all data, including skips and residuals
channels.frame: dashed box = an opened module (in the row and in the bottom panels); a dashed legend box keys the operators

quality.strengths: Flattening the U onto one row keeps the whole network readable left to right with the input and output as real photos, and the in-place expansion of the bottleneck STB shows its internals without a jump; operator circles are keyed once in a legend; the top-k mask is drawn as a small grid instead of described.
quality.weaknesses: The four nested skip arches are long detours over the full row and dominate the top of the figure; the three bottom panels are linked to the row only by their titles, not by tint or position, and MSFN/TKSA (the method's new parts) get no more space than MEFC; many near-identical blue bars make the TKSA and MSFN internals dense.

figures.lesson: Unfolding the U-shaped network onto a single row, with skip connections as nested arcs over the top, frees a full-width strip underneath for one equal-height dashed detail panel per proposed module, while the bottleneck block is expanded in place inside a tinted container of its own colour.

figures.title: DuDoRNet: Learning a Dual-Domain Recurrent Network for Fast MRI Reconstruction with Deep T1 Prior

taxonomy.task: accelerated MRI reconstruction with a T1 prior

arrangement.units: repeated recurrent blocks, each a dashed grey rounded container labelled in bold below its left corner, with an ellipsis between the 1st and Nth
arrangement.inputs_as: text boxes: Zero-Padding Reconstruction in line, T1 data prior at upper left, Sampled k-space at lower left
arrangement.shared: prior lines (green image, orange k-space) along the top and the sampled k-space line along the bottom, each feeding every block

insights.structure: A very wide, short strip: a Zero-Padding Reconstruction box at the left, then 1st ... Nth recurrent blocks in dashed grey rounded containers, each running Input_i -> iDRD-Net -> FT|DC -> Input_k -> kDRD-Net -> DC|IFT, ending in a blue Output Reconstruction box.
insights.data: No images: all data are text boxes; the T1 prior splits into 'kspace' and 'image' boxes at upper left, and 'Sampled k-space' is a grey box at lower left.
insights.emphasis: Colour marks domain: green for the image-domain network, its input outline and the image-prior line; orange for the k-space network, its input and the k-space-prior line; the two networks are the only solid-filled boxes.
insights.flow: Left to right with dotted arrows between stages; long coloured prior lines run along the top and drop into each matching input, and a thin grey line runs under the row and rises into each DC box.
insights.avoid: Everything is a text box, so neither the k-space nor image domain is visible, and the long feed lines from top and bottom make the strip hard to scan at its very wide aspect ratio.

core.what: a wide strip of recurrent blocks, the 1st and the Nth drawn as dashed grey containers with '...' between, each running the image-domain net then the k-space net with FT/DC/IFT boxes between them

relations.form: two identical dashed rounded containers labelled '1st Recurrent Block' and 'Nth Recurrent Block' on one row, joined by an ellipsis, from Zero-Padding Reconstruction to a blue Output Reconstruction
inside each block: Input_i -> green iDRD-Net -> FT|DC -> Input_k -> orange kDRD-Net -> DC|IFT, left to right with dotted arrows between domain stages
the two domains alternate within a block, image-domain net (green) then k-space net (orange), with FT and IFT boxes at the domain switches
a T1 prior at the upper left splits into 'kspace' and 'image' boxes whose long orange and green lines run along the top and drop into the matching Input_k and Input_i of every drawn block
one grey 'Sampled k-space' box at the lower left feeds a thin line running under the row that rises into each DC box

channels.colour: domain: green = image domain (iDRD-Net fill, Input_i outline, image-prior line), orange = k-space domain (kDRD-Net fill, Input_k outline, k-space-prior line); grey = acquired data and data consistency; blue = final output only
channels.shape: every element is a rectangle; the only shape cue is filled (network) vs outlined (data or operation)
channels.line: solid arrows = data within a block, dotted arrows = hand-off between stages and to the output; long coloured lines = prior inputs, thin grey lines = sampled k-space
channels.frame: dashed grey rounded container = one recurrent block

quality.strengths: Domain is carried by one colour channel consistently across nets, input outlines and prior lines, so the image/k-space alternation is readable from colour alone; the recurrent block is drawn twice identically, making the repetition explicit; the prior lines drop straight down into their inputs.
quality.weaknesses: No images are drawn: k-space, image, prior and output are all text boxes, so nothing shows what the domains look like; the long prior and sampled-k-space lines span almost the whole width; the strip is extremely wide and short, and the meaning of dotted versus solid arrows is not keyed.

figures.lesson: Colour names the domain, not the module type: green for everything in image space, orange for everything in k-space, and the prior's two feed lines carry the colour of the input they enter.

figures.title: DUSt3R: Geometric 3D Vision Made Easy

taxonomy.task: dense 3D reconstruction (pointmaps) from an uncalibrated image pair
taxonomy.note: family other: pairwise 3D reconstruction by pointmap regression (DUSt3R / MASt3R line)

arrangement.units: two unframed identical lanes (image 1 above, image 2 below) coupled between encoders and between decoders, plus an unframed 3D plot on the right
arrangement.inputs_as: one rendered RGB-faced cube per view, followed by a strip of patch tokens
arrangement.shared: the encoder is drawn twice, joined by a grey dashed vertical line labelled 'Shared weights'; the two decoders exchange through a grey double-headed arrow

insights.structure: Two identical stacked lanes run left to right (image -> patches -> ViT encoder -> decoder -> head -> pointmap + confidence), coupled by a dashed 'Shared weights' tie between the encoders and a double arrow between the decoders, and both feed one 3D plot on the right.
insights.data: Inputs are rendered cubes and tokens a strip of patches; outputs are text labels with shape labels, except the pointmaps, which reappear as red and blue dot grids with camera pyramids in a 3D plot.
insights.emphasis: The two output colours (red view 1, blue view 2) are the only saturated marks outside the inputs and continue on curved arrows into the 3D plot, where they overlap in camera 1's frame.
insights.flow: Short straight grey arrows left to right along each lane; the cross-lane couplings are vertical; two long red / blue curves arc from the pointmap labels across the gap to the plot.
insights.avoid: The input cubes' red / green / blue faces and the coloured patch strip reuse the hues that otherwise mean 'view 1' / 'view 2', and the confidence maps exist only as text.

core.what: two identical stacked lanes, one per view, coupled by a dashed 'Shared weights' tie between the encoders and a double-headed 'Information sharing' arrow between the decoders

relations.form: each lane is one left-to-right row: cube image -> patch strip -> ViT encoder -> F -> Transformer Decoder -> Head -> pointmap and confidence labels
the encoder drawn once per lane in the same column, joined by a vertical grey dashed line labelled 'Shared weights'
the two decoders sit in one column facing each other across a vertical grey double-headed arrow labelled 'Information sharing'

the outputs drawn as what they are: a red and a blue dot grid with a dark-red and a blue camera pyramid in one 3D axis frame on the right, reached by red and blue curved arrows from the pointmap labels

channels.colour: red = view 1, blue = view 2 (pointmap labels, curved arrows, point grids, camera pyramids); light grey = every module; the input cubes' red / green / blue faces are data colours that collide with the view hues
channels.shape: rounded rectangle = module; rendered cube = input image; patch strip = tokens; dot grid = pointmap; pyramid = camera
channels.line: thick grey arrows = data flow; grey dashed line = weight sharing; grey double-headed arrow = cross-decoder exchange; red / blue curves = placing each output in the 3D frame
channels.frame: none; no containers

quality.strengths: The siamese-with-cross-talk structure is pure geometry (mirrored lanes, a dashed tie between encoders, a double arrow between decoders); the outputs are drawn as what they are - two point grids with cameras in one frame - and the red / blue view colour carries one meaning from label to plot; arrows within each lane are short and straight.
quality.weaknesses: The token representations F1, F2 are arrow labels, not drawn; the decoders' cross-attention is one double arrow, so how they exchange is not shown; confidence maps are text only; the two long curved arrows to the plot cross the figure; the RGB input cubes reuse the view hues.

figures.lesson: Colour the two views' outputs and carry the same red / blue into a small 3D plot where both land in one coordinate frame, so the key property (both pointmaps share camera 1's frame) is shown, not stated.

figures.title: Learning to Model the World with Language

taxonomy.task: language-conditioned world model for agents: predict future latents and rewards, learn a policy in imagination

arrangement.units: two unframed panels side by side, (a) training with three observed timesteps and (b) imagination with one observed step then predicted steps; each holds one spanning World Model bar; each observation is a grey rounded frame
arrangement.inputs_as: real indoor-scene photo thumbnails paired with a one-hot token column, labelled x_t and l_t; actions as red joystick icons beside each latent
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; predicted latents z-hat and rewards r-hat (and in (b) values v) sit above the World Model bar at each step
arrangement.shared: one World Model bar spans all timesteps in each panel rather than a copy per step

insights.structure: Each panel puts all timesteps as columns under one wide World Model bar, so 'the same model at every step' is a single shape and the steps differ only in what sits above and below it.
insights.data: Inputs are real photo thumbnails with a one-hot token column in a grey frame, latents are tiny cell grids (black/white for encoded, grey shades for predicted z-hat), and reward, value and action are coin, trophy and joystick icons.
insights.emphasis: Panel (b) is set apart by its brown curved arrows that carry each predicted action and latent from above the bar back under it into the next step, the only curved lines in the figure.
insights.flow: Within a step data rises bottom to top (observation, encoder trapezoids, latent, bar, predictions); time runs left to right across columns; arrows are short and coloured by quantity (dark grey latents, gold rewards, red actions).
insights.avoid: The brown feedback arrows in (b) arc over and under the bar and end at bare arrowheads with no latent or action glyph at their landing point, so the fed-back input is implied rather than drawn.

core.what: per-timestep columns unrolled left to right under one World Model bar spanning them, inputs below and predictions above each step

relations.form: three timestep columns under one spanning World Model bar in each panel; in (b) brown curved arrows loop each step's predicted a and z-hat back under the bar into the next column
image thumbnail and one-hot token column each pass through their own small trapezoid encoder and converge into one latent grid z_t, with the red action arrow joining at the bar beside it
two side-by-side panels with the same bar-and-columns skeleton: (a) all steps observed, (b) one observed step then imagined steps with value and action outputs added

channels.colour: light orange = learned modules (World Model bar, encoder trapezoids); dark grey = latents; gold = reward (and value trophy); red = actions; brown = the imagination feedback loop in (b). Arrow colour repeats the colour of the quantity it carries
channels.shape: trapezoid = encoder; cell grid = latent; coin / trophy / joystick icons = reward / value / action; long rounded bar = the shared world model
channels.line: all straight arrows except the brown curved feedback arrows in (b), which alone mean 'fed back as next input'
channels.frame: grey rounded frame = one observation (image + token); panels unframed, separated by whitespace and sub-captions

quality.strengths: The unrolled-over-time structure is pure geometry (one spanning bar, repeated columns); every quantity is drawn as a noun (latent grids, coin, trophy, joystick, photo + token column) rather than a wire; arrow colour consistently encodes the quantity type; per-step arrows are short and vertical; panels (a) and (b) share one skeleton so the difference is only what changes.
quality.weaknesses: Gold fills both the reward coin and the value trophy icons, and a brown-orange colours both the value labels v and the curved feedback arrows; the recurrent state passed between steps inside the bar is not drawn; the curved feedback arrows in (b) are long detours that cross the bar and land on nothing.

figures.lesson: Draw a sequence model as one wide bar spanning every timestep, with each step's inputs as small data glyphs below and its predictions as glyphs above, and colour each arrow by the kind of quantity it carries (latent, reward, action) so the per-step roles read without labels.

figures.title: End-to-End Variational Networks for Accelerated MRI Reconstruction

taxonomy.task: multi-coil accelerated MRI reconstruction

arrangement.units: an unframed overview row, then three square-cornered tinted detail panels stacked top to bottom, each titled in bold above
arrangement.inputs_as: real multi-coil k-space slice decks with italic labels
arrangement.shared: module tint reused between overview box and detail panel; estimated sensitivity maps fed into the cascade and into the Refinement panel

insights.structure: An overview row across the top (input k-space, cascades of parallel DC and R boxes summed at circled plus, output k-space, IFT, RSS/crop to output) with an SME branch below, followed by three stacked tinted detail panels: Data Consistency, Refinement, Sensitivity Map Estimation.
insights.data: Every tensor is a real MRI image: multi-coil k-space and coil images as decks of offset stacked slices with visible undersampling lines, sensitivity maps as smooth grey blobs, the ACS-masked k-space with its outer region black.
insights.emphasis: Each module has one pastel tint (green DC, peach R, blue SME) used both for its small box in the overview and as the background of its detail panel.
insights.flow: Left to right throughout; in each detail panel inputs sit outside the tinted box on the left and outputs outside on the right, with operation names (IFT, Reduce, U-Net, Expand, FT, Divide by RSS) written on the arrows.
insights.avoid: The DC detail panel sits half-width to the right of the SME branch, breaking the otherwise even stack of detail panels, and the cascade's two side wires with ellipses are hard to follow.

core.what: a compact overview (cascades of parallel DC and R boxes summed at circled pluses, an SME branch below) plus three tinted detail panels, Data Consistency, Refinement and Sensitivity Map Estimation, each tinted like its small box in the overview

relations.form: two cascades drawn side by side in the overview, each a green DC box above and a peach R box below feeding a circled plus on the main line, with '...' between them on every wire
the overview runs left to right: stacked input k-space -> cascades -> output k-space -> IFT -> coil images -> RSS, crop -> single output image
three stacked panels below the overview carry the pastel tint of their overview box (green DC, peach R, blue SME), inputs placed outside the tinted box on the left and outputs outside on the right
the SME output (estimated sensitivity maps) is drawn once in the overview and wired into every R box; the input k-space likewise wires over the top into every DC box

each detail panel draws its operation on real MRI data: multi-coil k-space as offset stacks with visible undersampling lines, coil images, the ACS-masked k-space with black outer region, smooth sensitivity maps

in the DC panel input k-space and the intermediate meet at a minus circle and a lambda_i label drops into a multiply circle before 'Apply Mask'; in R the sensitivity maps rise into Reduce and Expand from a line along the bottom

channels.colour: module identity only: green = DC, peach = R, blue = SME, used for the small overview box and as its detail panel's background; all images are greyscale data
channels.shape: image stack = multi-coil tensor, single image = combined image, small rectangle = module, circle = arithmetic operator
channels.line: one style: thin black arrows for data
channels.frame: a tinted rectangle = the inside of one module

quality.strengths: Every tensor is drawn as real MRI data between the operations that transform it, so the reader sees k-space become coil images, a combined image and back; the zoom is tied by tint alone with one colour per module; detail panels share the same left-in, right-out layout.
quality.weaknesses: In the overview the input k-space and sensitivity-map wires detour round the top and bottom of the cascade with '...' breaks, which makes the shared inputs hard to trace; the DC panel sits off to the right while R and SME span the width, so the details are uneven in placement; the cascade, the method's repeated unit, gets less area than the SME detail.

figures.lesson: Operations are written on the arrows (IFT, Reduce, U-Net, Expand, FT) between real image stacks, so a module's detail panel reads as a chain of data states — k-space, coil images, combined image — rather than a chain of boxes.

figures.title: EAGLE: Speculative Sampling Requires Rethinking Feature Uncertainty

taxonomy.task: speculative sampling for faster LLM decoding

arrangement.units: top: two rounded containers (target LLM, draft model split into three forward columns by dashed lines); bottom: a token tree split into horizontal bands by dashed blue rules
arrangement.inputs_as: word token boxes ('How', 'can') at the bottom of each column
arrangement.shared: Forward 1/2/3 colour tags reused under the draft columns and beside the tree levels

insights.structure: Top half: a narrow rounded 'target LLM' container at left and a wide 'Draft model' container cut by vertical dashed lines into three columns with footer tags Forward 1/2/3; bottom half: the resulting token tree in banded rows (Query, Sampling using Original LLM, Drafting) with the Forward tags repeated at right.
insights.data: Tokens are white rounded word boxes (drafted ones red-outlined); per-position features are pink f_word boxes stacked on green e_word embedding boxes; the tree uses green dashed rounded nodes.
insights.emphasis: The only trainable module is a single yellow 'One Auto-regression Head' bar spanning the draft model, frozen LM Head and Embedding bars carry snowflake icons, and grey vs yellow footer tags separate the target model's forward from the draft forwards.
insights.flow: Bottom to top within each model column; orange dashed arrows carry features from one forward column to the next, and black dashed lines carry sampled tokens back down to become the next input.
insights.avoid: Orange and black dashed lines cross the column dividers in several places and overlap each other, which makes the feature hand-off between forwards hard to trace.

core.what: the draft model is unrolled over three forward passes as columns of one wide container split by vertical dashed lines and tagged Forward 1/2/3 in a footer, beside a narrow target-LLM container whose features are fed into it

relations.form: one wide rounded 'Draft model' container cut by vertical dashed lines into three columns, the shared Embedding, Auto-regression Head and LM Head bars spanning all columns, with yellow Forward 1/2/3 footer tags

the narrow 'target LLM' container on the left (Embedding, Transformer Layers, LM Head) stands beside the wide draft container, which replaces the Transformer layers with one yellow 'One Auto-regression Head' bar
each draft input is a stacked pair, a pink feature f over a green embedding e; orange dashed elbow lines bring each feature from the target LLM or from the previous draft column into the next pair

tokens flow bottom to top within each column (token -> embedding -> head -> feature -> LM Head -> sampling -> token), and black dashed lines carry sampled tokens back down into the next column's input

below the containers the drafted continuation is a token tree in three banded rows (Query 'How can', 'I' sampled by the original LLM, then dashed-outline drafted tokens make/help, a/our, with/you, ...), with the Forward tags repeated at the right

channels.colour: pink = feature vector, green = token embedding, light blue = frozen module (with a snowflake icon), yellow = the trainable auto-regression head; the footer tags use grey for the target forward and the same yellow for draft forwards, so yellow means both 'trainable head' and 'draft pass'; red outline = a draft-produced token or feature versus black for target-produced
channels.shape: wide rounded bar = layer shared across positions, small rectangle = token or vector, dashed-outline rounded box = drafted token in the tree
channels.line: solid black arrows = forward within a pass; orange dashed elbows = feature hand-off; black dashed = sampled-token hand-off; light-blue dashed rules = band separators in the tree
channels.frame: rounded containers = one model (target LLM, draft model); vertical dashed lines = one forward pass

quality.strengths: Unrolling the draft passes as columns that share spanning layer bars shows directly that one small head is reused per step, and the snowflake/yellow contrast picks out the only trainable part; features and embeddings are drawn as named vectors (f_how, e_can) between the modules that make and use them; the token tree below gives the output as data.
quality.weaknesses: Orange dashed feature lines bend repeatedly and cross column boundaries, making the one-step feature shift hard to follow; yellow carries two meanings and red outlines (draft-produced) are never keyed; the tree is a separate panel whose rows are tied to the columns only by repeated Forward tags rather than by alignment.

figures.lesson: Cut the draft model into vertical columns, one per forward pass, each with a coloured footer tag, and repeat those tags beside the levels of the draft token tree below, so every tree level maps to the forward pass that produced it.

figures.title: Equivariant Diffusion for Molecule Generation in 3D

taxonomy.task: E(3)-equivariant 3D molecule generation
taxonomy.note: architecture other: concept teaser showing equivariance, no network drawn

arrangement.units: four unframed drawings on a 2 x 2 grid tied only by arrows
arrangement.inputs_as: molecule graph glyphs (bottom row) with their noised atom clouds above
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the invariance equation under the bottom row
arrangement.shared: the same atom colour code in all four drawings

insights.structure: A 2 x 2 commutative square with no containers: noisy atom clouds in the top row, molecules in the bottom row, the left column original and the right column rotated.
insights.data: Atoms are flat filled circles with thick black outlines coloured by element (grey, pink, blue, small white), bonds are thick black lines, and the noisy states are the same circles scattered without bonds.
insights.emphasis: The bottom row ends in the equation p(x,h) = p(Rx,h) with the equals sign placed exactly between the two columns, so the property itself is the message.
insights.flow: Horizontal solid arrows labelled R with a dashed rotation glyph run across each row; between rows each column has a dashed curved pair of arrows labelled 'diffuse' with q(...) and 'denoise' with p(...).

core.what: an equivariance property drawn as a 2 x 2 commutative square on toy molecules: noisy atom clouds on the top row, molecules on the bottom row, original on the left and rotated by R on the right, ending in p(x,h) = p(Rx,h) with the equals sign between the columns

relations.form: the method acts on a small drawn molecule (a ring of grey atoms with red, blue and white substituents) and its noised version, a scatter of the same coloured circles without bonds
the two columns face each other across horizontal 'R' arrows with a small rotation icon, and the bottom row closes with p(x,h) = p(Rx,h), the equals sign centred between the columns
each column has a pair of opposed dashed curved arrows between the rows, 'diffuse' q(z_T,...|x,h) upward and 'denoise' p(x,h,...|z_T) downward

channels.colour: atom type only: grey, red, blue and white circles keep their colours from the molecule into the noise cloud and across the rotation; no colour is used for modules
channels.shape: circle = atom, size distinguishing heavy atoms from hydrogens; bond lines exist only in the clean molecules
channels.line: solid arrows = the rotation R, dashed curved arrows = the stochastic diffuse/denoise processes
channels.frame: none; the four states sit at the corners of the square

quality.strengths: The property itself is the geometry: two columns related by R, two rows related by diffusion, and the equality placed exactly between the column ends; data are drawn as molecules and atom clouds with consistent atom colours; no module boxes compete with the message, and every arrow is short and straight.
quality.weaknesses: Process names are written as typeset distributions beside the arrows rather than short names; the rotation icon is tiny and the top-right cloud is hard to check as a rotation of the top-left one; the claim is only stated for the bottom row, so the top row's role (that the noise process is also equivariant) is left implicit.

figures.lesson: State an equivariance claim as a commutative square: the object and its noised version in one column, their rotated copies in the other, rotation arrows across, diffuse/denoise arrows down, and the invariance equation set under the bottom row with '=' between the columns.

figures.title: E(n) Equivariant Graph Neural Networks

taxonomy.task: E(n)-equivariant learning on graphs / point sets

arrangement.units: four unframed graph drawings in a 2x2 grid tied only by four labelled arrows; no frames or panel letters
arrangement.inputs_as: toy node-link graph with per-node bar charts and dashed vector arrows
arrangement.shared: the same network phi on both vertical arrows

insights.structure: Four copies of the same four-node graph form an unframed 2x2 commutative square: input top-left, rotated input top-right, network outputs for each directly beneath.
insights.data: Each node is a sage-green circle labelled x1..x4 carrying a tiny three-bar chart (invariant features h_i) and a dashed coloured arrow (vector v_i); the input row uses blue bars and salmon arrows, the output row red bars and teal arrows.
insights.emphasis: There is no network box at all: the method is the single italic phi on the two vertical arrows, and the claim is made by the bars staying identical across each row while the arrows rotate with the graph.
insights.flow: Horizontal arrows labelled S_g (top) and T_g (bottom) with a small dashed rotation glyph carry the transformation left-to-right; vertical phi arrows carry the network top-to-bottom, so the reader checks both paths around the square agree.
insights.avoid: The colour swap between rows (blue/salmon to red/teal) is never keyed in the figure, so a reader cannot tell it means 'output' rather than a different quantity.

core.what: equivariance drawn as an unframed 2 x 2 commutative square of four copies of one four-node graph: input top-left, rotated input top-right (S_g), the network phi's outputs directly beneath each, related by T_g

relations.form: a toy graph of four green nodes x_1..x_4 with edges, each node carrying a small bar chart h_i (invariant features) and a dashed arrow v_i (a vector), redrawn in all four corners
the two columns face each other across horizontal arrows S_g (input transform) and T_g (output transform), each with a small rotation icon; the rows are tied by vertical arrows labelled only phi
within each column one short downward phi arrow maps input graph to output graph; no network box is drawn

channels.colour: two-colour scheme swapped between rows: on the inputs vectors are orange-red and feature bars cyan, on the outputs vectors are teal and feature bars orange-red, so orange-red means 'input vector' on top and 'output feature' below (one channel, two meanings); node green is constant
channels.shape: circle = node, bar chart = feature vector h, dashed arrow = vector v
channels.line: solid black arrows = maps (phi, S_g, T_g); dashed coloured arrows = per-node vectors; plain lines = graph edges
channels.frame: none

quality.strengths: The claim is made purely by geometry: the bars stay identical across each row while the vectors rotate with the graph, so invariance of h and equivariance of x and v are visible without text; there is no network box, only phi on the arrows, keeping all space for the data.
quality.weaknesses: The input/output colour swap makes orange-red mean two things and is not keyed; the rotation icons are tiny and the graph rotation is hard to check by eye; nothing shows the message passing inside phi, so the figure states the property but not how the layer achieves it.

figures.lesson: Attach each node's invariant features as a tiny bar chart and its vector as a dashed arrow, and swap the two colours between the input and output rows, so a reader sees the bars stay fixed under rotation while the arrows rotate with the graph.

figures.title: End-to-End Training of Multi-Document Reader and Retriever for Open-Domain Question Answering

core.what: the attention pattern is drawn as edges on a toy eight-node graph: input-graph edges (green), expander edges (blue) and virtual-node edges (red) each alone in a panel, then overlaid in (d)

relations.form: each edge source drawn as coloured edges on the same eight nodes, one panel per source
the bottom-right panel overlays green, blue and red edges on the shared node positions, the virtual node lifted above the octagon

figures.title: FedDG: Federated Domain Generalization on Medical Image Segmentation via Episodic Learning in Continuous Frequency Space

arrangement.units: two panels side by side separated by a vertical dashed line, labelled (a)/(b) beneath; (b) has an inner dashed rounded container for the local client
arrangement.inputs_as: pastel dashed domain ellipses with padlocks in (a); real fundus photographs in (b)
arrangement.shared: amplitude spectra from every client feed the local client in (b)

insights.structure: Two panels split by a vertical dashed line: (a) a hub-and-spoke with K client models in dashed-separated columns at the bottom, a server cloud in the middle and unseen target domains at the top; (b) one dashed rounded container 'Local client k' above the other clients' images.
insights.data: Clients are hourglass model glyphs over dashed pastel domain ellipses (S^1 blue, S^2 yellow, S^K green) with padlocks; in (b) real fundus photographs show local data and its transformed versions, and tiny grey amplitude-spectrum squares stand for frequency-space information.
insights.emphasis: The open problem is the two unseen domains T^1, T^2 marked by red question marks and red arrows; each client's pastel colour is carried from its ellipse to its spectrum arrow and the transformed image it produces in (b).
insights.flow: (a) reads bottom-to-top, client models up into the server cloud and red arrows out to unseen domains; (b) reads left-to-right local image -> transformed images, with coloured arrows rising from other clients' spectra into the container.
insights.avoid: The corner legend is cramped and misspelled ('Data parivacy'), the padlocks and spectrum thumbnails are tiny, and (a) and (b) are tied together by nothing but adjacency.

core.what: K client columns separated by vertical dashed lines along the bottom of panel (a), each a locked source-domain ellipse under its own model glyph, all sending grey arrows up to one server cloud, which sends red arrows to unseen target domains marked with red question marks

relations.form: equal client columns S^1, S^2, ..., S^K side by side with dashed separators and an ellipsis, each holding a coloured ellipse with a padlock and a bow-tie model theta^k
grey curved arrows converge from every client model onto one bow-tie theta inside a cloud in the middle of panel (a)
the server's red arrows fan up to two dashed ellipses T^1 and T^2 plus an ellipsis, each topped by a red question mark, separating unseen target domains from the sources below
in panel (b) a small grey amplitude-spectrum tile above each other client's fundus image is passed up by an arrow in that client's colour into the local client k's dashed container

inside the 'Local client k' container a real fundus photo leads by a hollow arrow to three transformed fundus photos, one per incoming spectrum, under the title 'Transformed data with multi-source distributions'

channels.colour: client identity: each source has a pastel (blue S^1, yellow S^2, green S^K, pink S^k) carried from its ellipse to its spectrum arrow in (b); red = unknown/unseen (question marks, arrows to targets); but the target ellipses are filled orange and light blue, close to client pastels, so the unseen/seen distinction rests on the dashed red outline
channels.shape: dashed ellipse = domain, bow-tie = model, cloud = central server, padlock = data privacy, real fundus photo = data, grey square = amplitude spectrum; keyed in a legend at top left
channels.line: grey arrows = model upload, red arrows = deployment to unseen domains, client-coloured arrows = spectrum sharing; a vertical dashed rule separates the panels
channels.frame: a dashed rounded container = one client's local learning

quality.strengths: Shape glyphs are keyed once in a legend and reused in both panels; the federated star topology is drawn as geometry (client columns under one server); data are real fundus photos, and the spectrum exchange is shown by client-coloured arrows feeding transformed images, so which source contributed which style is traceable.
quality.weaknesses: The target ellipses reuse pastel fills close to the client colours, so colour alone does not separate seen from unseen; the method (episodic learning with the transformed data) is only a title in panel (b) with no learning objective drawn; panel (a), mostly the problem setting, takes as much area as the method panel.

figures.lesson: Give each client one pastel colour carried through its domain ellipse, its arrow and the data it contributes, and put a padlock on every data glyph so privacy is a symbol, not a sentence.

figures.title: FEDformer: Frequency Enhanced Decomposed Transformer for Long-term Series Forecasting

taxonomy.task: long-term time-series forecasting

arrangement.units: two dashed grey rectangles (encoder band over decoder band) with repeat counts N x / M x in their top-right corners and names at lower-left
arrangement.inputs_as: rounded pills with tensor-shape labels
arrangement.shared: encoder output feeds the decoder's frequency-enhanced attention as K, V

insights.structure: Two dashed grey frames stacked vertically - 'FEDformer Encoder' (N x) above, 'FEDformer Decoder' (M x) below - each a left-to-right row of blocks with residual skips arching over the top and circled-plus adders.
insights.data: Inputs are rounded pills at the left edge ('Encoder Input', 'Seasonal Init', 'Trend Init') with tensor shapes beneath; every wire carries its seasonal / trend symbol (X_en^{l-1}, S_en^{l,1}, T_de^{l,k}), and the decoder's trend gets its own bottom lane summed by circled pluses.
insights.emphasis: Only the new blocks carry saturated fills - light green Frequency Enhanced Block and pink Frequency Enhanced Attention - against pale yellow MOE Decomp and grey Feed Forward, so the contribution reads as substitutions in a familiar Autoformer skeleton.
insights.flow: Left-to-right in each frame; one wire leaves the encoder's right end, drops down and enters the decoder's attention block as K and V, and the seasonal and trend lanes merge at a final adder to 'Output' on the right.
insights.avoid: The encoder-to-decoder wire enters the decoder frame from above and crosses its skip lines, the 'FEDformer Decoder' label collides with the trend lane, and the input pill reads 'Seasoal Init' (typo).

core.what: two stacked dashed frames, 'FEDformer Encoder' (N x) above and 'FEDformer Decoder' (M x) below, each a left-to-right row of blocks with residual skips arching over the top into circled-plus adders

relations.form: encoder row: Encoder Input -> green Frequency Enhanced Block -> + -> yellow MOE Decomp -> grey Feed Forward -> + -> MOE Decomp; decoder row adds a pink Frequency Enhanced Attention block and a third MOE Decomp before Output
each dashed frame carries an 'N x' or 'M x' tag at its top-right corner for the repeated layer, drawn once
the encoder output S_en^{l,2} leaves the top frame on the right, runs down and back left, and enters the Frequency Enhanced Attention block as K and V, with the decoder's seasonal stream as Q

the decoder runs two parallel lanes: the seasonal row through the blocks and a Trend Init line along the bottom, into which each MOE Decomp drops its trend part T_de^{l,i} at a circled plus, the two lanes summing at the final Output plus
the new frequency blocks are drawn as substitutions in the familiar decomposition skeleton, the only saturated green and pink boxes among pale yellow decomposition and grey feed-forward boxes

channels.colour: block type: green = Frequency Enhanced Block, pink = Frequency Enhanced Attention (the two new blocks), pale yellow = MOE Decomp, grey = Feed Forward; one meaning each
channels.shape: rectangle = block, circle with plus = addition, rounded pill = input or initialisation
channels.line: one style: thin black arrows for all data, including skips and the trend lane; the encoder's MOE Decomp down-arrows end in empty space
channels.frame: a dashed grey frame = one repeated encoder or decoder layer

quality.strengths: Novelty is carried by fill alone, so the reader sees the paper's change as two coloured substitutions inside a known Autoformer layout; the decoder's seasonal and trend lanes are separate horizontal lines that meet only at the output; encoder and decoder repeat the same block order, so the shared vocabulary is taught once.
quality.weaknesses: Every tensor is a typeset symbol (X_en^{l-1}, S_de^{l,1}, T_de^{l,3}) beside a wire rather than a drawn representation, and the inputs carry full shape formulas; the encoder-to-decoder link bends round the right edge and back across the decoder; the encoder MOE Decomp trend outputs are arrows to nowhere; the green FEB and pink FEA get no more area than the routine decomposition blocks.

figures.lesson: Label each wire with the layer's seasonal and trend symbols (S^{l,k}, T^{l,k}) so the decomposition bookkeeping is read off the arrows, and give the decoder's trend its own bottom lane summed by circled pluses.

figures.title: FEDformer: Frequency Enhanced Decomposed Transformer for Long-term Series Forecasting

arrangement.shared: none

the sampled Q~ and a cyan weight block R placed alone above the bottom row both run diagonally into one grey circled multiply, whose output Y~ continues to the right

each tensor is a 3-D block labelled with its shape (R^{L x D} on the top row, C^{N x D} or C^{M x D} on the bottom), so the truncation to M modes and padding back to N are shown as named shape changes

channels.shape: 3-D block = tensor, circle = multiply, flat box = the incoming layer input
channels.line: one style: short black arrows labelled with the operation (MLP, F, Sampling, padding, F^-1)
channels.frame: none

quality.strengths: Rows encode domain, so the round trip into the frequency domain and back is visible as geometry; every intermediate tensor is drawn between the operations that make and use it, and the single learnable weight is the only cyan block, set apart above the row; all arrows are short and straight.

figures.lesson: Put time-domain tensors on the top row and frequency-domain tensors on the bottom row, with the Fourier transform as the arrow going down and its inverse as the arrow coming back up, and mark each tensor ℝ or ℂ in its shape label so the domain is read from row and symbol.

figures.title: Tackling the Objective Inconsistency Problem in Heterogeneous Federated Optimization

figures.title: Tackling the Objective Inconsistency Problem in Heterogeneous Federated Optimization

taxonomy.task: normalized averaging of local updates in heterogeneous federated optimization
taxonomy.note: modality multi = abstract parameter-space sketch, no data modality

arrangement.units: two unframed panels with the same skeleton separated by a grey dashed vertical rule, joined by a grey block arrow carrying the change in words
arrangement.inputs_as: black start point x^(t,0) with black local step chains
arrangement.shared: identical black local step chains and red dashed endpoint line in both panels

insights.structure: Two panels split by a grey dashed vertical rule, each stacking a parameter-space sketch, the rule's bold name, its update equation, a short block arrow down and the objective it optimises; a thick grey block arrow sits between the panels.
insights.data: Clients' local steps are black arrow chains from x^(t,0) to x_1^(t,4) and x_2^(t,2); per-client changes are dashed coloured vectors, the server step a solid coloured arrow to a coloured dot, with a bracket on top marking Delta_1^(t) and its normalized fraction.
insights.emphasis: The proposed rule owns green (bold green name, green equation, green arrow and server dot) against FedAvg's blue, and the change is stated in words on the grey arrow: 'Average normalized gradients instead of local changes'.
insights.flow: Left panel then right panel across the central block arrow; within each panel top-to-bottom from sketch to rule name to equation to the 'Optimizes F~(x)' objective.

core.what: FedAvg's update rule (left, blue) and the proposed normalized rule (right, green) as two panels with the same skeleton, joined by a grey block arrow that states the change in words.

relations.form: two unframed panels split by a dashed vertical rule, each stacking parameter-space sketch, rule name, update equation, down arrow and the objective it optimises; ours on the right
clients' local steps drawn as black arrow chains from x^(t,0) to x_1^(t,4) and x_2^(t,2), with per-client changes as dashed vectors and the server step as a solid coloured arrow to a coloured dot
within each panel a top-to-bottom chain: sketch -> rule equation -> block arrow -> 'Optimizes F~(x)'

figures.title: FedProto: Federated Prototype Learning across Heterogeneous Clients

arrangement.units: one rounded server panel on top and two identical rounded client panels below (pale fill, thin grey outline), titled outside

channels.shape: rounded yellow box = representation, cylinder = data store, server-rack icon = server, tag + discs = label set

figures.title: Efficient Frequency Domain-based Transformers for High-Quality Image Deblurring

taxonomy.task: image deblurring

arrangement.units: three lettered panels separated by vertical dashed rules: (a) the network on two rounded tinted backgrounds (grey encoder, blue decoder), (b) FSAS on a pink rounded panel, (c) DFFN on an orange rounded panel
arrangement.inputs_as: tilted real blurry photo slab at the bottom of the encoder tower
arrangement.shared: colour legend shared by all panels
