core.what: An encoder-decoder U-shape drawn as two towers of tilted feature slabs: the blurry image climbs the left grey tower, crosses at the top by one long arrow and descends the right blue tower to the sharp image.

relations.form: panel (a): left tower rises bottom -> top through three levels (channel 48/96/192), a single bent arrow crosses at the top, right tower descends to the output slab
horizontal dash-dot skip lines run from each encoder level to a circled-C concatenation on the decoder side, and from the input to a circled-plus residual at the output
panels (b) FSAS and (c) DFFN beside (a), behind vertical dashed rules, each tinted in its module's legend colour (pink, orange) to tie it to the slabs of that colour
panels (b) and (c) read top to bottom as block chains (Norm -> Conv1x1 -> FFT -> product -> IFFT ...) with a residual line looping around the right edge
in (b) Q and K FFT branches meet at an element-wise product node, then join V at a second product node

channels.colour: operation type, keyed in the legend (grey conv, orange DFFN, pink FSAS, blue downsample, green upsample); panel tints also reuse pink/orange to mark the zoomed module, and grey/blue backgrounds mark encoder/decoder, so tint carries both op type and region
channels.shape: tilted slab = feature map, flat rounded box = operation, trapezoid = Conv1x1 change of width, circle glyph = merge operator (concat, sum, product)
channels.line: solid arrows = main data flow, dash-dot = skip connections
channels.frame: rounded tinted panel = one network region or one zoomed module; vertical dashed rules separate (a), (b), (c) and the legend

quality.strengths: Input and output are real photos drawn as slabs in the same 3-D style as the features, the U-shape is visible as two towers, and the two frequency modules (the contribution) get their own tinted panels with the FFT step boxed in a purple inset in (c).
quality.weaknesses: Stacked colour layers on each slab are hard to map to block order; the dash-dot skips are thin against the panel tints; the top crossing arrow is a long bend over the tower; panel tint reuses legend op colours as region markers, so one channel carries two meanings; no line ties (b)/(c) back to the slabs they expand.

figures.lesson: Each module's expanded detail panel is filled with that module's own legend colour (pink FSAS panel, orange DFFN panel), so the overview slab, the legend swatch and the zoomed panel read as one thing without any connector lines.

figures.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness

taxonomy.task: IO-aware exact attention
taxonomy.note: architecture other: a tiled GPU kernel / memory-hierarchy computation, not a network topology

arrangement.units: context (pyramid), method (tiled loops), result (bar chart), the last set off by a thin vertical rule, each titled underneath or above
arrangement.inputs_as: Q, K^T, V block strips placed around the attention matrix
arrangement.shared: orange = SRAM colour across panels

insights.structure: Three unframed panels in a row: a memory-hierarchy pyramid (SRAM/HBM/DRAM), the tiled computation with Q, K^T, V and output strips arranged around a dashed N x N box, and a stacked runtime bar chart split off by a vertical rule.
insights.data: Matrices are strips of green square blocks with typeset shapes (Q: N x d); a copied tile is a single orange square, and the result is a stacked bar (Matmul/Dropout/Softmax/Mask) against one short 'Fused Kernel' bar.

insights.flow: Red 'Outer Loop' arrows run over K^T and down V, blue 'Inner Loop' arrows down Q and under the output; purple dashed arrows carry tiles into the compute block.

core.what: Tiled attention drawn on the matrices themselves: Q, K^T, V and the output are strips of green blocks around a dashed N x N QK^T square, and single orange tiles are copied into the square to be computed 'on SRAM'.

relations.form: K^T as a horizontal block strip on top, Q and V as vertical strips left and right, the output strip at the bottom, the dashed N x N square in the middle where one orange tile is computed
loops drawn as long arrows along the strips: red 'Outer Loop' arrows over K^T and down V, blue 'Inner Loop' arrows down Q, beside V and under the output

a memory pyramid on the left (orange SRAM tip, green HBM, teal DRAM) whose tier colours are reused in the centre to say where each tile lives
a stacked runtime bar for PyTorch (Matmul / Dropout / Softmax / Mask / Matmul) beside one short 'Fused Kernel' bar for FlashAttention, split off by a vertical rule

channels.colour: memory tier, tied by the pyramid: orange = SRAM (tiles, 'SRAM' words), green = HBM (matrix strips, 'HBM' word), teal = DRAM; red and blue then mean outer vs inner loop, and purple = tile movement, so the arrow colours are a second, unkeyed code
channels.shape: row of squares = matrix in HBM, single square = tile, triangle = memory hierarchy, bar = runtime
channels.line: red / blue long arrows = loop order (outer / inner), purple dashed = tile copy into compute, black solid = copy-out or output write; dashed rectangle = the virtual N x N matrix never materialised
channels.frame: no frames; a vertical rule separates the runtime chart from the method

quality.strengths: The method acts on the matrix layout and is drawn on it: strips around a dashed (never stored) N x N square, one orange tile computed inside; the pyramid teaches the tier colours once and the centre reuses them so 'tile lives in SRAM' is read from colour alone; the runtime panel compares to the baseline with ours last.
quality.weaknesses: Four loop arrows (two red, two blue) on different sides make the nesting order take effort to reconstruct; the purple dashed copy arrows bend around the tile in the square; red/blue/purple add a second arrow colour code that is not keyed.

figures.lesson: Colour every tensor block by the memory level it sits in, using the colours of a memory-hierarchy pyramid drawn beside it, so moving a tile between memories reads as a colour change.

channels.frame: thin black frame = the opened Fourier layer; pale-yellow inner box = the spectral path

quality.strengths: The zoom ties the overview to the detail by both geometry (dashed fan-out lines) and matching tint; the spectral-truncation step is drawn as wave sketches rather than only named; both panels read strictly left to right.
quality.weaknesses: Learned maps (P, Q, R, W) and the fixed sum/activation share nearly the same orange, so role colour is hard to read; data (functions) and operations are both circles; the W path bends down and back up in long curves instead of running straight under the spectral box; the crop includes caption text under (b).

figures.lesson: Show spectral truncation as data, not a label: put tiny sine-wave sketches between the forward and inverse transform circles, many frequencies before the learned multiplier and only the low ones after it.

figures.title: Protein structure generation via folding diffusion

taxonomy.task: protein backbone generation via angle diffusion

arrangement.units: no frames; chain row on top, two state-illustration columns under its ends, angle-definition schematic in the bottom centre
arrangement.inputs_as: noise state x_T circle with its noisy heatmap and tangled structure below
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Top row is the diffusion chain x_T -> ... -> x_t -> x_{t-1} -> ... -> x_0 in large open circles; below each end sit an angle heatmap and a rendered structure, and the bottom centre holds a ball-and-stick backbone defining the six angles.
insights.data: States are shown three ways: as math circles, as angle heatmaps (noisy vs banded), and as green cartoon tubes (tangle vs helical bundle) labelled 'Corresponding structure'.
insights.emphasis: Torsions phi/psi/omega are orange with dashed circular arrows and bond angles theta1-3 dark green with dashed arcs, making the representation (angles, not coordinates) the visual centre.
insights.flow: Left-to-right along the chain with the learned reverse step p_xi as a solid arrow and the forward q as a dashed arrow curving back underneath; the lower content is read by column, not by arrows.
insights.avoid: The network that predicts the denoising step is never drawn, so the figure explains the representation but not the model.

core.what: The diffusion state is defined on a drawn protein backbone: a ball-and-stick chain at bottom centre with torsions phi/psi/omega (orange dashed circular arrows) and bond angles theta1-3 (green dashed arcs) marked where they act.

relations.form: a small backbone instance N - Ca - C - N - Ca with side groups R1/R2 and O, each of the six angles drawn at the bond or joint it measures
top row of large circles x_T -> ... -> x_t -> x_{t-1} -> ... -> x_0, with a solid learned reverse arrow p_xi and a dashed forward-noise arrow q bending back between x_t and x_{t-1}
under each end of the chain the same pair is drawn: an angle heatmap '= x_T' / 'x_0 =' and a rendered 'Corresponding structure' (tangle at left, helical bundle at right)

channels.colour: orange = torsion angles, dark green = bond angles; heatmaps use a viridis-like colormap for angle values; the green tube renders are a third green with no relation to the bond-angle green; light blue O and grey R are atom types
channels.shape: large open circle = diffusion state, small circle = atom, grey rounded square = side chain, heatmap = state as angle matrix, tube = 3-D structure
channels.line: solid arrow = learned reverse step, dashed curved arrow = forward noising; dashed arcs/circles = angles; thin black lines = bonds

quality.strengths: The representation (angles, not coordinates) is the visual centre and is drawn on the structure it parameterises; the two chain ends are shown as data in two forms (heatmap and rendered fold), making noise vs structure visible; forward vs reverse steps differ by line style.
quality.weaknesses: The backbone glyph sits between the two ends with no line tying it to x_t, so which state it describes is implicit; green is used for both bond angles and the protein renders; heatmap axes are unlabeled so the reader cannot tell rows are angles.

figures.lesson: When the generated variable is not coordinates, show each end of the chain twice - as the variable itself (a heatmap of angles per residue) and, below it, the 3-D structure it decodes to - and define the variable once in a small colour-coded chemical schematic between them.

figures.title: FourCastNet: A Global Data-driven High-resolution Weather Model using Adaptive Fourier Neural Operators

taxonomy.task: global medium-range weather forecasting

arrangement.units: Two round-cornered framed regions: (a) the AFNO architecture filling the left half; a right frame holding (b) fine-tuning, (c) precipitation model and (d) inference as three unframed sub-panels stacked top to bottom, each titled with its letter.
arrangement.inputs_as: a tilted 3-D stack of real gridded weather maps with a patch grid overlay and a dotted list of channel names fanning into its layers; in (b)-(d) a bold symbol X(k) entering from the left
arrangement.losses_at: none in (a); in (b) and (c) small L2 boxes sit above the model chain, fed by X_true / p_true arrows from the top and outputting 'loss' upward
arrangement.shared: the same 'AFNO model' box is drawn twice in (b) for the two unrolled steps; in (c) and (d) the backbone is a separate box with a bold outline (frozen), marked by an asterisk footnote in (c)

insights.structure: The left half is a vertical AFNO stack inside one frame, and the right half stacks three small block diagrams (fine-tuning, precipitation model, inference) that reuse the same 'AFNO model' box.
insights.data: Input and output are tilted 3-D stacks of real jet-colormap weather maps, the input overlaid with an h x w patch grid and a dotted list of channel names whose thin lines fan into each layer, with a row of p x p patch thumbnails between the stack and the embedding.
insights.emphasis: The spatial-mixing block is the only one expanded, through dashed zoom lines into an FFT / Multiply Frequency / IFFT column and again into a z -> MLP -> S(.) box, while all blocks stay uncoloured.
insights.flow: Panel (a) reads bottom to top on short parallel up-arrows between full-width blocks; panels (b)-(d) read left to right, with ground truth dropping in from above to L2 boxes and a loop arrow in (d) feeding X(k+1) back to the backbone input.
insights.avoid: The left half's dashed zoom lines cross each other and the detail boxes float at the frame's left edge, so it is hard to tell which zoom belongs to Spatial vs Channel Mixing; the channel-name list is also tiny italic text.

core.what: A bottom-to-top AFNO stack in panel (a): a tilted stack of real weather maps (input at time t) -> p x p patches -> patch embedding -> L layers of spatial and channel mixing -> linear decoder -> the output map stack at t + Δt.

relations.form: panel (a): one vertical column of rounded boxes with many short parallel arrows between them, input map stack at the bottom, output map stack at the top
dashed lines fan left from Spatial Mixing to an FFT / Multiply Frequency / IFFT column, and from Multiply Frequency again to a z -> MLP -> S(.) box; Channel Mixing fans to a smaller z -> MLP box
the input stack carries an h x w patch grid over latitude/longitude axes, with a row of p x p patch thumbnails between it and the embedding
a dotted list of channel names (U10, V10, T2m, ..., TCWV) sends thin lines fanning into the individual layers of the input stack
panels (b) fine-tuning, (c) precipitation model and (d) inference stacked on the right, each a left-to-right chain reusing the same rectangular 'AFNO model' box
(b) unrolls two AFNO steps X(k) -> X(k+1) -> X(k+2) with an L2 loss at each; (d) feeds X(k+1) back to the backbone input by a loop line over the top

channels.colour: no colour coding on the diagram; colour appears only inside the weather-map data (jet colormap)
channels.shape: rounded box = layer in (a), square-cornered box = model in (b)-(d), tilted image stack = field data, small square = loss
channels.line: solid arrows for all flow; dashed lines = zoom callouts; thin grey lines = channel-to-layer mapping
channels.frame: a large rounded frame per half: (a) on the left, (b)-(d) together on the right; rounded inner frame = 'L layers' repeated block

quality.strengths: Input and output are real stacked weather fields with the patch grid and channel list drawn on them, so the data's shape is visible; the frequency-domain mixing (the contribution) is the only block opened, twice; the three usage panels reuse one AFNO box so they read as the same model in different roles.
quality.weaknesses: With no colour channel, the opened Spatial Mixing column and its source box are tied only by thin dashed lines that cross the Channel Mixing callout; the zooms sit left of the stack and make the main column off-centre; the fan of thin channel lines is dense; the (c) panel explains the frozen backbone in a footnote instead of a visual code.

figures.lesson: Put real data at both ends of a vertical pipeline as 3-D map stacks and keep every block uncoloured, then expand only the novel layer through dashed zoom-in boxes on the side so the contribution is the one place with extra detail.

figures.title: Feature Pyramid Networks for Object Detection

taxonomy.task: multi-scale feature pyramid for object detection

arrangement.units: One overview (two pyramids side by side, predict boxes at the right) above a dashed detail frame for the merge block; the detail is linked by dashed leader lines, not set off as a separate titled panel.
arrangement.inputs_as: a faded real photo as the lowest, orange-outlined plane of the left pyramid
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn ('predict' boxes at each right-hand level)
arrangement.shared: none drawn (the caption-level fact that heads are shared across levels is not shown)

insights.structure: A shrinking bottom-up pyramid of planes sits on the left, a top-down pyramid of equal levels on the right, joined by one horizontal arrow per level, with a dashed detail frame for the merge block placed underneath.
insights.data: Feature levels are unfilled oblique planes whose outline weight grows with depth on the left, the input is a faded photo as the lowest plane, and outputs are small 'predict' text boxes.
insights.emphasis: The new top-down pathway is the uniformly heavy-outlined right pyramid, and its lateral merge is enlarged in a dashed zoom frame showing '1x1 conv', '2x up' and a circled plus.
insights.flow: Read up the left pyramid on short arrows, across on lateral arrows, down the right pyramid, then right to 'predict'; in the zoom, the lateral input enters from the left and the upsampled input from the top.
insights.avoid: The overview has no labels at all (no stage names, no scales), so the meaning of outline weight and the two pyramids is left entirely to the caption.

core.what: A shrinking bottom-up pyramid of planes on the left faces a top-down pyramid on the right, joined by one horizontal lateral arrow per level, so each output level visibly merges its same-scale bottom-up feature with the level above.

relations.form: one lateral arrow per level from a left plane to the matching right plane, meeting the downward top-down arrow inside that plane
left pyramid read bottom to top on short up-arrows from the photo plane through planes that shrink with depth; right pyramid read top to bottom on short down-arrows
a small dashed square on the middle right plane opens, by two dashed lines, into a large dashed frame below showing '1x1 conv' from the left, '2x up' from above and a circled plus
each right-pyramid level sends its own arrow to an identical 'predict' text box to the right

channels.colour: orange outline = the input image plane; blue outlines = feature maps, with outline weight growing with depth on the left and uniformly heavy on the right (weight = semantic strength)
channels.shape: oblique plane = feature map (size = resolution), plain box = operation or prediction head, circled plus = sum
channels.line: grey solid arrows for all flow; dashed = zoom region and its frame
channels.frame: dashed frame = enlarged merge block

quality.strengths: Position alone teaches the method: two pyramids facing each other with a lateral arrow per level show which scales are merged, plane size shows resolution and outline weight shows semantic strength; the merge block is opened in a tied dashed zoom with straight continuing arrows; the figure is compact.
quality.weaknesses: The lateral arrows into the right pyramid run close to the top-down arrows and the predict arrows, crowding the right side; the lateral arrows for the top two levels are bent and the photo plane's lateral is missing (correctly, but without saying so); predict boxes are text only.

figures.lesson: Encode feature strength as outline weight on the pyramid planes, and zoom one lateral merge into a dashed detail frame tied to it by dashed leader lines.

figures.title: SE(3) diffusion model with application to protein backbone generation

taxonomy.task: SE(3) protein backbone diffusion score network layer

arrangement.units: three unframed horizontal lanes (node in a grey orange-outlined container, edge, frame) in the left panel; a grey cyan-outlined EdgeUpdate detail panel at right
arrangement.inputs_as: small glyphs (cell columns, grid, frame axes) with bold math labels
arrangement.shared: updated node embedding feeds edge and backbone lanes

insights.structure: Left panel shows one layer as three horizontal lanes (node h through a grey NodeUpdate container, edge z through an EdgeUpdate box, frames T through a BackboneUpdate box); right panel opens EdgeUpdate with a small glyph legend beneath.
insights.data: Each lane's input is a tiny glyph: h0/h_l as green-yellow cell columns, z_l as a blue cell grid, T_l as a red three-armed frame; outputs are the bold symbols h_{l+1}, z_{l+1}, T_{l+1}.
insights.emphasis: Colour codes the stream: all NodeUpdate parts and arrows orange, all EdgeUpdate parts cyan (outline repeated in the zoom panel), frames black.
insights.flow: Left-to-right in each lane; the new node embedding drops down in orange into the edge and backbone updates, and inside the zoom h^m, h^n feed down into concatenations along the z line.
insights.avoid: Orange lines from z and T rise into the IPA box and cross the black lanes, which clutters the lower-left corner.

core.what: One network layer drawn as three horizontal lanes running left to right: node embedding h through a grey NodeUpdate container, edge embedding z through EdgeUpdate, frames T through BackboneUpdate, with the new h_{l+1} dropping down into the two lower lanes.

relations.form: three parallel left-to-right lanes stacked top to bottom, each starting at a small input glyph (cell column h, cell grid z, red three-armed frame T) and ending at a bold output symbol
orange lines rise from z_l and T_l into Invariant Point Attention inside NodeUpdate; orange lines from h_{l+1} drop down into EdgeUpdate and BackboneUpdate
inside NodeUpdate a left-to-right chain IPA -> + -> concat -> Transformer -> + -> MLP, with h_0 via a Linear above and a skip line below
right panel opens EdgeUpdate as a larger grey box with the same cyan outline: two Linear branches on h^m, h^n concatenated with z^nm, then MLP, skip and Linear

channels.colour: the stream that owns a block: orange = NodeUpdate parts and node arrows, cyan = EdgeUpdate (repeated in the zoom panel outline and arrows), black = frame lane; glyph fills (green-yellow node cells, blue edge grid, red frame) are a separate data colour code
channels.shape: cell column / cell grid / three-armed frame = node, edge and frame data; dotted-outline box = learned sub-module; circle glyphs = concatenate and skip, keyed under the right panel
channels.line: solid arrows coloured by stream
channels.frame: grey filled box = one update module (NodeUpdate container, BackboneUpdate, the opened EdgeUpdate)

quality.strengths: The three representations are drawn as nouns with their own glyph shape (column, grid, frame), the lanes make the per-type update visible, and the zoom panel is tied to EdgeUpdate by repeating its cyan outline; the merge glyphs are keyed.
quality.weaknesses: Orange carries both 'NodeUpdate' and 'h_{l+1} into the other updates', and the orange lines from z_l and T_l up into IPA cross the z lane's black arrow; the NodeUpdate container takes most of the space while BackboneUpdate, also method-specific, is a bare box; colour of glyph fills vs arrows are two unrelated codes.

figures.lesson: Draw the residue frame as a tiny three-axis glyph next to T and give it its own black lane under the coloured node and edge lanes, so the reader sees which stream updates geometry and which updates features.

figures.title: G-Retriever: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Textual Graph Understanding and Question Answering

taxonomy.task: question answering over textual graphs: retrieve a connected subgraph and give it to a frozen LLM as a graph token plus its textualised form

arrangement.units: four dashed panels, one per step, in a 2x2 grid with step titles on the frame lines
arrangement.inputs_as: a toy entity graph with quoted entity names and relation labels (top left) and the quoted question in a grey box (bottom left)
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; red arrows run from the answer tokens back down to the graph token and Projection in Step 4
arrangement.shared: the frozen LM that embeds nodes, edges and the query is drawn three times as separate grey boxes

insights.structure: Four dashed step panels in a 2x2 grid, the generation panel widest at the top right.
insights.data: Every intermediate is content: the entity graph, the quoted question, top-k node and edge lists, the pruned subgraph and the textualised node/edge table.
insights.emphasis: Trainable parts are the only yellow fills, with flame icons; frozen LMs carry snowflakes.
insights.flow: Down the left column (index, then retrieve into a Storage cylinder), right along the bottom to the subgraph, then up into the graph encoder and LLM; the subgraph-to-encoder arrow is the only drawn hand-off between panels.
insights.avoid: Do not typeset the retrieval and subgraph objectives as formulas in the panels, or leave the step-to-step hand-off undrawn.

core.what: graph embeddings and the query embedding meet at a Storage cylinder, the retrieved nodes and edges are listed as quoted text, and the connected subgraph built from them is redrawn as data

relations.form: four dashed step panels in a 2x2 grid, read down the left column then up the right
z_n and z_e from LM boxes and z_q from the question arrow into a Storage cylinder; retrieved nodes and edges listed in grey text boxes beside their top-k formulas
the subgraph S* is redrawn as the indexing panel's graph minus the pruned entities, keeping the entities' tints
a yellow graph token (from Graph Encoder and Projection) and blue text tokens (from the frozen text embedder over textualize(S*) and query q) enter the LLM as one row

channels.colour: pink = the question entity ('justin bieber', in the graph, the question and the subgraph), purple = the answer entity ('jaxon bieber'); yellow = trainable graph path, light blue = frozen LLM and its text tokens; red = arrows from the answer tokens back to the graph token (not keyed)
channels.shape: rounded grey boxes = frozen LMs, cylinder = storage, wide blue bars = LLM layers, small squares = tokens, grey text panels = retrieved lists and the textualised graph
channels.line: solid black arrows = data; solid and dashed red lines = the path back from the output tokens; dashed outlines = step panels and the z_n/z_e group
channels.frame: dashed rectangle = one step

quality.strengths: Data is drawn as data at every step: a toy graph with quoted entities, the question text, the retrieved node and edge lists, the subgraph and the textualised node/edge table fed to the LLM. The subgraph keeps the full graph's entity tints, so the cut is visible. Graph token and text tokens enter the LLM as one row told apart by colour. The generation step gets the widest panel.
quality.weaknesses: Retrieval and subgraph construction are given as typeset formulas (two argtopk lines and a prize-collecting argmax) rather than drawn. No arrow joins Step 2's retrieved lists to Step 3, so that hand-off is left to the step numbers. The panels run down, across and up, a U the reader must rebuild from the titles. The red backward path is not in the frozen/trainable key.

figures.lesson: Reuse the same toy graph in the indexing panel and the subgraph panel, the question entity and the answer entity in the same tints, so the retrieved subgraph reads as a cut of the full graph.

figures.title: Graph Attention Networks

taxonomy.task: node classification with attention-weighted neighbourhood aggregation

arrangement.units: two unframed panels side by side on whitespace: the attention-coefficient computation (left) and the multi-head neighbourhood aggregation around one node (right)
arrangement.inputs_as: left: a row of eight small unit circles under two curly braces W h_i and W h_j; right: neighbour feature nodes h2-h6 ringed around the centre node
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the figure shows the layer computation only
arrangement.shared: the attention mechanism of the left panel is not redrawn on the right; its output appears as alpha labels on each spoke

insights.structure: A narrow left panel (input units -> activation unit -> alpha_ij, stacked vertically) sits beside a wide right panel where the hub node h1 is ringed by five neighbours with an output node h1' off to the right.
insights.data: Every quantity is a white circle with a math label (h-vector, alpha_ij, h1'); feature vectors on the left are rows of tiny unit circles under curly braces, and attention weights are spoke labels rather than drawn values.
insights.emphasis: The three heads are the only coloured elements, each with its own line style, so multi-head attention stands out against the otherwise black line art.
insights.flow: Left panel reads bottom-to-top along converging arrows; right panel reads radially inward along the spokes to h1, then left-to-right along the thick concat/avg arrow to h1'.
insights.avoid: The head encoding (blue straight, green zigzag, purple wavy) has no key in the figure, and three parallel lines per spoke plus rotated alpha labels make the hub crowded.

core.what: Attention drawn on a toy graph: hub node h1 ringed by five neighbours h2..h6 plus a self-loop, each edge carrying three coloured head lines labelled alpha_1j, all converging on h1 and leaving as one bundle 'concat/avg' to h1'.

relations.form: a star neighbourhood of white circles around h1 with one spoke per neighbour and a self-loop on top, each spoke labelled with its attention coefficient
all spokes point into h1, then the three heads leave together as a thick braided bundle to the output node h1' on the right, labelled 'concat/avg'
three attention heads run in parallel on every spoke as three lines (blue straight, green and purple wavy) side by side
left panel: eight unit circles under two braces W h_i and W h_j all converge by straight arrows on one activation node, then softmax_j up to alpha_ij

channels.colour: attention head identity (blue, green, purple); everything else black
channels.shape: circle for every quantity: input units, activation, coefficient alpha_ij and node vectors alike
channels.line: line pattern repeats head identity (straight vs two wavy patterns) on top of colour; thickness of the outgoing bundle marks the aggregation

quality.strengths: The operation is drawn on a small instance of the structure it acts on, with the coefficients sitting on the edges they weight; the two panels separate how one coefficient is computed (left) from how coefficients aggregate a neighbourhood (right); the only colour is head identity.
quality.weaknesses: Head identity is carried redundantly by both colour and wavy line pattern, and the triple lines on each spoke make the hub crowded and the self-loop tangled; units, operations and outputs are all the same white circle; nothing ties alpha_ij on the left to the spoke labels on the right.

figures.lesson: Show multi-head attention on a graph as one hub node with neighbour spokes, each spoke carrying one parallel arrow per head in a distinct colour and line style, merging into one output arrow.

figures.title: Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks

taxonomy.task: semi-supervised node classification on graphs

arrangement.units: a schematic panel (two card stacks for input and output layers joined across a whitespace gap labelled 'hidden layers') and an unframed scatter-plot panel on the right, separated only by whitespace
arrangement.inputs_as: a small 4-node graph with node features X1-X4 inside the input-layer card stack
arrangement.losses_at: right of the output layer: dashed double-headed arrows from Z1 and Z4 to label nodes Y1 and Y4, coloured like their nodes
arrangement.shared: the graph structure (black edges) is redrawn identically inside the input and output layer stacks

insights.structure: Two card-stack layers (input C, output F) hold the same 4-node graph and face each other across a narrow gap marked 'hidden layers', with label nodes Y outside the output stack and a scatter plot filling the right third.
insights.data: Node features and outputs are tinted circles with math labels (X_i, Z_i), channel depth is the offset stack of card outlines, and the result is a dense t-SNE scatter of coloured dots.
insights.emphasis: Per-node colours carried through the connecting lines and dashed label arrows make the propagation and the partial labelling the visible point; there is no highlight box.
insights.flow: Left-to-right: each input node sends a curved line in its colour that converges into one dashed line through the hidden-layer gap, then fans out to its matching output node.
insights.avoid: The t-SNE panel sits in the same figure without a divider or label, and its class colours (red, yellow, grey, etc.) are unrelated to the node colours of the schematic, inviting a false match.

core.what: The same four-node graph drawn twice, as an input card stack (X_i, C channels) and an output card stack (Z_i, F channels) facing each other across a 'hidden layers' gap: the network maps a graph to the same graph with new node features.

relations.form: a toy graph of four nodes with black edges, identical topology in the input and output stacks, each stack an offset pile of card outlines for channels
input layer on the left, a dashed 'hidden layers' gap in the middle, output layer on the right
per-node coloured lines from X_1..X_4 bundle into the gap and fan back out to Z_1..Z_4
dashed double-headed arrows pair Z_1 with label Y_1 and Z_4 with Y_4 outside the output stack, and only those two, so partial labelling is visible

channels.colour: node identity, carried from X_i through its line to Z_i and Y_i; in the t-SNE scatter on the right the colours mean class, a different code reusing similar hues
channels.shape: circle = node, card stack = layer (offset depth = channel count), dot = embedded node
channels.line: black solid = graph edge, coloured curves = per-node propagation through the network, dashed double-headed = label supervision

quality.strengths: The method acts on graphs and the figure draws a graph in and the same graph out, so 'node features change, topology stays' is read from position; partial supervision is visible as only two dashed label pairings; channel depth is the card-stack offset.
quality.weaknesses: The bundle through 'hidden layers' hides what a layer does (no neighbourhood aggregation is drawn); per-node lines cross the graph edges on the input side; the t-SNE scatter takes the right third with no axis or key and its colours mean class, not node, so colour carries two meanings across the figure.

figures.lesson: To show a graph network, draw the same small graph inside each layer, keep one colour per node across layers, and attach supervision only to the few labelled nodes with dashed double arrows.

figures.title: Protein Representation Learning by Geometric Structure Pretraining

taxonomy.task: protein structure representation (relational GNN with edge message passing)
taxonomy.note: paradigm: relational GCN (R-GCN) style message passing

arrangement.units: three columns titled at top and separated by dotted rules; each method column has a dashed rounded inset of the local neighbourhood above per-type rows
arrangement.inputs_as: 3-D stick render of the protein in the top-left
arrangement.shared: edge-type colour key across all columns

insights.structure: Three titled columns divided by dotted vertical rules: protein graph construction, the relational GNN update of node 4, and the same update one level up for edge (4,7).
insights.data: A real stick model of a residue chain with circled residue centres sits top-left; the graph is numbered nodes with coloured directed edges, and features are small dark bars inside coloured frames.
insights.emphasis: Edge type is the single colour key (blue/yellow sequential, red kNN, green radius) given once in a rounded legend and reused for arrows, row frames and per-type weight bars.
insights.flow: Down within column 1 via a large hollow arrow, then left-to-right in columns 2-3 where each row's per-type transform curves into a circled-plus sum on the right.
insights.avoid: Column 3 recolours edge types (orange, purple, black) that the column-1 legend does not define.

core.what: A protein residue chain becomes a numbered graph with coloured edge types, and the relational update is drawn on that graph: node 4's neighbourhood (dashed inset) is split into one row per edge type, each row's features passed through its own weight and summed into node 4.

relations.form: three titled columns left to right separated by dotted rules: graph construction, node-level relational GNN, edge-level message passing
column 1: a stick model with circled residue centres, a hollow block arrow down to a 7-node graph whose directed edges are coloured by type
columns 2 and 3 each start with a dashed inset of the local neighbourhood (node 4; edge (4,7) in a line graph) taken from the graph
below each inset, one coloured row per relation (feature bars in a frame -> a coloured weight bar), curved coloured arrows converging on one circled-plus and the output bar
column 3 repeats column 2's row-and-sum skeleton one level up, with edges as nodes

channels.colour: edge type, keyed once in the legend (blue / yellow sequential, red kNN, green radius) and reused for graph arrows, row frames and weight bars in column 2; column 3's row frames and arrows switch to orange, blue, black and purple, which are not in the legend, so colour changes meaning between columns
channels.shape: numbered circle = residue node, rounded labelled box = edge-as-node, dark bar = feature vector, tinted bar = relation-specific weight, circled plus = sum
channels.line: coloured arrows = typed messages, hollow block arrow = construction step, dotted vertical rules = column dividers
channels.frame: dashed rounded box = local neighbourhood inset; coloured rectangle = features grouped by relation

quality.strengths: The relational aggregation is drawn as geometry: one row per edge type with its own weight, converging on one sum, under the neighbourhood it comes from; the edge-type colour key is taught once and carried from graph arrows into rows; columns 2 and 3 share a skeleton so the edge-level extension reads as the same operation one level up.
quality.weaknesses: Column 3's colours (orange, purple, black) are unkeyed and conflict with column 2's edge-type meaning; the converging arrows are long curves that cross; the stick model in column 1 is small and the circled residues are hard to map to graph node numbers.

figures.lesson: Fix one colour per edge type in the graph-construction panel and reuse it for the per-relation rows of the message-passing panels, so the reader can follow sequential, radius and kNN edges from the protein to the aggregation.

figures.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior

taxonomy.task: believable agent memory, reflection and planning

arrangement.units: one spine with a dashed sub-group around the memory part; Plan and Reflect float outside
arrangement.inputs_as: a 'Perceive' process box
arrangement.shared: memory stream read and written by both loops

insights.structure: A straight spine Perceive -> Memory Stream -> Retrieve -> Retrieved Memories -> Act, with the memory part enclosed in a dashed grey 'Generative Agent Memory' rectangle and Plan above, Reflect below outside it.
insights.data: No data shown; processes are white rounded boxes with italic labels and data stores are bevelled grey 3-D boxes with bold labels.
insights.emphasis: Memory Stream is the largest box with the heaviest bold text, and the two bevelled store boxes stand out against the flat process boxes.
insights.flow: Left-to-right along the spine, with two mirror arcs leaving Retrieved Memories, one over the top through Plan and one under the bottom through Reflect, both returning into Memory Stream.
insights.avoid: The bevelled 3-D boxes look dated; encode stores by a flat shape or fill instead.

core.what: A left-to-right spine Perceive -> Memory Stream -> Retrieve -> Retrieved Memories -> Act, with the memory store and retrieved set drawn as bevelled store boxes inside a dashed 'Generative Agent Memory' frame on the main flow.

relations.form: one horizontal spine of five boxes across the full width, Perceive at the left edge and Act at the right
Memory Stream (largest box, bold) and Retrieved Memories as bevelled grey 3-D boxes with Retrieve between them, all inside a dashed grey frame
two mirror-image arcs leave Retrieved Memories, one up to Plan and one down to Reflect, each curving back into Memory Stream, forming two loops above and below the spine

channels.colour: none; grey only marks the store boxes
channels.shape: bevelled 3-D box with bold label = data store, flat rounded box with italic label = process
channels.line: solid black arrows for all flow; dashed rectangle = memory subsystem boundary
channels.frame: dashed grey rectangle = the generative agent memory as one unit

quality.strengths: Shape separates stores from processes consistently (bevelled bold vs flat italic), the memory stream is the biggest element, and the plan / reflect feedback loops are symmetric arcs above and below a straight spine.
quality.weaknesses: No memory is drawn as data (no example observation, plan or reflection), so what is stored and retrieved is never shown; the retrieval scoring that defines the method is absent; the loops leave Retrieved Memories from its top and bottom edges rather than continuing a line, and Plan/Reflect sit outside the memory frame although they write into it.

figures.lesson: Separate stores from operations by shape alone (bevelled square plaques with bold labels for memories, light rounded boxes with italic verbs for processes) and route the plan and reflect loops as symmetric arcs above and below the spine that both write back into the main memory.

figures.title: Genie: Generative Interactive Environments

taxonomy.task: learning an action-controllable generative world model from unlabelled video

arrangement.units: one unframed left-to-right strip: input frame stack, two stacked module branches with their token rows, one merging module, output frame stack
arrangement.inputs_as: a stack of real platformer-game frames with a curly brace labelled 'T frames'
arrangement.shared: the input frames feed both branches through one forking line

insights.structure: A fork-and-merge: one input feeds two stacked parallel modules whose outputs reconverge on a third module, so the two-branch-then-fuse structure is visible before any label is read.
insights.data: Inputs and outputs are real game frames stacked with a 'T frames' brace, and both intermediate representations are drawn as token rows (tall navy bars for z, short yellow squares for a-tilde) between the module that makes them and the module that consumes them.
insights.emphasis: Nothing is singled out as new; the three modules carry equal size and saturation, separated only by hue.
insights.flow: Strictly left to right with short orthogonal black arrows: one fork after the input stack, one right-angle merge of the two token rows before the Dynamics model, one straight arrow to the output frames.
insights.avoid: The two token rows merge at a bare line junction, so how z and a-tilde are combined is not drawn, and line style does not mark which branch is used only in training.

core.what: input frames fork into two stacked branches (video tokenizer, latent action model) whose token rows converge by right-angle lines on one Dynamics model

relations.form: navy token row from the upper branch and yellow token row from the lower branch join in one right-angle merge into the Dynamics model box
the Video tokenizer and Latent action model sit one above the other in two equal-width parallel branches fed by a single forking line from the input stack
one left-to-right axis: input frame stack, modules, token rows, Dynamics model, output frame stack

channels.shape: rounded rectangle = module; solid bar / square = token (tall bar = video token, small square = latent action); stacked frames = video data
channels.line: one style only: thin black orthogonal arrows for data flow
channels.frame: none; no panels or containers

quality.strengths: The core fork-and-merge is pure geometry; each colour has one meaning (module identity carried onto its tokens); both compared representations are drawn as token rows between maker and consumer; real frames as input and output; all lines short, straight and orthogonal with a single fork and a single merge.
quality.weaknesses: Space does not follow novelty: the latent action model, tokenizer and dynamics model are equal-sized boxes, so the figure does not say which part is new; the merge of z and a-tilde is a bare junction; training-only vs inference paths are not distinguished by line style; no decoding step is drawn between the Dynamics model and the output frames.

figures.lesson: Colour each module's output tokens the same as the module, so when two branches merge into one model the reader sees which representation came from which branch without a legend.

figures.title: GeoDiff: a Geometric Diffusion Model for Molecular Conformation Generation

taxonomy.task: molecular conformation generation

arrangement.units: one unframed horizontal chain with renders under selected states
arrangement.inputs_as: grey noise state C^T with a tangled molecule render
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: One wide strip of state circles C^T ... C^t, C^{t-1} ... C^0 from left to right with ball-and-stick molecules tucked under three of them; no containers.
insights.data: Molecules are 3-D ball-and-stick renders: a tangled one under C^T, a ghosted trail of translucent overlapping copies near C^{t-1}, and a clean fused-ring molecule under C^0.
insights.emphasis: Fill alone separates noise from data: noisy states are grey circles and the final clean state is white; the conditioning on the graph G appears in the reverse label p_theta(C^{t-1}|G, C^t).
insights.flow: Solid arrows run left-to-right for the learned reverse process with its label above; a dashed curved arrow beneath returns from C^{t-1} to C^t for the forward q.
insights.avoid: Like most diffusion teasers it omits the denoising network, so it cannot serve as a model figure on its own.

core.what: A single left-to-right diffusion chain of state circles C^T -> ... -> C^t -> C^{t-1} -> ... -> C^0, with ball-and-stick molecules under three states showing a tangled conformation becoming a clean one.

relations.form: one horizontal row of circles joined by solid arrows, with a dashed arrow curving back from C^{t-1} to C^t for the forward noising q
3-D ball-and-stick renders tucked under C^T (tangled), near C^{t-1} (a ghosted trail of translucent copies) and under C^0 (clean fused-ring molecule)
conditioning on the molecular graph G appears only inside the reverse-step label p_theta(C^{t-1} | G, C^t), not as a drawn input

channels.colour: fill = noise level: grey circles = noisy states, white circle = clean C^0
channels.shape: circle = state, ball-and-stick = conformation
channels.line: solid arrow = learned reverse step, dashed curved arrow = forward noising

quality.strengths: Very compact; the denoising is shown as data (tangled to clean molecule) under the chain it belongs to, and the ghosted trail near C^{t-1} hints at atoms moving between steps; forward and reverse differ by line style.
quality.weaknesses: The conditioning graph G, central to the method, is only a symbol in a formula label; the method's equivariant network is not drawn; the molecules sit loosely beside rather than under their states, and the ghosted trail overlaps the ellipsis arrow so it is hard to tell which state it shows.

figures.lesson: Show what a denoising step does to the geometry as a ghosted trail of overlapping translucent molecule copies fading into the solid one, placed under the chain's latent circles, and fill clean-data circles white against grey noisy ones.

figures.title: Geometry-Informed Neural Operator for Large-Scale 3D PDEs

taxonomy.task: surrogate prediction of 3-D PDE solutions (surface pressure) on varying irregular geometries

arrangement.units: two unframed rows separated by whitespace: a block schematic on top and the rendered car pipeline below
arrangement.inputs_as: a grey 'Input Samples' box on top; a shaded 3-D car mesh below
arrangement.shared: the two GNO boxes are identical green boxes, and the two lattices below them are drawn the same way

insights.structure: Two aligned rows, abstract blocks on top and the same pipeline on a rendered car below, so the schematic and the instance explain each other.
insights.data: The input is a shaded car mesh, intermediates are green point clouds and wireframe lattices, and the output is the point-cloud car coloured by predicted values.
insights.emphasis: The operators are the only saturated-colour boxes; the red ball is the one accent and marks the graph neighbourhood that maps points to a lattice node and back.
insights.flow: Both rows read left to right on straight grey arrows; red and grey dashed lines between ball and lattice show the geometry-to-grid and grid-to-geometry maps.
insights.avoid: Green fills the operator boxes and also colours the mesh, points and lattices, and the output colour map has no key.

core.what: the operator chain drawn on one car: mesh to point cloud, a red neighbourhood ball mapping points onto a latent lattice, Fourier layers on the lattice, and a ball mapping back to points

relations.form: the bottom row renders each stage on the car: points, lattice, lattice, points, with a red ball and dashed lines showing the neighbourhood that links points and one lattice node
Input Samples, GNO, FNO, GNO, Prediction on one horizontal line with 'discretize' and 'query' labels on the end arrows
the top block row is placed over the bottom rendered row column by column, each block's role written under it, so a block and its geometry share a column

channels.line: solid grey arrows = flow; red dashed = points-to-lattice neighbourhood; grey dashed = lattice-to-points query
channels.frame: none; the only rounded frame encloses the Fourier-layer glyph

quality.strengths: The method is drawn on a small instance of its structure, as derive.md asks: the irregular point cloud, the regular latent lattice and the neighbourhood ball that maps between them are visible as geometry; the abstract row sits over the concrete row so labels need not be repeated; every arrow is straight and left to right; the operators are the only saturated boxes.
quality.weaknesses: Green carries both 'learned operator' and 'geometry'; the output colour map is unkeyed; the two rows are only roughly column-aligned (the second GNO box sits to the right of the second lattice it acts on); grey input/output boxes with white text are low-contrast; the SDF features the caption says are concatenated before FNO are not drawn.

figures.title: GLIGEN: Open-Set Grounded Text-to-Image Generation

taxonomy.task: grounded text-to-image generation

arrangement.units: overview panel (pale blue-grey rectangle) and zoom panel (pale-pink rectangle with thin orange border, titled top-left), side by side
arrangement.inputs_as: row of purple visual token squares
arrangement.shared: token colour legend

insights.structure: Left: a pale blue-grey panel stacking Self-Attention, Gated Self-Attention and Cross-Attention bars with token rows between them; right: a pale-pink bordered zoom panel of the gated layer.
insights.data: Tokens are rows of coloured squares (purple visual, yellow caption, green grounding) with a legend strip under the left panel; grey fan lines between rows show which tokens attend to which.
insights.emphasis: Frozen layers are blue with a snowflake and the inserted layer salmon with a flame; in the zoom, the gate gamma (init as 0) is the only red text beside a circled-times.
insights.flow: Bottom-to-top through the stack; two thin orange lines fan from the gated bar's right end to the zoom panel, where a skip line runs up the right side into a circled-plus.
insights.avoid: The dense grey all-to-all fan lines between token rows add noise and are hard to read as attention patterns.

core.what: A new salmon Gated Self-Attention layer is inserted between frozen blue Self-Attention and Cross-Attention bars; grounding tokens (green) join the visual token row only at that layer, and the zoom panel shows the gamma gate scaling its output before the residual sum.

relations.form: left panel bottom to top: visual token row -> Self-Attention -> row + green grounding tokens -> Gated Self-Attention -> row + yellow caption tokens -> Cross-Attention -> visual output row

grounding tokens are drawn as green squares concatenated to the left of the visual row entering the gated layer; caption tokens as yellow squares entering cross-attention; grey fan lines show which tokens attend to which
two orange lines flare from the Gated Self-Attention bar to the corners of a pale-pink bordered panel on the right that opens it
in the zoom, the self-attention output (grounding slots dashed, discarded) is multiplied by gamma (red, 'init as 0') at a circled-times and added to the skip line from the input row at a circled-plus

channels.colour: two codes, both keyed: token type for squares (purple visual, yellow caption, green grounding, legend below) and training status for layer bars (blue + snowflake frozen, salmon + flame trained); red is reserved for gamma
channels.shape: square = token, wide rounded bar = attention layer, circled glyphs = multiply and add, dashed square = dropped token slot
channels.line: thin grey lines = attention connectivity, black arrows = data flow in the zoom, orange lines = zoom callout
channels.frame: pale blue-grey panel = the UNet attention block; pink bordered panel = the opened new layer

quality.strengths: Tokens are drawn as nouns with a keyed type colour, so where grounding enters (only the new layer) is read from position; frozen vs trained is a separate keyed code on a different element type, so no channel is overloaded; the zoom is tied by flaring lines and the gate gamma is the single red element; dropped grounding outputs are drawn as dashed slots.
quality.weaknesses: The dense grey attention fans between rows add ink without distinguishing attention patterns; the skip line in the zoom runs out to the right edge and back in a long orthogonal detour; the left panel is narrow relative to the empty space beside the legend.

figures.lesson: Trainable versus frozen is encoded twice at once (salmon bar with a flame vs blue bars with snowflakes), and the salmon tint carries into the zoomed detail panel so the inserted layer is found and read without the caption.

figures.title: Grounded Language-Image Pre-training

taxonomy.task: phrase grounding / open-vocabulary object detection

arrangement.units: Two horizontal lanes, the text lane above the visual lane, with fusion blocks between them; the lanes meet in a word-region score matrix at the right.
arrangement.inputs_as: the prompt as coloured text in boxes above, the real photo with coloured boxes below
arrangement.losses_at: both losses leave the matrix at the far right edge (alignment loss, localization loss)
arrangement.shared: fusion blocks drawn between the lanes with short vertical arrows into each

insights.structure: A green text lane (Text Encoder, BERT Layers) sits above a blue visual lane (Visual Encoder, DyHead Modules) with yellow Fusion blocks stacked between them under a 'Deep Fusion' label, and both lanes run right into an N x M word-region score matrix.
insights.data: The prompt is quoted with phrases coloured to match the coloured boxes on the real photo at the left; the matrix's rows are photo crops of detected regions and its columns are word-feature token cells, each cell holding O_i·P_j.
insights.emphasis: Colour-matched words and boxes (green woman, yellow blow dryer, cyan goggles) make the grounding idea visible before any block is read, and the large matrix is the visual destination of both lanes.
insights.flow: Left to right in two parallel rows, with short vertical arrows P_i2t / O_t2i crossing up and down through the fusion blocks; both losses exit to the far right of the matrix.
insights.avoid: Word-token cells split words mid-token ('Pers on', 'Bicyc le') and the two stacked token rows partly overlap, which reads as a rendering glitch.

core.what: Region features (rows, as photo crops) and word features (columns, as token cells) meet in one N x M word-region alignment matrix at the right, each cell O_i·P_j, so detection is drawn as matching regions to words.

relations.form: a matrix with region crops O_1..O_N down its left edge and word-token cells P_1..P_M across its top, the matched cells shaded grey, feeding Alignment Loss on the right
a green text lane (Text Encoder -> P^0 -> BERT Layers) above a blue visual lane (Visual Encoder -> O^0 -> DyHead Modules), both running left to right
yellow Fusion blocks stacked between the two lanes under 'Deep Fusion', exchanging P_i2t up and O_t2i down at every layer, repeated with an ellipsis
input drawn as data: a real photo with coloured boxes and quoted prompts whose phrases share those colours (woman green, blow dryer yellow, goggles cyan)
the region features feed both the alignment matrix and, by a grey line along the bottom, the Localization Loss

channels.colour: modality for blocks (green = text, blue = visual, yellow = fusion); the same hues also tie prompt phrases to image boxes (green woman, yellow blow dryer, cyan goggles), so green and yellow carry both modality/module and object identity
channels.shape: rounded box = module (dotted outline = encoder), cell = token feature, photo crop = region, grid = score matrix
channels.line: coloured arrows = lane flow (green text, blue visual), grey arrows = cross-modal exchange and loss paths
channels.frame: green rectangles = prompts

quality.strengths: The objective is drawn as a matrix whose rows are real region crops and columns are word tokens, so what is matched is visible; the two encoders run as lanes with fusion literally between them; colour-matched prompt words and image boxes make grounding readable from the input alone.
quality.weaknesses: Green and yellow each carry two meanings (text lane / object 'woman'; fusion block / object 'blow dryer'); the word-feature strip is drawn twice with offset, crowding the matrix top; the Localization Loss line runs along the matrix bottom far from the region features it uses.

figures.lesson: Draw grounding-style detection as a word-by-region matrix whose rows are cropped thumbnails of the detected boxes and whose columns are the prompt's word tokens, with the same word colours used for the box outlines on the input photo.

figures.title: GNFactor: Multi-Task Real Robot Learning with Generalizable Neural Feature Fields

arrangement.inputs_as: a real RGB front-view photo stacked above its depth point cloud; a quoted instruction enters from the top
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn: the renderer's RGB and diffusion-feature images sit below the volume with no target beside them, and the Q-value symbols end the policy branch at the right edge

insights.emphasis: The 'Deep 3D Volume' is the only large 3-D object and carries a bold title; the frozen language encoder is marked with a snowflake.

rendering drawn on the volume itself: thin blue rays with circles sample cells of its wireframe lattice and pull out blue cubes

channels.shape: trapezoid = network, large cube = feature volume, small cubes = tokens, tilted tiles = rendered images
channels.line: thick solid arrows coloured by branch; thin blue rays ending in circles = rendering samples
channels.frame: no frames; orange borders mark the renderer's output tiles

quality.strengths: The shared representation is the biggest, central object with both consumers attached on two sides, so 'shared' is geometry. The input is a real photo and its point cloud, and the rendered outputs are drawn as images. Arrows are short, straight and coloured by branch.
quality.weaknesses: Blue marks both the policy branch and the render rays and sampled voxels. The reconstruction objective is not drawn: the rendered RGB and diffusion feature have no target or loss beside them. The renderer block overlaps the volume's lattice and hides its front cells.

figures.title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers

taxonomy.task: post-training weight quantization of LLMs
taxonomy.note: architecture 'other' = a layer-wise quantization procedure on one weight matrix; no network is drawn

arrangement.units: two unframed matrix panels side by side, each with a bold title above and a short plain caption below
arrangement.inputs_as: no separate inputs; the two matrices themselves are the objects
arrangement.shared: the current block is marked in both matrices with the same heavy outline, and a double-headed arrow links the two

insights.structure: Two matrices sit side by side as equals, the inverse Hessian on the left and the weight block on the right, joined by a double-headed arrow and keyed by one bottom legend.
insights.data: Matrices are drawn as plain rectangles: the Hessian's Cholesky factor is a grey staircase triangle and the weight matrix is vertical colour stripes whose hue says quantized or pending.
insights.emphasis: A heavy black frame around the current block, repeated on the matching rows of the Hessian, plus saturated orange/blue shades set the active block apart from pale finished and pending parts.
insights.flow: Read the two bold titles left to right, then the captions below each; the only connector is a horizontal double-headed arrow with no label.
insights.avoid: The double-headed arrow carries no label, so what passes between the Hessian and the weights is left to the caption.

core.what: The algorithm drawn on the two matrices it uses: the inverse Hessian's Cholesky factor (grey staircase triangle) on the left and the weight matrix as column stripes on the right, the current block framed heavily in both and joined by a double-headed arrow.

relations.form: two equal-sized matrices side by side as rectangles; the Hessian's lower part a grey staircase, the weights vertical stripes whose shade says quantized (orange) or still to be updated (blue)
a heavy black frame around block i in the weight matrix and around the matching rows of the Hessian, with a double-headed arrow between the two frames
column order left to right in the weight matrix: pale orange finished, saturated orange current-quantized, a white column being quantized, saturated blue current-pending, pale blue later columns

channels.colour: weight status, keyed in the bottom legend: orange = quantized, blue = unquantized and being updated; saturation adds a second meaning, in or out of the current block; the Hessian's blue shades reuse the weight blues without a key for what they mean there
channels.shape: rectangle = matrix, staircase = triangular Cholesky factor
channels.line: heavy black frame = current block (one meaning, used in both matrices); double-headed arrow = the two are used together
channels.frame: heavy black rectangle = the active block

quality.strengths: The method's lazy block update is drawn as geometry on the matrices themselves: one heavy frame marks the same block in both, and column colour shows the quantized / pending boundary moving left to right; the legend is one strip.
quality.weaknesses: Saturation carries a second meaning (inside the current block) that is not keyed; the Hessian's blue shading has no stated meaning; the white column under quantization is unlabeled; the double-headed arrow says only 'related', not which direction information flows.

figures.lesson: Show a column-by-column algorithm on a matrix by colouring stripes by state (done, current, pending) and outlining the current block with the same heavy frame in every matrix it touches.

figures.title: GraphCast: Learning skillful medium-range global weather forecasting

a greyed GAEs row underneath with the same three-box skeleton (GNN Encoder, MLP or Propagation, link / MSE reconstruction) branching from the input graph as prior work

channels.colour: grey fill = masked node or masked row; pale blue = learned representations (code grid, reconstructed node fills); blue underlined text = the method's own steps; greyed-out text and boxes = prior GAEs
channels.shape: numbered circle = node, bar glyph = node feature, cell grid = representation matrix, card stack = encoder layers
channels.line: hollow block arrows = pipeline steps; dashed rectangles = stage boxes (also used for the prior-work row); dash-dot timeline = phase spans
channels.frame: dashed box = one stage

quality.strengths: The representations are drawn as nouns between stages (code grid, re-masked grid, reconstructed features), masking is drawn on the graph and on the grid rows with one grey code, and the prior GAE pipeline sits underneath in grey with the same skeleton so the differences are located by position.
quality.weaknesses: Grey means both 'masked' and 'prior work' (greyed row); the method's novelties are marked only by blue underlined text rather than by space or fill; the graph is redrawn four times at similar size, so routine steps take as much space as the new re-mask step.

figures.lesson: Draw the baseline as a faded grey dashed row directly beneath the method row, one box per stage and aligned under its counterpart, so the reader compares stage by stage while the baseline never competes with the method for attention.

figures.title: Do Transformers Really Perform Bad for Graph Representation?

taxonomy.task: graph representation learning with structural encodings

arrangement.units: one framed figure with three columns: attention stack, encoding matrices, example graph
arrangement.inputs_as: a small coloured node-link graph v1-v5
arrangement.shared: a brace mapping the graph to all three encodings

insights.structure: A vertical attention block (Linear Q/K/V, MatMul, Scale, SoftMax, MatMul) on the left, two 5x5 encoding matrices (Spatial, Edge) in the middle, and the example 5-node graph on the right joined to them by a curly brace.
insights.data: Node feature and centrality encoding are coloured token rows at the bottom; spatial encoding is a blue-shade 5x5 grid and edge encoding a multi-colour grid whose cell colours match the dashed edge colours in the graph.
insights.emphasis: The encoding matrices are the largest, most colourful elements and inject into the plain attention block at the add node beside Scale, showing where the contribution plugs in.
insights.flow: Bottom to top through the attention block, with bracketed lines from the matrices entering sideways at the ⊕ before SoftMax; the brace reads right to left from graph to encodings.
insights.avoid: The bracket from the two matrices to the attention block is a thin, ambiguous line that can be read as feeding Linear V instead of the bias add.

core.what: Structural encodings derived from an example 5-node graph (right, tied by a curly brace) are drawn as 5x5 Spatial and Edge Encoding matrices and a Centrality Encoding row in the middle, and inject into a standard attention block on the left at a circled-plus before SoftMax.

relations.form: a 5-node graph with node sizes and fills varying and dashed coloured edges, joined by a brace to the 5x5 matrices indexed v1..v5 whose cells encode distances (blue shades) and edges (colours matching the graph's dashed edges)
left column bottom to top: node feature row -> Linear Q / K / V -> MatMul -> Scale -> circled-plus -> SoftMax -> MatMul

a single line from the matrices bracket runs left into the circled-plus between Scale and SoftMax as an attention bias; the Centrality Encoding row is added to the Node Feature row by a large circled-plus at the bottom

channels.colour: two codes: block fills mark operation types (blue MatMul, yellow Scale, green SoftMax, grey Linear), while in the encodings colour is data (blue shade = spatial distance, hue = edge type matched to the graph's dashed edges, node fills = node features); the green of SoftMax and of node features is unrelated
channels.shape: rounded box = operation, cell grid = encoding matrix, cell row = per-node vector, circle = graph node (size ~ centrality)
channels.line: solid arrows = attention data flow; dashed coloured lines = graph edges; a curly brace ties the graph to the encodings
channels.frame: one thin outer frame around the whole figure

quality.strengths: The contribution (the encodings) is the largest and most colourful part and is drawn as data indexed by node, between the graph that produces it and the attention it biases; edge-encoding cell colours match the graph's dashed edge colours so the mapping is visible.
quality.weaknesses: Block fills in the attention stack add an unkeyed colour code that competes with the data colours; the bias line from the matrices bends at a bracket and the V branch runs a long way up beside the stack; the centrality encoding's link to the graph (node size) is not stated.

figures.lesson: Colour the toy graph's dashed edges with the same hues as the edge-encoding matrix cells for those node pairs (grey cells for non-adjacent pairs) and tint its nodes like the node-feature strip, so each matrix cell traces to its edge by colour alone and one brace is enough to tie all encodings to the graph.

figures.title: From Local to Global: A GraphRAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization

taxonomy.task: query-focused summarization over a document corpus via an LLM-built knowledge graph

arrangement.units: Eight equal rounded boxes in two columns (four each) with no frames; a separate key row at the bottom repeats the two box styles.
arrangement.inputs_as: a box naming the input ('Source Documents'); no data drawn
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Eight same-size boxes form two columns joined at the bottom, the left column holding indexing products from documents down to the knowledge graph and the right column holding community products up to the global answer.
insights.data: Every intermediate is a named box (Text Chunks, Entities & Relationships, Graph Communities), and each transformation is a two-line label beside its arrow such as 'domain-tailored summarization'.
insights.emphasis: Stage membership is shown only by fill colour, lavender for indexing time and green for query time, with a key row at the bottom.
insights.flow: Read down the left column, across the bottom via 'community detection', then up the right column to 'Global Answer' at the top right.
insights.avoid: The knowledge graph and communities are drawn as plain text boxes, so the graph structure the method depends on never appears; a small node-link glyph would let the figure show it.

core.what: one chain of eight named products folded into a U: down the left column from Source Documents to Knowledge Graph, across the bottom via 'community detection', then up the right column to Global Answer

relations.form: same-size rounded boxes joined by short straight vertical arrows, each transformation written as a two-line label beside its arrow (e.g. 'domain-tailored summarization')

indexing-time vs query-time shown only by fill (lavender vs green), keyed by a bottom row 'Indexing Time | Pipeline Stage | Query Time'; the stage boundary falls inside the right column (Graph Communities and Community Summaries lavender, the top two green), not at the column split

channels.colour: fill = pipeline stage (lavender indexing time, green query time), keyed at the bottom
channels.shape: every box is the same rounded rectangle for documents, intermediates and the answer alike; no data vs operation distinction
channels.line: one line style: solid black arrows = processing steps, each labelled with its operation
channels.frame: none; columns are unframed

quality.strengths: Nouns are boxes and verbs are arrow labels, so every intermediate product (Text Chunks, Entities & Relationships, Community Summaries) is drawn; all arrows are short and straight and the U keeps the whole chain on one page width.
quality.weaknesses: The Knowledge Graph and Graph Communities the method is built on are text boxes, not a small node-link instance; the left/right column split does not match the colour-coded stage split, so position and colour say different things; all eight boxes are equal size, so nothing marks the novel community-summary step.

figures.lesson: For a pipeline whose steps are operations on data, make the boxes the intermediate data products and write each operation as a label on its arrow, folding the chain into a U so it fits a wide figure.

figures.title: Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs

taxonomy.task: inductive node embedding and node classification
taxonomy.note: training 'other' = the unsupervised graph-context objective, drawn as the graph pictogram output next to 'label'

arrangement.units: three unframed panels separated by whitespace, each a full copy of the same graph with a numbered caption beneath: sampling with dotted hop circles, aggregation with coloured arrows, prediction with output boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: the input graph itself: outlined circle nodes with bracketed feature column vectors next to the nodes
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the right panel ends in a 'label' box and a graph-context pictogram as the two prediction targets

insights.emphasis: Only the active neighbourhood is coloured (brown sampled edges in panel 1, green hop-2 and blue hop-1 arrows in panel 2) while the rest of the graph fades to light grey, and the target node is red in every panel.
insights.flow: Panels read left to right; inside panel 2 thick arrows run inward from green outer nodes to blue inner nodes to the red centre, and in panel 3 two black arrows leave the centre for the 'label' box and the graph-context pictogram.
insights.avoid: Hop colours are not consistent across panels (all sampled nodes are brown in panel 1 but blue/green per hop in panel 2), and the bracketed feature vectors are too small to read.

relations.form: three unframed panels left to right, each a full copy of the same graph with a numbered caption beneath (1. Sample neighborhood, 2. Aggregate, 3. Predict)
panel 1 marks two hops as dotted concentric circles labelled k=1 and k=2 around the red node and colours the sampled nodes and edges brown; the rest of the graph stays black outline

panel 2: thick green arrows run from hop-2 nodes into blue hop-1 nodes, and thick blue arrows from those into the red centre, with two arrow-shaped keys 'aggregator1' (blue) and 'aggregator2' (green) at top right
panel 3: two black arrows leave the centre node's feature vector for a 'label' box and a framed graph-context pictogram

channels.colour: red = target node in every panel; in panel 1 brown = sampled neighbourhood, in panel 2 blue/green = hop depth and its aggregator; light grey = inactive graph. The sampled nodes change colour between panels 1 and 2, so colour means 'sampled' in one panel and 'hop/aggregator' in the next
channels.shape: circles = nodes, bracketed column vectors = node features, boxes = outputs
channels.line: thin black/grey = graph edges, thick coloured arrows = sampling (panel 1) or message passing (panel 2), dotted circles = hop radius
channels.frame: none on panels; only the outputs in panel 3 are boxed

quality.strengths: The method's operations are drawn on a small graph instance, so a reader sees neighbourhood sampling and inward aggregation as geometry; the inactive graph fades to grey in panels 2-3 so only the active neighbourhood is salient; aggregation arrows are short and point inward to the target.
quality.weaknesses: Sampled nodes switch from brown (panel 1) to blue/green (panel 2), breaking one-meaning-per-colour across panels; the bracketed feature vectors are too small to read; the graph-context output is a tiny pictogram with no label.

figures.lesson: Redraw the same graph once per step and fade everything the step does not touch to light grey, keeping one fixed colour for the target node, so each panel shows only the active neighbourhood.

arrangement.units: two unframed halves separated by whitespace and a central pair of circular arrows: left the full graph with a bold sampled subgraph, right a three-row layered network of the sampled nodes
arrangement.inputs_as: the full graph of numbered circle nodes, sampled part bold and unsampled part pale grey
arrangement.shared: the sampled node IDs (0,1,2,3,5,7) appear in both halves and in every layer row on the right

insights.structure: Two unframed halves sit side by side: a numbered 10-node graph on the left and a three-row layered network on the right, joined by two curved arrows that form a circle between them.
insights.data: Nodes are numbered circles; the sampled ones (0,1,2,3,5,7) have bold dark outlines and thick edges while 4,6,8,9 are pale grey, and the right half repeats only the sampled IDs in each row with thin arrows following the subgraph's edges.
insights.emphasis: Contrast is only grey value: the sampled subgraph is dark and the rest faded, with no colour or named module.
insights.flow: The eye moves left to right through the circular arrows, which imply repetition, and inside the right half the arrows run bottom to top from layer to layer.
insights.avoid: There are no words at all (no 'sample', 'GCN' or layer names), so what the cycle and the rows mean relies entirely on the caption.

core.what: a sampled subgraph drawn bold inside a numbered 10-node graph on the left, and the same sampled node IDs unrolled into a three-row layered network on the right

relations.form: left: nodes 0,1,2,3,5,7 and their edges dark and thick, nodes 4,6,8,9 pale grey, all as numbered circles
two curved arrows forming a circle between the halves, implying sample-then-train repeated
right: three rows of the same six node IDs with thin upward arrows from row to row following the subgraph's edges (layer-wise propagation, bottom to top)
the sampled node IDs 0,1,2,3,5,7 reappear in every row of the right half, tying it to the bold subgraph on the left

channels.colour: none; grey value only: dark = sampled subgraph, pale grey = unsampled nodes
channels.shape: numbered circles = nodes in both halves
channels.line: thick dark curves = sampled-subgraph edges, thin grey = unsampled edges, thin arrows = inter-layer propagation, heavy curved arrows = the sample/train cycle
channels.frame: none

quality.strengths: The core idea (train on a sampled subgraph) is pure geometry: the subgraph is drawn bold on the real graph and the layered network reuses exactly its node IDs, so a reader can verify the correspondence node by node; one channel (grey value) carries one meaning.
quality.weaknesses: No words anywhere (no 'sample', 'GCN', layer labels), so the cycle arrows and the rows rely entirely on the caption; the dense crossing arrows in the right half make the layer connectivity hard to trace; nothing marks which part is the contribution versus standard GCN propagation.

figures.lesson: Mark the sampled subgraph by fading the unsampled nodes to pale grey, then rebuild the network from only the sampled node IDs beside it, so the reader sees that training never touches the rest of the graph.

figures.title: Grounding DINO: Marrying DINO with Grounded Pre-Training for Open-Set Object Detection

taxonomy.task: open-set object detection teaser

taxonomy.task: open-set object detection / grounding

arrangement.units: three numbered panels with purple pill titles, separated by purple rules: overall model on the left, two layer zoom-ins stacked on the right
arrangement.inputs_as: a quoted category prompt pill and a real cat photo
