channels.frame: purple pill-titled panels separated by purple rules; the zoomed layers have a coloured outer frame

quality.strengths: The two modalities are colour-coded consistently from features to modules, and the gradient fill turns 'this block mixes text and image' into colour; representations (text bars, image cubes, query sticks) are drawn between every module; zoom panels sit beside the block they open, at its height, tied by wedges.
quality.weaknesses: Text-feature skip lines leave the left column, loop round with a hop and cross other wires to reach Query Selection and the decoder; the contrastive grid at the top is small and partly occluded by a rotated sentence label, so the pairing that defines the loss is hard to read.

channels.line: solid black arrows = attention from query to keys, dashed grey arrow = score accumulation, dashed boxes = the KV-cache window
channels.frame: coloured frames = one method; a light blue rounded panel = the H2O mechanism; a horizontal and a vertical rule separate comparison, mechanism and result

figures.lesson: Frame each KV-cache policy's attention grid in the colour of its curve in the accompanying accuracy plot, and give the proposal's frame the same tint as its mechanism panel, so grid, curve and explanation are tied by one colour.

quality.weaknesses: Curved lines fan and cross between the attention and message panels (s1's line crosses s2's twice), making paths hard to follow; blocks carry formula-heavy names such as W^ATT_φ(e1) and Attention(s1,e1,t); node type is encoded twice (shape and colour).

figures.lesson: Give each node type one colour and repeat it on everything that belongs to that type - node glyph, hidden-vector capsule, type-specific Linear box and the curve between them - and give each relation-specific weight box a two-tone outline (target colour on top, source colour below), so heterogeneous paths can be traced without labels on the curves.

a dashed line drops from the Projector box into a rounded tinted panel below

quality.weaknesses: Yellow means 'visual token' and also the D-Abstractor's neighbourhood highlight; the C-/D-Abstractor arrows are dense and small; the top-row generic pipeline takes about half the height though it is routine.

figures.title: HuBERT: Self-Supervised Speech Representation Learning by Masked Prediction of Hidden Units

insights.avoid: The figure shows only the denoiser, not the unrolled k-space cascade that makes HUMUS-Net an unrolled network, and it carries two separate legends (bottom-left of each panel) instead of one key.

channels.shape: trapezoids = resolution change (extraction/reconstruction), triangles = patch embed/unembed (keyed), rectangles = blocks, ⊕ = residual add

channels.frame: grey rounded panel = the full denoiser; green panel = the inside of MUST; small legend boxes in each

quality.strengths: The contribution MUST is the one green box and its detail panel is the largest area, tied by both dotted lines and matching tint; the U geometry shows down/up levels with skip lines drawn straight across; real MR images mark input and output; line colours are keyed.
quality.weaknesses: Every U edge carries a typeset shape formula (h/4·w/4×2·d), which crowds the panel; F_H, F_L, F_D need a legend box because the features are names only; the global residual runs the full panel width over the top.

figures.title: IBRNet: Learning Multi-View Image-Based Rendering

taxonomy.task: generalizable novel view synthesis

arrangement.units: unframed scene area on the left, a beige tinted network panel in the middle with a rounded zoom inset, and an unframed output column on the right

insights.flow: Left to right along horizontal arrows from ray samples to MLPs to Ray Transformer to sigma outputs, then a hollow block arrow right to the density plot and a hollow arrow down to the loss.
insights.avoid: The colour-coded hatched feature swatches are small and need the inset key to decode; the scene zone has no frame so it is grouped only by proximity.

core.what: an orange target ray pierces a dotted cube around the real scene, and its blue sample points send dashed coloured lines into the green-framed source photos A and B, before feeding a row of per-sample MLPs

relations.form: left zone: real toy photos as source views (green frames A, B) and the target view (red dotted frame) around a wire cube; three blue dots on the orange ray, with dashed purple and cyan projection lines to views A and B

three straight horizontal arrows from the sample points to three MLP glyphs in a beige tinted zone, outputs c_i and f_σ,i, then into a rounded 'Ray Transformer', out as σ1-σ3; hollow block arrows lead on to Volume Rendering and down to Rendering Loss
inside the Ray Transformer thin criss-crossing lines join every sample's f_σ,i to every σ output

a beige wedge from the middle MLP opens a rounded inset where views A and B each supply a hatched feature bar (image colour / viewing direction / image feature, keyed) into one MLP giving 'color c' and 'density feature f_σ'
the loss is drawn as two coloured squares color_pred minus color_gt inside a squared norm, below a density-vs-ray-distance plot whose blue dots match the sample points

channels.colour: frame colour = view role (green solid source, red dotted target, keyed); orange = the target ray and its distance axis; blue dots = ray samples; purple/cyan dashes = source view A/B, reused as the outline of each view's feature bar; hatch colours = feature type (keyed), with purple meaning both 'view A' and 'viewing direction'
channels.shape: photos = views, three-bar glyphs = MLPs, rounded box = Ray Transformer, hatched bars = per-view features, coloured squares = pixel colours
channels.line: solid black = data flow, dashed coloured = projection to a source view, hollow arrows = stage transitions, thin violet lines = attention inside the transformer
channels.frame: beige tinted zone = the network; rounded inset = MLP detail; green/red frames = source/target views

quality.strengths: The geometry the method relies on (a target ray, its samples, their projections into source photos) is drawn on real images, and the samples keep their blue dots from the scene through to the density plot; the per-view features are drawn as keyed bars in the inset; the loss compares drawn colour patches, not a formula.
quality.weaknesses: Purple means both source view A and the viewing-direction hatch; the Ray Transformer's interior is a tangle of faint lines that conveys 'all-to-all' only vaguely; the output side (volume rendering, loss) switches to hollow block arrows and a separate column, so the flow bends down at the right.

figures.lesson: Reuse the scene ray as the density plot's x-axis, with the same coloured sample dots placed on it, so the volume-rendering step visibly comes from the ray drawn in the scene.

figures.title: What matters when building vision-language models?

taxonomy.task: vision-language model (image+text to text)

arrangement.units: one pipeline with module boxes (teal encoder, blue projection, tall peach LLM) and no enclosing frames
arrangement.inputs_as: an image icon with resolution text and a text glyph
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: A single top row Vision encoder -> hidden states -> 'Modality projection + Pooling' feeds a tall peach LLM column at the right, while a text line runs along the bottom into the same column.
insights.data: The image is an icon with 'Up to 980x980'; hidden states are stacked green squares, pooled visual tokens are labelled '64', and text tokens are dark orange squares, so the LLM's input column interleaves green and orange cells.
insights.emphasis: Colour carries the message: green visual tokens and orange text tokens alternate in the LLM's input column, showing images inserted into the text sequence.
insights.flow: Left to right, image path on top and text path along the bottom, both curving into the LLM's input column; outputs exit right as orange squares.
insights.avoid: The big serif 'TT' glyph for text and the curved arrows that cross each other just before the LLM are clumsy; no loss is shown.

core.what: green visual-token stacks and orange text-token squares interleave in one input column along the left edge of a tall peach LLM bar, with an image path along the top and a text line along the bottom curving into it

relations.form: top row left to right: image icon 'Up to 980x980' -> Vision encoder -> stacked green 'Hidden states' -> Modality projection + Pooling -> green stacks marked '64'

curved black arrows carry each pooled 64-token group into its slot of the LLM's input column, while hollow-headed arrows from the bottom text line enter at the orange slots, so green and orange cells alternate
image path along the top, text path as one long horizontal line along the bottom from a large serif 'TT' glyph, both ending at the LLM column

channels.colour: green = visual tokens/hidden states, dark orange = text tokens (input and output); module fills (teal encoder, pale blue projection, peach LLM) only separate modules
channels.shape: stacked squares = token groups, single squares = tokens, rounded rectangles = modules, a tall bar = LLM
channels.line: solid black arrowheads = visual-token routing, hollow arrowheads = text-token routing; all solid lines
channels.frame: none

quality.strengths: Interleaving is drawn as data: the LLM's input column literally alternates green image-token cells and orange text-token cells, and the same orange reappears on the outputs, so 'images inserted into the text sequence' reads without text.
quality.weaknesses: The text input is a large serif 'TT' glyph with no example text; curved routing arrows cross each other just before the LLM; the image is an icon, not a sample; the 64-token pooling, the paper's efficiency point, is only a small ':64' label.

figures.lesson: Turn the LLM into a tall vertical bar at the right edge and stack its input sequence as one column of squares down its left side, so interleaved image-token runs (green, counted '64') and text tokens (orange) read as one ordered sequence.

figures.title: ImageBind: One Embedding Space To Bind Them All

taxonomy.task: joint embedding of six modalities via image-paired data

arrangement.units: a row of samples, then the binding diagram at the right
arrangement.inputs_as: real photos, depth, thermal and video frames, each titled with its source
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: A row of five captioned real-data tiles (Web Image-Text, Depth Sensor Data, Web Videos, Thermal Data, Egocentric Videos) leads to a hexagonal graph on the right where the image node sits at the centre connected to the other modality icons.
insights.data: Each data source is a real photograph (or stacked frames for video) with the modality icons it pairs shown beside its title; a caption 'Sheep basking in the sun' stands for text.
insights.emphasis: The binding idea is drawn in the graph: thick solid edges for naturally aligned pairs (all through images) versus thin dashed edges for emergent alignment, with an 'IMAGEBIND' label and arrow pointing at the hub.
insights.flow: Read left to right across the data tiles into the graph; the top legend band is read first.
insights.avoid: It shows no encoders or loss, so it cannot serve as a model-architecture skeleton; the photos dominate and the key result (the graph) is small at the far right.

core.what: a hexagonal graph at the right with the image icon at the hub: thick solid edges join images to every other modality icon, thin dashed edges join the outer modalities to each other

relations.form: image (and video) icons sit at the centre of the graph, every naturally aligned edge passes through them, and an 'IMAGEBIND' label with a curved arrow points at the hub

a row of five real-data tiles (Web Image-Text with a caption 'Sheep basking in the sun', Depth Sensor Data, Web Videos, Thermal Data, Egocentric Videos), each titled with the two modality icons it pairs
thin dashed edges between the outer modality icons (text, depth, thermal, audio, IMU) form the hexagon's rim as emergent alignments

channels.colour: modality identity (blue images, purple videos/IMU, black text, light blue audio, green depth, yellow thermal), keyed in a top-left legend and reused in tile titles and graph nodes; purple is shared by videos and IMU
channels.shape: icons = modalities, photographs = data samples
channels.line: thick solid = naturally aligned pair (keyed), thin dashed = emergent alignment (keyed)
channels.frame: a tinted rounded legend box; tiles unframed (video tiles drawn as stacked frames)

quality.strengths: The binding idea is pure geometry: images at the hub, solid edges for paired data, dashed for emergent ones, both keyed; every pairing is grounded in a real data tile titled with the same icons used in the graph.
quality.weaknesses: The hub graph, the contribution, takes only about a sixth of the width while the five data tiles take the rest; videos and IMU share purple; the tiles and the graph are not linked, so the reader must match icons by eye.

figures.lesson: When the figure is about data pairings, show one real sample per pairing with its modality icons, and keep the icon key in one strip at the top edge.

figures.title: Informer: Beyond Efficient Transformer for Long Sequence Time-Series Forecasting

taxonomy.task: long-sequence time-series forecasting

arrangement.units: two blue dashed rounded frames, Encoder and Decoder, titled at the top inside
arrangement.inputs_as: cell strips of sequence tokens with math labels
arrangement.shared: encoder feature map feeds the decoder cross-attention

insights.structure: Two blue dashed rounded frames side by side, Encoder on the left and Decoder on the right, with a purple dashed 'Concatenated Feature Map' tab on the encoder and a Fully Connected Layer plus output row above the decoder.
insights.data: Inputs are two-row cell strips at the bottom (X_en, and X_de = {X_token, X_0} whose right half is filled with zeros); outputs are a cell row whose predicted cells are yellow.
insights.emphasis: Encoder self-attention layers are drawn as narrowing trapezoids stacked (plus a smaller side replica) to show the distilling halving, and the zero-padded decoder input marks the generative one-shot decoding.
insights.flow: Bottom to top within each frame; one line leaves the encoder top, runs over and down into the decoder's Multi-head Attention block from the left.
insights.avoid: The unlabeled small trapezoid stack beside the encoder is ambiguous without the caption.

core.what: two blue dashed frames side by side, Encoder left and Decoder right, with the encoder's concatenated feature map carried by one line over the top and down into the decoder's Multi-head Attention block

relations.form: bottom to top inside each frame: an input cell strip (X_en; X_de = {X_token, X_0}) -> stacked attention trapezoids -> output; above the decoder a Fully Connected Layer and an Outputs cell row

the encoder stacks two 'Multi-head ProbSparse Self-attention' trapezoids that narrow upward, with a smaller unlabelled replica stack beside them, both under a purple dashed 'Concatenated Feature Map' tab
a thin black line leaves the top of the feature-map tab, runs up, across the top of the figure and down into the decoder's Multi-head Attention from the left
the decoder input strip has green start-token cells followed by cells filled with '0', and the output row's right half is yellow for predicted steps

channels.colour: green = given input cells, yellow = predicted output cells; blue dashed = encoder/decoder frames, purple dashed = concatenated feature map, lavender = fully connected layer
channels.shape: trapezoid width = sequence length (narrowing = distilling), cell strips = time series, rectangles = attention layers
channels.line: one solid line style for data; dashed only on frames
channels.frame: blue dotted rounded frames = encoder and decoder; purple dotted tab = the concatenated output

quality.strengths: The distilling halving is drawn as narrowing trapezoids and the generative one-shot decoding as a decoder input whose second half is literal zeros, so both contributions are visible as data shapes.
quality.weaknesses: The encoder-to-decoder line takes a long detour up and over the top and back down; the smaller side replica stack has no label to say it is a lower-resolution copy; the predicted yellow cells and the zero placeholders sit at opposite ends of the decoder with nothing tying them.

figures.lesson: Draw the decoder input as a token row of filled start tokens followed by cells marked 0 for the horizon, and fill only the matching output cells, so start-token-plus-placeholder generative decoding is read from the cells.

figures.title: Informer: Beyond Efficient Transformer for Long Sequence Time-Series Forecasting

taxonomy.task: self-attention distilling in a time-series encoder

arrangement.units: one pipeline of 3-D blocks, each block labelled underneath in bold, no enclosing frames
arrangement.inputs_as: a 3-D slab of time-step cells with scalar and timestamp rows
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: One left-to-right chain of 3-D blocks: input embedding (scalar + stamp) -> Attention Block 1 -> Conv1d/MaxPool -> Attention Block 2 -> Conv1d/MaxPool -> Attention Block 3 -> Feature Map.
insights.data: The input window is a green slab of cells labelled T = t to T = t + D_x split into Scalar and Stamp; attention blocks are beige translucent boxes holding red head slices; Conv1d outputs are thin blue/cyan slabs; dimensions L, L/2, L/4, d, k, n-heads are written on edges.
insights.emphasis: The shrinking size of successive attention blocks (L -> L/2 -> L/4) makes the distilling halving visible without text.
insights.flow: Strictly left to right along teal arrows; dashed projection lines fan from the input slab into the embedding bars.
insights.avoid: Rotated dimension labels overlap the slabs ('MaxPool1d, padding=2' collides with L/2), and the dense 3-D perspective is heavy for what is a 1-D sequence.

core.what: one left-to-right chain of 3-D blocks whose attention blocks shrink in size (L, L/2, L/4) with Conv1d/MaxPool slabs between them, ending in a small purple Feature Map

relations.form: teal arrows run strictly left to right: input window -> embedding -> Attention Block 1 -> Conv1d/MaxPool -> Attention Block 2 -> Conv1d/MaxPool -> Attention Block 3 -> Feature Map
three beige translucent attention blocks of the same form, each holding red head slices, drawn successively smaller with the length printed on each (L, L/2, L/4)
the green input slab (T = t to T = t + D_x) splits into Scalar and Stamp; dashed projection lines lead to a blue and a grey embedding slab whose outputs meet at a green ⊕ node

channels.colour: green = input window, blue/grey = scalar/stamp embeddings, beige = attention block, red = attention heads, blue/cyan = Conv1d/MaxPool outputs, purple = feature map
channels.shape: 3-D slab size = tensor size (length shrinks block to block), slices inside a block = heads
channels.line: teal solid arrows = data flow, dashed black = projection from the input window
channels.frame: each translucent beige box = one attention block

quality.strengths: The distilling halving is geometry: each attention block is visibly smaller than the one before, so the L -> L/2 -> L/4 reduction reads without labels; the path is one straight left-to-right line.
quality.weaknesses: Rotated 'MaxPool1d, padding=2' labels and dimension letters (L/2, d, k) overlap the slabs and each other; heavy 3-D boxes with stacked red slices make the attention blocks the most saturated elements although the conv distilling between them is the contribution; dimension symbols carry meaning only with the text.

figures.lesson: Show sequence-length halving by drawing each successive attention block as a smaller 3-D box with L, L/2, L/4 written on its length edge, so the distilling is read from the geometry before any label.

figures.title: Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models

taxonomy.task: LLM planning for robot manipulation with closed-loop language feedback

arrangement.units: vertical columns, one per role (planner dialogue, feedback sources), divided by a dashed rule, plus an unframed photo column
arrangement.inputs_as: a quoted human instruction in a chat bubble with avatar
arrangement.shared: feedback bubbles reply to action bubbles across the dashed rule

insights.structure: Three titled columns: 'Robot Planning & Interaction' (a chat transcript), 'Grounded Closed-Loop Feedback' separated by a dashed vertical rule, and 'Robot Environments' with three stacked photos (a)-(c).
insights.data: Everything is real dialogue: human turns in grey bubbles with a person avatar, robot actions in dashed orange-labelled bubbles 'Action: "pick up the coke"', feedback bubbles from Scene Descriptor and Success Detector icons, plus one real scene photo.
insights.emphasis: Feedback outcomes are coloured red 'not successful' vs green 'successful', and a small hub diagram at the top of the middle column shows robot, human, scene descriptor and success detector exchanging messages.
insights.flow: Top to bottom as a conversation; grey diagonal arrows zigzag between the left action bubbles and the middle feedback bubbles to show the closed loop.
insights.avoid: The right environments column is unrelated to the loop and competes for attention; there is no explicit LLM block, so the planner is implicit.

core.what: the closed loop unrolled down the page as a zigzag: grey arrows run right from robot action bubbles in the left chat column to feedback bubbles in the middle column, and back left to the robot's next turn

relations.form: left column 'Robot Planning & Interaction' is a real chat transcript read top to bottom: human turns in grey bubbles with a person avatar, robot actions in dashed bubbles 'Action: "pick up the coke"' with a robot icon

short grey diagonal arrows cross the dashed vertical rule between columns: action -> Scene Descriptor 'I see: coke, water, chocolate bar.' -> robot question; 'pick up the coke' -> Success Detector 'not successful' -> repeated 'pick up the coke' -> 'successful' -> 'bring it to you'
a small hub at the top of the middle column: Robot, Human, Scene Descriptor and Success Detector icons in a ring with grey arrows between them
right column 'Robot Environments': three stacked photos (a) real robot kitchen, (b) simulated tabletop with bowls and blocks, (c) real tabletop with toy food, unconnected to the dialogue

channels.colour: icon outline colour = speaker (blue robot, green Scene Descriptor, purple Success Detector); orange = 'Action:' label; red 'not successful' vs green 'successful' = outcome, so green means both the scene descriptor and success
channels.shape: solid grey bubbles = utterances/feedback, dashed bubbles = robot actions, circular icons = speakers, photos = scenes
channels.line: grey diagonal arrows = messages between planner and feedback sources; a dashed vertical rule separates planning from feedback
channels.frame: none; three titled columns

quality.strengths: The closed loop is shown with real dialogue rather than boxes, and the zigzag between the two columns makes each feedback round visible as geometry, including the retry after 'not successful'; one real scene photo grounds the scene description.
quality.weaknesses: Green marks both the Scene Descriptor icon and the 'successful' outcome; the right column of environment photos has no link to the dialogue and takes about a sixth of the width; the top hub diagram repeats the speaker icons with arrows that carry no extra information.

figures.lesson: Draw the closed loop as a chat transcript: robot actions in dashed bubbles on one side, perception feedback in solid bubbles with source icons on the other, joined by zig-zag arrows in time order, with outcome words in red and green.

figures.title: Instant Neural Graphics Primitives with a Multiresolution Hash Encoding

taxonomy.task: multiresolution hash encoding for neural fields

arrangement.units: one pipeline with no frames; each step separated by whitespace
arrangement.inputs_as: a query point x arrow into a gridded domain over a faded 3-D object
arrangement.shared: same level colours reused across all steps

insights.structure: Four steps left to right: a 2-D domain with two grid levels over a faded bunny, two hash tables of size T each linked to a voxel square, a concatenated feature vector y, and an MLP m(y; Phi).
insights.data: Grid levels are colour-coded (red l=1, blue l=0) with vertex indices in circles; hash tables are 8-row two-column cell arrays whose looked-up rows are filled in the level colour; the feature vector stacks red, blue and green (auxiliary xi) cells with brackets L*F and E.
insights.emphasis: The two-colour level code runs consistently from grid to hash-table rows to interpolation squares to vector segments, so each level can be followed by hue.
insights.flow: Left to right: a curved arrow brings query x into the grid, elbow lines connect corners to table rows, curved arrows carry interpolated values into y, then straight arrows into and out of the MLP.
insights.avoid: The elbow connectors from table rows to square corners overlap and are hard to trace; step numbers and labels are cut off at the top of the crop.

core.what: a query point x sits inside two overlaid grid levels drawn on a 2-D domain over a faded bunny (red l=1, blue l=0), and each level's cell corners are followed by hue through a hash table to an interpolation square and into a segment of the feature vector y

relations.form: left: a square domain with dashed grid lines per level, the cell containing x outlined in each level's colour with corner vertices as numbered circles (red 2,0,3,6; blue 0,4,1,7)

two 8-row two-column hash tables of size T, one per level, whose looked-up rows (red 0,2,3,6; blue 0,1,4,7) are filled in the level colour and joined by thin elbow lines to the corners of a level-coloured square
the two levels run as parallel lanes, red on top and blue below, from table to interpolation square

dashed lines from each square's corners meet at the interpolated point; curved arrows from both points converge on the stacked vector y (red, blue cells bracketed L·F) and an auxiliary input ξ enters from below as green cells (E)
y -> an MLP drawn as grey node columns labelled m(y; Φ) -> output arrow, all left to right

channels.colour: resolution level (red l=1, blue l=0) carried consistently through grid, table rows, interpolation squares and y segments; green = auxiliary input ξ; grey = the MLP
channels.shape: numbered circles = grid vertices, cell arrays = hash tables and feature vector, node columns = MLP
channels.line: solid coloured = cell outline at that level, dashed coloured = grid lines in the domain and interpolation weights in the squares, thin black elbows = hash lookups, curved black arrows = data flow
channels.frame: none; four unframed steps separated by space

quality.strengths: One colour, one meaning across all four steps, so each level can be followed by hue from vertex to table row to vector segment; the data structures themselves (grid, hash table, feature vector) are drawn as the compared representations; the operation is shown on a small instance with real vertex indices.
quality.weaknesses: The thin black elbow lines from table rows to square corners route around the squares and bunch where the blue lines cross; dashed line style means both 'grid line' and 'interpolation weight'; the top-left labels 'L = 2, b = 1.5' and '1/N0' are cut by the frame edge.

figures.lesson: Explain a multi-level lookup on a 2-D slice: give each resolution level one colour and repeat it on its grid cell, its table rows and its slice of the concatenated feature column, leaving the downstream network grey.

figures.title: InstructBLIP: Towards General-purpose Vision-Language Models with Instruction Tuning

taxonomy.task: instruction-following vision-language model

arrangement.units: the overview column on the left (unframed) and a dashed rounded grey zoom panel on the right for the Q-Former internals
arrangement.inputs_as: two cartoon images under the frozen image encoder and the instruction as a quoted multi-line text card in the bottom-left corner; queries and instruction as token rows at the top of the column

grey dashed lines fan from the Q-Former's right corners to a dashed-outline 'Q-Former' panel at right showing Self Attention spanning queries and instruction, then Cross Attention (taking Image Embeddings from the left) and two Feed Forward blocks
in the detail panel one wide Self Attention bar spans both the Queries and the Instruction token rows, while Cross Attention and the purple Feed Forward sit only over the queries

channels.colour: pale yellow = trainable, solid blue with a snowflake = frozen; query squares red/yellow/green/blue = individual learned queries, empty squares = instruction tokens; tray outline colour (black, blue, green) changes after each stage without a key; sublayer fills in the detail panel (orange, grey, purple, green) only separate blocks

channels.line: solid black arrows = data flow, grey dashed = zoom projection
channels.frame: dashed rounded panel = Q-Former detail; a pale yellow box inside it = one Q-Former layer

quality.strengths: The contribution (instruction tokens entering the Q-Former) is drawn as data: instruction token rows sit beside the query rows at the Q-Former's input and again under one shared Self Attention bar in the detail panel; trainable vs frozen is one consistent fill code; the detail panel is beside the block it opens.
quality.weaknesses: The tray outlines change colour (black, blue, green) with no key, adding a meaningless channel; the instruction text card at bottom left has no arrow to the instruction token rows; Image Embeddings in the detail panel enter by a long elbow from the bottom-left corner.

figures.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback

taxonomy.task: aligning a language model with human feedback

arrangement.units: three columns divided by thin vertical rules, each titled 'Step N' plus a bold heading
arrangement.inputs_as: a light-blue prompt card with quoted example text
arrangement.losses_at: bottom of each column (trained SFT, RM, reward r_k)
arrangement.shared: the same prompt example reused in steps 1 and 2

insights.emphasis: Each step's sentence-per-card explanation lets a non-expert read it, and blue arrows mark where data trains a model (and the blue feedback loop from r_k back to PPO in step 3).
insights.flow: Top to bottom inside each column with grey arrows, columns read left to right; only step 3 has a return loop on the right edge.
insights.avoid: The heavy prose occupies half of each column, which suits a blog-style overview but not a dense paper figure; no arrows link the steps to each other.

core.what: three columns 'Step 1/2/3' separated by thin vertical rules, each a top-to-bottom stack of grey cards from a sampled prompt to the model it trains (SFT, RM, PPO)

relations.form: three equal-width columns left to right, each headed by a bold one-sentence title, with left-aligned plain-English sentences beside each card of a right-aligned card stack
inside each column short grey arrows run straight down the card stack: blue prompt card ('Explain the moon landing to a 6 year old') -> labeler avatar or policy -> output -> model glyph
Step 2: four lettered output cards A-D in a 2x2 grid gathered by a bracket into a labeler card with the ranking 'D > C > A = B', which reappears under the RM glyph
Step 3: a blue arrow runs from the r_k card up the right edge back into the PPO card
the same network glyph is reused for SFT, RM and PPO, and the same moon-landing prompt card appears in Steps 1 and 2

channels.colour: light blue fill = a prompt card; blue arrows = data used for training a model (and the reward loop); grey arrows = generation/flow; everything else neutral grey
channels.shape: rounded grey cards = steps, a network glyph = a model, a person avatar = labeler, lettered circles = ranked outputs, document icons = demonstration data
channels.line: solid arrows only; colour (blue vs grey) separates training from flow
channels.frame: thin vertical rules separate the three steps; no panel frames

quality.strengths: Each step is one column with a sentence per card, so a non-expert can read the pipeline; data is drawn as data (quoted prompts, sampled outputs A-D, a literal ranking 'D > C > A = B'); arrows are short and straight; blue marks where data trains a model and the RL loop.
quality.weaknesses: The three steps are not connected (no arrow carries the SFT model into Step 3's PPO or the RM into Step 3), so the dependency between stages is left to the text; all three columns get equal space although Step 3 is the RL contribution.

figures.lesson: Set a plain-language sentence beside each card, at the same height, in a left text column, so each column reads as a captioned storyboard and the cards themselves need only a word or an icon.

figures.title: InstructPix2Pix: Learning to Follow Image Editing Instructions

taxonomy.task: instruction-based image editing trained on generated paired data

arrangement.units: Two titled halves divided by a thin vertical rule; the left half holds three stacked grey rounded strips (a), (b), (c), the right half one grey rounded panel (d); every panel has a bold lettered title at its top left.
arrangement.inputs_as: quoted italic captions and instructions; real image pairs (generated) and a real painting at inference
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; training of the model is only stated in the caption

insights.data: All text is shown as real quoted strings ('photograph of a girl riding a horse' -> 'have her ride a dragon') and all images as real before/after photo pairs, four pairs in a row in strip (c).
insights.emphasis: The contribution is shown by example rather than by structure: panel (d) is the largest and holds a large before/after painting pair with the InstructPix2Pix box between them.
insights.flow: Inside each strip, short arrows run left to right from inputs through a blue model box to outputs; between strips the reader moves top to bottom, then across the divider to (d).
insights.avoid: No arrow links strip (c) to the model in (d), and no training step or loss is drawn, so how the generated dataset trains InstructPix2Pix is left to the caption.

core.what: two titled halves split by a vertical rule: training-data generation (left, three stacked strips a-c) and inference with the trained model (right, one tall panel d)

relations.form: left half 'Training Data Generation' and right half 'Instruction-following Diffusion Model' side by side under bold titles, divided by a thin vertical line

the data pipeline runs top to bottom through strips (a) text edits by GPT-3, (b) paired images by Stable Diffusion + Prompt2Prompt, (c) the resulting training examples, each strip reading left to right through one blue model box
panel (d) reads left to right: a real painting with its quoted instruction above, an arrow into the InstructPix2Pix box, an arrow out to the edited painting

channels.colour: pale blue rounded fill = a model (GPT-3, Stable Diffusion + Prompt2Prompt, InstructPix2Pix), all the same blue, so the trained contribution is not set apart from the off-the-shelf generators
channels.shape: rounded box = model; quoted italic strings = text data; photos = image data
channels.line: short dark-blue arrows = data passed into or out of a model
channels.frame: light-grey rounded strip = one lettered step

quality.strengths: Data is drawn as real data throughout: quoted captions and instructions ('have her ride a dragon') and actual before/after image pairs, with the same horse/dragon example carried from (a) to (b) to (c); panel (d) is the largest and makes the edit visible at a glance.
quality.weaknesses: No arrow links the stages: (a)'s edited caption is re-typed as (b)'s input instead of drawn as flowing into it, and nothing connects the (c) examples to the InstructPix2Pix model in (d), so the training step is only in the caption; the trained model has the same blue as GPT-3 and Stable Diffusion.

figures.lesson: When the contribution is a generated dataset plus a model, give the data pipeline lettered strips stacked on the left and the model a single tall panel on the right, and draw every example as real quoted text and real image pairs.

arrangement.units: three unframed panels separated by whitespace, each with a caption below
arrangement.inputs_as: plain text words
arrangement.losses_at: top, objective names joined by arcs
arrangement.shared: shared-weights double arrow between the two LLM trapezoids

insights.structure: Three captioned panels (a) Supervised, (b) Contrastive, (c) InternVL, built from the same white trapezoid encoders, with panel (c) holding three trapezoids (vision encoder, LLM, LLM).

insights.flow: Bottom to top within each encoder; curved arcs at the top join pairs of encoders into an objective, with one long arc from the vision encoder to the generative LLM.
insights.avoid: The long arc over panel (c) and the plain-word inputs make it a positioning diagram, not an architecture; nothing about the bridge module is shown.

core.what: three pre-training paradigms as side-by-side panels of the same white trapezoid encoders, supervised and contrastive first and InternVL last and widest

relations.form: panels (a) supervised, (b) contrastive, (c) InternVL in a row with captions below, built from the same trapezoid glyph, ours last with three trapezoids
inside each trapezoid an up-arrow from the input word below ('image', 'text', 'prompt') to an objective word above ('classes', 'contrastive', 'generative')
a curved arc joins the tops of two encoders into the word 'contrastive' in (b) and (c); in (c) a second long arc runs from the vision encoder over to the right LLM for 'generative'
a thick grey double-headed arrow labelled 'shared weights' between the two large-language-model trapezoids in (c)

channels.shape: trapezoid = encoder/model; bare words = inputs and objectives
channels.line: thin black arrows and arcs = data into encoders and outputs into objectives; thick grey double arrow = weight sharing
channels.frame: no frames; panels separated by whitespace and captions

quality.weaknesses: Representations are never drawn: arcs go from encoder tops straight to objective words; in (c) the long vision-to-generative arc passes over the 'contrastive' label and the middle LLM, and the new parts are distinguished only by text, not fill.

figures.lesson: Contrast pre-training paradigms with identical blank trapezoids and arched arrows to one objective word each, letting the 'ours' panel differ only by an extra trapezoid and one red-bold number written inside its encoder.

figures.title: IP-Adapter: Text Compatible Image Prompt Adapter for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

taxonomy.task: image-prompted text-to-image generation

arrangement.units: three unenclosed horizontal lanes (image, latent/U-Net, text); one orange dashed rounded box encloses the two parallel cross-attention modules
arrangement.inputs_as: real image thumbnail (top) and a quoted text prompt (bottom)
arrangement.shared: two horizontal buses above the U-Net carry both attention outputs to every U-Net block

insights.structure: Three horizontal lanes: image branch on top (Image Encoder, Linear, LN, Image Features row) ending in a dashed 'Decoupled Cross-Attention' box at top right, the bowtie Denoising U-Net with x_t and x_{t-1} slabs in the middle, and the text branch at the bottom (prompt, Text Encoder, Text Features row).
insights.data: The image prompt is a real painting thumbnail, the text prompt is a quoted sentence, features are short rows of cells, and the noisy latents x_t / x_{t-1} are 3-D slabs flanking the U-Net.
insights.emphasis: Trainable modules are pink with a flame icon and frozen ones light blue with a snowflake, so the new parts (Linear, LN, image Cross Attention) pop out; a two-swatch legend at bottom right explains the code.
insights.flow: Left-to-right in each lane; the two Cross Attention outputs drop as orange and blue buses onto every U-Net block bar, and the text-feature line runs to the right edge and climbs the whole height into the frozen Cross Attention.
insights.avoid: The long text-feature wire looping around the right edge up to the top box is a detour that is hard to follow; place the text and image attention inputs nearer their sources.

core.what: image and text features each feed their own cross-attention inside one dashed 'Decoupled Cross-Attention' box, and the two outputs drop on parallel orange and blue buses into every U-Net block

relations.form: three unframed horizontal lanes: image branch on top (Image Encoder, Linear, LN, Image Features), the U-Net with x_t and x_{t-1} in the middle, the text branch at the bottom (prompt, Text Encoder, Text Features)
two cross-attention boxes side by side at top right, each sending a bus that branches down into all seven U-Net blocks as adjacent orange and blue arrows
noisy latent slab x_t, an arrow into the bowtie Denoising U-Net, an arrow out to slab x_{t-1}, along the middle axis

channels.colour: fill: pink = trainable, light blue = frozen (keyed in a two-swatch legend), duplicated by flame/snowflake icons; line colour: orange = image-prompt path, blue = text/latent path, so colour carries both training status and stream
channels.shape: rounded box = module; row of cells = feature tokens; 3-D slab = latent; bowtie = U-Net
channels.line: solid arrows only; orange vs blue tells the stream
channels.frame: orange dashed rounded box = the new decoupled cross-attention module

quality.strengths: The new parts (Linear, LN, the image Cross Attention) are the only pink fills, and the dashed box names the contribution; image and text feature tokens are drawn as rows of cells between the encoders and the attention, and the per-block injection is shown by paired arrows into every U-Net block.
quality.weaknesses: Text features reach their cross-attention by a long wire that runs right and up the figure's edge round the U-Net; trainable status is coded twice (fill and icon) while colour also codes the stream on lines; the denoising loop and the training objective are not drawn.

figures.lesson: Two parallel buses above the backbone drop a side-by-side pair of arrows (blue from the original condition, orange from the added one) onto every U-Net block, showing that the new conditioning is injected alongside the old at each block without drawing any block internals.

figures.title: Interleaving Retrieval with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Knowledge-Intensive Multi-Step Questions

taxonomy.task: multi-step open-domain question answering by alternating chain-of-thought sentences and retrieval

arrangement.units: a large rounded frame holding the unrolled loop, a bottom rounded frame holding the collected documents, and a right column of two rounded frames with lilac title bars defining the two operations
arrangement.inputs_as: the quoted question in a full-width grey bar marked with a circled Q
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; termination is an orange 'Stop' hexagon at the end of the last arrow
arrangement.shared: the same Retrieve and Reason operations are drawn once each as definition panels on the right, while the main frame repeats them as labelled arrows

insights.structure: A two-column ladder - CoT sentences on the left, document stacks on the right - inside one frame, with the question above, the collected documents below and operation definitions in a side column.
insights.data: Every CoT sentence and the question are quoted verbatim; documents are page-stack icons coloured by the round that fetched them, and the Reason panel shows the actual prompt text.
insights.emphasis: Round colour is the main signal: T1, T2, T3 boxes and their document stacks share yellow-brown, blue and green, and the final collection shows the three colours added together.
insights.flow: Straight horizontal arrows alternate right (Retrieve) and left (Reason) down the frame; the question's line drops from the top bar and turns right into the first retrieval; one arrow leads down out of the frame to the collection.
insights.avoid: The arrow labels are typeset function calls (T2 <- Reason(Q, docs + docs, T1)), a formula carried on every arrow; name the step and let the colour show its inputs.

core.what: three unrolled rounds as a ladder: CoT sentence boxes T1-T3 down the left, document stacks down the right, alternating Retrieve (rightward) and Reason (leftward) arrows between them

relations.form: rounds stacked top to bottom inside one frame, each round one Retrieve arrow right and one Reason arrow back left, ending in an orange Stop hexagon
the document stores are page-stack icons in outlined squares in a right-hand column, one per round, each in that round's colour
accumulated context is written into each Reason arrow's label as miniature coloured document icons joined by '+', growing by one colour per round; the bottom frame shows all three stacks summed

a right column of two framed panels headed by lilac bars defines Retrieve(q) as q -> magnifier -> documents and Reason(Q, docs, T1) as the quoted prompt with a bracket marking the retrieved paragraphs

channels.colour: colour = round: yellow-brown, blue and green tint each CoT sentence box and the document stack retrieved in the round before it, and recolour the miniature document icons in labels; lilac title bars = operation definitions; orange = stop
channels.shape: tinted text boxes = generated CoT sentences, page-stack icons = retrieved documents, circled letters = variables (Q, T1-T3), hexagon = termination
channels.line: one style: straight black arrows, rightward = retrieve, leftward = reason; direction carries the operation
channels.frame: rounded frame = one unit (the loop, the final output, each operation definition)

quality.strengths: The alternation is geometry: sentences and documents face each other in two columns and arrows bounce between them, so the interleaving is visible before reading. Colour binds each sentence to the documents it triggered and the miniature icons in the labels show context accumulating. Data is quoted, and the Reason panel shows the real prompt.
quality.weaknesses: Every arrow carries a typeset function call (Reason(Q, docs+docs, T1)), a formula on the line instead of a drawn input. The definition panels on the right are not tied to the loop by tint or a callout - their lilac headers appear nowhere in the main frame. The question's line runs down then bends right across the frame header to reach the first document stack.

figures.lesson: Unroll a retrieve-reason loop as a ladder: reasoning sentences down the left, retrieved documents down the right, alternating arrows between them, each round in its own colour that also tints the tiny document icons inside the arrow labels.

figures.title: Transformers are Sample-Efficient World Models

taxonomy.task: model-based RL with imagined rollouts

arrangement.units: repeated unboxed time-step columns labeled by bottom braces; nested thin rectangles enclose the accumulated sequence
arrangement.inputs_as: symbol x_0
arrangement.shared: the same E, D, G, pi arrows repeat in every column

insights.structure: A timeline unrolled left-to-right into time-step columns t=0, t=1, ..., t=s marked by curly braces at the bottom, each column holding a dashed token box z^1..z^K plus action a_t; nested plain rectangles around the growing token sequence show the transformer context expanding.
insights.data: Everything is math symbols: frame x_0, tokens z, reconstructions x-hat, actions a, predicted reward r-hat and done d-hat; no images or blocks for networks, which appear only as letters on arrows (E, D, G, pi).
insights.emphasis: Each network gets a colour on its arrows: green for encoder/decoder E/D, indigo for the world-model G (thick), magenta for policy pi, making the imagination loop readable without boxes.
insights.flow: x_0 drops down via E into tokens, D drops to x-hat, pi hooks back up to a_t, and thick indigo G arrows run right to the next step while branching upward to r-hat and d-hat.
insights.avoid: The nested context rectangles are thin unlabeled outlines whose meaning (growing attention window) is not stated in the figure.

core.what: the imagination rollout unrolled into time-step columns t=0, t=1, ..., t=s under braces, chained left to right by thick indigo G arrows

relations.form: three columns of the same unit (token box, action, decoder down, policy back up) marked by curly braces, with an ellipsis column between t=1 and t=s
within a column: x_0 down by green E into dashed token box z^1..z^K, down by green D to the reconstruction x-hat, then a magenta pi elbow back up to action a_t
nested thin rectangles around the tokens and actions of steps 0, 0-1 and 0-2 show the growing context G conditions on
from each G arrow a branch rises to the predicted reward r-hat and done d-hat at the top

channels.colour: arrow colour = which network: green = autoencoder E/D, indigo = world model G, magenta = policy pi; one meaning
channels.shape: dashed box = a frame's set of tokens; everything else is symbols on arrows (no network blocks)
channels.line: thick indigo = the world-model transition; thin coloured arrows = encoder, decoder, policy
channels.frame: nested solid rectangles = the accumulated context the transformer attends to; braces = one time step

quality.strengths: Unrolling is drawn as geometry: identical columns under braces, the transformer as the thick indigo spine, and the growing context as nested rectangles; each network keeps one colour everywhere.
quality.weaknesses: Everything is notation (x_0, z, x-hat, a, r-hat): no frame image or token grid; the nested context rectangles are unlabelled and need the caption; the pi path bends in an L from x-hat back up to a_t and the r-hat/d-hat branches step up from the spine.

figures.lesson: Show a transformer's growing context by nesting thin outline rectangles, each one time step wider, around the unrolled tokens, instead of drawing attention arrows.

figures.title: ISTA-Net: Interpretable Optimization-Inspired Deep Network for Image Compressive Sensing

taxonomy.task: image compressive sensing reconstruction

arrangement.units: Top row: three pale-green rounded phase panels (1-th, k-th, Np-th) in a line, separated by dotted ellipses; bottom: a wide dashed-outline zoom box containing one enlarged green phase panel.
arrangement.inputs_as: a small real grayscale photo with a red border, followed by thin vertical bars for the image vector x and its measurements y
arrangement.shared: the same phase structure is drawn three times in the top row with superscripts (1), (k), (Np); the k-th copy is expanded below rather than redrawn separately

insights.avoid: Colour encodes three different things at once (vector role, pre/post-threshold feature maps, operator identity), and the tiny red 'CS Sampling' and green 'Initialization' labels are rotated vertically between bars, which is hard to read.

core.what: three identical pale-green phase panels (1-th, k-th, Np-th) in a row joined by dotted ellipses, the k-th opened below in a dashed zoom outline

relations.form: top row: the same phase panel (r bar, F, Soft, inverse F) drawn three times with superscripts (1), (k), (Np) and x-iterate bars between them
a grey dashed trapezoid outline flares from the k-th phase down to a full-width detail panel of the same green tint showing Conv-ReLU-Conv stacks around Soft
left to right: image with red border, vector x, CS sampling to y, initialization to x(0), the phases, the output x(Np) and reconstructed image
in the detail, F(k) and its inverse are red dotted frames placed symmetrically on either side of the Soft threshold

channels.colour: two meanings: bar colour codes vector role (green x, dark blue r, orange y) while green is also the phase background and the post-threshold feature maps, and orange/yellow is both y and the Soft block; blue F and purple inverse F tags mark the learned transforms
channels.shape: thin upright bar = a vector; stacked rectangles = N_f feature maps; rounded tag = an operation
channels.line: thick grey arrows = data flow; short diagonal arrows into and out of Soft
channels.frame: pale-green rounded panel = one phase; grey dashed outline = zoom; red dotted rectangles = the F and inverse-F transforms

quality.strengths: The unrolled-iteration and zoom forms are textbook: identical phase panels in a row, the opened copy tied to its source by a dashed callout and matching tint; the vectors x, y, r are drawn as data bars between operations, and the transform/inverse symmetry is visible as mirrored frames.
quality.weaknesses: Colour is overloaded (green for phase panels, x-iterates and post-threshold features; orange for y and for Soft); 'CS Sampling' and 'Initialization' are rotated coloured labels squeezed between bars; the Soft step is reached by diagonal arrows off the main line.

figures.lesson: Draw an unrolled optimiser as a row of identical tinted phase panels with ellipses between them, and pull one phase out through a dashed zoom box into a full-width detail panel, keeping the same tint so the reader knows it is the same unit.

figures.title: iTransformer: Inverted Transformers Are Effective for Time Series Forecasting

taxonomy.task: multivariate time-series forecasting

arrangement.units: two unenclosed rows (Transformer view, iTransformer view), each a plot followed by a 3-D cube pipeline
arrangement.inputs_as: multivariate line plots with token markings
arrangement.shared: same pipeline order (embedding, attention, FFN, representation) in both rows

insights.structure: Two stacked rows contrast the vanilla Transformer view (top) with the iTransformer view (bottom), joined by a purple 'Invert' arrow on the left; each row pairs a multivariate line plot with a 3-D cube pipeline of attention and FFN.
insights.data: Inputs are three coloured time-series curves; tokens are red vertical bars across time (top) vs dashed boxes around each whole series (bottom); representations are stacks of coloured cubes, grey for mixed and teal/gold per variate for unmixed.
insights.emphasis: Colour carries the argument: red marks the time-step token and 'Mixed', blue marks the variate token and 'Unmixed', and the bottom row keeps per-variate colours through the cubes while the top row turns grey.
insights.flow: Each row reads left-to-right from plot through a hollow arrow into embed, attention slab, FFN slabs and output cubes; the eye compares the rows vertically.
insights.avoid: The translucent attention and FFN slabs are nearly identical between rows, so the difference relies on small rotated labels and cube colours.

core.what: Transformer view (top) and iTransformer view (bottom) as two identical rows, joined by a purple 'Invert' arrow, each pairing the tokenized series on the left with its 3-D token stack, attention and FFN on the right

relations.form: two rows with the same layout (series plot, hollow arrow, cube stack, attention box, FFN slabs, output cubes), prior on top and ours below, a big purple downward 'Invert' arrow between their labels
tokens are drawn on the series plots themselves: red vertical bars across all three curves at single time steps (top) versus blue dashed boxes around each whole curve (bottom)
in each row left to right on the right side: embedded token cubes, a translucent beige attention volume, translucent blue FFN slabs, then the output representation cubes

channels.colour: curve colours (light blue, teal, yellow) = the three variates, carried into the bottom row's cubes so 'unmixed' is visible, while the top row's cubes are grey = mixed; red vs blue also mark the two views and their token outlines, so red/blue carry view while the variate palette carries identity
channels.shape: cubes = embedded token entries; translucent box = attention; stacked translucent slabs = FFN; curves = raw series
channels.line: hollow block arrows = data into the model; black double arrows label the Embedding / Time Steps / Variates axes
channels.frame: red outline = one temporal token, blue dashed outline = one variate token

quality.strengths: The inversion is pure geometry: the same pipeline drawn twice, tokens cut vertically across time in one and horizontally per series in the other, and the representations are drawn as cube stacks whose colour shows variate-mixed (grey) versus variate-unmixed (per-variate colours).
quality.weaknesses: Attention and FFN are blank translucent volumes with no indication of what attends to what; the 3-D cubes are ink-heavy and the axis arrows (Embedding, Time Steps, Variates) crowd the first stack.

figures.lesson: Contrast two tokenizations on the same drawn curves (a vertical bar across all variates at one time step vs a dashed box around one whole variate) and keep the variate colours in the 3-D token cubes only for the proposed row, with grey cubes meaning mixed.

figures.title: K-Planes: Explicit Radiance Fields in Space, Time, and Appearance

taxonomy.task: radiance fields for static and dynamic scenes factorised into planes over every pair of space and time axes

arrangement.units: no enclosed regions: two plane triads, a zoom detail tied by a light-blue wedge, an equation, a plot and a loss equation, each with a lettered caption
arrangement.inputs_as: a 3-D render of a person labelled 'Training Image' with a camera glyph and a ray leaving it
arrangement.losses_at: bottom right, a typeset sum of three loss terms under the rendering plot
arrangement.shared: none

insights.data: The training image is a 3-D person render; the query point is a gradient sphere projected onto grid planes; rendering is drawn as a density-vs-distance plot and a colour swatch.
insights.emphasis: Size and perspective: the plane triads are the largest, most three-dimensional objects, and the red/blue scale cells are the only saturated marks on them.
insights.flow: Left to right along the ray, then a straight arrow into the zoom, down to the equation, a dashed S-curve up to the decoder and rendering plot, and down to the loss.
insights.avoid: Do not replace the combination step and the objective with typeset equations, and keep the step order on one reading line instead of a lettered zigzag.

core.what: the query point q on a camera ray is projected by dotted lines onto six perspective grid planes, drawn as two intersecting triads (Space, Space-Time), with its sampled cells marked red and blue per scale

relations.form: two 3-D plane triads crossed by the ray, q as a gradient sphere at each, dotted projections ending in red and blue cells on each plane
a light-blue wedge from the Space-Time q to a flat grid detail where red (S=1) and blue (S=2) squares interpolate the centre from their corners
lettered captions a) to f): planes, interpolation, product, decoder, rendering, loss, placed in a zigzag (b and d top, c and f bottom) joined by a straight arrow and a dashed S-curve
the combination of plane features is a typeset union-of-products equation equated to the sphere glyph, not drawn

channels.shape: perspective grid = feature plane, sphere = query point / its feature, square cells = sampled grid cells, corner circles = grid vertices, line plot = density along the ray, square swatch = predicted colour
channels.line: solid dark line = camera ray; dotted teal = projection onto a plane; dashed S-curve = jump to the decoder; thin coloured arrows = interpolation weights
channels.frame: none; the zoom is tied by a translucent wedge instead

quality.strengths: The factorisation itself is the figure's geometry: the six planes drawn in perspective with the point projected onto each, so the reader sees what is looked up where; scale is coded red / blue identically on the planes and in the zoomed interpolation; the input is a real render with the ray leaving it.
quality.weaknesses: The feature combination (c) and the loss (f) are typeset equations instead of drawn terms; the decoder (d) has no block; the step order zigzags between rows and needs the letters, with a dashed S-curve from c up to d; blue is reused for the camera, wedge and density curve besides scale S=2; no ground truth is drawn beside the predicted colour.

figures.lesson: Draw a factorised field as the planes themselves in perspective, with the query point projected onto each by dotted lines and the sampled cells coloured by scale, then zoom one plane into the interpolation in the same colours.

figures.title: Generalization through Memorization: Nearest Neighbor Language Models

taxonomy.task: language modeling with nearest-neighbor retrieval

arrangement.units: each step is a bordered table panel with a header title and formula; panels align in two rows (datastore, test)
arrangement.inputs_as: quoted text contexts in table cells
arrangement.shared: the encoder f appears as identical Representation panels in both rows
