core.what: a datastore drawn as a table of training contexts, targets and key vectors on the left, queried by the test representation q through a distance column, the k nearest rows carried right as their target words

relations.form: datastore table (contexts c_i, targets v_i, representations k_i as rows of shaded circles) at top left, retrieved neighbours shown as real words (Hawaii, Illinois, Hawaii) with their distances in a separate 'Nearest k' card
the test representation q (bottom left) sends a line up into the 'Distances' column, where it meets an arrow from every key row, giving one distance per row
titled table cards left to right: Distances, Nearest k, Normalization, Aggregation, each a column of the same words with a new number column
the kNN distribution (Aggregation, top right) and the LM distribution (Classification, bottom middle) converge on one 'Interpolation' card at bottom right

channels.colour: fill = kind of datum: cyan = context text, yellow = target words, pink = vector representations, green = distances, lavender = probabilities; one meaning each, kept across all cards
channels.shape: titled table card = one computed quantity; row of grey-shaded circles = a vector
channels.line: thin black arrows = values passed between cards; crossing arrows between Distances and Nearest k show re-sorting
channels.frame: each card's white header holds its name and the symbol or formula it computes

quality.strengths: Every intermediate is drawn as data with the same running example (Obama's birthplace, Hawaii/Illinois) and a consistent colour per kind of value, so the reader can follow numbers from distance 3 to probability 0.7 to 0.8 to the interpolated 0.6.
quality.weaknesses: Card headers carry full formulas (p(k_i) proportional to exp(-d_i), the aggregation sum and the interpolation equation) instead of names; the query path runs a long line along the bottom and up into Distances, and the arrows from Distances to Nearest k cross each other.

figures.lesson: Colour encodes the kind of value (sentence, word, vector, distance, probability) and stays the same in every table, so one worked example can be traced row by row through the pipeline without a legend.

figures.title: Language Is Not All You Need: Aligning Perception with Language Models

taxonomy.task: multimodal LLM with in-context learning
taxonomy.note: the figure draws the MLLM as one decoder bar over embedded multimodal input; paradigm GPT = a causal language model taking interleaved input

arrangement.units: an unframed model schematic across the top half, then three rounded outlined example panels of equal width in a row
arrangement.inputs_as: real photos, a receipt image and a waveform inside one rounded grey tray, labelled Vision and Audition
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; 'output' with an up-arrow at the top-right of the model bar
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: The top half is a three-level bottom-to-top schematic (input tray, Embedding chip, model bar) and the bottom half three equal rounded example panels, so model and capability demos are separated by whitespace.
insights.data: Inputs are real images, a receipt and a waveform in one grey tray, and the interleaved input is a sentence with three green token squares inline; demos are chat bubbles, pale blue for prompts and pale pink for model output.
insights.emphasis: The MLLM bar spans the full width in bold type with a robot icon, and 'Kosmos-1' is bold at the start of the sentence beneath it.
insights.flow: Short black up-arrows run tray -> Embedding -> sentence -> MLLM -> output; the example panels below have no arrows and are read left to right.
insights.avoid: The model is a single undifferentiated bar, so the figure says nothing about how the embedding connects to the language model; it works only as a teaser, not as an architecture reference.

core.what: one full-width light-blue 'Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM)' bar across the top, over a single input sentence that interleaves words with green embedding squares, standing for one model behind all modalities and tasks

relations.form: the MLLM bar spans the whole figure width above the input line and the three example panels
a grey tray of image, document and audio samples (Vision, Audition) sends one up-arrow into an 'Embedding' tag, whose green squares sit inline in the text sentence fed to the MLLM
three rounded panels at the bottom each hold a chat read top to bottom: blue prompt bubbles with images, pink answer bubbles (duck-rabbit dialogue, woodpecker question, a Raven-style puzzle)

channels.colour: light blue = both the model bar/Embedding tag and the user-side prompt bubbles (two meanings); pink = model answers; green squares = non-text embedded tokens
channels.shape: speech bubbles = dialogue turns; real photos, a receipt, a waveform and line drawings = input data
channels.line: only two up-arrows (into Embedding, out of the MLLM to 'output')
channels.frame: light-grey rounded tray = the perceivable modalities; white rounded panels = one example task each

quality.strengths: Inputs are real data (a Wall-E still, a receipt, an audio waveform) and the interleaving of modalities into a language sequence is shown concretely by green squares placed between words; the one-model-many-tasks claim is shown by a single bar over everything.
quality.weaknesses: The three example panels, which take over half the area, are not connected to the model by any line, and the model itself is an opaque bar; light blue marks both the model and the user prompts; 'Audition' is greyed out without a key saying why.

figures.lesson: Show that a model reads interleaved modalities by writing a plain sentence with small coloured token squares set inline where the image would go, directly under the model bar.

figures.title: Label Words are Anchors: An Information Flow Perspective for Understanding In-Context Learning

taxonomy.task: explaining in-context learning in GPT models as information flow through label-word tokens across layers
taxonomy.note: family other = interpretability analysis of in-context learning in decoder-only language models

arrangement.units: two unframed horizontal lanes, each one prompt strip with its arcs above and a coloured depth tag at the right; a vertical ellipsis between the lanes stands for the intermediate layers
arrangement.inputs_as: abbreviated quoted demonstrations and a query as tinted text bands, label words in red
arrangement.shared: the same prompt strip is drawn identically in both lanes

insights.structure: Two copies of one prompt strip stacked by layer depth, shallow above and deep below, each with its own flow drawn as arcs over it.
insights.data: The prompt is the real data: two sentiment demonstrations and a query as tinted bands with their abbreviated text, the label words in red.
insights.emphasis: All arcs converge on or leave from the red label words, and the two flows differ by arc colour (blue aggregation, orange prediction) matching the depth tags.
insights.flow: In the shallow strip, short blue arcs fan from within each demonstration into its label word; in the deep strip, long orange arcs leave both label words and converge on the query's final ':'.
insights.avoid: The arc labels are curved WordArt text that is harder to read than straight labels, and shallow-above-deep reverses the usual bottom-to-top layer order; set depth top-down only with an explicit tag as here.

core.what: the information flow is drawn as arcs directly over the prompt's token strip - blue arcs into each label word in shallow layers, orange arcs from the label words to the prediction slot in deep layers

relations.form: arcs drawn above a strip of tinted prompt segments, their ends placed on the actual words they connect
several blue arcs fan in from inside a demonstration to one arrowhead on its label word; two orange arcs from both label words converge on the query's ':'
the strip is repeated twice top to bottom, shallow layers then deep layers, separated by a vertical ellipsis, each tagged at the right in its arc colour

channels.colour: band tint = prompt segment (two greens for demonstrations, yellow for the query); arc and tag colour = layer depth and its flow (blue shallow aggregation, orange deep prediction); red text = label words and the prediction slot
channels.shape: bands = prompt segments, arcs = information flow, small boxes = depth tags
channels.line: one style: curved arcs with a single arrowhead at their convergence point; colour, not style, distinguishes the two flows
channels.frame: none; lanes are separated by whitespace and an ellipsis

quality.strengths: The hypothesis is drawn on its structure: arcs land on the actual tokens, so 'demonstrations flow into label words, label words flow into the answer' reads from geometry alone. Each channel holds one meaning - band tint for segment, arc colour for depth, red for the anchors - and the depth tags reuse the arc colours as a key. Minimal ink: two strips and two arc families.
quality.weaknesses: Shallow-aggregation arcs start at unlabelled points inside each demonstration, so which tokens feed the label word is suggested, not shown. The curved WordArt arc labels are hard to read. The strip is shown only twice with an ellipsis, so the shallow-to-deep transition the paper studies is not drawn.

figures.lesson: Draw an information-flow hypothesis on the prompt itself: repeat the token strip once per depth and draw that depth's flow as arcs over it, colouring the arcs like the depth tag at the strip's end.

figures.title: Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning, Acting, and Planning in Language Models

taxonomy.task: LM agent reasoning, acting and planning via Monte Carlo tree search

arrangement.units: six unbordered columns, one per search operation, each titled with a number and name and holding a small tree or LM chain
arrangement.inputs_as: a blue 'Input' ellipse as the tree root at the top of each panel
arrangement.shared: the LM is redrawn as the same lavender box in the Evaluation and Reflection panels

insights.structure: Six borderless panels in a single row, each a numbered MCTS operation drawn on the same small tree of an Input ellipse and S1/S2/S3 squares, with the Evaluation and Reflection panels replacing the tree by a vertical LM -> Value / LM -> Reflection chain.
insights.data: States are small labelled squares (S1, S2, S3), the root and terminal are blue Input and green Output ellipses, the language model is a lavender 'LM' box and its products are pale yellow 'Value' and 'Reflection' boxes.
insights.emphasis: Colour carries the operation: the selected node is solid red, the active branch is pink with red arrows, unexplored siblings are grey, and backpropagation adds thicker red upward arrows beside the downward ones.
insights.flow: Read panels left to right by their 1) to 6) titles; within each panel arrows run top to bottom down the tree, except Backpropagation where paired arrows point back up to the root.
insights.avoid: The 'Value' and 'Reflection' boxes use very small type relative to the S-node labels, and the panels have no separators so 'S' in panel 6 floats without context.

core.what: six numbered operation panels left to right (Selection, Expansion, Evaluation, Simulation, Backpropagation, Reflection), each a small search tree or LM step

relations.form: six unframed columns with numbered titles in one row, the tree growing from one level (Selection) to three levels (Simulation, Backpropagation)
each tree operation is drawn on a small toy tree of state boxes S1-S3 under an Input ellipse, the active path pink and the unexplored siblings grey
Evaluation and Reflection are vertical chains: state S or Output into a purple LM box, out to a yellow Value or Reflection box ('Reflection + S')
Backpropagation draws paired arrows on each tree edge, pink down and bold red up from Output to Input

channels.colour: node colour = search status: dark red = the selected node, pink = nodes on the current path, grey = unexplored; blue ellipse = input, green ellipse = output, purple = LM, yellow = LM product (value, reflection); arrow colour follows the node colour, and bold red additionally means the upward value update
channels.shape: ellipse = input/output text, square = state, rounded box = LM, flat box = scalar or text produced
channels.line: arrows = tree edges/transitions; red upward arrows = backpropagated value
channels.frame: none; panels separated by whitespace and titles

quality.strengths: The tree operations are drawn on an actual tree that grows across panels, and status colouring (selected, on-path, unexplored) is consistent in panels 1, 2, 4 and 5.
quality.weaknesses: Evaluation and Reflection switch to a separate LM chain, so the node being scored or reflected on is not located in the tree; no arrow returns from 6) to 1), so the loop of the search is only implied by numbering; the selected node is dark red in 1) but pink in 2), and dark red reappears on the free-standing S in 3).

figures.lesson: Show a search algorithm as a filmstrip of the same tree, one panel per operation, recolouring only the nodes the current operation touches.

figures.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models

taxonomy.task: conditional image synthesis in a learned latent space

arrangement.units: three tinted, rounded panels side by side: Pixel Space (red tint), Latent Space (green tint, with a nested Denoising U-Net frame), Conditioning (grey)
arrangement.inputs_as: image x as a purple rounded square at top-left; conditioning types (semantic map, text, representations, images) as stacked coloured cards at right
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Three tinted panels left to right (pixel, latent, conditioning), with the U-Net nested as a second-level frame inside the latent panel and a glyph legend under all three.
insights.data: Images are symbolic purple squares x and x~, latents are tall dark-green bars labelled z, z_T, z_{T-1}, and the conditioning inputs are overlapping coloured cards rather than real examples.
insights.emphasis: The orange Q/K/V cross-attention squares are the only warm colour inside the blue U-Net, and every conditioning arrow from tau_theta lands on them.
insights.flow: Top row runs left to right (x -> E -> z -> diffusion -> z_T), then the bottom row runs back right to left through the U-Net and decoder to x~, with a small loop marked x(T-1) for repeated denoising.
insights.avoid: Conditioning lines from tau_theta run along the bottom edge and up into each attention block, crossing the grey dashed skip arrows, and the 'switch' glyph is hard to decode without the legend.

core.what: three tinted regions left to right: Pixel Space (pink, encoder and decoder), Latent Space (green, diffusion and the denoising U-Net) and Conditioning (grey), so diffusion is visibly enclosed between encoding and decoding

relations.form: pink Pixel Space panel at left, a larger green Latent Space panel in the middle, a grey Conditioning panel at right, each with a bold title
a U-shaped path: top row x, encoder E, latent z, a 'Diffusion Process' bar to z_T; bottom row back from z_T through the U-Net to z_{T-1}, z, decoder D and x-tilde
a small denoising-step glyph between z_{T-1} and z with a curved self-loop labelled x(T-1)

the conditioning inputs (semantic map, text, representations, images) funnel down into encoder tau_theta, whose output wire runs along the bottom and up into each QKV cross-attention block inside the U-Net, and a switch icon at the U-Net's lower right where a curved concat arrow also enters
the denoising U-Net is drawn opened inside its own green inner panel, its two trapezoid halves holding four QKV blocks with dashed skip connections above

channels.colour: region tint = space (pink pixel, green latent, grey conditioning); dark-green bars = latents z; light-blue trapezoids = networks; orange-outlined QKV boxes = cross-attention; conditioning samples each a different colour by modality
channels.shape: trapezoid = encoder/decoder/U-Net half; tall thin bar = latent; square glyphs for denoising step, cross-attention and switch keyed in a bottom legend
channels.line: solid black = data; dashed grey = skip connection; curved arrow = concat (keyed)
channels.frame: rounded tinted panel = a space; inner rounded panel = the U-Net

quality.strengths: The paper's point that diffusion runs in latent space is shown by position and tint: the diffusion and U-Net sit inside the green Latent Space between a pink pixel-space encoder and decoder; the latent z is drawn as a bar at every hand-off and every glyph type is keyed in a legend.
quality.weaknesses: The conditioning wire from tau_theta bends along the bottom and branches up into the U-Net, crossing the switch and the return path; the bottom row reads right to left against the top row; the T-1 denoising loop is compressed into a tiny glyph.

figures.lesson: Make the paper's key idea a region rather than a box: tint each 'space' (pixel, latent, conditioning) as its own panel so a reader sees where the computation happens before reading any module.

figures.title: LERF: Language Embedded Radiance Fields

taxonomy.task: language-queryable 3-D field by distilling a multiscale CLIP feature pyramid into a radiance field queried along rays with a scale

arrangement.units: two unframed halves split by a vertical dashed line, each with a title: rendering (left), CLIP preprocessing (right)
arrangement.inputs_as: left: a real reconstructed tabletop scene with a camera glyph and image plane; right edge: a real training photo with nested green crop squares, then three real image patches
arrangement.losses_at: one pink 'Language Loss' box at the lower centre-left, under the network's CLIP output and fed from the pyramid across the divider
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Two titled halves split by a vertical dashed line, the rendering half left and the target-building half right, joined only at the Language Loss box.
insights.data: The scene is a real reconstruction render with the ray drawn through it; the training image, its nested crops and three real patches are photos; CLIP features are a three-level pyramid of tilted mosaic planes.
insights.emphasis: No highlight box; the red scale cube on the ray and the green crop squares on the image are the only saturated marks besides the purple pyramid.
insights.flow: Left half runs left to right from camera along the ray into the network and down to the loss; right half runs right to left from the training image through CLIP into the pyramid and out to the loss.
insights.avoid: Do not loop arrows out of an encoder and back into a stack - place the pyramid so each level is reached by a straight line.

core.what: the field's rendered CLIP feature (left half) and the multiscale CLIP pyramid built from image crops (right half) flow toward each other and meet at one Language Loss box beside the dashed divider

relations.form: rendering path left of the divider, pyramid path right of it, their outputs converging on the pink Language Loss box at the lower centre
the ray is drawn through the real reconstructed scene with dots along it and a red wireframe cube sitting on it for the sampled volume and its scale
a blue arrow (x,y,z,theta,phi) and a red arrow (scale) leave the ray and converge on the teal Network bars
right half read right to left: training image with nested green squares -> three crops -> CLIP trapezoid -> hooked arrows into the three pyramid levels

channels.colour: quantity: blue = position and view (camera, blue arrow), red = 3-D scale (cube, 'scale' arrow), green = image crop scale (nested squares, s_img bracket); lavender = CLIP side (encoder, Volume Render); pink = loss; the pyramid's purple mosaic is feature values and its orange cells have no key
channels.shape: trapezoid = CLIP encoder, bars = MLP network, tilted tiled planes = feature pyramid, rounded pills = operations and loss, photos = data, wireframe cube = sampled volume
channels.line: thick black arrows = data flow (curved and hooked on the right); coloured arrows = network inputs; navy line with dots = camera ray; dotted lines join the pyramid levels
channels.frame: none; a vertical dashed line separates the two halves

quality.strengths: The two sources of the objective face each other across a divider with the loss between them; the data is drawn throughout (real scene and ray, real crops, the pyramid as tilted tiled planes); scale is coded by colour on both sides, a red cube on the ray against green nested crops on the image.
quality.weaknesses: The right half reads right to left through hooked arrows that loop out of CLIP and back into each pyramid level; the loss where everything meets is a small pill at the lower edge; three of the four network outputs (R,G,B, Density, DINO Features) are dead-end text labels; the orange cells in the pyramid are unexplained.

figures.lesson: Draw the target-building path as the mirror of the rendering path - each half flowing toward the one loss at the divider - and colour the scale on both sides (a red cube on the ray, green nested crops on the image).

figures.title: Lift, Splat, Shoot: Encoding Images From Arbitrary Camera Rigs by Implicitly Unprojecting to 3D

taxonomy.task: lifting image features to a 3-D frustum

arrangement.units: one unboxed scene: a perspective camera sketch beside a labeled matrix with dimension brackets
arrangement.inputs_as: real street photo on a tilted image plane
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Two halves: on the left a tilted street photo with rays fanning from a camera icon and bars along one ray; on the right a C x D heat-map grid labeled 'per-pixel outer product'.
insights.data: Depth distribution alpha is drawn as blue bars of varying length along the ray and as a vertical colour strip, feature c as a second strip; their product is a blue-shaded matrix with columns alpha_0 c ... alpha_D c.
insights.emphasis: The darkest column in the matrix matches the longest bar on the ray, visually tying the peak depth to where the feature is placed.
insights.flow: Two black arrows lead from the alpha and c strips into the matrix, left to right; rays converge on the camera at bottom right.

core.what: the lift drawn on the camera geometry: rays fan from a camera icon to a street photo, and along one ray black depth points carry blue bars whose length is the depth distribution alpha

relations.form: light-blue rays from a camera icon at bottom right to the corners and pixels of a perspective street image at left; one ray marked with discrete black depth points, each with a slanted blue bar

two diagonal arrows carry the depth distribution alpha and the 4-cell feature vector c into a D x C grid at right, its columns labelled alpha_0 c, alpha_1 c, ..., alpha_D c and captioned 'per-pixel outer product'

channels.colour: blue intensity = magnitude: bar length/shade for depth probability, cell shade for feature value and for the product in the grid; light-blue thin lines = camera rays
channels.shape: black dots = depth bins on a ray; slanted bars = per-bin probability; cell grid = the lifted frustum feature for one pixel
channels.line: thin light-blue = camera rays; black arrows = values combined into the outer product
channels.frame: brackets with D and C mark the grid's axes

quality.strengths: The operation is drawn on its structure: discrete depths along a real camera ray, and the outer product as an actual D x C grid whose darkest column matches the most probable depth, so the reader sees the feature being placed at a depth.
quality.weaknesses: The label 'depth distribution alpha' sits beside the ray while a separate 4-cell column is labelled 'feature c', and the two arrows into the grid start from loosely placed points, so which arrow carries alpha and which c is not explicit; only one ray of the image is lifted.

figures.lesson: Draw per-pixel depth as bars of different length laid along the camera ray, then show the lifted feature as a blue-shaded depth x channel matrix with dimension brackets, so the depth peak reappears as the matrix's darkest column.

figures.title: Lift, Splat, Shoot: Encoding Images From Arbitrary Camera Rigs by Implicitly Unprojecting to 3D

taxonomy.task: bird's-eye-view semantic segmentation from multi-camera images

arrangement.units: four unboxed pictorial stages, each captioned below
arrangement.inputs_as: stack of real camera photos
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Four stages in a row with captions underneath: stacked camera photos, a wireframe frustum labeled xN, six photos arranged around a top-down car with blue camera frusta, and a stack of BEV output maps.
insights.data: Inputs are real multi-camera photos stacked with grey arrows, the lift is a line-drawn frustum, the splat is the car icon with photos at their mounting positions, outputs are white maps with coloured blobs.
insights.emphasis: The central splat panel is the largest and most colourful, with blue translucent frusta radiating from the car, making the camera-to-BEV projection the focal point.
insights.flow: Strictly left-to-right with plain black arrows between stages; captions under each stage name the operation.
insights.avoid: No module boxes or tensor shapes are given, so it conveys the idea but not the network; the frustum xN glyph is abstract.

core.what: four pictures in one left-to-right row joined by short black arrows: a stack of camera images, a lifted frustum, the six views splatted around a top-down car, a stack of bird's-eye-view output maps

relations.form: image stack, frustum glyph labelled 'xN', splat composite, BEV map stack, each with its step name ('Per-Image CNN + Lift', 'Extrinsics + Splat', 'Bird's-Eye-View CNN') as a caption underneath
the splat is drawn in the vehicle's own frame: six real camera images placed around a top-down car icon with translucent blue frustum wedges fanning out from it

channels.colour: translucent blue = camera frustums in the splat; orange, cyan and magenta marks in the BEV maps = predicted classes, unkeyed
channels.shape: photo stacks = per-camera inputs, wire-frame frustum = the lifted per-image volume, stacked white squares = BEV output channels
channels.line: four short black arrows, straight and aligned on the row's centre line
channels.frame: none

quality.strengths: The middle panel, which is the novel step, is the largest and shows the splat geometrically: real images in their true positions around the car with their frustums overlapping in the shared BEV plane.
quality.weaknesses: No networks are drawn; the step names are captions under pictures, so the CNNs are implied only by text; the output maps' colours are not keyed and the frustum glyph's 'xN' is the only hint that each image is lifted separately.

figures.lesson: Show the camera-to-BEV step as a top-view ego car ringed by its camera images, each under a translucent blue frustum fanning out from the car, so the rig geometry itself is the transform stage rather than a labelled box.

figures.title: LightGCN: Simplifying and Powering Graph Convolution Network for Recommendation

taxonomy.task: collaborative filtering recommendation

arrangement.units: two mirrored towers (user, item), each with stacked layer cards inside a dotted rectangle
arrangement.inputs_as: neighbor node circles with embedding symbols
arrangement.shared: the same LGC layer structure in both towers

insights.structure: Two mirrored columns, user u1 on the left and item i4 on the right, each a stack of Layer 1-3 cards inside a dotted box labeled Light Graph Convolution, with embedding stacks above meeting in a top prediction node.
insights.data: Neighbors are small circles with embedding symbols, the aggregator is a 'Normalized Sum' grey box, layer embeddings e^(k) are three-cell colour rows on a slanted parallelogram, e^(0) sits alone beside them.
insights.emphasis: Red text labels the two contributions ('Layer Combination (weighted sum)', 'Light Graph Convolution (LGC)'), and the dashed yellow loop arrows show layer repetition.
insights.flow: Bottom-up: neighbors feed the Normalized Sum, layers stack upward into embedding rows, which combine via circled-plus nodes into the red Prediction node at top.
insights.avoid: The slanted parallelograms and stacked card shadows add depth that conveys nothing and crowd the labels.

core.what: a user tower (u1, left) and an item tower (i4, right) mirror each other and meet at one pink ⊗ Prediction node at top centre

relations.form: the two towers stand side by side, each ending in a ⊕ node, and the two ⊕ outputs converge on a single ⊗ Prediction circle between them
inside each Layer 1 card, neighbour nodes drawn as circles (i1, i2, i3 for u1; u2, u3 for i4) with their embeddings e^(l-1) send arrows into a grey dashed 'Normalized Sum' box
three offset stacked cards 'Layer 1', 'Layer 2', 'Layer 3' under each tower, with a yellow dotted curved arrow at each Normalized Sum
the layer embeddings e^(1), e^(2), e^(3) stacked in a blue parallelogram and the input embedding e^(0) beside them are joined into the ⊕ 'Layer Combination (weighted sum)'

channels.colour: cell shade in embedding bars = values (blue tones on the user side, grey tones on the item side, so shade also marks the side); red text = the two named components (LGC, Layer Combination); yellow dotted = the recurrence across layers
channels.shape: circle = graph node; 3-cell bar = embedding; ⊕ / ⊗ circles = sum and inner product
channels.line: grey arrows = embeddings passed upward; yellow dotted curved arrows = repeated layer application
channels.frame: dotted rectangle = the Light Graph Convolution region; stacked cards = layers; pale-blue parallelogram = the set of per-layer embeddings

quality.strengths: Every compared representation is drawn as a cell bar with its layer index, between the graph convolution that makes it and the combination and prediction that use it; the two sides are symmetric so the inner-product pairing reads as geometry.
quality.weaknesses: The e^(0) bars sit off to the side and reach their ⊕ by elbowed lines; the yellow dotted arrows are unexplained; the vertical arrows from the layer stack jump from the back cards to the parallelogram without showing which layer feeds which bar.

figures.lesson: Draw the user and the item as mirror-image towers, each fed only by its own few labelled neighbour circles and ending in an embedding row, so the towers meet at one score node at the top and the symmetry itself says 'user and item are treated alike'.

figures.title: LightGlue: Local Feature Matching at Light Speed

taxonomy.task: matching sparse local features between two images with adaptive depth and width
taxonomy.note: family other: sparse local feature matching (SuperGlue line), not covered by the family list

arrangement.units: four rounded tinted panels left to right: grey Layer #1 (opened), pale-green Pruning, narrow grey Layer #N (collapsed), pale-green Matching
arrangement.inputs_as: two tilted image parallelograms with blue (A) and red (B) keypoint dots, labelled 'local features'
arrangement.shared: each image's rail passes its own tan 'self' box, and one 'cross' box sits between the two rails, tapped by both

insights.structure: Two colour-coded rails (A blue on top, B red at the bottom) run through four tinted panels left to right; inside Layer #1 each rail passes its own self-attention box and both meet at one cross-attention box between them, and an exit gate hangs below each layer.
insights.data: Inputs are keypoint dots on image parallelograms, pruned points are black crosses on the same drawings, and the output is a similarity matrix with A's descriptor column and a pink row beneath.
insights.emphasis: The new mechanisms take space: Pruning is its own green panel drawn on the keypoints, Layer #N is shrunk to a narrow strip, and the exit decision is a black line from each confidence head down to a gate answering 'no' or 'yes!'.
insights.flow: The coloured rails are straight horizontal lines across the whole figure with short vertical taps into the attention boxes; black control lines drop from the confidence heads to the gates and turn back up into Pruning or Matching.
insights.avoid: The 'no' branch hooking back up into the Pruning panel is cramped, and the door-shaped exit icon is not readable without its 'exit?' label.

core.what: the layer stack drawn as Layer #1 opened in full, a Pruning panel, then a collapsed narrow Layer #N, each layer with an exit gate below that answers 'no' (prune and continue) or 'yes!' (go to Matching)

relations.form: A's blue rail above and B's red rail below face each other across one cross-attention box in Layer #1 and end on a similarity matrix with A's descriptor cells as a column at its left and a pink row beneath
each image's rail passes its own tan self-attention box, the two stacked one above the other in Layer #1
pruning drawn on the keypoints themselves: the image parallelograms repeated in the Pruning panel with black crosses on the dropped blue and red points
four tinted panels in one left-to-right row (Layer #1, Pruning, Layer #N, Matching) ending in an 'assignment' arrow

channels.colour: blue = image A, red = image B (dots, rails, descriptor cells; the pink row under the matrix, fed by B's rail, is labelled 'matchability'); tan = attention units; grey = confidence classifiers and the layer-panel tint; pale green = non-layer stages (Pruning, Matching); grey shading inside the matrix = similarity value
channels.shape: rounded rectangle = learned unit; circled plus = residual add; circled dot = positional encoding; parallelogram with dots = an image's keypoints; grid = similarity matrix; door icon = exit gate
channels.line: coloured arrows = per-image data; black arrows = control (confidence -> exit decision)
channels.frame: tinted rounded panel = one layer or stage; narrow panel = a collapsed repeat of the layer

quality.strengths: Data is drawn as keypoints and the matching as a matrix; one colour per image is held from inputs to output; pruning is drawn on the keypoints themselves; the repeated layer is taught once and collapsed later, so space goes to the adaptive mechanisms (exit gates, pruning); the rails are straight lines through the whole figure and control signals are separated from data by black line colour.
quality.weaknesses: The pink row under the matrix is fed by B's red rail yet labelled 'matchability', so whether it shows B's descriptors or a matchability score is unclear; the 'no' hook back into Pruning is cramped; the exit icon is cryptic without its label.

figures.lesson: Teach a repeated layer once in full and collapse its later copy to a narrow strip showing only what changes (the confidence heads), so the space goes to the new mechanisms - exit gates and pruning - drawn between the layers.

figures.title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models

taxonomy.task: training a chat LLM

arrangement.units: three rounded white panels with pill-shaped stage tags; a nested grey sub-panel for RLHF
arrangement.inputs_as: icon of pretraining data
arrangement.shared: a feedback loop from Llama-2-chat back into human feedback

insights.structure: Three rounded white panels with dark pill tags: HUMAN FEEDBACK at top left, PRETRAINING at bottom left, FINE-TUNING on the right containing a grey RLHF sub-panel and the Llama-2-chat block.
insights.data: Data and models are icons (cloud-database, person with speech bubbles, shield and hand icons for reward models); steps are diamonds and models are grey rounded rectangles.
insights.emphasis: Self-supervised learning is the only saturated blue diamond, and Llama-2-chat is the largest dark block; the RLHF loop is drawn as two circular arrows between the sub-panel and the chat model.
insights.flow: Bottom row runs left-to-right from pretraining data to Llama 2 to SFT to Llama-2-chat; a thick line from chat climbs over the top and returns into human feedback, whose reward models feed the RLHF sub-panel.
insights.avoid: Very low contrast pale grey arrows and lavender diamonds on a pale grey background make the flow hard to read in print.

core.what: Llama-2-chat at bottom right loops back twice: by two curved arrows into the RLHF box above it, and by a long wire over the top of the figure into Human Feedback

relations.form: three white rounded panels tagged by grey pill labels: Pretraining along the bottom left, Human Feedback at top left, Fine-tuning at right
along the bottom: pretraining data cloud, blue diamond Self-supervised learning, grey box Llama 2, lavender diamond Supervised fine-tuning, dark grey Llama-2-chat
inside Fine-tuning, a grey RLHF panel holds Rejection Sampling and Proximal Policy Optimization joined by a curved arrow, with curved arrows cycling between it and Llama-2-chat below
from the human preference icon two arrows lead to the Safety and Helpful reward model icons, and one arrow leaves the Human Feedback panel into the RLHF box

channels.colour: dark grey = models (Llama 2, Llama-2-chat); saturated blue = the self-supervised pretraining step only; lavender = fine-tuning procedures; grey pills = stage names; one meaning each
channels.shape: diamond = training procedure, rectangle = model, circle icon = data or reward model
channels.line: thick light-grey arrows = flow; curved light-grey arrows = the RLHF loop
channels.frame: white rounded panel = one stage; inner grey panel = RLHF

quality.strengths: Procedure versus model is kept apart by shape (diamonds vs rectangles), and the iterative RLHF is drawn as an actual cycle around the model rather than stated.
quality.weaknesses: The only saturated element is pretraining's blue diamond, not the fine-tuning contribution; the feedback wire wraps around the whole figure's top and right edge; the two reward models are not connected individually to PPO or rejection sampling, only one arrow leaves their panel; preference data and comparisons are icons, not data.

figures.lesson: Encode node kind by shape across a multi-stage training pipeline (diamonds for training procedures, rounded grey boxes for model checkpoints, pale icon circles for data and reward models) and name each stage with an uppercase pill tab on its region's edge, so the stages and the iterative loops stay readable with only light-grey arrows.

figures.title: Visual Instruction Tuning

taxonomy.task: visual instruction following

arrangement.units: horizontal colored bands for modules (LM, projection, encoder) with token rows floating between them
arrangement.inputs_as: math symbols X_v Image and X_q Language Instruction
arrangement.shared: one LM band spans all tokens

insights.avoid: The fan of thin grey lines through the LM band is faint and does not convey causal decoding; the curved Z_v arrow overlaps the stacked encoder bands awkwardly.

relations.form: two groups of three house-shaped tokens placed in one row, image tokens left and instruction tokens right, both feeding the same green 'Language Model f_phi' band
bottom left, the image X_v enters the blue Vision Encoder band, a curved arrow labelled Z_v rises past the orange Projection W band to H_v; on the right X_q rises straight to H_q
bottom to top across the language-model band: input tokens below, response tokens X_a above

channels.colour: band fill = module (blue vision encoder, orange projection, green language model); token fill = source (white image, grey instruction, green response) — green carries both the language-model band and its output tokens
channels.shape: pentagon 'house' = one token; wide pale band = a module
channels.line: thin grey lines = every input token conditioning every output token; dark arrows = Z_v and H_q
channels.frame: none

quality.strengths: The representations are named and drawn as tokens (Z_v, H_v, H_q, X_a), and placing image and instruction tokens in one row under one band shows the concatenated input directly.
quality.weaknesses: The dense fan of thin lines through the language-model band crosses itself; the Z_v arrow curves out of the encoder and back round the projection band instead of passing straight through it; the projection W, the trained connector, is a thin band at the edge, and the image itself is only the symbol X_v.

figures.lesson: Token glyphs graded by fill (light grey for visual, darker grey for instruction, saturated green for response) separate inputs from generated tokens without a legend.

figures.title: LLM.int8(): 8-bit Matrix Multiplication for Transformers at Scale

taxonomy.task: 8-bit matrix multiplication for LLM inference

arrangement.units: two stacked horizontal lanes, each a dashed-border rectangle titled just outside its top-left corner, with numbered steps inside
arrangement.inputs_as: small numeric matrices X and W with cells coloured cyan (regular) or yellow (outlier)
arrangement.shared: X and W are drawn once at the left and reach both lanes by two curved arrows; the lanes' outputs meet at one circled plus

insights.structure: Two dashed lanes stacked top and bottom, each with numbered steps inside, fan out from one input pair at the left and close at one circled plus at the right.
insights.data: Inputs and intermediates are toy numeric matrices with numbers in every cell, cyan for regular values and yellow for outlier columns, with precision tags as subscripts.
insights.emphasis: The yellow outlier columns are the thread: coloured in the inputs, absent from the 8-bit lane, and reappearing alone in the 16-bit lane.
insights.flow: Start at the large title and the inputs at the left, follow the curved arrows into each lane, read its steps (1)-(4) left to right, then exit right into the plus and the output.
insights.avoid: Equations are set in a sans-serif font with uneven subscripts, and the large method name in the corner takes space without carrying content.

core.what: the input matrices X and W split by two curved arrows into two dashed panels, 8-bit vector-wise quantization above and 16-bit decomposition below, whose outputs meet at one ⊕

relations.form: two dashed-outline panels stacked on the right, each with a bold title, fed from X and W at left by one curved arrow each

X and W are drawn as small numeric matrices; the outlier columns of X and matching rows of W are yellow, and the bottom panel shows only those yellow slices while the top shows only the cyan remainder
numbered sub-steps read left to right inside each panel: (1) find constants, (2) quantize, (3) int8 matmul, (4) dequantize above; (1) decompose outliers, (2) FP16 matmul below
a vertical arrow from the top panel and a horizontal arrow from the bottom panel converge on a large ⊕ circle that outputs Out_FP16

channels.colour: cyan = regular values, yellow = outliers, keyed in a legend at bottom left; one meaning
channels.shape: numeric grid = matrix; circle ⊕ = sum
channels.line: black arrows = data; curved arrows = the split
channels.frame: dashed rectangle = one precision path

quality.strengths: The decomposition is shown on the data itself: real numbers in X and W with outliers (45, -63, -83) coloured yellow, and each path's panel holds exactly its slice of the matrices; the two paths are symmetric dashed panels joined at one sum.
quality.weaknesses: Steps (2)-(4) of the 8-bit path and step (2) of the 16-bit path are typeset equations rather than drawn operations; the vector-wise constants C_x and C_w are pointed at by small arrows to row/column labels that are easy to miss; the large 'LLM.int8()' title spends top-left space.

figures.lesson: Put toy numeric matrices in the figure and colour the special entries (outliers) in one hue, then show those same coloured columns pulled out into their own branch, so the split is visible without reading the text.

figures.title: LongLoRA: Efficient Fine-tuning of Long-Context Large Language Models

taxonomy.task: extending the context length of LLMs by fine-tuning with shifted sparse attention
taxonomy.note: architecture other: no network is drawn; the figure shows an attention-pattern change (token groups shifted across half of the heads)

arrangement.units: one dashed rounded frame labelled 'S²-Attn' holding the step grids and the two masks; no inner frames
arrangement.inputs_as: an 8-row by 4-column grid of numbered token cells shaded by position, with 'Heads' and 'Tokens' axis arrows
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: A left-to-right strip of four token-by-head grids, one per step of the operation, ending in two equal attention masks side by side, all inside one dashed frame.
insights.data: Tokens are numbered rows shaded by position, heads are columns, and the result is shown as two cream query-key masks with orange attended cells.
insights.emphasis: The shifted half carries the visible change (token 8 moved to its top), and the shifted mask's blue outline includes a lone corner block that the unshifted red mask lacks.
insights.flow: Grey block arrows labelled Step 1/2/3 join the grids on one horizontal line; dashed elbow connectors run beneath from 'Pattern1' and 'Pattern2' to the matching mask.
insights.avoid: The step-3 grid is linked to its masks by two long dashed elbow wires running under the row, and blue is used both for the token-position shading and for pattern 2's outline.

core.what: shifted sparse attention drawn on an 8-token by 4-head grid: split into two halves, the second half rolled by half a group (token 8 moves to the top), rows grouped in pairs by thick outlines

relations.form: each step is a copy of the same numbered token-by-head grid, so the split, the roll of the second half and the pairwise grouping are read off the row numbers
four grids left to right joined by grey block arrows labelled 'Step 1 Split', 'Step 2 Shift', 'Step 3 Group' with a one-line description under each grid
two same-size attention masks side by side at the right, 'w/o shift' with red block outlines and 'w shift' with blue outlines offset by half a block plus a wrapped corner block
dashed connectors run from 'Pattern1' and 'Pattern2' under the grouped grid to the mask each produces

channels.colour: blue shading = token position (pale for token 1 to dark for token 7, token 8 dark grey); red outline = pattern 1 (no shift), blue outline = pattern 2 (shifted); orange cells = attended query-key pairs on cream. Blue carries two meanings (token position and pattern 2)
channels.shape: cell grids = token-by-head tensors or query-key masks; grey block arrows = operations
channels.line: thick black outlines = a token group; brackets = half heads / group size; thin dashed elbows = which pattern makes which mask; a dashed arrow = the shift by half a group
channels.frame: one dashed rounded frame = the S²-Attn module

quality.strengths: the operation is drawn on a small numbered instance, so a reader sees the roll (token 8 wrapping to the top) without the text; each step is the same grid shape so the change between steps is the only change; the two masks are compared as identical panels side by side with the shifted one last, its extra corner block showing the cross-group link
quality.weaknesses: the masks are reached from step 3 by long dashed elbow wires under the strip instead of sitting where the grouped halves end; blue shading for token position collides with the blue pattern-2 outline; the masks show their groups with outlines whose relation to the four row-groups of step 3 the reader must count out

figures.lesson: Draw a tensor manipulation on a small numbered instance (8 tokens x 4 heads), one grid per step joined by labelled block arrows, so split, shift and group are read off the numbers before any text.

figures.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models

taxonomy.task: parameter-efficient fine-tuning of LLMs

arrangement.units: no enclosures: two side-by-side columns (a frozen-weight square and a stacked pair of trapezoids) between an input bar at the bottom and an output bar at the top
arrangement.inputs_as: a yellow bar labelled x with a brace marking its width d
arrangement.shared: the input x feeds both columns through two hollow block arrows, and their outputs meet at one plus glyph below h

insights.structure: A frozen weight square and a trainable trapezoid pair stand side by side as two parallel paths between one input bar and one output bar.
insights.data: Input and output are flat yellow bars labelled x and h, with their dimension given by a brace (d) rather than a tensor drawing.
insights.emphasis: Saturated orange trapezoids that pinch to a labelled width r set the trainable low-rank path apart from the single blue pretrained block.
insights.flow: Read bottom to top: from x up through both columns along hollow block arrows into the plus and out to h.
insights.avoid: Nothing in the figure marks W as frozen and A, B as trained; that distinction lives only in the caption.

core.what: two side-by-side paths from input x, a large blue 'Pretrained Weights' square and an orange bottleneck of two trapezoids A and B, summed at a + into h

relations.form: hollow arrows from the yellow x bar into both the blue square and trapezoid A, and from both the square and trapezoid B into one + above, then into the yellow h bar
bottom to top on the right: A narrows from width d to width r, B widens back, the bottleneck drawn as two facing trapezoids
brackets mark d under x and r at the bottleneck, so the low rank is visible as the narrow waist between A and B

channels.colour: blue = frozen pretrained weights, orange = the added low-rank factors, yellow = activations x and h; one meaning each, unkeyed but obvious
channels.shape: square = full d x d matrix, trapezoid = a rank-changing projection, flat bar = activation vector
channels.line: hollow outline arrows only
channels.frame: none

quality.strengths: The method is geometry: shape width encodes dimension (d-wide square, trapezoids pinching to r), the new part is the saturated orange pair beside the frozen blue block, and input and output are drawn as bars at the bottom and top with only short straight arrows.
quality.weaknesses: Blocks carry formulas (W in R^{d x d}, A = N(0, sigma^2), B = 0) for initialisation rather than names; the colour roles (frozen vs trained) are not keyed and rely on the caption.

figures.lesson: Draw a low-rank factorisation as two trapezoids that pinch to a narrow waist labelled r, beside one large square for the full matrix, so the size contrast says 'small trainable add-on' without text.

figures.title: LRM: Large Reconstruction Model for Single Image to 3D

taxonomy.task: single-image to 3D reconstruction

arrangement.units: three dashed rounded boxes (encoder, triplane decoder, NeRF) arranged as stacked rows in a Z path
arrangement.inputs_as: real photo of the object with size annotation
arrangement.shared: camera features feed the M modulation diamonds across the decoder

insights.structure: Three dashed containers in a Z-shaped path: Image encoder (top row), Image-to-Triplane Decoder (middle row), Neural Radiance Field (bottom row), each annotated with layer counts and dimensions.
insights.data: Input and output are real renders of a toy giraffe, tokens are tall coloured column stacks (green image features, white positional embeddings, blue triplane tokens), the triplane is three intersecting blue planes and the NeRF is a wireframe cube around the 3-D model.
insights.emphasis: Every tensor carries an explicit 'Dim:' annotation and camera modulation is an orange M diamond explained in a top-right legend, so precise shapes rather than colour emphasize the design.
insights.flow: Top row left-to-right, a curved line drops image features into the decoder's Cross block, middle row runs right to DeConv and Reshape, then down to the triplane and the bottom row runs right-to-left to the rendered image.
insights.avoid: Dense dimension text in small font under nearly every element clutters the figure; the reversed right-to-left bottom row can surprise the reader.

core.what: a three-row Z path: image through the ViT encoder to image features (top), learnable embeddings through the image-to-triplane decoder to triplane tokens and DeConv (middle), triplane through an MLP into a NeRF and volumetric rendering (bottom, right to left)

relations.form: top row left to right, middle row left to right, a Reshape arrow down the right edge, bottom row right to left to the rendered novel image at bottom left
the image encoder and image-to-triplane decoder are dashed rounded boxes opened to show one layer (Self, MLP with residual ⊕; Cross, Self, MLP with residual ⊕) captioned with layer counts

a long curved wire brings the image features from the top-right column into the decoder's Cross block, and three curved wires fan from an orange camera-features cube to orange 'M' modulation diamonds before each sub-block
the triplane is drawn as three intersecting blue planes with a 3-D point and its orange projection lines onto them, yielding a 3-cell point-feature column

channels.colour: green = image-side tokens and Conv; blue = triplane tokens, Cross and DeConv; yellow = self-attention blocks and also point features (two meanings); orange diamond = camera modulation (keyed); grey = MLPs
channels.shape: column of cells = token sequence or feature; rounded box = layer; diamond = modulation; ⊕ circle = residual (keyed)
channels.line: solid arrows = data; dashed line from MLP to the NeRF box = the field's query; thin curved wires = cross-attention and camera inputs
channels.frame: dashed rounded rectangle = a module (encoder, decoder, NeRF)

quality.strengths: Representations are drawn between every module with their dimensions (image features, triplane tokens, point features), real input and rendered images bracket the path, and the triplane lookup is shown on a drawn triplane rather than described.
quality.weaknesses: The image-features wire sweeps from the top right back across to the decoder's left; the bottom row reverses direction; yellow means both self-attention and point features; dimension annotations under almost every element add dense small text.

figures.lesson: Fold a long encoder-decoder-renderer into three rows that read as a Z, put the drawn 3-D representation (intersecting feature planes) at the bottom-right turn, and write a 'Dim:' line under every data item so tensor sizes can be followed.

figures.title: M3D-NCA: Robust 3D Segmentation with Built-in Quality Control

taxonomy.task: 3-D medical image segmentation with neural cellular automata applied repeatedly across image scales

arrangement.units: a full-width light-grey panel for the training pipeline (with a lavender tinted inner region for one level) above two light-grey panels side by side for the NCA architecture and batch duplication; each titled in large bold text
arrangement.inputs_as: a 3-D MRI volume cube labelled 'Input Image', and below it a cube with a highlighted random patch
arrangement.losses_at: a yellow 3-D 'Dice FocalLoss' block at the bottom of the lavender region, fed by the ground-truth patch from its left and by an orange arrow from the NCA output above, with an italic note 'After n levels calculate loss on final patch'
arrangement.shared: the NCA is drawn twice as a purple cube with a circular arrow ('NCA m_x' in the pipeline, 'M3D NCA' in batch duplication); the downscale and upscale prisms share one grey style

insights.structure: A full-width training-pipeline panel on top and two smaller detail panels below it, each panel framed in light grey with a large bold title and a lavender tint marking what repeats.
insights.data: Images are 3-D cubes showing MRI slices: the input volume, a selected patch with a purple predicted-mask overlay, the downscaled intermediates and the ground-truth patch; batch duplication shows three copies of one input cube.
insights.emphasis: The NCA cube is the only saturated purple element in the pipeline and is circled by the largest arrow, at the centre of the lavender region.
insights.flow: The main row runs left to right in short straight arrows; the per-level repetition returns as a long dark arrow from Concatenate under the row to the patch, and orange arrows run up from the patch into Downscale and down from the NCA output into the loss.
insights.avoid: Every routine operation (downscale, upscale, concatenate) is a heavily shaded 3-D block as prominent as the NCA, and orange is used for two unrelated arrows without a key.

core.what: two nested repetitions drawn at two sizes: a circular arrow hugging the NCA cube ('Apply Model m_x -> s times') inside the lavender per-level region, and a long return arrow ('For each level n-1') from Concatenate under the whole row back to the patch selection

relations.form: the NCA's s steps as one circular arrow wrapped round the purple cube, not unrolled
the level loop as a long dark arrow leaving Concatenate, running left under the row and down into 'Select Random Patch', which re-enters Downscale by an orange arrow
input cube -> Downscale prism -> downscaled cube -> NCA cube -> output cube -> Upscale prism -> Concatenate block, one horizontal row of short arrows

the NCA Architecture panel below opens the NCA cube (Conv3d and Identity branches -> Dense-h -> Batch Norm -> ReLU -> Dense-c -> '+' Update Cell), tied to it only by the shared purple, not by a callout
Batch Duplication: one input batch fans out into three identical copies stacked in a lavender column (⊙ between them) that converge on one M3D NCA cube

channels.colour: purple = the NCA (cubes, architecture layers, predicted mask overlay) and, as a pale lavender tint, the region that repeats per level - one hue family for module and scope; yellow = loss; light grey/white = fixed scaling and concatenation ops; orange arrows = two different paths (patch into the next level, output into the loss), unkeyed
channels.shape: 3-D cubes = image volumes and the NCA, prisms = scale changes, tall block = concatenate, flat 3-D slabs = layers, '+' and ⊙ glyphs = operations
channels.line: dark grey arrows = data flow, circular arrows = repetition, thick orange arrows = patch-to-level and output-to-loss
channels.frame: light-grey rounded panel = one sub-figure with one job; lavender inner region = what repeats per level or what is inside the NCA

quality.strengths: the method's two repetitions are distinguished by geometry (a tight circular arrow round the NCA vs a long return arrow round the row); data is drawn as data - MRI volume cubes, the selected patch, the predicted mask in purple, the ground-truth patch; each panel has one job (pipeline, cell update, batch duplication) and the pipeline panel takes most of the area
quality.weaknesses: all operations are shaded 3-D extruded blocks, so the routine Downscale/Upscale/Concatenate weigh as much as the NCA; orange carries two unrelated paths without a key; the level-loop arrow detours around the entire row; what Concatenate joins (the input arrow along the top edge with the upscaled output) is not explained by the drawing; purple means both 'NCA' and 'repeated region'

figures.lesson: Draw a model applied s times as a cube with a circular arrow wrapped round it, and the outer per-level repetition as a long return arrow around the whole row, so the two nested repetitions differ by size.

figures.title: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners

taxonomy.task: self-supervised image pretraining

arrangement.units: unboxed chain of image grids, token columns and two rounded grey module boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: real photo with a patch-mask grid
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Five-step horizontal chain: masked input grid, column of visible patches, a large grey encoder, a long token column, a smaller grey decoder, a red token column, and the target image grid.

insights.flow: Strictly left-to-right with grey arrows; vertical token columns interleave teal and grey cells to show mask tokens being inserted.

core.what: one left-to-right row: masked image grid, the few visible patches, a tall encoder, short cyan token column, a long column of cyan and grey mask tokens, a small decoder, red output tokens, the reconstructed target

masking drawn on the real image: a 5 x 5 patch grid with most patches filled flat grey and only a few photo patches showing
the encoded cyan tokens are re-inserted among grey mask tokens in one long column before the decoder

channels.colour: grey = masked patch / mask token, cyan = encoded visible token, red = decoder output token; one meaning each
channels.shape: photo squares = patches; flat rectangles = tokens; grey rounded box = network
channels.line: short grey arrows on one axis
channels.frame: none

figures.title: Magic3D: High-Resolution Text-to-3D Content Creation

taxonomy.task: text-to-3D mesh generation
taxonomy.note: training-free here means the diffusion priors are frozen and only the 3D representation is optimised per prompt via score distillation

arrangement.units: two tinted rounded panels (pink stage 1, green stage 2) each holding render -> noise -> diffusion prior -> L_SDS; the 3D representation for each stage sits just outside the panel's left edge, the final model at the far right outside both
arrangement.inputs_as: a quoted text prompt in a yellow-glowing rounded box spanning both panels; the initial 3D representation is a rendered voxel-grid rabbit at the left
arrangement.losses_at: inside each stage panel at its right end (L_SDS over a residual image), with a coloured curved 'update' arrow running back under the panel to the 3D model
arrangement.shared: the single text prompt box feeds both stages by two yellow arrows

insights.structure: Two tinted rounded stage panels sit left and right with large numerals '1.' and '2.', each 3D representation placed in the gap before its panel, and a bottom label row with a thick green arrow naming the representation change.
insights.data: Every 3D state is a real render of the same rabbit (octree-voxel NeRF, coloured mesh, final textured model), the prompt is quoted verbatim, and noise is a small colour-noise square above each prior.
insights.emphasis: The prompt box glows yellow and feeds both priors via thick yellow arrows, while bold 'image' vs 'latent' under the two priors marks the one change between stages.
