in each stage a long curved 'update' arrow, coloured with the panel's tint, returns from L_SDS beneath the panel to the 3-D representation on its left
one yellow-glowing prompt box 'a stuffed grey rabbit holding a pretend carrot' spans the top, with yellow arrows bending down into both diffusion priors
inside each panel left to right: orange render arrow from the camera to a rendered image, ⊕ with noise, the prior network, ⊖, the SDS gradient image

channels.colour: panel tint and update-arrow colour = stage (red low-res, green high-res); yellow = text conditioning; orange = rendering; the rainbow gradient on the prior networks and purple encoder carries no meaning
channels.shape: stacked slabs = network layers; wire-frame pyramid = camera; ⊕ / ⊖ circles = noise add and subtract
channels.line: grey thin arrows = noise and data paths; thick curved coloured arrows = parameter updates; big gradient arrow at the bottom = mesh extraction
channels.frame: tinted rounded panel = one optimization stage

quality.strengths: The coarse-to-fine cascade is drawn as two panels with identical internal structure differing in prior type and resolution, the 3-D representation of each stage is drawn as a real render, and the single shared prompt above both shows one condition across stages.
quality.weaknesses: The update arrows are long curves under the panels back to the representation; the networks' rainbow fill is decorative; the bottom timeline restates the stage order in a separate band of text and arrows.

figures.lesson: Show a coarse-to-fine method as two tinted panels with identical internal wiring (render -> add noise -> prior -> L_SDS -> curved update arrow back to the 3D model), so the only visible differences between the stages are the ones that matter.

figures.title: Make-A-Video: Text-to-Video Generation without Text-Video Data

taxonomy.task: text-to-video generation

arrangement.units: four perspective film-strip boxes of increasing size, each bordered in its stage colour
arrangement.inputs_as: quoted text prompt on a card plus fps token
arrangement.shared: the prior embedding line feeds every stage

insights.structure: A cascade of perspective film-strip boxes receding diagonally: Spatiotemporal Decoder D^t (smallest, back), Frame Interpolation F, Spatiotemporal Super-Resolution SR_l^t and Spatial Super-Resolution SR_h (largest, front), with the text prompt and red prior P at left.
insights.data: Video is drawn as strips of real yoga-at-sunset frames growing in size and resolution, noise as grainy frames, the prompt as quoted text on a white card, the prior as a red 3-D bar.
insights.emphasis: Each stage has its own colour (blue, green, purple, black) for its title, box border and inter-frame arrows, and growing strip size encodes increasing resolution.
insights.flow: Text enters the prior at left, coloured feed lines rise into each stage, and arrows run diagonally front-down from each strip into the next larger one until the Generated Video y-hat.
insights.avoid: The overlapping perspective boxes and many small coloured arrows make it hard to see which frames interpolate or upsample which; ellipsis dots crowd the strips.

core.what: the cascade drawn as four perspective frame strips stepping diagonally from small at top left to large at bottom right (Spatiotemporal Decoder D^t, Frame Interpolation F, Spatiotemporal Super-Resolution SR_l^t, Spatial Super-Resolution SR_h), each outlined in its network's colour

relations.form: four overlapping 3-D strips of video frames, each larger and with more frames than the last, the final one ending at 'Generated Video y-hat'
short coloured arrows run from each frame of one strip to frames of the next, so upsampling and frame insertion are drawn on the actual frames
the input text x enters a red prior box P with an 'fps' tag; red and black wires run right under the strips and rise by vertical arrows into each stage

channels.colour: outline and arrow colour = network (blue D^t, green F, purple SR_l^t, black SR_h), echoed in the coloured labels and dots; red = the prior P and its output wire
channels.shape: perspective frame strip = a video at that stage's resolution; dots = latent/noise placeholders; 'Fixed Noise' panels at strip ends
channels.line: short coloured arrows between frames = stage mapping; long red/black elbows from P = conditioning
channels.frame: coloured strip outline = one stage

quality.strengths: Resolution and frame count grow visibly from strip to strip using real generated frames, and each network has one colour shared by its outline, arrows and label.
quality.weaknesses: The strips overlap in perspective so the earlier stages are partly hidden and the frame-to-frame arrows crowd; the conditioning wires from P bend under the strips and rise behind them; the decoder, interpolation and super-resolution networks themselves are not drawn, only their effect.

figures.lesson: Draw a cascade of video stages as receding film strips in perspective, each stage's strip, frame-to-frame arrows and name in its own colour, so temporal upsampling (more frames) and spatial upsampling (larger frames) show up as strip length and frame size.

figures.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces

taxonomy.task: linear-time sequence modeling (selective SSM)

arrangement.units: no enclosed regions; a top band of state lanes and a lower band of parameter columns, separated only by position and colour
arrangement.inputs_as: x_t as a cell column at lower left and h_{t-1} as stacked sheets at upper left
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: One unrolled recurrence step with no containers: four parallel orange state lanes span the top band from the stacked h_{t-1} sheets at far left through the A column (top centre) to h_t at far right, while x_t, B_t, Delta_t, C_t and y_t hang as green columns in a lower band.
insights.data: Vectors are tall pale-green columns (x_t and y_t as columns of square cells with only the top cell filled), each hidden state is a stack of offset orange sheets to show channels, and every element carries a large italic math symbol.
insights.emphasis: The selection mechanism is the only blue in the figure: a small 'Project' box plus three thick blue arrows into B_t, Delta_t and C_t, labelled once in bold blue 'Selection Mechanism' along the bundle.
insights.flow: State flows left to right along the straight orange lanes; the lower band feeds in by elbow-routed lines rising from B_t into the lanes before A and dropping from the lanes into C_t after A, with dashed fan lines from x_t into Project and a dashed 'Discretize' arrow from Delta_t.
insights.avoid: The GPU SRAM/HBM triangle in the bottom-right corner encodes memory levels only by colour reuse and is easily mistaken for part of the computation; the dense orange elbow crossings around A are hard to trace individually.

core.what: one recurrence step spanning the width: the stacked state h_{t-1} at left sends four orange channel lanes through the transition A to the state h_t at right, dashed ends continuing the recurrence

relations.form: four parallel orange lanes from h_{t-1} through A to h_t, with dashed stubs entering at left and leaving at right
the input x_t enters B_t, whose four orange lines elbow up into the lanes before A; after A the lanes elbow down into C_t, which feeds y_t
green curved arrows x_t → B_t at left and C_t → y_t at right, under the lanes
a blue 'Project' box fed by x_t sends blue wires labelled 'Selection Mechanism' to B_t, Delta_t and C_t; Delta_t sends a dashed 'Discretize' arrow to A and B_t

channels.colour: orange vs green = memory level (GPU SRAM vs GPU HBM), keyed by a two-tier pyramid at bottom right: the expanded state lives in orange, inputs, outputs and parameters in green; blue = the input-dependent selection mechanism
channels.shape: column of cells = a vector or parameter; stacked sheets = the expanded state; triangle pyramid = memory-hierarchy key
channels.line: solid orange = state channels, green = input/output paths, blue = selection, dashed black = discretization
channels.frame: none

quality.strengths: Colour carries one unusual but keyed meaning (where a tensor is stored), which makes the hardware-aware point visible; the recurrence is a straight spine across the figure and every parameter (A, B_t, C_t, Delta_t) is drawn as a vector at the point it acts.
quality.weaknesses: The B_t and C_t couplings are fans of four rounded elbow lines each, dense around A; the blue selection wires run long horizontal paths to C_t; the Project box, the paper's new mechanism, is the smallest element.

figures.lesson: Reserve one hue for the contribution and use it nowhere else: here a single blue box plus its blue arrow bundle, labelled once along the bundle, sits under an orange/green recurrence, so the eye finds the new mechanism without any container.

figures.title: Autoregressive Image Generation without Vector Quantization

taxonomy.task: image generation by autoregression over continuous tokens in random order with several tokens predicted per step (masked autoregression)
taxonomy.note: architecture 'other': this figure draws only the generation order over tokens, no network.

arrangement.units: three unframed rows, one per generation order, each a 4x4 grid at left and a titled 1-D token sequence at right; a colour key strip at the bottom
arrangement.inputs_as: a 4x4 grid of coloured token cells standing for the image

insights.structure: Three identical rows, ours last, each pairing a 2-D token grid with its 1-D sequence, so the variants differ only in cell colours and arc endings.
insights.data: Tokens are drawn as square cells coloured by state (known, predicted at this step, unknown), both in the image grid and in the flattened sequence.
insights.emphasis: The masked variant stands out only by position (last row) and by the run of several orange cells where the other rows have one.
insights.flow: Rows read top to bottom from the standard to the generalised order; within a row, grey arcs fan from known tokens to the predicted token or, in (c), to a bracket over the predicted set.
insights.avoid: In (b) the sequence is drawn exactly like (a)'s, so the random permutation shows only in the grid; nothing ties a grid cell to its place in the sequence.

core.what: raster AR, random-order AR and masked AR as three identical rows stacked top to bottom, ours last, differing only in which grid and sequence cells are orange

relations.form: three rows with the same 4x4 grid and the same 16-cell sequence, titled (a), (b), (c), the masked variant last
each order is drawn on a small token grid: lavender known cells, one or several orange cells to predict, grey unknown cells
thin grey arcs from every known token converge on the predicted token, or in (c) on a bracket spanning the predicted run

channels.colour: lavender = known/predicted, orange = to predict at this step, grey = unknown (keyed at the bottom); one meaning in both grid and sequence
channels.shape: square cells = tokens; grey arcs = conditioning on earlier tokens; a bracket = a predicted set
channels.frame: none; rows are separated by whitespace

quality.strengths: The comparison is pure geometry: identical rows, ours last, where only cell colours change; one keyed colour code serves grid and sequence alike; the token grid and its sequence are both drawn, so the reader sees which image positions each step predicts.
quality.weaknesses: Rows (a) and (b) have identical sequences, so the random permutation is visible only in the grids; no line or index links a grid cell to its sequence position; the model's own row is not enlarged or marked beyond being last.

figures.lesson: Compare generation orders as identical rows that differ only in which cells are coloured, with the 2-D grid beside its flattened sequence so the reader sees both the spatial pattern and the step.

figures.title: Repurposing Diffusion-Based Image Generators for Monocular Depth Estimation

taxonomy.task: monocular depth estimation by fine-tuning a pretrained latent diffusion model

arrangement.units: one unframed diagram of three converging input rows; the objective alone sits in a pale-yellow rounded box
arrangement.inputs_as: a real RGB image slab and a colour-mapped depth slab, plus a grey 't ~ U(T)' tag on the bottom row
arrangement.losses_at: bottom right: below the U-Net output epsilon-hat and at the end of the sampled-noise line running along the bottom
arrangement.shared: the frozen latent encoder is drawn twice, once per input row, both pink with padlocks

insights.structure: Three stacked input rows (image, depth, timestep) run left to right; the depth latent is noised and joins the image latent at a concat node, the U-Net predicts epsilon-hat, and the objective box at bottom right takes epsilon-hat from above and epsilon from the bottom row.
insights.data: Image and depth are real slabs, every latent and noise tensor is a textured cube (z^(x), z^(d), z_t^(d), epsilon, epsilon-hat), and the objective repeats the epsilon and epsilon-hat thumbnails inside its norm.
insights.emphasis: Padlocks and pink fill mark the frozen encoders, leaving the blue U-Net as the trained part; the pale-yellow objective is the largest coloured box.
insights.flow: Thin black orthogonal arrows, mostly straight left to right; t enters Add Noise and the U-Net as short vertical side tags; epsilon runs along the bottom to the objective with one branch up into Add Noise.
insights.avoid: Blue fills both the trained U-Net and the parameter-free Add Noise / Sample Noise steps, so colour does not separate learned from fixed operations; the concat node - the method's conditioning - is the smallest element.

core.what: the image latent z^(x) from the top row and the noised depth latent z_t^(d) from the middle row converge on one white 'concat' circle that feeds the U-Net

relations.form: each input row runs left to right: input slab -> padlocked pink encoder -> textured latent cube; the depth row continues through Add Noise to z_t^(d)
the frozen latent encoder appears twice as identical pink padlocked trapezoids stacked in one column, one per input row
epsilon from the bottom row and epsilon-hat from the U-Net meet in the objective box, drawn as two noise thumbnails inside ||. - .||^2
the timestep t enters Add Noise and the U-Net as grey tags on short vertical arrows from above and below

channels.colour: pink = frozen VAE encoder; light blue = operations, both the trained U-Net and the fixed Add Noise / Sample Noise (blue carries two meanings; the padlock separates frozen from trained only on the encoders); pale yellow = training objective; grey = scalar inputs (t); mosaic textures = latents and noise
channels.shape: trapezoid = encoder, bow-tie = U-Net, rounded square = operation, circle = concat, cube = latent or noise tensor, slab = input image / depth, padlock icon = frozen
channels.line: one style: thin black arrows; t enters through short vertical arrows
channels.frame: only the objective has a container (pale-yellow rounded box)

quality.strengths: Every representation is drawn as a textured cube between its maker and its consumer, and the loss shows epsilon and epsilon-hat themselves rather than a formula in a box; frozen vs trained is marked by padlock icons on the encoders; image conditioning by concatenation is visible as two rows converging on one node; arrows are short and orthogonal.
quality.weaknesses: Blue fill is shared by the trained U-Net and the fixed noise operations; the concat node (the method's conditioning) is the smallest element while the generic objective box is the largest; t is drawn twice as separate tags; no line style separates the training-only path.

figures.lesson: Draw the loss as its own terms - the sampled noise thumbnail and the predicted one inside the norm - fed by straight lines from where each is made, so the objective visibly compares two drawn representations.

figures.title: Mask R-CNN

taxonomy.task: instance segmentation
taxonomy.note: family other: two-stage CNN instance segmentation (Faster R-CNN plus a parallel mask head); the taxonomy has no CNN-detector family.

arrangement.units: No enclosed units: one left-to-right row of photo, feature slab, two RoI cubes and output photo, with a spur above the first cube.
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo in perspective with one lavender RoI box drawn on it; the output is the same photo faded, overlaid with coloured instance masks
arrangement.shared: the first RoI cube feeds both the class/box spur (up) and the conv mask path (right)

insights.structure: One row in shared perspective: input photo, a large feature slab, two gridded RoI cubes linked by 'conv' arrows, and the output photo, with the class/box head lifted onto a short spur above the first cube.
insights.data: Inputs and outputs are real photos as tilted planes, the output overlaid with coloured instance masks; RoIs are lavender rectangles on the slab and RoI features are cubes with a gridded front face.
insights.emphasis: The RoIAlign step is the only coloured stroke (lavender RoI outlines and the RoIAlign arrow), and the mask branch is the main line ending at the masked photo.
insights.flow: Left to right along thin black arrows; one arrow branches up and right from the first cube to the 'class / box' bar, the rest runs straight to the output.
insights.avoid: The large feature slab and the RoI source (backbone, region proposals) carry no label, so a reader cannot tell what the slab is from the figure alone.

core.what: one left-to-right row: input photo with a box, a large perspective feature-map slab, RoIAlign from one region of it to a small gridded volume, two conv volumes, and the output photo with coloured instance masks

relations.form: photo, feature-map slab, RoIAlign arrow, gridded RoI feature, 'conv', second gridded volume, 'conv', output photo, joined by short straight arrows
region boxes are drawn on the feature map itself, the selected one overlaid with a sampling grid from which the lavender RoIAlign arrow leaves; the same box appears on the input photo
from the first RoI feature a short elbow rises to a thin flat slab labelled 'class box', while the main row continues through the convs to the masks

channels.colour: lavender = regions of interest (boxes on the image and map, the RoIAlign arrow); the output's yellow, purple, blue and orange fills = individual predicted instances
channels.shape: perspective slab = feature map; gridded cube = fixed-size RoI feature; thin flat slab = the class/box head
channels.line: short black arrows = data flow; lavender arrow = the RoIAlign mapping
channels.frame: none

quality.strengths: Input and output are real photos so the task is legible at once, RoIAlign is drawn as a grid on the region it samples, and the mask branch continues the main axis while the class/box branch is a short side elbow.
quality.weaknesses: The backbone is an unlabeled blank slab; nothing marks the mask head, the paper's addition, as new (same black outline as the rest); the class/box head is a tiny flat box with no output drawn.

figures.lesson: Make the added branch the figure's main line and push the inherited heads onto a short side spur, so the new output reads as the destination.

figures.title: Masked-attention Mask Transformer for Universal Image Segmentation

taxonomy.task: universal image segmentation

arrangement.units: two side-by-side regions split by a dashed rule: an unframed overview with coloured containers (blue decoder box, green trapezoid) and a framed grey detail panel of one layer
arrangement.inputs_as: query squares at left of the decoder; image features, mask and query features as small glyphs at the bottom of the detail panel
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; class and mask output boxes at right of the decoder
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Overview on the left and, across a dashed vertical rule, a tall grey detail panel of one decoder layer on the right; in the overview an orange Backbone trapezoid sits bottom-left, a green Pixel Decoder trapezoid widens diagonally up-right, and a light-blue 'Transformer Decoder L x' container with three grey blocks sits above it.
insights.data: Image features are lilac planes that grow in size along the pixel-decoder trapezoid; queries are a vertical rounded bar of four coloured squares that reappears as the output row at the top of the detail panel; class and mask outputs are small cream boxes.
insights.emphasis: In the detail panel the 'masked attention' box is the only saturated (deep pink) block with 'masked' in bold, and a cream 'mask' input enters it from outside the container in the same cream as the overview's mask output.
insights.flow: Overview reads backbone to pixel decoder left to right, then slanted arrows rise from successive feature maps into successive decoder blocks, and the decoder output meets the largest feature map at a circled-times to give the mask; the detail panel reads bottom to top with residual arrows looping up its right side.
insights.avoid: The long slanted arrows from feature maps to decoder blocks cross the gap at different angles and are hard to pair at a glance; the overview never shows where the detail panel's layer sits beyond the shared colours.

core.what: the meta-architecture on the left (backbone, pixel-decoder pyramid, Transformer decoder) and, past a dashed vertical rule, one decoder layer opened on the right with its bold red 'masked attention' block at the bottom

relations.form: a grey rounded panel at right shows one layer as a bottom-to-top stack (masked attention, add & norm, self-attention, add & norm, FFN, add & norm) separated from the overview by a dashed line
the pixel decoder's three increasingly large lavender feature maps each send one diagonal arrow up into one of the three successive grey layer boxes inside the blue Transformer Decoder

orange backbone trapezoid, a bar, the green pixel-decoder wedge, left to right; and coloured query squares entering the decoder at left, passing three layer boxes ('Lx') to class and mask outputs at right
the decoder output meets an arrow up from the largest feature map at a ⊗ node that produces 'mask'

channels.colour: fill = component: orange backbone, green pixel decoder, blue Transformer decoder, lavender image features, pale yellow mask/class, red masked attention (the novelty), pink self-attention, teal FFN; the four coloured squares = individual queries
channels.shape: trapezoid/wedge = CNN backbone and decoder; rounded box = layer; column of coloured squares = query set
channels.line: solid arrows = data; residual connections drawn as right-side elbows in the detail
channels.frame: blue rounded box = the Transformer decoder; grey rounded panel = one decoder layer; dashed rule = overview vs detail

quality.strengths: The novelty is the most saturated block (red, bold 'masked'), the multi-scale feeding is shown by geometry (pyramid levels growing left to right under successive layers), and queries, image features and mask are drawn as data entering the detailed layer.
quality.weaknesses: The detail panel is not tied to the overview by matching tint or a callout (blue decoder vs grey panel); the three diagonal arrows from the pyramid cut up through the decoder's edge at different angles; residual wires bend around the right side of the stack.

figures.lesson: Draw the multi-scale pixel decoder as a widening trapezoid of feature maps whose sizes grow along it, with one arrow from each map to a successive decoder block, so 'one resolution per layer' is read from geometry alone.

figures.title: Per-Pixel Classification is Not All You Need for Semantic Segmentation

taxonomy.task: semantic segmentation as mask classification

arrangement.units: two formulations side by side split by a thin vertical rule; the right one holds N identical rounded-outline prediction boxes under a bracket
arrangement.inputs_as: the same real photo drawn as a tilted plane under each formulation
arrangement.losses_at: as coloured block arrows from ground-truth planes above each prediction; the per-pixel loss as a label at top-left
arrangement.shared: the same input photo is drawn once per formulation

insights.structure: A narrow left column (per-pixel formulation) and a wide right part (per-mask formulation) separated by a thin grey vertical rule; the right part repeats one rounded box N times ('prediction 1', 'prediction 2', ..., 'prediction N') gathered by a long grey bracket.
insights.data: Everything is drawn as tilted parallelogram planes: the input photo at the bottom, a colour semantic map and a K-channel stack on the left, grey binary ground-truth masks above and predicted soft masks inside each box on the right, each with a small column of coloured class cells braced 'K + 1'.
insights.emphasis: The proposed side takes about three quarters of the width and its two losses are the only saturated colours (orange mask-loss arrows, purple classification arrows labelled with the class name in that class's colour or the empty-set symbol).
insights.flow: Bottom to top: hollow white block arrows carry the input photo up into each formulation, and coloured block arrows come down from the ground truth onto the predictions.
insights.avoid: The left formulation's planes are stacked so tightly that the K-channel volume and its K brace are hard to read at small size.

core.what: per-pixel classification (left, narrow) against mask classification (right, wide), split by a vertical rule, each drawn on the same photo with its own loss

relations.form: left panel: photo, hollow arrow up to a stack of K per-pixel class planes, black arrow from a ground-truth map above; right panel: the same photo below a row of N prediction cards, prior first and ours second
each prediction card holds a binary mask drawn as a tilted image plane plus a (K+1)-cell class vector, with N cards side by side joined by an ellipsis and one bracket
above prediction 1 and 2, ground-truth masks send an orange arrow into the predicted mask and a class name ('building', 'sky', 'Ø') sends a purple arrow into the class vector

channels.colour: arrow colour = loss type, keyed bottom right (orange per-pixel binary mask loss, purple per-mask classification loss; black = per-pixel classification loss on the left); class colours (brown building, cyan sky, green) match across label text, class-vector cells and the left segmentation
channels.shape: tilted plane = a map or mask; cell column = class vector; hollow arrow = image into the model
channels.line: short thick vertical arrows = losses; hollow arrows = input
channels.frame: rounded card = one mask prediction; vertical rule = the two formulations

quality.strengths: Both formulations are drawn on the same image with their supervision shown as short vertical loss arrows, the per-mask pairing of ground truth to prediction is visible card by card, and class colour is kept consistent across text, vectors and maps.
quality.weaknesses: The two panels use different layouts (vertical stack vs horizontal row), so the comparison is not panel-for-panel; the network itself is reduced to a hollow arrow; the bracket under the N cards and the K / K+1 braces are small and easy to miss.

figures.lesson: Contrast two segmentation formulations by drawing the outputs themselves as tilted mask planes: one K-channel volume for per-pixel classification against a row of N binary-mask planes each with its own (K+1) class column, with the two losses as two arrow colours.

figures.title: MAXIM: Multi-Axis MLP for Image Processing

taxonomy.task: multi-axis gated MLP block for image restoration
taxonomy.note: paradigm: gMLP / MLP-Mixer-style token mixing

arrangement.units: two horizontal tinted bands, one per branch, each running from its split grid to its merged grid; a separate framed detail panel at the right
arrangement.inputs_as: a bare arrow into the LayerNorm stem; data as cell grids inside each band
arrangement.shared: stem and tail layers drawn once outside the bands

insights.structure: A main block with two stacked rounded tinted bands (pale pink 'Local Branch', pale green 'Global Branch', titles in bold red/green to their left) between a shared LayerNorm-Dense-GELU stem and a Concat-Dense-add tail, plus a separate pale-blue 'gMLP Block' detail panel at the far right behind a dashed rule.
insights.data: Tensors are drawn as literal 6 x 4 cell grids at each step (split, blocked/gridded, processed, unblocked), with processed cells outlined in different colours to show which tokens are mixed, and bracket shape annotations like [3 x 2, 2 x 2, C/2] whose changing numbers are coloured red or green.
insights.emphasis: The word 'gMLP' is bold blue at each application in both branches and matches the detail panel's blue title, while each branch's colour ties its title, its shape numbers and its axis label together.
insights.flow: Left to right through the stem, splitting into the two bands that run in parallel to a concat, then a dashed shortcut arrow from the stem rejoins at the final add; the detail panel reads bottom to top with a skip arrow up its left side.
insights.avoid: The multi-coloured cell outlines in the processed grids carry a lot of meaning but are too thin to decode at print size, and the gridded global result is hard to tell apart from the blocked local one.

core.what: two equally wide tinted lanes, pink Local Branch above and green Global Branch below, run the same four-step tensor sequence (split, block/grid, gMLP, unblock/ungrid) in parallel between one shared stem and one concat tail

relations.form: the pink and green bands are stacked with identical columns (1/2 Heads grid, blocked/gridded input, processed, 1/2 Heads grid), so the Block-vs-Grid difference reads by comparing the two rows column by column
left to right: LayerNorm-Dense-GELU stem, Split Heads into the two bands, Concat Heads, Dense, then an add node; a dashed shortcut rises at the left and re-enters at the add

each operation is drawn on a literal 6 x 4 token grid: blocking cuts it into 2 x 2 windows, gridding interleaves it, and the processed grids outline the mixed tokens in red/green/blue/magenta/orange to show which cells one gMLP mixes

a separate pale-blue 'gMLP Block' panel behind a dashed vertical rule at the far right opens the gMLP step bottom to top (LayerNorm, Dense, GELU, Split, LayerNorm, Spatial Proj, multiply, Dense, add), tied to the bands only by the blue 'gMLP' word

channels.colour: band tint and title colour = branch (pink/red local, green global), and the same red/green colours the changing numbers in shape annotations; box fill = layer type (grey norm, green Dense, purple GELU, pink Spatial Proj, yellow Split); outline colour on processed grids = token group mixed together - so red and green carry both branch identity and, in the processed grids, mixing groups
channels.shape: cell grids = tensors; rounded upright rectangles = layers; circles = add / multiply
channels.line: solid arrows = data flow; dashed arrows = shortcut connections
channels.frame: tinted rounded band = one branch; pale-blue panel behind a dashed rule = the opened gMLP block

quality.strengths: the local/global contrast is geometry: two identical lanes whose only drawn difference is how the 6 x 4 grid is cut (contiguous 2 x 2 windows vs interleaved grid), with the mixed tokens outlined so the reader sees which cells meet; tensor shapes in brackets colour only the dimension that changes; the gMLP internals are taught once in a side panel instead of repeated
quality.weaknesses: red and green mean branch in the titles and shape numbers but token-group in the processed grid outlines, which also use blue, magenta and orange; the detail panel is linked to the bands only by the word 'gMLP', not by a callout or matching tint

figures.lesson: Draw the token layout as an actual small grid of cells at each reshaping step (split, blocked, processed, unblocked) and colour the shape numbers that change in the branch's own colour, so the reshaping reads from the drawing alone.

figures.title: MedCLIP: Contrastive Learning from Unpaired Medical Images and Text

taxonomy.task: medical image-text contrastive pretraining with decoupled unpaired data

arrangement.units: the unpaired sources in a top row; the paired data below in one frame with two dashed columns
arrangement.inputs_as: real X-rays and quoted report sentences with keywords highlighted
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; positive / negative captions under each column
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Two dashed boxes on top ('Medical image datasets' with three X-rays, 'Medical text datasets' with bulleted report lines) above one large solid frame 'Medical image-text datasets' that holds two dashed columns facing each other across a central dashed grey circle.
insights.data: Inputs are real chest X-ray thumbnails and quoted report sentences in boxes with medical keywords ('opacity', 'pneumonia', 'extrapleural mass') highlighted in yellow.

insights.flow: Inward: lines from the anchor image and its report (left) and from the negative image and its report (right) converge on the central circle that stands for the embedding space.
insights.avoid: The central grey circle is unlabelled, so the reader must infer that it is the shared embedding space; the figure motivates the problem but shows no encoder or loss.

core.what: an anchor image-report column (left) and a negative image-report column (right) face each other across one central dashed grey circle, their four connecting lines converging on it to show a semantically matching report counted as a negative

relations.form: inside the 'Medical image-text datasets' frame, two dashed columns sit left and right of the circle; black lines run from the anchor X-ray and its report box, red lines from the negative X-ray and its red-dashed report box, all ending at dots on the circle's rim

the two columns are drawn identically (X-ray above, report box below, caption at the foot) so the only differences are the colour of lines and caption: blue 'True positive' vs red 'False negative', with 'opacity' highlighted in both reports

a top row of two dashed boxes shows the unpaired sources separately, 'Medical image datasets' with three X-ray thumbnails and 'Medical text datasets' with bulleted report sentences, above the solid paired-data frame

channels.colour: black vs red lines and report border = true pair vs false-negative pair; blue vs red caption text = the same distinction; yellow highlight = shared medical keywords across reports
channels.shape: photo thumbnails = images; bordered text boxes = reports; grey dashed circle = the (unlabelled) embedding space
channels.line: solid lines with dot ends = which sample maps into the space; dashed borders = a group or column, solid border = the paired dataset
channels.frame: dashed box = one data source or one sample pair; the large solid frame = paired image-text data

quality.strengths: the problem is shown with real data: two actual X-rays and quoted reports, the shared word 'opacity' highlighted in both, so the reader sees why the 'negative' is not really negative; the two columns are mirror-placed around the meeting point
quality.weaknesses: the central grey circle is unlabelled, so the reader must infer it is the embedding space; no encoder, representation or loss is drawn, so it motivates the problem but does not show how MedCLIP fixes it; the top unpaired-data row is not connected to anything below

figures.lesson: Show a supervision problem on two real image-report pairs with the words they share highlighted, instead of describing it.

figures.title: Segment Anything in Medical Images

taxonomy.task: universal medical image segmentation (dataset coverage teaser)

arrangement.units: one tiled mosaic of image cells with an overlaid illustration; no enclosed method regions
arrangement.inputs_as: real scans with colour mask overlays
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: A 6-row grid of real medical image tiles (CT, MRI, ultrasound, fundus, X-ray, dermoscopy, endoscopy, pathology) behind a large translucent anatomical body illustration placed over the centre.
insights.data: Each tile is a real scan with its segmentation mask laid on as a translucent colour overlay (cyan, green, orange, purple).
insights.emphasis: Coverage is the message: the body silhouette over the tiles ties the many modalities and organs to one model, with no diagram or labels at all.
insights.flow: No reading order; the eye scans the grid roughly head (top rows: brain scans) to pelvis and gut (bottom rows).
insights.avoid: The translucent body covers and washes out the central tiles, and there are no labels naming modality or target, so the figure carries no method information.

core.what: a mosaic of real scans with translucent coloured segmentation masks, arranged roughly head to pelvis behind a translucent human body silhouette, showing one model's coverage of modalities and organs

relations.form: each tile is a real scan (CT, MRI, ultrasound, fundus, X-ray, dermoscopy, endoscopy, pathology) with its target drawn as a translucent cyan, green, orange, purple or yellow mask
the body illustration over the centre (brain, lungs, heart, kidneys, gut) loosely ties tile rows to body regions: brain scans in the top two rows, chest in the third, abdomen and pelvis lower

channels.colour: mask colour = segmented target, with no key and no consistent mapping across tiles; body organ colours are illustrative
channels.shape: square tiles = individual images; the silhouette = the body
channels.frame: none beyond the tile grid

quality.strengths: the breadth claim is carried by real data: dozens of actual scans across many modalities, each with its mask, so the reader sees scope without reading
quality.weaknesses: no method structure is drawn at all (no model, prompt or output relation); the translucent body washes out the central tiles; there are no labels naming modality or target, and the mask colours carry no keyed meaning; the head-to-pelvis order is only approximate

figures.lesson: For a 'one model for every task' teaser, tile real scans with their masks as translucent colour overlays, order the rows head to pelvis and lay a translucent anatomical body over the centre, so coverage is the whole message without any diagram.

figures.title: Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads

taxonomy.task: LLM inference acceleration with extra decoding heads

arrangement.units: three rounded tinted containers in a row (base model, added heads, predictions) plus a bottom row of grey boxes for input, candidates and output
arrangement.inputs_as: a grey box with a quoted question
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Three rounded tinted containers left to right: blue 'Original Model' (Embedding, Transformer Layers, LM Head stacked bottom-up), red 'Medusa Heads' (three stacked numbered heads) and purple 'Top-k Predictions' (one text row per head), with three grey boxes along the bottom for Input, Candidates and Single step prediction.
insights.data: Tokens are shown as quoted text: a real question in the Input box, comma-separated top-k tokens per head ('is, ', the'), and candidate continuations with green-check / red-cross marks.
insights.emphasis: The added heads sit in the only red container with a flame icon in its title, while snowflake / flame icons on the original model mark it as frozen or trained.
insights.flow: Input rises into the original model, 'Last Hidden' fans right into each Medusa head, each head (and the LM head) feeds its own row of top-k tokens, then a return arrow drops into Candidates and on to the final single-step prediction at bottom right.
insights.avoid: The decorative llama-logo mascot at top centre carries no information and takes prime space.

core.what: one 'Last Hidden' state from the original model's Transformer Layers fans right into three stacked Medusa Heads beside the LM Head, each head feeding its own row of top-k tokens in a column on the right

relations.form: a single line leaves Transformer Layers labelled 'Last Hidden' and branches with right-angled turns into Medusa Head 1, 2 and 3, while the same output also goes up into the LM Head

inside the blue 'Original Model' container the flow runs bottom to top (Input box, Embedding, Transformer Layers, LM Head); the bottom row then runs left to right from Input to Candidates to Single step prediction

four parallel head-to-row lanes: the LM Head and Medusa Heads 1-3 each send one horizontal arrow into its own row of the purple Top-k Predictions column ('It, I, As'; 'is, ', the'; 'difficult, is, ''; 'not, difficult, a'), every row level with its head
a line from the bottom of the Top-k column drops into the Candidates box, which lists combined continuations with green check / red cross marks before the Single step prediction 'It is difficult'

channels.colour: container tint = role (blue original model, red added Medusa heads, purple predictions, grey data boxes); snowflake / flame icons = frozen / trained
channels.shape: rounded white boxes = modules or token rows; grey rounded boxes with icons = data (input, candidates, output)
channels.line: solid arrows = data flow throughout
channels.frame: rounded tinted container = one component group

quality.strengths: the added part is the only red container and sits between the base model and its outputs; each head's prediction row is level with the head so the one-to-one mapping reads by position; data is drawn as real quoted tokens and candidate continuations with accept/reject marks
quality.weaknesses: the llama mascot logo takes the top-centre space and carries nothing; the shared 'Last Hidden' wire bends three times to reach the heads; how candidates are verified (the tree attention) is not drawn, only the selected result

figures.lesson: Mark frozen and trained parts with snowflake and flame icons in the container titles, and draw the added prediction heads as a stack of identical numbered boxes, each wired to its own row of top-k token text, so 'one head per future position' reads at a glance.

figures.title: Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads

taxonomy.task: tree attention for verifying candidate continuations

arrangement.units: an unframed token tree with tinted per-head containers on the left and an unframed attention grid on the right
arrangement.inputs_as: candidate tokens as labelled circles
arrangement.shared: the same token groups and tints appear in both the tree and the grid header

insights.structure: A token tree on the left (grey Root, a pink 'Head 1' container with 'It', 'I', an orange 'Head 2' container with two sub-groups of 'is, ', the') and an 8 x 8 attention grid on the right whose column header is the same tokens grouped in the same tinted boxes.
insights.data: Tokens are circles with the word inside; the mask is a grid of empty cells with purple check marks where a query may attend to a key.
insights.emphasis: Colour-matched groups: each head's tint (pink, yellow, green) is repeated in the key header above the grid, so the block structure of the check marks reads as the tree.
insights.flow: The tree branches downward from Root with elbow lines that run right into the grid rows, so each query token on the left lines up with its row; keys read across the top.
insights.avoid: The 'Tree Mask' title with a tree emoji sits at lower left in large bold type, far from the grid it names.

core.what: a token tree on the left (Root, Head 1's two tokens, Head 2's three tokens under each) is laid against an 8 x 8 attention grid whose query rows are the tree's nodes and whose tinted key header repeats the same token groups, so the check marks trace the tree's ancestor paths

relations.form: the mask is drawn as a literal 8 x 8 grid of empty cells with purple check marks where a query may attend a key, the checks forming the tree's root-to-leaf paths

elbow lines from each tree node run right so every query token sits level with its grid row, while the same tokens appear as the column header across the top in matching tinted boxes (pink 'It, I', yellow and green 'is, ', the')
the tree branches downward from the grey Root through the pink Head 1 container into the orange Head 2 container, which holds two sub-groups (yellow, green), one per Head 1 token

channels.colour: container tint = which head / which parent's branch a token belongs to (pink Head 1; orange Head 2 with yellow and green sub-groups), repeated on the key header; purple = an allowed attention entry
channels.shape: circles = tokens; grid cells = query-key pairs; check mark = allowed attention
channels.line: solid elbow arrows = tree edges and row alignment at once
channels.frame: rounded tinted box = one head's candidate set or one branch's sub-group

quality.strengths: the mask is explained by placing its two sources against it: tree nodes are the rows and the same tinted token groups are the columns, so the block pattern of checks reads as the tree's ancestry without a formula; tokens are real words
quality.weaknesses: the tree edges double as row-alignment wires, so long elbow lines from Head 1 tokens snake down past the Head 2 container; the orange Head 2 tint in the tree does not appear in the key header (only its yellow and green sub-groups do); the big 'Tree Mask' title with an emoji sits at the lower left far from the grid

figures.lesson: Align the candidate-token tree row for row with the attention-mask grid and colour the grid's key header with the same per-head tints as the tree, so each allowed cell can be traced back to a tree path.

figures.title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems

taxonomy.task: virtual context management for LLMs with tiered memory

arrangement.units: a top lane holding the context window as coloured segments in dashed prompt/completion frames under a brace, and a bottom lane holding two grey manager boxes between two storage cylinders
arrangement.inputs_as: no explicit input; the context segments are labelled bars
arrangement.shared: the Function Executor is the single hub connected to archival storage, working context and recall storage

insights.structure: Two horizontal rows: the LLM context window as a strip of four coloured segments under a brace on top, and the managers (Function Executor, Queue Manager) flanked by Archival and Recall storage cylinders on the bottom.
insights.data: Memory regions are solid colour bars sized roughly by role (System Instructions black, Working Context orange, FIFO Queue blue with a magenta head), external stores are database cylinders, and no actual tokens or text are shown.
insights.emphasis: Bold two-line captions under each region state its read/write rule, and colour-matched block arrows (orange, magenta, blue, green) tie each manager action to the exact memory it changes.
insights.flow: Arrows run mostly bottom-to-top from managers into the context strip, sideways between storages and managers, and a large U-shaped blue arrow returns from Recall Storage under the row back to the Function Executor.
insights.avoid: Black and blue double-headed arrows between the two managers and the long U-shaped return arrow carry no label, so the read path from recall storage has to be inferred from the captions.

core.what: the LLM's finite context window drawn as one strip of coloured segments under a brace on top, with two managers and two external storage cylinders in a row below that read and write into it through colour-matched block arrows

relations.form: a green Archival Storage cylinder at the bottom left exchanges two green block arrows with the Function Executor; a blue Recall Storage cylinder at the bottom right receives a blue arrow from the Queue Manager and returns a long blue U-shaped arrow under the row to the Function Executor

the context window is drawn as a strip of segments (black System Instructions, orange Working Context, a magenta head plus blue FIFO Queue) inside a dashed 'Prompt Tokens' frame, with a separate dashed 'Completion Tokens' frame holding the Output Buffer, each segment captioned with its read/write rule
a short arrow runs from the FIFO Queue right to the Output Buffer, the prompt-to-completion order of the window

short upward block arrows tie each manager to the exact segment it writes: orange from the Function Executor into Working Context, magenta and blue from the Queue Manager into the FIFO Queue head and body; a black double arrow joins the two managers

channels.colour: segment fill = memory region (black system, orange working context, magenta/blue queue, green archival, blue recall), and each block arrow takes the colour of the memory it touches - so blue means both the FIFO Queue and Recall Storage
channels.shape: flat bars = in-context memory; cylinders = external storage; grey rounded boxes = managers
channels.line: thick block arrows = read/write actions; thin arrow = token order to completion
channels.frame: dashed frames = prompt vs completion tokens; a brace = the whole finite context window

quality.strengths: the core idea - a bounded window paged against external stores - is geometry: the window is a single strip on top under a brace, the stores sit outside it below, and every write arrow lands on the exact segment it changes; each region is captioned with its read/write rule
quality.weaknesses: blue codes both the FIFO Queue and Recall Storage, so the queue-to-recall eviction and recall-to-executor retrieval are hard to tell apart; the recall-to-executor arrow is a long U-turn under the whole row; no actual tokens or messages are drawn, only labelled bars

figures.lesson: Draw a context window as a single strip of coloured segments under a brace, and let every arrow that writes into a segment take that segment's colour.

figures.title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework

taxonomy.task: multi-agent software development with shared message pool

arrangement.units: a rounded frame for the agent team around a shared pool on the left, and a larger blue rounded zoom panel for one agent on the right with nested white cards
arrangement.inputs_as: agent profile text and structured messages
arrangement.shared: the shared message pool, drawn once at the centre of the left panel

insights.structure: Left: a rounded frame with five role avatars (Architect, Project Manager, Engineer, Product Manager, QA Engineer) placed around a central purple 'Shared Message Pool'; right: a large blue zoom panel pulled out of the Engineer, holding an 'Agent Profile' card on top and an 'Iterative Programming' loop below.
insights.data: Agents are cartoon avatar portraits with tool icons, one message is expanded as key: value fields (content, cause_by, sent_from, send_to), and the engineer's work is shown as a real code snippet next to a sticky note and a memory tape strip.
insights.emphasis: The shared message pool is the central tinted block with double-headed blue arrows to every agent, and a curved black line zooms from the Engineer into the right-hand panel.
insights.flow: Agents publish to and subscribe from the pool by vertical double arrows; dotted arrows trace the hand-off order around the perimeter; in the right panel the loop runs write code, execution, check/cross, then Debug or Add Code back around.
insights.avoid: Too many small icons (pdf, python, image, document glyphs floating near agents) and two separate loops of dotted arrows make the left panel busy, and the 'Tools' legend sits detached below.

core.what: five role avatars placed around one central purple Shared Message Pool, each tied to it by a vertical blue double arrow, with one expanded message shown as key-value fields inside the pool

relations.form: the purple pool sits in the middle of the left frame; Architect and Project Manager above, Product Manager and QA Engineer below, and the Engineer at the right connect through 'subscription' and 'publish' boxes on the pool's right edge
dotted arrows around the outside of the left frame chain the roles Architect to Project Manager to Engineer to QA Engineer to Product Manager
a curved black line leaves the Engineer and opens a large blue rounded panel on the right holding an 'Agent Profile' card (Name, Profile, Goal, Constraint) and the engineer's working loop

inside the zoom panel a dotted 'Iterative Programming' frame draws a loop: a code snippet produced from 'Write game.py' goes to Execution, a red cross returns through Debug and a 'Feedback' line to the LLM icon, a green check sends 'Add Code' up to History Message
a Memory tape strip at the top of the work area is read by 'Memory Retrieval' into a History Message box listing PRD Document, System Design and Code

channels.colour: purple = the shared pool and also the History Message header; blue double arrows = publish/subscribe; red cross / green check = execution failed / passed; tool icons coloured by tool (keyed in a Tools legend at the bottom)
channels.shape: cartoon avatars = agents; grey 'msg' tabs = messages; key-value text = one message's fields; a code listing = real output
channels.line: solid blue double arrows = pool traffic; dotted arrows = role-to-role order; curved black lines = zoom from the Engineer
channels.frame: black rounded frame = the agent team; blue rounded panel = one agent opened up; dotted frame = the iterative-programming loop

quality.strengths: the shared pool is literally central with every agent wired to it, and one message is expanded as its real fields (content, cause_by, sent_from, send_to); the zoom panel shows the agent's work as real code and an execution/debug loop
quality.weaknesses: the zoom panel is larger than the team overview and densely packed, so the eye goes to the code listing rather than the pool; the dotted role-order arrows run around the frame edge and are easy to miss; purple marks both the pool and History Message; a second curved line from the panel's bottom back to 'publish' crosses the gap with no label

figures.lesson: For a team of role agents, place avatar portraits around a central shared store linked by double-headed arrows, show one message expanded as key: value fields, and pull one agent out into a side panel that zooms into its profile, memory and execute-feedback loop.

figures.title: Multi-Granularity Cross-modal Alignment for Generalized Medical Visual Representation Learning

taxonomy.task: multi-granularity medical image-text representation learning

arrangement.units: three tinted regions, one per alignment objective, between and right of the encoder bars
arrangement.inputs_as: real X-ray thumbnails and quoted report lines and words
arrangement.losses_at: each objective in its own tinted region where the two modalities meet
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Green Image Encoder bar on top and purple Text Encoder bar at the bottom, with three tinted regions for the objectives: yellow CTA between the encoders, pink ITA similarity matrix to the right, blue CPA prototype-clustering panel at the far right.
insights.data: Inputs are real chest X-rays with zoomed patch circles and quoted report lines split into word chips; representations are vertical columns of green or purple squares, token embeddings are multi-coloured cell rows, and the ITA is a 4 x 4 grid with blue diagonal cells.
insights.emphasis: Each alignment objective gets its own tinted region with its acronym in a matching colour (CTA orange, ITA red, CPA blue), explained in a dashed key at bottom right.
insights.flow: Left to right from inputs to encoders to representation columns; green lines run from the image side and purple lines from the text side into each objective, with curved black 'Align' arrows inside CTA.
insights.avoid: The purple 'Query' lines in CTA loop around the cross-attention boxes and cross the green ones, making the token-wise alignment hard to trace.

core.what: the green Image Encoder (top) and purple Text Encoder (bottom) feed three tinted objective regions at three granularities - yellow token-level CTA between the encoders, pink instance-level ITA similarity matrix, blue prototype-level CPA clustering at the far right

relations.form: green lines from the image representation column and purple lines from the text representation column each branch to both the pink ITA box and the blue CPA panel, while dashed callouts pull token embeddings R_i and Z_i into the yellow CTA region
the ITA box draws a 4 x 4 similarity matrix with green image squares across the top, purple text squares down the left and blue diagonal cells
the CPA panel draws two partitioned embedding spaces (image above, text below) with squares, crosses and circles in cells around prototypes, linked by green and purple 'Cross-modal prediction' arrows

inside the CTA region two Cross Attention blocks take Key/Value from one modality's token row and Query from the other via elbow lines, with curved black 'Align' arrows tying the attended rows back to the original token rows
left to right from inputs (real chest X-rays with zoomed patch circles; quoted report lines split into word chips) to the encoders, to vertical representation columns v_i and t_i, to the objectives

channels.colour: green = image side, purple = text side (encoders, lines, representation columns, query/key arrows); region tint = objective (yellow CTA, pink ITA, blue CPA), keyed in a dashed legend; multicolour cells = token embeddings, and blue also fills the ITA diagonal
channels.shape: vertical square columns = global representations; multicolour cell rows = token embeddings; squares/crosses/circles = cluster members; dark rounded bars = encoders
channels.line: solid lines = data flow; dashed lines = callouts to token embeddings; curved black arrows = alignment
channels.frame: tinted rounded region = one alignment objective; dashed rounded outline = a representation pulled out

quality.strengths: modality is one colour everywhere (green image, purple text), the compared representations are drawn as square columns and token rows between encoders and objectives, the ITA is a real matrix and the CPA is a drawn clustering, and each objective has its own tinted region keyed at the bottom right
quality.weaknesses: the CTA region sits between the encoders and dominates the centre although token-level alignment is one of three objectives; the multicolour token cells reuse the blue of the CPA tint and ITA diagonal; the encoder outputs travel long elbow lines from the left edge past CTA to reach ITA and CPA

figures.lesson: Colour the image path green and the text path purple all the way through, and give each alignment objective its own tinted region with its own abbreviation.

figures.title: MiniGPT-4: Enhancing Vision-Language Understanding with Advanced Large Language Models

taxonomy.task: image-grounded chat / description

arrangement.units: one unframed vertical stack: vision block, Linear Layer, Vicuna bar, with dashed text bubbles around it
arrangement.inputs_as: the image (a pink flamingo logo drawing) at the bottom right; the prompt as quoted text in green dashed bubbles at the Vicuna bar's lower edge
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; the generated answer is a quoted paragraph in a dashed bubble at the top
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Three solid module boxes are stacked bottom-to-top (Q-Former & ViT, Linear Layer, a full-width Vicuna bar) with the text prompt pieces as dashed bubbles flanking the Linear Layer just under the LLM bar.
insights.data: The prompt and the answer are drawn as real quoted text in green dashed rounded bubbles, the answer as a long paragraph whose key phrases are bold magenta, and the image enters as a picture from the bottom right.
insights.emphasis: Colour encodes trainability: the Linear Layer is the lone orange box while every frozen part is blue with a white snowflake.
insights.flow: Read from the bottom up: thick green arrows run picture -> vision block -> Linear Layer -> Vicuna, the side bubbles feed Vicuna from below, and one arrow at the right end of Vicuna rises into the answer bubble.
insights.avoid: The answer paragraph takes about a third of the figure and the input image sits outside any frame, so the model itself is visually smaller than its example output.

core.what: a bottom-to-top tower - picture into a frozen Q-Former & ViT box, up through the single orange Linear Layer, into a full-width frozen Vicuna bar, whose output rises into an answer bubble on top

relations.form: thick green arrows run from the flamingo drawing at the bottom right left into Q-Former & ViT, then straight up through the Linear Layer into Vicuna, and up from Vicuna's right end into the answer
two dashed prompt bubbles ('### Human:' at left, 'What do you think of this logo design? ### Assistant:' at right) flank the Linear Layer and each send an arrow up into Vicuna beside the image path

channels.colour: box fill = trainability (blue with a white snowflake = frozen, orange = trained Linear Layer); green = all text bubbles and arrows; bold magenta = key phrases of the generated answer
channels.shape: solid rectangles = modules; dashed rounded bubbles = text tokens (prompt pieces and answer); the drawing = the image input
channels.line: solid green arrows = data flow, one style throughout
channels.frame: none beyond the module boxes

quality.strengths: the one trained component is the only orange box and sits exactly where image features enter the language model, so 'only a projection is learned' reads in seconds; prompt and answer are real quoted text, and the input is the actual picture
quality.weaknesses: the answer paragraph fills about a third of the figure with prose, larger than any module; the image enters from the side at the bottom right instead of below the vision box, adding a horizontal turn; the visual tokens between the Linear Layer and Vicuna are not drawn as tokens like the text pieces are

figures.lesson: When a model adds one trainable piece between two frozen giants, make it the single warm-coloured box in a stack of cool frozen ones and mark the frozen ones with a snowflake glyph.

figures.title: Mip-NeRF: A Multiscale Representation for Anti-Aliasing Neural Radiance Fields

taxonomy.task: anti-aliased neural radiance fields

arrangement.units: unframed side-by-side sub-figures with letter captions beneath, the same camera-and-grid motif in each
arrangement.inputs_as: camera glyph and pixel grid drawn in perspective
arrangement.shared: the same camera and pixel-grid motif repeated in each panel

insights.structure: Two captioned sub-figures side by side, 'a) NeRF' at left and 'b) Mip-NeRF' at right, each built from the same camera glyph and tilted pixel grid; the Mip-NeRF part is two steps joined by an arrow labelled N.
insights.data: Rays are black lines with point samples, the cone is a translucent purple solid cut into frustum segments between t0 and t1, and the frustum is then shown as stacked purple Gaussian blobs; the encoding is written as gamma(x) versus E[gamma(x)].
insights.emphasis: The only colour is purple on the Mip-NeRF cone and Gaussians plus a red pixel footprint, against a black-line NeRF panel.
insights.flow: Left to right: ray to cone to Gaussians, with curved arrows lifting each sample up to its encoding label.
insights.avoid: Small italic labels (r-dot, t0, t1) sit inside the translucent cone and are hard to read.

core.what: NeRF (a, left) and Mip-NeRF (b, right) drawn side by side from the same camera glyph and tilted pixel grid: a single ray with point samples against a cone cut into a conical frustum, ours last

relations.form: both panels reuse the identical camera and 3 x 3 pixel grid; NeRF draws a black ray o + td with purple sample dots and gamma(x) lifted from one point, Mip-NeRF replaces it with a translucent purple cone over a red pixel footprint
the Mip-NeRF cone is cut into a frustum segment between t0 and t1 with the pixel radius r-dot marked on the footprint, the operation drawn on the ray geometry itself
within b) an arrow labelled N leads right from the frustum to the same scene where the frustum is replaced by stacked purple Gaussian blobs, lifted by a curved arrow to E[gamma(x)]

channels.colour: purple = the sampled volume (sample points in NeRF, cone and Gaussians in Mip-NeRF); red = the pixel's footprint; black = geometry (camera, grid, ray)
channels.shape: camera triangle, tilted grid = image plane; line = ray; cone/frustum = conical sample volume; ellipsoids = Gaussians
channels.line: solid = ray and cone edges; dashed = the faded continuation of the cone; curved arrows = encoding of a sample
channels.frame: no frames; panels separated by whitespace and captions

quality.strengths: the difference between point sampling and cone sampling is pure geometry on a shared scene - same camera, same grid, ray vs cone - so it reads with labels covered; the representation that is encoded (a point, then a Gaussian) is drawn at the spot it comes from with its encoding label above; one accent colour marks what changed
quality.weaknesses: r-dot, t0 and t1 are small italic labels sitting inside or under the translucent cone and are hard to read; purple marks both NeRF's sample points and Mip-NeRF's volumes, which is consistent in meaning but makes the NeRF sample dots faint

figures.lesson: Contrast ray-based and cone-based sampling with the same camera-and-pixel-grid motif in each panel: a black line with point samples versus a translucent purple cone cut into frustum segments, then the same segment as stacked Gaussian blobs.

figures.title: Mixtral of Experts

taxonomy.task: sparse mixture-of-experts language modelling

arrangement.units: one unframed pipeline row: router box, expert deck, merge operator; no enclosing regions
arrangement.inputs_as: a single arrow labelled 'inputs' in monospace; no token or vector is drawn
arrangement.shared: the gating weights are one dotted line from the router that splits to both selected expert outputs

insights.structure: A router box on the left feeds a diagonal deck of overlapping expert cards in the middle, whose outputs merge at a circled-plus on the right, all on one horizontal line with no frames.
insights.data: Data is only named on arrows ('inputs', 'outputs'); the per-expert weights are a separate dotted line labelled 'gating weights' that loops over the top of the deck.
insights.emphasis: The two selected experts are solid and saturated while the others are dashed and faded, which makes top-2 selection the visual focus.
insights.flow: Solid arrows run left-to-right through router, experts and sum, while the dotted gating line climbs from the router, runs across the top and drops down onto the two expert output lines just before the sum.
insights.avoid: The 'expert' label is greyed and partly overlapped by the faded cards in front, and the two solid expert cards overlap so heavily that it is hard to see that exactly two are active.

core.what: a diagonal deck of overlapping expert cards between a router and a sum node, two drawn solid and saturated and the rest dashed and faded, showing top-2 selection among many experts on one horizontal line

relations.form: inputs enter the router at the left, two elbow arrows run into the two solid expert cards, and their outputs merge at a circled-plus on the right into 'outputs'
the experts are a stack of offset cards; the two selected ones are solid orange-bordered, the others dashed and pale, so selection is drawn as salience
a dotted 'gating weights' line rises from the router, runs over the top of the deck and drops onto each selected expert's output line just before the sum

channels.colour: orange fill for router and experts (one kind: learned module); saturation = selected vs unselected expert
channels.shape: rounded rectangles = router / expert modules; circled plus = weighted sum
channels.line: solid arrows = token data; dotted lines = gating weights (control signal); dashed card borders = unselected experts
channels.frame: none

quality.strengths: sparse top-2 routing is shown by salience within one deck rather than by text: two saturated cards among faded ones; the control signal (gating weights) is a different line style from the data path
quality.weaknesses: the two solid expert cards overlap so heavily their separate outputs are hard to trace; the 'expert' label is greyed and partly covered by faded cards; the gating weights travel a long dotted detour over the deck instead of sitting as a label at the sum; the title is cut at the top of the crop

figures.lesson: Show sparse routing by drawing all experts as one overlapping deck and fading the unselected ones, so 'k of N are active' reads at a glance without drawing N separate boxes.

figures.title: MLP-Mixer: An all-MLP Architecture for Vision

taxonomy.task: image classification backbone
taxonomy.note: architecture 'other' = a stack of all-MLP mixer layers (token-mixing MLP then channel-mixing MLP with skips), transformer-like but without attention

arrangement.units: One overview tower, unframed, bottom-centre; two dashed rounded detail frames (Mixer Layer across the top, MLP at bottom-right) set off by whitespace.
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo cut into a 3 x 3 patch grid, then laid out as a row of photo tiles
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; the tower ends in a plain 'Class' label at its top
arrangement.shared: weight sharing shown by repeating an identical 'MLP 1' / 'MLP 2' pill on every row

insights.structure: The expanded Mixer Layer spans the whole top width in a dashed frame, the compact classification tower sits bottom-centre, and the two-layer MLP internals sit in a second, narrow dashed frame at bottom-right.
insights.data: Patch tokens are coloured pills whose colours reappear as the rows of a patches x channels table and, after a curved 'T' transpose arrow, as its columns, while the input is a real photo split into a 3 x 3 grid of tiles.
insights.emphasis: The contribution is made to stand out by expansion rather than colour: the one 'N x (Mixer Layer)' box is opened into the full-width detail, where repeated identical 'MLP 1' / 'MLP 2' pills show weight sharing.
insights.flow: The tower reads bottom-to-top (photo tiles, per-patch FC, tokens, N x Mixer Layer, pooling, FC, 'Class'), the detail panel reads left-to-right, and skip-connections are labelled lines that arch over the top of the panel.
insights.avoid: The detail frame is tied to its 'N x (Mixer Layer)' box only by name (no zoom lines or matching tint), and the MLP frame's arrow just points up into empty space, so the reader must match the parts by label.

figures.title: MoDL: Model Based Deep Learning Architecture for Inverse Problems

taxonomy.task: model-based deep learning for MRI reconstruction

arrangement.units: three captioned sub-figures stacked vertically, each a different zoom level (module, loop, unrolled); in (c) one red frame per iteration

insights.avoid: The red iteration frames in (c) and the red skip line in (a) use red only for grouping, which competes with the emphasis colours.

core.what: the denoiser-plus-data-consistency loop shown twice: as a compact two-box cycle with an 'Iterate' return arrow in (b), then unrolled into three red-framed iterations (1st, k-th, K-th) sharing one weight box in (c)

relations.form: (b) draws yellow D_w and green DC side by side with an 'Iterate' line looping back along the bottom from x_{k+1}; (c) repeats the yellow-green pair in three red frames joined by dotted arrows x_{k-1} ... x_K
one tan 'Shared Weights W' box below (c) sends upward arrows into the D_w block of every iteration
in (b) and (c) a line from x_0 = A^H b runs along the top and drops into every DC block, the measurement entering each data-consistency step
(a) opens D_w as a yellow frame around a tan N_w block of Layer 1 ... Layer N columns (Conv, BN, ReLU) with a red skip line into a circled plus

channels.colour: yellow = denoiser D_w, green = data-consistency layer, kept across (b) and (c); tan = learned network weights (N_w in (a), Shared Weights in (c)); red = the skip connection in (a) and the iteration frames in (c)
channels.shape: rectangles = operators; teal small boxes in grey columns = network layers; circled plus = residual addition
channels.line: solid arrows = signal flow; dotted arrows = 'N-times' / skipped iterations
channels.frame: red frame = one unrolled iteration; yellow frame = the denoiser D_w

quality.strengths: the unrolling is taught in two scales - loop then unrolled copies - with yellow/green held constant so each copy is recognisable; weight sharing is drawn as one box feeding every denoiser; the x_0 line along the top shows the measurement entering every DC step
quality.weaknesses: the DC block in (b) carries a typeset formula (A^H A + lambda I)^{-1} and D_w = I - N_w; red means both the skip connection in (a) and the iteration frames in (c); the long top bus and the Shared Weights lines in (c) bend around the frames; (a) and (b) are tied only by the symbol D_w, not by a callout

figures.lesson: Draw the method twice: as a compact two-box loop with an 'Iterate' return arrow, then unrolled into K red-framed iterations whose denoisers all take arrows from one 'Shared Weights' box beneath.

figures.title: Eyes Wide Shut? Exploring the Visual Shortcomings of Multimodal LLMs

arrangement.inputs_as: a grey '<text>' box quoting the question 'How many eyes can you see in this image? (a) 1 (b) 2' above a light-blue '<image>' box holding a real cat photo, at the bottom right of every panel
