channels.line: solid black = global mode, dashed blue = breakpoint mode (keyed); merge-line thickness = weight in the weighted sum
channels.frame: the beige rounded panel = the consolidation procedure; the Q-Former is a dash-dot frame around token cells, the same frame style as the memory cells

quality.strengths: The novel consolidation is the biggest element and its steps are drawn on the tokens (pairs, scored circles, weighted merge); both memories are drawn as token bars, not labelled boxes; the two inference modes are separated by line style and keyed; inputs are a real film strip with the sliding window drawn on it.
quality.weaknesses: The cleared/re-initialised buffer is drawn as an extra purple bar that reads as a third memory; the loop around short-term memory uses a line that bends round its left side; beige marks both the consolidation panel and the V/P trapezoids; the dashed breakpoint lines run long and cross the Extend Positional Encoding bar.

figures.lesson: Put the operation that moves data between two stores in the centre as the largest panel, with the two stores as same-colour token bars on either side, and draw its steps on the tokens themselves (pairs, scored circles, a weighted merge).

figures.title: Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry

taxonomy.task: molecular property prediction (DFT surrogate)

arrangement.units: two horizontal lanes without frames: top lane a single 'DFT' box, bottom lane the 'Message Passing Neural Net' box holding three graph snapshots; both converge on a 'Targets' box at top right
arrangement.inputs_as: a grey circle holding a white skeletal drawing of the molecule
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the 'Targets' box (E, ω0, ...) is the shared output
arrangement.shared: the input circle and the Targets box are shared by both lanes

insights.structure: A grey input circle on the left forks into two parallel grey boxes, a small 'DFT' box on top and a wide 'Message Passing Neural Net' box below, which both feed one 'Targets' box at top right.
insights.data: The molecule is a white skeletal drawing in the input circle and, inside the MPNN box, three ball-and-stick graphs whose node dots change colour (white, blue, red, purple) from snapshot to snapshot.
insights.emphasis: Large serif annotations '~10^3 seconds' and '~10^-2 seconds' under the two routes make the cost contrast the message, and the MPNN box is the only one with content inside.
insights.flow: Arrows leave the input circle right and fork up and down, the DFT path runs straight into Targets, and the MPNN path turns upward into Targets from below.
insights.avoid: All boxes share the same flat mid-grey fill, so the proposed net is not set apart from the DFT baseline by colour, and the node colours inside the snapshots have no key.

core.what: one molecule in a circle forks into two routes to the same Targets box - a small DFT box above (~10^3 seconds) and a wide Message Passing Neural Net box below (~10^-2 seconds) - so the cost contrast reads as two parallel paths

relations.form: arrows leave the input circle and fork up into DFT and down into the MPNN box; both end at the Targets box (E, omega_0, ...) at the top right, the DFT path straight across and the MPNN path turning up from below
inside the MPNN box three ball-and-stick copies of the molecular graph, joined by white arrows, show node dots changing colour (white, blue, red, purple) as messages pass

channels.colour: node-dot colour = node state at each message-passing snapshot; all boxes share one grey fill
channels.shape: circle = the input molecule; rectangles = methods or targets; ball-and-stick graphs = the molecular graph
channels.line: solid black arrows = computation routes; white arrows = message-passing steps
channels.frame: grey box = one route or the target set

quality.strengths: the claim (MPNN replaces DFT at a fraction of the cost) is drawn as two routes from one input to one output with the runtimes in large type under each; message passing is shown on the actual molecular graph, with node states changing colour step by step
quality.weaknesses: every box shares the same grey fill, so input, method and output are told apart only by shape and text; the node colours are unexplained and their meaning must be guessed; the MPNN path makes a right-angle turn up into Targets instead of meeting it head on

figures.lesson: Put the proposed model and the expensive baseline on parallel paths from the same input to the same target and print each path's cost under its box, so the speed-up reads at a glance.

figures.title: Multi-Stage Progressive Image Restoration

taxonomy.task: image restoration (deraining, deblurring, denoising)

arrangement.units: one unboxed horizontal lane per stage, labelled 'Stage 1/2/3' at its left; Stage 3's ORB chain is enclosed in a grey ORSNet box
arrangement.inputs_as: real degraded photos, split into patches differently per stage
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; restored outputs at the right of each lane
arrangement.shared: the same degraded image enters every lane; SAM outputs pass up between lanes

insights.structure: Three horizontal stage rows stacked with Stage 1 at the bottom and Stage 3 at the top, each starting from a degraded image on the left and ending in a restored image on the right, with a legend box for ORB/SAM/CAB in the bottom-right.
insights.data: Inputs are real rainy car photos split into 4 patches (Stage 1), 2 patches (Stage 2) and whole (Stage 3) with coloured borders; U-Nets are grey trapezoid pairs with small 3D coloured feature cubes labelled 'cat'.
insights.emphasis: Repeated stage-specific modules use saturated fills (orange Conv, green SAM, yellow ORB in a grey ORSNet box) and the cross-stage connections are distinct colours: green solid arrows from SAM to the next stage and magenta dotted arrows between U-Net encoders/decoders.
insights.flow: Each stage reads left to right; information climbs upward between stages via green SAM-output arrows and magenta dotted feature links, so the overall progression runs bottom to top.
insights.avoid: Bottom-to-top stage ordering against top-down reading, plus many crossing coloured inter-stage lines, makes the cross-stage wiring hard to follow.

core.what: three horizontal stage rows stacked bottom to top, each running from the same degraded image (split into 4 patches, 2 patches, then whole) to its own restored image, with green SAM arrows and magenta dotted encoder-decoder arrows passing upward between stages

relations.form: Stage 1 at the bottom and Stage 3 at the top each start with Conv and CAB blocks on the left and end in Restored X1, X2, X3 on the right; stages 1 and 2 use a grey trapezoid U-Net, stage 3 an ORSNet box of ORB_1 ... ORB_n
the rainy car photo is drawn cut into four coloured-border patches in Stage 1, two in Stage 2 and whole in Stage 3, the patch hierarchy drawn on the image

a green solid arrow rises from each stage's SAM into the next stage's concatenation circle C, and magenta dotted arrows rise from each U-Net's encoder and decoder into the next stage's U-Net or ORSNet
within each row, left to right: degraded image, Conv, CAB, concatenation, U-Net or ORSNet, SAM or Conv, add, restored image; a long line over the top of Stage 3 carries the input to the final add

channels.colour: block fill = module type (orange Conv, pale green CAB, green SAM, yellow ORB), keyed in a legend at the bottom right; green arrows = SAM features to the next stage; magenta dotted = cross-stage encoder/decoder features; image border colour = patch identity; small coloured cubes = feature concatenation - so green means both the SAM block and its outgoing arrows, and CAB's pale green is close to SAM's
channels.shape: grey trapezoid pairs = U-Net encoder/decoder; small rectangles = layers; circles = concatenation or add; photos = images
channels.line: solid black = within-stage flow; solid green = SAM output to next stage; dotted magenta = cross-stage feature fusion
channels.frame: grey rounded box = ORSNet; legend box at the bottom right

quality.strengths: the multi-stage progression is geometry: three rows, each a full degraded-to-restored path with its own output image, the input's patch split shrinking stage by stage; the two kinds of cross-stage connection have their own colour and dash so they can be traced upward
quality.weaknesses: Stage 1 sits at the bottom and Stage 3 at the top, against the top-to-bottom reading of rows; green carries both the SAM block fill and the cross-stage arrow, and CAB's pale green is near it; the input-to-SAM and input-to-add lines run long under each row and over the top of Stage 3

figures.lesson: Stack the stages bottom to top and re-show the input at each stage as a thumbnail cut into fewer patches (quadrants, halves, whole) with coloured patch borders, so the coarse-to-fine progression is drawn on the image itself.

figures.title: Multi-Stage Progressive Image Restoration

taxonomy.task: supervised attention module for image restoration

arrangement.units: unboxed tensor stacks and small orange Conv tags connected by arrows with circle operators
arrangement.inputs_as: a feature stack F_in (top) and a real degraded photo (bottom)
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Two horizontal tracks: a feature track on top from F_in (left) to F_out (right) and an image track below from Degraded I through Restored X_S to attention maps M, joined by vertical connections.
insights.data: Features are drawn as stacked viridis-coloured slices labelled H x W x C, images as real rainy viaduct photos labelled H x W x 3, and attention maps as a stack of greyscale slices.
insights.emphasis: The only supervised output, Restored X_S, carries a pink 'Loss' tag beneath it, and the attention maps re-enter the feature track through a multiply circle before the residual add.
insights.flow: F_in branches down via a Conv to a residual R_S added to the degraded image; the restored image goes right through Conv and sigmoid to M, which rises to multiply the conv'd features, then adds back to F_in to give F_out.

core.what: a feature track on top (F_in to F_out) and an image track below (Degraded I to Restored X_S to attention maps M), joined by vertical links: features drop down to form a residual, and attention maps computed from the restored image rise back to multiply the features

relations.form: the attention-map stack M at the lower right sends an arrow straight up into a multiply circle on the feature track, gating the Conv'd F_in before the residual add and F_out
the image track runs left to right: Degraded I (real rainy photo), an add with the residual R_S, Restored X_S, Conv, a sigmoid circle, the greyscale attention-map stack
the feature track runs along the top from a viridis slice stack F_in through Conv to the multiply and add, with a skip line over the top from F_in to the final add, parallel to the image track below
every tensor is drawn as data with its shape: viridis feature slices labelled H x W x C, real photos labelled H x W x 3, greyscale attention slices labelled H x W x C

channels.colour: viridis = feature tensors; real photo colour = images; greyscale = attention maps; orange = Conv blocks; pink = the Loss tag
channels.shape: slice stacks = multichannel tensors; photos = images; small rectangles = Conv; circles = add / multiply / sigmoid (sigmoid keyed at bottom right)
channels.line: solid black arrows = data flow, one style
channels.frame: none

quality.strengths: every intermediate is drawn as the actual thing - feature slices, rainy and restored photos, greyscale attention maps - with its shape label, so the reader sees that supervision acts on an image and attention returns to features; the two tracks are straight horizontal lines joined by short vertical links; the one supervised output carries the only pink tag
quality.weaknesses: the skip line from F_in to the final add arches over the top of the whole feature track; the second Conv on the feature track has no label distinguishing it from the R_S Conv; the attention stack is labelled H x W x C but drawn in the image track's greyscale, so its kind (feature-shaped, image-derived) is not obvious

figures.lesson: Draw a module's tensors as stacks of real data - viridis activation maps for features, the actual photo for the intermediate image, greyscale maps for attention - each with its shape above, so every arrow visibly changes the data.

figures.title: Motion Transformer with Global Intention Localization and Local Movement Refinement

taxonomy.task: multimodal motion prediction

arrangement.units: dashed-border rounded panels labelled (a), (b), (c); the encoder and scene column are unboxed
arrangement.inputs_as: top-down road-scene sketch with car icons, encoded to agent/map token rows
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; output tensor boxes at the top of panel (c)
arrangement.shared: encoder features shared as key/value by the decoder

insights.structure: Three zones left to right: a narrow scene column (road map, polyline encoder, local graph), a central encoder stack with two dashed sub-panels (a) Dense Future Prediction and (b) Dynamic Map Collection above it, and a large grey dashed panel (c) holding the stacked xN decoder layer.
insights.data: Agent features are blue squares and map features grey circles in rounded token rows, scenes are top-down road sketches with car icons, and decoder tensors are white boxes labelled with shapes like K x T x 2 and K x (2+2).
insights.emphasis: The decoder panel (c) is the largest region with a grey background and xN multiplier, and the two dashed sub-panels illustrate their outputs with coloured dotted predicted trajectories and translucent trajectory-specific map regions.
insights.flow: Bottom-up within the encoder (local graph tokens to Transformer Encoder to sub-panels), then a long 'Key & Value' elbow line carries features right into the decoder, which itself reads bottom-up from three query initialisations to GMM Prediction and outputs.
insights.avoid: Long elbow lines (Key & Value, the loop from Dynamic Map Collection back) cross the panel boundaries and are hard to trace.

core.what: left to right: a scene encoded into agent and map token rows by a Transformer Encoder, two dashed sub-panels illustrating dense future prediction and dynamic map collection above it, then a large grey xN decoder panel that turns motion query pairs into predicted trajectories

relations.form: the scene column at the far left (road sketch, Polyline Encoder, Local Graph) feeds a token row of blue agent squares and grey map circles into the Transformer Encoder, whose output row splits into agent and map halves, then a 'Key & Value' arrow runs right into the decoder panel

two dashed sub-panels (a) and (b) sit above Dense Future Prediction and Dynamic Map Collection, each illustrating its output on a top-down road sketch: dotted yellow trajectories in (a), coloured trajectory-specific map strips in (b)

the decoder layer is one grey dashed panel (c) marked xN, with Transformer Decoder Layer, GMM Prediction and three output tensors (K x T x 2, K x (2+2), K x D) whose 'Query Updating' outputs feed the next layer
a long elbow line from the Predicted Trajectory Initialization tensor at the bottom right runs left under the decoder into Dynamic Map Collection, which gathers map tokens along each trajectory
the encoder's token rows are drawn as data: blue squares = agent features, grey circles = map features, the same glyphs as dots on the local-graph road sketch

channels.colour: blue squares = agent features, grey circles = map features (keyed in a bottom legend); dotted yellow / green / red = predicted trajectories and trajectory-specific map features in the sub-panels; grey fill = modules and the decoder panel background
channels.shape: squares vs circles = agent vs map token; rounded white boxes = output tensors labelled with shape; grey rectangles = modules; car icons = interested / other agent (keyed)
channels.line: solid arrows = data flow; dotted arrows in the sketches = predicted trajectories
channels.frame: dashed blue frame = an illustrated sub-step (a), (b); grey dashed panel with xN = the repeated decoder layer

quality.strengths: token kinds are distinct glyphs (squares vs circles) kept from the road sketch through the encoder rows, with a full legend; the two auxiliary steps are illustrated on actual top-down scenes; decoder tensors carry their shapes
quality.weaknesses: the decoder panel, the method's core, reads bottom to top while the encoder reads left to right and the sub-panels sit above the encoder, so there is no single reading axis; the line from Predicted Trajectory Initialization to Dynamic Map Collection and the Key & Value line are long elbows crossing the gap between zones; dense token rows and two sketch panels crowd the centre

figures.lesson: Use two token glyphs (blue squares for agents, grey circles for map polylines) in every token row, and pair each module with a top-view mini-scene showing its output as dotted trajectory arrows and translucent map bands, all decoded by a glyph legend along the bottom.

figures.title: MuRAG: Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generator for Open Question Answering over Images and Text

taxonomy.task: multimodal retrieval-augmented open question answering

arrangement.units: two rows (stages) by three columns (retriever, memory, reader), each cell a rounded panel with a coloured header bar
arrangement.inputs_as: real photos and quoted question text with dataset labels
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; output tokens y1..yn at the top of the reader panel
arrangement.shared: same three-panel layout and modules repeated in both rows

insights.structure: Two identical rows (Pre-Training Stage top, Fine-Tune Stage bottom), each with three column panels: Retriever Stage, External Memory and Reader Stage, joined by big grey block arrows labelled MIPS and Top_K(M).
insights.data: Queries are real photos plus quoted text with dataset tags (CC, PAQ, VQA); memory entries are rows of pink embedding dots next to text, photos or a Wikipedia snippet; the reader is two node-link transformer layers f_theta and g_theta over ViT/Emb input boxes.
insights.emphasis: Each column header is tinted (blue retriever, yellow memory, pink reader) and the per-row caption states what changes between stages, while ViT boxes are yellow and Emb boxes blue throughout to show which modalities enter.
insights.flow: Left to right within each row via the fat grey arrows; the two rows are read top then bottom as training stages.
insights.avoid: The 'Empty' checkered placeholders and tiny unreadable Wikipedia snippet text add clutter, and generic node-link drawings stand in for transformers without saying anything specific.

core.what: two identical three-column rows - Pre-Training Stage on top, Fine-Tune Stage below - each Retriever Stage, External Memory and Reader Stage joined by grey block arrows labelled MIPS and Top_K(M), so what changes between stages reads column by column

relations.form: the two rows reuse the same tinted column headers and layout; their captions and contents differ: image-text queries over a text memory above, text queries over an image-text memory below

the yellow External Memory column sits between retriever and reader, its entries drawn as rows of pink embedding dots beside the stored item (text, photos, a Wikipedia snippet, or an 'Empty' placeholder)
a grey block arrow 'MIPS' leads from the retriever's query embedding into memory, and a second block arrow 'Top_K(M)' leads from memory into the reader
the reader's input row lists query and retrieved items as yellow ViT and blue Emb boxes (x_I, x_p, m_1, ..., m_k) under two node-link layers f_theta and g_theta producing y_1 ... y_n

channels.colour: column-header tint = stage role (blue retriever, yellow memory, pink reader); yellow box = ViT (image) input, blue box = Emb (text) input - so yellow and blue mean both column role and modality encoder; pink dots = embeddings; lavender nodes = transformer units
channels.shape: node-link layers = transformer; dot rows in rounded capsules = embeddings; photos and quoted text = data
channels.line: grey block arrows = retrieve / read steps; thin black arrows = attention edges inside the reader
channels.frame: framed column = one stage; dashed separators = memory entries

quality.strengths: the retrieve-then-read pipeline is a clear three-column skeleton repeated for both training phases, so the difference between phases is placed in matching cells; memory entries and queries are real photos and quoted text
quality.weaknesses: the retriever and reader are drawn as generic node-link meshes that look alike and carry no information; yellow and blue code both stage columns and ViT/Emb inputs; the query embedding entering MIPS is a lone capsule beside the retriever, so what is compared with the memory index is only implied

figures.lesson: Each encoder box is filled with the tint of a column header (ViT boxes share the External Memory yellow, Emb boxes the Retriever blue-grey), so the interleaved image/text input sequence fed to the reader reads as a colour pattern without a legend.

figures.title: Muse: Text-To-Image Generation via Masked Generative Transformers

taxonomy.task: text-to-image generation training

arrangement.units: unboxed horizontal tracks of rounded coloured module boxes alternating with token grids
arrangement.inputs_as: real photos at two resolutions and a quoted text prompt
arrangement.shared: one text embedding feeds both transformers

insights.structure: Three horizontal tracks: text prompt and text encoder on top, a 256x256 base track in the middle and a 512x512 super-resolution track at the bottom, each image track being VQ Tokenizer, Mask, token grid, Transformer, reconstructed grid.
insights.data: Inputs are real dog-and-cat photos labelled with resolution, the text prompt is quoted in italics, the text embedding is a row of green cells, and tokens are small blue/grey grids where grey cells are masked.
insights.emphasis: Each module box has its own pastel fill and border (orange and green tokenizers, blue base, purple SuperRes transformer), and the two token grids before and after each transformer make the masked-to-filled change visible.
insights.flow: Left to right in each track; the text embedding arrow drops into both transformers, and a dashed line carries base reconstructed tokens down into the SuperRes transformer.

core.what: two parallel image tracks - a 256x256 base track and a 512x512 super-resolution track below it - each VQ Tokenizer, Mask, masked token grid, Transformer, reconstructed grid, with one text-embedding line from the top feeding both transformers

relations.form: the base track (middle row) and super-resolution track (bottom row) run left to right in the same order with the same glyphs; a dashed line from the base reconstructed tokens joins the line down into the SuperRes Transformer

the text prompt 'A cat looking at a dog' goes through a Text Encoder to a row of green embedding cells on top, whose line branches down into the Base Transformer and, along the right, into the SuperRes Transformer

tokens are drawn as small blue grids with grey masked cells (4 x 4 for the base, 8 x 8 for high-res), the masked grid before each transformer and the fully filled grid after it, with 'Cross Entropy Loss' under each reconstructed grid

channels.colour: box fill/border = module (orange and green tokenizers, blue base, purple SuperRes); blue cells = tokens, grey cells = masked; green cells = text embedding
channels.shape: photos = inputs; cell grids = token maps; rounded boxes = modules; tall narrow box = mask operation
channels.line: solid arrows = data flow; dashed line = the base output conditioning the super-resolution stage
channels.frame: none

quality.strengths: the masked-to-filled change is drawn as data: the same grid before and after each transformer, grey cells filled in; the two resolution tracks are aligned rows with token grids sized by resolution; real photos labelled with their sizes
quality.weaknesses: the dashed base-output line merges into the text-embedding line before reaching SuperRes, so the two conditions arrive as one wire; each module has its own pastel colour with no shared meaning, so the two VQ Tokenizers look like different kinds of module; the text-to-SuperRes line takes a long path down the right side

figures.lesson: Draw a two-resolution cascade as two rows with the same image-tokenizer-mask-grid-transformer-grid sequence, enlarging the input photo and the token grid in the lower row to show the higher resolution, and bring the shared condition down from a top row as elbow arrows into each row's transformer.

figures.title: Mastering Atari, Go, Chess and Shogi by Planning with a Learned Model

taxonomy.task: model-based planning for games

arrangement.units: three unboxed panels lettered A, B, C separated by thin rules
arrangement.inputs_as: Go-board state icons on a horizontal timeline
arrangement.shared: the same h/g/f colour code and s-node glyphs across all panels

insights.structure: Three panels: A (left, full height) a search tree, B (top right) acting in the environment over three time steps, C (bottom right) the unrolled training of the model aligned with the same steps; a vertical rule and a horizontal rule split them.
insights.data: Board states are tiny Go-board icons, hidden states are circles labelled s0..s3, policies are green bar histograms in brackets, and functions are single italic letters h, g, f.
insights.emphasis: Each function has its own colour carried across panels: cyan for h (representation), green for g (dynamics) and its s nodes, pink for f outputs p,v, while unexplored tree nodes are pale grey.
insights.flow: A reads top-down along the green path of the tree; B and C read left to right along a dashed-in timeline, with C's h arrow rising from the board row to s0 and g arrows conditioned on actions coming up from below.

core.what: the same three learned functions h, g, f drawn three ways - a search tree of hidden states (A), acting in the environment over three steps (B), and training the model unrolled over the same steps (C) - each function in its own colour across all panels

relations.form: panel C unrolls the model in a row: board icon up through cyan h into s0, then green g steps to s1 and s2, each g taking an action a_{t+1}, a_{t+2} from the board row below, with pink f lifting p, v above every state

panel A draws the search on a tree: a Go board at the top through h into s0, green g edges labelled a, r down one branch through s1, s2, s3, pink f giving p, v at each node, and unexplored nodes pale grey

panel B runs left to right over three board states joined by u_{t+1}, u_{t+2}, u_{t+3}; under each a small grey search tree yields a green policy histogram pi whose curved arrow chooses the next action
B and C stack on the right, aligned on the same three time steps, so acting (top) and training (bottom) compare column by column

channels.colour: cyan = representation h and s0; green = dynamics g and the states s1..s3 it produces, and also the policy histograms pi in B; pink = prediction f and its outputs p, v; pale grey = unexplored tree nodes; dark grey = environment flow
channels.shape: circles = hidden states; Go-board icons = observations; bracketed bar histograms = policies; single italic letters = functions
channels.line: solid coloured arrows = learned-function steps; grey arrows = environment transitions; dashed grey = earlier / later time
channels.frame: no frames; a vertical and a horizontal rule split the three panels

quality.strengths: one colour per learned function, held across all three panels, makes the tree, the acting loop and the training unroll readable as the same model; hidden states are drawn as nouns (s0..s3 circles) between the functions; the training unroll in C is aligned under the acting row in B on the same time steps
quality.weaknesses: green also fills the policy histograms in B, which are search outputs not dynamics; the functions are only single italic letters, so h/g/f must be learned from the caption; the small grey search trees in B are too small to read as the panel-A tree

figures.lesson: Give each learned function one colour and paint its letter, its arrow and its output in it across every panel, so the same model is recognisable both as a path through a search tree (A) and as a straight unrolled chain (C).

figures.title: MVDream: Multi-view Diffusion for 3D Generation

taxonomy.task: text-to-3D generation by score distillation from a camera-conditioned multi-view diffusion UNet trained on rendered views

arrangement.units: no lanes; a dashed rounded frame groups the 2x2 rendered views, and a lavender panel above the UNet opens one block, tied by a dashed line
arrangement.inputs_as: a rendered 3-D robot with camera icons around it, and its four rendered views as image tiles; Text, Timestep and Camera are plain labelled boxes
arrangement.losses_at: not drawn as elements: 'Training Loss' and 'Score Distillation' are labels on the arrows between the rendered views and the UNet
arrangement.shared: the UNet is drawn once at the right; the training arrow enters it and the score-distillation arrow leaves it on the same side

insights.structure: Three columns on one axis (3D model, a dashed-framed 2x2 view grid, the UNet hourglass) with the UNet's block opened in a panel above and conditioning boxes below.
insights.data: The 3D asset is a shaded render ringed by camera icons and the training sample is four rendered views in a 2x2 grid; text, timestep and camera are plain labelled boxes.
insights.emphasis: Inside the opened block only 3D SelfAttention is filled blue; the two uses carry coloured labels on their arrows.
insights.flow: Blue arrows point right from the 3D model through the views into the UNet, green arrows point back left; conditioning enters the UNet from below and the text from the left of the opened block.
insights.avoid: Do not reuse the training-direction colour for the new module, and do not leave the largest area to the routine input render while the contribution sits in a corner.

core.what: 3D model -> 2x2 rendered views -> multi-view UNet on one horizontal axis, read left to right by a blue training arrow and right to left by a green score-distillation arrow, with the rendered view set drawn as data in the middle

relations.form: three columns left to right with paired blue (rightward) and green (leftward) arrows between each, so both uses run along the same axis in opposite directions
one UNet bar is tied by a dashed line to a lavender panel above holding ResBlock -> 3D SelfAttention -> CrossAttention stacked top to bottom
Timestep and Camera boxes join at a circled plus below the UNet and enter its bottom; a Text box feeds CrossAttention from the left inside the opened block

channels.colour: use: blue = training / multi-view generation, green = 3D generation by score distillation; blue also fills the new 3D SelfAttention block and outlines the UNet bars, so blue carries a second meaning (the model and its new part)
channels.shape: hourglass = the UNet, rounded grey rectangles = modules and conditioning inputs, render tiles = data, camera icons = viewpoints, circled plus = addition
channels.line: solid coloured arrows = the two uses; thin black arrows = conditioning; a thin dashed line = callout to the opened block
channels.frame: dashed rounded frame = one multi-view sample; lavender panel = the opened UNet block

quality.strengths: The multi-view sample that both uses exchange is drawn as an actual 2x2 grid of renders between the 3D model and the UNet; training and distillation are opposite arrows on one axis, coloured and labelled per use; the only new module, 3D SelfAttention, is the only filled block in the opened UNet block; camera reaches the UNet by a short straight wire through a circled plus.
quality.weaknesses: Blue marks both the training direction and the UNet / new attention block. The 3D model render is the largest element though the contribution (the attention change) sits in a small corner panel. The two small arrows between the 3D model and the views are unlabelled, and neither loss is drawn as an element - only as arrow labels.

figures.lesson: When one model is trained and then used in the opposite direction, put the shared data between them and run the two uses as opposite-pointing arrows of two colours on the same axis.

figures.title: N-BEATS: Neural basis expansion analysis for interpretable time series forecasting

taxonomy.task: univariate time-series point forecasting

arrangement.units: Three rounded tinted panels in one row: left blue panel = one block (FC stack splitting into backcast and forecast heads), middle orange panel = one stack (Block 1, 2, ..., K on a residual spine with a forecast sum), right yellow panel = the model (Stack 1..M summed into the global forecast); a real series plot sits above the right panel without a frame.
arrangement.inputs_as: a real time-series line plot with lookback and forecast horizons marked by double arrows and a red split line; inside the panels inputs are text labels (Block Input, Stack Input)
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; outputs exit at the bottom (Backcast, Forecast, Stack residual) or top right (Global forecast)
arrangement.shared: each panel expands one box of the panel to its right via dashed zoom lines; nothing is drawn twice

insights.structure: Three panels in a row nest model, stack and block from right to left, each panel tinted differently and linked to the box it expands by dashed diagonal zoom lines.
insights.data: The input series appears once, as a real teal line plot across the top right with lookback and forecast horizons marked by double-headed arrows and a red vertical split, and its two horizons drop as labelled arrows into the model panel.

insights.flow: Inside each panel data runs top to bottom with right-angle bends; the reader enters at the top-right plot and descends levels by following the zoom lines leftward.

inside each panel data runs top to bottom: Stack 1, 2, ..., M in the model; Block 1, 2, ..., K in the stack; FC Stack, two FC heads, g^b and g^f in the block
forecast arrows from every block converge on one plus circle at the stack's right (Stack forecast), and from every stack on one plus circle at the model's right (Global forecast)
a column of minus circles down the stack panel's left spine subtracts each block's backcast from its input, the residual passing to the next block and out as 'Stack residual (to next stack)'

the input series is a real teal line plot across the top right, its Lookback Period and Forecast Period marked by double-headed arrows split by a red vertical line, dropping into the model as 'Lookback window'

channels.colour: panel and box tint = nesting level (yellow model, orange stack, blue block), each box filled with the tint of the panel that opens it; teal = the data series; red line = lookback/forecast split
channels.shape: rounded boxes = layers or sub-models; circles with minus / plus = residual subtraction / forecast summation
channels.line: solid black arrows = data flow; dashed coloured diagonals = zoom ties
channels.frame: rounded tinted panel = one level of the hierarchy

quality.strengths: the doubly residual idea is geometry: minus circles stack down one spine and forecast arrows converge on one plus on the other side; the three-level hierarchy is tied by matching tints and dashed zoom lines; the input is a real series with its two horizons marked
quality.weaknesses: the block panel puts g^b(theta^b) and g^f(theta^f) as formulas inside boxes; reading order is right to left across panels while each panel reads top to bottom; the forecast lines from Stack 2 and Stack M bend diagonally into the plus

figures.lesson: A three-level hierarchy (model > stack > block) can be drawn as three side-by-side panels whose child boxes take the tint of the next panel and are tied to it by dashed zoom lines, so the reader can descend levels without nested boxes.

the red devil Adversary at far left receives a dashed w from the server and a fat blue arrow carrying w1 ... wN, drawn beside the first client

figures.title: NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields for View Synthesis

insights.flow: Left to right with curved blue arrows linking a sample point to the input tuple, the network to the output tuple, and each ray's curve to its loss term.

relations.form: four unboxed columns each headed by a two-line title and lettered (a)-(d) below, read left to right
(a) and (b) draw the operation on the actual scene: rays through a dotted bounding box of the Lego bulldozer with two real image planes, sample points as dots on the rays
a curved blue arrow lifts one sample point to the tuple (x,y,z,theta,phi), through the three-bar network F_Theta, to (RGB sigma), and down onto the same point in (b)
in (d) each rendered pixel swatch sits inside a squared-norm bar beside 'g.t.', one row per ray, tied by a curved arrow from that ray's curve in (c)
Ray 1 and Ray 2 run as two stacked rows through (c) and (d), each with its own density curve and its own loss term

channels.colour: the yellow-to-red gradient means predicted colour/density consistently: on sample points in (b), on the curves in (c) and on the pixel swatches in (d); blue = the network and its connecting arrows; red = rays
channels.shape: dots = sample points, three bars = the MLP, curves = density along ray distance, swatches in norm bars = rendered pixels
channels.line: solid red arrows = camera rays; curved blue arrows = 'feeds' links between stages
channels.frame: no frames; columns separated by whitespace and lettered captions

quality.weaknesses: The network F_Theta, though central, is a tiny three-bar glyph floating between (a) and (b); the curved arrows from points to tuples are short but leave the main left-to-right reading for an arc above the scene.

figures.lesson: Draw the radiance-field step inside a wireframe scene cube with real image planes and red rays carrying sample dots, and carry two named rays as parallel lanes into the density plots and the loss so the reader can follow one pixel end to end.

inputs on the left, MLPs in the middle, outputs (RGB, sigma, beta) on the right, all on straight horizontal arrows

figures.lesson: Show high-order connectivity by drawing the bipartite graph once as two columns (users blue, items grey) and once unrolled as a tree rooted at the target user, with nested shaded ellipses marking hop distance l = 1, 2, 3.

figures.title: nnU-Net: Self-adapting Framework for U-Net-Based Medical Image Segmentation

taxonomy.task: 3D medical image segmentation (U-Net cascade)

arrangement.units: two grey tinted background panels, 'stage 1' (wide) and 'stage 2', titled at top-left
arrangement.inputs_as: a schematic grey plane (no real scan)
arrangement.shared: none: each stage has its own bow-tie U-Net glyph

figures.title: Null-text Inversion for Editing Real Images using Guided Diffusion Models

taxonomy.task: inverting a real image into a text-guided diffusion model for editing, by optimising the unconditional (null-text) embedding per timestep around a DDIM-inversion pivot

arrangement.units: two panels stacked under centred titles and split by a dashed rule (whole-trajectory inversion above, one-step null-text optimisation below), plus an unframed column of three photos at the right

arrangement.losses_at: the red dashed L_MSE arrow at the right of the bottom panel, from the step output z-bar_{t-1} up to the pivot z*_{t-1}

insights.data: Latents are dots along a trajectory, the caption and the empty null-text are quoted, and the input and its reconstructions are real photos.
insights.emphasis: Red is reserved for what is optimised: the circular tuning arrow around the null-text embedding and the dashed L_MSE arrow.
insights.flow: The top panel runs right to left along the DDIM inversion pivots, then the tuned trajectory steps back left to right below it on dashed grey arrows; the bottom panel runs left to right into a weighted sum and up to the pivot.
insights.avoid: The bottom panel is tied to the top only by shared symbols (z-bar_t, z*_{t-1}), and the photo column is not connected to either panel by any line.

core.what: the DDIM inversion trajectory unrolled as a row of dark dots z*_T..z*_0 with the tuned trajectory z-bar as lighter dots stepping below it, each tuned step tied up to its pivot

relations.form: a row of pivot dots joined by solid leftward arrows with ellipses for the middle steps, and a second row of lighter dots below on dashed arrows

the caption branch and the null-text branch each pass through a DM hourglass; their outputs are scaled by w and 1-w at circled x signs and meet at one + circle
the lower panel expands one step t of the upper trajectory, separated by a dashed rule and linked only by the shared symbols
Input Image, Initial Inversion and Final Inversion photos stacked in one right-hand column at the same size

channels.colour: red = optimised (the tuning arrow and the MSE loss); dark vs light grey dots = pivot trajectory vs tuned trajectory; grey = the frozen diffusion model; one meaning each
channels.shape: dots = latents, grey hourglass = the diffusion model, circles = operators, quoted text = text conditions
channels.line: solid arrows = DDIM inversion and forward computation; grey dashed arrows = the tuned trajectory; red dashed arrow = the loss; red circular arrow = per-step tuning
channels.frame: no frames; a dashed horizontal rule separates the two panels

quality.strengths: The pivot trajectory and the tuned trajectory are drawn as two rows of dots, so what is compared is visible; red is reserved for the one optimised variable and its loss; the two DM copies are identical silhouettes, so the classifier-free-guidance pair reads at a glance; the compared photos (input, initial, final inversion) are drawn at the same size.
quality.weaknesses: The tuned trajectory zig-zags down and back with dashed arrows of mixed directions; the one-step panel is tied to the trajectory only by symbols, not by a callout or tint; the photo column is unconnected to either panel; only one of the T pivot links is labelled 'Pivotal tuning'.

figures.lesson: Mark the only optimised variable with a circular red 'tuning' arrow around it, and draw its loss as a red dashed arrow to the target it is pulled toward, leaving everything frozen in grey and black.

figures.title: Navigation World Models

taxonomy.task: visual navigation planning by rolling out a conditional diffusion world model and scoring imagined trajectories against a goal image

arrangement.units: three unframed panels split by dashed rules: (a) model, (c) imagined trajectories in a 2 x 4 image grid, (b) planning across the full bottom width in two frame rows plus a goal column
arrangement.inputs_as: real fisheye photos with a yellow action arrow painted on the first frame; the action vector (Δx, Δy, Δφ, k) as a typeset label entering the model from above; the goal as a real photo at the right
arrangement.losses_at: no training objective is drawn; the planning score sits at the right end of each rollout row in (b), between that row's last frame and the goal photo
arrangement.shared: the goal photo is drawn once and wired up to the top row's Score box and down to the bottom row's

insights.structure: A small model panel and a result grid share the top row; the full-width bottom panel stacks two candidate rollouts as rows of five frames and ends both at one goal photo in a right-hand column.
insights.data: Every state is a real fisheye frame tagged input / gen. (t=k) / Goal; candidate actions are yellow arrows painted on the input frame, so each row's plan is visible on its own first image.
insights.emphasis: Salience comes from area and the two Score outlines: the planning panel takes the bottom half, and green vs red outlines say which rollout wins.
insights.flow: Each row reads left to right through time; short elbow and curved black arrows take the last generated frame and the goal into each Score box; the model panel has three straight arrows (action from above, input from the left, output to the right).
insights.avoid: The model itself is a bare labelled trapezoid while a results grid (c) takes the same area as it; the Score boxes carry a small list-with-arrow icon whose meaning is not decodable from the figure.

core.what: two candidate trajectories are two aligned rows of generated frames, both ending at one goal photo where a green and a red Score box rank them

relations.form: two identical rows of five equal frames stacked in panel (b), each starting from the same input photo with a different yellow action arrow
each row unrolls the rollout in time as columns tagged gen. (t=4), (t=8), (t=12), (t=16)
each row's last frame and the goal photo meet in that row's Score box at the right edge, the goal sitting between the two boxes and wired up and down
in panel (a) the action and time vector enters the trapezoid by a curved arrow from above while the stacked input photo enters from the left

channels.colour: yellow = action trajectory painted on a frame; green vs red Score outline = selected vs rejected rollout; light-blue tag = given input (input, Goal), grey tag = generated frame; the model's teal outline carries no other use
channels.shape: trapezoid = the model, photo = a state, rectangle with list icon = scoring
channels.line: one style: thin black arrows for data flow; dashed black rules only separate panels
channels.frame: no frames; panels are split by dashed rules

quality.strengths: The planning comparison is drawn as geometry: two equal rollout rows side by side in time, each closed by a score against one shared goal photo; every state is a real frame and the candidate action is painted on the input, so what is compared (last frame vs goal) is visible; tag colour separates given from generated frames; arrows are short.
quality.weaknesses: The model panel (a) is a black-box trapezoid and the result grid (c) takes as much area as it; the score glyph (a list with a curved arrow) is not explained; the green / red outlines are the only cue for which rollout is kept; dashed panel rules use the same black as the data arrows.

figures.lesson: Show planning with a world model as candidate rollouts in aligned rows of generated frames, each ending in a score box against one shared goal image, with the candidate's action drawn as an arrow on its first frame.

figures.title: Octo: An Open-Source Generalist Robot Policy

insights.emphasis: The finetuning row repeats the pretraining row with every unchanged column faded to a ghost, leaving only dashed, saturated new observation tokens, the new action-space readout and a 'New Action Head', each named by a callout box.

insights.avoid: The transformer bar is drawn on top of the column groups and covers their middles, so the token columns look cut in half rather than passing through the model.

core.what: pre-training and finetuning drawn as two stacked rows of the same token sequence crossed by one Octo Transformer bar, the finetuning row greying out unused groups and adding dashed new observation, action-space and head elements

relations.form: two identical rows split by a thin grey rule and labelled 'Pre-Training' (up arrow) and 'Finetuning' (down arrow); the lower row fades unchanged token groups and outlines the new ones in dashed lines

channels.colour: green = task/language tokens, blue = observation tokens, purple = readout tokens and action heads; fade (low opacity) = untouched in finetuning
channels.shape: rounded pills = tokens, tall tinted columns = token groups, long bar = the transformer, trapezoid = CNN, box = encoder/head

channels.frame: rounded grey frames hold the two tokenizer panels; the two right-hand rows are unframed

quality.strengths: The finetuning claim is visible as geometry: the same row is repeated below with faded unused groups and dashed new slots, so what is reused and what is added can be read without text; token colours carry one meaning each and are taught once in the tokenizer panels; inputs are real data (quoted words, a patched photo).
quality.weaknesses: The New Observation callout routes with two long elbowed lines to slots far apart; the transformer bar overlaps and hides the middle of every token column, so the input/output token correspondence is implicit; the octopus logo is decoration inside the main block.

figures.lesson: Show finetuning as a copy of the pretraining row with everything unchanged faded to a ghost, so only the new observation tokens, action space and head - dashed and saturated, each with a callout - stand out.

figures.title: Once-for-All: Train One Network and Specialize it for Efficient Deployment

taxonomy.task: elastic-width supernet training (progressive shrinking)
taxonomy.note: family other = neural architecture search / once-for-all supernet; architecture other = weight-sharing elastic supernetwork

arrangement.units: three dotted rectangles, each a stage, with nested smaller dotted rectangles inside later stages; captions below each; connectors are rounded number boxes between stages
arrangement.inputs_as: the full-width channel stack in the first dotted box
arrangement.shared: the same four coloured channel sheets appear in every stage

insights.structure: Three dotted-rectangle stages left to right, each holding a vertical stack of channel sheets with a caption below ('train with full width', 'progressively shrink the width' twice); between stages a rounded black-outlined column of channel-importance numbers with arrows labelled 'channel sorting' and 'reorg.'.
insights.data: Channels are flat coloured parallelograms (grey, orange, green, blue) that keep their colour as they are re-ordered between stages; importance scores are printed decimals; nested smaller dotted rectangles mark each sub-network's channel subset.
insights.emphasis: The same coloured sheets visibly change order after sorting, and each nested dotted box has its own output arrow O1, O2, O3 at its lower right, so the shrinking sub-networks read as nested.
insights.flow: Strictly left to right along straight black arrows, from full width through the importance column to each shrunken stage; the last stage ends with a trailing 'channel sorting' arrow.
insights.avoid: The nested dotted rectangles in the third stage are very close together and their O1/O2/O3 taps overlap, making it hard to tell which box each output belongs to.

core.what: three dotted-rectangle stages left to right, each a stack of coloured channel sheets, with channel-importance number columns between them and nested dotted boxes marking ever-smaller sub-networks

relations.form: three dotted rectangles in a row, captioned 'train with full width', then 'progressively shrink the width' twice, joined by arrows labelled 'channel sorting' and 'reorg.'
the sort - reorganise - shrink step is drawn twice in sequence, with a trailing 'channel sorting' arrow out of the last stage implying it continues
nested smaller dotted rectangles inside later stages enclose the top channels of each sub-network, each with its own output arrow O1, O2, O3
four coloured parallelogram sheets stand for channels and keep their colour while their order changes after sorting, so the reordering is seen on the channels themselves
between stages a rounded black-outlined column of importance scores (0.02, 0.15, 0.85, 0.63, then 0.82, 0.11, 0.46) sits on the main horizontal arrow, between 'channel sorting' and 'reorg.'

channels.colour: colour = channel identity (grey, orange, green, blue), held constant across stages so movement is traceable
channels.shape: parallelogram = a channel; rounded box of numbers = importance scores
channels.line: solid black arrows = process steps and outputs O_i
channels.frame: dotted rectangle = one (sub-)network width; nesting = smaller width shares weights with the larger

quality.strengths: Colour has one meaning, channel identity, so the effect of sorting is visible as the same sheets changing order; nested dotted boxes make weight sharing between widths a containment relation, each with its own output O_i; arrows are short and on one horizontal line.
quality.weaknesses: The importance columns have four scores before the second stage but only three in the second, and which score belongs to which sheet is only inferable by order; captions repeat 'progressively shrink the width' verbatim, and the score columns are drawn in the same black rounded box style a module would get.

figures.lesson: Show elastic width as the same coloured channel sheets re-sorted between stages by a printed column of importance scores, with nested dotted boxes marking each sub-network's channel subset and its own output tap.

figures.title: One for All: Towards Training One Graph Model for All Classification Tasks

arrangement.units: three unframed rows tinted by domain plus a fourth 'More data and tasks.' row of ellipses, crossed by two tall boxes spanning all rows; a ruler under the figure names the columns

insights.emphasis: The shared models stand out by height and label size; the prompt node is the only orange element.
insights.flow: Left to right through seven columns named on a bottom ruler; curly braces gather each row, curved tinted arrows converge on and fan out from the shared boxes, and grey dashed arrows continue a fourth 'more data' row.
insights.avoid: Do not colour connective glyphs (here the commas) with colours that look like a code but mean nothing.

core.what: one LLM box and one 'Single GNN' box each span all three domain rows, the per-domain arrows fanning into and out of them

relations.form: two tall boxes, each exactly as tall as the three domain rows it serves
three domain rows stacked, each in its own tint from input box to prediction box, a fourth row of grey dashed arrows for further data
seven columns left to right, named by a tick-separated ruler along the bottom
the task prompt is drawn on each feature graph: an orange prompt node joined by dashed lines to nodes of the graph, with the task questions in tinted boxes beside it

Inputs carry real domain imagery (molecule render, citation network of documents).
quality.weaknesses: The prompt node, the method's novelty, is a small orange dot among large domain panels, so space follows the domains rather than the contribution. Curly braces on both sides of every column plus curved fan-in and fan-out arrows add much ink. The commas between input and description boxes are coloured orange, blue and green, unrelated to the row colours. The column names live in a separate ruler band below the figure.

figures.title: Tracking Everything Everywhere All at Once

taxonomy.task: dense long-range motion estimation (a trajectory for every pixel of a video)

arrangement.units: (a) wide unframed panel: frame i photo + local volume L_i at left, cloud-shaped canonical volume G at centre, frame j + L_j at right; (b) narrow panel right of a vertical dashed rule: sigma plot over ray samples and composite / project block arrows
arrangement.inputs_as: real video frames (a girl on a swing) as tilted photos with translucent local volumes behind them; the query pixel is an orange dot
arrangement.shared: the canonical volume G is drawn once in the centre and both frames' bijection curves end at its single point u

insights.structure: Panel (a) mirrors frame i (left) and frame j (right) around the canonical volume G in the centre, so the two frames visibly meet only through G; panel (b), behind a vertical dashed rule, unpacks how a query pixel's ray samples become a 2D location.
insights.data: Frames are real photos, local volumes translucent photo cubes and the canonical volume a cloud filled with a faded frame; the tracked point is drawn as a coloured dot at every stage (orange p_i, red x_i / u / x_j, grey ray samples, purple p-hat_j).
insights.emphasis: The canonical volume is the largest, central element and every mapping curve ends at its single red point u; the blue bijection boxes are the most saturated marks.
insights.flow: Left to right: a black ray through p_i into L_i, a blue double-headed curve via T_i to u, another via T_j to x_j in L_j; F_theta hangs above u on a green curve. In (b) samples drop by short down arrows from x_i^k to x_j^k, then block arrows composite and project to p-hat_j.
insights.avoid: Panel (b)'s light-blue 'Project' block arrow is close in hue to the blue bijection boxes of (a), and the ray samples are redrawn in (b) as an abstract row instead of being tied to the ray in (a).

core.what: one tracked point's mapping drawn on the 3D structure itself: a ray of sample dots through frame i's translucent local volume, a double-headed blue curve (T_i) to point u in the cloud-shaped canonical volume, and another (T_j) to x_j in frame j's volume, the two frames mirrored on either side of G

relations.form: frame i with L_i on the left and frame j with L_j on the right face each other across the canonical volume, which they meet only through the shared point u
the green F_theta box above G is reached by a single green curve from u and emits (c, sigma) to its right as text

panel (b) reads top to bottom then right: sigma plot over samples x_i^1..x_i^K, short down arrows to x_j^1..x_j^K, then grey 'Alpha composite' block arrow to x-hat_j and light-blue 'Project' block arrow to the purple p-hat_j
panel (a) (the representation) and panel (b) (computing 2D motion) side by side, separated by a vertical dashed rule, (b) narrow

channels.colour: blue fill = the bijections T_i, T_j; green = the MLP F_theta and its query curve; dot colour = point role (orange query p_i, red mapped location, grey other ray samples, purple predicted p-hat_j); in (b) block-arrow colour = operation, keyed below (grey alpha composite, light-blue project) - the light blue nearly repeats the bijection blue
channels.shape: square box = learned function; translucent photo cube = a frame's local volume; cloud = canonical volume; tilted photo = video frame; dot = point; thick block arrow = rendering operation in (b)
channels.line: double-headed blue curves = invertible mappings; single-headed green curve = querying F_theta; straight black line with arrowhead = camera ray; thin black arrows in (b) = per-sample mapping
channels.frame: vertical dashed rule = panel split; dashed cube edges = local volumes; no container boxes

quality.strengths: The representation is drawn as structure - per-frame volumes and the canonical cloud filled with the real scene - and the tracked point is drawn at every stage (p_i, ray samples, x_i, u, x_j, p-hat_j), so the correspondence reads as geometry; frames i and j mirror around G, making 'two frames meet only through the canonical volume' visible without labels; the mapping curves are short and labelled by boxes at their midpoints.
quality.weaknesses: Panel (b) redraws the ray samples as an abstract row under a sigma plot instead of on the ray in (a), so x_i^k must be matched across panels by symbol; the light-blue 'Project' arrow in (b) nearly repeats the bijection blue of (a); F_theta's (c, sigma) output is text above G with no visible link to the sigma plot in (b) that uses it.

figures.lesson: Show a correspondence method by drawing one point's round trip on real data - query pixel, ray samples in frame i's local volume, the shared canonical point u, and its landing point in frame j - with the two mappings as labelled double-headed curves meeting at the shared centre.

the modality-token pair q_m enters from a top-left strip via a line labelled 'select & concatenate' and stacks above the feature column x_m with a '+'
three identical salmon Projection Expert boxes stacked inside the projection panel, fanned from one arrow and gathered into one circled-cross node

quality.strengths: Sharing is geometry (one tall encoder bar spanning all tokenizer rows); the contribution is the largest panel; the token columns q_m and x_m and the routing weights are drawn as data between their makers and the combination node; arrows are short, straight and horizontal on one axis; a top legend keys icons.
quality.weaknesses: Salmon marks both modality tokens and experts and light blue marks both tokenizers and features; the projection module and LLM carry a combined flame/snowflake mark that does not say which part is trained when; the 'select & concatenate' line runs across the top over the encoder from a strip far to the left; the dropped-token arrow is a faint curve below the panel.

figures.title: OpenVLA: An Open-Source Vision-Language-Action Model

bottom to top inside the dashed OpenVLA container: encoders (1), projector (2), Llama 2 7B (3), purple action pills, Action De-Tokenizer, then out to the right as a bracketed [dx; dtheta; dGrip] vector and a robot arm photo
DinoV2 (yellow) and SigLIP (blue) share a dashed sub-container, fed by one forked line from the input photo, and the MLP projector's yellow-to-blue gradient carries both their colours

channels.colour: yellow = DinoV2, blue = SigLIP, yellow-to-blue gradient = their fused features and vision tokens, green = text/tokenizer, purple = action tokens and de-tokenizer, grey = the LLM
channels.shape: pills = tokens, rounded boxes = modules, wide bar = the LLM, circled numbers 1-3 = component tags
channels.line: one style of thin grey arrows for all data flow

quality.weaknesses: The image and instruction lines take long elbowed routes down and around under the encoders and the tokenizer instead of entering directly; the action output leaves the top-right of the de-tokenizer and turns twice; the frozen/trained status of the parts is not shown.

figures.lesson: Tint each token row with the colour of what produced it - a yellow-to-blue gradient for tokens fused from two vision encoders, green for text, purple for actions - and end at a bracketed Δx/Δθ/ΔGrip vector above the robot it drives.

figures.title: Simple Open-Vocabulary Object Detection with Vision Transformers

taxonomy.task: open-vocabulary object detection

arrangement.units: two rounded light-grey-outlined frames, one per training stage, each titled in large type above
arrangement.inputs_as: quoted text strings in typewriter font above, patch-gridded photos below, at each frame's left edge
arrangement.losses_at: right end of each frame as a bold-italic text note (and a +/- matrix in the left frame)
arrangement.shared: text and vision encoders redrawn in identical positions in both frames

insights.structure: Two rounded grey-outlined frames side by side, each titled above ('Image-level contrastive pre-training', 'Transfer to open-vocabulary detection'); in both, a Text Transformer encoder sits above a Vision Transformer encoder in the same position, and the right frame adds two rotated orange heads beside the vision tokens.
insights.data: Text inputs are typewriter-font quoted strings, images are photos with a white patch grid; embeddings are small squares (lilac text, green image, white box); the left loss is a small +/- grid with green plus on the diagonal; detection outputs are rows of printed class scores with the chosen quoted class and rows of (x, y, w, h) tuples.
insights.emphasis: The added detection parts (Linear projection, MLP head, token pooling) are the only orange elements, and the closing bold-italic loss phrases contrast 'images in a batch' with 'objects in an image'.
insights.flow: Each frame reads left to right from inputs through encoders to outputs; in the right frame text query embeddings drop down as column headers of the score table and output rows curve into the set prediction loss note.
insights.avoid: The right frame's many thin curved lines from the pink vision-token tabs to the heads cross and bunch together, and the score digits are tiny.

core.what: two framed panels side by side, contrastive image-level pre-training then open-vocabulary detection transfer, with the text and vision encoders redrawn in the same positions so the added heads and changed objective stand out

relations.form: two rounded grey frames left to right, each titled above, the second reusing the identical Text Transformer encoder above Vision Transformer encoder
left panel: the text embedding feeds the columns and the image embedding the rows of a small +/- matrix, labelled 'contrastive loss over images in a batch'
right panel: lilac query embeddings form the columns of a score table whose rows are per-token green object image embeddings, with predicted class labels at each row's end
in the right panel each vision output token fans to both a rotated 'Linear projection' head (class embeddings) and a rotated 'MLP head' (boxes), giving one class row and one box row per token
inputs drawn as data: quoted typewriter strings for text and patch-gridded photos (a bird; giraffes) for images

channels.colour: lilac = text/query embeddings, green = object image embeddings, white = box embeddings (keyed in the right panel's legend), orange = new or pooling heads, grey = encoders; class-name string colours (green/red) mark which query is meant
channels.shape: small squares = embeddings, rounded boxes = encoders/heads, matrix of numbers or +/- = the compared scores
channels.line: grey arrows for all data flow; one long curved arrow per panel points from the predictions to a bold-italic loss note
channels.frame: rounded grey frame = one training stage

quality.strengths: The transfer story is visible by position: identical encoders in identical places in both stages, so the change from a pooled image embedding to per-token heads is the only thing that moves; the compared representations (text and image embeddings) are drawn as squares on the axes of the score matrices; the loss notes contrast 'images in a batch' with 'objects in an image'.
quality.weaknesses: Orange is used both for the pooling+projection block of stage 1 and the two new heads of stage 2 although they play different roles; the per-token fan-out lines from the vision encoder to the two heads converge and cross at the rotated heads; long curved arrows to the loss notes stand in for the loss itself.

figures.lesson: Make open-vocabulary detection readable by turning text embeddings into the column headers of a per-box score table, printing the actual scores and the chosen class string in each row next to a parallel row of (x, y, w, h) box tuples.

figures.title: Recommendation as Language Processing (RLP): A Unified Pretrain, Personalized Prompt & Predict Paradigm (P5)

taxonomy.task: unified multitask recommendation via prompts

arrangement.units: one hub composition; prompt and answer boxes are pastel rounded rectangles; a dashed horizontal rule splits pretraining tasks (above) from the zero-shot task (below), each labelled in italic
arrangement.inputs_as: real prompt text in task-tinted rounded boxes with bold task titles above
arrangement.shared: the single P5 hub serves all tasks
