insights.data: Prompts are full real prompt text with user and item IDs written out in serif, inside rounded boxes tinted one pastel per task; answers ('1581', '5.0', 'broke immediately') sit in small boxes of the matching tint.
insights.emphasis: The model is the hub where every curve converges, set in the largest bold italic text inside the only thick-outlined box.
insights.flow: Left to right: smooth black curves converge from every prompt into the hub and fan out to every answer; colour, not lines, pairs each prompt with its answer.
insights.avoid: All curves are identical black and cross near the hub, so line identity is lost and the reader must rely on colour to pair prompts and answers; the model's internals are not shown at all.

core.what: one central P5 hub box joined by curved lines to six task prompt boxes stacked down the left and their answer boxes stacked down the right, showing one model serving every task

relations.form: a single heavy-outlined grey 'P5' box in the centre receives a curved line from every prompt and sends one to every answer
each prompt on the left and its answer on the right share one pastel tint (orange sequential, pink rating, blue explanation, green summarization, yellow direct, lilac zero-shot)
a dashed horizontal rule near the bottom separates five multi-task pretraining prompts above from one zero-shot new-product prompt below, each labelled in italic
prompts and answers are drawn as real text with user and item IDs written out, e.g. a purchase history '4110 -> 4467 -> 4468 -> 4472' answered by '1581'

channels.colour: pastel tint = task family, shared by a prompt and its answer
channels.shape: large rounded boxes = prompts, small rounded boxes = answers, heavy square box = the model
channels.line: curved black lines = input to and output from the hub; dashed rule = pretraining vs zero-shot split
channels.frame: none beyond the boxes

quality.strengths: Colour has one meaning (task) and links each prompt to its answer across the hub, and the data are shown as real prompts, which makes the text-to-text unification concrete; the zero-shot case is set apart by a dashed rule and labelled.
quality.weaknesses: Every line converges on one point of the hub so the twelve curves bundle and fan out like a starburst and none can be followed by position alone; the model is an empty labelled box with nothing inside; the long prompt texts take most of the area while the right side is mostly blank.

figures.lesson: Make the teaser a hub: each task's real prompt text in a box tinted with its own colour on the left, its answer in a small box of the same tint on the right, so colour pairs inputs with outputs through the single model in the middle.

figures.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention

taxonomy.task: KV-cache memory management for LLM serving

arrangement.units: three unframed tables side by side, each titled above: logical blocks grid, block table, physical blocks grid
arrangement.inputs_as: a circle labelled 'Request A' with the quoted prompt and output words beside it, at the top left
arrangement.shared: the block table in the middle is the only link between the grids; arrows enter it from logical rows and fan out from it to physical rows

insights.structure: A short logical grid on the left and a tall physical grid on the right flank a small block table, and arrows through the table land on non-adjacent physical rows.
insights.data: Real prompt words (italic) fill the KV cells, one word per cell, so the same words can be found again in the scattered physical blocks.
insights.emphasis: Red 'Logical' and 'Physical' title words and darker yellow-orange cells for newly generated tokens make the two address spaces and the growth step stand out.
insights.flow: Start at the request top-left, read the logical grid, pass through the block table, then follow the arrows right to the physical rows; circled numerals give step order.
insights.avoid: The long thin arrows from the block table cross each other on the way to the physical grid, and the circled numerals on them are too small to read at print size.

core.what: a logical KV-block grid on the left and a taller physical KV-block grid on the right flank a small block table, and arrows through the table land on non-adjacent physical rows filled with the same words

relations.form: both grids are tables of 4-slot blocks filled with the real prompt words ('Four score and seven', 'years ago our fathers', 'brought'), one word per cell
arrows run from each logical block row into the block table and out to its physical block (logical 0 -> physical 7, 1 -> 1, 2 -> 3), so the scattered placement is seen by where the arrows land
small circled step numbers on cells, table entries and arrows mark the order of allocation, and '# filled' entries show updates like 3 -> 4
the request is a circle 'Request A' at top left with its quoted prompt and outputs, whose words reappear in the grids below

channels.colour: pale yellow = filled KV slot from the prompt, darker yellow-orange = newly generated token; red title words separate 'Logical' from 'Physical'
channels.shape: grid of cells = KV blocks, small two-column table = block table, circle = request
channels.line: thin black arrows = address mapping through the block table
channels.frame: none; the three tables stand unframed side by side, titled above

quality.strengths: The method is drawn on its own data structure: the same words can be found in contiguous logical blocks and in scattered physical blocks, so non-contiguous paging is visible as geometry; the block table sits exactly between the two address spaces it maps; newly generated tokens are distinguished by one tint.
quality.weaknesses: The mapping arrows from the table to physical blocks 1, 3 and 7 are long diagonals that cross each other; circled step numbers are tiny and repeated on cells, table and arrows, making the order hard to read at print size; red is used only on two title words.

figures.lesson: Show an indirection (virtual-to-physical mapping) as two grids of the same row height on either side of a small lookup table, writing the same real words into matching cells so the reader can check the mapping by content.

figures.title: PAL: Program-aided Language Models

taxonomy.task: arithmetic and symbolic reasoning by generating interleaved reasoning and Python code that an interpreter executes
taxonomy.note: family other = LLM prompting / in-context reasoning with tool execution (no agent loop or environment)

arrangement.units: two columns, prior method left and ours right, each an Input frame over a Model Output frame, frames tagged by pill labels on their top edge
arrangement.inputs_as: the full quoted few-shot example and test question (a word problem) inside the Input frame
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; correctness is a red cross or green tick at the bottom of each output frame
arrangement.shared: the same exemplar question and the same test question are repeated verbatim in both columns

insights.structure: Two identical column skeletons - Input frame over Model Output frame - side by side, prior method left, ours right.
insights.data: Everything is real text: the word problems, the generated reasoning and the generated Python lines, with the interpreter's output '74' printed on a black terminal band.
insights.emphasis: Highlight colours carry the difference: the left column is uniformly cyan, the right alternates cyan sentences with pink monospace code, ending in a black interpreter band and a green tick.
insights.flow: No arrows: reading runs top to bottom within each column (input, then output) and left to right between methods.
insights.avoid: The interpreter that does the arithmetic is not drawn as a component, only as a terminal snippet in the output; when an external executor is the contribution, give it a box.

core.what: chain-of-thought and PAL drawn as two identical Input-over-Output columns side by side on the same question, ours on the right

relations.form: two columns with the same frame skeleton and the same quoted questions, prior method left titled with its citation, ours right titled '(this work)', a red cross and a green tick at the bottom
within each column an Input frame sits above a Model Output frame, joined by position only
in the PAL column each cyan natural-language sentence is immediately followed by the pink code line that implements it, alternating line by line

channels.colour: highlight colour = kind of generated text: cyan = natural-language reasoning, pink monospace on grey = code, green on black = interpreter run; pill tags: light blue = Input, light green = Model Output; red cross / green tick = wrong / right
channels.shape: only text and frames; the pill tag shape names a frame's role
channels.line: none; no arrows are drawn
channels.frame: a rounded frame = one prompt part (input or model output)

quality.strengths: The comparison is drawn as two identical columns on the same quoted question, ours last, so the only visible difference is the content. One highlight per text kind, keyed in the caption and consistent across both columns, makes the code-vs-prose interleaving visible at a glance. The outputs are real generations with the interpreter's result.
quality.weaknesses: The left Input frame has a large empty band at its top because the two columns' texts differ in length, so the rows do not align. The figure is text only: the Python interpreter, the component that computes the answer, appears only as a black terminal line, not as a step. Green is used for the Output pill, the interpreter text and the correct tick.

figures.lesson: Compare two prompting methods by setting the same few-shot example and test question in identical Input/Output frames side by side, and colour-code the kinds of generated text (natural-language step vs code vs interpreter run) with one highlight each.

figures.title: Pangu-Weather: A 3D High-Resolution System for Fast and Accurate Global Weather Forecast

taxonomy.task: global medium-range weather forecasting
taxonomy.note: modality = gridded atmospheric fields (3-D pressure-level and 2-D surface variables)

arrangement.units: one composition; two thin blue-outlined square containers (Encoder, Decoder) each holding two grey layer boxes, labelled in bold below
arrangement.inputs_as: colormapped field renders (3-D cubes and flat maps) with tensor sizes underneath
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Mirror-symmetric left to right: input fields and patch tokens on the far left, two thin blue-outlined square containers 'Encoder' and 'Decoder' in the middle each holding two grey layer boxes stacked vertically, then patch tokens and output fields mirrored on the far right, under a bold centred title.
insights.data: Upper-air variables are three rendered 3-D cubes with colormapped faces, surface variables three flat colormapped maps; tokens are columns of five small colormapped cubes; each layer box states block name with repeat count and tensor size in math.
insights.emphasis: Colour is spent on the real data fields while the network stays grey, and identical renderings on both sides make 'field in, same field out' visible; the model name is the large bold title.
insights.flow: Thick orange arrows run left to right, merging the two input rows into Layer 1 and splitting out of Layer 4; dotted orange vertical arrows show down-sampling in the encoder and up-sampling in the decoder.
insights.avoid: The two-level U is drawn inside two separate boxes, so the skip from Layer 1 to Layer 4 looks like an ordinary forward arrow rather than a skip connection.

core.what: a mirror-symmetric left-to-right pipeline: upper-air and surface fields are patch-embedded and merged into a two-level encoder, then a two-level decoder whose output is split and patch-recovered into the same two field sets

relations.form: left to right on thick orange arrows: input fields, patch tokens, Encoder, Decoder, patch tokens, output fields, mirrored about the centre
the upper-air (top) and surface (bottom) token columns converge with orange arrows labelled 'merge' onto Layer 1, and leave Layer 4 by two diverging arrows labelled 'split'
upper-air variables (three 3-D cubes) and surface variables (three flat maps) run as two stacked rows at both ends, each with its own patch embedding/recovery size

inside two blue-outlined squares, Layer 1 over Layer 2 (encoder) and Layer 4 over Layer 3 (decoder), linked by dotted orange down-sampling and up-sampling arrows and horizontal skip arrows at each level
inputs, tokens and outputs are drawn as colormapped renders of the actual atmospheric fields with tensor sizes under each

channels.colour: orange = all data-flow arrows; colormapped renders = data; grey fill = layer boxes
channels.shape: 3-D cube = upper-air field, flat map = surface field, small cubes in a column = patch tokens, grey box = a layer
channels.line: solid orange = data flow and skip, dotted orange = down/up-sampling
channels.frame: thin blue square = Encoder or Decoder group

quality.strengths: The data are drawn as data (colour-mapped field cubes and maps with their tensor sizes), the mirror layout makes input and output symmetric so the encoder-decoder reads at a glance, and line style separates resampling (dotted) from data flow (solid).
quality.weaknesses: The Earth-Specific Block, the paper's contribution, is a text label inside plain grey boxes with nothing drawn of its 3-D attention; the field renders take most of the area while the layers are small; the merge/split arrows are long diagonals across empty space.

figures.lesson: Mirror the input and output fields on both sides with identical renderings (3-D cubes for pressure-level variables, flat maps for surface ones) and their tensor sizes underneath, so the model reads as field in, same field out, with a compact grey network between.

figures.title: Scaling Autoregressive Models for Content-Rich Text-to-Image Generation

taxonomy.task: autoregressive text-to-image generation over image tokens

arrangement.units: One composition: orange encoder box (lower left), blue decoder box (centre, raised) and a green rounded ViT-VQGAN container (right) holding the tokenizer and detokenizer; no outer frames.
arrangement.inputs_as: the plain-text sentence 'Two dogs running in a field' under orange token bars at the bottom left, and a real photo at the bottom right feeding the tokenizer
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the Train dashed path from the tokenizer to the decoder's last input token stands in for teacher forcing
arrangement.shared: the same dog photo appears as input below and output above the ViT-VQGAN container

insights.structure: A small encoder at lower left feeds a large decoder in the middle, and a separate green tokenizer container stands at the right with the image above and below it.
insights.data: Text and image tokens are rows of small coloured bars with math labels underneath (t_1..t_N; <sos>, i_1..i_M), the outputs i_1..<eos> are bare labels on arrows above the decoder, and the image is a real photo.
insights.emphasis: Size and position carry importance: the blue decoder is the biggest box and sits highest among the models; the tokenizer is grouped in its own green frame.
insights.flow: Bottom-up arrows into each model, one elbow arrow from encoder to decoder, and two dashed elbow lines labelled Train (tokenizer -> decoder inputs) and Inference (decoder <eos> -> detokenizer) crossing between the decoder and the tokenizer.
insights.avoid: The Train and Inference dashed lines run in opposite directions through the same gap and cross the decoder's output side, so the two modes are easy to confuse; the prompt sentence sits detached below the encoder.

core.what: text tokens enter a small Transformer encoder at lower left, which feeds a large Transformer decoder in the centre that emits image tokens i_1, i_2, ... <eos>, turned into an image by a ViT-VQGAN container at the right

relations.form: left to right: orange text token bars t_1..t_N under the encoder box, an arrow into the side of the blue decoder box, output token labels above the decoder, then a dashed 'Inference' line to the detokenizer and the generated photo above it
the decoder's inputs <sos>, i_1, i_2, ..., i_M are drawn as blue bars below it, shifted by one from its outputs i_1, i_2, i_3, <eos> above, showing autoregressive decoding
a green rounded ViT-VQGAN container at the right stacks Image Tokenizer under Image Detokenizer, with a real photo below as tokenizer input and the same photo above as detokenizer output
two dashed paths leave the side of the ViT-VQGAN container: 'Train' from the tokenizer to the decoder's input tokens, 'Inference' from the decoder's output tokens to the detokenizer

channels.colour: orange = text side (encoder and text tokens), blue = image-token decoder and its tokens, green = ViT-VQGAN, light grey = its two sub-modules
channels.shape: thin vertical bars = tokens, rounded boxes = modules, photos = image data
channels.line: solid = model data flow, dashed = phase-specific connection (Train vs Inference) to the tokenizer
channels.frame: green rounded container = the separately trained ViT-VQGAN

quality.strengths: Colour separates text side, image-token decoder and the image tokenizer, and the decoder is the largest element; tokens are drawn as bars on both the decoder's input and output so the shift-by-one is visible; the image appears as a real photo at both ends of the tokenizer.
quality.weaknesses: The Train dashed line runs from the tokenizer back to only the last input token i_M and the Inference line from only <eos>, so which tokens pass between decoder and VQGAN is ambiguous; the encoder-to-decoder arrow enters with an elbow; the text prompt is a loose sentence under the token bars with no link to them.

figures.lesson: Show a two-part generator by colour-matching each tokenised input row to its model (orange text bars under the encoder, blue image bars under the decoder) and connect the image tokenizer by dashed lines labelled Train and Inference rather than by solid flow.

figures.title: A Time Series is Worth 64 Words: Long-term Forecasting with Transformers

taxonomy.task: long-term multivariate forecasting

arrangement.units: top: one full-width unframed overview row with a caption; bottom: two unframed vertical layer stacks side by side with a grey rounded zoom box between
arrangement.inputs_as: multivariate series drawn as curve strips (top); a pale 'Input Univariate Series' band at the bottom of each stack
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; reconstructed masked patches as grey bars atop the right stack
arrangement.shared: the zoomed Transformer block between the two stacks

insights.data: Series are real curves in thin-framed horizontal strips, green for inputs and blue for outputs; layers are wide flat coloured rectangles (yellow norm/patching and embedding, orange encoder, green head); patches are a row of separated pale-blue vertical bars, masked ones drawn as empty dashed outlines, reconstructions as grey bars.
insights.emphasis: Channel independence is shown by five separate green strips feeding one shared grey 'Transformer Backbone' bar; masking is made visible by dashed empty patches only in the right stack.
insights.flow: Top row reads left to right with hollow block arrows labelled in bold purple ('Channel-independence', 'Concatenate'); the stacks read bottom to top, with a dotted vertical axis at far left listing each layer's tensor shape.

relations.form: top row: the M-channel input block is split by a 'Channel-independence' arrow into five separate green curve strips, each passing by its own arrow through one tall grey Transformer Backbone bar into a blue output strip
the single grey Transformer Backbone bar spans all channel strips, one model applied to every channel

below, two identical vertical layer stacks side by side: supervised (Flatten + Linear Head, output series) on the left and self-supervised (Linear Layer, reconstructed masked patches) on the right, sharing the same norm/patching, projection and encoder layers

each stack reads bottom to top from 'Input Univariate Series' through patching, projection, encoder and head, with a dotted axis at the far left naming each intermediate shape x^(i), x_p^(i), x_d^(i), z^(i), x-hat^(i)
a grey rounded box between the stacks opens the Transformer Encoder (multi-head attention, add & norm, feed forward, n x), tied to the left encoder by orange dashed lines
patches are drawn as a row of pale vertical bars; in the self-supervised stack some are dashed empty outlines for masked patches, reappearing as grey bars at the top as reconstructions

channels.colour: green curves = input series, blue curves = forecast; in the stacks, yellow = normalisation/patching/projection layers, orange = Transformer encoder, green = head layer, pale blue = data bands and patches (green therefore means input series at top and output head below)
channels.shape: curve strips = series, wide flat rectangles = layers, vertical bars = patches, dashed outline = masked patch
channels.line: plain arrows = flow; hollow block arrows = reshaping operations (channel-independence, concatenate); orange dashed = zoom callout; dotted vertical axis = shape annotations
channels.frame: grey rounded box = zoomed encoder detail

quality.strengths: Channel independence is drawn as geometry: one block becomes five strips through one shared bar and back; the two training regimes are identical stacks side by side so only the head and the masked patches differ; data are real curves and patches are drawn as bars, with masked ones as empty dashed outlines.
quality.weaknesses: Green means input series in the overview and the head layer in the stacks; the left shape axis applies only to the left stack; the zoomed Transformer block is a generic re-drawing that takes the central position though it is not the contribution, and the patching step, the core idea, is a single yellow layer.

figures.lesson: Draw patches as a row of separated vertical bars between the patching and embedding layers, show masking by turning some of them into empty dashed outlines, and track each layer's tensor shape on a left-margin axis.

figures.title: PCT: Point Cloud Transformer

taxonomy.task: point cloud classification and segmentation (offset-attention module)

arrangement.units: one unframed chain of tensor slabs and operator circles/boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: a light-blue 3-D slab labelled N x d
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: No containers: one left-to-right chain of tensors and operators with a skip line running along the bottom from the input to the subtraction and the final adder, and a top line carrying the input to the value branch; a two-row legend underneath.
insights.data: Tensors are 3-D slanted slabs with gradient shading, one saturated colour per role (input light blue, query orange, key teal, attention map blue, value magenta, attention feature purple, output navy), with proportions following shape (flat key, largest N x N map) and italic shape labels above.
insights.emphasis: The offset-attention change is carried by the minus circle (input minus attention feature) and a lever-like switch selecting the solid SL path over the dotted SS path; the legend names everything.
insights.flow: Thick black orthogonal arrows run left to right, with the key branch dipping below via a T (transpose) box and the long input skip running along the bottom edge.
insights.avoid: The dotted alternative paths (SS, the dotted arrow after the attention feature) end in open space, and the switch glyph is not self-explanatory without the legend.

core.what: one left-to-right chain of colour-coded tensor slabs and operator circles computing offset attention, with the input carried along the bottom to a subtraction (input minus attention feature) and a final addition

relations.form: left to right: input slab, linear, query and key slabs, matrix-multiply circle, SS/SL normalisation boxes, N x N attention map, multiply with value, attention feature, subtract, LBR, add, output slab
query and transposed key lines converge on one multiply circle; the attention map and the value (brought by a line over the top from the input) converge on a second multiply circle

a lever-shaped switch selects between the SS (scale + softmax, dotted path) and SL (softmax + l1 norm, solid path) branches, and a second switch selects the offset (subtract) path over the dotted plain-attention exit
the input is reused by a long line along the bottom of the figure that feeds both the subtract circle and the final add circle

channels.colour: one saturated colour per tensor role: light blue input, orange query, teal key, blue attention map, magenta value, purple attention feature, navy output; pale green linear and darker green LBR layers, as keyed in the legend
channels.shape: slanted 3-D slabs = tensors, proportioned to their shape (flat key, large N x N map); circles = matrix multiply/add/subtract; small rounded boxes = normalisation and transpose ops; lever glyph = switch
channels.line: solid = the path taken in offset attention, dotted = the alternative (SS / plain attention) path not taken
channels.frame: none; a two-row legend strip underneath keys every glyph

quality.strengths: Every intermediate representation (query, key, attention map, value, attention feature) is drawn as its own slab whose shape follows its tensor size, between the operation that makes it and the one that consumes it; the offset is visible as a subtract circle fed by the input along the bottom; the switches make the two design choices explicit.
quality.weaknesses: Seven tensor colours plus two layer greens require a legend lookup for each slab; the input's two reuse lines (over the top to value, along the bottom to subtract/add) run the full width of the figure; operator circles carry only symbols so the meaning of each is legend-dependent.

figures.lesson: Give each tensor role its own colour and a 3-D slab whose proportions follow its shape (flat key, large square attention map), and decode colours and operator glyphs in a legend row underneath so the drawing itself carries only shape labels.

figures.title: PDE-Refiner: Achieving Accurate Long Rollouts with Neural PDE Solvers

taxonomy.task: autoregressive neural PDE rollout with an iterative denoising refinement of each step
taxonomy.note: modality time-series stands for a 1-D PDE state evolving in time (the KS equation in this paper)

arrangement.units: left: unframed 'Initial Prediction' stage; right: grey rounded 'Refinement process' panel holding one refinement step; a dashed loop under the panel returns the output to the input
arrangement.inputs_as: a blue waveform u(t - dt) and a flat line for the zero initial guess; the step index k enters each network from the top
arrangement.shared: the same light-green vertical Neural Operator box is drawn once per stage, fed by the same blue previous-state waveform

insights.structure: Two stages left to right, the second framed as one step that loops back on itself.
insights.data: Every state is a small waveform: the conditioning state in blue, the prediction (clean and noised) in orange, the predicted noise as a green noisy trace.
insights.emphasis: The refinement step gets the grey frame and most of the width; nothing else is highlighted.
insights.flow: Left to right on one baseline; the noise enters the add node from below, a curved line carries the noised input past the network to the subtract node, and a dashed path returns under the frame.
insights.avoid: The loop-back is a long dashed detour around the whole panel, and green fills the network box while also colouring the predicted-noise curve.

core.what: one refinement step framed in a grey panel (add noise, predict noise, subtract) with a dashed 'Repeat for k = 1..K' loop from its output back to its input

relations.form: the step is drawn once and closed by a dashed line from the refined output down and under the panel back to the step's input, labelled with the repeat range
'Initial Prediction' and 'Refinement process' side by side left to right, the network the same green box in both
noise enters the add node from below as a labelled side input; the step index k and the previous state enter the network from the top and left
noised input, network, predicted noise, subtract and refined output on one horizontal line inside the panel

channels.colour: blue = previous state (conditioning), orange = the prediction being refined, green = predicted noise; light-green fill also marks the network box, so green carries two meanings
channels.shape: tall rounded box = network, waveform = state or noise, circled plus/minus = arithmetic
channels.line: solid = data within a step, dashed = hand-off between the initial prediction and the refinement and the loop between steps
channels.frame: grey rounded panel = one refinement step

quality.strengths: The loop is the method and is drawn as one: a framed step with a single labelled dashed return; every intermediate the step compares is drawn as data (the noised input, the predicted noise, the refined output) rather than a wire into a block; the network is the same shape and fill in both stages; noise and k are short labels at the node that uses them.
quality.weaknesses: The dashed loop travels around the bottom of the whole panel instead of a short return; the curved line from the noised input to the subtract node bends under the network; green is both the network fill and the predicted-noise colour; the decreasing noise level across steps, which the caption calls the point, is only a subscript in the noise label.

figures.lesson: Draw one iteration of a refinement loop as a framed step with every intermediate shown as data (noised input, predicted noise, refined output), and close the loop with one labelled dashed line outside the frame.

figures.title: PETR: Position Embedding Transformation for Multi-View 3D Object Detection

taxonomy.task: multi-view camera 3D object detection

arrangement.units: one canvas: an unframed image-path row at top, a dashed rounded panel for the 3D Coordinates Generator at bottom left, and free-standing encoder/decoder trapezoids at the right
arrangement.inputs_as: a fanned stack of real multi-view street photos (top) and plotted camera-frustum point grids (bottom panel)
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; outputs end in 'class' and 'bbox' arrow labels
arrangement.shared: the camera frustum meshgrid is drawn once with 'N x' to mean one per view

insights.structure: An image path (top) and a dashed 3D-coordinates panel (bottom left) both feed a pair of facing trapezoids in the middle right, encoder then decoder, with the query generator stacked under the decoder.
insights.data: Multi-view inputs are a fanned stack of real street photos with 'N x', 2D features a single blue slab with H_F / W_F labels, the 3D coordinates as two blue dot meshgrids with axis glyphs, and queries as rows of small cream squares.
insights.emphasis: The new 3D Position Encoder is the biggest tinted shape at the junction of both inputs, and the coordinate generator gets its own dashed frame with a title, making both contributions the largest regions of the figure.
insights.flow: Elbow (right-angle) black arrows bring the feature slab down and the coordinate panel up into the encoder, a straight arrow carries it to the decoder, queries rise vertically from the Query Generator, and two arrows exit right to 'class' and 'bbox'.
insights.avoid: The two point-cloud plots are dense blue dots of small size whose axis labels (u, v, d, x, y, z) and the 'Front' tag are barely legible, and the figure is embedded as a single raster.

core.what: 2D image features from the top row and 3D coordinates from a dashed generator panel below converge on a 3D Position Encoder trapezoid, which feeds a facing Decoder trapezoid that outputs class and bbox per query

relations.form: an elbowed line from the 2D feature slab above and one from the 3D World space meshgrid below enter the left side of the green 3D Position Encoder trapezoid
top row left to right: fanned multi-view street photos (N x), grey Backbone box, a blue 2D-feature slab labelled H_F, W_F

a dashed rounded panel '3D Coordinates Generator' draws the camera frustum as a blue point meshgrid with a red image plane, transformed by an arrow into a 3D world-space point cloud, each with its own axis glyph
a row of yellow query squares from a grey Query Generator below enters the Decoder from underneath
the encoder trapezoid widens into the facing decoder trapezoid, whose output is a column of yellow squares with arrows to 'class' and 'bbox'

channels.colour: grey = off-the-shelf modules (backbone, query generator), green = 3D position encoder, yellow = decoder and query/output embeddings, blue = feature and coordinate data; red outline = image plane
channels.shape: trapezoids = encoder/decoder, rounded box = generic module, slab = feature map, point grid = coordinates, small squares = query embeddings
channels.line: one style of thin black arrows for all flow
channels.frame: dashed rounded frame = the 3D Coordinates Generator component

quality.strengths: The contribution, generating 3D coordinates from the camera frustum, gets the largest panel and is drawn on its actual structure (a frustum meshgrid and its world-space transform); data are drawn as data (real photos, a feature slab, point grids, query squares); the two inputs converge on the encoder from above and below.
quality.weaknesses: Both inputs reach the encoder via elbowed lines that turn twice; the 'Transform' arrow has a stray vertical line into it from below; how 2D features and 3D coordinates are combined inside the encoder is not shown; 'N x' labels are scattered small text.

figures.lesson: Give the geometric input its own dashed panel drawn as actual plotted point grids (camera frustum -> world space) under the image path, so both streams visibly arrive at the one new block in the middle.

figures.title: Personalized Federated Learning using Hypernetworks

taxonomy.task: personalized federated learning
taxonomy.note: architecture other = a server-side hypernetwork h(.; phi) that generates each client's weights

arrangement.units: two unframed panels (overview of all clients, detail of one client) separated by whitespace; boxes are flat rounded rectangles
arrangement.inputs_as: math symbols v_i and x with arrows down (right panel)
arrangement.losses_at: below the client box in the right panel (L_i)
arrangement.shared: the grey server box h(.; phi) appears in both panels

insights.structure: Two unframed panels separated by whitespace: left, a grey server box in the centre with three client boxes to its left, below and right; right, the exchange for one client i, server on the left and client on the right.
insights.data: Boxes hold only functions in math notation (h(.; phi), f_k(.; theta_k)); each link is a pair of thin opposite arrows labelled theta_k (to the client) and Delta theta_k (back); in the right panel inputs v_i and x enter from above and the loss L_i leaves below the client.
insights.emphasis: Each client has its own fill (pink, peach, lilac) and the math labels on its arrows are set in the same colour, so what travels per client is legible without a legend; the server stays neutral grey.
insights.flow: Hub-and-spoke on the left with bidirectional arrow pairs; the right panel reads top to bottom (inputs down into h and f_i, loss out below) with the theta_i / Delta theta_i exchange horizontal.
insights.avoid: Math-only labels with no words: a reader who has not read the text cannot tell that h is a hypernetwork or that v_i is a client embedding.

core.what: one grey hypernetwork box h(.; phi) at the centre exchanges a pair of opposite arrows (theta_k out, Delta theta_k back) with each client box arranged around it

relations.form: left panel: the grey server box in the centre with three client boxes f_1, f_2, f_3 to its left, below and right, each linked by its own arrow pair
each link is two thin opposite arrows labelled theta_k toward the client and Delta theta_k back, labels in the client's colour

right panel repeats one exchange for a generic client i: server box on the left, client box on the right, with client embedding v_i entering the server from above, input x entering the client from above and loss L_i leaving below

channels.colour: colour = client identity (red f_1, orange f_2, purple f_3 and f_i), applied to the box fill and its theta/Delta theta labels; grey = the shared hypernetwork
channels.shape: rounded boxes for all networks, each labelled by its function in math notation
channels.line: one style; direction alone separates parameters sent (theta) from updates returned (Delta theta)
channels.frame: no frames; the two panels are separated by whitespace

quality.strengths: Colour has one meaning, client identity, carried consistently from box to arrow labels; the hub-and-spoke placement makes the one-to-many generation visible by position; the detail panel adds the inputs and loss for one client without crowding the overview.
quality.weaknesses: Boxes contain only formulas (h(.; phi), f_i(.; theta_i)) with no names, against the names-not-formulas principle; the generic client i reuses f_3's purple, so it reads as client 3; the arrow pairs are long thin parallels whose labels sit outside them; neither the embedding v_i nor the generated weights are drawn as data.

figures.lesson: Draw each client link as a pair of opposite arrows labelled with what travels - weights down, weight update up - and set those labels in the client's own fill colour so the exchange is legible per client without a legend.

figures.title: π0: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control

taxonomy.task: generalist robot manipulation control
taxonomy.note: training 'other' = flow matching for the action expert; built on a PaliGemma-style VLM (SigLIP + Gemma); the VLM and action expert act as two weight sets in one transformer

arrangement.units: one model composition flanked by two bracketed side stacks (training data on the left, target embodiments on the right) of tan rounded boxes; the model has two colored token-column groups (blue VLM, green action expert inside a tan panel)
arrangement.inputs_as: real camera photos under ViT trapezoids plus a quoted instruction and noise/state labels
arrangement.shared: one long white bar across each expert's token columns shows shared attention layers

insights.structure: Three columns: a left stack of tan data boxes (pi dataset, Internet pre-training, OXE) gathered by a bracket, a center model where blue VLM token columns and green action-expert token columns are threaded by one long white bar per expert, and a right stack of three tan embodiment boxes (14/18/7-8 DoF) gathered by a bracket.
insights.data: Inputs sit under the model: three real camera frames feed ViT trapezoids, the instruction appears as the quoted string "fold shirt", q_t and noise arrive as bare labels with arrows, and the output action chunk a_t ... a_t+H is a bracketed token row on top.
insights.emphasis: Color splits the two experts (blue = pre-trained VLM, green = action expert with a tan backing panel), and the dashed looping arrows inside the green panel signal iterative flow-matching denoising of the action tokens.
insights.flow: Left-to-right at the top level (data -> model -> robots), but bottom-to-top inside the model (images/text/noise up through token columns to actions).
insights.avoid: The left data panel and right robot panel connect only through brackets, so it is unclear whether they are inputs/outputs or just context; the parameter counts in grey compete with the expert names.

core.what: one model of two token-column groups, blue VLM columns for images and the instruction and green action-expert columns for state and noisy actions, each group threaded by one long white bar, flanked by a bracketed data stack on the left and a bracketed embodiment stack on the right

relations.form: a long white 'pre-trained VLM' bar crosses all four blue token columns and a white 'action expert' bar crosses the green columns, sitting end to end on one line so the two experts read as one transformer
inputs enter each column from below: three camera photos through ViT trapezoids, the quoted 'fold shirt' instruction, the state q_t, and 'noise' under the action-expert panel
inside a tan panel the action-expert columns carry dashed loop arrows from bottom to top, the flow-matching refinement, emitting the action chunk a_t, a_t+1, ..., a_t+H above

left to right: training data stack (pi dataset, Internet pre-training, OXE) gathered by a bracket into the model, then a bracket out to three target-robot boxes (14 DoF bimanual, 18 DoF mobile, 7 and 8 DoF single arm)
data are drawn as data: real robot photos in the dataset and embodiment boxes, real camera frames of a shirt under the ViTs, a globe glyph for OXE

channels.colour: blue = VLM (vision-language) tokens and ViTs, green = action-expert tokens, tan = data/embodiment boxes and the action-expert's surrounding panel (tan carries two roles)
channels.shape: rounded columns with pills = token groups, long white bar = transformer layers, trapezoid = ViT, brackets = grouping of datasets and of robots
channels.line: solid arrows = inputs and outputs; dashed looped arrows = iterative denoising inside the action expert
channels.frame: tan rounded boxes = one dataset or robot type; tan panel = the action expert's denoising scope

quality.strengths: The two-expert design is visible as geometry: token columns of two colours share one bar line, the action expert is visibly smaller, and the denoising loop is drawn as dashed loops on its own columns; inputs and embodiments are real photos so the cross-embodiment claim is concrete.
quality.weaknesses: Tan fills both the data/robot boxes and the action-expert panel; the large brackets to the side stacks connect them to the whole model by one line each, so which data trains which part is not shown; the side stacks take about half of the width.

figures.lesson: Bracket the many training-data sources into the model on the left and fan the model out with a mirrored bracket to the robot embodiments it controls on the right, so the figure reads as many datasets -> one policy -> many robots.

figures.title: Image-to-Image Translation with Conditional Adversarial Networks

taxonomy.task: paired image-to-image translation (edges to photo)

arrangement.units: two unframed halves split by a vertical dotted rule: the fake pair path (with G) on the left, the real pair path on the right
arrangement.inputs_as: real image thumbnails: an edge sketch x on the left of each half and a real shoe photo y on the right half
arrangement.losses_at: no loss box; the discriminator's verdict words 'fake' (red) and 'real' (green) at the right end of each half stand for the objective
arrangement.shared: D is drawn twice as the same three-bar glyph with the same label, one per half; x is drawn twice on the fake side (input and copy to D)

insights.structure: Two mirrored cases sit side by side behind a dotted rule - generated pair on the left with G in front, real pair on the right - and both end in an identical D glyph.
insights.data: Inputs and outputs are the actual images (edge sketches, synthesized and real shoe photos) labelled with italic x, y, G(x); networks shrink to three outlined bars.
insights.emphasis: The only colour is the verdict text, red 'fake' and green 'real', and the conditional input is made visible by bracketing x with each photo going into D.
insights.flow: Each half reads left to right along straight black arrows; a dashed curved arrow carries x from the input down to D's bracket on the fake side.
insights.avoid: The three-bar network glyphs carry no information about the architecture, and the generator's training signal (L1 term) is not drawn at all, so the figure explains only half of the objective.

core.what: two mirrored halves behind a dotted rule: the generated pair (x, G(x)) into D giving 'fake' on the left and the real pair (x, y) into the same D giving 'real' on the right

relations.form: left half and right half each end in an identical D three-bar glyph followed by a verdict word, split by a vertical dotted rule
in each half two images stacked vertically are joined by a bracket into D: G(x) over x on the left, y over x on the right, so the discriminator always sees the edge map with an output
left half reads left to right: edge sketch x, generator G (three bars), synthesized shoe G(x)
a dashed curved arrow copies x from the input down to the lower slot of the fake pair, the same x that conditions the real pair

channels.colour: colour only on the verdicts: red 'fake' and green 'real'; images are the data in their own colours
channels.shape: three vertical bars = a network (G or D); images = data; bracket = a pair fed together
channels.line: solid = network data flow, dashed curve = copying the condition x into the pair; dotted vertical rule = separates the two cases
channels.frame: none

quality.strengths: The conditional-GAN idea is shown by position: both halves pair the same edge map with an output and feed identical D glyphs, so the only difference between fake and real is the upper image; all data are actual images, networks are reduced to small glyphs, and lines are short and straight.
quality.weaknesses: The dashed copy of x curves under G and could be misread as a second path through the network; the generator's U-Net and the L1 loss are not drawn, so only the adversarial half of the objective appears.

figures.lesson: Show a conditional discriminator as two mirrored cases split by a dotted rule, each bracketing the condition with the image into the same three-bar D glyph, and colour only the outputs (red fake, green real).

figures.title: pixelNeRF: Neural Radiance Fields from One or Few Images

taxonomy.task: novel view synthesis from one or few images

arrangement.units: no enclosures; three loose clusters (3-D scene with encoder, MLP with its inputs, rendering plot with loss) separated by whitespace
arrangement.inputs_as: schematic image card of colored shapes plus a target camera glyph
arrangement.losses_at: right, under the volume-rendering plot as a norm equation
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Single left-to-right strip: a 3-D scene cluster on the left (input view, yellow CNN encoder slab, gridded feature volume W, wireframe cube with a red ray and target camera), then the MLP f as four green bars, then a volume-rendering plot and a rendering-loss equation stacked on the right.
insights.data: The input view and target view are flat schematic cards of colored shapes, the feature volume is a gridded 3-D slab, query samples are purple dots on the red ray, and the fetched feature W(pi x) is a small blue cuboid icon under f.
insights.emphasis: Color-coding ties symbols together: the purple underline on x and red underline on d match the sample dots and ray, and the blue underline on W(pi x) matches the projected feature patch.
insights.flow: A curved black arrow lifts the ray sample out of the 3-D scene into (x,d), then straight arrows run right through f to (RGB sigma), a curve drops into the density plot, and a final curve drops to the loss below.
insights.avoid: The left 3-D cluster overlaps encoder, feature grid and scene cube so tightly that the projection pi x is hard to see; the projection of x onto W is implied, not drawn.

core.what: a query point on a target-view ray in a 3-D scene is projected into the CNN feature volume W of the input view, and that fetched feature W(pi x) conditions the NeRF MLP f, drawn left to right from scene to rendering loss

relations.form: left cluster: input view card, yellow CNN encoder slab, gridded feature volume W and a wireframe cube with a red target ray and purple sample dots; a blue line projects one sample back onto a highlighted cell of W
the tuple (x, d) enters the green four-bar MLP f from the left and the fetched feature W(pi x), a small blue cuboid, enters it from below
left to right: scene, curved arrow from a sample point to (x, d), f, (RGB sigma), curved arrow into the volume rendering plot, curved arrow down to the rendering loss
the rendering loss draws the rendered blue pixel swatch against 'g.t.' inside a squared norm

channels.colour: colour ties symbols to geometry: purple underline on x = sample points, red underline on d = ray, blue underline on W(pi x) = the projected feature and its highlighted cell; green = the MLP, yellow = CNN encoder; the rendering curve uses a purple-to-blue gradient
channels.shape: cards = views, gridded slab = feature volume, bars = MLP, cuboid = a fetched feature, curve plot = density along the ray
channels.line: red = the camera ray, blue = projection to the feature grid, black curved arrows = stage hand-offs
channels.frame: none; clusters separated by whitespace

quality.strengths: The method's addition to NeRF, fetching an image feature by projecting the query point, is drawn on the scene itself and made the largest element; colour underlines bind each symbol to the geometry it came from; the representations (x, d), W(pi x), RGB sigma and the rendered pixel are all drawn between the steps that make and consume them.
quality.weaknesses: The curved arrow from the sample point to (x, d), the arc from (RGB sigma) into the plot and the hook down to the loss all leave the straight reading line; the input view, encoder slab and feature grid overlap in one perspective stack, so where encoding ends and the feature volume begins is hard to see; the CNN encoder is labelled only below the stack.

figures.lesson: Show image-conditioned rendering by projecting the query point on the ray back onto a gridded feature volume and carrying the picked cell, as a matching-coloured cuboid, into the MLP as a side input.

figures.title: pixelSplat: 3D Gaussian Splats from Image Pairs for Scalable Generalizable 3D Reconstruction

taxonomy.task: generalizable 3D Gaussian prediction from image pairs
taxonomy.note: architecture 'other' = per-pixel probabilistic depth prediction (discrete depth distribution sampled with reparameterization)

arrangement.units: two grey-filled boxes stacked in the middle (probability histograms, Gaussian placement along rays) between unframed 3-D frustums at left and right
arrangement.inputs_as: a 3-D camera frustum with a gridded feature map and three colored pixel rays
arrangement.shared: per-pixel color coding (red/blue/green) runs across all columns

insights.structure: Three columns: a left camera frustum with feature map F and three colored rays, a middle pair of grey boxes stacked vertically (top: three depth-probability histograms; bottom: three ray lines with sampled Gaussian means), and a right frustum with the resulting 3-D Gaussians.
insights.data: Each of three pixels a, b, c keeps one color (red, blue, green) everywhere: highlighted cells on F, ray arrows, histogram bars, blurred Gaussian blobs on lines, and the parameter tuples.
insights.emphasis: The consistent per-pixel color triple is the main device; the stochastic step is spelled out by the 'sample z ~ p_phi(z)' arrow running from the top box to the bottom box.
insights.flow: F[a],F[b],F[c] curve down into network f, which fans out right into both boxes; top box feeds the bottom via the sample arrow; bottom box exits right and up through the parameter tuples into the 3-D Gaussian frustum.
insights.avoid: The network f is three bare unlabeled bars and the fan-out lines from f to six arrows are long and thin, making the split into (phi) and (Sigma, S) easy to miss.

core.what: three pixels a, b, c each keep one colour (red, blue, green) through every step: feature-map cell and ray, depth-probability histogram, sampled Gaussian position along the ray, and finally a 3-D Gaussian in the right frustum

relations.form: three colour-coded rows inside each of the two middle grey boxes, one per pixel, stacked in the same a, b, c order
left: a camera frustum with the gridded feature map F, three highlighted cells and three coloured rays; right: the same frustum with blurred coloured 3-D Gaussians placed along those rays

F[a], F[b], F[c] go by a curved arrow into network f, which outputs phi (to the top box) and (Sigma, S) (to the bottom box); the top box's 'sample z ~ p_phi(z)' arrow passes to the bottom box, whose tuples feed the right frustum
two stacked grey boxes: the top draws per-pixel depth distributions p_phi(z) as histograms, the bottom draws each ray as a line with the sampled mean mu = h(z) as a blob and opacity alpha = p_phi(z)

channels.colour: colour = pixel identity (red a, blue b, green c), used on cells, rays, parameter vectors, histogram bars, blobs and subscripts; no other colour
channels.shape: frustums = camera space, histograms = probability distributions, blurred ellipses = Gaussians, bars = network f, small striped bars = parameter vectors phi
channels.line: black arrows for flow; coloured arrows for pixel rays
channels.frame: grey-filled boxes = the two probabilistic depth steps

quality.strengths: One channel carries one meaning throughout: a pixel's colour follows it from feature cell through histogram and sampled blob to the final Gaussian, so the per-pixel pipeline reads without labels; the distributions and samples are drawn as data (histograms, blobs on rays) rather than boxes; the 3-D frustums on both ends show the method on its structure.
quality.weaknesses: Formulas are typeset inside the grey boxes (mu = h(z), alpha = p_phi(z)) and as tuples beside them; the curved arrow from F to f and the line from f fanning to six arrows make an indirect, elbowed route; network f is a tiny glyph at bottom left.

figures.lesson: Follow three pixels by colour from feature-map cell to ray, depth histogram, sampled Gaussian on a depth axis and finally a blurred Gaussian on its ray inside the camera frustum, so per-pixel prediction reads as geometry.

figures.title: Plenoxels: Radiance Fields without Neural Networks

taxonomy.task: novel view synthesis / radiance field optimization
taxonomy.note: architecture 'other' = an explicit sparse voxel grid storing density and spherical-harmonic coefficients, with no neural network

arrangement.units: four unframed steps in one horizontal strip, separated by whitespace and named by sub-labels a) Sparse Voxel Grid, b) Trilinear Interpolation, c) Volumetric Rendering, d) Optimization
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo (a plant) on a tilted image plane with a camera glyph, labelled 'Training Image'
arrangement.losses_at: bottom right, as a typeset 'minimize L_recon + lambda L_TV' equation under the rendering plot, with no arrow to it
arrangement.shared: the ray is one continuous black arrow drawn again in the zoomed cube

insights.structure: A single left-to-right strip of four steps, where the first two are one 3-D scene (grid then zoomed cell) and the last two shrink to a 2-D plot and an equation at the right edge.
insights.data: The input is a real photo on a perspective image plane, the voxels are coloured dots on a dashed wire grid, the SH coefficients are a palette of shaded spheres, and the rendered output is a single teal colour swatch.
insights.emphasis: The translucent blue voxel and its light-blue zoom cone pull the eye to the enlarged cell, where yellow arrows from the eight corner spheres converge on the sample point.
insights.flow: The camera ray runs as one thick black arrow through the grid and on through the zoomed cube; a dotted curved arrow then jumps up and right to the rendering plot, and step d has no arrow at all.
insights.avoid: The optimization step d is detached text with no arrow back to the voxels, so the loop that trains the grid is not drawn.

core.what: a ray through a sparse voxel grid, with one cell opened into an enlarged cube where yellow arrows interpolate the eight corner spherical-harmonic values onto the sample point, then rendering and optimisation at the right

relations.form: a shaded blue cell in the sparse grid widens through a pale blue wedge into the enlarged dashed cube of panel b, the ray drawn again through it
panel a draws the method on its data: a real plant photo on a tilted image plane with a camera glyph, the ray through a dashed wire grid of coloured voxel dots
in panel b eight yellow arrows from the cube corners converge on one sample point on the ray; a sigma-sum arrow brings a palette of spherical-harmonic spheres into a corner
four sub-labelled steps a) to d) in one horizontal strip: grid, interpolation, a 2-D density-vs-distance plot with a predicted colour swatch, and an optimisation objective
a dotted curved arrow carries the ray from panel b to the rendering plot, whose arrow leads to the predicted colour

channels.colour: voxel and corner colours = the stored per-voxel values (spheres shaded as SH colour); yellow = interpolation weights; blue = the zoomed cell and wedge; the SH palette groups red, green, blue bands
channels.shape: dots on a wire grid = voxels, shaded spheres = SH coefficients, curve plot = density along ray, square = predicted colour

channels.shape: grids of square cells = feature tensors (edges as 2-D grids, nodes as rows), rounded boxes = sub-modules and input/output, a circle = the sampling loop, ribbon renders = protein structures
channels.line: solid black arrows = data flow, dashed arrows = repeat loops (3x) in panel A and pointers to the key in panel B, dashed thin lines = inter-atom distances

figures.lesson: Carry chain identity through every tensor: colour each chain once in the input cartoon and then split every node and edge feature grid into the same two colours, so multi-chain conditioning reads without labels.

figures.title: Point Transformer V3: Simpler, Faster, Stronger

arrangement.shared: the same toy point set is reused in all four patterns

insights.flow: Left to right inside a triplet (curve, overlay, path) with no connecting arrows; comparison runs across the 2x2 grid.
insights.avoid: Do not overlay a faded curve, a grid and an arrowed path in the same grey family - give the resulting order its own colour.

four identical triplets in a 2x2 grid, base patterns on top and their transposed variants directly below
within each triplet three equal grids left to right: curve, curve plus points, resulting path - no arrows between them

figures.title: Q-Transformer: Scalable Offline Reinforcement Learning via Autoregressive Q-Functions

taxonomy.task: robot offline RL with per-dimension autoregressive Q-values
taxonomy.note: Q-Transformer itself; paradigm closest listed sequence-model RL

arrangement.units: unframed columns of cells, one per action dimension, separated into time steps by dashed vertical lines
arrangement.inputs_as: stack of real robot camera frames labelled history of states
arrangement.shared: bottom time axis with step bars (t, t+1, T)

insights.structure: One column per action dimension, each a vertical stack of discretised bin cells over a grey token square, grouped into environment steps t, t+1 and T by vertical dashed separators and grey bars along the bottom.
insights.data: Q-value bins are coloured cells by role: green for the dataset action's target, red with a white '->0' glyph for unobserved actions, pale yellow for the max carried from the next dimension; the state history is a stack of real robot photos at the far left.
insights.emphasis: The conservative '->0' red cells dominate the grid and a dotted legend box top right decodes the three cell colours, making the regulariser as visible as the Bellman target.
insights.flow: Bottom-to-top inside a column (token, bins, max), then grey elbow arrows route each 'max' back into the previous column's target cell; across columns left to right along a long time axis, with the Monte-Carlo return box looping a line over the top back to the start.
insights.avoid: The many thin grey back-arrows from 'max' boxes into earlier columns cross each other and are easy to misread as forward flow.

core.what: autoregressive per-dimension Q-update unrolled as columns: each action dimension is a vertical stack of discretised bin cells over a grey token square, and a 'max' box over the next column sends its value back left into the previous column's green dataset-action cell, columns grouped into environment steps t, t+1, T

relations.form: time runs left to right on a long grey axis at the bottom, with grey bars labeled t, t+1, T under vertical dashed separators and the caption 'Autoregressive conservative Q-update for each action dimension' under the axis
in each column the dataset action's bin is green (target from the next dimension's max) and every other bin is red with a white '->0' glyph, the conservative regulariser drawn per cell
short bent arrows run from each column's bins up into a 'max' box above the next column and back down-left into the green cell of the preceding column
at the step boundary the first dimension's max at t+1 passes through a Hadamard dot with gamma, then plus R_t, chained as small operator glyphs left to right
a Monte-Carlo return box MC_{t:T} in the T region sends a long wire up and across the top of the figure into every max box
the state history s_{t-w:t} is a stack of real robot camera photos at the far left feeding the token row

channels.colour: bin fill = role of a Q-value, keyed in a dotted legend box: yellow = maximum Q-value carried from the next dimension, green = target Q-value of the dataset action, red = target of unobserved actions (pushed to 0); grey = tokens and steps; one meaning each
channels.shape: rounded cells = Q-value bins, grey squares = transformer tokens, white rounded boxes = operations (max, gamma, R_t, MC), dot/plus circles = operators
channels.line: solid grey arrows throughout; vertical dashed lines separate environment steps; the long top wire carries the MC return
channels.frame: no frames on the method; a dotted rounded box holds the legend; a curly brace labels the 'Discrete action bins' column

quality.strengths: the per-dimension target structure is drawn on the bins themselves - green, red '->0' and yellow max cells keyed once - so both the Bellman target and the conservative regulariser are visible as data; dimensions and steps are unrolled columns on a time axis rather than a loop; the robot history is a real photo stack
quality.weaknesses: the MC return's wire runs the full width of the figure across the top and bends down into each max box; the max arrows bend back leftward over the cell columns, crowding the top; ellipsis columns and the near-empty t+1 and T regions take space without content; 'Q-Transformer steps' label floats far from the tokens it names

figures.lesson: Keep two time scales apart by stacking them: per-dimension token columns above, environment steps as grey bars on an axis beneath, with dashed vertical rules where one environment step ends - and colour the cells only by their role in the target.

figures.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs

taxonomy.task: memory-efficient LLM finetuning with 4-bit base
taxonomy.note: training: parameter-efficient finetuning with quantized frozen base

arrangement.units: three unframed columns separated by thin vertical rules, sharing row labels

insights.structure: Three method columns (Full Finetuning, LoRA, QLoRA) separated by thin vertical rules share one set of bold row headers on the left (Optimizer State 32 bit, Adapters 16 bit, Base Model) and each ends in a precision label underneath.

insights.emphasis: The proposed column alone gains magenta paging arrows to a dashed CPU box and a shrunken base-model box; the added mechanism, not a colour fill, is the highlight.
insights.flow: Blue arrows run down for parameter updates and green arrows run up for gradient flow within each column; columns are read left to right as a progression; a corner legend names the three arrow colours.

core.what: three method columns (Full Finetuning, LoRA, QLoRA) separated by thin vertical rules share one set of row headers (Optimizer State 32 bit, Adapters 16 bit, Base Model), so memory per component is compared row by row through box sizes, ours last

relations.form: the same three rows are drawn in each column: one huge optimizer box in Full Finetuning versus three small ones in LoRA and QLoRA; no adapters in the first column; a wide base model box in the first two versus a narrow one labeled '4-bit Transformer' in QLoRA

channels.shape: outlined rounded rectangles whose size encodes memory footprint; page icons = paged optimizer state
channels.line: solid arrows only; style is constant, colour separates flows
channels.frame: a dashed box = CPU memory (off-device); thin vertical rules separate the three methods

quality.strengths: the comparison is pure geometry - identical row headers across three columns, box size encodes memory, so the shrinking optimizer and base model read without labels; arrow colour has one keyed meaning; arrows are short, straight and vertical; the only added mechanism in the proposed column (paging to a CPU box) is the one new element and draws the eye
quality.weaknesses: box sizes are qualitative, not to scale, and no numbers are given; the 4-bit quantisation is shown only as a narrower box with a caption, not what NF4 or double quantisation do; the magenta paging arc is drawn from the first optimizer box only, so it is unclear whether all states page

figures.lesson: Lay the compared fine-tuning methods out as columns over shared row labels for memory tiers with their bit widths, so the size of each box alone shows the memory saved, and keep arrow colour for the kind of flow (updates, gradients, paging) with a small legend.

figures.title: Qwen-VL: A Versatile Vision-Language Model for Understanding, Localization, Text Reading, and Beyond

relations.form: within each column thin up-arrows run from the camera icon through ViT and the CrossAttn bar into QwenLM; a document icon with its own up-arrow enters QwenLM from the lower right

channels.shape: outlined rectangles = feature tensors, their height decreasing slightly with point count toward the bottleneck; operations are only arrow labels
channels.line: solid black arrows = main data flow, grey dashed arrows = skip connections
channels.frame: one rounded tinted container = the whole network

quality.strengths: the arrows are all short, straight and on one axis; the dashed skip arcs nest without crossing and use their own line style; tensors are drawn as the nouns with shapes printed, and real input/output scans bracket the network
quality.weaknesses: the novel parts (local feature aggregation LFA and random sampling RS) are only arrow labels the same size as FC or MLP, with nothing salient marking them; tensor heights shrink so little that the 4x per-level reduction must be read from text; the bottleneck and FC head boxes take as much space as the encoder stages

figures.lesson: Put every layer on one tinted rounded backdrop named after the network, write each layer's operations above and below its arrow, and size each box by its tensor (height for point count, width for channels) so down- and up-sampling are visible without extra marks.

figures.title: RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval

taxonomy.task: building a recursively clustered and summarised tree over long-document chunks for retrieval-augmented QA

arrangement.units: three grey-framed rounded panels with bold titles: the tree overview, one layer's formation, one node's contents
arrangement.inputs_as: five numbered pastel squares labelled 'Text chunks' at the bottom of the middle panel
arrangement.shared: a chunk belonging to two clusters is drawn as a copy inside each cluster container (chunks 3 and 5 appear twice)

insights.structure: Three framed panels in a row, each a zoom into one element of the previous: the full three-layer tree, the formation of one layer, and the fields of one summary node.
insights.data: Text chunks are numbered pastel squares under the label 'Text chunks', clusters are grey containers holding copies of their member squares, and a node's embedding is a bracketed column of numbers.
insights.emphasis: The middle panel is the largest and the only one with per-chunk colours, so clustering-then-summarisation, the step that builds the tree, draws the eye first.
insights.flow: Inside the middle panel lines run bottom to top from chunks through clusters to summaries, marked by a side arrow labelled '1. Clustering' and '2. Summarization by LLM'; between panels, dashed curved arrows from magnifier icons carry the reader left to right.
insights.avoid: Colour changes meaning between panels: all tree nodes are pink on the left, while in the middle pink marks chunk 1 only and summaries are grey-blue.

core.what: the method drawn on a toy tree: five numbered chunk squares at the bottom are wired up into three cluster containers and each cluster up to one summary node, the same construction shown as layers of the full tree on the left

relations.form: a small instance of the tree (leaves 1-5, summaries 6-8, roots 9-10) drawn with numbered square nodes and straight parent-child lines in the left panel
magnifier icons on the leaf layer and on node 8, each with a dashed curved arrow to the next framed panel to its right, which shows that part enlarged
inside the middle panel, chunks -> clusters -> summaries run bottom to top, with a side arrow labelled '1. Clustering' and '2. Summarization by LLM'
crossing straight lines from the five chunks converge into grey cluster containers, one chunk feeding two containers where clusters overlap

channels.colour: in the middle panel fill = chunk identity (one pastel per chunk, kept when the chunk is copied into a cluster), grey-blue = generated summary; in the left panel every node is pink, so colour carries no consistent meaning across panels
channels.shape: square tiles = tree nodes / chunks, grey rounded containers = clusters, stacked rounded boxes = fields of a node, magnifier glyph = zoom point
channels.line: thin solid lines = parent-child or chunk-to-cluster membership; thick dashed curved arrows = zoom into the next panel
channels.frame: a thin grey rounded frame = one panel at one zoom level; grey containers inside = one cluster

quality.strengths: the recursion is taught by geometry rather than words: tree -> one layer -> one node, linked by magnifier glyphs; overlapping clusters are shown by copying a chunk's square into two containers; the right panel draws the node as its actual fields (index, child ids '2, 3', summary text, an embedding vector) and the ids match node 8's children in the middle panel
quality.weaknesses: colour is per-chunk in the middle panel but uniform pink in the left panel, so the tree overview cannot be traced back to clusters; the chunk-to-cluster lines cross each other in a tangle below the containers; the left panel's tree is drawn without the clustering frames that define it, so it reads as a generic graph

figures.lesson: Teach a recursive data structure as a zoom chain: the whole tree small on the left, one level of its construction in the middle, one node's fields on the right, each step entered by a magnifier glyph and a dashed curved arrow.

figures.title: Re-Imagen: Retrieval-Augmented Text-to-Image Generator

taxonomy.task: text-to-image generation conditioned on retrieved image-text neighbours

arrangement.units: one unframed pipeline; only the retrieved-neighbours row is enclosed, in a black dashed rectangle
arrangement.inputs_as: the prompt quoted as text ('c_p: Two Chortai are running on the field.'), the noisy image x_t as a real noisy photo, the database as a server-and-cylinder icon
arrangement.losses_at: no loss is drawn; each UNet carries its prediction epsilon_theta(x_t, c_p, c_n, t) as a label above it
arrangement.shared: one neighbours box serves both unrolled steps, each step's Attention block pointing into it from above

insights.structure: Two unrolled denoising steps run along the top row; below them a single dashed neighbours box spans both; the prompt and the database sit in a left column joined to that box by the Query and Retrieval arrows.
insights.data: The image is drawn at every step as a real photo going from noise to a clean picture, and the retrieved neighbours are three real photos plus a quoted sentence, not an abstract block.
insights.emphasis: Thick lavender block arrows mark the retrieval path and the neighbours box is the widest element; the UNets are small light-blue boxes.
insights.flow: The top row reads left to right with straight thin arrows; short vertical arrows run from each UNet down to its Attention block and from Attention down into the neighbours box; the lavender arrows run down (Query) and right (Retrieval) in the left column.
insights.avoid: The arrows from each Attention block point down into the neighbours box, the reverse of the neighbours conditioning the step, and nothing returns from Attention to the next image; the prediction formula is typeset above each UNet.

core.what: the retrieved neighbours (three photos and a sentence) are drawn once in a dashed box under the denoising chain, spanning both unrolled steps, fed from a database icon by a thick Retrieval arrow

relations.form: prompt at the top left, a lavender Query arrow down to the database icon, a lavender Retrieval arrow right to the dashed neighbours box
two unrolled steps along the top row, each a light-blue UNet between real images x_t, x_{t-1}, then an ellipsis to the clean x_0
one neighbours box spans under both steps, and each step's purple Attention block connects to it by a short vertical arrow
each UNet sits on a vertical with its Attention block directly below it, the conditioning drawn as a column rather than a converging bundle

channels.colour: light blue = UNet, light purple = Attention, lavender = the retrieval path (Query and Retrieval arrows); data itself is shown as real photos
channels.shape: rounded rectangle = network module, photo = image state or retrieved image, server-and-cylinder icon = database
channels.line: thin black arrows = data flow through the model; thick lavender block arrows = retrieval (query and fetch)
channels.frame: black dashed rectangle = the set of retrieved neighbours c_n

quality.strengths: Retrieval is drawn by its form: the store is a database icon beside the main chain and the retrieved items are drawn as data (real photos and a sentence) in their own dashed box; the box spans both unrolled steps, so the reuse of the same neighbours at every step is visible from position; image states are real photos from noise to clean; line style separates the retrieval path from model data flow; all lines are short and straight.
quality.weaknesses: The Attention arrows point from the step into the neighbours box, so the conditioning direction reads backwards and no line returns from Attention to x_{t-1}; the prediction epsilon_theta(...) is typeset above each UNet; the Retrieval arrow ends short of the neighbours box with a gap; the database icon takes more area than the UNets.

figures.lesson: Draw the retrieved neighbours once, as real images and quoted text in one dashed box spanning every unrolled denoising step, so the reader sees that the same neighbours condition each step.

figures.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

taxonomy.task: interleaved reasoning and acting with LLM prompting

arrangement.units: white rounded transcript panels with overlapping grey title tabs, arranged in two task rows
arrangement.inputs_as: question/task text box at the top of each row
arrangement.shared: outcome marks (cross/check) in panel corners

insights.structure: Two task rows split by a long dashed rule: HotpotQA on top (question box, stacked Standard and CoT panels, Act-Only panel, tall ReAct panel on the right) and AlfWorld below (task box over Act-Only on the left, ReAct on the right); each prompting style is a white rounded panel with a grey tab title numbered (1a)-(2b).
insights.data: Everything is monospace transcript text with bold Thought/Act/Obs prefixes, tool verbs (Search, Finish, Think) in bold blue with bracketed arguments.
insights.emphasis: Highlighter rectangles mark the story: red behind wrong reasoning or failed observations, green behind the facts leading to the answer, blue behind Think steps; red crosses vs green checks in each panel corner give outcomes, and ReAct always takes the right-hand, tallest panel.
insights.flow: Read top to bottom inside each transcript, left to right across baselines to the method; no arrows at all.
insights.avoid: Dense small monospace text makes it a reading figure rather than a diagram; it only works at full page width.

core.what: prompting styles as side-by-side transcript panels per task, baselines left and the tall ReAct panel rightmost: HotpotQA row (Standard, CoT, Act-Only, then ReAct) above a dashed rule, AlfWorld row (Act-Only, then ReAct) below, each panel ending in a red cross or a green check

relations.form: each prompting style is a white rounded panel with a grey numbered tab title (1a)-(1d), (2a)-(2b); the ReAct panels sit at the right of each row and are the tallest
each row opens with one task box (the HotpotQA question, the AlfWorld room description) above the panels that all answer it
inside the panels the agent loop is written as numbered Thought/Act/Obs lines stacked top to bottom, unrolled step by step rather than drawn as a cycle
a long horizontal dashed rule splits the figure into two task rows with the same left-baseline / right-ReAct arrangement

channels.colour: highlighter colour = role of a span: red = wrong reasoning or failed observation, green = facts leading to the answer, blue = Think steps (and bold blue = tool verbs Search/Finish/Think); red cross vs green check marks outcome; blue carries two meanings (tool verb text and Think-step highlight)
channels.shape: rounded panels = one prompting method's transcript; tab labels = method names; everything inside is monospace text
channels.line: no arrows; one dashed rule between task rows
channels.frame: each rounded panel = one method on one task

quality.strengths: data is drawn as data - real question, real transcripts - and highlights trace the story (where the baselines go wrong in red, which retrieved facts the ReAct chain uses in green) so the outcome is checkable; baselines and ReAct are placed in parallel panels with ReAct last; outcome icons give the 5 s answer
quality.weaknesses: the figure is almost entirely text, so the Thought/Act/Obs loop - the method - is never drawn as structure; panels differ in size and are packed irregularly (Standard and CoT stacked beside Act-Only), so the comparison is not identical panels; long transcripts make the 30 s read hard; blue does double duty

figures.lesson: An agent's reasoning-acting loop can be shown with no arrows at all: print the trajectory as Thought/Act/Obs lines in monospace, colour the tool verbs, highlight right and wrong spans in green and red, and end each competing transcript with a check or a cross.

figures.title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training

taxonomy.task: retrieval-augmented LM pretraining and open-domain QA

arrangement.units: two unframed vertical pipelines separated by whitespace
arrangement.inputs_as: grey dashed text box with a real example sentence
arrangement.shared: same module boxes and green knowledge-corpus note in both halves

insights.structure: Two identical vertical pipelines side by side (pre-training left, fine-tuning right) with no titles or divider, each a spine of input text, retriever, encoder and answer box with corpora hung off the right.
