insights.data: Text instances are grey dashed-border boxes with real typewriter examples ([MASK] in red); learned modules are pale-blue rounded boxes; data sources are folded-corner notes, yellow for sampled training data and green for the knowledge corpus; every element carries a blue italic symbol (x, z, theta, phi, y).
insights.emphasis: Only the corpus notes and the example text change between halves, so the reader sees the same retrieve-then-encode architecture serves both stages.
insights.flow: Top to bottom down each spine; dashed arrows labelled 'sample' and 'retrieve' come in from the right-side notes, and a curved skip arrow on the left carries x past the retriever into an (x, z) pair.
insights.avoid: The two halves have no headings, so pre-training vs fine-tuning must be inferred from the example text and data notes.

core.what: two identical top-down pipelines side by side, pre-training left and fine-tuning right: input text -> Neural Knowledge Retriever -> Knowledge-Augmented Encoder -> Answer, with a retrieved-from corpus note hung off the retriever's right and a sampled-from data note at the top right; only the data and the example text change

relations.form: each half is a vertical spine of straight down-arrows: grey dashed text box (x) -> pale-blue retriever (theta) -> pale-blue encoder (phi) -> grey dashed answer box (y)
a green folded-corner 'Textual knowledge corpus (Z)' note sits right of the retriever and a dashed arrow labeled 'retrieve' points from it into the retriever
a curved arrow from the input text and a short arrow from the retriever meet at a bare italic '(x, z)' label left of the spine, which then curves into the encoder
a yellow folded-corner note (Pre-training corpus X / Supervised data) at the top right sends a dashed 'sample' arrow curving into the input text box
inputs and answers are real typewriter examples: 'The [MASK] at the top of the pyramid' -> '[MASK] = pyramidion', 'what's the angle of an equilateral triangle?' -> '60 degrees'

channels.colour: fill = kind of element: pale blue = learned modules, grey with dashed border = text instances, yellow note = sampled training data, green note = knowledge corpus; red = the [MASK] token; blue italic = each element's symbol; one meaning each
channels.shape: rounded rectangles = learned modules, dashed-border boxes = text instances, folded-corner notes = data sources/corpora
channels.line: solid arrows = forward computation, dashed arrows = sampling from and retrieving from a corpus
channels.frame: no frames; the two halves are separated only by whitespace and carry no titles

quality.strengths: the two stages are identical pipelines placed side by side, so the reader sees one retrieve-then-encode architecture serving both; data is drawn as real examples with [MASK] in red; corpora are a distinct glyph beside the flow with their own dashed line style; colour and shape each carry one meaning; spines are straight
quality.weaknesses: the retrieved document z is never shown as text - only the bare '(x, z)' symbol in the margin - so what the encoder reads is hidden; the two halves have no titles saying pre-training vs fine-tuning; the (x, z) join is drawn as two curved arrows bending round the left edge; the retrieval as a latent variable and the backprop to the retriever are not drawn

figures.lesson: Drawing pre-training and fine-tuning as two identical copies of one pipeline, changing only the example text and the data note, shows that the modules are shared without any arrow or label saying so.

figures.title: ReconFormer: Accelerated MRI Reconstruction Using Recurrent Transformer

taxonomy.task: accelerated MRI reconstruction with recurrent transformers

arrangement.units: three unframed repeated 3-D scenes each with a cloud call-out
arrangement.inputs_as: MRI slice on a perspective patch-grid plane
arrangement.shared: identical scan and call-out composition repeated in each panel

insights.structure: Three equal unframed panels in a row, captioned (a) Swin/PVT, (b) SwinIR/ViT, (c) ReconFormer (ours), each repeating one scene: scan on a patch plane, layer stack above it, cloud call-out on the right showing the layer's inside.
insights.data: A brain MRI slice lies on a tilted perspective plane cut by a white patch grid; layers are red wireframe slabs joined to the image by a red vertical line; inside the cloud, tokens are pale-blue parallelograms with a coloured attention quad and an FFN up-arrow.
insights.emphasis: The stack shape differs per panel (shrinking pyramid in a, constant in b and c) and only (c) adds overlapping multi-scale coloured attention quads in its cloud, plus '(ours)' in the caption.
insights.flow: Bottom to top from scan to stack, then a thick dashed arrow out to the cloud and back; panels compare left to right.
insights.avoid: The difference between (b) and (c) is a small change inside the cloud that is hard to see at print size, and the earlier reader described the pyramid in (a) as widening upward though it narrows.

core.what: three equal unframed panels in a row - (a) Swin/PVT, (b) SwinIR/ViT, (c) ReconFormer (ours), ours last - each the same scene: an MRI slice on a tilted patch-gridded plane, a red wireframe layer stack rising from it, and a cloud call-out of the layer's inside

relations.form: the layer stack shape differs per panel: a pyramid of red slabs narrowing upward in (a), a constant-width column in (b) and (c)
a thick dashed arrow leaves the 'Transformer Layer' slab into a cloud on its right and another returns, the cloud showing self-attention between pale-blue token parallelograms and an FFN up-arrow
the operation sits on a real brain MRI slice drawn on a perspective plane cut into patches by a white grid, with a red vertical line joining the patch plane to the layer stack
only the cloud in (c) shows overlapping multi-scale tokens with coloured (red, green, orange) attention quads, where (a) and (b) show a single green link between two same-size tokens

channels.colour: red = the layer stack wireframe and its link to the image in every panel; green/coloured quads in the clouds = attention regions, multiple colours only in (c) to mark multiple scales; pale blue = tokens
channels.shape: red wireframe slabs = transformer layers (their width = feature resolution), parallelograms = tokens, a cloud = zoom into one layer
channels.line: thick black dashed arrows = zoom into and out of the cloud; a thin red vertical line ties the stack to the image
channels.frame: no frames; each panel is set off by whitespace and a caption below

quality.strengths: three identical scenes side by side make the difference (stack shape, multi-scale attention in ours) the only change, with ours last; the operation is drawn on a real MRI slice with its patch grid; each cloud opens the layer in the same place
quality.weaknesses: the figure is small and the key difference in (c) - overlapping coloured quads in the cloud - is a few tiny shapes, not the most salient element; perspective wireframes and cloud call-outs add ink without meaning; the coloured quads are not keyed, so what each colour means (scale) is left to the caption; (b) and (c) stacks look identical, so the recurrence ReconFormer adds is not visible

figures.lesson: Compare architectures by repeating one identical 3-D scene - the scan on a gridded patch plane, the layer stack above it, the attention sketch in a cloud call-out - and change only the stack's shape and the attention sketch between panels.

figures.title: ReconFormer: Accelerated MRI Reconstruction Using Recurrent Transformer

taxonomy.task: recurrent multi-scale attention for MRI reconstruction

arrangement.units: three unframed lettered panels, one top band and two bottom halves
arrangement.inputs_as: MRI slice thumbnail with coloured multi-scale patches
arrangement.shared: scale colour coding across (a)

insights.structure: Three lettered unframed panels: (a) multi-scale attention fills the top band with Scale Head 1-3 stacked as rows under Query/Key/Value column headers, (b) the recurrent cell and (c) the transformer layer share the bottom row.
insights.data: (a) starts from an MRI slice with translucent coloured patches of three sizes; Q/K/V are wireframe cuboids subdivided more as scale grows, becoming solid coloured bars after attention and grey bars after the linear layer; (b) uses yellow rounded K/Q/V boxes with circled x/+ and hidden states c^(t), h^(t).
insights.emphasis: One colour per scale (green, orange, blue) is carried from the patches on the scan through the Q/K/V cuboids to the concatenated token row.
insights.flow: Left to right within each panel; (b) branches h^(t) into K, Q, V with brackets and merges to c^(t+1) and output; (c) has residual loops beneath to circled +.
insights.avoid: Typos and tiny labels ('Liner', italic 'SoftMax' on arrows) and the three panels are not visually connected, so how (b) and (c) relate to (a) is left to the caption.

core.what: panel (a) fills the top band with three scale heads stacked as rows (Scale Head 1-3) under shared Query/Key/Value column headers, one colour per scale carried from patches of three sizes on the MRI slice through the Q/K/V cuboids to coloured bars that are concatenated and projected

relations.form: the input is a real MRI slice cut by a white grid with translucent green, orange and blue patches of increasing size overlaid at its top right
(a) reads left to right: MRI slice -> 'Projection' arrow -> the 3x3 grid of Q/K/V cuboids -> a column of concatenated green/orange/blue bars -> 'Liner' arrow -> grey output bars
each scale head is one row of three wireframe cuboids (Q, K, V) bracketed together, the cuboids subdivided into more cells as the scale grows

(b) at lower left draws the recurrent cell: c(t) and h(t) enter at left, yellow K, Q, V boxes, a circled product and a plus with SoftMax produce c(t+1) on the right and a second product with Linear produces the Output
(c) at lower right is a transformer layer as a row: LayerNorm -> RSA -> plus, LayerNorm -> MLP -> plus, with residual wires looping underneath each pair

channels.colour: in (a) colour = attention scale (green scale 1, orange scale 2, blue scale 3) from patches to cuboids to bars, then grey = after the linear layer; in (b) and (c) yellow and white fill only mark operation boxes, a separate use of fill
channels.shape: wireframe cuboids = Q/K/V tensors (subdivision = number of tokens at that scale), solid bars = attended features, rounded boxes = operations, circled glyphs = product/sum
channels.line: solid black arrows throughout; residual paths in (c) are rectilinear loops under the blocks
channels.frame: square brackets group each scale head's Q/K/V; panels are unframed and lettered (a)-(c)

quality.strengths: the multi-scale idea is carried by one colour per scale from the patches on a real MRI slice through the cuboids to the concatenated bars, so the reader traces each scale; the token count per scale is drawn as cuboid subdivision; the three scale heads are identical rows, easy to compare; (b) draws the recurrent update as its terms rather than a formula block
quality.weaknesses: the hidden states c(t)/h(t) in (b) are not tied to (a) or (c) by any line or colour, so how the recurrent cell sits inside the layer is left to the reader; the 'Liner' label is a typo for Linear; the large Q/K/V grid takes most space while the recurrence (the 'Recurrent' in RSA) is a small panel; ellipses in the concatenated column hide how many bars there are

figures.lesson: Give each attention scale one colour and carry it from that scale's patches on the input scan, through its Q/K/V cuboids, into its slot of the concatenated token row.

figures.title: Flow Straight and Fast: Learning to Generate and Transfer Data with Rectified Flow

taxonomy.task: learning straight-path ODE transport between two distributions (rectified flow) and straightening it by repeated reflow
taxonomy.note: architecture 'other': no network is drawn, only trajectories on 2-D toy data; training 'other': the flow is fit to straight-line interpolations of a coupling, then refit on its own coupling (reflow). modality 'image' is the paper's main application; the figure itself draws 2-D points.

arrangement.units: four unframed plots in one row separated by whitespace, a crossing-arrows glyph between plots 2 and 3, a bordered legend box at the right end
arrangement.inputs_as: purple point clouds (pi_0) at the left of every plot; the targets are red point clouds at the right
arrangement.shared: the same two source and two target clouds are redrawn in every plot at the same positions

insights.structure: Four same-size plots in a row are the four steps of the procedure, with the crossing-arrows glyph placed at the hinge between the first rectification and the reflow.
insights.data: Source and target distributions are drawn as purple and red point clouds in the same four positions in every plot, and the transport as bundles of individual trajectories.
insights.emphasis: The contribution shows as the change in geometry: crossing dashed bundles in plot 1, uncrossed solid bundles in plot 2, parallel straight bundles in plot 4.
insights.flow: Left-to-right reading order with no arrows between plots; the step order is carried by position and by the X_0 (Z_0) / Z_1 relabelling in the middle glyph.
insights.avoid: The panel letters and step names live only in the caption, so without it the reader cannot tell which plot is interpolation and which is the learned flow except through the legend.

core.what: the procedure unrolled as four identical toy plots in a row: interpolation (dashed), rectified flow (solid, uncrossed), interpolation of the new coupling, reflow (solid, straight)

relations.form: two rounds of interpolate-then-rectify drawn as plots 1-2 and 3-4 on the same point clouds, the second round's bundles straight and parallel
the transport is drawn on a small 2-D instance: two purple source clouds at left, two red target clouds at right, bundles of trajectories between them
a crossing-arrows glyph between plots 2 and 3 enlarges one intersection: dashed straight paths X_0 to X_1 cross, solid paths bend away to Z_1 and X_1
within each round the dashed interpolation plot sits immediately left of the solid flow plot on identical clouds, so the two couplings are compared by position

channels.colour: purple = source distribution pi_0, red = target pi_1; blue and green separate the two trajectory families in every plot and in the glyph
channels.line: dashed = linear interpolation, solid = rectified flow (keyed in the legend); one meaning throughout
channels.frame: only the legend is framed; plots are unframed and separated by whitespace

quality.strengths: The procedure is shown as geometry on one toy instance repeated four times, so crossing, uncrossing and straightening are visible without reading; line style carries exactly one meaning (interpolation vs flow) and is keyed; the hinge glyph enlarges the one event (rewiring at an intersection) the method rests on.
quality.weaknesses: No panel letters, step names or arrows between plots inside the figure, so the order and the split into two rounds depend on the caption; the second and third plots are spaced like the others, so the reflow boundary is marked only by the small glyph; the legend at the far right is detached from the plots it keys.

figures.lesson: Teach a procedure on a toy instance by repeating one plot per step with the same point clouds, so only the trajectories change, and key the step type (interpolation vs learned flow) by line style alone.

figures.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning

taxonomy.task: verbal self-reflection for LLM agents

arrangement.units: One grey framed 'Agent' region holding the loop of modules; the environment sits below it outside the frame; an algorithm box on the right half.
arrangement.inputs_as: the environment box below the agent frame
arrangement.losses_at: no loss; feedback arrows run inside the frame
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Panel (a) is a light-grey square 'Agent' container holding five rounded boxes (Self-reflection, Evaluator, Actor as LM roles; Trajectory and Experience as memories) with the Environment box below and outside; panel (b) beside it is Algorithm 1 pseudocode at equal height.
insights.data: Components are text-only rounded boxes; LM roles are blue-grey and memories pale yellow, each with its memory type in parentheses on a second line.
insights.emphasis: The contribution is the inner loop Trajectory -> Evaluator -> Self-reflection -> Experience -> Actor drawn above the classic Action/Obs-Reward loop, distinguished by the two colour families rather than an accent.
insights.flow: Elbowed orthogonal arrows: Actor out right to Environment (Action), back up the left edge (Obs / Reward) into Trajectory and Self-reflection; inner arrows labelled Internal feedback, External feedback, Reflective text.
insights.avoid: The External feedback line runs along the container's left edge and overlaps the outer loop line, so the two returns are hard to separate.

core.what: two nested loops in panel (a): the classic agent-environment loop (Actor -> Action -> Environment -> Obs/Reward -> back into the Agent box) and, inside the grey Agent container, the reflection loop Trajectory -> Evaluator -> Self-reflection -> Experience -> Actor drawn above it

relations.form: elbowed orthogonal lines leave the Actor on the right, drop to an Environment box below the Agent container ('Action'), and return along the left edge ('Obs / Reward') into Trajectory and up into Self-reflection as 'External feedback'

inside the container short vertical and horizontal arrows run Trajectory -> Evaluator ('Internal feedback') -> Self-reflection -> 'Reflective text' -> Experience -> Actor -> Trajectory, a loop over the stacked boxes
two pale-yellow memory boxes, Trajectory (short-term memory) and Experience (long-term memory), sit beside the LM boxes and feed the Actor from the left and from above
panel (b) is Algorithm 1 pseudocode at equal height to the right of the diagram, restating the loop as a while-loop rather than drawing it

channels.colour: fill = kind of component: blue-grey = LM roles (Self-reflection, Evaluator, Actor), pale yellow = memories (Trajectory, Experience), light grey = the Agent container and Environment; one meaning, keyed by '(LM)' / '(... memory)' subtitles
channels.shape: rounded boxes = components, a square-cornered grey box = Environment; no data glyphs
channels.line: solid thin grey arrows throughout with orthogonal elbows; feedback types are only text labels on the lines
channels.frame: a large light-grey square = the agent boundary, with Environment outside it

quality.strengths: the agent boundary frame separates the new inner reflection loop from the classic environment loop, and the two-colour code (LM roles vs memories) states the components' kinds without a legend; arrows are short inside the container
quality.weaknesses: no data is drawn - the reflective text, the trajectory and the reward never appear as examples, so the 'verbal' reinforcement that defines the method is invisible; the outer loop's wires run the full height of the figure along the left and right edges; the external-feedback wire snakes from the left edge over to Self-reflection; half the width is pseudocode that repeats the loop in text

figures.lesson: Draw the agent as one large container and the environment as a box outside it, close the classic loop with Action / Obs-Reward elbow arrows around the container, and colour the boxes by kind: model roles in one cool tint, short- and long-term memory in one warm tint.

figures.title: REPLUG: Retrieval-Augmented Black-Box Language Models

taxonomy.task: retrieval augmentation for black-box LMs via ensembling

arrangement.units: unframed overview on the left; one tinted rounded detail panel on the right with three parallel rows
arrangement.inputs_as: grey box with the test context sentence
arrangement.shared: colour identity for documents (blue) and context (grey) across both halves

insights.structure: Left ~40%: an unframed overview on a loose 2x2 grid (Retriever, retrieved documents, test context, black-box LM); right ~60%: a pale-yellow rounded 'Ensemble' panel expanding the Input Reformulation step, tied to the overview by a speech-bubble pointer.
insights.data: Documents are light-blue rounded boxes and the test context grey boxes with real example text; the LM is a black cube with an orange question mark; each of three rows ends in a small horizontal bar chart over apple/pear/not.
insights.emphasis: The Retriever is a solid dark-red block and retrieval labels are dark red, while the ensemble panel's per-row bar colours (green, purple, pink) are stacked into one merged chart via a curly brace.
insights.flow: Thick grey arrows: context up to Retriever, right to documents, down into the LM, output 'Apple' below; in the panel three parallel left-to-right rows converge through a brace to the merged distribution.

core.what: a dark-red Retriever block left of the main flow sends light-blue stacked document cards (with real text) down into the black-box LM, which the grey test-context box enters from the left

relations.form: Test Context box -> up arrow 'Document Retrieval' -> Retriever -> right arrow -> a stack of three light-blue document cards with real sentences, then a down arrow into the LM cube
the document arrow from above and the test-context arrow from the left converge on one black cube labelled Black-box LM, which outputs 'Apple' below
a pale-yellow rounded 'Ensemble' panel on the right, attached by a speech-bubble pointer at the 'Input Reformulation' label, expands the LM step

inside the panel, three identical rows each prepend a different document d_i (blue card) to the same context x (grey card), feed an identical black cube and end in a small bar chart over apple/pear/not
a right curly brace gathers the three per-row bar charts into one stacked bar chart whose segments keep each row's colour (green, purple, pink)

channels.colour: fill = kind of data: light blue = retrieved document, grey = test context, black cube = the frozen LM; bar colour = which document the probability came from; dark red marks both the Retriever block and the math labels d_i and x, so red carries 'retrieval' and 'variable name' at once
channels.shape: rounded text cards = data with real text, black 3-D cube with a question mark = black-box model, bar charts = output distributions
channels.line: thick grey arrows in the overview, thin black arrows inside the ensemble panel; no line-style distinction of meaning
channels.frame: one tinted rounded panel = the expanded ensemble step; the overview is unframed

quality.strengths: documents and context are drawn as real sentences, and the per-document output distributions are drawn as bar charts, so what is ensembled is visible; the three ensemble rows are identical copies differing only in the document; the brace-to-stacked-bar merge shows the weighting as geometry
quality.weaknesses: the largest, most saturated element is the off-the-shelf Retriever (solid dark-red block) while the ensemble contribution sits in a pale panel; the speech-bubble tie to 'Input Reformulation' points at a label rather than at the LM node it expands; red is shared between the retriever and generic math symbols

figures.lesson: The ensemble is drawn as data, not as an operator box: each pass gets its own bar colour, and a curly brace gathers the three bar charts into one stacked chart whose segments keep those colours, so each document's contribution stays visible in the merged result.

figures.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition

taxonomy.task: image classification
taxonomy.note: architecture other: a deep stack of conv layers with identity skip connections around each pair (residual blocks); the taxonomy has no residual/skip-connection key.

arrangement.units: Three unframed columns side by side, each headed by its model name; rows aligned across columns by output size, with an 'output size' label in the left margin.
arrangement.inputs_as: a plain text label 'image' at the top of each column
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn (each column ends in an 'fc 1000' box)
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Three tall columns (VGG-19, plain, residual) stand side by side with rows aligned so equal output size sits at equal height, and long empty arrows in the VGG column keep it in register.
insights.data: Every layer is a small tinted box with its kernel, width and stride written inside, and the output resolution is a left-margin label rather than a drawn tensor.
insights.emphasis: The residual column repeats the plain column box for box and adds only curved shortcut arcs on its right, solid for identity and dotted where the dimensions change.
insights.flow: Each column reads strictly top to bottom on short straight arrows; the shortcut arcs bow out to the right and rejoin the column two boxes lower.
insights.avoid: The figure is extremely tall and narrow with very small box text, so it only works at full page height; a shorter version would group repeated layers with a repeat count.

core.what: three equal columns side by side (VGG-19, 34-layer plain, 34-layer residual, ours last) with rows registered by output size, the residual column identical to the plain one except for the shortcut arcs on its right

relations.form: three unframed columns headed by model name, the plain and residual columns box-for-box identical so the shortcut arcs are the only difference
each column reads top (image) to bottom (fc) along short straight downward arrows between layer boxes
'output size: 224/112/56/28/14/7/1' labels in the left margin mark horizontal bands across all three columns, and box tint changes per band
curved arcs on the right of the residual column leave above a pair of boxes and rejoin two boxes lower, solid for identity shortcuts, dotted where the dimension changes

channels.colour: box tint = output-size stage (blue, orange, lavender, green, pink, grey-blue per resolution), consistent across all three columns; white = fully connected layers
channels.shape: all layers are identical small rectangles with kernel, width and stride written inside; pooling is a text label on the arrow, not a box
channels.line: solid arc = identity shortcut, dotted arc = projection shortcut where dimensions increase; straight arrows = forward flow
channels.frame: no frames; columns and margin labels do the grouping

quality.strengths: the comparison is pure geometry: equal-width columns aligned row-by-row so a reader sees the depth difference against VGG and the single added element (arcs) against plain; each channel has one meaning (tint = resolution stage, arc style = shortcut type); shortcut arcs are short and repeat regularly
quality.weaknesses: very tall aspect; VGG's column uses long empty arrows to stay in register, leaving large blank stretches; no tensors or data are drawn, only layer names, and the arcs (the contribution) are thin black lines no more salient than the forward arrows

figures.lesson: Draw the proposed network as an exact copy of its baseline column with only the new connections added, and align both columns row by row, so the contribution is the visible difference.

figures.title: Restormer: Efficient Transformer for High-Resolution Image Restoration

taxonomy.task: high-resolution image restoration (denoising, deblurring, deraining)

arrangement.units: Top row: input photo -> conv -> Transformer level 1 ... refinement -> conv -> output photo, unframed. Left/middle: the U (encoder column down, decoder column up), unframed. Right: two full-width tinted panels (b) GDFN and (a) MDTA, each a borderless tinted rectangle labelled in its top-right corner; lower-left: a framed legend box.
arrangement.inputs_as: a real degraded photo top-left, mirrored by the restored photo top-right, joined by a long global residual line over the top
arrangement.shared: none; repeated Transformer blocks are drawn once per level with an 'x L_i' repeat count

insights.structure: A U-shaped encoder/decoder occupies the left two columns while two tinted detail panels (GDFN above, MDTA below) fill the right, with the glyph legend boxed in the lower-left corner.
insights.data: Only the degraded and restored real photos appear (top-left and top-right); every intermediate is a line labelled with its tensor size such as H/4xW/4x4C, and the attention is a tiny grey C-hat x C-hat matrix inside panel (a).
insights.emphasis: The proposed MDTA and GDFN are coloured yellow and cyan inside one expanded decoder block and blown up into panels whose background tint matches the wedge leading from that block.
insights.flow: The main path reads left to right along the top row, drops down the encoder column via red downsample arrowheads, climbs back up via green upsample arrowheads, and each detail panel reads left to right ending in a circled + at the right edge.
insights.avoid: The 14-entry legend repeats glyphs that are already labelled in place and the translucent wedges cross the decoder's skip lines, so the left-centre gets crowded.

core.what: one decoder Transformer block opened into its MDTA (yellow) and GDFN (cyan) parts, each blown up into a full-width tinted detail panel on the right, tied by translucent wedges whose tint matches the part

relations.form: a top row runs degraded photo -> 3x3 conv -> Transformer Block -> ... -> Refinement -> 3x3 conv -> + -> restored photo, with a global residual line over the top
a U on the left: encoder blocks step down a column via red downsample triangles (L1..L4, sizes H/2..H/8 written beside), decoder blocks climb back up via green upsample triangles
horizontal skip lines from each encoder level end in circled-C concatenation nodes on the decoder column, followed by a blue 1x1 bar
wedges from the expanded GDFN/MDTA block fan out to panel (b) GDFN (pale cyan) and panel (a) MDTA (pale beige), each a left-to-right chain from X to X-hat with its own residual line
in panel (a) the transposed attention map A is drawn as a small grey C-hat x C-hat matrix between the Q-K product and the V product

channels.colour: fill = operation type, keyed in a framed legend (orange Transformer block, yellow MDTA, cyan GDFN, red Norm, green depth-wise conv, blue 1x1); panel tint repeats the colour of the part it expands; red text marks the C-hat dimension in panel (a)
channels.shape: rounded rectangles = blocks, red/green triangles = down/upsample, circled glyphs = element-wise ops; 1x1 conv is a blue trapezoid in panel (b) but a blue rectangle in panel (a) and the U
channels.line: solid arrows only; tensor sizes written on the lines
channels.frame: tinted borderless panels = a zoomed module; a framed box = legend

quality.strengths: the novel modules get roughly half the area as zoom panels while the routine U is compact; colour per operation type is keyed and reused across overview and panels; the attention map is drawn as a matrix so the transposed (channel) attention is visible
quality.weaknesses: the 1x1 conv changes shape between panels; tensor-size labels on almost every line crowd the U; the zoom wedges are drawn across the decoder skip connections; the legend occupies a full column of the left edge

figures.lesson: Put a hierarchical U on the left two-thirds and expand the proposed sub-blocks into tinted detail panels on the right, tying each panel to its tiny source box by a translucent wedge of the same tint.

figures.title: Retinexformer: One-stage Retinex-based Transformer for Low-light Image Enhancement

taxonomy.task: low-light image enhancement

arrangement.units: three tinted square-cornered background panels: one full-width top band, two half-width detail panels below
arrangement.inputs_as: real low-light photo plus illumination prior map
arrangement.shared: op-type colour coding and a shared legend across panels

insights.structure: A pale-green full-width band (a) holds the illumination estimator (i) on the left and the U-shaped corruption restorer (ii) on the right; below, a cream panel (b) details the attention block and a peach panel (c) details the illumination-guided self-attention, each titled in bold coloured text top-left.
insights.data: Real photos for input, light-up map, lit-up and enhanced images; feature maps as stacks of coloured slabs; layers as oblique 3-D cuboids and thin parallelogram slabs coloured by op type (yellow IGAB, blue LN, green stride conv, orange deconv), with tensor sizes in grey beside each.
insights.emphasis: The light-up feature F_lu is drawn as a real colour-mapped image and routed by long lines from (a) into the IG-MSA blocks of (b) and (c), plus coloured callouts (i over-exposure, ii amplified noise) showing the problem being fixed.
insights.flow: Estimator left to right; restorer encoder runs right along the top row, turns down at the right edge and returns left along the bottom to the enhanced image; panel (c) runs left to right through Q/K/V token stacks to the output feature.
insights.avoid: Very dense: two legend boxes, many grey size labels and long cross-panel lines make it crowded at column width.

core.what: a full-width band (a) holds two titled stages side by side: (i) Illumination Estimator on the left turning the input image and illumination prior into a lit-up image and light-up feature, (ii) the U-shaped Corruption Restorer on the right producing the enhanced image

relations.form: band (a) split into (i) Illumination Estimator (left, real photos and colour-mapped maps) and (ii) Corruption Restorer (right, a U of yellow IGAB cuboids), each captioned in bold below
inside (ii) the U runs right along the top (conv, IGAB, stride-conv slabs), down the right side, and back left along the bottom to I_re, then + I_lu into the Enhanced Image
the light-up feature F_lu, drawn as a real colour-mapped image, leaves (i) on a long line down into IG-MSA in panel (b) and on to the Y branch of panel (c), where it multiplies the value tokens
panel (b) (cream) expands one IGAB into LN -> IG-MSA -> + -> LN -> FFN -> +; panel (c) (peach) expands IG-MSA into tokenised Q/K/V stacks, a C x C attention map and positional encoding
in panel (c) features are reshaped into rows of small token squares (orange Q, green K, blue V) and the attention is a small dark C x C matrix
blue and red squares on the lit-up and enhanced images lead to boxed crop insets labelled i (over-exposure) and ii (amplified noise, colour distortion)

channels.colour: layer colour = operation type, keyed in a top legend (yellow IGAB, beige conv 1x1, blue depth-wise conv, brown conv 3x3, green stride conv, orange deconv); token colour = Q/K/V role; blue/red insets = the two corruption types; panel tint = which part is expanded - colour carries at least three meanings
channels.shape: oblique 3-D cuboids and parallelogram slabs = layers, real images and colour maps = data, circled glyphs = element-wise ops
channels.line: solid black arrows only; blue and red thin lines tie image regions to their crop insets
channels.frame: tinted square-cornered panels = (a) whole model, (b) and (c) detail; rounded boxes = legends and corruption insets

quality.strengths: intermediate data is drawn as real images (light-up map, lit-up image, colour-mapped light-up feature), so the illumination guidance is visible as data; the guided attention is drawn as token stacks and an attention matrix rather than a block; each operation type is keyed
quality.weaknesses: the F_lu guidance line runs diagonally across the band border and then the full width of panel (b) into (c), the longest wire in the figure; colour carries op type, Q/K/V role, corruption type and panel identity at once; the corruption insets sit in the middle of the band between the two stages; the detail panels are tied to their parent block only by titles and approximate tint

figures.lesson: Each detail panel's background tint repeats the fill of the block it expands (cream-yellow panel for the yellow IGAB cuboid, peach panel for the salmon IG-MSA block), and one guidance line runs from the overview across the panel border into both detail panels, so the reader can follow both the zoom-in and the conditioning signal.

figures.title: Retentive Network: A Successor to Transformer for Large Language Models

taxonomy.task: language modelling with parallel training and recurrent inference

arrangement.units: (a) Parallel representation: unenclosed vertical stack on white; (b) Recurrent representation: a light-blue rounded panel holding the per-step cell, with state and output arrows running out of it; captions (a)/(b) below each
arrangement.inputs_as: the typeset symbol X (and X_n with the word 'Input' in (b))
arrangement.shared: the same symbols Q, K, V and the GN pill appear in both panels; nothing is linked between them

insights.structure: Two panels sit side by side, an unenclosed narrow parallel-form stack on the left and a wider light-blue recurrent-cell panel on the right, each captioned (a)/(b) underneath.
insights.data: All intermediates are typeset math symbols floating on the canvas (Q, K, V, S_{n-1}, O_n) rather than boxed tensors, and the parallel computation is written as one equation instead of drawn.
insights.emphasis: The recurrent form is the only part on a tinted background, and its state line S_{n-1} to S_n runs straight across the panel as the longest line in the figure.
insights.flow: Panel (a) reads bottom-to-top from X to GN; panel (b) reads bottom-up from X_n into Q/K/V, then left-to-right along the state line and out through GN to O_n on the right.
insights.avoid: Panel (a) collapses the whole parallel computation into a single equation with no visual counterpart to the decay matrix D, so the two forms cannot be matched piece by piece.

core.what: two side-by-side computations of the same retention - (a) the parallel form as a bottom-up stack ending in one equation, (b) the recurrent form as a tinted per-step cell with a state line running across it

relations.form: (a) narrow unframed stack on the left and (b) wider light-blue cell on the right, captioned underneath, sharing the symbols Q/K/V and the GN pill but not drawn as identical panels
(a) reads bottom-to-top: X branches into Q, K, V, which join into the typeset expression (QK^T ⊙ D)V and then GN
(b) a straight horizontal state line S_{n-1} -> + -> S_n crosses the top of the cell, with only one step drawn
in (b) V_n and K_n meet at a circled-x node whose output joins the decayed state at a circled +, and Q_n multiplies the new state before GN gives O_n

channels.colour: blue marks operations (GN pills, circled op nodes) and the light-blue tint marks the recurrent cell; data are black typeset symbols
channels.shape: pills = group norm, circles = element-wise/matrix ops, bare math symbols = tensors
channels.line: solid black arrows only
channels.frame: the tinted rounded rectangle = one recurrent step; panel (a) has no frame

quality.strengths: the recurrent state is the longest, straightest line in the figure so the recurrence reads at a glance; the two panels use the same symbols so the equivalence is implied
quality.weaknesses: panel (a) typesets the whole computation as one equation instead of drawing it, so the two forms cannot be compared element for element; the panels have different widths, orientations and framing; only one recurrent step is drawn, not unrolled; the decay γ is a small label on the state line

figures.lesson: When a method has two equivalent forms, draw both side by side with the same variable names and let the second panel add only the extra pieces (the state line, the operators), so the reader sees what changes.

figures.title: Improving language models by retrieving from trillions of tokens

taxonomy.task: language modelling with chunk-wise retrieval

arrangement.units: one overview made of two rows (retriever on top inside a purple dashed frame, layer stack below with the repeated block in an orange dashed frame) plus a separate red-dashed zoom panel on the right expanding one block
arrangement.inputs_as: a vertical column of chunk-coloured token cells, plus a 'Retrieval dataset' cylinder at top-left
arrangement.shared: the encoded neighbours E1, E2 are drawn in both the overview and the zoom panel

insights.structure: The left two-thirds stacks a retrieval row (dataset cylinder, purple dashed 'Frozen kNN Retriever' with two BERT boxes, Transformer Encoder, encoded neighbours) over a layer row (EMB, orange dashed 'RETRO block (x L)' holding ATTN-CCA-FFW, READ), and the right third is a red dashed zoom panel of CCA.
insights.data: Input tokens are a vertical 12-cell column coloured green/blue/yellow per chunk with curly braces C1-C3, and each chunk's retrieved neighbours are 2x5 cell strips in a paler tint of that chunk's colour.
insights.emphasis: CCA is the only red-outlined block in the stack and the zoom panel repeats that red in its dashed frame, title and inner CA boxes, tying detail to block by colour.
insights.flow: The input column feeds right through the layer row while thin coloured elbow lines climb the left edge from each chunk into the retriever, and the encoded neighbours drop down into CCA as K and V.
insights.avoid: The long chunk-routing elbows run around the whole figure's left and top edges and cross the 'Condition' line, which is hard to trace; route them shorter if copying.

core.what: a retrieval row above the model row: Retrieval dataset cylinder -> purple dashed Frozen kNN Retriever -> neighbour cell strips -> Transformer Encoder -> encoded neighbours E1, E2, which drop down as K, V into the CCA block of the layer stack

relations.form: the store (cylinder) and frozen BERT retriever sit top-left beside the main flow; retrieved neighbours are drawn as 2x5 cell strips in pale versions of their chunk's colour
bottom row left to right: token column X -> EMB -> ATTN -> CCA -> FFW -> READ, the middle three inside an orange dashed 'RETRO block (x L)' frame
input tokens are a vertical 12-cell column split by braces into chunks C1 (green), C2 (blue), C3 (yellow)
the encoded neighbours enter CCA from above as K and V while Q arrives from ATTN on the left; a 'Condition' line also runs from ATTN up into the encoder
a red dashed panel on the right redraws CCA: the hidden column H is shifted into chunks H1+, H2+, each paired with its own E_i in a red CA box, dotted lines marking chunk boundaries
chunk colour pairs each token chunk with its neighbours (green C1 -> E1, blue C2 -> E2), repeated in the zoom panel
the 'x L' in the orange dashed frame title marks the repeated block; no unrolling

channels.colour: cell fill = chunk identity (green, blue, yellow) for tokens and their neighbours; block outline colour = module (purple retriever, orange/yellow model blocks, red = CCA, the contribution); colour therefore carries both data identity and module identity
channels.shape: cylinder = dataset store, cell strips/columns = token data, tall rounded rectangles = layers
channels.line: black arrows for model flow; green and blue wires carry each chunk to the retriever; dotted horizontal lines mark chunk boundaries in the zoom
channels.frame: dashed frames = groups: purple = frozen retriever, orange = repeated block, red = zoomed CCA

quality.strengths: retrieved neighbours and tokens are drawn as data with matching chunk colours, so which chunk attends to which neighbours is visible; the zoom panel repeats the CCA red in its frame, title and CA boxes; the novel CCA is the only red block
quality.weaknesses: the green and blue chunk wires to the retriever loop out around the left edge and back across the top, a long detour; EMB, ATTN, FFW and READ are drawn as tall as CCA, so space does not follow novelty; the zoom panel has no connector to the CCA it expands

figures.lesson: Each input chunk keeps one fill colour (green, blue, yellow) everywhere it appears, in the input column, in its retrieved neighbours as a paler tint, and in the detail panel, so a reader can follow which chunk attends to which neighbours without reading labels.

figures.title: RMA: Rapid Motor Adaptation for Legged Robots

taxonomy.task: legged-robot locomotion with online adaptation

arrangement.units: three light-grey tinted bands (Phase 1, Phase 2, Deployment) with dark tab labels, the first two grouped under a section title and separated from the third by a thick grey rule
arrangement.inputs_as: rounded boxes with math symbols (states, actions, history stack, privileged environment factors)
arrangement.losses_at: between lanes: the green 'Regress' double arrow linking the two latents in the gap between Phase 1 and Phase 2
arrangement.shared: the Base Policy appears in all three bands and the simulator render is shared by both training bands at the right

insights.structure: Two sections split by a grey rule ('A) Training in Simulation', 'B) Deployment'); section A holds two grey bands tagged 'Phase 1' and 'Phase 2', section B one band, each a left-to-right chain of input box, trapezoid encoder, latent box, trapezoid base policy, a_t.
insights.data: Inputs are rounded boxes with serif math (x_t, a_t-1; a stacked history x_t-51...x_t-1 with a vertical ellipsis; a box listing mass, friction, terrain height), and the environment is a simulator render (training) or a real photo (deployment) at the right edge.
insights.emphasis: Modules trained in a phase are outlined red (explained by '*Trainable Modules in Red'), frozen ones black, and a green double arrow labelled 'Regress' joins z_t and ẑ_t across the two training bands.
insights.flow: Each band reads left to right into a_t, and dashed elbow arrows close the loop from a_t through the environment picture back over the top and under the bottom to the observation boxes.
insights.avoid: The deployment history box reads 'x_t-50, a_t-51' while phase 2 reads 'x_t-51, a_t-51' — an index inconsistency; keep labels identical across repeated bands.

core.what: three stacked grey bands - Phase 1, Phase 2 (under 'A) Training in Simulation') and Deployment (under 'B)', below a thick rule) - each the same left-to-right chain input -> trapezoid encoder -> latent -> trapezoid Base Policy -> a_t, with latents and policies aligned in columns

relations.form: Phase 1, Phase 2 and Deployment as equal-width tinted bands stacked top to bottom with dark tab labels, the Base Policy in the same column in each
a vertical green double arrow labelled 'Regress' joins z_t in Phase 1 to ẑ_t in Phase 2 across the gap between the bands
within each band: input box(es) -> trapezoid encoder/adaptation module -> small latent box -> Base Policy (with x_t, a_{t-1} entering from above) -> a_t
the x_t, a_{t-1} box above each Base Policy feeds it alongside the latent arriving from the left
dashed loops carry a_t into the environment picture (simulator render for training, real photo for deployment) and observations back over the top or under the bands into the inputs
a dashed arrow drops from Phase 1's Base Policy into Phase 2's, marking the same policy reused

channels.colour: red outline = trainable in that phase (keyed by '*Trainable Modules in Red'), black outline = frozen; green = the regression objective; grey tint = one phase
channels.shape: trapezoids = networks (narrowing encoders, widening policy), rounded boxes = data and latents; environment = a simulator render or real photo
channels.line: solid = data flow within a step; dashed = both the environment loop (actions out, observations back) and the policy hand-over from Phase 1 to Phase 2, so dashed carries two meanings
channels.frame: tinted band = one phase; a thick grey rule separates training from deployment

quality.strengths: the three phases are drawn as the same chain in aligned columns, so what changes (encoder input, which modules are red) reads by comparison; the regression is drawn between the two latents it compares; trainable vs frozen is a single keyed outline colour
quality.weaknesses: the environment loops are long dashed wires around the top and bottom of the bands; dashed also marks the weight hand-over; the history indices differ between Phase 2 (x_{t-51}) and Deployment (x_{t-50}) boxes; the Regress arrow is labelled in grey text that is less visible than the red outlines

figures.lesson: Close the agent-environment loop with dashed arrows from a_t through a picture of the environment - a simulator render in training, a real photo at deployment - back to the observation boxes, and outline only the modules trained in that phase in red.

figures.title: Reasoning on Graphs: Faithful and Interpretable Large Language Model Reasoning

taxonomy.task: knowledge-graph question answering: an LLM generates relation paths as plans, retrieves reasoning paths from the graph with them, and answers from those paths

arrangement.units: unframed, with one dashed rounded frame round the knowledge graph at the top; grey panels for relation paths (left) and reasoning paths (right); question box, LLM and answer box in a row at the bottom
arrangement.inputs_as: the quoted question in a grey box with its entity highlighted orange; a toy knowledge graph of real entities and relation labels
arrangement.losses_at: two dashed boxes: 'Planning Optimization' below the knowledge graph, joined by a hooked white arrow to P_theta(z|q) beside the LLM's planning arrow; 'Reasoning Optimization' below the answer box, joined by a U-turn white arrow to P_theta(a|q,Z,G)
arrangement.shared: one LLM box both generates the relation paths and reasons over the retrieved paths, one arrow leaving it up-left and one entering it from the upper right

insights.structure: A loop round a knowledge graph: the graph in a dashed frame at the top, path panels on both shoulders, question, LLM and answer as the bottom row.
insights.data: Every text is real: the question, three relation paths, two reasoning paths as arrow chains, both prompts and the answer; the graph is a toy one with real entities and relation labels.
insights.emphasis: The LLM is the only saturated fill and carries a flame; the entities of the question and the answer are tinted orange and pink wherever they appear.
insights.flow: The bottom row runs left to right; the loop runs up-left from the LLM through the graph and down-right back to it; two kinds of thick block arrows, keyed bottom left.
insights.avoid: Do not hang training objectives off hooked U-turn arrows placed away from the outputs they supervise.

core.what: plans rise from the LLM to the knowledge graph at the top and retrieved reasoning paths come down from it to the LLM, a loop of thick arrows round the graph

relations.form: the knowledge graph in a dashed frame at the apex, relation paths on the rising arrow and reasoning paths on the descending arrow
numbered steps 1 Planning, 2 Retrieval, 3 Reasoning along the loop LLM, relation paths, graph, reasoning paths, LLM; the question and the answer on one bottom row through the LLM
relation paths and reasoning paths are written as edge-labelled entity chains taken from the drawn graph (Joe Biden, born_in, Scranton, city_of, USA)
one LLM box is both the planner and the reasoner, the loop leaving and re-entering it

channels.colour: orange = the question's entity (in the question and the graph), pink = the answer entity (in the graph and the answer), teal = other graph entities, yellow = the LLM, dark blue text = prompts
channels.shape: pills = graph entities, grey rounded rectangles = text data (question, paths, answer), dashed rounded boxes = objectives, the yellow rounded box = the model
channels.line: filled blue-grey block arrows = inference, white outlined block arrows = instruction finetuning (keyed bottom left); thin blue arrows = graph relations
channels.frame: dashed rounded frame = the knowledge graph

quality.strengths: The plan-retrieve-reason loop is geometry: arrows rise from the LLM to the graph and descend from it back to the LLM, the graph at the apex. Relation paths and reasoning paths are drawn as their real text chains between the LLM and the graph. The question entity and the answer entity keep their orange and pink tints from the question through the graph to the answer. Arrow style is keyed for inference versus finetuning.
quality.weaknesses: Both training arrows are hooked (the planning one bends down and left, the reasoning one U-turns upward), so the objectives hang off the loop as detours. The planning objective sits under the graph, away from the relation-path panel it trains. The objectives are written as probability formulas beside the arrows. The arrow key takes the bottom-left corner beside the question box.

figures.lesson: Draw plan-then-retrieve as a loop round the knowledge graph: an arrow up from the LLM through the generated plans into the graph, an arrow down from the graph through the retrieved paths back into the LLM.

figures.title: Accurate prediction of protein structures and interactions using a 3-track network

taxonomy.task: protein structure prediction

arrangement.units: one grey tinted band per track (1D, 2D, 3D) with a boxed tag at its corner; repeated blocks are coloured outline rectangles overlaid across exactly the bands they update
arrangement.inputs_as: real data plots (MSA as a coloured matrix plot, pair features as a matrix with axes) entering the 1D and 2D bands
arrangement.shared: outputs at the right edge (SE(3)-Transformers box, combined pair map) take from both the 1D and 2D bands

insights.structure: Three grey horizontal bands stacked top to bottom (1D track, 2D track, and a 3D track under the right half only), each named by a boxed corner tag, with a yellow outline around the 2-track block and a larger blue outline around the 3-track block spanning all three bands.
insights.data: Every state is a picture of its data: viridis heatmap tiles for 1D features, dark pair maps with a bright diagonal for 2D, rainbow cartoon proteins for 3D, and the inputs are a coloured MSA plot and a pair-feature matrix with axes.
insights.emphasis: The repeated 3-track block is the largest coloured frame and the only one crossing all three bands, keyed against the smaller yellow 2-track block by a two-entry outline legend at top right.
insights.flow: States move left to right along each band, operations (Attention, Outer product & aggregation, Graph-Transformer, SE(3)-Transformer) label vertical and diagonal arrows between bands, and dashed arrows stand for skipped repeated blocks before the outputs branch up to a BB-only model and down to a full-atom model.
insights.avoid: The diagonal arrow labels ('Outer product & aggregation', rotated 'Masked Attention') are rotated and crowd the tiles; small axis tick labels on the input plots are illegible at figure size.

core.what: 1D, 2D and 3D tracks as stacked grey horizontal bands, with each repeated block drawn as a coloured outline frame spanning exactly the bands it updates - a yellow 2-track block over 1D/2D, a larger blue 3-track block over all three

relations.form: three equal-height grey bands tagged '1D track', '2D track', '3D track' in boxed corner labels, the 3D band present only under the right half
vertical and diagonal arrows between bands inside each block ('Outer product & aggregation', 'Attention', 'Masked Attention') exchange information between tracks
dashed horizontal arrows between blocks stand for the repeated blocks not drawn; the 3D structure feeds back into the next block
every state is its data: viridis feature tiles in 1D, pair maps with a bright diagonal in 2D, rainbow protein cartoons in 3D; inputs are a coloured MSA plot and a pair-feature matrix
outputs on the right: dashed lines carry 1D and 2D into 'Combine all crops' and a grey SE(3)-Transformers box, then up to a BB-only model and down via gradient-based folding to a full-atom model
panels B and C below are horizontal bar charts with error bars comparing TM-score on CASP14 and lDDT on CAMEO across methods

channels.colour: outline colour = block type (yellow 2-track, blue 3-track, keyed top-right); data colours are intrinsic to the data plots; bar colours in B and C identify methods but are reassigned between the two charts (RoseTTAFold is purple/brown in B, blue in C)
channels.shape: square heatmap tiles = sequence/pair features, protein cartoons = 3-D structure, the one grey box = SE(3) refinement module
channels.line: solid arrows = operations within a block (labelled by name), dashed = skipped repeats and the long feeds to the output stage
channels.frame: grey band = track; coloured outline = one block, spanning the tracks it couples

quality.strengths: the core novelty - a block that couples three tracks - is visible as one outline frame crossing all three bands; every intermediate is drawn as its actual data type; operations are named labels on arrows rather than boxes
quality.weaknesses: the output path at the right runs long dashed lines out of both bands; repeats are only implied by dashed arrows with no count; bar colours change meaning between panels B and C; the 3D band is drawn as a half-width band while its tag sits under the blue frame

figures.lesson: Draw the 1D, 2D and 3D representations as three stacked horizontal bands in which every state is a thumbnail of its own data (feature tile, pair map, cartoon structure), and mark one repeated block by a coloured outline that spans exactly the bands it updates.

figures.title: RRHF: Rank Responses to Align Language Models with Human Feedback without tears

taxonomy.task: aligning LLMs with human feedback by ranking
taxonomy.note: architecture other = a single policy model scoring several sampled responses against a ranking, contrasted with PPO's four-model setup

arrangement.units: two panels inside one dashed frame separated by a dashed vertical rule, each titled by a bold method name at its top-left
arrangement.inputs_as: lavender rounded pills labelled 'Query'
arrangement.losses_at: top of each panel: Advantage pill at the top of PPO, the bold 'Align by ranking' statement at top-right of RRHF
arrangement.shared: the same colour code for models, responses and queries across both panels

insights.structure: One dashed outer frame split by a dashed vertical rule into a 'PPO' half (four model boxes in a 2x2 grid around Query, Model Response, Value and Advantage pills) and an 'RRHF' half (one Language Model box above three query-response rows and a Human Label/Reward Model box).
insights.data: Models are large yellow (trained) or dark-gold (fixed) rounded boxes, queries are lavender pills, responses and scores are green pills shaded dark-to-light, and scores are numeric pills 100/80/60.
insights.emphasis: The RRHF half needs a single yellow model where PPO needs four, and its takeaway is set in large bold black text 'Align by ranking SFT from best' beside a dashed green group of three score pills.
insights.flow: In PPO the query flows bottom-up into two models with a dashed Advantage loop back around the outer edges; in RRHF responses go right into the reward box, scores rise to the bold text, and a dashed arrow returns left into the Language Model.
insights.avoid: Yellow vs dark-gold is the only cue for trained vs fixed and is never keyed; colour roles should get a small legend or label.

core.what: PPO (left) and RRHF (right) side by side inside one dashed frame, ours on the right, so the four big model blocks of PPO set against RRHF's one Language Model and one scorer read as a difference in count

relations.form: two halves of equal width headed 'PPO' and 'RRHF' in bold, each laid out on its own grid rather than as identical panels
PPO: Query -> Language Model / Value Model -> Model Response / Value -> Reward and Reference Models -> Advantage, read bottom to top

RRHF: three query rows each paired with a response from a different source (expert, ChatGPT, model), a Human Label/Reward Model assigning 100/80/60, and a dashed-framed stack of Expert/ChatGPT/Model scores above the Language Model
dashed lines return the update signal: from Advantage around both sides to the Language and Value models in PPO, from 'Align by ranking SFT from best' to the Language Model in RRHF

channels.colour: yellow = trained models, mustard = frozen scoring/reference models, green shades = responses and their scores by source (dark expert, mid ChatGPT, light model), pale blue = query; green also fills PPO's Advantage and Value, so green means both 'response/score' and 'PPO signal'
channels.shape: large rounded rectangles = models, pills = data and scores
channels.line: solid = forward data, dashed = training update
channels.frame: one outer dashed frame for the figure; a green dashed frame groups the score stack

quality.strengths: the two methods sit side by side at equal width, and model blocks are large and data pills small, so PPO's extra models are visible at a glance; response source is coded by green shade consistently from response to score
quality.weaknesses: the ranking objective is a bold text label ('Align by ranking SFT from best') rather than drawn ranked pairs; only the ChatGPT row has an arrow into the Human Label/Reward Model; the long arrow from the scores up to the text crosses the empty right side; the two halves use different layouts so parts do not line up for comparison

figures.lesson: Keep one colour code for roles across both halves (models as large yellow/gold boxes, text as green pills, queries as lavender pills) so the reader can count the models each method needs, and shade one colour family dark-to-light to tie each candidate response to its score.

figures.title: RT-1: Robotics Transformer for Real-World Control at Scale

taxonomy.task: language-conditioned robot manipulation policy
taxonomy.note: adapter-conditioning here = FiLM layers conditioning the image backbone on the sentence embedding; rl-offline = imitation learning from demonstrations

arrangement.units: one tall column: a stacked set of rounded cards for the per-frame FiLM-EfficientNet + TokenLearner tower, then separate rounded boxes for tokenized inputs, Transformer and Action, with a left column for the instruction encoder and a right column of text annotations
arrangement.inputs_as: a stack of six real robot-camera frames (top right) and a quoted instruction sentence in a rounded box (top left)
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the Action box of discrete action tokens ends at a real output photo
arrangement.shared: the per-frame image tower is drawn once as a stack of offset copies (one per frame)

insights.structure: One vertical column holds the whole policy, with the per-frame vision tower drawn as a stack of offset rounded cards, the language encoder parked in a narrow left column, and a right column of headings plus hyper-parameter text bracketed to each stage.
insights.data: The instruction is quoted text above a row of light-blue word tokens, the input and output are real robot-camera photos (a stacked six-frame input at top, a single gripper photo at bottom), and intermediates are rows of small coloured token squares (coral vision, green action) and a 9x9 dotted token grid.
insights.emphasis: Emphasis is by naming rather than highlighting: each stage gets a large right-column title with its parameter count, and FiLM conditioning is shown by repeating the typeset (1+gamma) . + beta row after every MBConv bar.
insights.flow: Data runs straight down the centre with short arrows, the sentence embedding branches out of the left column as thin horizontal light-blue lines into each FiLM row, and six pink arrows fan the per-frame tokens into the concatenated token row.
insights.avoid: The right-column text is a dense list of hyper-parameters in small grey type (pixel sizes, block counts, parameter counts) that competes with the diagram and would not survive scaling to one column.

core.what: one vertical tower read top to bottom: image history and instruction -> FiLM EfficientNet -> 9x9 vision-language tokens -> TokenLearner -> 48 tokenized inputs -> decoder-only Transformer -> 11-D discrete action -> robot photo

relations.form: a single top-to-bottom column, each stage named in large type in a right-hand text column with its sizes and parameter counts beneath
the 512-d Universal Sentence Encoder embedding runs down a pale-blue bus on the left and branches right into every (1+γ)·+β FiLM layer between the MBConv blocks
the image card and the EfficientNet/TokenLearner frame are drawn as a stack of offset copies with a 'Time' arrow, one per history image, whose outputs join into one token row
tokens are drawn as their structure: a 9x9 grid of dots, 8 small grid tiles for TokenLearner, then rows of pink squares for 8 and 48 tokens
a sine-wave glyph adds positional encoding to the token stream at a circled + from the right
repeated MBConv/FiLM pairs and self-attention layers are shown as two or three copies with vertical ellipses, scope marked by grey brackets on the right

channels.colour: pink/red = tokens (linear 1x1 conv output, token rows); blue = both the language side (instruction, encoder, 512 bus) and the Transformer's self-attention blocks; green = action; the MBConv blocks each take a different colour (orange, yellow, green, purple) that encodes nothing keyed
channels.shape: rounded bars = layers, small squares = tokens, real photos = observations, circled glyphs = FiLM/positional ops
channels.line: thin pale-blue lines for the conditioning bus, grey/pink arrows for the main flow; grey brackets mark the extent of each named stage
channels.frame: a stacked rounded frame = per-image vision backbone; thin outlined boxes = token rows and action vector

quality.strengths: language conditioning arrives on its own side bus and enters each FiLM layer at the block that uses it; tokens and actions are drawn as data with their counts; the image history is shown by stacked copies rather than a label; the right-hand text column keeps sizes out of the blocks
quality.weaknesses: blue means both 'language' and 'Transformer layer'; the four MBConv colours are decorative; the FiLM backbone takes nearly half the height although it is the pretrained part; parameter counts and specs crowd the right column

figures.lesson: For a tall single-path model, put the stage names and their hyper-parameters in a right-hand text column with vertical span brackets, keeping the drawing itself to coloured bars and token rows.

figures.title: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control

taxonomy.task: vision-language-action robot control

arrangement.units: three tall rounded outline panels left to right (data, model, deployment), each titled in grey text inset into its top border
arrangement.inputs_as: white cards each pairing a real photo with a Q:/A: example
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; training is the 'Co-Fine-Tune' arrow label along the bottom
arrangement.shared: purple answer/action boxes recur in the data panel and the model panel

insights.structure: Three grey-outlined rounded panels side by side with titles set into their top border: data examples (left), the RT-2 model (wide middle, a grey box holding a blue ViT and an orange Large Language Model panel), and closed-loop control photos (narrow right).
insights.data: Training data are photo cards with Q:/A: text and a grey token-number answer, the visual input is a 3x3 grid of robot camera frames, tokens are small pill rows, and actions are written as ΔT/ΔR vectors in purple boxes.
insights.emphasis: Actions are drawn in the same purple as the text answers of web VQA examples, and the purple thread runs from braced output tokens through 'De-Tokenize' to a 'Robot Action' box, with 'RT-2' as the largest bold text.
insights.flow: Panels are connected only by two grey elbow arrows along the bottom ('Co-Fine-Tune', 'Deploy'); inside the middle panel the prompt and images enter from the left, rise through the LLM, and output exits down via a purple elbow.
insights.avoid: The token-number answers in light grey ('A: 311 423 ...') are nearly invisible against white; the 3x3 robot frame grid is too small to read.

core.what: three titled rounded frames left to right - training data, the RT-2 vision-language-action model, closed-loop robot control - joined by grey 'Co-Fine-Tune' and 'Deploy' arrows along the bottom

relations.form: left data frame -> 'Co-Fine-Tune' arrow up into the centre model frame -> 'Deploy' arrow down-right into the right frame of robot photos with instructions

the left frame stacks three identical Q/A cards (English VQA, French VQA, a robot <task>), each with a grey token-number answer and a purple decoded answer, so robot actions share the text-answer format
orange text-token pills from the prompt and blue image tokens from the ViT (fed a 3x3 grid of robot frames) enter one orange 'Large Language Model' panel
output tokens under the LLM are bracketed and routed down to 'A: 132 114 ...', then 'De-Tokenize' to ΔT/ΔR in a 'Robot Action' box

channels.colour: orange = text tokens and the LLM (and the <task> placeholder), blue = image tokens and ViT, purple = answers/action tokens and the decoded action; grey = token-number strings and pipeline arrows
channels.shape: pills = tokens, rounded rectangles = models and answers, photos = observations
channels.line: solid grey arrows for stage transitions and data, purple line for the action-token path
channels.frame: three outlined rounded frames = data / model / deployment stages; tinted inner panels = model components

quality.strengths: the key idea - actions written as text answers - is visible because the robot card has the same form and purple answer box as the two VQA cards; tokens are drawn as coloured pills so the image and text inputs to the LLM are seen as data; the action is shown as real numbers and real robot photos
quality.weaknesses: the LLM is a single empty bar between two token rows; the purple action path loops out of the model frame and back in to reach 'De-Tokenize'; orange marks both text tokens and the whole LLM panel; the co-fine-tuning mixture is not drawn beyond the three example cards

figures.lesson: Give robot actions the same colour as the text answers in the training-data examples (purple boxes) and carry that colour along the output tokens -> de-tokenize -> ΔT/ΔR box, so 'actions are just another answer' reads without a word.

figures.title: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era

taxonomy.task: RNN-style language modelling with transformer-like parallel training

arrangement.units: left: the residual block in a light-grey rounded frame, containing two darker blue-grey sub-panels (Time Mixing, Channel Mixing); right: the full model column with the same grey frame holding collapsed Time/Channel Mixing boxes, topped by a light-blue 'RWKV-LM Head' frame
arrangement.inputs_as: a pink 'Input Embedding' box at the bottom of the right column; the left column takes a bare arrow from below
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; the head frame ends in 'Output Probabilities' text over the Softmax box
arrangement.shared: the residual block is drawn twice, collapsed on the right and expanded on the left, matched by name and frame style only

insights.structure: The expanded residual block (left) and the full model column (right) stand side by side at the same height, each in a light-grey frame, with the LM head as a separate light-blue frame on top of the right column.
insights.data: No tensors or tokens are drawn; inputs and intermediates are single-letter symbol boxes (R, K, V, mu, sigma) and the output is only the text 'Output Probabilities'.
insights.emphasis: Saturated salmon (WKV), orange (sigma) and yellow (mu) fills appear only inside the zoomed Time and Channel Mixing panels, while the collapsed blocks on the right are flat grey.
insights.flow: Both columns read bottom-to-top along a central spine, with residual lines leaving below each LayerNorm, running up the frame's left side and rejoining at a circled-plus.
insights.avoid: Nothing ties the left panel to the right one (no zoom lines or matching tint), so a reader must infer from the names that the left column is the inside of the right column's grey frame.

core.what: two towers side by side: on the right the full model (Input Embedding -> LayerNorm -> residual Time Mixing and Channel Mixing -> RWKV-LM head), on the left the same residual block opened to show the R/K/V/WKV and R'/K'/V' internals of each mixing block

relations.form: the left panel repeats the right panel's block with Time Mixing and Channel Mixing as grey tinted sub-panels containing their operations; no connector ties the two
both towers read bottom to top on straight vertical arrows, with LayerNorm before each mixing block
residual lines run up the left side of each tower and rejoin at circled + nodes above each mixing block
inside Time Mixing, σ(R) and WKV meet at a circled ⊗ before Out; in Channel Mixing σ(R') and V' meet at ⊗

channels.colour: fill = operation type: light orange LayerNorm, pale yellow token shift μ, salmon R/K/V projections, orange σ, cyan Out, green Softmax, grey mixing blocks; pink-red marks both the WKV operator and the Input Embedding, so that colour carries two meanings; blue tint = the LM head
channels.shape: all operations are rounded rectangles; circled glyphs = add/multiply
channels.line: solid arrows only; residual paths are the same weight as data paths
channels.frame: grey rounded panel = one repeated block (both towers); grey inner panels = Time/Channel Mixing; blue panel = head

quality.strengths: the WKV operator is the widest, most saturated box in the time-mixing panel; the two towers share bottom-up reading and the same operation colours; residual lines are straight and short
quality.weaknesses: the detail and overview are not tied by connector or matching position; WKV and Input Embedding share the same pink; the right tower draws loop arrows into the left and right sides of Time Mixing whose meaning is not labelled; the token-shift and recurrence that make WKV novel are a single box rather than drawn over time

figures.lesson: Put the full stack and its expanded block side by side at the same height, with the collapsed blocks in plain grey on one side and their saturated internals on the other, so colour marks where the new operators live.

figures.title: SALMONN: Towards Generic Hearing Abilities for Large Language Models

taxonomy.task: generic hearing (speech, audio events, music) by an LLM through a window-level Q-Former bridge and LoRA

arrangement.units: one composition without frames: encoders and Q-Former on the left, the feature row in the middle, LLM bar with attached LoRA box across the top, a legend box in the top-left corner
arrangement.inputs_as: clip-art icons (music notes, equalizer bars, a speaking person) at bottom-left for audio; a person-with-lightbulb icon under 'Text instruction prompt' at bottom-right
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the output is the label 'Text response' above the LLM
arrangement.shared: the LLM is one bar spanning both the auditory and the textual embedding rows

insights.structure: Two encoder boxes stacked at left feed one row of feature columns in the middle; that row and the text prompt rise into one LLM bar along the top, with LoRA attached as a separate box at the bar's right end.
insights.data: Every representation is a row of narrow rounded cells in its own keyed colour: queries, Whisper and BEATs features (stacked per frame), auditory and textual embeddings.
insights.emphasis: Salmon fill plus a flame icon marks the trained parts (Q-Former, LoRA); frozen modules are light grey with a snowflake.
insights.flow: Thin arrows fork from the audio icons into both encoders; thick black block arrows carry the main flow upward into the LLM and on to 'Text response'.
insights.avoid: The Q-Former sits at the far left and its per-window use is drawn as a long dashed line running right across the window arrows to the text prompt, which reads as if it fed the prompt.

core.what: Whisper and BEATs encoders fork from one audio input and converge into a single row of frame columns, each a blue Whisper cell stacked on a green BEATs cell, bracketed into windows that rise as grey auditory tokens

relations.form: two stacked encoder boxes send block arrows into one row where each frame column stacks a light-blue cell on a green cell, windows marked by brackets above
the auditory-embedding row and the textual-embedding row rise side by side into one LLM bar that spans both
bottom to top on thick block arrows: feature row, auditory embeddings, LLM, 'Text response'
the Window-level Q-Former is one box at the left whose use on every window is a dashed horizontal line crossing the windows' upward arrows

channels.colour: token cells: kind of representation (yellow queries, light-blue Whisper, green BEATs, dark-grey auditory, beige textual), keyed in the legend; module fill: light grey = frozen, salmon = trainable, the same meaning also carried by snowflake/flame icons; the light-grey module fill sits close to the dark-grey auditory tokens
channels.shape: wide rectangles = modules, narrow rounded cells = tokens/embeddings, clip-art icons = raw inputs and the instructing user
channels.line: thick black block arrows = main data flow, thin arrows = fork into encoders and window outputs, dashed line = the Q-Former applied across windows
channels.frame: only the legend box is framed

quality.strengths: Every compared or passed representation is drawn as a row of keyed cells between its maker and the LLM; frame-aligned stacking of the two encoders' features makes the fusion visible as geometry; frozen vs trainable is keyed and consistent; block arrows run straight upward.
quality.weaknesses: The Q-Former, the contribution, sits far from the windows it processes and is joined to them by a long dashed line that ends at the text prompt label; the salmon 'trainable' fill is not itself in the legend (only the flame icon is); the legend takes most of the top-left quarter.

figures.lesson: Stack the two encoders' feature cells frame-aligned, one colour per encoder, and bracket them into windows, so window-level fusion is visible as geometry before any label is read.

figures.title: SAM 2: Segment Anything in Images and Videos

taxonomy.task: promptable video object segmentation

arrangement.units: one unframed row of modules; time shown by faded copies behind each module rather than by panels
arrangement.inputs_as: a stack of real video frames with a diagonal 'time' arrow at the left edge; prompts as the words mask, points, box under the prompt encoder
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; the predicted mask is a real frame with a coloured overlay in the middle of the row
arrangement.shared: the memory bank's output is drawn as several return arrows over the top, one per stored frame, all landing on the single memory attention block

insights.structure: All seven parts sit on one horizontal row, with the prompt encoder dropped just below the mask decoder and a memory loop arching back over the top from the memory bank to memory attention.
insights.data: Input and output are real video frames, each a stack of fading copies receding up-left, and the output frame carries a green mask overlay; prompts are the plain words mask, points and box with up-arrows.
insights.emphasis: Recurrence is the visual idea: every module has ghosted copies behind it and the memory feedback lines fade from dark (latest) to pale (oldest), so the memory mechanism stands out without a highlight colour.
insights.flow: Short dark arrows run left to right along the row; the grey return lines leave the memory bank upward, run left along the top with right-angle bends and drop into memory attention.
