insights.avoid: The ghosted copies are very faint and the return lines stack close together, which makes it hard to count how many memories feed back.

core.what: a left-to-right per-frame chain (frame -> image encoder -> memory attention -> mask decoder -> masked frame -> memory encoder -> memory bank) closed by grey lines that run back over the top from the memory bank into memory attention, with past frames as faded stacked copies behind every element

relations.form: one horizontal row of modules joined by short dark arrows, the input photo at the left and the masked photo in the middle

every element has two or three faded copies stacked behind it along a 'time' diagonal, and four lines of decreasing darkness loop from the memory bank stack over the top into the memory attention stack
the memory bank sits at the right end of the row and its stored memories return to memory attention on the overhead lines
a lavender prompt encoder directly below the mask decoder takes mask, points and box as text labels and feeds up into the decoder with three short arrows

channels.colour: fill = module identity (green image encoder, blue memory attention, orange mask decoder, lavender prompt encoder); pink marks both memory encoder and memory bank, grouping the memory path; the mask is a green tint on the photo
channels.shape: trapezoids = encoders, rounded rectangles = other modules, photos = frames
channels.line: opacity = time: the darkest return line and front copy are the current frame, fainter lines and copies are older frames
channels.frame: no grouping frames

quality.strengths: the streaming memory is drawn as geometry: stacked faded copies give the time axis and the overhead lines give the recurrence without a separate diagram; opacity carries one meaning (age) for both copies and lines; the main row is straight with short arrows
quality.weaknesses: the memories themselves are not drawn as data - the bank is a box and its contents are only faded copies of that box; the prompts are text labels; the predicted mask is a small green tint on the photo, easy to miss

figures.lesson: Draw a streaming, frame-by-frame model by stacking faded translucent copies behind each module and the input frame, and run the memory feedback as nested right-angle return lines over the top that fade with age.

figures.title: Segment Anything

taxonomy.task: promptable image segmentation

arrangement.units: three unframed panels separated by whitespace, each captioned below with a letter and bold keyword; they are facets (task, model, data) rather than sequential stages
arrangement.inputs_as: a row of four drawn prompt squares gathered by a curly brace, plus a photo thumbnail labelled 'image'
arrangement.shared: the pale-yellow model box appears in all three panels

insights.structure: Three panels in a row separated by whitespace and captioned beneath '(a) Task', '(b) Model', '(c) Data': (a) inputs-model-output, (b) an opened pale-yellow model container with three coloured sub-blocks, (c) a model/data annotate-train loop above a large blue dataset card.
insights.data: The four prompt types are drawn literally in identical black-outlined squares (red/green dots, a rectangle, a blue blob, the words 'cat with black ears'), and input/output are photo thumbnails with a translucent blue mask on the output.
insights.emphasis: The model keeps one pale-yellow identity colour in all three panels, and captions bold the keyword and the acronyms SAM and SA-1B.
insights.flow: Panels (a) and (b) read bottom-to-top from prompt/image to 'valid mask'; panel (c) is a clockwise loop of thin arrows labelled annotate and train with a dashed grey arrow down to the dataset card.
insights.avoid: Panel (c)'s dataset card uses a tiny photo and four grey bullets that read as text clutter beside the diagram panels.

core.what: a segmentation prompt and an image converge on one model that outputs a valid mask - in (a) four prompt glyphs gathered by a brace plus a photo, in (b) a small prompt encoder and a large image encoder feeding one lightweight mask decoder

relations.form: (a) a brace collects the prompt squares and an arrow from the image photo meets them at a wide yellow 'model' box, with the masked photo above; (b) prompt and image arrows rise from below into their encoders and then into the decoder bar
(a) four equal white squares side by side show the prompt types: points (coloured dots), a box, a mask blob, and text 'cat with black ears'
(b) is a large pale-yellow panel with the same tint as (a)'s 'model' box, opening it into the prompt encoder, image encoder and mask decoder
(c) top: a rectangular loop model -> annotate -> data -> train -> model drawn with right-angle arrows
(c) bottom: a grey dashed line from the 'data' pill leads to a blue rounded card listing SA-1B facts with a sample masked photo

channels.colour: yellow = the model in every panel (a, b, c); green = image encoder, purple = prompt encoder, orange = decoder; blue = data (data pill, SA-1B card) and also the blue mask-prompt blob in (a)
channels.shape: rectangles = models, pill = data, white squares = prompts, photos = images and masks
channels.line: solid grey arrows = flow; one grey dashed line = 'detail of' from data to the dataset card
channels.frame: panels separated by whitespace and captions; the yellow panel in (b) frames the model

quality.strengths: each panel has one job (task, model, data) and the yellow model tint ties all three; box size encodes cost in (b) - a large image encoder beside a small prompt encoder under a thin 'lightweight' decoder; prompts are drawn as glyphs of their kind
quality.weaknesses: panel (b) draws no data between encoders and decoder (no embedding); the data-engine loop in (c) is four words around two boxes with long right-angle arrows; blue means both 'data' and a mask prompt

figures.lesson: Show a promptable model's interface by drawing every prompt type literally in small identical squares (dots for points, a rectangle for a box, a blob for a mask, the words for text) bracketed into a single input arrow beside the image.

figures.title: Segment Anything

taxonomy.task: promptable image segmentation

arrangement.units: one unframed pipeline; modules grouped only by colour family (green image side, purple prompt side, orange decoder)
arrangement.inputs_as: a large real photo at the left, with prompts entering as word labels from the bottom
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: A single main row without containers: photo, a very wide green image encoder, a column of grey embedding squares, a circled plus, an orange mask decoder bar, then three stacked output photos; the purple prompt side (conv trapezoid, prompt encoder bar) sits under the decoder.
insights.data: The input is a large photo, the image embedding is a vertical column of five small grey squares, prompts are plain word labels (mask, points, box, text) with up-arrows, and outputs are three copies of the photo with blue masks of different extent each tagged ', score'.
insights.emphasis: Box size encodes cost: the heavyweight image encoder is the largest box while the prompt encoder and mask decoder are thin bars, and the fan to three masks shows ambiguity handling.
insights.flow: The image path runs left to right along the main row, prompts enter from below with short vertical arrows, and one branching arrow fans out to the three outputs at the right.
insights.avoid: The ', score' text beside each output is a placeholder rather than a value; show actual scores or a symbol.

core.what: one left-to-right row where the image embedding (a column of grey cells) from a large green image encoder meets prompts at a thin orange mask decoder: a dense mask prompt added via a conv at a circled +, sparse points/box/text entering from a purple prompt encoder directly below

relations.form: photo -> large green image encoder -> image embedding cells -> + -> mask decoder -> three output masks, on one straight horizontal axis
the mask input passes through a purple trapezoid conv up into a circled + on the embedding line; points, box and text pass through the prompt encoder bar up into the decoder with three short arrows
the decoder fans out into three stacked photos with different blue mask overlays, each followed by ', score', showing several valid masks for one ambiguous prompt

channels.colour: green = image side (encoder), purple = prompt side (conv and prompt encoder), orange = decoder; grey = the embedding data; blue = predicted mask overlay
channels.shape: rectangles = encoders and decoder, trapezoid = conv, stacked small squares = embedding, photos = input and outputs
channels.line: solid black arrows only, all straight
channels.frame: no grouping frames

quality.strengths: the image embedding is drawn between its encoder and the decoder; each prompt enters at the block that uses it from below; the ambiguity-aware output is drawn as three real masks with scores; all lines are short and straight
quality.weaknesses: the largest element is the image encoder (an off-the-shelf ViT, sized for cost) while the promptable decoder is a thin bar; prompts are only words under arrows; the score is a text suffix, not drawn

figures.lesson: Show an ambiguity-aware segmenter's output as a short vertical stack of the same photo with different mask extents, each tagged with a score, fanned from the decoder by one branching arrow.

figures.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation

taxonomy.task: sequential next-item recommendation
taxonomy.note: modality 'tabular' stands for item-ID interaction sequences; the photos only depict items

arrangement.units: unframed horizontal rows (embedding, self-attention band, FFN, prediction) named at the right edge, crossed by three time-step columns; a left brace groups attention + FFN as one stackable block
arrangement.inputs_as: real product photos in a curly-bracketed row labelled 'Training Action Sequence'
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the top bracketed row of product photos ('Expected Next Item') is the target
arrangement.shared: the self-attention layer is one band spanning all three columns; FFN boxes repeat per column

insights.structure: Three time-step columns run upward through four unframed rows named at the right edge, with a left brace marking attention + FFN as one stackable block and curly brackets around the input and target photo rows.
insights.data: Items are real product photos at bottom and top, each item's embedding is a solid red, green or blue bar, and the prediction bars mix those colours in proportion.
insights.emphasis: Self-attention is the only element spanning all columns: a wide salmon band with black arrows of varying thickness running from earlier positions to later ones.
insights.flow: Reading goes bottom to top along vertical arrows in each column, and inside the attention band the diagonal arrows only go up and to the right, showing causality.
insights.avoid: The fourth input photo has no column above it and the multi-colour prediction bars have no key, so the shift-by-one target and the colour mixing must be inferred from the caption.

core.what: causal self-attention drawn on a three-item sequence: one wide orange layer spanning three position columns, with arrows rising from each position's input to the same and every later position only

relations.form: three columns, one per sequence position, with item photos at the bottom (computer, mouse, printer, plus a fourth box) and the next items (mouse, printer, box) at the top, shifted by one
each column reads bottom to top: item photo -> coloured embedding bar -> self-attention layer -> FFN -> prediction bar -> expected next item
inside the self-attention layer, arrows from the first position fan to positions 2 and 3, and from position 2 to 3; prediction bars are split into the colours of the earlier items they draw on
one wide orange layer spans all positions while the FFN is drawn as an identical small box per column
a left brace over attention + FFN labelled 'One Block (Can Stack More)' stands for stacking, with no repeat drawn

channels.colour: red / green / blue = item identity, from the embedding bars into the mixed prediction bars; orange = attention layer, light blue = FFN
channels.shape: photos = items, coloured bars = embeddings and predictions, rectangles = layers
channels.line: arrows = information flow; the arrows from the first position are drawn heavier, with no key
channels.frame: braces group the input sequence, the output items, and the repeatable block

quality.strengths: the causal mask is visible as geometry (arrows only go up and to the right); the representations are drawn as coloured bars, and the prediction bars' mix of input colours shows which past items each output uses; items are real product photos
quality.weaknesses: attention arrows overlap in the orange band and their varying weight is unkeyed; the fourth input item has no column, so the one-step shift between input and target rows has to be inferred; the right-hand label column carries layer names far from their layers

figures.lesson: Draw causal self-attention as one wide band across the time-step columns with arrows that only go up-and-right, and colour each item's embedding so its share in later prediction bars is visible.

figures.title: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances

taxonomy.task: grounding LLM plans in robot affordances

arrangement.units: two unframed halves (baselines, method) side by side; the method half's core is enclosed in a dashed grey rounded container
arrangement.inputs_as: a blue speech bubble with the quoted user request, repeated over each half
arrangement.shared: the same user request bubble heads both halves

insights.structure: Two halves each headed by the same blue speech bubble; the left half stacks three rows of model-name box plus reply bubble (GPT3, LaMDA, FLAN), the right half holds a dashed rounded container with LLM and Value Functions bubbles above a combined SayCan bubble and a numbered plan bubble outside.
insights.data: Candidate skills are quoted italic phrases inside speech bubbles whose font size encodes each skill's score, with small robot photos inset in the Value Functions and SayCan bubbles.
insights.emphasis: The name is split 'Say' in LLM blue and 'Can' in value-function red, and the SayCan bubble fill is a blue-to-pink gradient, so the combination is shown by colour alone.
insights.flow: Reading is left to right from the baselines to the method; inside the container the two scorer bubbles' tails point down into the SayCan bubble, which points right to the plan.
insights.avoid: The smallest scored phrases are illegibly tiny, so the size encoding is visible but the low-scoring text cannot be read.

core.what: inside a dashed frame a blue LLM bubble and a red Value Functions bubble both point into one SayCan bubble whose fill blends blue into red, each listing the same candidate skills with font size giving that source's score

relations.form: left: GPT3, LaMDA and FLAN as three stacked blue boxes, each with a grey speech-bubble answer; right: SayCan under the same 'I spilled my drink' prompt bubble, ending in a grey bubble with a numbered plan
LLM (top left) and Value Functions (top right, with a robot photo) bubbles taper down into the SayCan bubble below them, whose list re-ranks the candidates ('find a sponge' largest)
the SayCan bubble, a robot photo, and the grey answer bubble listing 'find a sponge ... done' read left to right

channels.colour: blue = language model (LLM bubble, 'Say', prior LLM boxes), red = value functions/affordance ('Can'), blue-to-red gradient = their combination; grey = model answers
channels.shape: speech bubbles = utterances and scored candidate lists, rounded boxes = prior models, photos = robot and scene
channels.line: no connecting lines; bubble tails point to the source or target
channels.frame: a grey dashed frame encloses the SayCan system

quality.strengths: the combination is drawn rather than named: two colour-coded sources taper into one bubble that blends their colours, and the candidate lists show the scores by font size so the re-ranking is visible; the same prompt heads both halves, setting prior answers against SayCan's plan
quality.weaknesses: font size as score is unkeyed and the lowest-scored candidates are too small to read; the prior LLMs get a third of the width only to show failure; the robot photos are small and their role is not labelled

figures.lesson: Encode each candidate skill's score by its font size inside the speech bubbles, and blend the LLM bubble's blue and the value-function bubble's red into the combined bubble and the two halves of the method's name.

figures.title: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances

taxonomy.task: affordance value functions for robot skills
taxonomy.note: architecture other = a bank of skill-conditioned value functions scoring every skill from one observation

arrangement.units: three unframed panels captioned (a)-(c) below; (b) and (c) share an identical chart-plus-photo skeleton while (a) shows the module
arrangement.inputs_as: a real robot-camera photo above the module box
arrangement.shared: the same five skills listed in (b) and (c)

insights.data: Per-skill scores are bold numerals at the left spoke ends coloured green (high) or dark red (low), skill names at the right spoke ends, and bar charts with values 0 to 1.00 on a lavender background.
insights.emphasis: The pink box is the only filled shape in (a) and reuses the Value Functions pink of Figure 1; high bars in (b) are pink against near-zero pale blue bars in (c).
insights.flow: In (a) the photo arrow runs down into the box and hairline spokes fan out left and right; (b) and (c) are read as chart-then-photo pairs left to right.
insights.avoid: Bar-chart text and score numerals are small and low-contrast at column width, and the symmetric left/right spoke fans split score from skill name across the figure.

core.what: panels (b) and (c) place the same horizontal bar chart of values over five 'Pick up' skills beside two different scene photos, so the values change with the scene (apple on a table vs empty floor)

relations.form: (b) and (c) are identical bar-chart + photo pairs side by side, same skills and 0-1 axis, differing only in the scene
(a) one pink 'Value Functions' box under a scene photo fans out to twelve skill labels on its right and twelve numeric values on its left
in (a) each value (green high, dark red low) is matched to its skill only by row, across the box

channels.colour: pink = value functions and value bars; value numbers green for high (0.6-0.8) and dark red for low (0.1-0.2)
channels.shape: rounded box = the value function, small circles = output nodes, bars = values, photos = scenes
channels.line: thin curved fan lines from the box to each output circle
channels.frame: none; panels separated by whitespace and (a)-(c) captions

quality.strengths: values are drawn as numbers and bars beside the real scene photo, so the affordance grounding is shown on data; (b) and (c) are identical layouts so the scene-dependence reads by comparison
quality.weaknesses: in (a) values and skill names sit on opposite sides of the box, so pairing them needs row counting; the bars in (c) are near-invisible thin slivers; nothing ties (a) to (b)/(c); the panel captions are the only description of what changes

figures.title: SayPlan: Grounding Large Language Models using 3D Scene Graphs for Scalable Robot Task Planning

taxonomy.task: LLM task planning for robots over large 3-D scene graphs by semantic search of a collapsed graph and simulator-checked iterative replanning

arrangement.units: an unframed overview strip of five lavender graph panels on top; below it an unframed two-loop diagram split left (semantic search) and right (iterative replanning) about the central LLM, with dashed grey frames around each prompt and around the filmstrip
arrangement.inputs_as: a quoted instruction in a blue speech bubble ('Make Peter a coffee') at top centre, a 3-D render of the office at top-left, and the same quote again inside each prompt
arrangement.losses_at: none (training-free); a red dashed 'Simulator Feedback' box with a quoted error feeds the replanning prompt
arrangement.shared: one LLM box serves both loops; the scene graph simulator is drawn twice (steps 3 and 9) as the same yellow box with a graph-and-document icon

insights.structure: A thin overview strip of five graph panels across the top, and below it two loops placed symmetrically left and right of one central LLM box, with a filmstrip of search states at bottom-left.
insights.data: The scene graph is always a small tree of red, green and blue sphere nodes, plans and graph API calls are code-like text boxes, the instruction is a quoted speech bubble, and simulator feedback is a quoted error in a red dashed box.
insights.emphasis: The central yellow LLM box is the biggest saturated element, and the two method phases are named in bold capitals with refresh glyphs on either side of it.
insights.flow: The top strip reads left to right through wide lilac arrows; the left loop runs prompt 1 -> LLM -> API call 2 -> simulator 3 -> expanded graph 4 -> back to the prompt, and the right loop runs prompt 5 -> LLM -> high-level plan 6 -> path planner 7 -> executable plan 8 -> simulator 9 -> feedback back to the prompt, all with wide grey block arrows and numbered circles.
insights.avoid: Yellow fills both the LLM and its tools (scene graph simulator, path and motion planners), and pink fills both plans and the feedback arrow, so fill does not separate reasoner, tool and data.

core.what: the method drawn on a toy 3-D scene graph: the same small red/green/blue sphere-node tree appears at every stage (full, collapsed to room level, partly expanded, plan path highlighted in yellow) and inside each prompt and filmstrip frame

relations.form: a small tree glyph with level-coloured sphere nodes drawn in every graph panel, collapsing and expanding from panel to panel, the plan path traced in yellow in the last top panel
top strip: five lavender panels left to right joined by wide lilac arrows labelled '3D Scene Graph', 'Collapse Graph', 'Semantic Search', 'Iterative Replanning'
two loops of wide grey block arrows on either side of the central LLM, each step marked by a numbered circle (1-4 on the left, 5-10 on the right) and each loop labelled with a refresh glyph
one central LLM box that both loops enter and leave, the left loop on its left side and the right loop on its right
'Full Search Sequence': five graph thumbnails unrolled in a row inside a dashed frame, the final one outlined green

channels.colour: lavender = scene-graph panels; blue = instruction and prompt specifications; yellow = the LLM and also its tools (simulator, path planner, motion planner); light green = the graph API call; pink/red = plans and the simulator-feedback arrow; inside the graph glyph node colour = hierarchy level and yellow = plan path. Yellow and pink each carry two meanings
channels.shape: rounded boxes for modules and data alike; sphere-node trees = scene graph; monospace text boxes = API calls and plans; speech bubble = instruction; refresh glyph = loop; robot render = execution
channels.line: wide grey block arrows = flow in both loops; wide lilac arrows = overview stages; a pink block arrow = simulator feedback; a green block arrow = executable plan to motion planner
channels.frame: dashed grey frame = one prompt (instruction, specifications, graph, memory) or the search filmstrip; numbered circles give step order

quality.strengths: the scene graph is drawn as the same tree glyph at every step, so what the method does to the graph (collapse, expand, trace a path) is visible without reading; the two phases sit symmetrically either side of one central LLM; prompts are drawn as their real parts (quoted instruction, specification list, graph, memory dots) and plans as code; the search is also unrolled as a filmstrip
quality.weaknesses: dense: ten numbered steps, two loops, an overview strip and a filmstrip in one figure; yellow fills both the LLM and its tools and pink both plans and feedback; the two loops turn in opposite directions and need the numbered circles to be followed; the graph glyphs are small, so node colours are hard to read at print size; the strip's last panels repeat what the loops below show

figures.lesson: Put the one LLM in the centre and draw its two uses as two loops on either side, and show the state at every step as the same small scene-graph glyph so the reader watches the graph collapse and expand.

figures.title: SCAFFOLD: Stochastic Controlled Averaging for Federated Learning

taxonomy.task: federated optimisation under client drift
taxonomy.note: modality multi = the method is data-agnostic; the figure is a parameter-space sketch with no data

arrangement.units: one unframed vector sketch with labels placed at path ends
arrangement.inputs_as: a dark filled circle labelled x (starting parameters)
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; optima squares at the right stand for the objectives
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: A parameter-space sketch with no containers: two clients' iterate chains diverge from a start point x (client 1 up, client 2 down), a dark 'server' point sits between them, optima are square markers to the right, and a legend column fills the far right.
insights.data: Iterates are filled circles (dark start and server, blue client iterates, pale grey intermediate averages), optima are squares (blue true optimum x*, orange client optima x1*, x2* joined by a dashed line), and small white squares mark centralised SGD steps.
insights.emphasis: No method is drawn; the problem is made visible as geometry — the server point lands off the true optimum because blue client chains bend toward their orange optima.
insights.flow: Reading is left to right from x along colour-coded thin arrows (blue client steps, green server steps, black vertical drift arrows), ending at the legend.
insights.avoid: Legend arrows are drawn as tiny vertical strokes that are hard to match to the thin diagonal arrows in the sketch; the grey intermediate circles are not keyed.

core.what: federated updates drawn as iterates in a 2-D parameter plane: from a dark start point x, blue client steps head toward client 1 and client 2, green server steps go to grey averages, and orange client optima x1*, x2* and a blue true optimum x* are placed as squares off to the right

relations.form: circles are iterates placed in parameter space; client optima and the true optimum are squares at their positions, with a dashed line joining x1* and x2*
two rounds unrolled left to right: x splits into y1 (up) and y2 (down), each client takes further blue steps along its own path, and the server node is drawn after the second round
green server-update arrows run from x and from the first-round iterates into grey midpoint circles between the two client paths, averaging them
vertical black 'client drift' arrows with small white 'SGD update' squares connect grey/server points with client points to mark how far each client wanders

channels.colour: arrow colour = update type (blue client, green server, black drift); node fill = role (dark x/server, blue client iterate, grey average); square fill = optimum type (orange client, blue true) - blue thus means both 'client' and 'true optimum'
channels.shape: circles = iterates, filled squares = optima, small white squares = SGD updates
channels.line: solid arrows = updates; one dashed line joins the two client optima
channels.frame: none; the legend is an unframed column at the right

quality.strengths: the method's problem (client drift) is drawn on the space it happens in, so the gap between averaged iterates and the true optimum is visible as distance; arrow colours are keyed
quality.weaknesses: blue codes both client iterates and the true optimum; the grey average nodes are not in the legend; the white 'SGD update' squares sitting on drift arrows are hard to decode; the optima are placed far right, away from the trajectories they explain

figures.lesson: Show heterogeneity as geometry: draw each client's local steps as a dot chain bending toward its own optimum marker and the server point as their average, so client drift is visible without a single equation.

figures.title: SCAFFOLD: Stochastic Controlled Averaging for Federated Learning

taxonomy.task: federated optimisation with control variates
taxonomy.note: modality multi = the method is data-agnostic; the figure is a parameter-space sketch with no data

arrangement.units: one unframed vector sketch reusing the teaser's markers
arrangement.inputs_as: a dark filled circle labelled x
arrangement.shared: marker and colour code shared with Figure 1

insights.structure: One row of iterate dots from x to y1 along the bottom left, the two optimum markers (x1*, x*) stacked in a middle column, and a legend column at the right.
insights.data: Iterates are filled circles (dark start, blue later ones), each step is drawn as vector addition: a dashed black local-gradient segment rising up-right plus a red downward correction arrow, with their sum as the blue step.
insights.emphasis: The correction term is the only red element and repeats at every local step, visibly bending the path down toward x* away from x1*.
insights.flow: Left to right along the iterate chain, with each step read as dashed up, red down, blue along.
insights.avoid: The optimum markers are placed in a separate middle column away from the path, so the 'toward x*' direction must be inferred rather than shown by an arrow.

core.what: the corrected client update drawn as vector sums along a trajectory: from x, each step's dashed local-gradient direction (up-right, toward client optimum x1*) is pulled down by a red correction arrow, and the blue resulting steps run flat toward y1

relations.form: iterates are circles in parameter space with the orange client optimum x1* top right and the blue true optimum x* below it
three steps unrolled left to right along one blue path x -> two blue circles -> y1
at each step a dashed segment rises from the current point and a red arrow drops from its end onto the next point, so update = gradient + correction as a drawn triangle

channels.colour: red = correction, blue = client update and also the true optimum x*, orange = client optimum, dark = start point
channels.shape: circles = iterates, squares = optima
channels.line: dashed = local gradient direction, solid = applied update or correction
channels.frame: none; a legend column at the right

quality.strengths: the correction is shown as vector geometry, three repeated triangles that keep the path level instead of drifting toward x1*; line style and colour each separate one thing in a figure with only three kinds of mark
quality.weaknesses: blue is shared by the update arrows and x*; the two optima squares sit apart from the path with no line to show the dashed gradients point at x1*; the legend takes nearly half the width

figures.lesson: Draw the inside of a local update as vector addition per step - dashed raw gradient, the proposed correction as a red arrow, the resulting step in the client colour - reusing the marker and colour code of the teaser.

figures.title: Scaffold-GS: Structured 3D Gaussians for View-Adaptive Rendering

taxonomy.task: novel-view rendering with anchor points on a sparse voxel grid that spawn view-adaptive neural Gaussians

arrangement.units: (a) unframed point-cloud render with a voxel inset; (b) a large grey rounded panel holding two voxel-layout states and a pink dashed zoom circle; (c) unframed camera, splats and two image tiles
arrangement.inputs_as: a grey SfM point-cloud render of the object with a voxel grid on it and a blue camera picking out visible voxels
arrangement.losses_at: below the splatting view in (c): the loss names as a typeset label above the Rendered RGB and GT tiles
arrangement.shared: none

(a) voxelisation, (b) derivation, (c) splatting as three titled columns left to right, the middle one framed and widest
one voxel tinted pink with a dashed pink border, tied by pink lines to a large pink dashed circle that opens it with its offsets O1-O4 and attribute mappings

inside (b) a fat pink block arrow leads from 'Position & Opacity' to 'Color, Scale & Quaternion'
