insights.structure: Three identical columns (frame -> enc trapezoid -> latent tile) stand side by side, with the latent tiles linked horizontally into a chain at mid height.
insights.data: Observations are real frames, the latent is a 5x5 grid of red-tinted cells inside a grey rounded tile, and the outputs are only bold hatted symbols (a-hat, r-hat, q-hat) with no decoded images.
insights.emphasis: The whole drawing uses one salmon-red family, so nothing competes; the grid-textured latent and the absence of any decoder carry the message.
insights.flow: Each column reads bottom-to-top (frame to latent to three fanned outputs) while the chain reads left-to-right, with the action a_t curving in from above onto each horizontal transition arrow.
insights.avoid: The middle encoder's 'enc' label is a slightly different (magenta) colour from the other two without explanation, which reads as a stray difference.

core.what: three identical columns side by side, one per time step: an observation frame s_t at the bottom, an 'enc' trapezoid above it, a latent z_t drawn as a grid of tinted cells, and three predicted quantities fanning out on top; horizontal arrows carry z_t to z_{t+1}

relations.form: the latent dynamics are unrolled into three columns (s1, s2, s3), a straight horizontal arrow linking each latent grid to the next
the action a_t is a label above the gap between two latents, its arrow curving down into the horizontal latent-to-latent arrow
inside each column the path reads bottom to top: rendered frame of the dog robot -> enc trapezoid -> latent grid
each latent grid fans three straight arrows upward to a-hat, r-hat and q-hat, the same three heads repeated per step

channels.colour: one salmon hue for every structural element (arrows, encoders, latent frames); cell saturation inside the latent grids = activation values; dark red = the predicted quantities' labels; the middle 'enc' label is a different magenta with no stated meaning
channels.shape: rendered simulator frames = observations; trapezoids = encoders; grey rounded squares holding a cell grid = latent states; bare letters with hats = predictions
channels.line: all solid salmon arrows; encoding, dynamics and prediction heads are distinguished only by direction

quality.strengths: the recurrence is unrolled as three identical columns, so 'the model plans in latent space' reads from geometry - observations enter from below only to start each column while latents run left to right; the nouns are drawn: real frames of the dog robot as s_t and each z_t as a tinted cell grid between its encoder and its heads
quality.weaknesses: a single hue carries encoder, latent, dynamics and heads, so module types are separated only by shape; the model's consistency objective between the predicted z_{t+1} and the encoded z_{t+1} is not drawn, so the two arrows arriving at z2 and z3 look like a merge rather than a comparison; the middle 'enc' label's different colour is unexplained

figures.lesson: Use one hue family for the whole model and draw the latent state as a small tinted grid inside a tile, so a recurrent world model reads as three clean repeated columns with the outputs as coloured symbols on top.

figures.title: An Image is Worth One Word: Personalizing Text-to-Image Generation using Textual Inversion

taxonomy.task: personalizing a frozen text-to-image model with a learned pseudo-word

arrangement.units: One composition with three rounded sub-containers: a grey Text Encoder (left, holding the step boxes and the blue zoom bubble), a green Generator column and a grey Noised Sample column (right), plus cream boxes for the prompt and input photo at the top.
arrangement.inputs_as: a quoted prompt 'A photo of S_*' in a cream box at the top left, and a real photo labelled Input Sample in a cream box at the top right
arrangement.losses_at: not written as a loss: dashed double-headed arrows between each generator output and the matching noised sample, row by row between the two right-hand columns

insights.structure: A grey Text Encoder container fills the left half with its steps stacked top-to-bottom and a blue zoom bubble beside them; the right third is two tall paired columns (green Generator outputs, grey Noised Samples) of four photos each.
insights.data: Tokens are drawn as their actual integer ids (508, 701, 73, <*>), embeddings as rows of coloured cells, and images as real photos of one alarm clock at four noise levels.
insights.emphasis: Padlocks on the table, Text Transformer and Generator make the single unlocked row v_* with '?' cells the obvious trainable part.
insights.flow: Thick black vertical arrows carry the prompt down through the encoder, one thick horizontal arrow labelled c_theta(y) runs along the bottom to the generator, and dashed horizontal double arrows tie each output to its noised target.
insights.avoid: The objective is implied only by unlabelled dashed double arrows, and the Generator column's photos are not explained as denoising steps, so a reader must infer the reconstruction loss from the caption.

core.what: the Embedding Lookup bar inside the grey Text Encoder is opened, by two thin blue guide lines, into a large blue detail panel: a locked table of existing rows v_0 ... v_701 with coloured cells, and below it one separate row v_* whose cells are all '?' - the single thing being learned

relations.form: two thin blue lines run from the Embedding Lookup bar's corners to a rounded blue detail panel to its right, which shows the lookup as a table with a padlock and the new v_* row set apart below it
the prompt '"A photo of S_*"' flows top to bottom through four parallel arrow columns: Tokenizer -> token ids (508, 701, 73, <*>) -> Embedding Lookup -> vectors v_508 ... v_* -> Text Transformer
one long horizontal arrow labelled c_theta(y) runs from the Text Transformer right into the Generator column
the Generator column of four progressively blurrier denoised images faces a Noised Sample column of the input image at four noise levels, each pair joined by a dashed double-headed arrow
the yellow Input Sample photo drops by a thick arrow into the top of the Noised Sample column; the Generator's top output image sits above its column

channels.colour: yellow = user-given data (prompt, input photo); light green = modules (Tokenizer, Text Transformer, Generator) and also the new v_* row, so green carries both 'frozen module' and 'learned embedding'; blue = the Embedding Lookup and its detail panel; grey = the Text Encoder frame and the Noised Sample frame; cell colours in the table only show that vectors differ
channels.shape: rectangles = modules; tables of cells = embedding vectors; photos = data; padlock icons = frozen parts
channels.line: solid arrows = forward data flow; dashed double-headed arrows = the reconstruction comparison; thin blue lines = zoom callout
channels.frame: grey rounded region = the text encoder; green rounded frame = generator; grey rounded frame = noised targets

quality.strengths: the contribution is the most enlarged thing: the lookup is opened into a detail panel where the only unknown is the '?' row v_*, while padlocks mark everything else frozen; the data are drawn as data - a quoted prompt with S_*, real token ids, and the clock photo at four noise levels facing the generator's outputs
quality.weaknesses: the objective is only dashed double arrows between the two image columns with no loss named, and the gradient path back to v_* is not drawn; light green fills both frozen modules and the trainable v_* row; the Generator's top output image sits outside its column with no label, so what it represents is unclear

figures.lesson: To show that only one tiny parameter is trained in an otherwise frozen pipeline, put a padlock on every frozen box and give the trainable vector its own row of '?' cells inside a zoom bubble, so the reader sees exactly which numbers change.

figures.title: Temporal Fusion Transformers for Interpretable Multi-horizon Time Series Forecasting

taxonomy.task: multi-horizon quantile forecasting with static, past and known-future inputs

arrangement.units: Main area: a bottom row of per-step columns (Variable Selection > LSTM > Add&Norm/Gate) for past and known-future steps, under one lavender band (the decoder) divided into three labelled layers by dotted rules, with Dense heads and quantile outputs above the band; a right column holds two black-framed detail panels (GRN on top, Variable Selection Network below).
arrangement.inputs_as: serif math symbols per time step (past, known future) with curly brackets labelling each group; static metadata as a symbol at bottom left feeding brown encoder boxes
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; quantile forecasts written as math at the top edge
arrangement.shared: GRN, Gate and Add&Norm glyphs are redrawn identically at every step and layer; the GRN and variable-selection internals are drawn once in the side panels

insights.structure: Per-time-step columns run along the bottom (past encoder steps left, known-future decoder steps right) beneath one lavender decoder band split by dotted rules into three named layers, with two framed detail panels stacked in a right-hand column.
insights.data: Inputs are large serif math symbols at the bottom grouped by curly brackets (Past Inputs, Known Future Inputs) and outputs are quantile math at the top, so there are no data thumbnails at all.
insights.emphasis: The contribution band is the only tinted background region, its attention layer is one long maroon bar across all steps, and the GRN and variable-selection submodules get their own framed zoom panels.
insights.flow: Data rises bottom to top inside each step column, with dash-dot curves bypassing each block as gated skips and orange-brown elbows carrying static context sideways from the left-hand static encoders.
insights.avoid: Many dash-dot skip curves, orange context lines and a long purple dash-dot bypass overlap near the band's lower edge, making individual connections hard to trace.

core.what: the time axis is unrolled as identical columns (chi_{t-k} ... chi_t past, x_{t+1} ... x_{t+tau_max} known future), each rising bottom to top through Variable Selection, an LSTM encoder or decoder, Gate/Add & Norm, and the stacked layers of a lavender Temporal Fusion Decoder, with quantile forecasts only above the future columns

relations.form: four drawn time-step columns with '...' between them, past and future columns side by side along one row, LSTM Encoder boxes chained to LSTM Decoder boxes by horizontal arrows

within each column, bottom to top through layer bands labelled at the left edge (Static Enrichment, Temporal Self-Attention, Position-wise Feed-forward) separated by dotted lines, ending in Dense and quantile outputs y-hat(0.1/0.5/0.9)
one wide maroon 'Masked Interpretable Multi-head Attention' bar spans all columns inside the decoder, every column's GRN feeding up into it

static metadata s rises on the far left through Variable Selection and Static Covariate Encoders, then brown lines run right along the bottom and up into every Variable Selection, the first LSTM, and every Static Enrichment GRN

two framed panels on the right open the Gated Residual Network (Dense, ELU, Dense, Gate, Add & Norm with a dash-dot residual) and the Variable Selection Network (per-variable GRNs, a softmax GRN, and a weighted sum), tied to the main figure only by their captions
past inputs and known future inputs are two groups of columns under separate braces, blue for the past and red for the future

channels.colour: colour carries two meanings: input kind (brown = static, blue = past, red = future) and layer type (green Add & Norm, orange Gate, maroon attention, navy and purple GRNs, olive Dense); in the zoom panels blue and red return as Dense and GRN fills, so the same hues mean different things in different panels
channels.shape: rectangles for every module; a red dot = dropout; a circled times = weighted sum; formulas appear in the zoom panels
channels.line: solid black = data flow; brown solid = static context; black dash-dot = gated skip connections; purple dash-dot = long skips around the decoder; grey arrows = optional external context
channels.frame: lavender rectangle = the Temporal Fusion Decoder; dotted lines inside = layer bands; outlined boxes on the right = component detail panels

quality.strengths: time is unrolled as columns, so the split into past and known-future inputs and the fact that only future columns emit quantile forecasts read from position; the shared attention bar spanning every column shows that attention mixes all steps; layer names are put once at the left margin instead of in every column
quality.weaknesses: colour codes both input kind and layer type, and blue/red mean different things in the zoom panels; the purple dash-dot skip lines leave the decoder frame and bend round it to the outputs, and the brown static lines run long under the whole figure; the dense repetition of Gate / Add & Norm in every column takes as much space as the attention and static-enrichment ideas that distinguish the model

figures.lesson: Colour the per-time-step boxes by input role (past = blue, known future = red, static = brown) so the encoder/decoder split along the time axis reads without a legend, and expand the repeated submodules in framed panels to the right.

figures.title: TIES-Merging: Resolving Interference When Merging Models

taxonomy.task: merging several fine-tuned models into one multitask model
taxonomy.note: family other: model merging; architecture other: no network drawn, only parameter vectors; depicts plots = per-parameter update arrows drawn on an axis like a stem plot

arrangement.units: five black-outlined rounded panels, one per vector state, with grey numbered operation boxes between them; no enclosing frame
arrangement.inputs_as: a panel of three models' task vectors drawn as coloured up/down arrows on five parameter squares
arrangement.shared: the trimmed vectors feed both Aligned Values (up) and Elect Sign (down) through two elbow arrows from one panel

insights.structure: Vector states are framed panels and operations are small grey boxes between them, with the sign election as a lower branch that feeds back up into the aligned values.
insights.data: Each task vector is drawn as five parameter squares on an axis with a coloured arrow per model whose direction and length show the update's sign and magnitude.
insights.emphasis: The operations are emphasised only by numbering; the effect of each is the visible change in the arrows (dotted ones dropped by Trim, minority-sign ones dotted in Aligned Values, all green after Disjoint Merge).
insights.flow: Thick black arrows run left to right but turn right angles: up from Trimmed into Aligned Values, down and back up through Elect Sign, and down from Disjoint Merge into the merged vector.
insights.avoid: The main chain zigzags in height (Aligned Values sits above the other states, the sign branch below), and green means both the elected sign vector and the merged model.

core.what: three numbered operations (Trim, Elect Sign, Disjoint Merge) between framed vector states, each state drawn as the same five-parameter axis so the effect of each stage is visible in its arrows

relations.form: framed vector panels left to right with grey numbered operation boxes '(1) Trim', '(2) Elect Sign', '(3) Disjoint Merge' between them
every state is a horizontal axis of five white parameter squares with coloured per-model arrows up or down, so trimming and sign conflicts are shown on the parameters themselves
the trimmed vectors (from the left) and the elected sign vector (from below) both enter the Aligned Values panel
Aligned Values -> Disjoint Merge -> Merged Task Vector continues right then turns down into the final panel

channels.colour: arrow colour = which model an update comes from (purple Model 1, pink Model 2, gold Model 3), green = merged model, keyed in the legend; the elected sign vector is also green, so green carries two meanings
channels.shape: white squares = parameters, coloured arrows = updates, grey filled rounded boxes = operations, black-outlined rounded panels = vector states
channels.line: solid arrows = influential values, dotted arrows = redundant or discarded values (keyed); thick black arrows = order of operations
channels.frame: one rounded black frame = one vector state, named with its symbol above or below

quality.strengths: the representations are drawn between the operations, as the same toy vector at each stage, so a reader sees what Trim removes and which arrows lose the sign vote; one keyed code each for model identity (colour) and kept vs discarded values (solid vs dotted); operations are compact grey boxes while the vector states get the space
quality.weaknesses: the chain changes height three times (up into Aligned Values, down to Elect Sign and back up, down into the merged vector), with right-angle elbows instead of one reading axis; green is used for both the elected sign and the merged model; the legend takes the top-left corner while the Aligned Values panel is pushed up to the top edge beside it

figures.lesson: Draw every step of a parameter-level procedure on the same toy vector (five parameter squares with per-model up/down arrows) so trimming, sign election and merging show up as arrows vanishing, turning dotted or recolouring.

figures.title: Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval

taxonomy.task: generative retrieval for sequential recommendation

arrangement.units: two unframed side-by-side regions (ID generation, then sequence model) with no titles
arrangement.inputs_as: item table rows on the left; token chips with concrete semantic-ID values under the encoder on the right
arrangement.shared: semantic-ID colour (orange) ties the two halves

insights.structure: Two unframed halves: left an item table (ItemID, Title, Description, Categories, Brand | Semantic ID) above a loop Item Content -> Content Encoder -> Embedding -> Quantization; right a bidirectional Transformer encoder feeding a Transformer decoder.
insights.data: Semantic IDs are shown as concrete tuples (Item 233 = (5,23,55)) in orange boxes and expanded into grey token chips t_5, t_23, t_55 under the encoder; the user is a green User_5 chip.
insights.emphasis: Orange is used consistently for anything semantic-ID: the Quantization box, the table's Semantic ID column, item boxes and the predicted Next Item (Item 64).
insights.flow: Left half loops: red arrow from a table row down to content, right through encoder to quantization, orange arrow back up into the Semantic ID column; right half reads bottom (tokens) to encoder, right through a hollow 'Encoded Context' arrow to the decoder, up to the next item.
insights.avoid: The two halves are not labelled as stages (a)/(b) nor linked by any arrow, so the reader must infer that the left produces the IDs the right consumes.

core.what: every item is drawn as an orange box carrying its Semantic ID tuple ('Item 233, Sem. ID = (5, 23, 55)') with that tuple's codeword tokens t_5, t_23, t_55 as grey boxes above it, so a user's history visibly becomes a token sequence that an encoder reads and a decoder continues

relations.form: two unframed panels side by side: on the left the semantic-ID construction, on the right generative retrieval over those IDs; orange links the Quantization box on the left to the item boxes on the right

left panel: a red curved arrow leaves a highlighted row of an item table (ItemID, Title, Description, Categories, Brand) down to Item Content Information -> Content Encoder trapezoid -> vertical Embedding bar -> Quantization, and an orange curved arrow returns up into the table's separate Semantic ID column
right panel: a green User_5 box with token t_u5, then two orange item boxes each with three grey token boxes above it, bracketed below as 'Item Interaction History of User 5'
a hollow block arrow labelled 'Encoded Context' runs straight from the yellow Bidirectional Transformer Encoder to the yellow Transformer Decoder
the decoder's inputs '<BOS> t_5 t_25 t_55' sit below it and its outputs 't_5 t_25 t_55 <EOS>' above it, shifted by one, topped by the orange 'Item 64, Sem. ID = (5, 25, 55)' bracketed as 'Next Item'

channels.colour: fill = kind of element: orange = semantic IDs (the Quantization step and every item box), red = raw item content, blue = content encoder and embedding, pale yellow = the two transformers, green = the user token, grey = individual tokens - one meaning each
channels.shape: a table = the item catalogue; trapezoid = encoder; thin vertical bar = embedding vector; rounded boxes = modules; small square boxes = tokens
channels.line: thin grey arrows = token inputs and outputs; red and orange curves = taking content from and writing IDs back into the table; a '//' mark on the embedding-to-quantization arrow is unexplained; hollow block arrow = encoder context

quality.strengths: the data are drawn as data - a catalogue table with real column names, items with literal Semantic ID tuples, and tokens whose numbers match the tuples (t_5, t_23, t_55 under (5, 23, 55)), so the reader can trace how an item becomes tokens; orange consistently marks semantic IDs across both panels
quality.weaknesses: the semantic-ID construction, the paper's new step, is the smaller left panel and its Quantization is one box that does not show how three codewords arise; the two panels have no frames or labels; the left panel's loop leaves and re-enters the table by long curves, and the '//' on the embedding arrow is not keyed

figures.lesson: Render each item in the user's history as an orange box carrying its ID tuple, with the tuple's code tokens as a row of small grey boxes directly above it, so the reader sees both the item and the tokens the sequence model actually reads.

figures.title: Time-LLM: Time Series Forecasting by Reprogramming Large Language Models

taxonomy.task: forecasting with a frozen LLM: time-series patches reprogrammed against text prototypes, prefixed by a language prompt, and projected to forecasts

arrangement.units: an unframed central overview plus four dashed-framed detail panels in the corners, each joined to its block by dotted callout lines
arrangement.inputs_as: a time-series line plot in a dashed box and a grey prompt card quoting the template ('### Domain: <domain knowledge>', '### Instruction: <task information>', '### Input statistics:') with coloured placeholders
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; red backward arrows run beside the forward arrows from Output Projection down through the LLM body and the token row into Patch Reprogram, marking the trained path
arrangement.shared: the pre-trained LLM appears twice as the same pale-blue snowflake box, once as Embedder and once as Body

insights.structure: A central bottom-to-top overview with one corner detail panel per opened block, each panel placed in the corner nearest its block and tied by dotted callouts.
insights.data: Inputs are drawn as data (a real-looking series and a quoted prompt template); intermediate embeddings are cell strips coloured by source, and the output is a forecast line plot.
insights.emphasis: Flame vs snowflake icons and pale-blue fills separate trained from frozen parts, and red circled numbers 1-5 walk the reader through the steps.
insights.flow: Short straight vertical arrows up each branch into the shared token row and on through the LLM; red backward arrows run beside them only on the trained path.
insights.avoid: Colours are reused with different meanings (pale blue = frozen module and prompt cells; yellow = patch cells and also Tokenization, Patch Embedder and Add & Layer Norm boxes), and the reprogramming panel, the method's core, is no larger than the routine Transformer-layer panel.

core.what: the prompt branch (frozen LLM embedder) and the time-series branch (patching, Patch Reprogram) rise side by side and meet in one dashed token strip, blue prompt cells then yellow patch cells, which feeds the frozen LLM body

relations.form: two vertical branches end under the left and right halves of one concatenated token strip; inside the bottom-right panel, patch embeddings and red-dashed Text Prototypes (from pre-trained word embeddings) converge on one Multi-Head Attention bar
bottom to top on one axis: series -> Instance Norm -> Patching -> Patch Reprogram -> token strip -> LLM Body -> output token strip -> Output Projection, with red step numbers 1-5
four dashed corner panels (forecast head, LLM layer, embedder, reprogramming) each joined to its block by two thin dotted diagonal callouts
the same pre-trained LLM drawn as two identical pale-blue snowflake boxes, Embedder at the left branch and Body above the token strip

channels.colour: two meanings on colour: pale blue = frozen pre-trained module and also prompt-embedding cells; yellow = patch-embedding cells and also Tokenization, Patch Embedder and Add & Layer Norm boxes; pink = trained linear layers; green = output embedding cells and Feed Forward; red text = step numbers and Text Prototypes
channels.shape: rounded rectangle = module, strip of square cells = token sequence, line plot = series data, grey card = prompt text; snowflake / flame icons = frozen / trained
channels.line: black arrow = forward, red arrow = backward (keyed); thin grey dotted lines = zoom callouts
channels.frame: dashed rectangle = detail panel; dashed rounded box = one token sequence or input; red dashed outline = the text prototypes

quality.strengths: The core fusion is geometry: each branch rises directly beneath its half of one two-colour token strip; inputs are data (series plot, quoted prompt template) and every intermediate representation is drawn as a cell strip; trained vs frozen is keyed by icon and the backward path by red arrows next to the forward ones; lines are short and vertical; each detail panel sits in the corner nearest its block.
quality.weaknesses: Colour carries two meanings (pale blue = frozen and prompt cells; yellow = patch cells and unrelated boxes in the detail panels); the reprogramming panel (the contribution) gets the same small corner as the standard Transformer-layer panel; the dotted callouts run long diagonals across the page; text prototypes appear only as a label box, never as data.

figures.lesson: Show two inputs reaching a frozen model by concatenating their embeddings into one token strip whose cells are coloured by source (prompt cells then patch cells), with each branch's own pipeline rising directly beneath its half.

figures.title: A decoder-only foundation model for time-series forecasting

taxonomy.task: zero-shot time-series forecasting foundation model

arrangement.units: dotted rounded horizontal bands per layer type, with one grey tinted band for the transformer and repeated per-patch columns
arrangement.inputs_as: a plotted time-series line divided into dashed patch boxes
arrangement.shared: '(same network)' notes mark residual blocks shared across columns

insights.structure: Horizontal dotted bands stacked bottom to top: input series, input Residual Block band, yellow Token+PE row, grey Transformer band (SA ovals + FFN), output Residual Block band; four columns repeat per patch with '...' between.
insights.data: The series is a real-looking blue line split by blue dashed boxes into input patches (input_patch_len=32) and longer green solid output windows (output_patch_len=128), annotated in monospace below.
insights.emphasis: Yellow Token+PE boxes are the only saturated fill; long green dashed arrows run from each output token back down to the next, longer output window to show input-short/output-long patching.
insights.flow: Bottom to top within each column; causal attention fan-in lines go from earlier tokens diagonally up to later SA ovals; green dashed diagonals cross the whole figure.
insights.avoid: The green dashed output arrows cut diagonally across every band and the causal attention lines, cluttering the centre.

core.what: a plotted time series along the bottom is cut into blue dashed patches (input_patch_len=32), each patch rising as its own column through a Residual Block, Token + PE, a causal self-attention layer and an output Residual Block, while longer green solid boxes over the same series mark the output patches (output_patch_len=128)

relations.form: the series itself is drawn as a light-blue trace, segmented by blue dashed boxes for input patches and overlapping green solid boxes for output patches, with patch lengths written in code font under braces
four identical columns (with '...' between) pass through dotted rounded bands labelled 'Residual Block (same network)', so one network is applied per patch
each column reads bottom to top: patch -> teal Residual Block -> yellow 'Token + PE' -> blue SA ellipse -> teal FFN -> teal Residual Block -> up arrow out of the top
thin black lines fan from each Token + PE box to the SA ellipses of its own and every later column, drawing causal self-attention as converging edges inside the grey Transformer band

two long green dashed diagonals run from the top outputs of the first two columns down to the start of the green output-patch boxes on the series, mapping each column's prediction to the span it forecasts

channels.colour: blue dashed = input patches, green = output patches and the dashed lines that map predictions to them, yellow = tokenised patches, teal = learned blocks, light-blue ellipses = attention - one meaning each
channels.shape: split rectangles = residual blocks; ellipses = self-attention; small rectangles = FFN and token boxes; the series is a plotted trace
channels.line: solid black arrows = per-column data flow; thin black fan = causal attention connections; green dashed diagonals = prediction-to-target mapping
channels.frame: dotted rounded rectangles = a shared-weight layer band; grey filled rounded region = the stacked transformer ('x num_layers'); a nested dotted box only annotates the FFN

quality.strengths: the input is drawn as real data with the patching made visible on it, and the different input and output patch lengths are shown as different box widths on the same series; repeating identical columns with '(same network)' makes weight sharing across patches geometric
quality.weaknesses: the two green dashed diagonals cross the entire figure from top to bottom over the transformer and residual bands to reach their targets; the causal-attention fan of many thin lines is hard to read between the token row and the SA ellipses; input and output patches overlap on one trace, so where training targets end is hard to see

figures.lesson: Overlay the patch windows directly on the drawn series (short dashed boxes for input patches, longer solid boxes for output patches) and run dashed arrows from each output token back down to the window it forecasts.

figures.title: Is Space-Time Attention All You Need for Video Understanding?

taxonomy.task: video classification (space-time attention design)

arrangement.units: five unframed columns of identical frame stacks, each captioned underneath
arrangement.inputs_as: real video frames tiled into patches
arrangement.shared: row labels frame t-delta / t / t+delta at the left apply to all columns

insights.structure: Five identical columns, one per attention scheme (Space, Joint Space-Time, Divided Space-Time, Sparse Local Global, Axial), each a vertical stack of three frames (t-delta, t, t+delta) cut into 4x4 patch grids.
insights.data: Frames are real video frames split into patches with white gutters; one query patch is blue and the patches it attends to are tinted with translucent colour overlays.
insights.emphasis: Colour encodes attention type and is echoed in the column caption letters (S red, T green, L yellow, G magenta, W/H), so each caption doubles as a legend.
insights.flow: Read column by column left to right comparing schemes; within a column top to bottom across time; no arrows at all.
insights.avoid: Overlapping translucent tints (red over patches, yellow over magenta) make some attended regions hard to tell apart, and the blue query patch is small.

core.what: five identical panels side by side, one per self-attention scheme (Space, Joint Space-Time, Divided Space-Time, Sparse Local Global, Axial), each the same three video frames cut into 4x4 patches with the same blue query patch and the attended patches tinted by colour

relations.form: five equal columns on one row with aligned frame rows, captioned beneath with the scheme name and its colour-coded letters (S, ST, T+S, L+G, T+W+H)

each scheme is drawn directly on real video frames (a hand and a bottle) split into a patch grid, the query patch tinted blue in frame t and the patches it attends to washed in colour across frames t-delta, t and t+delta
frames stack top to bottom (frame t-delta, frame t, frame t+delta) with the row labels written once at the far left

channels.colour: tint = which attention step covers a patch, keyed by the coloured letters in each caption (red S/ST, green T, yellow L or W, magenta G or H); blue = the query patch, unkeyed; yellow and magenta carry different meanings in the Sparse Local Global and Axial panels
channels.shape: square image patches only; no module shapes are drawn
channels.frame: white gaps separate patches and frames; panels are separated only by spacing

quality.strengths: the compared designs are drawn as identical panels on the same frames and the same query, so the difference between schemes is only which patches are tinted - a reader sees at a glance that joint attention covers everything while divided attention covers one row of time plus one frame; the caption letters double as the colour key, so no separate legend is needed
quality.weaknesses: yellow and magenta change meaning between the last two panels (local/global vs width/height), and the blue query patch is not keyed; the proposed Divided Space-Time scheme sits in the middle with no emphasis, so the paper's choice does not stand out; the red wash over whole frames in the Space and Joint panels hides the image content it covers

figures.lesson: Explain attention variants with a grid of real frames: columns = variants, rows = three consecutive frames cut into patches, the query patch in blue and each attended set in a translucent tint whose colour matches the coloured letter in the column label.

figures.title: TimesNet: Temporal 2D-Variation Modeling for General Time Series Analysis

taxonomy.task: general time-series analysis (1D-to-2D periodic transform)
taxonomy.note: architecture = reshaping a 1D series into 2D tensors by period (multi-periodicity), shown conceptually

arrangement.units: unframed three-column progression (1D plot, per-period segments, 2D planes)
arrangement.inputs_as: a plotted 1D time series with period spans marked
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Three columns left to right: a single value-time plot with three nested period spans, a middle column of three stacked series segmentations (Period 1/2/3), and right three slanted 2D planes of decreasing period length.
insights.data: Series are grey jagged line plots; same-phase time points are hollow circles joined by dashed lines; segments are tinted blue (interperiod) and red (intraperiod) bands; 2D tensors are drawn as skewed parallelograms holding short squiggles.
insights.emphasis: Two colours carry the whole idea: blue arrows for interperiod variation along rows and red arrows for intraperiod variation along columns, repeated on each 2D plane and in the bottom-left legend.
insights.flow: Long black dashed arrows fan from each period span on the left plot to its segmented copy in the middle, then hollow block arrows point right to the 2D plane.
insights.avoid: The middle column's overlapping, offset series copies with dashed connectors and circles are very busy and partly illegible.

core.what: a 1D series plotted at the top left is cut at three period lengths, and for each period the cut segments are drawn as stacked, offset copies of the series whose same-phase points are joined, ending (via hollow arrows) in a flat 2D tensor whose columns are the segments - the 1D-to-2D fold drawn on the data itself

relations.form: the folding is shown on the actual trace: segments laid over one another on red and blue bands, with circled time points at the same phase linked across segments by thin dashed lines

three folds, one per period (Period 1, 2, 3), are stacked diagonally down the middle and each feeds its own parallelogram tensor on the right, the three tensors stacked vertically with different column widths
left to right: series with bracketed period lengths -> long black dashed arrows to each period's stacked segments -> hollow arrow -> 2D tensor

blue arrows along each segment mark interperiod variation and red arrows across segments mark intraperiod variation, repeated as a blue arrow along the top and a red arrow up the side of each 2D tensor

channels.colour: blue = interperiod variation, red = intraperiod variation (bands, arrows and the tensor axes alike), grey = the raw series - keyed in a legend at the lower left, one meaning each
channels.shape: circles = time points at the same phase; parallelograms = the 2D tensors; plotted squiggles = series data throughout
channels.line: long black dashed arrows = period extraction; thin black dashed lines = same-phase correspondence; coloured arrows = variation direction; hollow arrows = reshaping into 2D

quality.strengths: the method's transformation is drawn as geometry on real-looking data - the reader sees segments being stacked and same-phase points lining up, then the same segments becoming columns of a 2D grid whose two axes carry the two variation colours; colour carries exactly one meaning and is keyed
quality.weaknesses: the three long black dashed arrows fan diagonally from the top-left series across to the folded stacks, crossing each other and the plot; the offset translucent strips with dashed links and circles overlap densely, so the Period 1 stack is hard to read; the tensors are ordered Period 3 top to Period 1 bottom with no label tying each tensor to its period

figures.lesson: Explain a 1-D-to-2-D reshape by cutting the drawn series into period segments stacked as offset copies with same-phase points joined, and give the two resulting axes their own colours (blue across periods, red within) on both the curves and the final 2-D planes.

figures.title: TimeXer: Empowering Transformers for Time Series Forecasting with Exogenous Variables

taxonomy.task: forecasting an endogenous series with exogenous variables as auxiliary input

arrangement.units: one central grey rounded container (the repeated layer) between two pink Embedding blocks and a Projection block; four black-framed white detail panels in the corners, each tied by yellow dashed lines to the block it opens
arrangement.inputs_as: 'Endogenous Input' below the stack and 'Exogenous Input' from the left, each shown in its detail panel as small multicolour line plots
arrangement.shared: the endogenous tokens (purple cubes plus the red-dashed global token) are redrawn in panels (a), (c) and (d) with the same colours

insights.structure: A vertical layer stack in the centre with each attention and embedding block opened in a framed corner panel tied by dashed callouts.
insights.data: Series are small line plots, tokens are coloured cubes in the colour of their source series, and the two attention patterns are drawn as a 1 x C colour bar and an (N+1) x (N+1) heatmap.
insights.emphasis: Orange fill on the two attention blocks, red dashed outline on the global token, and red titles on the attention maps mark what is new.
insights.flow: The stack reads bottom to top with short vertical arrows; the exogenous signal comes in from the left on its own straight line into Cross-Attention; panels read embedding on the left, attention on the right.
insights.avoid: Panel letters run out of reading order (b above a, d above c), and red is used both for the global-token outline and for the attention-map titles.

core.what: exogenous variate tokens enter the endogenous layer stack from the side on their own line into Cross-Attention, and panel (d) shows them as keys against the endogenous query tokens

relations.form: the exogenous Embedding sits left of the stack and sends one straight horizontal line into Cross-Attention; in panel (d) the variate cubes are keys and the purple patch row plus global token are queries into one Cross-Attention box
Embedding, Self-Attention, Cross-Attention, Feed-Forward and Projection stacked bottom to top with residual circled-plus nodes between
four corner panels each opening one block of the stack, tied to it by yellow dashed callout lines
the layer is drawn once inside a grey container labelled 'L x', with a brown dashed 'Forward to the Next Layer' arrow between panels (d) and (c)

channels.colour: two meanings on two element kinds: block fill = module type (pink embedding, orange attention, yellow-green LayerNorm, light blue Feed-Forward, lavender Projection); token and curve colour = which variable (blue/teal/yellow exogenous variates, purple endogenous); red is both the global-token outline and the attention-map titles
channels.shape: rounded rectangle = module, cube = token, line plot = series, heatmap/colour bar = attention weights, circled plus = residual add
channels.line: solid black = data flow in the stack, pink arrows = steps inside the embedding panels, yellow dashed = zoom callout, brown dashed = forward to the next layer, red dashed outline = global token
channels.frame: grey rounded container = the repeated layer; black-bordered white box = one detail panel; dashed rectangle in (a) = concatenated token set

quality.strengths: The exogenous signal enters Cross-Attention on its own straight side line, the fusion form derive.md names; every compared representation is drawn as tokens in its source series' colour (variate cubes as keys, patch row plus global token as queries) between the embedding that makes them and the attention that uses them; the global token keeps one red-dashed mark across panels (a), (c) and (d); the stack's arrows are short and vertical.
quality.weaknesses: The routine part (three LayerNorms, Feed-Forward, Projection) takes as much of the central stack as the two attention blocks; panel letters are placed out of reading order (b top-left, a bottom-left, d top-right, c bottom-right); the yellow dashed callouts run long diagonals from the stack to the corners; red serves both the global-token outline and the attention titles; residual lines wrap around the right side of each block to reach the adds.

figures.lesson: Give each input variable one colour and carry it from its line plot into its token cube and its attention input, so the reader can follow which variable meets which without a key.

figures.title: TinyBERT: Distilling BERT for Natural Language Understanding

taxonomy.task: language model compression by knowledge distillation

arrangement.units: unframed two-row flow of cylinders and rounded boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: database cylinders for corpora
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Two rows: top row Large-scale Text Corpus -> General TinyBERT -> Fine-tuned TinyBERT; bottom row Task Dataset -> Augmented Task Dataset, whose arrow rises into the second top-row arrow.
insights.data: Datasets are drawn as database cylinders and models as rounded rectangles, all black outline with no fill.
insights.emphasis: Only the three process names (General Distillation, Data Augmentation, Task-specific Distillation) are coloured, in red-pink, placed above their arrows so the two-stage method reads as labelled edges.
insights.flow: Left to right along each row; the bottom row joins the top with one vertical arrow into the task-specific distillation step.
insights.avoid: The teacher BERT is not drawn anywhere, so the distillation edges have no visible source model.

core.what: a top row of two consecutive distillation stages read left to right: Large-scale Text Corpus -> 'General Distillation' -> General TinyBERT -> 'Task-specific Distillation' -> Fine-tuned TinyBERT

relations.form: two arrows on one horizontal line, each labelled above in red with its stage name, joining a dataset cylinder and two model boxes
a lower row: Task Dataset cylinder -> red 'Data Augmentation' arrow -> Augmented Task Dataset cylinder
a vertical arrow rises from the Augmented Task Dataset cylinder into the middle of the Task-specific Distillation arrow, the second stage's data entering from below

channels.colour: red text = processes (the two distillations and data augmentation); everything else is black on white - one meaning
channels.shape: cylinders = datasets; rounded rectangles = models
channels.line: solid black arrows only

quality.strengths: the two-stage schedule is one straight row with the stage names in red on the arrows themselves, and the augmented data joins the second stage by a short straight vertical arrow, so 'what data feeds which stage' reads from position; datasets and models are separated by shape
quality.weaknesses: the teacher BERT, which both distillation stages compare against, is not drawn, so the figure shows no comparison at all; the distillation objectives (which layers or representations are matched) are absent; the figure is a schedule of boxes with no representation drawn between maker and objective

figures.lesson: Draw datasets as cylinders and model checkpoints as rounded boxes and name each distillation stage in red over its arrow, so the stages are the arrows and the boxes are only artefacts.

figures.title: Token Merging: Your ViT But Faster

taxonomy.task: faster ViT inference by token merging

arrangement.units: three black-outlined rounded panels with tab titles (a) result strip, (b) block diagram, (c) algorithm steps; (c) is a zoom of the ToMe box in (b)
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo at the left of panel (a); x as a grey pill at the left of (b)
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Three rounded panels with tab labels: (a) a photo strip top-left, (b) a transformer block top-right with the new ToMe trapezoid between Attention and MLP, and (c) a full-width five-step strip below that a wedge from the ToMe box opens into.
insights.data: Tokens are drawn as two columns of small circles (red Set A, blue Set B) with grey candidate edges and dark kept edges; merged tokens become overlapping circles that turn purple, while (a) shows the real dog photo with coloured patch outlines that coarsen from Patchfied to Block 32.
insights.emphasis: The contribution is the only light-blue trapezoid in panel (b), narrowing in the flow direction, and the zoom wedge from it makes the whole bottom panel its explanation; the title bolds 'To' and 'Me'.
insights.flow: Panels (a) and (b) read left to right on the top row, then the wedge drops the eye into (c), whose steps run left to right joined by black arrows, each with a bold 'Step N:' caption underneath.
insights.avoid: Panel (a) has no arrows or link to (b), so the reader must infer that the merging snapshots are produced by stacking the block in (b).

core.what: the widest panel, (c) Bipartite Soft Matching, runs the algorithm on a toy set of eleven token circles in five steps left to right: split into red Set A and blue Set B columns, draw each A token's edge to its most similar B token, keep the top r edges, merge the connected pairs, concatenate - each step captioned beneath

relations.form: token circles in two facing columns with straight edges between them; kept edges drawn dark and dropped ones light grey; merged tokens drawn as overlapping red-blue circles and then as purple circles
five step columns in one row inside panel (c), joined by straight black arrows, each with a bold 'Step n:' caption under it
the blue ToMe trapezoid in panel (b) widens into a callout wedge that opens down onto panel (c), tying the operation to the block it lives in
panel (b) is one horizontal block: X -> pink Attention -> residual + -> blue ToMe -> green MLP -> residual + -> Y, with residual lines running beneath
panel (a) shows a dog photo, then the same photo with patch outlines after patchifying and after blocks 11, 22 and 32, coloured outlines growing as tokens merge

channels.colour: red = Set A tokens, blue = Set B tokens, purple = merged tokens (the mix of the two) in panel (c); in panel (b) blue also fills the ToMe trapezoid and pink/green fill Attention/MLP, so blue carries two meanings; outline colours in panel (a) only separate merged groups
channels.shape: circles = tokens; a trapezoid narrowing to the right = ToMe (fewer tokens out); rounded rectangles = transformer sub-layers; small circled plus = residual addition
channels.line: black arrows = step order and data flow; straight edges = similarity matches, dark = kept, light grey = dropped
channels.frame: three rounded panels with tab labels a), b), c), the zoom wedge joining b) to c)

quality.strengths: the new operation is the biggest panel and is drawn as geometry on a small instance - the reader watches edges appear, get pruned to the top r and collapse into purple merged tokens, so bipartite matching is understood without the text; the trapezoid shape for ToMe says 'fewer tokens out' and the callout wedge places it inside the block; panel (a) shows the effect on a real image at three depths
quality.weaknesses: blue means both Set B tokens and the ToMe block; in Step 4 the merged pairs are drawn as overlapping circles that are easy to misread as three tokens; panel (a)'s coloured patch outlines are not explained, so the grouping they show must be inferred

figures.lesson: Draw a token-reduction module as a trapezoid that narrows in the flow direction, then zoom it into a step strip where tokens are two-colour circles that visibly fuse into overlapping mixed-colour circles.

figures.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools

taxonomy.task: self-supervised tool-use data generation for LMs
taxonomy.note: training 'other': self-supervised filtering of API calls by LM loss reduction, then finetuning on the augmented dataset

arrangement.units: one row of pipeline boxes; the three processing steps are grouped on a grey background band, each step heading a column of example text
arrangement.inputs_as: a dataset box plus quoted example text beneath it
arrangement.losses_at: filter criterion written as inequalities under step 3
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: One row of five rounded boxes, mauve 'LM Dataset' at each end and three numbered light-blue steps (Sample, Execute, Filter API Calls) sitting together on a grey band that runs down to the figure bottom.
insights.data: Under every box a column continues one worked example: the Pittsburgh text spans x, two candidate calls c_i^1 and c_i^2 as questions, their results r_i, and the filter inequalities on tinted strips (green with '<' kept, pink with '>' dropped).
insights.emphasis: The kept/dropped decision is colour-coded green vs pink-red and carried into the output, where the inserted call '[QA(What ...? -> Steel City)]' appears in bold magenta inline in the sentence.
insights.flow: Strictly left to right: grey arrows from and to the dataset boxes, blue arrows between the steps; the example text is read top to bottom inside each column.
insights.avoid: The two candidate calls are tracked only by row position and superscripts; nothing marks that the dropped c_i^2 is discarded before the output column.

core.what: one row of five headers read left to right - pink LM Dataset, three numbered blue steps (Sample, Execute, Filter API Calls) on a grey band, pink LM Dataset with API Calls - with a worked example written under each header, so the example flows through the steps in columns

relations.form: header boxes joined by short straight arrows (grey into and out of the band, blue between steps), and each step's example text placed directly beneath its header
two candidate calls c_i^1 and c_i^2 run as two aligned rows across the columns: question, then executed result (Steel City, United States), then the filter verdict
under Filter API Calls each candidate's loss with its result is set against the minimum of the two baselines, highlighted green with '<' for the kept call and red with '>' for the rejected one

the input text x is split into prefix 'Pittsburgh is also known as' and continuation 'the Steel City', and the output x* re-joins them with the kept call '[QA(What ...? -> Steel City)]' inserted in magenta

channels.colour: pink = datasets (and the inserted API call in the output text, the new dataset content); blue = the three pipeline steps; green highlight = call kept, red highlight = call rejected - one meaning each
channels.shape: rounded rectangles only; the content is text, with losses typeset as expressions
channels.line: grey arrows = data in and out of the pipeline; blue arrows = step to step
channels.frame: a light grey band behind the three steps = the annotation pipeline

quality.strengths: the data are drawn as data: one real sentence is carried through every step with two candidate calls in aligned rows, so the reader sees what is sampled, what comes back and why one is kept; the green/red highlight with '<' and '>' makes the filter's decision readable without the formula; the step boxes form one straight row with the pipeline band marking the new part
quality.weaknesses: the filter criterion is shown as typeset loss expressions L_i(...) and min(...), which the reader must parse to see what is compared; the model that does the sampling and scoring is never drawn; the rejected call's row simply ends, with no mark of it being dropped in the output column

figures.lesson: Run one concrete example under each pipeline stage in aligned columns, and show the keep-or-drop decision by tinting the kept candidate green and the rejected one red, so the tool-call insertion can be read off the bottom row.

figures.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models

taxonomy.task: Game of 24 reasoning with LM-generated and LM-evaluated thoughts

arrangement.units: two unframed horizontal rows (a) generation and (b) evaluation, each prompt panel -> LM -> output panel, plus an unframed tree column at left
arrangement.inputs_as: the search tree with real arithmetic nodes; 'Input: 4 9 10 13' at its top
arrangement.shared: the LM box is drawn once per row

insights.structure: A search tree on the left feeds two stacked rows on the right, (a) Propose Prompt -> LM -> Thought Generation and (b) Value Prompt -> LM -> Thought Evaluation, with the same three-column alignment in both rows.
insights.data: Prompts and outputs are panels with a monospace title bar and real prompt text, italic grey placeholders ({one example}, {...more lines...}) for elided parts; tree nodes are bare arithmetic steps coloured green (kept) or red (dead end) with a small '(left: ...)' remainder.
insights.emphasis: Colour links context to module: a grey dashed box around the tree's first level and a grey arrow go to row (a), an orange dashed box around one node and an orange arrow go to row (b), whose title bars are cream-orange.
insights.flow: Left to right: tree -> thick coloured arrows -> prompt panel -> LM box -> output panel; the tree itself reads top to bottom.
insights.avoid: The tree's lower levels have no link back from Thought Evaluation, so how the value verdict prunes the tree is left to the colours alone.

core.what: a Game-of-24 search tree on the left (Input: 4 9 10 13 at the root, arithmetic thoughts with their remaining numbers as nodes) has two nodes boxed by dashed outlines - grey around the root, orange around a '4+9=13' child - and a thick arrow from each box points to the prompt row that is applied to that node

relations.form: the tree is drawn three levels deep with real thoughts ('10-4=6 (left: 6 9 13)', '4*6=24 (left: 24)'), green nodes for promising and red for failing ones, '......' for elided branches
a grey dashed box around the root sends a thick grey arrow right to the (a) Propose Prompt row; an orange dashed box around one child sends a thick orange arrow down-right to the (b) Value Prompt row
each of two rows reads left to right: a prompt card with its literal text -> an 'LM' box -> an output card (Thought Generation with candidate steps; Thought Evaluation ending in 'impossible')
the two rows are stacked with their LM boxes aligned one above the other, the same model used for proposing and for valuing

channels.colour: in the tree green = viable thought, red = failing thought; grey vs orange = generation vs evaluation (dashed box, arrow, card header); pink highlight = the node's numbers being judged and the verdict, grey highlight = the chosen generated thought - several tints but each with one job; the green/red code is not keyed
channels.shape: plain text nodes = tree states; cards with monospaced headers = prompts and outputs; rounded square = LM
channels.line: thin grey arrows = tree edges and data flow; thick grey/orange arrows = which node a prompt is applied to
channels.frame: dashed outlines = the node selected for a prompt

quality.strengths: the method acts on a structure and the figure draws that structure as a small real instance, with the node each prompt reads boxed and colour-matched to its row (grey = propose, orange = value); prompts and outputs are quoted literally, including the few-shot placeholders and the 'impossible' verdict, so the reader sees exactly what the LM is given and returns
quality.weaknesses: the two LM boxes are separate copies whose sameness rests on the label; the green/red node colours are unkeyed; how the evaluation result feeds back to prune or expand the tree is not drawn, so the search loop is implied rather than shown; the orange arrow crosses diagonally from the tree's middle into the lower row

figures.lesson: Tie each highlighted part of a search tree to the prompt row that produces or judges it with a matching coloured dashed box and arrow, so the tree and the prompt templates explain each other.

figures.title: Offline Reinforcement Learning as One Big Sequence Modeling Problem

taxonomy.task: offline RL as sequence modelling of discretised trajectories

arrangement.units: one composition: input token row, model bar, output token row; no frames
arrangement.inputs_as: a row of coloured token tiles with math symbols
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn (implied by shifted output row)
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Three horizontal bands: an input token row at the bottom, one full-width 'Trajectory Transformer' bar in the middle, and the output token row at the top shifted one slot left.
insights.data: Each token is a rounded tile holding a bold math symbol: blue for state dimensions s_t^i, salmon for action dimensions a_t^j, orange for reward r_t; runs are elided by three dots tinted in the run's colour.
insights.emphasis: The shift of the output row by one token makes next-token prediction visible without any text; colour families separate state, action and reward.
insights.flow: Bottom to top: short black arrows from each input tile up into the bar and from the bar up to each output tile.
insights.avoid: Arrows are drawn only in columns that hold a tile on that side, so a few columns look disconnected; there is no causal-mask cue.

core.what: a trajectory is drawn as one flat row of per-dimension tokens - state dimensions s_t^1 ... s_t^N in blue, action dimensions a_t^1 ... a_t^M in red, reward r_t in orange - entering a single wide Trajectory Transformer box from below, and the same row leaves above shifted one position left, i.e. next-token prediction

relations.form: token boxes in one horizontal line in trajectory order (state dims, action dims, reward, next state), with coloured dots marking elided runs
the output row is the input row shifted by one token (input starts s_t^1, output starts s_t^2 and ends with s_{t+1}^1), every input arrow directly below the token it predicts
one wide rounded box spans the whole row, each input token entering it by a short vertical arrow and each output leaving by one

channels.colour: fill = token type: blue = state dimension, red = action dimension, orange = reward; the ellipsis dots take the colour of the elided tokens - one meaning
channels.shape: rounded squares = tokens; one long rounded rectangle = the model
channels.line: short straight vertical arrows only

quality.strengths: the two ideas - treating each state and action dimension as its own token, and predicting the next token - are both geometry: the row is visibly cut per dimension and the output row is shifted one slot against the input; colour is a single type code that also tints the elisions; all lines are short and straight
quality.weaknesses: the discretisation of continuous values into tokens and the causal mask are not shown, and the transformer is an empty box; the per-dimension superscripts are small, so the shift has to be read from the labels rather than from a visual offset in the boxes, which are aligned in the same columns

figures.lesson: Autoregressive next-token prediction is shown by placing the same colour-coded token row below and above one wide model bar with the upper row shifted one slot left, so the offset reads without a label.

figures.title: TransBTS: Multimodal Brain Tumor Segmentation Using Transformer

taxonomy.task: 3D brain tumor segmentation from multimodal MRI

arrangement.units: one row encoder -> transformer panel (peach rounded tint) -> decoder; a grey rounded detail inset below
arrangement.inputs_as: a stack of real MRI slices
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: A single left-to-right row: green 3-D encoder blocks shrink from stacked MRI slices to a bottleneck, a peach panel holds the Transformer section, blue decoder blocks grow to the segmented slice; a grey inset below the bottleneck expands one Transformer Layer, with legends in both lower corners.
insights.data: Feature maps are extruded 3-D slabs labelled with tensor sizes such as (128, H/8, W/8, D/8); tokens are columns of grey circles; input and output are real MRI slices, the output with red/green/blue tumour overlays.
insights.emphasis: The Transformer bottleneck is the only peach-tinted region, set mid-row and expanded in the inset joined by dotted zoom lines.
insights.flow: Left to right along the row with green downsample and blue upsample arrows; three nested orange dashed skip arcs rise over the top to magenta dashed concatenation boxes on the decoder.
insights.avoid: The legend is split into two lower corners around the inset, so the reader looks in two places for symbol meanings.

core.what: one left-to-right encoder-bottleneck-decoder line: a stack of MRI slices X, shrinking green 3D feature slabs, a beige central panel holding Linear Projection, + PE, token columns and stacked Transformer Layers, Feature Mapping, then growing blue slabs ending in a brain slice with a coloured tumour segmentation

relations.form: feature volumes on one horizontal axis, each slab connected to the next by a short green (downsample) or blue (upsample) block arrow, tensor shapes such as (128, H/8, W/8, D/8) written under the slabs
dotted lines drop from the stacked Transformer Layers into a grey detail panel below: Layer Norm -> Multi-Head Attention -> + -> Layer Norm -> FFN -> + with residual lines

three orange dashed skip connections arc over the top from encoder slabs to decoder slabs, each landing in a magenta dashed box marking feature concatenation, labelled with its shape (16, H, W, D) etc.
two Transformer Layer bars with '...' between and 'xL' above
the feature map is drawn as a column of circles (tokens, d=512, N) entering and leaving the transformer stack

channels.colour: green = encoder features and downsampling, blue = decoder features and upsampling, orange = skip connections, magenta = concatenation, beige = the transformer bottleneck, pink/yellow = attention/FFN in the detail panel - mostly keyed; red/green/blue in the output segmentation are tumour classes, unkeyed, and green there reuses the encoder colour
channels.shape: 3D slabs = feature volumes; tall rounded bars = layers; circles = tokens; circled plus = addition; circled PE = position embedding (keyed)
channels.line: orange dashed = skip connection; green and blue block arrows = down/upsample; thin black arrows = data flow; dotted = zoom ties - all keyed in a legend
channels.frame: beige rounded panel = transformer bottleneck; grey panel = transformer layer detail; magenta dashed box = concatenation

quality.strengths: the transformer sits at the exact centre of the U, in its own tinted panel, so 'transformer at the bottleneck of a 3D CNN' is position; data are real (MRI slices in, segmented slice out) and every tensor carries its shape; legends key line style, arrow colour and symbols so each channel has one stated meaning
quality.weaknesses: the transformer panel is about the same size as the slabs around it, and its layer detail is pushed below, so the contribution is not the most salient element; skip connections run as long arcs across the top of the whole figure; the output's class colours are unkeyed and reuse the encoder green

figures.lesson: Put the novel bottleneck on its own tinted panel between the shrinking and growing 3-D blocks and drop its internal layer into a detail panel straight below, tied by dotted lines, so the hybrid's new part reads at both scales without interrupting the left-to-right flow.

figures.title: Attention Is All You Need

taxonomy.task: sequence-to-sequence machine translation

arrangement.units: two vertical lanes, encoder (left) and decoder (right); each holds a rounded light-grey frame around the repeated layer labelled 'Nx', with embeddings and positional encoding below the frame and (decoder only) Linear + Softmax above it
arrangement.inputs_as: plain words 'Inputs' and 'Outputs (shifted right)' under the two Embedding boxes
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; the decoder ends in 'Output Probabilities' text above the Softmax box at the top right
arrangement.shared: the encoder output is one line that leaves the top of the encoder frame and drops into the decoder's second attention block; nothing is duplicated

insights.structure: Encoder and decoder stand as two upright grey-framed towers marked 'Nx', side by side, with the decoder taller by one extra attention sub-layer and topped by Linear and Softmax.
insights.data: Data appears only as words at the ends ('Inputs', 'Outputs (shifted right)', 'Output Probabilities'); no tensors or token cells are drawn, only the operations.
insights.emphasis: Pastel fills code block type (orange attention, blue feed-forward, yellow-green Add & Norm, pink embeddings), so the repeated attention blocks stand out in both towers without any extra highlight.
insights.flow: Both towers read bottom-to-top along a central spine; residual lines loop out the side of each sub-layer back into its Add & Norm bar, and one line crosses from the encoder top into the decoder's middle block.
insights.avoid: The encoder-to-decoder line enters the cross-attention block as three forked arrows that are hard to tell apart from the decoder's own residual line next to them, so which input is K/V versus Q is not readable from the drawing.

core.what: two towers side by side, each read bottom to top - encoder on the left (Inputs -> Input Embedding -> + positional encoding -> a grey Nx frame of Multi-Head Attention and Feed Forward), decoder on the right (shifted Outputs -> Output Embedding -> a taller Nx frame of Masked Multi-Head Attention, Multi-Head Attention, Feed Forward -> Linear -> Softmax -> Output Probabilities)

relations.form: each tower is one vertical axis of stacked sub-layer boxes joined by short straight arrows

the encoder tower's top output runs up, right across the gap and down into the decoder's middle Multi-Head Attention, entering as two of its three input arrows while the third comes from the decoder's own masked attention below
each tower's repeated layer is drawn once inside a grey rounded frame labelled 'Nx' beside it
positional encoding is a sine-wave glyph beside each tower, joined to the embedding output by a circled plus
the input arrow into each attention box splits into three arrowheads (query, key, value), and a residual line leaves below each sub-layer and re-enters its Add & Norm from the side

channels.colour: fill = sub-layer type: pink embedding, orange attention, blue feed-forward, yellow Add & Norm, lavender Linear, green Softmax - one meaning, the same in both towers
channels.shape: rounded rectangles = sub-layers; circled plus = addition; a sine-wave circle = positional encoding
channels.line: solid black arrows for data flow, residual shortcuts and the cross-tower link alike
channels.frame: grey rounded rectangle = one repeated layer (Nx)

quality.strengths: the encoder-decoder structure is pure position - two towers side by side, a reused sub-layer drawn with the same shape and fill in both, and the decoder's extra cross-attention placed exactly where the encoder's wire enters it; a single colour code for sub-layer type holds across the whole figure; the Nx frame avoids drawing the stack repeatedly
quality.weaknesses: no data or representation is drawn - tokens, the encoder memory and attention weights are only implied by arrows; the cross-tower wire rises out of the encoder, turns twice and drops into the decoder, bending round the decoder's lower blocks; the three-way query/key/value split is unlabelled and residual lines use the same style as the main flow

figures.lesson: Colour each block by its type (attention, feed-forward, norm, embedding) rather than by stage, so the same operation is recognisable wherever it repeats across two towers.

figures.title: TransFuse: Fusing Transformers and CNNs for Medical Image Segmentation

taxonomy.task: polyp and medical image segmentation fusing CNN and transformer

arrangement.units: two coloured rounded branch panels (Transformer orange, CNN green L-shape) with a shared fusion column and decoder between; dashed detail insets
arrangement.inputs_as: real endoscopy image tiles at top-left, real image at bottom-right
arrangement.losses_at: next to each predicted mask at three heads (left bottom, centre, top right)
arrangement.shared: BiFusion boxes in the middle take one input from each branch

insights.structure: Two branch panels face each other: an orange Transformer Branch on the left and a green L-shaped CNN Branch at lower right, with three BiFusion boxes in a central column between them and the attention-gated decoder climbing to the upper right.
insights.data: Features are pale 3-D cuboids labelled t^i, g^i, f^i with resolutions (H/16, W/16) on the arrows; inputs are a real endoscopy photo and its patch tiles; predictions are black-and-white masks next to loss terms L(G, head(.)).
insights.emphasis: The new BiFusion module gets the large pink dashed inset at top centre, joined by red dashed zoom lines to the f^0 box; each branch has its own colour family.
insights.flow: Branch outputs run horizontally into the central BiFusion column (transformer from the left, CNN from the right), then the decoder goes up and right through AG gates; colours of arrows encode operations per the legend.
insights.avoid: Insets fill every gap (transformer layer far left, BiFusion top, legend right) and the CNN panel is notched to let the decoder pass, so the layout feels packed and the eye has no single starting point.

core.what: an orange-framed Transformer Branch on the left and a green-framed CNN Branch on the right face each other across a middle column of three BiFusion boxes, one per scale (t^0/g^0 at H/16, t^1/g^1 at H/8, t^2/g^2 at H/4), each fed by a horizontal arrow from each side

relations.form: three rows of straight horizontal arrows converge on the three BiFusion boxes from left (transformer features t^i) and right (CNN features g^i), outputs f^0, f^1, f^2 labelled beneath

two framed branches on opposite sides: the transformer branch runs top to bottom (patched image -> Linear Projection -> Transformer stack -> z^L -> t^0, t^1, t^2 via upsampling), the CNN branch runs bottom to top from an endoscopy photo through g^2, g^1, g^0

a pink dashed panel above the middle opens the BiFusion module (pooling, FC, sigmoid, product, conv, concat, residual between t^i, g^i, b^i, f^i), tied to the top BiFusion box by red dashed lines; a cream panel at the far left opens a transformer layer, tied to the stack by grey dashed lines

the decoder climbs to the upper right: f^0 -> upsample -> concatenated with f^1 via an attention gate -> f-hat^1 -> upsample -> concatenated with f^2 via another gate -> f-hat^2, with tensor sizes over each stage

three brown 'Pred. Head' arrows lead to binary mask images with loss labels L(G, head(t^2)), L(G, head(f^0)) and L(G, head(f-hat^2)), placing deep supervision at the branch, the fusion and the decoder outputs

channels.colour: orange = transformer branch, green = CNN branch (frame and feature cubes), pink = BiFusion, blue/purple = decoder features; arrow colour = operation (blue Conv, green Upsample, grey Reshape, brown prediction head, yellow AG), keyed - green therefore marks both the CNN branch and upsampling arrows
channels.shape: translucent 3D cubes = feature maps; rounded boxes = modules; yellow circles = attention gates; binary mask images = predictions; small circled letters in the detail panel = sigmoid, product, concat
channels.line: solid black arrows = features into BiFusion; dotted black = attention-gate inputs; coloured block arrows = keyed operations; dashed lines = zoom ties
channels.frame: orange rounded frame = transformer branch; green L-shaped frame = CNN branch; blue dashed boxes = concatenations in the decoder; pink and cream dashed panels = component details

quality.strengths: the parallel-branch design is placed as geometry - the two branches sit on opposite sides and meet only at the BiFusion column, one row per scale, so 'fuse at three resolutions' reads from position; the BiFusion detail is the largest inset; real data appear as the patched input, the endoscopy photo and binary masks at each supervision point
quality.weaknesses: green codes both the CNN branch and the upsample arrows; the dotted attention-gate lines rise and turn across the decoder and cross the BiFusion outputs; the BiFusion inset is packed with tiny labels (W_1^i, Avg Pool, [Max, Avg] Pool) and symbols keyed only in its corner; two detail panels, a decoder and three losses compete in one figure, so the eye has no single entry point

figures.lesson: Operation type is carried by the colour of short thick block arrows rather than by extra boxes, and the legend sets each operation's name in its arrow's own colour, so the arrows read without matching swatches.

figures.title: TransFuser: Imitation with Transformer-Based Sensor Fusion for Autonomous Driving

taxonomy.task: end-to-end driving waypoint prediction from camera and LiDAR

arrangement.units: a large titled frame holding two grey-tinted branch lanes with four rungs between them; outside it, a waypoint-decoder row at bottom right and a dashed light-green detail panel at top right
arrangement.inputs_as: real sensor images: an RGB camera frame and a LiDAR BEV render, each with a two-line label above
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the GRU chain ends in delta-w waypoint outputs
arrangement.shared: each fusion Transformer is drawn once between the bands with arrows to and from both branches

insights.structure: Two grey branch bands (image above, LiDAR BEV below) inside one titled frame are tied together by four green Transformer rungs at matching stages, and a separate waypoint decoder row and a dashed detail panel sit outside the frame on the right.
insights.data: Inputs are a wide dark RGB frame and a square black LiDAR BEV image at the left edge, each stage's feature map is a coloured cuboid with its exact C x H x W printed beside it, and the fused vectors are thin upright bars labelled 512 and 64.
insights.emphasis: Green is reserved for the fusion transformers and their zoomed detail panel (with an 'x L' repeat marker), so the contribution reads as the repeated element bridging two otherwise pastel branches.
insights.flow: Thin black lines run straight left to right along each band through circled-plus nodes, short vertical arrows go up and down between bands and rungs, the two branch outputs converge diagonally to one sum node, and the GRU chain steps right with green dashed arrows rising from a Goal Location bar.
insights.avoid: Lines are hairline-thin and the GRU/goal row plus the detail panel's token cubes are tiny relative to the frame, so the output stage and the attention mechanism are hard to read at column size.

core.what: two horizontal lanes - an Image Branch fed by an RGB photo above, a BEV Branch fed by a LiDAR bird's-eye image below - with a row of four green Transformer boxes between them, each taking a vertical arrow from both lanes and returning a vertical arrow into a circled plus on each lane, once per resolution

relations.form: two grey bands stacked inside a 'TransFuser' frame, each a left-to-right chain of trapezoid conv blocks and feature cubes labelled with sizes (176x40x72 ... 22x5x1512 on top, 64x64x72 ... 8x8x1512 below), ending in AvgPool + FC
four Transformer boxes sit in the gap between the lanes, aligned under the four stages, with straight vertical arrows down/up from each lane into the box and back to that lane's circled plus

dashed grey lines run from the last Transformer box to a green-tinted panel at the upper right showing image and BEV token cubes (H1xW1xC1, H2xW2xC2) flattened into one stack, through Self-Attention, and split back, 'x L'
the two lanes' pooled outputs converge by diagonal lines on one circled plus outside the frame, then a 512 bar -> MLP -> 64 bar
four GRU cells unrolled left to right, each emitting a waypoint offset delta-w_i above and taking the previous waypoint below, with green dashed arrows from a 'Goal Location' box feeding every cell

channels.colour: warm yellows to pinks = image-branch blocks, cool teals to blues = BEV-branch blocks (hue = modality, shade changes per stage without stated meaning); green = transformer fusion, but green also fills the Goal Location box and its dashed arrows; the token cubes in the zoom panel are multicoloured cells
channels.shape: trapezoids = conv stages; 3D cubes = feature maps with their sizes; rectangles = transformers and heads; tall thin bars = feature vectors; circled plus = element-wise sum
channels.line: solid black arrows = data flow; green dashed arrows = goal-location conditioning; dashed grey lines = zoom tie
channels.frame: one large outlined frame = the TransFuser backbone; grey bands = the two branches; a dashed-outlined green panel = transformer detail

quality.strengths: the multi-scale fusion is geometry: two equal lanes with the transformers in the corridor between them, one per resolution, connected by short straight vertical arrows; real inputs (a night street photo and a LiDAR BEV raster) start each lane, and every feature cube carries its size; the waypoint decoder is unrolled into four GRU steps
quality.weaknesses: the transformer detail panel, which explains how the two modalities are fused, is the smallest and densest element at the far right edge; green means both 'fusion transformer' and 'goal location'; the shade changes along each lane look meaningful but are not; the pooled outputs leave the frame on diagonals to a sum node that sits outside the backbone
