figures.lesson: Draw two-sensor fusion as a ladder: two tinted branch bands with matching stage-by-stage feature cuboids, and the fusion module repeated as same-coloured rungs between them, one rung zoomed into a tinted detail panel in the corner.

figures.title: Transfusion: Predict the Next Token and Diffuse Images with One Multi-Modal Model

taxonomy.task: one transformer trained with next-token prediction on text and diffusion on image patches in a single interleaved sequence

arrangement.units: one row of positions: input tokens under a single Transformer slab and output tokens over it; only the output image patches are enclosed (red frame)
arrangement.inputs_as: plain words of a caption and a question ('A cute cat .', 'What color is its nose') with <BOI>/<EOI> markers around four noisy real image patches
arrangement.losses_at: not labelled; the objectives are implied by the output row (shifted words in blue boxes, clean patches in a red frame)
arrangement.shared: one Transformer slab spans every position, text and image alike

insights.structure: A single slab spans one interleaved sequence, inputs below and outputs above, one column per position.
insights.data: Text is the actual words and images are actual patches: noisy versions in the input row and clean versions in the output row.
insights.emphasis: The image outputs are grouped by a red frame while text outputs sit in individual blue boxes, so the two prediction kinds differ at a glance.
insights.flow: Short straight vertical arrows, one per position, up into and out of the Transformer; the text outputs are shifted one position right of their inputs.
insights.avoid: Neither objective is named or keyed in the figure and the dashed empty box above <BOI> is unexplained, so the red-vs-blue distinction relies on the caption.

core.what: one Transformer slab spans an interleaved sequence of words and image patches, with text predicted next-token and patches denoised in the same output row

relations.form: a single wide slab spanning every input position, text and image
two output treatments in one row: blue-boxed words shifted one position right vs four clean patches grouped in a red frame directly above their noisy inputs
one column per position, bottom to top: input token, arrow, Transformer, arrow, output

channels.colour: output box colour = prediction kind: blue outline = text token, red frame = image patches; the slab is neutral grey
channels.shape: boxed cells = output tokens, plain words and patch images = inputs, one wide rectangle = the model
channels.line: short vertical arrows = per-position data flow only; dashed outline = an empty output slot
channels.frame: the red rectangle = one image as a unit of output

quality.strengths: Data drawn as data (real words, noisy and clean patches); the next-token shift and noisy-to-clean denoising are visible from position alone; one meaning per channel; all lines short, straight and aligned in columns.
quality.weaknesses: The two objectives are not named or keyed, the dashed empty box above <BOI> is unexplained, and the attention pattern (causal for text, bidirectional within an image) is not shown; the plain grey slab gives no hint where the modalities are treated differently.

figures.lesson: Show two objectives in one model by the outputs alone: text targets shifted one position (next-token) in one box style, image patches noisy below and clean above (denoising) in a differently coloured frame.

figures.title: Transolver: A Fast Transformer Solver for PDEs on General Geometries

taxonomy.task: PDE solving on general geometries (Physics-Attention)
taxonomy.note: modality: mesh / physical field data

arrangement.units: left: dashed layer box plus a solid zoom panel; right (after a dashed vertical rule): unframed data drawing of the same module
arrangement.inputs_as: a textured 3-D slab of the physical field
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Left third: a dashed pre-norm layer with a zoom into a black-framed block diagram of Physics-Attention (stacked frames for heads); a vertical dashed rule; right two-thirds: the same attention drawn again with the data.
insights.data: The input field is a 3-D slab with a flow-field texture, fanned by navy lines into a staircase of slabs weighted by slice weights, pooled into small blue token cubes, mixed by pink attention lines, then broadcast back to blue-gradient slabs and merged into an output slab; shapes labelled N x C, M x (N x C), M x C.
insights.emphasis: Physics-Attention is the only pink box in the layer and its token step is dark-red text in both the block diagram and the data drawing, tying the two views together.
insights.flow: The left layer reads bottom to top; the right half reads left to right Slice -> Attention for Tokens -> DeSlice, with a brown arc for slice weights over the top.
insights.avoid: The right half's many crossing navy and pink lines make individual slices hard to trace; a lighter or fewer-slice version would read faster.

core.what: the large right panel performs Physics-Attention on a drawn field: an N x C mesh slab is 'Slice'd by fanning blue lines into a staircase of M weighted copies of the field, each aggregated by a green arrow into one physics-aware token cube, the tokens attend to each other through a pink web of edges, are broadcast back to M slabs, and 'DeSlice' blue lines converge into the output N x C slab

relations.form: the field is drawn as a coloured mesh image around an airfoil-like hole, repeated on each slice slab with different weight colourings, so slicing is shown on the data
left to right: input slab -> Slice -> M slice slabs (M x (N x C)) -> M tokens (M x C) -> attention -> M tokens -> M broadcast slabs -> DeSlice -> output slab, each stage labelled with its shape below
a brown arc labelled 'Slice Weights N x M' sweeps over the top from Slice to DeSlice, the same weights used to split and to recombine

on the left a transformer block (LayerNorm, Physics-Attention, LayerNorm, Feed-Forward with residual pluses) has its pink Physics-Attention box opened by two dashed lines into a panel: Linear -> Slice -> Aggregate -> Attention for Tokens -> Broadcast -> Deslice -> Linear, with a Slice Weights slab beside it and stacked frames labelled 'Heads'
at DeSlice, blue lines from every broadcast slab converge on one point before the output slab

channels.colour: blue lines and blue labels = slice/deslice assignment, green arrows = aggregate and broadcast (keyed), brown = slice weights (arc, label and detail-panel slab), pink/red = attention among tokens (edge web, 'Attention for Tokens' label, the Physics-Attention block fill), navy shades = token cubes; the same codes hold between the detail panel and the big panel; field colours inside slabs = physical values; blue also fills the unrelated Feed-Forward block
channels.shape: slabs in perspective = fields over the mesh; small cubes = physics-aware tokens; rounded rectangles = layers
channels.line: solid coloured lines = the operations named above; dashed black lines = zoom tie; a vertical dashed line separates the two panels
channels.frame: a dashed rounded frame = one transformer block; a solid rounded panel = the Physics-Attention module with stacked copies for heads

quality.strengths: the new attention is the largest element and is drawn on the structure it acts on - the reader sees N mesh points fold into M slice tokens and unfold again, with tensor shapes under every stage; the detail panel and the big panel use the same words and colours (Slice, Aggregate, Broadcast, Deslice, brown Slice Weights), so the module and its picture can be matched term by term; the shared slice weights are one arc spanning exactly from Slice to DeSlice
quality.weaknesses: the pink all-to-all attention web and the fanning blue slice lines overlap the token row, making the middle of the panel busy; the staircase of perspective slabs partly hides each slice's field; blue fills the Feed-Forward block while also meaning slice assignment

figures.lesson: Explain the new operator twice side by side — a small block diagram zoomed from its box, then the same steps drawn on the physical field itself (field slab split into weighted copies, pooled into a few token cubes, broadcast back) — and give the shared step the same text colour in both.

figures.title: TransUNet: Transformers Make Strong Encoders for Medical Image Segmentation

taxonomy.task: multi-organ CT segmentation

arrangement.units: (b) the main architecture with sub-groups (lilac CNN frame, green transformer frame, dashed concatenation squares); (a) a cream rounded detail inset at the far left, linked by dashed zoom lines
arrangement.inputs_as: a real CT slice above the CNN encoder
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; the decoder ends at a segmentation head arrow into a coloured-mask CT slice at top-right

(16, H, W))

panel (a) on the left opens one Transformer Layer (Layer Norm, MSA, +, Layer Norm, MLP, +, with residual lines) from 'Embedded Sequence x_p^1 ... x_p^N' to z_1, tied to the green transformer frame by grey dashed lines
two Transformer Layer bars with a vertical ellipsis and '(n = 12)' between them

channels.colour: purple = CNN encoder features (also inside the concatenation boxes, so skip origin is visible), blue = decoder features, green frame = transformer encoder, yellow/orange = transformer sub-layers and projection; arrow colour = operation, keyed (blue Conv3x3 ReLU, green Upsample, yellow segmentation head); output colours = organ classes, unkeyed
channels.shape: 3D slabs = feature maps; rounded bars = layers; circled plus = residual addition; CT images = data
channels.line: coloured block arrows = keyed decoder operations; black dotted arrows = 'Downsample' in the legend, but the same dotted style draws both the CNN's internal downsampling and the long skip curves, so dotted carries two meanings; grey dashed lines = zoom tie
channels.frame: pink rounded frame = CNN; green rounded frame = transformer; grey dashed boxes = concatenation (keyed); cream panel (a) = layer detail

quality.strengths: the hybrid encoder is one vertical column and the decoder one rising staircase, so the U-shape reads from position with every slab carrying its tensor shape; encoder purple reappears inside each concatenation box, so the reader sees which feature is skipped where; real CT input and a coloured segmentation output frame the pipeline; a legend keys arrow colours and the concatenation frame

figures.title: Tune-A-Video: One-Shot Tuning of Image Diffusion Models for Text-to-Video Generation

channels.line: short black down arrows only between the source row and the first edit; plus signs mark combination
channels.frame: grey dashed rounded column = the family of pluggable pretrained T2I models

quality.strengths: the edited videos are drawn as identical rows under the source with frame columns aligned, so 'motion preserved, subject and style changed' is read by scanning down a column; the changed words of each prompt are tinted, so the edit is legible without comparing sentences
quality.weaknesses: the method itself is not shown - Tune-A-Video is one box and its relation to the T2I models is a plus sign; the left-column variants are only loosely aligned with the rows they produce; the down arrows exist only between the source and the first edited row; blue codes both prompt edits and model fills

figures.lesson: In a video-editing teaser, put the source clip as the top row of frames with small down-arrows to the edited rows below, and introduce each edited row with its prompt written between the rows with only the changed words coloured.

figures.title: Tune-A-Video: One-Shot Tuning of Image Diffusion Models for Text-to-Video Generation

taxonomy.task: one-shot tuning of T2I diffusion for text-to-video

arrangement.units: two unframed sections Fine-Tuning and Inference, separated by a vertical rule, each with a large title
arrangement.inputs_as: a stack of real video frames with a quoted prompt below
arrangement.losses_at: reconstruction loss as a line arching over the top of the fine-tuning section
arrangement.shared: the same video drawn as input in both sections

insights.structure: Two sections split by a thin vertical rule, titled 'Fine-Tuning' (wide, left) and 'Inference' (narrow, right); the fine-tuning U-Net container has a blue strip zooming one attention column into ST-Attn, Cross-Attn, FFN, T-Attn.
insights.data: Every video is an offset stack of about six frames (real ski photos or grey noise); the prompt is a handwritten quote; Q and KV projections are small split squares, orange when updated, grey when frozen.
insights.emphasis: Orange 'Updated' vs grey 'Frozen' fill marks exactly which projections are tuned; the edited prompt words are blue in the inference half.
insights.flow: Fine-tuning reads left to right video -> diffusion -> noise -> U-Net -> video, with a 'Reconstruction Loss' line arching over the top; inference is a clockwise loop DDIM inversion -> noise -> denoising -> edited video.
insights.avoid: The prompt line in Fine-Tuning runs along the bottom and up into Cross-Attn through the zoomed inset, a long route that is easy to miss.

core.what: two panels split by a vertical rule: a wide 'Fine-Tuning' panel on the left (skiing video -> diffusion xT -> noise -> U-Net -> reconstructed video, with a Reconstruction Loss line over the top) and a narrower 'Inference' panel on the right (same video -> DDIM inversion -> noise -> denoising with a new prompt -> Spider-Man video)

relations.form: large titles 'Fine-Tuning' and 'Inference' head two side-by-side panels separated by a thin vertical line, the same source clip starting both
fine-tuning reads left to right along one line of frame stacks and boxes; inference runs right through DDIM inversion to a noise stack, then down and back left through denoising to the edited clip
blue dotted lines drop from one attention block of the U-Net into a blue panel below it showing ST-Attn, Cross-Attn, FFN and T-Attn, each attention split into a Q cell and a KV cell
a line leaves the input video, runs over the whole panel and drops into the reconstructed video, labelled 'Reconstruction Loss'
the prompt 'A man is skiing' sends a line along the bottom and up into the Cross-Attn KV cell; at inference the new prompt enters the denoising box from below
'xT steps' labels above the diffusion box, the U-Net frame and DDIM inversion stand for the repeated denoising

channels.colour: orange = updated parameters (every Q cell), light grey = frozen (KV cells, FFN), light blue = attention blocks - keyed; but grey also fills the Conv Block glyph, so grey carries both 'conv block' and 'frozen'; blue text in the inference prompt = edited words
channels.shape: stacked frames = video clips; noise stacks = latents; tall capsules = U-Net blocks (grey conv, blue attention, keyed); rounded boxes = processes
channels.line: solid black arrows = data flow; dashed arrows inside the U-Net = skip connections; blue dotted lines = zoom tie
channels.frame: a rounded frame = the U-Net; a blue rounded panel = the opened transformer block

quality.strengths: what is trained is drawn at the finest grain - inside the opened attention block only the Q cells are orange, so the reader sees that the method updates query projections and leaves the rest frozen; data are real (the skiing clip, noise stacks, the edited Spider-Man clip and quoted prompts) and the two phases share the source clip so their difference is visible
quality.weaknesses: grey means both convolution block and frozen parameter; the reconstruction-loss line runs over the top of the entire panel and the prompt line along its bottom, each with right-angle bends; the inference path turns back on itself (right, down, left), so its output lands to the left of its input

figures.lesson: Draw every video tensor - clean, noised, edited - as the same offset stack of frames so the noise and editing stages read as changes to one clip, and mark which projections are trained inside the zoomed attention blocks with an orange/grey Q|KV split keyed by a short legend.

figures.title: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation

taxonomy.task: biomedical image segmentation

arrangement.units: no enclosed regions: one U-shaped composition, levels separated only by vertical position
arrangement.inputs_as: a text label 'input image tile' beside the first one-channel bar
arrangement.losses_at: no loss drawn; the right arm ends in a text label 'output segmentation map'
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: The contracting path descends the left side and the expanding path climbs the right side, with each resolution level drawn at its own height so the two arms mirror each other across an open gap.
insights.data: Feature maps are flat blue bars sized by channels (width) and resolution (height), labelled with channel counts above and rotated spatial sizes beside, and copied encoder maps appear as white bars joined to the decoder's blue ones.
insights.emphasis: Nothing is accented; the U silhouette and the four long grey copy-and-crop arrows spanning its gap carry the idea on their own.
insights.flow: Read down the left arm (dark red pool arrows), across the bottom, up the right arm (green up-conv arrows), with short navy conv arrows stepping left-to-right inside each level and grey skips running straight across.
insights.avoid: Input and output are plain text labels ('input image tile', 'output segmentation map') rather than a picture of the data, and the many small rotated size labels are hard to read at print size.

core.what: the network is laid out as a literal U: feature maps step down the left side level by level (572x572 to 32x32) and climb back up the right side to the output segmentation map, with each level's left and right halves facing each other across a straight grey 'copy and crop' arrow

relations.form: feature maps drawn as blue bars in rows, each row one resolution level; dark red down arrows between levels on the left, green up arrows on the right, short blue arrows between bars within a level

at each level a long straight grey arrow runs horizontally from the last left-side map to a white (copied) bar placed flush beside the first blue bar of the right side, the concatenation drawn as two adjoining bars

each bar's height tracks spatial size and its width channel count, with channel numbers above (64, 128 ... 1024) and spatial sizes rotated beside (572x572, 284^2 ... 28^2); a dashed outline inside the left bars marks the crop region

channels.colour: arrow colour = operation, keyed at lower right: dark blue conv 3x3 ReLU, grey copy and crop, dark red max pool 2x2, green up-conv 2x2, teal conv 1x1; bar fill: blue = computed feature map, white = copied feature map - one meaning each
channels.shape: vertical bars = multi-channel feature maps, sized by resolution and channels; arrows are the only operation glyphs
channels.line: all solid arrows; operation is coded by colour and direction (down = pool, up = up-conv, right = conv or copy)

quality.strengths: the architecture's defining shape is the drawing itself - depth = resolution, so contracting and expanding paths face each other level by level and every skip is a short horizontal straight arrow between the two sides; the feature maps are drawn as nouns with their sizes, so the cropping (568 vs 392) and the channel doubling are readable; one keyed colour per operation and white for copied maps leave no channel carrying two meanings
quality.weaknesses: no real image or segmentation is shown, only the words 'input image tile' and 'output segmentation map'; the grey dimension labels are small and rotated; the dashed crop outlines are not in the legend

figures.lesson: Let vertical position encode resolution and bar width encode channel count, so the descending and ascending arms and the skip bridges between equal heights read as the architecture without a single container.

figures.title: All are Worth Words: A ViT Backbone for Diffusion Models

taxonomy.task: ViT backbone for diffusion models

arrangement.units: one vertical stack plus a right column (legend and block detail) behind a dashed rule
arrangement.inputs_as: tokens t, c and real noisy image patches in a dashed box; tiled x_t photo at lower right
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: One vertical stack: input tokens, Embedding Layer, five peach Transformer Blocks, Linear, output patches, Rearrange, Conv3x3, Predicted noise; a dashed vertical rule sets off a right column with the legend and Transformer Block internals.
insights.data: Inputs t, c and image patches are a row of small squares in a dashed box captioned 'All as words', with the noisy x_t as a 3x3 tiled photo; outputs are noise patches and a noise image; embedded tokens are numbered tiles.
insights.emphasis: The long skip connections are thick black nested elbows on the stack's right, merging at circled-C nodes, which carries the U-Net idea inside a plain ViT.
insights.flow: Bottom to top along the stack; the skips loop from lower blocks up the right side into upper blocks.

core.what: one vertical stack read bottom to top: a dashed box of inputs 'All as words' (a t token, a c token and the noisy image x_t cut into patches) -> Embedding Layer -> numbered tokens -> five Transformer Blocks -> Linear -> noise patches -> Rearrange to 3xHxW -> Conv3x3 -> a predicted-noise image

relations.form: full-width blocks stacked on one vertical axis, joined by short straight up arrows, with token-level arrows only at the bottom (into and out of the embedding) and top (out of the last block into Linear)
time t, condition c and each image patch sit side by side in one dashed row as equal tokens, the patches cut from the dog image x_t drawn at the right; the outputs are drawn as a row of noise patches

two thick black long skip connections leave the outputs of the lower blocks, run right and up in nested brackets, and enter circled-C (concatenate + linear) nodes just before the upper blocks, the outermost skip joining the first and last blocks

a separate panel to the right of a dashed vertical rule shows one Transformer Block (Embeddings -> Norm -> Multi-Head Attention -> + -> Norm -> MLP -> +, with residual lines), in the same peach frame as the stack's blocks

channels.colour: peach = transformer blocks (in the stack and the detail frame), cyan = linear/conv/MLP layers, pink = Norm, green = attention, lavender = embedding; the input chips are grey (t), yellow (c) and purple-tinted position numbers - mostly one meaning each, though the purple position chips are unkeyed
channels.shape: wide rounded bars = layers; small chips = tokens; image tiles = patches; circled plus = add, circled C = concatenate + linear (both keyed at top right)
channels.line: thin arrows = data flow; thick black elbowed lines = long skip connections (labelled)
channels.frame: dashed rounded box = the token sequence ('All as words'); a dashed vertical rule separates the block detail

quality.strengths: both of the design's ideas are drawn: conditions and patches sit as equal chips in one input row, and the long skips are nested brackets whose nesting shows that shallow blocks connect to deep ones in a U pattern inside a plain stack; data appear as data at both ends (the patched dog image in, noise patches and a predicted-noise image out)
quality.weaknesses: the long skips leave the stack, turn twice and re-enter, so each runs as a bracket around the blocks it skips; the two output arrows for the t and c tokens above the last block lead nowhere; the block-detail panel is not tied to the stack by any line or matching label beyond its peach frame

figures.lesson: Each input's tint (grey time, yellow condition, blue patches) continues from its input tile into a matching segment of the shared Embedding Layer bar and onto its embedded token, so which slots belong to which input can be traced without labels.

figures.title: Uformer: A General U-Shaped Transformer for Image Restoration

taxonomy.task: general image restoration (denoise, derain, deblur)

arrangement.units: three unframed panels (a) overview, (b) block detail in a grey dashed container, (c) modulator detail, separated by dashed vertical rules
arrangement.inputs_as: text label 'Degraded Image'
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Three panels in a row separated by black dashed rules and labelled (a)-(c) underneath: (a) the U-shaped overview takes about 60% of the width, (b) the LeWin block internals, (c) how a modulator is added per window.
insights.data: No tensors drawn: shapes like 2C x H/2 x W/2 are light grey-blue text above each encoder column; in (c) a feature map is a 2x2 tinted grid whose quadrant tints repeat on the per-window squares.
insights.emphasis: The new Modulators sit in a labelled dashed box in the bottom-right of (a) as coloured squares, matching the blue Modulator square in (c).
insights.flow: (a) runs left to right along the top encoder row, down to the bottleneck at the right, and back right to left along the bottom decoder row, with vertical skip arrows between partners; (b) and (c) read bottom to top.
insights.avoid: Modulator lines in (a) run back under the whole decoder row to each block, adding long lines that cross the bottom of the panel.

core.what: panel (a) folds the U into two rows: the encoder runs left to right along the top (Degraded Image -> Input Projection -> LeWin Blocks xN1 -> down-sampling -> LeWin Blocks xN2 -> ...), a bottleneck LeWin Blocks xN5 sits at the right between the rows, and the decoder runs right to left along the bottom to Output Projection and Restored Image

relations.form: two horizontal rows of rounded blocks joined by short arrows through circled down- and up-sampling glyphs, with feature sizes (3xHxW, CxHxW ... 16C x H/16 x W/16) written in grey above the top row

short straight vertical arrows drop from each encoder LeWin block to the decoder LeWin block directly below it (skip connections); a separate line from the degraded input runs down into a circled plus before the restored output (global residual)
a dashed 'Modulators' box at the lower right holds small blue and cyan squares whose lines run left beneath the decoder row and up into each decoder block
panel (b), behind a dashed vertical rule, opens one LeWin block (LN -> W/MW-MSA -> + -> LN -> LeFF -> +); panel (c) opens the modulated window attention - neither is tied to (a) by a line
panel (c) splits a 2x2 'Feature map' into four tinted windows, each window lifted to its own tinted box, a Modulator square added to each by grey lines and circled pluses, then one MSA per window

channels.colour: light blue = LeWin blocks, grey-blue = projections; in (b) green LN, blue MSA, orange LeFF; in (c) peach/grey/yellow/green = which window, and blue = the modulator and the MSA boxes; blue therefore carries LeWin block, attention and modulator
channels.shape: rounded rectangles = blocks; circled down/up arrows = down- and up-sampling (keyed); circled plus = addition; small squares = modulators
channels.line: solid black arrows = feature flow and skips; grey double lines in (c) = the modulator being added to each window
channels.frame: dashed box = the set of modulators; dashed grey panel = one LeWin block; dashed vertical rules separate panels (a), (b), (c)

quality.strengths: folding the U into two rows makes every skip connection a short straight vertical arrow between blocks of the same scale; panel (c) draws the window attention on a small instance - a feature map split into colour-coded windows that reappear as separate boxes, each receiving the same modulator - so the modulator's role is geometric; tensor sizes are written once above the encoder row
quality.weaknesses: the modulator lines leave the dashed box and run as long L-shaped wires beneath the whole decoder row to reach each block; blue fills LeWin blocks, MSA and modulators alike; panels (b) and (c) have no tie back to the blocks in (a) they detail, and the bottleneck's connection from '...' is a bent arrow down the right edge

figures.lesson: Fold the U on its side - encoder along the top row, decoder returning along the bottom row, bottleneck dropped at the right end - so input and output share the left edge, every skip is a short vertical arrow, and the freed bottom-right corner holds the new component (a dashed 'Modulators' box) wired into each decoder block from below.

figures.title: Hierarchical Text-Conditional Image Generation with CLIP Latents

taxonomy.task: text-to-image generation via CLIP image embeddings
taxonomy.note: the prior is drawn in two variants (autoregressive, diffusion); diffusion decoder

arrangement.units: two unframed horizontal lanes separated by a dotted rule: CLIP training (top) and prior + decoder generation (bottom)
arrangement.inputs_as: a quoted text prompt in large blue type at the far left
arrangement.losses_at: the 'CLIP objective' as a double-headed arrow between the text and image embeddings in the top lane; no loss drawn for prior or decoder
arrangement.shared: one text encoder on the left whose output embedding is split by a bracket into both lanes

insights.structure: Two lanes split by a stepped dotted rule, CLIP training above and generation below, with the text encoder trapezoid on the left spanning both and a bracket fanning its embedding into each lane.
insights.data: The input is a quoted prompt in large blue text, embeddings are vertical columns of shaded cells coloured by modality (blue text, brown image), and outputs are real generated corgi images at the right edge of each lane.
insights.emphasis: The prior's two variants are stacked grey boxes with miniature attention-arc and diffusion-circle diagrams, and the cell colour switching from blue to brown across them shows the text-to-image embedding mapping.
insights.flow: Strictly left to right in both lanes: prompt -> text encoder -> embedding -> (CLIP objective | prior -> decoder) -> image.
insights.avoid: The dotted divider bends diagonally under the text encoder and the two halves have no titles, so a reader must rely on the caption to know the top lane is training-only.

core.what: one text encoder at the far left whose embedding is bracketed into two lanes split by a stepped dotted rule: the CLIP training lane above and the prior-plus-decoder generation lane below

relations.form: in the top lane the text-embedding column and the image-embedding column face each other across a double-headed 'CLIP objective' arrow, the image encoder trapezoid and the real corgi image behind it on the right
bottom lane runs left to right: text embedding -> prior box -> image-embedding column -> decoder (columns of circles) -> generated corgi image
the prior's two variants stacked as grey rounded boxes, an autoregressive one drawn as attention arcs over a row of circles above a diffusion one drawn as three columns of circles
two unframed horizontal lanes (training above, generation below) separated by a dotted rule that steps down around the text encoder

channels.colour: modality: blue for text (prompt type, text encoder, text-embedding cells) and brown for image (image encoder, image-embedding cells); the decoder's circles shade blue -> purple -> brown, so colour also tracks progress from text to image there
channels.shape: trapezoids are encoders, vertical cell columns are embeddings, grey rounded boxes are the prior variants, circle columns are diffusion steps
channels.line: solid arrows are data flow; the double-headed arrow is the contrastive objective; the dotted rule is the lane divider
channels.frame: none for the lanes; only the two prior variants are boxed

quality.strengths: The shared text encoder straddles the dotted rule so its reuse in both lanes is visible by position; embeddings are drawn as cell columns between encoders and the objective; the blue-to-brown cell colour across the prior shows what the prior produces; real prompt and generated images are drawn as data.
quality.weaknesses: The prior and decoder, the paper's contribution, are labelled only by small text under the bottom lane and are no larger than the pretrained CLIP part; the decoder's circle columns blend colour meanings (modality vs denoising progress); no objective is drawn for the prior or decoder.

figures.lesson: Show a model built on a pretrained one by drawing the pretrained training above a dotted rule and the new generation pipeline below, sharing one input encoder that straddles the rule.

figures.title: UNet++: A Nested U-Net Architecture for Medical Image Segmentation

taxonomy.task: medical image segmentation

arrangement.units: (a) main node graph top-left, (b) zoomed top row below it, (c) a column of four pruned copies at right; all separated by whitespace and lettered underneath; the only frame is the dashed grey 'Backbone' band
arrangement.inputs_as: the first node circle X^{0,0}; no data shown
arrangement.losses_at: one boxed L at the top centre, with red lines dropping to each top-row output node
arrangement.shared: the backbone nodes are drawn once and reused by every nested row

insights.structure: Panel (a) arranges circle nodes as an inverted triangle with the encoder on a tilted dashed 'Backbone' band, (b) zooms into the top row below it, and (c) stacks four pruned variants down the right edge.
insights.data: There is no image data at all: every block is an outlined circle named X^{i,j}, and (b) writes each node's input as an equation over its neighbours.
insights.emphasis: Original U-Net nodes are black while the added nested nodes are green and the dense skips blue, and the red deep-supervision lines converge on one boxed L.
insights.flow: Read down the backbone diagonal, then rightward along each row through dotted skip arcs, with green arrows lifting each node into the row above toward the output X^{0,4} at the top right.
insights.avoid: Overlapping blue and black dotted arcs between the same nodes pile into a hatched band along the top rows, and the legend floats in the gap between panels (a) and (c).

core.what: the network drawn as an inverted triangle of X^{i,j} circle nodes, encoder down the left diagonal and the added nested nodes filling the triangle, with green up-arrows and blue dense skips between them

relations.form: backbone nodes descend a diagonal inside a tilted dashed 'Backbone' band, then each row runs left to right toward the output node X^{0,4} on the right edge

each nested node receives dotted skip arcs from all earlier nodes in its row plus a green up-sampling arrow from the row below; panel (b) writes each fusion as an equation x^{0,j}=H[...] above its node
panel (b) re-draws only the top row of (a) below it, enlarged, with the U(x^{1,j}) inputs labelled beneath each node
panel (c) stacks four pruned copies UNet++ L4, L3, L2, L1 down the right edge, each a smaller triangle with fewer rows
red lines rise from every top-row nested node to one boxed loss L above the triangle (deep supervision)

channels.colour: black = original U-Net nodes and arrows, green = the added nested nodes and their up-sampling arrows, blue dotted = the dense skips, red = deep-supervision wires; the paper's additions are exactly the coloured elements
channels.shape: circles are convolution nodes, a small square box is the loss, arrow-head types are keyed (down-sampling, up-sampling, skip)
channels.line: solid arrows = down/up-sampling, dotted arrows = skip connections (black for plain U-Net skips, blue for the dense ones), red solid = supervision
channels.frame: a tilted dashed grey band marks the backbone; panels (a)/(b)/(c) are separated by space and letters only

quality.strengths: Baseline in black and additions in green/blue make the contribution an overlay on the familiar U shape; the triangle geometry itself shows the nested-depth relation; the pruned variants in (c) reuse the exact same glyphs at small size; a key explains every arrow style.
quality.weaknesses: Panel (b) types fusion equations above nodes rather than drawing them; dotted skip arcs in the top row stack into a dense tangle that is hard to follow; no feature maps or image data are drawn, so nothing shows what X^{i,j} holds.

figures.lesson: Draw the baseline network in black and only the added nodes and connections in colour, so the contribution reads as an overlay on the familiar skeleton.

figures.title: UNETR: Transformers for 3D Medical Image Segmentation

taxonomy.task: 3D medical image segmentation

arrangement.units: one composition: grey encoder panel (x12) at left, unframed decoder staircase; framed legend box
arrangement.inputs_as: a stack of real MRI slices at top-left
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: The transformer encoder is one vertical grey column at the far left; tokens z3, z6, z9, z12 leave it as horizontal rails at even heights and the CNN decoder climbs as a diagonal staircase to the top right, merging one rail per step at blue C nodes.
insights.data: Convolution blocks are coloured 3-D cuboids in short runs (blue, yellow, green, grey by operation) with tensor shapes like H/16 x W/16 x D/16 x 768 typeset under each rail; the input and output are real brain MRI slices, the output with a red overlay.
insights.emphasis: The rails from evenly spaced transformer layers make the 'skip from transformer depth' idea the dominant visual; the decoder staircase is the only diagonal element.
insights.flow: Input top-left goes down the encoder column; rails run right; the decoder rises bottom-centre to top-right ending at the output at upper right.
insights.avoid: Transformer internals are flat square boxes while decoder blocks are 3-D cuboids, two unrelated drawing registers in one figure; the legend box takes a large bottom-right area.

core.what: a vertical transformer column on the left emits tokens z3, z6, z9, z12 as horizontal rails at even heights, and the CNN decoder climbs a diagonal staircase up to the top right, merging one rail per step at a blue C node

relations.form: each staircase step is a blue concatenation circle where a horizontal skip rail from the encoder meets the upsampled path from below; the full-resolution input rail runs along the top to the last C node
the grey encoder column draws one transformer layer (Norm, Multi-Head Attention, add, Norm, MLP, add) with residual loops and a 'x12' tag
input MRI volume at top left -> linear projection -> embedded patches -> transformer column; output segmentation volume at top right

channels.colour: cube colour = decoder operation type keyed in the legend box (green deconv, blue deconv+conv+BN+ReLU, yellow conv+BN+ReLU, grey 1x1x1 conv); inside the encoder colour only separates block types (yellow Norm, green MHA, teal MLP, orange embedded patches) with no key
channels.shape: 3-D cubes are conv operations, flat rectangles are transformer sub-blocks, circles are concatenation (C) or addition (+)
channels.line: single solid black arrows for all data flow; tensor sizes are written under each segment
channels.frame: a grey panel encloses the repeated transformer layer

quality.strengths: Each merge node sits at the height of the rail it consumes, so which encoder depth feeds which decoder step reads from geometry alone; tensor sizes under every rail make resolution changes legible; real MRI input and red/green segmentation output are drawn as data.
quality.weaknesses: Colour carries two codes (decoder op type keyed in the legend, encoder block types unkeyed); the legend box takes a large lower-right area; the transformer encoder, the novelty, is a narrow grey strip while routine conv cubes occupy most of the canvas.

figures.lesson: Pull skip features out of a vertical encoder column as horizontal rails at evenly spaced heights and let the decoder climb a diagonal staircase back up, so every merge node sits at the height of the rail it consumes and its tensor size is written just under it.

figures.title: UNETR++: Delving into Efficient and Accurate 3D Medical Image Segmentation

taxonomy.task: 3D medical image segmentation

arrangement.units: left: unframed U-net overview whose encoder stages sit in dotted tan rounded containers; right: one dashed brown detail panel (EPA) with two tinted sub-bands (spatial blue, channel green)
arrangement.inputs_as: a CT volume cube labelled Input HxWxDx4 at the top-left corner
arrangement.shared: shared W^K and W^Q drawn once in a dotted column straddling both attention branches, marked K_shared/Q_shared

insights.structure: The left half is the U-shaped overview (encoder column of dotted EPA+downsampling containers descending the left edge, decoder staircase climbing to the upper right), and the right half is a large dashed brown panel zooming into the EPA block, split into a blue spatial-attention band on top and a green channel-attention band below with a shared W^K/W^Q column straddling both.
insights.data: Input and output are black 3-D cubes with a CT slice on the front face (output overlaid with coloured organ masks), feature maps inside the EPA panel are grey slab stacks, and the attention maps are striped pastel cuboids labelled with D/C/HW axes; every skip arrow carries its tensor shape (H/4 x W/4 x D/4 x C1, ...).
insights.emphasis: The contribution (EPA) is pink in every stage of the overview and is blown up by a pink translucent zoom wedge from one EPA box into the detail panel, with the shared K/Q weights marked by curved K_shared / Q_shared arrows.
insights.flow: The overview reads top-left input down the encoder, across the skips to the decoder and up to the output at the top centre; the detail panel reads left to right from the input slabs to the two attention outputs merging with + at the right edge, with a dashed skip connection looping around the bottom.
insights.avoid: The tensor-shape fractions on every skip line crowd the overview and are near-illegible at column width; the zoom wedge also covers a large empty area between the two halves.

core.what: a small U-shaped overview in the left half and a large Efficient Paired-Attention block detail in the right half, tied by a translucent pink wedge fanning from the top decoder EPA box

relations.form: encoder stages descend the left edge as dotted containers (downsampling cube + pink EPA box) and the decoder climbs a staircase to the upper right, with a full-resolution path along the top from input volume to output volume
each decoder step is a circled + where a horizontal skip from an encoder stage meets the upsampled path from below, the skip's tensor size written along it
inside the detail the spatial-attention branch sits in a blue-tinted upper band and the channel-attention branch in a green-tinted lower band, each ending in a stacked attention-map volume
the shared W^K and W^Q projections sit in one dotted container straddling the two tinted bands, with curved arrows labelled K_shared and Q_shared
the same pink EPA box repeats in every encoder and decoder stage

channels.colour: in the overview colour = block type keyed in the legend (light blue downsampling, dark blue upsampling, pink EPA, green ConvBlock, grey 1x1x1 conv); in the detail tint = branch (blue spatial, green channel), while projection boxes use another set (yellow W^K, purple W^Q, grey/orange W^V) - colour carries three codes
channels.shape: 3-D cubes are conv operations, rounded pink boxes are EPA blocks, small circles/rounded boxes are operators (dot product, softmax, transpose, addition)
channels.line: solid arrows are data flow; dashed lines are skip connections (keyed); curved coloured arrows mark weight sharing
channels.frame: dotted containers group each encoder stage; a dashed brown frame encloses the EPA detail; tinted bands enclose each attention branch

quality.strengths: The contribution (EPA) gets the most space and is tied to its place in the U-Net by a wedge; shared Q/K weights are shown by a container straddling the two branch bands, i.e. sharing by position; attention maps are drawn as volumes with their sizes; a full legend keys every glyph.
quality.weaknesses: Colour carries block type, branch identity and projection identity at once; the detail panel is dense with small operator glyphs and long wires that bend round the attention maps; the overview's decoder staircase is cramped at small size.

figures.title: CLIP-Driven Universal Model for Organ Segmentation and Tumor Detection

core.what: one light-grey ground divided by a bottom ruler into four phases (Backbone, Vectorized Scene Learning, Planning Inferring Phase, Planning Training Phase), the motion and map transformers mirrored above and below the BEV features and the training-only constraints in a tall grey panel at the right

relations.form: multi-view images -> BEV encoder trapezoid -> BEV feature grid -> vectorized transformers -> ego query -> Planning Transformer -> ego vector, left to right
agent query -> Vectorized Motion Transformer runs along the top and map query -> Vectorized Map Transformer along the bottom, symmetric about the BEV features
a grey stack of three tinted ego-query squares sends k,v / q / k,v arrows into the Planning Transformer, with Ego Status from above and the 'Turn Left' driving command from below
motion vectors, map vectors and the planned ego trajectory are drawn as small top-down vector illustrations on grey rounded tiles on the arrows
motion, ego and map vectors run as long arrows into the right panel's three green constraint boxes (ego-agent collision, ego-boundary, ego-lane)

channels.colour: blue tint = agent/motion side, pink tint = map side, green = planning (Planning Transformer, constraint boxes, ego query), beige = BEV features; each query square takes the tint of the transformer that consumes it
channels.shape: trapezoid = encoder, rounded rectangles = transformers, small squares = queries, grey tiles = rendered vector outputs
channels.line: single solid black arrows for all flow; k, v and q labels on the arrows into the planner
channels.frame: a darker grey rounded panel sets apart the training-only constraints; a grey pill groups the ego query

quality.strengths: The motion/map symmetry about the BEV features shows two parallel scene streams by position; vectorized outputs are drawn as small scene illustrations rather than named; the phase ruler separates inference from training-only parts; query tints match their consumers.
quality.weaknesses: Updated agent/map query arrows cross between rows with L-bends; the long motion and map vector arrows run across the whole planning area to reach the constraint panel; the constraints are text boxes only, with their meaning left to Figure 3.

figures.lesson: Draw the scene outputs as small vector illustrations on grey rounded tiles placed on the arrows between modules (cars with curved trajectory arrows, lane arrows crossing an intersection), so the vectorized representation is seen rather than named.

figures.title: VAD: Vectorized Scene Representation for Efficient Autonomous Driving

taxonomy.note: illustration of loss constraints, not a method/architecture figure

arrangement.losses_at: each panel illustrates one loss, named in its caption
arrangement.shared: none

insights.emphasis: Yellow measurement brackets and arrows with yellow labels (Longitudinal Safety, Lateral Safety, Boundary Safety, Lane Direction as Guidance) are the only annotation, so the constrained quantity pops off the dark road.
insights.flow: No pipeline; each panel is read independently, motion read bottom-to-top along the ghost trails.
insights.avoid: Not a method diagram; the ghosted car trails are faint and hard to read at print size.

core.what: three equal top-down road panels side by side, one per planning constraint (ego-agent collision, ego-boundary overstepping, ego-lane direction), each with the constrained quantity marked in yellow

relations.form: each constraint is drawn on a small instance of a two-lane road with rendered cars, the ego in cyan and other agents in red
each car's future is shown as fading ghost copies along its path

channels.frame: each road is its own panel with a bold caption below

figures.lesson: Illustrate each driving constraint as a top-down road panel where cars are ghosted repeats along their future path (red for others, cyan for ego) and the constrained distance is a yellow I-beam bracket with a yellow label.

figures.title: Neural Codec Language Models are Zero-Shot Text to Speech Synthesizers

taxonomy.task: zero-shot text-to-speech
taxonomy.note: training 'other' = a non-autoregressive stage that predicts the remaining codec quantizer levels in parallel

arrangement.units: left: an unframed column of two attention-mask grids with a swatch key; right: two full-width coloured decoder bands stacked (NAR above AR), each with its own input boxes beneath, titled in bold at the bottom
arrangement.inputs_as: the word 'Text' into a G2P box and a blue waveform glyph into an EnCodec box, then rows of italic code-token symbols
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; output token symbols sit above each band
arrangement.shared: G2P and EnCodec are drawn again under each decoder band

insights.structure: Two wide decoder bands are stacked on the right (NAR blue above AR green), each with G2P and EnCodec input boxes underneath, and a separate left column holds the matching attention-mask grids.
insights.data: Speech is a blue vertical-bar waveform glyph, text is the word 'Text', and every token is a typeset italic symbol (c_{0,1}, c~, <EOS>) on its own thin arrow instead of a drawn cell.
insights.emphasis: The two decoder bands are the only saturated fills and carry the largest type; the AR band's dash-dot loops from each output back to the next input make the autoregression the figure's most distinctive mark.
insights.flow: Inputs rise from the boxes into each band and outputs leave upward; in the AR band dash-dot curves loop every output down to the next input position, while the NAR band takes an NAR ID j on a dashed arrow at its right.
insights.avoid: The NAR stage sits above the AR stage although it runs second, so reading top-down gives the wrong order, and the mask grids have no connector to the bands they describe.

core.what: two full-width decoder bands stacked on the right, the NAR Transformer Decoder (blue) above the AR Transformer Decoder (green), each fed from below by a G2P text box, an EnCodec box over a waveform glyph, and its code tokens

relations.form: under the AR band, dash-dot loops carry each predicted first-codebook token c_{t,1} out of the top and back in as the next input, ending in <EOS>
text phonemes x, acoustic prompt codes c-tilde and previous codebook tokens enter each band side by side along its bottom edge; the NAR band also takes a dashed 'NAR ID j' input at its right end
at the left two 4x4 attention-mask grids with the same row/column token labels: NAR all white (attend to all tokens) above AR with grey upper-right cells (attends only left), and a two-swatch key

channels.colour: band colour = decoder stage (blue NAR, green AR), and the input boxes reuse paler hues (pale green G2P, pale blue EnCodec) that do not match their bands, so the tints carry no single meaning; grey vs white cells in the mask grids = disallowed vs allowed attention
channels.shape: wide bands are decoders, small rounded boxes are front-end encoders, a waveform glyph is the audio prompt, typeset c symbols are tokens
channels.line: solid arrows are token flow; dash-dot loops are autoregressive feedback; a dashed arrow is the NAR stage index
channels.frame: no frames; the masks and the decoders are separated by whitespace

quality.strengths: The attention masks are drawn as grids with token labels on both axes, so causal vs full attention is visible as grey cells; the AR feedback is drawn as unrolled loops per token; the two stages are the largest, most saturated elements.
quality.weaknesses: Tokens are typeset subscript symbols (c_{0,1:j-1}) rather than drawn as code grids, so which codebook each stage handles is hard to see; G2P/EnCodec tints reuse the band hues with swapped meaning; the AR band, which runs first, sits below the NAR band, so reading order is bottom to top without a cue.

figures.lesson: Beside a stack of decoder stages, draw each stage's attention mask as a small white/grey grid with the same token symbols on its axes, so causal vs full attention is shown rather than stated.

figures.title: Visual Autoregressive Modeling: Scalable Image Generation via Next-Scale Prediction

taxonomy.task: class-conditional image generation by next-scale prediction

arrangement.units: two unframed stage panels separated by a vertical dash-dot rule, each headed by a centred two-line title (Stage 1: tokenizer training, Stage 2: transformer training); in stage 2 each scale's tokens are enclosed by a dashed rounded box
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo (parrot) as the first slanted plane in stage 1; in stage 2 the token groups r_1, r_2 enter from the bottom
arrangement.losses_at: stage 2: a 'Cross-Entropy' box at the top right receiving arrows from the target r rows and the predicted r-hat rows; stage 1's loss is not drawn
arrangement.shared: the token maps r_k link the stages only by name (r_1, r_2 ... appear in both); no drawn connector across the rule

insights.structure: Two stages sit side by side behind a dash-dot rule, the tokenizer as a perspective chain of planes on the left and the autoregressive transformer as a bottom-to-top token stack on the right, with the causal mask tucked into the right panel's bottom corner.
insights.data: Token maps are drawn twice: as grid-patterned planes that grow r_1 to r_K in stage 1, and as dashed boxes of 1, 4, 9 numbered rounded token squares in stage 2, with the input and output photos as the end planes of stage 1.
insights.emphasis: The idea is shown by growth in group size (1 -> 4 -> 9 tokens) and the 1/4/9 blocks outlined in light blue on the mask, closed by the equation L = 1^2 + 2^2 + 3^2 = 14; only the [S] start token gets a colour (yellow).
insights.flow: Stage 1 reads left to right along a stepped arrow baseline with stage labels under it; stage 2 reads bottom to top, embedding bar -> transformer bar -> predicted rows, with each prediction fanning out from the transformer to the next row above and the loss arrows running right to the Cross-Entropy box.
insights.avoid: Stage 1's overlapping semi-transparent planes and tiny tilted labels (f, r_1, r_K) are hard to read, and nothing links the two stages except repeated symbol names.

core.what: two stages side by side split by a vertical dash-dot rule, each under its own centred title: Stage 1 a multi-scale VQVAE drawn as a perspective run of slanted planes, Stage 2 the causal VAR transformer over per-scale token groups

relations.form: Stage 1 runs left to right over a stepped baseline labelled VAE encoding / multi-scale quantization & embedding / decoding: parrot photo -> blurred feature map f -> a receding stack of token-grid planes r_1...r_K growing in size -> f-hat -> reconstructed parrot

Stage 2 reads bottom to top: token groups r_1, r_2 -> word embedding and up-interpolation -> e_1, e_2 rows -> VAR Transformer (causal) bar -> predicted r-hat groups, each scale's prediction conditioned on the coarser ones
predicted r-hat rows sit directly under the target r rows and both feed a Cross-Entropy box at the top right
a block-wise causal mask grid at the bottom right with nested blue blocks labelled 1, 4, 9 and L = 1^2+2^2+3^2 = 14
the r_k groups produced by Stage 1 reappear as the token groups Stage 2 consumes, drawn as dashed boxes of numbered cells

channels.colour: grey-blue cells = tokens (darker for the start token r_1 and its prediction), yellow [S] = the start token with condition; blue outlines in the mask grid = scale blocks; real-image colour only in the photos
channels.shape: slanted planes are image/feature maps in Stage 1, numbered rounded cells are tokens in Stage 2, wide grey bars are operations
channels.line: solid arrows for data flow; the vertical dash-dot rule separates the stages
channels.frame: dashed rounded boxes group the tokens of one scale

quality.strengths: Stage 1 draws the multi-scale token maps as planes that grow in size, so coarse-to-fine is visible geometry; the causal mask is drawn as a block grid matched to scale sizes; real image in and out; predictions are placed directly against targets before the cross-entropy.
quality.weaknesses: The two stages use different drawing languages (perspective planes vs flat token rows), so the r_k tie between them is by symbol only; Stage 2 arrows from e-rows into the transformer fan and cross; the mask grid carries a typeset sum formula.

figures.lesson: Draw the same unit of the idea (a scale's token map) in both stages - as a growing plane in the tokenizer and as a dashed group of numbered tokens in the transformer - and add the attention-mask grid with the group blocks outlined, so the reader sees which tokens may attend to which.

figures.title: VectorNet: Encoding HD Maps and Agent Dynamics from Vectorized Representation

taxonomy.task: behaviour/trajectory prediction from vectorized HD maps

arrangement.units: unframed left-to-right stages; per-polyline subgraphs in coloured rounded tiles paired with dashed polyline boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: schematic arrowed polylines labelled Crosswalk, Lane, Agent
arrangement.losses_at: right edge, as the two output tasks
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Four columns linked by thick grey block arrows: vectorized scene, a column of six dashed polyline boxes each feeding a small polyline subgraph, a fully connected global interaction graph, and two output rows (Map Completion above, Trajectory Prediction below).
insights.data: The input is a schematic of red crosswalk and blue lane and green agent polylines made of arrowed vectors; each polyline becomes a rounded tile holding a 3-node graph in its own colour, then a single coloured node in the global graph.
insights.emphasis: A consistent colour code (red crosswalk, blue lane, green agent) carries every element from raw vectors through subgraphs to global nodes, and the dashed-outline node in Map Completion marks the masked feature.
insights.flow: Strictly left to right with thick grey arrows between stages; the last arrow forks into two auxiliary/main outputs.
insights.avoid: The global graph is drawn as a dense mesh of all-pairs lines that takes the biggest space but says only 'fully connected'.

core.what: the scene drawn as vector polylines (crosswalk, lanes, agents), each polyline turned into a small subgraph tile and then a node of a fully connected global graph, left to right across four columns joined by thick grey block arrows

relations.form: vectorized scene -> column of dashed polyline boxes each feeding a polyline subgraph tile -> hexagonal fully connected global interaction graph -> outputs, left to right
the global graph forks into two outputs at the right: a smaller copy of the graph with one dashed node (map completion) above an agent feature box with a dashed green predicted trajectory below
each polyline is shown cut out in its own dashed box next to its three-node subgraph

channels.colour: colour = map-element identity kept through every stage: red crosswalk, blue lanes, green agents, from vector drawing to subgraph tile to global node to the predicted trajectory
channels.shape: arrows are vectors, circle-and-edge tiles are polyline subgraphs, rounded rectangles are polyline nodes in the global graph
channels.line: thick grey block arrows = stage transitions; thin black lines = graph edges; a dashed green arrow = the predicted future; a dashed node outline = the masked node to complete
channels.frame: dashed boxes isolate each input polyline; rounded tinted tiles hold each subgraph

quality.strengths: The method is drawn on a toy instance of its structure at every stage; one colour per element type carried end to end lets the reader follow any polyline without labels; the hierarchy local subgraph -> global graph is visible by position; the masked node and predicted trajectory are drawn as dashed versions of the same glyphs.
quality.weaknesses: The global graph's all-to-all edges are dense and the node features are empty boxes, so what a node holds is not shown; the 'Agent Feature' output is detached from the graph with no line showing it was read from a green node.

figures.lesson: Keep each map element's colour (red crosswalk, blue lane, green agent) from its vector drawing through its local subgraph tile to its node in the global graph, so every element can be followed across stages without labels.

figures.title: Align your Latents: High-Resolution Video Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models

taxonomy.task: text-to-video latent diffusion (temporal alignment concept)

arrangement.units: two unframed 3-D diffusion boxes (before / after), captioned below, joined by a big block arrow
arrangement.inputs_as: noisy image frames and labelled text boxes for noise
arrangement.shared: same box skeleton redrawn in both panels

insights.structure: Before/after diptych: two identical 3-D boxes of stacked frame slices (diffusion time vs batch/frame axis) with a large dark 'Temporal Video Fine-Tuning' arrow between them, each captioned below.
insights.data: Denoising trajectories are coloured noisy curves through the box ending in coloured dots, the marginal distribution is a purple density curve on the box side, and real generated frames fan out above (noisy) and below (clean samples).
insights.emphasis: The contrast is in the samples: unrelated images on the left versus a consistent panda sequence on the right, plus red connecting links between the final dots in the right box.
insights.flow: Left to right across the central arrow; within each box, top-to-bottom from noise to data, with peach arrows fanning from dots to sample thumbnails.
insights.avoid: Highly decorative 3-D boxes with many thin peach arrows; the crop cuts off the top label and the mechanism (which layers are added) is not shown.

core.what: a before/after diptych of two identical 3-D volumes (denoising time along one axis, batch/video frame axis along the other) joined by a large dark 'Temporal Video Fine-Tuning' arrow, unrelated samples fanning out of the left volume and one coherent panda clip out of the right

relations.form: inside each volume coloured noisy trajectories run across stacked frame slices from a noise distribution curve on the left face to a data distribution on the right; after fine-tuning the end points are joined by a red line
each volume has a denoising arrow along its top edge with a column of progressively less noisy frames above it (astronaut left, panda right)
thin orange lines tie each trajectory end point on the frame axis to its decoded sample frame in the fan below the volume

channels.colour: trajectory colours (blue, cyan, green) distinguish batch elements; a red link marks the aligned end points after fine-tuning; orange lines tie points to samples and annotations to their targets; the magma-coloured density curves are the noise and data distributions
channels.shape: 3-D box = the diffusion process over a batch, slices = frames, dots = samples at a step, photo thumbnails = decoded frames
channels.line: the large dark block arrow = the method step; thick black arrows = axes; thin orange lines = callouts
channels.frame: rectangular text boxes for the callout labels

quality.strengths: Identical volumes on both sides make the change visible as the samples' content (unrelated images vs one panda clip); real generated frames are drawn as the output; the frame axis is labelled on the volume itself.
quality.weaknesses: Each volume is densely layered (trajectories, distribution curves, slices, many orange callout lines), so the converging red link, the actual change, is small; orange carries both callout and point-to-sample ties; the top labels are cut at the crop edge and the denoising and frame axes are drawn in perspective that is hard to read at size.

figures.lesson: Show temporal alignment as a before/after pair of identical 3-D volumes whose depth axis is labelled as the frame axis, with sample frames fanning out of each: unrelated images before, one coherent clip after.

figures.title: Align your Latents: High-Resolution Video Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models

taxonomy.task: temporal layers inserted into an image LDM

arrangement.units: left: one trapezoid layer stack; right: vertical column of layer boxes (detail), unframed
arrangement.inputs_as: typeset latent tensor z and condition c_S
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Left: a trapezoid stack alternating grey spatial layers (theta) and green temporal layers (phi) between the input and output latent z; right: a vertical zoom of one spatial-temporal pair showing Conv3D and temporal attention layers each followed by an alpha-mixing box.
insights.data: Latents are typeset tensors (z in R^{B T C H W}), reshapes are printed as einops strings in monospace inside the green boxes, and the mixing is the equation alpha z + (1 - alpha) z'.
insights.emphasis: Green fill marks the new trainable temporal layers against grey frozen spatial layers, with large theta/phi glyphs labelling which parameters each layer owns.
insights.flow: Top to bottom in both halves; dashed lines carry the skip to the mixing equation; a small inset with icons explains the conditioning c_S.
insights.avoid: The left stack and right detail are not visually linked by a zoom cue, and the conditioning inset in the upper right is cramped.

core.what: one trapezoid stack on the left alternating pale grey spatial layers (theta) with saturated green temporal layers (phi) between an input and output latent, and on the right one spatial/temporal pair unrolled top to bottom

relations.form: the right column expands the stack: spatial layer -> Conv3D temporal layer -> alpha-mix spatial layer -> temporal attention layer -> alpha-mix spatial layer, each temporal box printing its tensor reshape such as (b t) c h w -> b c t h w in monospace
dashed side arrows carry each layer's input z_i past the temporal layer into a grey mix box that combines alpha z_i + (1-alpha) z'_i
a conditioning c_S enters at the top right through a Resize and green Conv2D 'Learned Downsampling' path into z_i, with a small key for the two conditioning cases

channels.colour: green = new temporal layers (phi), pale grey = frozen pretrained spatial layers (theta), with the Greek letters as a second cue; the small Conv2D in the downsampling path is also green, marking it as learned
channels.shape: wide bands are layers; the trapezoid outline shows the stack narrowing; a small trapezoid is the resize
channels.line: solid arrows are the main flow; dashed arrows are skip inputs to the mix and the conditioning bypass
channels.frame: no frames; the overview and the detail are placed side by side without a callout tie

quality.strengths: Frozen vs new parameters are carried by one channel (grey vs green) and doubled by theta/phi; interleaving is visible as alternating bands; reshapes are printed inside the layer that does them, showing where time becomes its own axis; the mix is drawn as its two input arrows.
quality.weaknesses: The detail column is not tied to the stack by tint or callout, so which band it opens is inferred; the alpha-mix formula is typeset into the mix boxes; the dashed bypass lines bend in long L-shapes along the left of the detail column.

figures.lesson: Interleave frozen per-frame layers and new temporal layers as alternating bands of one stack (pale grey vs saturated green) and print the tensor reshape such as (b t) c h w -> b c t h w in monospace inside each temporal layer, so the reader sees where time is folded into the batch and where it becomes its own axis.

figures.title: Video-LLaMA: An Instruction-tuned Audio-Visual Language Model for Video Understanding

taxonomy.task: audio-visual video understanding with an LLM

arrangement.units: two vertical dotted-border lanes, one per branch, titled at their top corners; the LLM is a single box spanning both above
arrangement.inputs_as: a framed strip of real video frames over an audio waveform
arrangement.shared: the LLM drawn once above both lanes; the input strip drawn once below

insights.structure: Two dotted-border lanes stand side by side (Vision-Language Branch left, Audio-Language Branch right), each a bottom-up tower of frozen encoder -> feature columns + positional embeddings -> Q-Former -> query tokens -> Linear, and both feed one LLM bar spanning the top.
insights.data: The input is a framed strip of real rocket video frames above an audio waveform at the bottom centre; tokens are coloured squares (pastel for video, saturated for audio), and the output is a quoted caption in a green dashed box above the LLM.
insights.emphasis: Snowflake (frozen) and flame (trainable) icons mark the training state, with trainable modules in orange and frozen ones in blue.
insights.flow: Bottom-up: the shared input strip sends one line to each branch's encoder, and the two Linear outputs rise into the LLM with quoted prompt text ('# Human:', 'Describe this video:') beside the joining lines.
insights.avoid: The input strip is shared and sits below both lanes, so its feed lines cross outside the lane frames.

core.what: two equal dotted-border lanes side by side, the Vision-Language Branch on the left and the Audio-Language Branch on the right, each a bottom-up tower that feeds one LLM bar spanning both at the top

relations.form: each lane reads bottom to top: frozen encoder trapezoid -> row of per-frame feature columns -> timestep boxes t_i joined by circled plus -> Q-Former -> query tokens -> Linear
both Linear outputs rise into the single LLM bar, interleaved with dashed green text prompts ('# Human:', 'Describe this video:')

the video is drawn as a row of feature columns of stacked coloured squares (one column per frame) and the audio as a row of tall blue columns, each tagged with its own timestep box t^v_i / t^a_i into a circled plus
one framed input strip at the bottom holds both the video frames of a rocket launch and the audio waveform, with one line to each encoder

channels.colour: blue = frozen modules (encoders, LLM), orange = trainable (Q-Formers, Linear), doubled by snowflake and flame icons; dashed green = text prompts and output; the coloured query squares only distinguish tokens
channels.shape: trapezoids are encoders, rounded rectangles are modules, small squares are tokens, circled plus is positional addition
channels.line: solid arrows for all flow; dashed green borders mark text
channels.frame: dotted rectangles enclose each branch; a solid rectangle groups the per-frame features and another the input strip

quality.strengths: Equal-width lanes make the two modality branches parallel by position; trainable vs frozen is one colour pair reinforced by icons; frame-wise positional encoding is drawn as timestep boxes into each column; real frames, waveform, prompts and generated text are drawn as data.
quality.weaknesses: The query-token colours (red/yellow/green/purple) look like a code but carry no meaning; the input strip's lines to each encoder bend round the lane borders; the Q-Formers, the trainable core, are the same size as the frozen encoders.

figures.lesson: Draw a video as a row of per-frame feature columns (stacked coloured squares, one column per frame), each tagged with a small timestep box t_i and a circled plus into the aggregator, so frame-wise position encoding is drawn instead of stated.

figures.title: Video Swin Transformer

taxonomy.task: video recognition backbone

arrangement.units: four dashed rounded containers in a row, one per stage, each holding a narrow embedding/merging bar and a large transformer-block box, with the stage name on the top border and ×N on the bottom border
arrangement.inputs_as: a plain box labelled 'Videos' with the input shape T×H×W×3 written above it
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: One row of four dashed rounded stage containers after a Videos box and a tall patch-partition bar, each container holding a narrow down-sampling bar and a large transformer-block box.
insights.data: No data is drawn: the input is a 'Videos' text box and every intermediate is a typeset tensor shape (T/2×H/8×W/8×2C …) above the stage boundaries.
insights.emphasis: Only size separates the method's block from the plumbing: the Video Swin Transformer Block box is the largest shape in every stage, all in plain black outline.
insights.flow: Strictly left to right on one horizontal centreline, with straight arrows crossing the dashed container borders between stages.
insights.avoid: Monochrome boxes-only rendering hides what is new (the 3D shifted window), and the inter-stage arrows run straight through the dashed borders so the frames and arrows tangle at each crossing.

core.what: one left-to-right row of four dashed rounded stage containers, each a narrow Linear Embedding or Patch Merging bar followed by a large Video Swin Transformer Block box with its repeat count under it

relations.form: Videos box -> tall 3D Patch Partition bar -> Stage 1 -> Stage 2 -> Stage 3 -> Stage 4, single arrows on one horizontal line
block repetition written as x2, x2, x6, x2 under each stage container rather than drawn

channels.colour: none: black outline on white throughout
channels.shape: tall narrow bars = token reshaping (partition, embedding, merging), large rounded boxes = transformer blocks, a plain rectangle = the input
channels.line: solid black arrows for data flow
channels.frame: dashed rounded frames = one stage; tensor shapes are written above each stage boundary

quality.strengths: Arrows run on one straight line through every stage; the repeated stage unit is drawn identically four times; tensor shapes above the boundaries show the resolution pyramid; the transformer block is the largest box in each stage.
quality.weaknesses: No data is drawn (the video is a box labelled Videos, tokens are not shown), so the 3D shifted-window idea, the contribution, is invisible here; the four stages are identical boxes and only text says they differ; no colour or emphasis marks what is new versus Swin.

figures.lesson: Write the tensor shape (T/2 × H/4 × W/4 × C …) above each stage boundary and the repeat count (×N) under each dashed stage frame, so a hierarchical backbone's scale schedule is read along one line.

figures.title: VideoAgent: Long-form Video Understanding with Large Language Model as Agent

taxonomy.task: long-form video question answering by an LLM agent that captions sampled frames, self-reflects on its confidence and retrieves more frames with CLIP until confident

arrangement.units: a frame strip across the top; three rounded panels in a row below (captioner, LLM agent, retriever), each enclosed by an olive outline
arrangement.inputs_as: a fanned strip of real video frames, most faded grey, the sampled ones in full colour with olive borders and the retrieved one with a red border; a quoted multiple-choice question in a blue box
arrangement.shared: the frame strip is drawn once and read by both rounds; the LLM panel lists round-1 and round-2 results side by side in each step

insights.structure: The data (frame strip) spans the top and the three actors sit in one row below, so the loop runs down, across and back up over the strip.
insights.data: Frames are real video stills, captions are quoted with timestamps, the retrieval query is quoted, and round results are written in the LLM's step boxes.
insights.emphasis: Colour carries the round: olive for round 1 and red for everything round 2 adds, including the newly retrieved frame.
insights.flow: Curved lines drop from selected frames into the caption panel; short arrows go captions to LLM; a 'Confident?' branch goes Yes up to the answer and No right to Retrieve Frames, from which a red line climbs and runs back along the top to the new frame.
insights.avoid: The return line is a long wire around the whole figure, and the question box floats above the LLM panel with no line to it.

core.what: two columns rising from footer bars, a narrow Multimodal Prompt column on the left and a wide Interaction column on the right, which meet only through yellow elbow lines from the Prompt Tokens panel into each Cross-Attention bar of the right-hand stack

two columns on their own green and blue footer bars, prompt left and interaction right

channels.frame: rounded tinted panels hold the token sequences; a green rounded frame holds the prompt pieces

quality.strengths: Prompt conditioning is visible as one colour of line entering every cross-attention layer from the side; real prompt pieces and real scene renders with object crops are drawn as data; tokens are coloured by type with a key; the repeated per-step unit is drawn three times identically.
quality.weaknesses: Colour carries token type, layer type and module role at once (yellow for prompt panels and the History Tokens panel too); the yellow elbow lines run long up the gap between columns; the alternating cross/self-attention stack takes the most area though it is a standard decoder.

figures.title: Learning a Variational Network for Reconstruction of Accelerated MRI Data

insights.structure: Two stacked sub-figures: (a) a pipeline where sensitivity maps and k-space data feed an A* block to give a zero-filled image, and all three enter a tall green 'Variational Network (VN)' block that outputs the reconstruction; (b) a chain GD^1...GD^t...GD^T with GD^t zoomed via trapezoid lines into a pale-green box showing the gradient step.
