sensitivity maps and k-space each send one line into A* from above and below, and both also run straight on into the VN block, so three lines converge on VN
panel (b) unrolls the steps as three identical dark-green GD boxes on one horizontal line with ellipses between them, u^0 entering and u^T leaving
inside the zoom box the learned filters are drawn as small grey RE/IM kernel patches and the activation functions as blue curve plots, between the filter and its transposed filter
GD^t is linked by two diverging lines to an enclosed box beneath that shows the data-consistency term on the top line and the filter-activation-filter branches below, joined at two summation circles

channels.colour: dark green fill with white text = a learned or operator block (A*, VN, GD); pale green fill = the opened interior of one GD step; blue = the activation-function curves
channels.shape: square/rectangular boxes = operators, image stacks = data, circles with Sigma = sums
channels.line: solid black arrows only, carrying data; no line-style distinction between training and inference
channels.frame: the pale-green box frames one unrolled gradient step

quality.strengths: Inputs and intermediates are drawn as real data (coil sensitivity maps, k-space stack, zero-filled and reconstructed knee images) with their dimension labels; the unrolled GD chain plus the trapezoid zoom on GD^t shows both the iteration and its interior in one column; the filter/activation branches are drawn as actual kernel patches and curves rather than named boxes.
quality.weaknesses: Dark green is used both for the fixed operator A* and the learned VN/GD blocks, so colour does not separate learned from fixed; the data-consistency term lambda^t A*(Au^t - f) is typeset as a formula on the wire; in (a) the VN block is a plain box whose link to (b) is left to the captions rather than drawn.

figures.lesson: Coil data are drawn as decks of offset stacked slices with their array dimensions (n_FE, n_PE, n_CH) printed along the edges, so the multi-coil axis needs no legend.

figures.title: Voicebox: Text-Guided Multilingual Universal Speech Generation at Scale

taxonomy.task: text-guided speech infilling and TTS
taxonomy.note: figure shows task formats, not the network; Voicebox is a flow-matching infilling model trained on masked speech (architecture/training not drawn)

arrangement.units: cells of a task-by-stage grid separated by dashed rules, no boxes
arrangement.inputs_as: spectrograms with quoted transcripts
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: A 3 x 3 grid: columns are tasks (Denoising, Zero-shot TTS, Text-Only Sampling) with underlined bold headers, rows are Raw data / Model Input / Model Output separated by grey dashed horizontal rules.
insights.data: Audio is drawn as purple-orange spectrogram strips, masked spans as solid yellow-orange blocks, and transcripts as quoted capital text, with content text in red and style/reference text in blue.
insights.emphasis: Coloured outlines label roles: a grey 'noise' box on the noisy segment, blue 'Ref' boxes around the reference audio, and a red 'Target' box around the generated segment, matching the red/blue text colours.
insights.flow: Top to bottom within each column (raw -> input -> output), with no arrows; columns are read independently left to right.
insights.avoid: There are no arrows or model block at all, so the figure explains the input/output format but not how the model works; it should not be reused as a method overview.

core.what: three tasks (Denoising, Zero-shot TTS, Text-Only Sampling) are drawn as three side-by-side columns of a grid with the same three rows Raw data / Model Input / Model Output, so the same in-filling format is compared across tasks

relations.form: three task columns with bold underlined headers, each cell row-aligned with the same stage in the neighbouring columns, separated by grey dashed horizontal rules
top-to-bottom within each column from raw data to model input (masked span drawn as a solid yellow block) to model output spectrogram, with no arrows
the masking is drawn on the spectrogram strip itself: a yellow block replaces the noisy span in Denoising, precedes the Ref spectrogram in TTS, and fills the whole strip in Text-Only Sampling

channels.colour: red = content text and the generated Target segment, blue = style/reference text and the Ref segment, grey = the noise segment; yellow-orange solid = masked span to infill; the purple-orange colormap is the spectrogram itself
channels.shape: spectrogram strips = audio, quoted capital text = transcripts, no operation shapes
channels.line: dashed grey rules separate stages; outline boxes mark the role of an audio span
channels.frame: coloured outline rectangles (noise, Ref, Target) mark one audio span's role

quality.strengths: The task-by-stage grid makes every task's input and output directly comparable by row; data is drawn as real spectrograms and quoted transcripts; red/blue is used consistently for content/target versus style/reference in both text and box outlines.
quality.weaknesses: No model block or arrow appears anywhere, so the figure shows input/output formats but not the method; Text-Only Sampling uses a different output layout (three stacked samples) than the other columns; grey labels the noise box and also the 'Sample #' labels, giving grey two uses.

figures.lesson: Explain an in-context generative model with a tasks x (raw data, model input, model output) grid of spectrograms, showing masking as a flat solid block and colouring each text snippet like the box around the audio it controls.

figures.title: VoxPoser: Composable 3D Value Maps for Robotic Manipulation with Language Models

taxonomy.task: zero-shot language-conditioned manipulation: an LLM writes code that queries a VLM to compose 3-D affordance and constraint value maps for a motion planner
taxonomy.note: architecture other: frozen LLM generating code that calls a frozen VLM to build voxel value maps, followed by a classical motion planner; no trained network

arrangement.units: (a) composition: two stacked model boxes, one code box, two dotted-framed map pairs; (b) motion planning: one scene render; the stages are separated by whitespace and named by bold under-captions
arrangement.inputs_as: a point-cloud render of the real scene with two camera glyphs, and the quoted spoken instruction beside a user icon in a grey rounded box
arrangement.losses_at: none (training-free); the composed maps feed the planner through a bracket
arrangement.shared: the code box is drawn once and both map frames come out of it; VLM and LLM are drawn once each

insights.structure: A left-to-right pipeline whose middle is one large code box flanked by two stacked model boxes on its left and two stacked dotted map frames on its right.
insights.data: Inputs and outputs are drawn as the real thing: a point-cloud render with camera glyphs, a quoted instruction, the generated Python, heatmaps on real views and a dotted trajectory in the final render.
insights.emphasis: Emphasis comes from size and position only: the code box is the biggest element at the centre; the models are pastel and carry lock icons to read as frozen tools.
insights.flow: Straight grey arrows run left to right from each model into the code, from the code to each map frame, and from a bracket around both frames into the final render.
insights.avoid: Avoid a double circular arrow for 'calls'; draw the call as a labelled arrow from the code to the model and back.

core.what: the value maps the generated code builds are drawn as heatmaps over two camera views of the real scene, and the plan they produce as an orange dotted path inside the scene's point cloud

relations.form: affordance (blue spot) and constraint (red-orange region) heatmaps overlaid on two real camera views each, and the final trajectory drawn as a dotted curve in the 3-D render
one left-to-right axis: inputs, models, code, maps, planner render, with short grey arrows between columns
the scene row (VLM) and the instruction row (LLM) both point into the single code box, the VLM by a two-way circular arrow
the two dotted map frames are joined by a right-hand bracket whose single arrow enters the motion-planning render

channels.colour: two meanings: tints name the model (salmon = VLM, light blue = LLM, also in their bold initials), while in the maps blue and red-orange are heatmap values; orange dots = planned trajectory
channels.shape: tinted rounded boxes = models, white outlined box = code, dotted frames = map groups, renders and camera views = data
channels.line: short solid grey arrows for data flow; one two-way circular arrow for the VLM-code exchange; a bracket for merging the maps
channels.frame: dotted black frame = one kind of value map (two views)

quality.strengths: Every intermediate is drawn as the real artefact: the actual Python of both map functions, heatmaps on the real camera views, the planned path in the scene. The code box, the method's interface, is the largest central element. Arrows are short, straight and all run one way.
quality.weaknesses: The VLM-code relation is a vague two-way circular arrow, so the reader cannot see that the code calls the VLM. The salmon and blue model tints come back as heatmap colours with another meaning. The input point cloud takes a large area and its camera glyphs are hard to read.

figures.lesson: Show what an LLM-written program produces by placing its output as heatmaps on the real camera views right beside the code, then bracket those maps into the final trajectory drawn in the same scene.

figures.title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models

taxonomy.task: lifelong embodied agent in Minecraft

arrangement.units: three vertical columns each topped by a coloured header pill; only the skill library is enclosed in a yellow panel
arrangement.inputs_as: curriculum of task screenshots
arrangement.shared: the Minecraft environment and self-verification sit centrally under the prompting column and connect to all three

insights.structure: Three titled columns with coloured header pills: Automatic Curriculum (purple, a cycle of circular game screenshots), Iterative Prompting Mechanism (blue, a code panel above a Minecraft screenshot and a magnifier 'Self-Verification' icon), and Skill Library (yellow, a list of item icons with skill names).
insights.data: Tasks are circular Minecraft screenshots, the program is a real JavaScript snippet in a grey code panel with item icons pinned to called functions, and skills are pixel-art item icons beside names.
insights.emphasis: Arrow and text colours match the module they belong to: purple 'New Task' and 'Update Exploration Progress', blue 'Skill Retrieval', red 'Refine Program' with an X, green 'Add New Skill' with a check.
insights.flow: Curriculum feeds a new task rightward into the code panel, the library feeds skills leftward into it, code goes down to the environment and feedback up, and self-verification branches up (refine) or right to the library (add).
insights.avoid: The long thin coloured arrows along the bottom are faint and cross under icons, and skill names in the library change colour (blue/green/black) with no legend.

core.what: the yellow Skill Library panel sits to the right of the central code panel, feeding retrieved skills leftward into the program and receiving verified new skills by an arrow from self-verification

relations.form: the automatic curriculum is a circular cycle of round Minecraft task screenshots (Mine Wood Log -> Make Crafting Table -> Combat Zombie -> Mine Diamond) joined by curved arrows, one dashed

the iterative prompting loop is a vertical pair of arrows between the code panel and the Minecraft environment screenshot (Code as Actions down, Env Feedback / Execution Errors up) plus a red Refine Program arrow up from Self-Verification
Skill Retrieval is a blue arrow from the library panel into the code panel, and the retrieved skills are drawn as item icons pinned by dotted lines to the code lines that call them
three titled columns left to right (Automatic Curriculum, Iterative Prompting Mechanism, Skill Library) with a purple New Task arrow from the curriculum into the code panel
the program is a real JavaScript snippet in a grey code panel, tasks are game screenshots, and skills are pixel-art item icons with names

channels.colour: header pill colour = module (purple curriculum, blue prompting, yellow library), and arrow/text colour matches the module that owns it (purple New Task and Update Exploration Progress, blue Skill Retrieval); red/green additionally mean fail/pass (Refine Program with an X, Add New Skill with a check), and green also marks the newly added skill in the library list
channels.shape: circles = tasks, grey code panel = program, magnifier icon = self-verification, item icons = skills
channels.line: solid arrows for control/data, one dashed curriculum arrow for a not-yet-reached task, dotted lines tie code lines to skill icons
channels.frame: only the skill library is enclosed in a yellow panel

quality.strengths: Every noun is real data (screenshots, an actual combatZombie program, item icons); the library-to-code retrieval and the verification-to-library addition are both drawn as short arrows with matching colours; the three columns match the three named components.
quality.weaknesses: Colour carries two meanings (module identity and pass/fail), and green is reused for the added skill text; the Update Exploration Progress and Add New Skill arrows run long L-shaped paths along the bottom, the latter across the whole right half to reach the library.

figures.lesson: Give each agent component its own pastel heading bar and draw its arrows in a darker shade of that hue, then show the real artefacts in place (task screenshots on an arc, the generated code listing, an icon-per-row skill list) with a check or cross deciding which arrow fires.

figures.title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models

taxonomy.task: skill library storage and retrieval

arrangement.units: two horizontal rows divided by a dashed rule, each a chain of unenclosed panels and pills ending in a yellow list panel
arrangement.inputs_as: generated program code (top) and a task question (bottom)
arrangement.shared: GPT-3.5 and Embedding pills repeated in both rows at the same x positions

insights.structure: Two rows separated by a dashed rule: top row 'add' (program -> GPT-3.5 -> description -> Embedding -> Key, program -> Value, both into the yellow Skill Library), bottom row 'retrieve' (task question -> GPT-3.5 -> plan text with environment feedback -> Embedding -> Query -> Skill Library -> Top-5 Relevant Skills).
insights.data: Programs and descriptions are real code panels (description shown as an italic comment), the task is a pink quoted question, model calls are small dark green (GPT-3.5) and black (Embedding) pills, skills are icon lists.
insights.emphasis: The newly added skill 'Combat Zombie' is green in the library to match the green 'Add' arrow, and retrieved skills are blue to match the blue 'Retrieve' arrow.
insights.flow: Both rows run left to right with the same column positions, so the two operations align vertically (GPT-3.5 over GPT-3.5, Embedding over Embedding).
insights.avoid: The Value arrow is a long thin line running the full width under the description panel, and the skill library is drawn twice (as a panel and as a small yellow box) which may read as two different stores.

core.what: adding a skill (top row) and retrieving skills (bottom row) are two horizontal rows split by a dashed rule, with the GPT-3.5 and Embedding pills at the same x in both rows so the shared pipeline lines up vertically

relations.form: top row left to right: program code panel -> GPT-3.5 pill -> program description panel -> Embedding pill -> Key, with the program also running on a long arrow to Value
bottom row left to right: pink task question -> GPT-3.5 -> lilac plan text with Environment Feedback -> Embedding -> Query -> Skill Library -> Top-5 Relevant Skills

the skill library is a yellow icon list at the right end of both rows: Key and Value converge on it via a green Add bracket on top, and on the bottom a small yellow Skill Library pill returns a blue list of five retrieved skills
the same GPT-3.5 (dark green) and Embedding (black) pills are repeated in both rows at matching positions

channels.colour: pill fill = model (dark green GPT-3.5, black Embedding); yellow = skill library; green = the add operation and the newly added skill, blue = the retrieve operation and the retrieved skills; pink and lilac panels distinguish the task question from the generated plan
channels.shape: pills = model calls, grey code panels = programs and descriptions, icon lists = skill stores
channels.line: solid arrows carry data; green and blue arrows mark add versus retrieve
channels.frame: the dashed horizontal rule separates the two operations

quality.strengths: The two operations share column positions so the reused GPT-3.5 and Embedding stages align vertically; data is drawn as real code, a real description comment and real skill icons; the green/blue arrow colour is echoed in the library entries it adds or retrieves.
quality.weaknesses: The Value arrow is a long thin line running under the description panel across half the width; the Skill Library is drawn twice (a full yellow list on top, a small yellow pill on the bottom) so the store's identity across rows is left to the label.

figures.lesson: Draw writing to and reading from an agent memory as two stacked rows that share the same stages and the same store panel, colouring the write path green and the read path blue down to the text of the added and retrieved entries.

figures.title: Vector Quantized Diffusion Model for Text-to-Image Synthesis

taxonomy.task: text-to-image generation

arrangement.units: two rounded grey-bordered panels stacked vertically, each titled with its step; the decoder is a nested blue panel with inner rounded block pairs
arrangement.inputs_as: a photo (step 1) and a quoted caption (step 2)
arrangement.shared: the codebook token indices link the two steps

insights.structure: Two stacked rounded panels titled 'Step1: VQ-VAE' (photo -> trapezoid Encoder -> Q(.) with a lilac Codebook z1..zK above -> green token grid -> Decoder -> photo) and 'Step2: VQ-Diffusion' (a chain of green token-state circles x_T ... x_t, x_{t-1} ... x_0 above a blue 'Diffusion Image Decoder' box of AdaLN + Transformer Block pairs).
insights.data: Discrete latents are green number grids and number strips with 'M' for masked tokens, shown above each diffusion state; the text prompt is a quoted sentence going through BPE and a peach trapezoid Text Encoder.
insights.emphasis: The token strips over x_T to x_0 show masks being replaced by indices step by step, and the forward q and reverse p_theta transitions are labelled with their equations on dashed and solid arcs.
insights.flow: Step 1 runs left to right; in Step 2 the state chain runs left to right on top, while the decoder below takes x_t, t and the text embedding and loops its output back up to x_{t-1}.
insights.avoid: Many thin grey feedback lines inside the decoder box (t and text embeddings to every block) crowd the lower panel.

core.what: two stacked rounded panels, Step1: VQ-VAE above Step2: VQ-Diffusion, where the green token grids of step 1 become the token-state strips over each diffusion state of step 2

relations.form: two full-width rounded panels stacked vertically, each titled with its step
step 1 runs left to right: giraffe photo -> trapezoid Encoder -> Q(.) -> green token grid -> trapezoid Decoder -> photo
a lilac Codebook panel of vectors z1..zK sits above Q(.) and drops one line into it
step 2 draws the diffusion chain as green state circles x_T ... x_t, x_{t-1} ... x_0 on one line, each with a token strip above showing masked 'M' tokens replaced by indices

the blue Diffusion Image Decoder box below the chain takes x_t from above, the timestep t on a line entering from the left, and the text embedding from a peach trapezoid Text Encoder fed by a quoted caption through BPE, and returns its output up to x_{t-1}
the decoder box encloses repeated AdaLN + Transformer Block pairs with a blue ellipsis between them

channels.colour: green = discrete tokens and diffusion states, lilac = codebook, grey-blue = VQ-VAE encoder/decoder and decoder blocks, peach = text encoder, blue box = the diffusion decoder
channels.shape: trapezoids = encoders/decoders, circles = diffusion states, number grids/strips = token maps, rounded rectangles = blocks
channels.line: dashed arc = forward noising q, solid arc = learned reverse p_theta, solid grey lines = data
channels.frame: rounded grey panels = training step; the nested blue panel = one network

quality.strengths: The discrete latent is drawn as actual token grids and strips, and the strips over x_T..x_0 show masks being filled step by step; the forward/reverse transitions are separated by line style; text conditioning enters the decoder from its own side.
quality.weaknesses: Equations q(x_t|x_{t-1}) and p_theta(x_{t-1}|x_t,y) are typeset on the arcs; the decoder output line loops right and back up to x_{t-1}, and the thin grey feed lines into each AdaLN and Transformer Block bend and cross inside the decoder box; the link between step 1's token grid and step 2's strips is only implied by matching green.

figures.lesson: One green token motif carries the discrete latent through the whole figure - a 2-D index grid after quantization, then 1-D index strips with grey 'M' mask cells above each Markov-chain state - so the reader sees corruption go from all-masked x_T to fully filled x_0 without reading a formula.

figures.title: Taming Transformers for High-Resolution Image Synthesis

taxonomy.task: high-resolution image synthesis

arrangement.units: one large rounded VQGAN panel at the bottom plus two rounded side panels (Codebook, Transformer) above it
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo with patch callouts
arrangement.shared: the codebook is shared between VQGAN quantization and the transformer

insights.structure: A large rounded 'VQGAN' panel spans the bottom (photo -> CNN Encoder E -> 3-D latent grid z-hat -> quantization -> coloured index cube z_q -> CNN Decoder G -> photo), a dashed CNN Discriminator D rises from it to a real/fake grid, and above sit a Codebook Z table and a Transformer panel.
insights.data: Latents are 3-D cubes, the quantised one with coloured cells carrying codebook indices; the codebook is a table of coloured rows linked by yellow/blue lines to image patches on the large photo; the transformer shows a coloured index sequence with a '?' next token and a bar-chart distribution.
insights.emphasis: Index colours are shared across the codebook, z_q cells and the transformer sequence, so one colour = one code throughout; the generator and discriminator use dashed trapezoid outlines in one teal.
insights.flow: Bottom row left to right, with a dashed double arrow from the argmin quantization up to the codebook and a two-way arrow pair between codebook and transformer; the discriminator flows upward to its patch output.
insights.avoid: The big top-left dog photo with patch call-outs duplicates the small input photo and pushes the encoder input into a cramped corner.

core.what: the VQGAN autoencoder runs left to right inside a large enclosed panel along the bottom: dog crop -> CNN Encoder E -> z-hat grid -> quantization -> coloured index grid z_q -> CNN Decoder G -> reconstructed dog

relations.form: one horizontal axis through the VQGAN panel, encoder and decoder as facing trapezoids with the latent cubes between them

the Codebook Z is a table of coloured entries above the panel, tied to the quantization step by a dashed double-headed arrow, and its entries are linked by yellow and blue lines to dashed patches on the dog image

the quantized latent z_q is a 4x4 grid of codebook indices whose cell fills match the codebook entry colours, and the transformer sequence s_<i is the same coloured index cells laid out in a row with a '?' for s_i
the transformer panel at top predicts the next index: coloured index strip s_<i plus a dashed '?' cell, with a bar-chart distribution above it
a dashed-outline CNN Discriminator D sits on top of the reconstruction and outputs a 4x4 real/fake patch grid
the input crop at bottom-left is tied by two lines to a dashed square on a larger dog photo top-left, on which the codebook links land

channels.colour: index colours (yellow, orange, purple, blue, green...) = codebook entry identity, consistent across codebook, z_q grid and transformer sequence; teal = CNN networks; pale grey = enclosing panels
channels.shape: trapezoids = CNNs, 3-D cubes = latent tensors, tables/grids = codebook and index maps
channels.line: solid grey arrows = data flow; dashed double arrow = codebook lookup; dashed outlines mark the discriminator and the predicted token, i.e. dashed means two different things (auxiliary/training-only module and unknown token)
channels.frame: rounded panels = a model (VQGAN, Transformer) or the codebook

quality.strengths: Codebook identity is carried by one colour channel all the way from the codebook table into z_q and the transformer sequence, so the reader sees that the transformer models the same indices; the latents are drawn as tensors and index grids rather than boxes; real images at both ends.
quality.weaknesses: The argmin quantization formula and the product formula p(s) are typeset in the figure; dashed line style carries several meanings (lookup arrow, discriminator outline, unknown token, image patches); the two-way arrows between codebook and transformer are unexplained short stubs.

figures.lesson: Every discrete code keeps one colour and one integer wherever it appears (image-patch zoom box, codebook row, quantized-cube cell, transformer token), so the hand-off from the autoencoder stage to the sequence-model stage reads without a legend.

figures.title: VS-Net: Variable splitting network for accelerated parallel MRI reconstruction

taxonomy.task: accelerated parallel MRI reconstruction

arrangement.units: Identical dashed-outline stage frames in a row, each titled 'Stage k' above; the last is separated by a bold dotted ellipsis.
arrangement.inputs_as: real grayscale MR images: the zero-filled input above, then stacks of undersampled k-space images, coil sensitivity maps and line masks down the left edge
arrangement.shared: auxiliary inputs are drawn once at the left and fan into every stage through long horizontal bus lines, one line style per input (solid, dotted, dashed)

insights.structure: A row of identical dashed stage frames, each with DB and DCB stacked on its left feeding WAB on its right, sits above a band of long bus lines that carry the shared inputs.
insights.data: Input and output are real grayscale knee MR images at the top corners, and the auxiliary inputs (undersampled k-space, coil sensitivities, mask) are offset stacks of small images labelled above, stacked down the left edge.
insights.emphasis: Block types are coded only by grey level (white DB, dark grey DCB with white text, light grey WAB), repeated identically in every stage, so the unrolled structure itself is the message.
insights.flow: The main path runs left to right across the top through the stages, while each auxiliary input runs right along its own line style (solid k-space, dotted sensitivities, dashed mask) and turns up with an arrowhead into the DCB and WAB of every stage.
insights.avoid: Three auxiliary line styles are told apart only by dash pattern with no legend, and they cross each other where they turn up into the stages, making the bus band dense and hard to trace.

core.what: the unrolled network is a row of identical dashed-framed stages (Stage 1, Stage 2, ... Stage n_it), each holding the same DB, DCB and WAB boxes, from the input image on the left to the output image on the right

relations.form: three identical dashed stage frames on one horizontal axis with a dotted ellipsis before the last, each frame's WAB feeding the next frame's DB and DCB
inside each stage the input splits into a white DB and a dark-grey DCB box, whose outputs converge on a light-grey WAB box

undersampled k-space, coil sensitivities and the sampling mask are drawn as image stacks down the left edge, each sending one horizontal bus under all stages with vertical branches up into every DCB (and sensitivities also into every WAB)

channels.colour: greyscale fill = block type (white DB, dark grey DCB, light grey WAB)
channels.shape: rectangles = blocks; image stacks = MRI data (input image, k-space, sensitivities, mask)
channels.line: line style = which side input a bus carries: solid = undersampled k-space, dotted = sensitivities, dashed = mask; thin solid arrows also carry the image between blocks
channels.frame: a dashed frame = one unrolled stage

quality.strengths: Repeated stages are identical frames with identical block fills, so the unrolled iteration reads at a glance; the side inputs are drawn as real k-space, sensitivity and mask images with one bus each rather than separate wires per stage; input and output are real knee images.
quality.weaknesses: Line style carries both the identity of each side input and (solid) the main image flow, so the solid k-space bus is not distinguished from data arrows; the three buses produce many long vertical branches crossing under the stages; the internal content of DB, DCB and WAB is not shown.

figures.lesson: Draw an unrolled network as identical dashed stage frames with fixed grey levels per block type, and route each auxiliary input (k-space, sensitivities, mask) as its own line style along a bus under the stages so it can reach every stage without crossing the main flow.

figures.title: A Simple and Effective Pruning Approach for Large Language Models

taxonomy.task: LLM weight pruning
taxonomy.note: no network drawn; worked numeric example of a pruning metric on a weight matrix

arrangement.units: two unboxed panels separated by a vertical rule, each a row of three captioned matrices
arrangement.inputs_as: weight matrix with numeric entries (plus activation-norm row for Wanda)
arrangement.shared: same weight matrix values in both panels

insights.structure: Two side-by-side panels split by a grey vertical rule: 'Magnitude Pruning' (Weights -> Weight Importance -> Pruned Weights) and 'Wanda' (Weights plus an activation-norm row -> Weight Importance -> Pruned Weights), each a three-step left-to-right chain of 3 x 4 matrices.
insights.data: Matrices are grids of real small integers with cells coloured yellow (kept) or light blue (pruned/zero); activation norms ||X||_2 are a row of orange-shaded cells whose depth scales with value; the scoring formula S sits above each importance matrix.
insights.emphasis: Dashed boxes show the comparison group: one box around the whole matrix ('grouped per layer') for magnitude pruning versus one dashed box per row ('grouped per output') for Wanda, and the darkest orange activation (8) visibly flips which weights survive.
insights.flow: Left to right with small grey arrows inside each panel; the two panels are read in parallel as baseline versus proposed.

core.what: magnitude pruning (left) and Wanda (right) are two panels split by a vertical grey rule, each running Weights -> Weight Importance -> Pruned Weights on the same toy 3x4 weight matrix

relations.form: two side-by-side panels titled Magnitude Pruning and Wanda, ours on the right, with the same matrix values and the same three-step layout
within each panel, three matrices left to right joined by short grey arrows: weights, importance scores, pruned weights
in the Wanda panel the weight matrix W and an orange activation-norm vector ||X||_2 below it both feed the importance matrix S = |W| . ||X||_2
the method is shown on a small concrete matrix: every cell has a numeric value, and the cells to be pruned are tinted blue in the importance and pruned matrices
dashed boxes around the importance matrix show the comparison group: one box around the whole matrix ('grouped per layer') versus one dashed box per row ('grouped per output')

channels.colour: yellow = weights kept, blue = weights removed (pruned or to be pruned), orange shades = activation-norm magnitude
channels.shape: grid matrices = weights/scores, a single row = the activation norm vector
channels.line: solid grey arrows = steps; dashed outlines = the grouping over which weights are compared
channels.frame: a dashed frame = one comparison group

quality.strengths: The contribution is shown as a side-by-side comparison with the prior method on the identical toy matrix, so the reader can see exactly which cells change; numbers in the cells make the scoring checkable; dashed group frames encode the per-layer vs per-output difference as geometry; the activation vector is drawn as data feeding the score.
quality.weaknesses: The score formulas S = |W| and S = |W| . ||X||_2 are typeset above the matrices; the two panels are not quite identical in layout because the Wanda panel adds the activation vector below, offsetting its matrices vertically.

figures.lesson: Use a tiny integer-valued weight matrix with cells tinted kept versus pruned, and draw the comparison group as dashed boxes (whole matrix versus one per row), so a reader can check each pruning decision by reading the numbers.

figures.title: wav2vec 2.0: A Framework for Self-Supervised Learning of Speech Representations

taxonomy.task: self-supervised speech representation learning

arrangement.units: one unframed stack of horizontal tiers (waveform, CNN, latents with quantizers, Transformer band, context outputs), named by a left margin column of labels
arrangement.inputs_as: a real raw audio waveform drawn as a dense black trace across the full width
arrangement.losses_at: top: a single loss symbol L above the context row, reached by curved arrows from the quantizer circles and from the masked context square
arrangement.shared: the CNN is drawn as five identical overlapping triangles, one per time step

insights.structure: Five horizontal tiers stacked bottom to top (waveform, CNN triangles, latents plus quantizers, Transformer band, context squares), each named in a left label column with its math symbol.
insights.data: The input is a real dense waveform trace, latent and context vectors are small blue squares per time step, quantized targets are green 'q' circles, and the masked position's output is the one grey square.
insights.emphasis: The loss is pulled out to the top as one italic L that curved arrows converge on, and the wide yellow Transformer band is the only warm colour in the figure.
insights.flow: Straight short arrows run upward through each tier, while long curved arrows sweep from the green q circles over the Transformer to the loss at top, making the target path visibly bypass the context network.
insights.avoid: The curved loss arrows cross the Transformer band and each other, so which q pairs with which context output is hard to trace.

core.what: a bottom-to-top tower over the waveform where curved arrows from the quantized q nodes and from a context output converge on one contrastive loss symbol L at the top, pairing context representations with quantized targets

relations.form: bottom to top with named rows on the left: raw waveform X -> overlapping blue CNN triangles producing latent squares Z -> a wide yellow masked Transformer -> context squares C
long curved arrows from several green q circles and from the grey masked-position context square run up to a single L at the top labelled Contrastive loss
each latent square z sends one arrow up into the transformer and a short diagonal arrow to its own green q circle, so the same latent feeds both the context network and the quantized target
the raw waveform is drawn as a real black audio trace spanning the full width under five overlapping CNN receptive-field triangles

channels.colour: blue = CNN encoder and its latent/context vectors, green = quantized representations, yellow = transformer, grey = the context vector at the masked position
channels.shape: triangles = convolutional receptive fields, small squares = per-step vectors, circles = quantizer outputs, wide box = transformer
channels.line: straight short arrows = forward data, long curved arrows = inputs to the contrastive loss
channels.frame: no grouping frames; row names with symbols on the left act as a key

quality.strengths: Every representation in the objective (Z, Q, C) is drawn as its own row of nodes with a named key, and the loss is drawn as the point where the q and c nodes meet; the receptive fields are drawn as overlapping triangles on a real waveform; the masked position is singled out by a grey context square.
quality.weaknesses: The contrastive pairing is a tangle of long curved arrows crossing the transformer to one L, so which q is positive versus distractor is not shown; blue covers both the CNN and the context outputs C; the masking itself is only a word inside the transformer box rather than drawn on the masked latents.

figures.lesson: Label each horizontal tier once in a left margin column with its name and math symbol (X, Z, Q, C) so the drawing itself can stay free of text and the reader matches tiers to the paper's notation.

figures.title: WavLM: Large-Scale Self-Supervised Pre-Training for Full Stack Speech Processing
figures.venue: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Signal Processing

taxonomy.task: self-supervised speech representation

arrangement.units: one grey rounded container around the CNN and transformer blocks
arrangement.inputs_as: waveform thumbnail with an overlapped green segment
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: A single grey rounded container holds two stacked orange blocks, a thin 'CNN Encoders' bar and a large 'Transformer Encoder with Gated Relative Position Bias' block, with a row of frame tokens between them; target tokens z1..z6 sit above the container and a green 'Mask Prediction Loss' pill on top.
insights.data: The input is a blue waveform with a green overlapped segment (simulated interfering speech); frame features are blue x_i boxes and masked ones are brown [M] boxes; targets are grey z_i boxes.
insights.emphasis: Red dashed lines from z2, z3, z4 converge on the loss pill, showing loss only on masked positions, and the green-overlaid waveform shows the denoising input without a separate label.
insights.flow: Strictly bottom to top with vertical black arrows: waveform -> CNN -> tokens (masked) -> transformer -> outputs -> loss.
insights.avoid: The overlapped-speech augmentation, the key difference from HuBERT, is only a green tint on the waveform with no label, so readers can miss it.

core.what: a single bottom-to-top tower inside one rounded grey frame: waveform -> CNN Encoders -> frame tokens with three masked [M] slots -> Transformer Encoder with Gated Relative Position Bias -> outputs z1..z6 -> Mask Prediction Loss

relations.form: vertical stack read bottom to top, every stage spanning the same width with straight parallel arrows between them
masking is drawn on the token row itself: x1, x5, x6 stay blue while the three middle slots become dark-gold [M] boxes; the waveform below has a green overlapping segment marking mixed-in speech
red dashed lines from only the masked-position outputs z2, z3, z4 converge on a red point under the green Mask Prediction Loss box

channels.colour: orange = network modules (CNN encoders, transformer), blue = unmasked frame features and the primary waveform, dark gold = masked [M] tokens, green = the overlapped interfering speech and also the loss box, grey = output vectors z
channels.shape: large rounded rectangles = modules, small squares = per-frame tokens
channels.line: solid black arrows = forward pass, red dashed = which outputs enter the loss
channels.frame: the rounded grey frame encloses the model

quality.strengths: Masked positions are drawn as distinct tokens in the row, and only their outputs are wired to the loss by a separate red dashed style, so which positions are predicted is visible; the overlapped utterance is shown on the real waveform by a second colour.
quality.weaknesses: Green carries two meanings (the interfering speech in the waveform and the loss box); the prediction targets (pseudo-labels) that the loss compares z against are not drawn, so the objective has only one side; the contribution (gated relative position bias) is only text inside the generic transformer box, which is the same orange as the CNN.

figures.lesson: Masked positions are shown by absence as well as by colour: the CNN sends no arrow into the [M] slots, and only those columns get the red dashed curves into the loss, so the training objective reads from the drawing without a text label.

figures.title: Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision

taxonomy.task: multitask multilingual speech recognition and translation

arrangement.units: top-left: grey rounded panel of data examples; top-right: unboxed model area with teal/red block stacks grouped by curly braces; bottom: full-width grey rounded panel that zooms into the decoder input strip
arrangement.inputs_as: quoted example sentences with speaker/notepad icons in a panel, feeding a log-Mel spectrogram raster via a hollow block arrow
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; a 'next-token prediction' label on the arrow out of the decoder top
arrangement.shared: token-type colour code (orange/blue/green) reused across the model's token strips and the format panel

insights.structure: Three zones: a tall grey rounded data panel at top-left, an unboxed encoder/decoder pair at top-right (teal encoder stack and red decoder stack side by side, each grouped by a coloured curly brace), and a full-width grey 'Multitask training format' panel at the bottom that flares up in a wedge from the decoder's input token strip.
insights.data: Training data is shown as paired lines per task (speaker icon + navy quoted speech, notepad icon + green transcript, in English, Spanish and Korean), audio input is a small log-Mel spectrogram raster under a lilac Conv1D trapezoid, and decoder input/output are rows of adjacent square cells coloured orange (special), blue (text) and green (timestamp), the output row shifted one cell left.
insights.emphasis: The model itself is drawn as stock Transformer blocks; the contribution (data scale and token format) gets the two big bold-titled panels, and red arrows with labels name the task each special token selects (Language identification, X->X Transcription, X->English Translation, VAD, Custom vocabulary).
insights.flow: Read left to right: data panel -> large hollow block arrow -> spectrogram, encoder up bottom-to-top, a 'cross attention' bus leaving the encoder top and dropping into every decoder block, decoder up to next-token output; then down into the bottom state machine read left to right from a start dot through PREV / SOT / LANGUAGE TAG / TRANSCRIBE-or-TRANSLATE / timestamps to EOT, with dotted skip paths to EOT.
insights.avoid: The bottom state machine is dense (crossing arrows between TRANSCRIBE/TRANSLATE and begin-time/NO TIMESTAMPS, a long dotted line along the panel bottom from NO SPEECH to EOT) and the block-internal labels (MLP, cross attention, self attention) are set very small inside thin bars.

core.what: the encoder-decoder transformer at top right takes a log-Mel spectrogram up a teal encoder tower and multitask-format tokens up a red decoder tower, with cross-attention lines from the encoder top into every decoder block

relations.form: two bottom-to-top towers side by side: spectrogram -> 2x Conv1D + GELU trapezoid -> teal encoder blocks (left), token row -> red decoder blocks -> shifted token row with next-token prediction (right)

one line from the encoder top branches horizontally into each decoder block, labelled cross attention; positional encodings enter each tower's input at a circled plus from the side (a sine glyph and a database cylinder)

the training-data panel on the left lists four task types (English transcription, any-to-English translation, non-English transcription, no speech), each as an audio-quote line and a transcript line, feeding the model through a large hollow arrow
the decoder input token row is tied by two diverging lines to a full-width bottom panel 'Multitask training format' that expands its grammar

the bottom panel is a left-to-right token state graph: start dot -> PREV -> previous text tokens -> START OF TRANSCRIPT -> LANGUAGE TAG or NO SPEECH -> TRANSCRIBE or TRANSLATE -> timestamped or NO TIMESTAMPS branches -> EOT, with red arrows and labels naming the task each token selects

channels.colour: token colour = token kind (orange special tokens, blue text tokens, green timestamp tokens, keyed bottom-left), consistent between the decoder's token rows and the format panel; teal = encoder blocks, red/pink = decoder blocks; in the data panel navy = audio content and green = transcript text, so green is reused for timestamps; red arrows/brackets = task annotations
channels.shape: rounded boxes = tokens and transformer blocks, trapezoid = conv stem, circled plus = addition, cylinder = learned embedding table
channels.line: solid arrows = data/token order, dotted line = the no-speech path to EOT, red arrows = task labels pointing into tokens
channels.frame: rounded grey panels = the training data and the training format; braces group encoder and decoder blocks

quality.strengths: Token kinds are keyed and coloured identically in the decoder rows and the format grammar, and the zoom lines tie the token row to its expansion; data is real (spectrogram, multilingual quoted sentences); the multitask format, which is the paper's contribution, gets the full bottom width.
quality.weaknesses: Green means both transcript text in the data panel and timestamp tokens in the format panel; the cross-attention bus is a long line that loops above the encoder and down the gap; the no-speech dotted path runs a long detour along the bottom of the format panel to EOT.

figures.lesson: A token-type colour code is defined once in a small legend and reused in the model's input and output strips and in the state-machine panel that wedges out of the input strip, so that panel reads as an expansion of those tokens without any connecting arrow.

figures.title: Whisper-AT: Noise-Robust Automatic Speech Recognizers are Also Strong General Audio Event Taggers

taxonomy.task: audio event tagging from a frozen speech recogniser's layer representations
taxonomy.note: family other = general audio tagging head on a frozen ASR model (closest family: speech-recognition)

arrangement.units: a top lane holding the frozen Whisper encoder/decoder chain; three unframed vertical columns (one per shown layer) below it, separated by whitespace and '......'; a bottom lane for the layer-wise fusion and classifier
arrangement.inputs_as: a rotated text label 'Input Audio (10s)' with an arrow into the first encoder block
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the output 'Audio Labels' sits at the bottom-right end of the classifier row
arrangement.shared: the Temporal Transformer is drawn once per column and the copies are joined by dashed rounded 'Shared' capsules between them

insights.structure: The frozen Whisper chain runs along the top, an identical processing column hangs below each shown layer output, and a bottom row fuses the gathered column outputs.
insights.data: Every intermediate is drawn as a stack of square token cells sized to its length (500 cells beside each Whisper block, 25 after pooling, one cell for a 512-d vector, a 32-cell row after gathering) and labelled with its shape.
insights.emphasis: The two new Transformers are the only saturated orange boxes; the frozen backbone is grey with dashed borders and rotated labels.
insights.flow: Columns read top to bottom from each backbone layer, a brace gathers their outputs into one horizontal row, and the classifier row reads left to right to 'Audio Labels' at the bottom right.
insights.avoid: The first Temporal Pooling of each column sits inside the backbone row, between a Whisper block and the next, so the frozen chain and the new branch share one row and their arrows interleave.

core.what: the outputs of identical per-layer columns converge through one brace into a (32, 512) token row that a single Layer Transformer reads

relations.form: the frozen Whisper encoder blocks and decoder run left to right along the top row to 'Text'
three identical vertical columns, evenly spaced, each hanging from one backbone layer's token column, with '......' marking the elided layers
the per-column Temporal Transformer copies are linked by small dashed 'Shared' capsules between neighbouring columns
a curly brace under the three column outputs gathers them into one 32-cell token row feeding the orange Layer Transformer at bottom left of the classifier row

channels.colour: kind of block: grey = frozen Whisper, lavender = lightweight per-layer operations and classifier, orange = the new Transformers
channels.shape: square-cell stacks = token sequences (count of cells ~ length), rounded boxes = operations
channels.line: solid arrows for data flow; dashed outlines mark frozen Whisper blocks, and a dashed capsule marks weight sharing, so dashing carries two meanings
channels.frame: none; columns are units by alignment only

quality.strengths: The convergence is visible as geometry (identical columns, a brace, one row); every tensor between modules is drawn as token cells with its shape, so what the Layer Transformer attends over is shown; the contribution is the only saturated fill; weight sharing is marked between the copies rather than by a far-off note.
quality.weaknesses: Dashed lines mean both 'frozen' (Whisper block borders) and 'shared' (capsules); the first pooling step sits inside the backbone row so the frozen chain's arrows interleave with branch arrows; the input label is rotated vertical text at the far left; tensor-shape labels in every row add dense text.

figures.lesson: Hang one identical column under each backbone layer, join the copies of a weight-shared module by small dashed 'Shared' capsules, and gather the columns' outputs with a brace into one token row that the fusion module reads.

figures.title: Wide & Deep Learning for Recommender Systems

taxonomy.task: app recommendation / click prediction

arrangement.units: four horizontal dashed bands (Sparse Features, Dense Embeddings, Hidden Layers, Output Units) crossed by three unframed model columns named in a grey chevron band at the bottom
arrangement.inputs_as: a row of grey and yellow circles for the sparse features
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; a single yellow output unit tops each column
arrangement.shared: the layer bands and their bold labels are shared by all three columns

insights.structure: Three model columns (Wide, Wide & Deep, Deep) stand on four shared horizontal dashed bands, with the band names in bold between the middle and right columns and the model names in a grey chevron strip at the bottom.
insights.data: Sparse features are a row of grey circles with a few yellow active ones, dense embeddings are grey rounded bars holding four dark-to-light circles, and hidden and output units are yellow circles with a black activation stroke.
insights.emphasis: The proposed model is placed between its two parents, and its one output unit collects both a long fan of lines from the sparse features and the lines from its hidden stack.
insights.flow: Everything reads bottom to top along thin grey lines that fan in from features to embeddings, hidden layers and a single output unit per column.
insights.avoid: The dashed bands start at different x positions and their labels sit inside the gap between columns, and the dense identical grey fans make individual wide connections hard to follow.

core.what: three network diagrams side by side on shared horizontal layer bands — Wide Models, Wide & Deep Models (centre), Deep Models — so the joint model reads as the left and right models merged

relations.form: three node-link networks on one canvas with labels on a grey arrow-ended band at the bottom, the combined model in the middle rather than last
dashed horizontal bands labelled Output Units, Hidden Layers, Dense Embeddings, Sparse Features run across all three models so the same layer sits at the same height
in the centre model the wide sparse features connect directly to the output unit while the deep path goes through embeddings and hidden layers into the same output unit
each layer is drawn as actual neuron circles and every connection as a grey line, with embeddings as grey-shaded circle groups

channels.colour: yellow = active sparse features and neurons with activation glyph, grey = inactive features and connections; grey shades in dense embeddings = embedding values
channels.shape: circles = units, circles with a sigmoid glyph = neurons with activation, shaded rectangles = embedding vectors
channels.line: thin grey lines = weights; dashed rectangles = layer bands
channels.frame: dashed bands = one layer type across models

quality.strengths: Aligning all three models on the same layer bands makes the combined model visibly the union of the wide and deep models; layers are drawn as actual units, so the wide model's single layer versus the deep model's stack is geometry, not text.
quality.weaknesses: The combined (proposed) model is placed in the middle rather than last, and is not visually emphasised over the baselines; the dense fan of grey connection lines makes the centre model heavy; yellow marks both active sparse inputs and all neurons, mixing 'active feature' with 'neuron'.

figures.lesson: Draw the proposed hybrid as the middle column between its two parent models on shared layer bands, so the reader sees it is literally the union of the wide fan and the deep stack.

figures.title: World Models

taxonomy.task: visual reinforcement learning with a learned world model and a compact controller
taxonomy.note: training 'other': the controller C is optimised by evolution strategies (CMA-ES), separately from the VAE and MDN-RNN

arrangement.units: one blue dotted rounded frame for the world model (V over M); environment box, observation image and controller triangle float outside it on whitespace
arrangement.inputs_as: one real game frame (VizDoom screenshot) captioned 'observation', fed by an arrow from the environment box above
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the figure shows only the inference/control loop
arrangement.shared: the action output of C is split: one line returns up the right edge to the environment, another runs along the bottom back into M, both labelled 'action'

insights.structure: V (hourglass) sits above M (rounded box) inside one dotted 'world model' frame in the centre, with the environment box above, the observation frame to the left and the controller triangle to the right, so the loop circles the frame.
insights.data: The observation is a real game screenshot while the latent signals are just single italic letters on the arrows (z out of V, h out of M), with no tensor drawings.
insights.emphasis: Colour is spent only on the blue dotted frame and its blue label, so the named model stands out without filled boxes.
insights.flow: Clockwise loop: environment -> observation -> V -> z down to M and across to C, h from M to C, then 'action' arrows exit C back up to the environment and back along the bottom into M.
insights.avoid: The two 'action' lines and the h line cross and bend around C's lower-right corner, so the return path into M is hard to trace.

core.what: an agent-environment loop: observation enters the VAE, the controller C outputs an action that runs up the right side and back along the top into the environment box, which returns the next observation

relations.form: a closed rectangular cycle around the figure: environment (top) -> observation frame (left) -> VAE -> C (right) -> action back to environment, plus a second action line from C looping under the MDN-RNN back into it
inside the world model, the VAE (hourglass) sends z straight down into the MDN-RNN box
z from the VAE and h from the MDN-RNN converge on the triangular controller C from the left
V and M are grouped in a dotted blue rounded frame labelled 'world model', separate from C

channels.colour: blue = the world-model grouping (dotted frame and its label); everything else black on white
channels.shape: hourglass = VAE, rounded rectangle = recurrent model and environment, triangle = controller, image = observation
channels.line: solid black arrows for all data and actions; dotted blue only for the grouping frame
channels.frame: dotted blue frame = the world model (V + M)

quality.strengths: The observation is a real game frame; shapes separate the three components (hourglass VAE, box RNN, triangle controller); the world-model grouping is a single dotted frame that excludes the controller, matching the paper's V/M/C split.
quality.weaknesses: The action feedback into the MDN-RNN is a long line that wraps under the world model frame and back up, and the action to the environment runs around the right and top edges; the z line to C forks off the VAE-to-RNN line with a corner, so the controller's two inputs are not parallel short paths.

figures.lesson: Draw an agent as a closed loop around the environment and wrap only the learned model in one coloured dotted frame, so the reader sees which part is 'the world model' and which is the small policy.

figures.title: Wuerstchen: An Efficient Architecture for Large-Scale Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

taxonomy.task: efficient text-to-image generation

arrangement.units: three unboxed full-width horizontal bands divided by dashed rules, each one training stage with a large text label at its left edge
arrangement.inputs_as: photo thumbnail drawn as a slanted 3-D slab with its pixel size on the edges
arrangement.losses_at: top of each band (teal 'diffusion loss' box above the model, Stages B and C)
arrangement.shared: modules reused across bands keep the same frustum shape and fill (light-green f4 encoder in A and B, peach Semantic Compressor in B and C)

insights.structure: Three full-width horizontal bands (Training of Stage A / B / C) separated by dashed grey rules, each with a large left-hand stage label and its own left-to-right pipeline; Stage A is a mirror-symmetric hourglass, Stages B and C split into a main row and a second row for the Semantic Compressor or noising path.
insights.data: Input and output images are photo thumbnails drawn as slanted slabs with pixel sizes written along their edges (1024/1024/3, 768/768/3), latents and VQ tokens are small 3-D cubes tiled with multicolour cells, and tensor shapes (4x256x256, 1280x24x24, 16x24x24) are written on the arrows.
insights.emphasis: Each band's diffusion model is the largest shape with the largest label ('Model' plus italic symbol): a pale-yellow notched U-Net-like block in Stage B and a slate-purple cuboid in Stage C, the darkest fill in the figure; encoders and the Semantic Compressor are translucent frustums whose narrowing shows the downsampling factor (f4, f32).
insights.flow: Each band reads left to right; loss paths leave the latent cube, run up and across to a teal 'diffusion loss' box above the model and back down from the output, and the conditioning branch (Semantic Compressor -> 1x1 conv -> c_sc) enters the Stage B model from below with text-conditioning joining it.
insights.avoid: The same role gets different fills across bands (yellow model in B, purple in C) and the Stage A band draws no loss at all; small connector labels (1024->786 in a pale-yellow box, against 768 written on the Stage C image) are tiny and visibly inconsistent.

core.what: three training stages stacked as horizontal bands separated by grey rules (Stage A VQGAN reconstruction, Stage B latent image decoder, Stage C text-conditional generation), each read left to right

relations.form: three full-width bands top to bottom with large 'Training of Stage A/B/C' titles on the left
Stage A: image -> green trapezoid encoder f_Theta -> blue Quantizer Q -> coloured token cube -> lilac decoder -> image
the green f_Theta encoder from Stage A reappears in Stage B, and the peach Semantic Compressor e_phi appears in both Stage B and Stage C, drawn in the same shape and fill
in Stage B the compressed semantic code C_sc (through a 1x1 conv) and text-conditioning arrive from below into the yellow Model f_theta, which also takes the noised latents from the left
in Stages B and C a green 'diffusion loss' box sits above the model, with a line from the clean latent on the left and a line from the model output on the right meeting in it

channels.colour: fill = component identity (green VQGAN encoder, lilac decoder, blue quantizer, peach semantic compressor, yellow Stage B model, purple Stage C model, grey latent noising, teal-green loss); multicolour cubes = latent tensors
channels.shape: 3-D trapezoids/frusta = encoders/decoders with resolution change, flat image tiles = images, cubes = latent tensors, flat boxes = operations or losses
channels.line: solid black arrows only, with tensor sizes as labels
channels.frame: no enclosing frames; thin grey horizontal rules separate the stages

quality.strengths: Reused components keep their shape and fill across stages (f_Theta in A and B, e_phi in B and C), so the cascade's reuse reads without labels; tensor shapes are written on the wires (4x256x256, 16x24x24); both sides of each diffusion loss are drawn.
quality.weaknesses: The diffusion-loss inputs run on long lines that rise above the model and back down; the Stage B and Stage C models differ only in fill and could be mistaken for unrelated networks; the text-conditioning in Stage B enters from below via a long multi-segment path.

figures.lesson: For a multi-stage training figure, give each stage its own full-width band under a dashed rule and redraw a module that is reused across stages with the same shape and fill colour in every band, so the reader can track the reused parts without separate frozen or shared markers.

figures.title: xDeepFM: Combining Explicit and Implicit Feature Interactions for Recommender Systems

taxonomy.task: CTR prediction with explicit feature interactions
taxonomy.note: architecture other: the Compressed Interaction Network, a stack of layers each formed by outer products with the input field embeddings and compressed into feature maps, sum-pooled per layer

arrangement.units: three unboxed sub-figures side by side, each named by a bold sub-caption beneath it
arrangement.inputs_as: circle-grid embedding matrices (x^k, x^0) with brace-labelled dimensions
arrangement.shared: x^0 field-embedding matrix drawn in every panel; peach for active slices

insights.structure: Three sub-figures in one row with bold captions (a)-(c): (a) outer product of x^k and x^0 producing the tensor Z^{k+1}, (b) the k-th layer compressing Z^{k+1} into H_{k+1} feature maps, (c) the whole CIN with layers x^1...x^k side by side and x^0 below.
insights.data: Embedding matrices are boxes holding grids of circles (rows = fields, columns = embedding dims) labelled by curly braces (m, D, H_k); the intermediate tensor Z^{k+1} is an oblique 3-D slab of stacked sheets; layer outputs in (c) are tilted sheets of grey ellipses.
insights.emphasis: Colour marks only the data taking part in the step: the active column slice is peach and boxed by a dashed rectangle while other circles are grey, and in (b) olive and teal fans of lines converge from the peach circles onto two coloured feature-map dots.
insights.flow: Panels read left to right as zoom-out from one operation to the module; inside (a) and (b) the flow goes bottom to top (matrices up to the tensor, tensor up to feature maps), in (c) thick blue block arrows go from x^0 to every layer and between layers, then sum-pooling arrows rise to a top bar of yellow circles and a gold output arrow.
insights.avoid: Panel (b)'s two fans of about two dozen thin crossing lines are cluttered, and panel (c)'s sheet labels (H_1, H_2, D, Sum pooling) are very small; the three panels also use different projections for the same tensor.

core.what: the compressed interaction network is shown operating on the embedding matrix itself: (a) the outer product of x^k and x^0 columns forms a 3-D tensor Z^{k+1}, (b) that tensor is compressed by lines from its cells into feature maps of x^{k+1}

relations.form: matrices are drawn as grids of circles with the operated column highlighted orange inside a dashed frame, and the product tensor Z^{k+1} is a 3-D slab with orange circle cells
three captioned sub-figures (a), (b), (c) left to right: one interaction, one layer, the whole architecture
in (b) many thin lines from the cells of Z^{k+1} converge on one dark-green and one teal node at the top, each a feature map of x^{k+1}
in (c) the layers x^1, x^2, ..., x^k are a row of stacked-slice glyphs joined by thick blue arrows, with x^0 at the bottom sending a blue arrow up into every layer
in (c) each layer is sum-pooled upward into a yellow node row that ends in a brown output arrow

channels.colour: orange = the entries taking part in the current interaction, grey = other embedding entries; dark green vs teal = two different feature maps and their weight lines; blue = layer-to-layer and x^0 arrows; yellow = pooled outputs
channels.shape: circle grids = embedding matrices, 3-D slabs = intermediate tensors, stacked slices = layer outputs
channels.line: thin black arrows in (a), coloured thin lines for filter weights in (b), thick blue arrows for the recurrence in (c); dashed rectangles mark the operated column or feature-map slice
channels.frame: dashed frames = the slice being operated on

quality.strengths: The interaction is drawn on the actual matrix and tensor shapes with dimension braces (H_k, m, D), so the outer product and compression are visible as geometry; the three panels zoom out from one product to one layer to the network; x^0 feeding every layer is drawn as fan-in arrows.
quality.weaknesses: The panels are not tied to each other except by symbols (no matching tint or callout from (c) to (b)); the green and teal line fan in (b) is dense and crosses; the orange highlight means 'current column' in (a) but all cells in Z^{k+1}, so its meaning shifts between panels.

figures.lesson: Draw the field-embedding matrix as a grid of circles (m fields × D dims) and colour only the slice being combined against grey dots, so a tensor operation reads as which dots light up.

figures.title: Zero-1-to-3: Zero-shot One Image to 3D Object

taxonomy.task: single-image novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction

arrangement.units: one unframed composition: a top conditioning row in brackets and a bottom noise -> model -> output row
arrangement.inputs_as: a photorealistic render of an object plus the math tuple (R,T) inside large square brackets; Gaussian noise as a colour-noise square at the left of the bottom row
arrangement.shared: none

insights.structure: Two rows: a bracketed condition [input view, (R,T)] on top, and noise -> yellow 'Zero-1-to-3' box -> output view below, joined by a curly brace pointing down into the box.
insights.data: Input and output are the same photorealistic retro computer rendered from two viewpoints, so the viewpoint change is visible, while the camera transform is only the symbol (R,T).
insights.emphasis: The single saturated yellow box carries the method name in large type over a tiny network icon, the only coloured shape in the figure.
insights.flow: The bottom row reads left to right through two thick black block arrows, and the condition enters from above through the brace.
insights.avoid: The figure hides the denoising loop and the network internals entirely, so it cannot show where the pose conditioning is injected; it works only as a concept sketch.

core.what: a brace under the bracketed pair [input view image, (R, T)] converges onto the yellow Zero-1-to-3 latent diffusion box from above, while noise enters from the left and the novel view leaves on the right

relations.form: one horizontal row: Gaussian noise image -> thick black arrow -> yellow Zero-1-to-3 box -> thick black arrow -> rendered output view
the conditioning tuple is drawn as a large bracketed pair (a rendered retro computer and the text (R, T)) above the model, gathered by one curly brace pointing down into it
the input view (front-facing computer) and output view (same computer seen from another angle) are the same object rendered from two viewpoints, at the top and the right

channels.colour: yellow = the model (the only coloured element); images carry their own colour
channels.shape: rounded box = model, images = input/output/noise, brace and square brackets = the conditioning tuple
channels.line: thick black block arrows for the generation path; the brace stands in for the conditioning line
channels.frame: square brackets frame the conditioning pair

quality.strengths: Input, noise and output are real images, and the same object shown from two viewpoints makes the task (novel view synthesis from a relative camera transform) clear without text; the conditioning tuple is drawn as a literal bracketed pair rather than a wire.
quality.weaknesses: The model is a single opaque box with a tiny network icon, so how the image and (R, T) are injected is not shown; the camera transform is only a typeset symbol (R, T) rather than drawn as a viewpoint change; the large rendered computer takes most of the space while the method occupies a small box.

figures.lesson: For a conditioning contribution, write the condition as a bracketed tuple of real data and a pose symbol, then use a curly brace to funnel it into a single bright model box sitting on the noise-to-output row.

figures.title: Zip-NeRF: Anti-Aliased Grid-Based Neural Radiance Fields

taxonomy.task: anti-aliased grid-based radiance fields: multisample each conical frustum with a rotated hexagonal pattern to query a multi-resolution grid

arrangement.units: two unframed panels side by side, each a perspective ray with four tinted frustums and a circular along-the-ray inset in its lower right
arrangement.inputs_as: a toy ray with an exaggerated pixel width
arrangement.shared: the same ray and frustums in both panels; only the sample pattern's rotation and flip differ

insights.structure: Two identical panels (training, testing), each a perspective ray of four tinted frustums with a head-on circular inset in the lower right.
insights.data: The data is toy geometry: a ray, its cone frustums and their sample points; numbers in the inset index the samples of each frustum.
insights.emphasis: Only colour structures it: each frustum, its samples and its inset ring share one tint.
insights.flow: The ray runs from its origin dot at the bottom left to the top right; the panels compare left to right; no arrows.
insights.avoid: Do not leave the only difference between two panels to be found in two small insets; mark what changes.

core.what: the multisample pattern is drawn on the ray itself: each of four tinted frustums carries its sample dots, and a head-on inset shows the same samples as numbered markers in matching rings

relations.form: sample dots placed inside each translucent cone frustum along the ray, in the frustum's tint
(a) training and (b) testing as identical panels side by side, differing only in how the patterns are rotated
a circular inset in each panel's lower right shows the view along the ray, tied to the frustums by matching tints, with no leader line
the four frustums run from near (blue) to far (red) along one diagonal ray

channels.colour: frustum identity (blue, orange, green, red from near to far) on the frustum fill, its samples and its ring in the inset; one meaning throughout
channels.shape: dots = samples, numbered circles = samples seen head-on in the inset, grey squares on the ray (meaning not given in the figure)
channels.line: grey line = the ray; thin tinted lines join samples within a frustum; dark ellipses = frustum boundaries
channels.frame: none

quality.strengths: The sampling is drawn on the geometry it acts on, a ray of cone frustums, not as a block. One colour per frustum, carried into the inset. Training and testing are identical panels, so only the pattern differs. The head-on inset makes the hexagonal pattern's rotation readable where the perspective view cannot.
quality.weaknesses: The inset is tied to the ray only by tint, with no callout. The difference between (a) and (b) must be found by comparing digit positions in two small insets. The grey squares on the ray and the thin lines joining samples are not explained in the figure. The far frustum's large translucent fill dominates the panel though every frustum carries the same number of samples.

figures.lesson: Show where samples fall in a 3-D volume twice, in perspective along the ray and as a head-on inset with the same tints and numbered markers, so the pattern's rotation can be read.
